items.title: Disjoint Borel annuli that every injective ray meets infinitely often at Borel asymptotic separation index one
items.author: Felix Weilacher
items.work: Borel Edge Colorings for Finite Dimensional Groups
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the article's Lemma lem:rainbow at source lines 173-175: from asi_B(G)=1 and a dimension d it must produce pairwise disjoint Borel sets V_i that every injective G-ray meets infinitely often. The construction can only be read off after fixing the two-piece Borel partition at the scale N=4d+1 and taking V_i = A(U_0,2(i-1),2i) (source line 180), and the real work is then to rule out the one way it could fail, namely a ray that keeps within distance 2d of U_0; that step needs the finite-component hypothesis on G^{<=N} restricted to U_0 together with local finiteness (source line 182) and a separate symmetric argument for U_0. Local combinatorics of a single ray does not give this, because the hypothesis is a global finiteness condition on distance-N components and the annuli exist only relative to a partition chosen beforehand; the change-of-distance-by-one step at line 184 is what finally converts a crossing of the two pieces into an edge inside every annulus.

items.title: Hyperfiniteness on the set covered infinitely often by separated Borel sets of a bounded-degree decomposition
items.author: Bal\'azs Bursics, Zolt\'an Vidny\'anszky
items.work: Hyperfiniteness on Topological Ramsey Spaces
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Theorem t:separation2 at source lines 425-430: an increasing sequence of bounded-degree Borel graphs G_n covering a CBER E, a scale f with f(n+1) >= 2(f(n)+1), and Borel sets B_n that are f(n)-separated in G_n jointly force E restricted to B, where B is the set of points lying in infinitely many B_n, to be hyperfinite. The construction H_{n+1} = H_n union the G_{n+1}-edges inside B meeting B_{n+1} (source line 593) is one line, but the diameter bound is not: the inner Claim at lines 597-606 first has to exclude two points of B_{n+1} in one component of H_{n+1} by routing the interior of a shortest path through a single component of H_n and applying the induction hypothesis, which yields dist_{G_{n+1}}(x,x') <= f(n)+2 <= f(n+1) against the separation of B_{n+1} (line 602). The remaining vertices are then one H_n-component per G_{n+1}-neighbour of the single B_{n+1}-point, giving diam(H) <= 2(f(n)+1) <= f(n+1) (lines 604-605). The factor 2 with the +1 offset is what makes this induction close, so neither a bounded-degree counting argument alone nor a direct matching decomposition of E restricted to B reaches the conclusion.

items.title: Uniformly computable arrays of thin colourings whose thin sets compute the k-th Turing jump
items.author: Lorenzo Carlucci, Oriola Gjetaj, Quentin Le Hou\'erou, Ludovic Levy Patey
items.work: Ramsey-like theorems for the Schreier barrier
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Lemma lem:arrays at source lines 683-685: two arrays of Turing indexes must be produced so that the k-th-jump-computable colourings f_n^k from n-element subsets onto n colours exist uniformly in n and k and every infinite f_n^k-thin set computes the k-th jump through the single index d_{n,k}. The colouring at source line 690 encodes a uniform modulus g_k of the k-th jump into a colour by comparing x_1 with g_k(x_0) and otherwise returning the largest i < n-1 with g_k(x_0) > x_{i+1}, and the three steps that follow are each needed: the top colour n-1 is avoided outright (line 692), thinness for any smaller colour c has to be pushed up to the colour n-2 by extending a tuple beyond g_k(x_0) (line 694), and only then does thinness for n-2 give the growth bound g_k(x_i) <= x_{i+n-1} which makes the jump computable from H (line 696). The uniformity in n and k, which the finite-dimensional result this lemma improves does not supply, is what cannot be obtained by quoting that result, and the article says so in the paragraph preceding the lemma.

Part (1) needs the weight computation, the annihilation by x^+_alpha (x) 1 through the root theta - alpha, and the standard sl_2 argument (source lines 469-476); part (2) requires specialising Garland's current-algebra identity to r = 2, s = 3k+1-i, alpha = theta, recognising that the resulting double sum can be grouped modulo the submodule generated by (x^-_theta (x) t^{2k+2-i}) wbar, and then acting by x^+_{theta-alpha} to convert the expansion into the claimed vanishing (lines 477-491). items.difficulty_reason: The proposition compares two polytopes that are only normally equivalent, and its proof must first replace the definition of the diagonal by a normal-fan condition: for x in the relative interior of a face F and y in the relative interior of a face G, the pair (x,y) lies in im(triangle_P) exactly when no vector w with <v,w> > 0 lies in -N_P(F)^* cap N_P(G)^* (source lines 1134-1146). items.title: Doubling an admissible hypercube matching profile into a perfect admissible tuple
items.author: Joshua Erde
items.work: Matchings in the hypercube with specified edges
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Lemma l:admissible at source lines 67-69: if x in N^n is an admissible profile and the new coordinate satisfies x_{n+1} = 2^n - 2||x||_1, then the concatenated tuple (2x, x_{n+1}) must be a perfect admissible tuple. The adjacent proof at source lines 70-84 has to construct the matching in the right ambient cube: it takes two disjoint copies of a matching M_1 with profile x inside Q^{n+1} (lines 71-76), then uses exactly the vertex set X of Q^n left uncovered by M_1, whose size is 2^n - 2||x||_1 = x_{n+1}, to add the direction-e_{n+1} edges joining the two copies of every uncovered vertex (lines 78-81). Both conclusions must then be checked, namely that M_3 is a matching with profile (2x, x_{n+1}) and that it is perfect because 2||x||_1 + |X| = 2^n (line 83). The step that is not a routine verification is the choice of the leftover set and the dimension, which makes the new coordinate absorb precisely the uncovered vertices; the argument is short and elementary once that choice is made, so it is rated H2.

items.title: A CW model for the open/closed Sullivan spaces: cells indexed by Sullivan-type arc graphs, cellular gluing maps and a deformation retraction onto the subspace of unit incoming weights
items.author: Ralph M. Kaufmann
items.work: Open/Closed String Topology and Moduli Space Actions via Open/Closed Hochschild Actions
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 6 (2010) article 036, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2010.036; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition asserts three things at once about the subspace Sull_1 of the weighted open/closed Sullivan space on which every incoming window has weight one: that it is a CW complex, that it is a sub-topological quasi-PROP, and that it is a deformation retract of the full Sullivan space, with k-cells indexed by Sullivan-type arc graphs with k + 1 arcs and attaching maps given by deleting arcs. The proof has to construct the cell decomposition before passing to PMC orbits, because only then do the weighted graphs of a fixed Sullivan type form a product of simplices whose sides may still be identified by the action, giving cells C(Gamma) with interiors the products of open simplices Delta^{|{arcs incident to w}|} over the incoming windows w (source lines 1586-1597). The step that cannot be done routinely is the associativity on the nose of the induced cellular gluing maps: the author transfers it from the closed case of the cited cell-operad theorem and then argues the open case separately, since gluing keeps the punctures and the 'twisted at the boundary' condition of the closed case does not arise (source lines 1607-1610).

items.title: Hausdorff dimension n-2 of the symmetric boundary of a strictly convex projective domain with C1 boundary
items.author: Olivier Glorieux; Daniel Monclair; Nicolas Tholozan
items.work: Hausdorff dimension of limit sets for projective Anosov representations
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 10 (2023), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.241
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem computes the Hausdorff dimension of the symmetric boundary partial Omega^sym = {(x,x*) : x in partial Omega} of a strictly convex projective domain with C^1 boundary, where the duality homeomorphism x -> x* is not C^1 unless the boundary is C^2, so the dimension of its graph is not immediate (the authors say so at source line 1014). The proof chooses two boundary points, identifies an affine patch with V x R, writes the boundary as the graph of a C^1 strictly convex function f, computes the dual point (u,f(u))* = (-d_uf, d_uf(u) - f(u)) and reduces the claim to the set {(u, d_uf)} in V x V*. The step that cannot be done routinely is the dimension bound itself: the authors introduce the symmetric bilinear form <(u,alpha),(v,beta)> = alpha(v) + beta(u) of signature (n-2,n-2), prove that difference vectors of the set have strictly positive square using d_uf(v-u) < f(v) - f(u), and then combine injectivity of the orthogonal projection onto a spacelike subspace with Brouwer's invariance of domain to exhibit the set as a 1-Lipschitz graph of dimension n-2 (source lines 1043-1060).

items.difficulty_reason: The statement fixes two orthogonal almost complex structures J and J' inducing the same orientation on a closed Riemannian six-manifold and asks for the homological intersection number of the two induced sections of the positive twistor space, a pairing that exists only because two six-dimensional fibres meet in a twelve-dimensional total space. items.title: Two-thirds power decay of the normal width of a centred section at the non-convex transport singular set
items.author: Shibing Chen, Jiakun Liu
items.work: Regularity of singular set in optimal transportation
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the lemma labelled ide1 at source lines 838-844: for a centred section of the potential v at the singular point's image y-zero, the maximal displacement d at e-one inside the target component obeys d at most a constant times h to the power two thirds minus epsilon, and every tangential width has its square bounded by that normal width. The proof is a volume comparison whose two sides must be matched in the right scale: the planar region D cut off by the uniformly convex boundary of Omega-sub-one-star contributes a factor of the three-halves power of the normal width (source lines 855-858), while thickening it by the tangential points at distance a constant times h to the power one half plus epsilon, taken from the tangential regularity of v at the base point, contributes the factor h to the power (one half plus epsilon) times (n minus two) (source lines 860-863). Comparing that product with the volume of the centred section, which is comparable to h to the power n over two (source lines 865-869), is exactly what produces the exponent two thirds minus epsilon, and it is the balance of the exponent one half plus epsilon from the tangential estimate against the inverse-square-law exponent from uniform convexity that makes the claim true. The second half of the statement is a different estimate, obtained by the uniform convexity inequality that turns a tangential displacement into a normal one (source lines 871-873). Nothing in the article before this point supplies the width bound, and neither a single-scaled barrier argument nor the volume estimate alone reaches it.

items.title: No omega-stable type of limit Morley rank has nonminimality degree equal to the Morley-sequence invariant together with definable Morley sequences
items.author: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
items.work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants

The argument turns on a strict Morley-rank gap: a single formula phi has to be extracted by compactness out of the set sigma of formulas that fork over A at every realization of q = (p) to the n-th tensor power, and lambda-prime = RM(phi(x, b_0 ... b_n) union p(x)) has to be shown strictly below lambda = RM(p), after which the limit ordinal lambda supplies lambda-prime-prime with lambda-prime < lambda-prime-prime < lambda and a type q in S(B) of that rank (source line 2893). The contradiction then makes one sequence play two roles at once: a Morley sequence in q over B is not a Morley sequence over A, since Kim's lemma would otherwise make B independent from a_0 over A, yet precisely its failure to be Morley over A makes phi(a_n, a_0 ... a_{n-1}) true and forces RM(phi(x, a_0 ... a_n) union p(x)) to be at least lambda-prime-prime, against the A-equivalence of a_0 ... a_{n-1} and b_0 ... b_{n-1}. The reduction to an algebraically closed base in T^eq, the stationarity of p and the two-sided reading of the single formula phi are compressed into one paragraph and are not a routine unfolding of definitions.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the lemma labelled lem:shore-blocking-wf at source lines 426-431: from any failure of well-foundedness below an ordinal beta witnessed by one of finitely many Turing functionals, it builds a single Turing functional Gamma-sub-k whose output is an M-infinite decreasing sequence below the natural product beta times k, with an index computable in k. The work is concentrated in the second half of the proof: the functionals are first twisted so that convergence at an input forces convergence at every smaller input and a strictly decreasing run of values below beta (source lines 434-439), and only then can the measurement alpha(sigma,e) be defined as the last convergent value and proved monotone in the oracle segment (source line 441). The blocking functional searches beyond the length of the previously found segment rather than beyond the previous input, which is what makes the newly found value strictly smaller than the old one (source lines 443-444 and 448-449); the natural sum of the k measurements is what converts k separate partial failures into one sequence, and the natural product bound beta times k is exactly what the companion lemma lem:wf-product needs. Totality of the blocking functional is not free either: it comes from totality of a single Phi-sub-e to the X plus the induction scheme for Sigma-0-1 formulas available in the model (source lines 446-447).

items.title: The 2-inverted Witt sheaf of a Z[1/2]-scheme is the pushforward of the Witt sheaf of its characteristic-zero fibre
items.author: Frédéric Déglise; Jean Fasel; Fangzhou Jin; Adeel A. Khan
items.work: On the rational motivic homotopy category
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.153
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Proposition 13.2 at source lines 2513-2519, label prop:Witt_2inverted: for a Z[1/2]-scheme S and a subring Lambda of Q with 2 invertible, the canonical map from the Lambda-linear Witt sheaf of S to the pushforward of the Lambda-linear Witt sheaf of the characteristic-zero fibre is an isomorphism. The proof at source lines 2520-2568 is the Witt analogue of the paper's key lemma but is proved directly and not deduced from it: it reduces to regular S and to the map on Witt groups W(S)[1/2] to W(S_Q)[1/2], then uses Balmer's Witt groups with support and the long exact localization sequence of a closed pair to reduce the claim to the vanishing of W^i(S,S_p)[1/2] for every odd prime p, and finally writes down the niveau/Gersten-Witt spectral sequence of W^{-i-j}(S,S_p) whose E^1 terms purity identifies with W(kappa(x)) when i+j is 0 mod 4 and with 0 otherwise. The non-routine step is the last one: those surviving E^1 terms are 2-primary torsion precisely because the residue fields have positive characteristic, so inverting 2 collapses the spectral sequence, and it is this observation, not the machinery itself, that decides the proposition. The argument is a self-contained appendix computation in which each tool is standard but the order and the reduction are specific, so the card is rated H2.

items.author: Maxim Nazarov
items.work: Yangian of the General Linear Lie Superalgebra

items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Proposition 3.1 at source lines 877-886, label zu: there is a formal power series Z(u) in u^{-1} with leading term 1 and central coefficients such that for all i, j the two displayed sums, the sum of T_kj(u+M-N) T'_ik(u) and the sum of T'_kj(u) T_ik(u+M-N), both equal delta_ij Z(u). The proof at source lines 888-977 must first build the rank-one operator Q = (id tensor tau)(P), compute Q^2 = (M-N)Q and invert (id tensor tau)(R(u)) as 1 + Q(u-M+N)^{-1}, then take the residue of the rescaled RTT relation at u = v+M-N; the non-routine step is the conclusion that either side of the resulting identity must equal Q tensor Z(v) because Q has one-dimensional image, which is what produces the series Z(v) instead of only a relation among generators. Centrality is a second, separate computation at source lines 941-977 with the projector Q_23 and the identity Q_23 R-hat_S_13(u+M-N) R_12(u) = (1-u^{-2}) Q_23, where the scalar factor is not invertible as a formal series and the conclusion has to be drawn from the two displays rather than by dividing. Both computations are self-contained once the paper's own RTT machinery is available, so the card is rated H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a possibly infinite Galois extension k-bar/k, a k-scheme X and a closed subset T-bar of X_k-bar that is stable under every sigma in Gal(k-bar/k), and asks for a closed subset T of X whose inverse image is T-bar (statement lines 900-909). After the reduction to X = Spec(A) the proof has to descend a radical ideal I-bar of the infinite tensor product A ⊗_k k-bar along the Galois action, and the two steps that are not formal are the finiteness reduction - an arbitrary x in I-bar already lies in A ⊗_k k' for some finite Galois subextension k'/k, so that the orbit polynomial P(T) = prod_{sigma in G}(T - sigma(x)) can be formed and is monic of degree |G| (proof lines 918-923) - and the identification of the invariants of that finite stage with A, which puts all coefficients a_i into A and hence, by sigma-invariance of I-bar, into I = A cap I-bar (proof lines 924-927). Only then does P(x) = 0 yield x^d in I(A ⊗_k k-bar), i.e. membership in a radical, which is what turns Galois invariance into an actual descent statement for closed subsets (proof lines 928-931).

items.title: Refining a one step devissage along an elementary etale neighbourhood of the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma must upgrade a one step devissage (Z, Y, i, pi, G, z, y) of F/X/S at x, after an arbitrary elementary etale neighbourhood (Y', y') -> (Y, y) -> (S, s), into a fresh one step devissage of the pullback F'' on a newly manufactured X'' together with an open Y'' of Y' x_{S'} S'' and Z'' = Z x_Y Y'' (statement lines 1049-1062). The proof manufactures X'' by applying the etale lifting lemma to the composite Z'' -> Z_{S''} -> X_{S''} so that Z'' = X'' x_{X_{S'}} Z_{S'} while keeping X'' affine, and then verifies every clause of the definition except one (proof lines 1065-1110). The clause that does not follow from the construction is geometric irreducibility of the fibres of Y'' -> S'', and the proof repairs exactly that: it takes the irreducible component T of Y'_{s'} through y', converts kappa(s) algebraically closed in kappa(y) into geometric connectedness of T and smoothness of T into geometric irreducibility, and only then invokes the normal-morphism lemma for the final elementary etale (S'', s'') -> (S', s'') with all fibres geometrically irreducible (proof lines 1112-1133). The same passage also has to preserve pi'' finite with pi''^{-1}({y''}) = {z''} and the dimension n of the support in the fibre, both checked through residue-field equalities and etale invariance of dimension at a point.

items.title: Products of varieties over an algebraically closed field are varieties
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma claims that over an algebraically closed field the product of two varieties is again a variety, i.e. integral, separated and of finite type over k (statement lines 90-92). After the finite-affine-covering reduction the whole content sits in the affine statement that A ⊗_k B is a domain for finitely generated k-domains A and B: the proof assumes a zero product of two nonzero tensors, normalises the coefficients to k-linearly independent families b_i and d_j with a_1, c_1 nonzero, and then consumes algebraic closedness of k at exactly one point, namely the Hilbert Nullstellensatz applied to the nonempty open D(a_1c_1) to obtain a maximal ideal m with A/m = k (proof lines 118-131). Evaluating the tensor relation at m then contradicts k-linear independence and the fact that B is a domain (proof lines 132-140). The step is not formal: over a non-algebraically-closed field the corresponding maximal ideal need not have residue field k, and the statement really fails there, as the chapter's own example example-product-not-a-variety at lines 70-77 shows.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:chow.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The statement asks for one finite extension A contained in B, with B/A killed by a power of the maximal ideal, over which several given nonzerodivisors a_1, ..., a_r simultaneously become unit multiples of a single local parameter at every maximal ideal of B. The proof reduces to r = 2 and then inducts on ell = min(length_A(A/a_1A), length_A(A/a_2A)): local solutions are first spread to A through the formal glueing lemma (chow.tex lines 681-693), A is then replaced by the blow-up ring of (a_1, a_2) built in lines 730-735 so that a_2 lies in (a_1), and the exponent m in a_2 = a_1^m c is shown to stay maximal under every further admissible finite extension by the discrete-valuation domination bound of lines 612-638. What is not routine is the termination step at lines 740-751: the pair must be rerun as (a_1, c), where one alternative is excluded by maximality of m and the other strictly decreases ell, so the induction closes only after combining the glueing, the blow-up and the boundedness input in that order.

items.title: Truncation level of the induction map along an n-connected map into a family of k-types
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file homotopy.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 8.6.1 at source lines 1569-1572: for an n-connected f and a family P of k-types with k >= n, the precomposition map (blank o f) is (k-n-2)-truncated, proved at source lines 1574-1590. The proof inducts on k - n with the fixed-level induction principle as base case (source line 1576) and then has to make the level drop by exactly one. That requires computing the fibre of (blank o f) at a section l as Sm{g : Prd{b:B}P(b)} Prd{a:A} g(f(a)) = l(a) (line 1580), computing the identity type of two such pairs as Sm{r : g ~ h} (r o f = p . q^-1) (lines 1582-1584), and then recognising that last type as the fibre of the same precomposition map for the family Q(b) := (g(b) = h(b)) (lines 1585-1587). items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.4.9 at source lines 693-703: for a functor F between precategories, being an isomorphism of precategories, admitting G with eta, eps satisfying the labelled triangle equation (9.4.10), and merely admitting such data, are equivalent. The 90-line proof is a three-way equivalence whose real content is (i)<->(ii): the first reduction turns the equation between equalities of functors into the object-level triangle identity (lines 708-714), the action of the inverse functor on hom-sets must then be manufactured by conjugating with idtoiso of the object-level isomorphism and inverting the fully faithful F (lines 718-723), and the two functor identities 1_A = GF and FG = 1_B require a multline computation with functoriality, preservation of idtoiso and the triangle identity (lines 725-750). The reverse direction rebuilds full faithfulness through a second comparison map G-bar (lines 752-777), and the two round trips are not symmetric: the object parts are recovered in one direction while the other needs the equivalence of the two triangle identities (lines 779-795). The statement records none of the transport bookkeeping along eta_0 and eps_0 that the proof depends on.

The proof is a single application of the (R_C,close)-recursion principle, but every obligation of that principle is discharged by hand: the extension is defined on both constructors (lines 1085-1095), the limit clause is legitimate only after showing that lam eps. f-bar(x_{eps/L}) is again a Cauchy approximation (lines 1097-1100), separatedness is checked against arbitrary pairs rather than against f-bar (line 1102), and each of the four constructor conditions converts a close_{eps-delta} hypothesis into the L-scaled close_{L eps - L delta} one before applying the matching constructor (lines 1106-1116). items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.1.13 at source lines 537-540: if A is a mere proposition then its suspension is a set and A is equivalent to the path space north = south. The 71-line proof is an encode-decode argument that has to be built from scratch: it defines a family P on susp(A) x susp(A) with values unit and A (lines 543-554), checks that this definition survives the meridian, which is where an inhabitant of A is used to make A equivalent to unit and univalence turns the equivalence into the needed identity (lines 555-569), and checks mere-propositionality of every P(x,y) by double induction (lines 569-571). Sethood is then obtained from the author's criterion for reflexive mere relations, so the rest of the proof is the construction of tau : prd{x,y} P(x,y) -> (x = y) by double induction together with the two transport conditions along the meridian, the first of which needs function extensionality and the computation refl . merid(a) = merid(a) (lines 576-608). The statement records neither P nor the transport conditions.

items.difficulty_reason: The statement identifies two objects that are built by completely different means: isomorphism classes of H-torsors on a site and the first cohomology group H^1(C, H) of an abelian sheaf (statement lines 292-295). The proof has to construct both directions explicitly. The first construction is a pushout followed by a boundary operator: it forms the free abelian sheaf on the torsor, its augmentation sigma, the map a from Ker(sigma) to H determined by the torsor action through h.s' = s, pushes the sequence defining Z[F] out along a, and takes the image of 1 under the connecting homomorphism (proof lines 299-333). The second is a representability argument that needs an injective embedding, the vanishing of H^1 of an injective sheaf, and the identification of the preimage of a global section of Q = I/H as a torsor (proof lines 336-356). What the author does not do is verify that the two constructions are mutually inverse; that verification is declared omitted at proof lines 358-360 and is retained verbatim in the delivered item, so the bijection itself is asserted by the author and not carried out in the printed argument.

items.title: Existence of the universal first order thickening of a formally unramified morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The statement asserts that a formally unramified morphism h : Z to X admits a first order thickening Z in Z' that is universal for all diagrams T in T' over X (statement lines 1026-1028), an object defined by a lifting property rather than constructed by a formula. The proof is a construction with a chain of genuinely separate steps: it first derives uniqueness and the localisation of the universal property for open subschemes from the definition (proof lines 1040-1061), then upgrades the algebra lemma from affine test diagrams to arbitrary ones by an affine open covering of T' and a glueing with uniqueness (proof lines 1063-1081), then produces the global Z' by glueing affine pieces along open subschemes that are identified as universal thickenings of the intersections, which is what yields the cocycle condition (proof lines 1083-1101). The final and least formal step is the descent of the universal property itself: local universality on a cover of Z has to be converted into the lifting property for an arbitrary diagram, which is done by covering T' so that each a(T_i) lands in some Z_i and then comparing two solutions through the universal thickening of Z_i cap Z_j (proof lines 1108-1126). Formal unramifiedness is consumed at exactly one point, proof line 1086.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that after an arbitrary affine base change S' -> S every member of a complete devissage family (Z_k, Y_k, i_k, pi_k, G_k, alpha_k)_{k=1..n} has a primed counterpart that is again a complete devissage of the pulled-back pair F'/X'/S' (statement lines 1272-1284). The reduction to the one step case is immediate, but the two remaining conditions have to be checked through the pushforward: the cokernel of alpha_k must commute with base change, which is not formal because Coker is formed after the finite morphism pi_k, and condition (2) must be preserved through the residue-field extension kappa(xi_k) -> kappa(xi'_k) at the generic points of the fibres (proof lines 1295-1309). Both steps are short and consist of identifying a fibre of a pullback with a scalar extension, which is why the claim is H2.

items.title: The law of Arratia's random integer J_x^*: P[J_x^* = j] = (1/(j log x))(1 + O(1/log x))
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia’s coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.317
items.difficulty_reason: The claim pins down the exact law of Arratia's random integer J_x^* = prod_{i=1}^K Q_i^*, built from the transformed Poisson process R^*, up to relative error O(1/log x). The proof does not estimate P[J_x^* = j] by inclusion-exclusion: it first identifies the law of the partial product I_t^* from the Dirichlet series prod_q exp((Lambda(q)/(q^{1+t} log q))(q^{-s} - 1)) = zeta(1+t+s)/zeta(1+t), which forces P[I_t^* = i] = i^{-1-t}/zeta(1+t) (source 774-778), and then writes the indicator of {J_x^* = j} as a sum over Poisson points with Q^* > x/j and evaluates it with the Mecke equation (778-787). The remaining step is a genuine asymptotic in t: Mertens plus partial summation give sum_{q>x/j} Lambda(q)/q^{1+t} = (x/j)^{-t}(1+O(t))/t, and the split at t = 1 using 1/zeta(1+t) = t + O(t^2) produces the main term 1/(j log x) (788-800).

primary.label: Lemma lem:probaj (Arratia): law of the random integer J_x^* built from the transformed Poisson process

proof_spans.label: complete author proof: Poisson prime-power counts, Dirichlet-series inversion, Mecke expansion, Mertens partial summation and the zeta expansion at t = 0

items.title: Kac chaos with explicit k/sqrt(N) and k/N total-variation rates for the canonical tensor product
items.author: Pietro Caputo and Daniel Parisi
items.work: Nonlinear recombinations and generalized random transpositions
items.source_version: Official published version, Annales Henri Lebesgue 7 (2024), 10.5802/ahl.219
items.difficulty_reason: The claim carries two different total-variation rates for the same object - Ck/sqrt(N) for an arbitrary admissible sequence and Ck/N for the canonical sequence rho^pi_N - so the proof cannot stop at an asymptotic local CLT. It inverts the Fourier transform of the measure conditioned on Omega_{rho_N} and works with the quotient (eq:chao5) of two such integrals, using the exponential bound |psi_N(s)| <= exp(-a<s,s>/N) from the irreducibility lemma to dominate the denominator and the far region (source 626-642), and then needs the exact second moment k^2<V_1^{-1/2}s, pi-rho_N>^2 + k<s,s> together with the assumption <pi-rho_N, pi-rho_N> = O(1/N) to reach Ck/sqrt(N) (643-656). The sharper k/N display is not a rescaling of the first: it subtracts the linear approximation g = (1/k)<V_1^{-1}v, S_k> so that the first-order term vanishes identically (662-668), uses the O(1/N^2) accuracy of the canonical sequence twice (line 658 and (eq:chaoap1)), and still has to prove a fourth-moment bound of order k^2 (702-716).

primary.label: Theorem th:eqens: total-variation rate Ck/sqrt(N) for any admissible sequence and Ck/N for the canonical sequence

proof_spans.label: complete author proof: conditioned-measure Fourier quotient, exponential characteristic-function bound, covariance estimate, and the linear-approximation subtraction giving the k/N rate

items.title: Quantitative multivariate local central limit theorem for irreducible measures on the discrete cube
items.author: Pietro Caputo and Daniel Parisi
items.work: Nonlinear recombinations and generalized random transpositions
items.source_version: Official published version, Annales Henri Lebesgue 7 (2024), 10.5802/ahl.219
items.difficulty_reason: The claim is a lattice local CLT for mu^{otimes N} on {0,...,N}^K with error C/N^{(K+1)/2} that is uniform over the maximum in M_N, so the proof must compare an exact point mass with a Gaussian density rather than a distribution function. The complete proof at 2289-2325 splits the Fourier difference into three pieces - the Gaussian comparison on A_N = {|s| <= 1/(4L_N)}, the far region Q_{N,K} minus A_N killed by the exponential characteristic-function bound |psi(t)| <= exp(-c<t,t>) coming from irreducibility, and the Gaussian tail on the complement of A_N - each shown to be O(1/sqrt(N)) before the prefactor B_N^{-1} = N^{-K/2}(det V_1)^{-1/2}. The first piece is not free: it needs the uniform comparison |phi_N(t) - exp(-<t,t>/2)| <= 16 L_N|t|^3 exp(-<t,t>/3) for |t| <= 1/(4L_N), whose proof at 2213-2286 is a two-regime argument that restarts at |t| < (1/2)L_N^{-1/3} because the cubic Taylor remainder is not small there.

items.title: A maximal coupling of two laws on the positive integers: Y = f(X;U,U') with P[X != Y] = d_TV(mu,nu) and Y of law nu
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia’s coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.317
items.difficulty_reason: The claim is the existence of a coupling of two laws mu, nu on the positive integers with P[X != Y] exactly equal to d_TV(mu,nu) and with Y a function of X and two independent uniforms, so the proof must construct the coupling rather than invoke a metric. It defines the normalised partial sums z_j from the negative parts and a two-branch map f_{mu,nu}(m;a,b) on N x (0,1)^2 (source 1747-1753), and the decisive step is the equivalence f_{mu,nu}(m;a,b) != m <=> a*mu(m) > nu(m) (1755-1760), which reduces the change event to {U*mu(X) > nu(X)}. Both conclusions are then computed exactly rather than estimated: P[X != Y] = sum_m (mu(m)-nu(m))^+ through the counting-measure identity proved at 1723-1737, and P[Y = n] = nu(n) by splitting on the two disjoint events producing Y = n and using sum_m (mu(m)-nu(m))^- = d_TV(mu,nu) (1785-1791).

primary.label: Lemma lem:coupling-dtv (Arratia): existence of a coupling with P[X != Y] = d_TV(mu,nu) and Y of law nu

items.title: Wasserstein rate for finite irreducible aperiodic Markov chains from an arbitrary initial law
items.author: R. Srikant
items.work: Rates of Convergence in the Central Limit Theorem for Markov Chains, with an Application to TD Learning
items.difficulty_reason: The claim removes both stationarity and periodicity from the finite-state Markov-chain CLT and allows an arbitrary initial law, so the stationary asymptotic covariance cannot be reused as it stands. With V_k = sum_{j=k}^n E(Sigma_j) and D_k = V_k^(-1/2)E(Sigma_k)V_k^(-1/2), the proof must rebuild the two-sided sandwich c(n-k+1)I <= V_k <= C(n-k+1)I from geometric ergodicity alone (source 1186-1204), read off Tr(D_k) <= C/(n-k+1) (1217-1224) and thereby keep the two Taylor remainders of the retained martingale theorem at C(1-beta)^(-2)n^(-beta/2) (1225-1230). The non-routine step is the covariance-interaction term at 1232-1357: the bounded solution Phi of Phi - PPhi = Sigma_infinity - v must be centred by E[Phi(X_k)], which is now k-dependent, giving E(Sigma_k) - Sigma_k = Phi_(k-1)~ - Phi_k~ + Gamma_k (1276-1287), and summation by parts then needs ||H_k - H_(k-1)||, which is re-derived from the covariance increments V_(k-1) - V_k = E(Sigma_(k-1)) and V_k - V_(k+1) = E(Sigma_k) rather than from stationarity (1333-1351). This is not a formal substitution into the stationary theorem, and the paper's own general state-space extension later reuses exactly this nonstationary argument (1441-1443).

primary.label: Corollary cor: MC CLT nonstationary: finite-state irreducible aperiodic chain from an arbitrary initial law, with the beta-uniform bound and the O((log n)^2/sqrt n) rate

items.title: The hierarchy of n-types is cumulative: an n-type is also an (n+1)-type
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file hlevels.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.1.7 at source lines 113-116: if X is an n-type and n >= -2 then X is also an (n+1)-type. The proof (source lines 118-133) is short but its base case is a nontrivial computation: one must show that the path space of a contractible type is contractible, which means producing the centre contr_x `ct` opp(contr_y) for arbitrary endpoints x, y (source line 124) and then proving at lines 126-128 that any p : x = y equals it, a step that only closes after path induction, where it becomes the triviality refl x = contr_x `ct` opp(contr_x). The induction step at lines 130-132 is then a single application of the hypothesis, so the whole weight of the theorem is in the boundary case n = -2 that the retained context flags.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of Theorem 7.1.7, retained line for line

contexts.label: the author's remark that the previous theorem fails at n = -2, which is the boundary the cumulativity statement has to start from

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.1.9 at source lines 171-174: if every B(a) is an n-type then prd x:A B(x) is an n-type, for arbitrary A. The proof (source lines 176-185) is an induction whose step is not a direct application of the hypothesis: to show that f = g is an n-type one must first pass from the identity type of two dependent functions to the product prd a:A (f(a) = g(a)), which uses function extensionality (source line 183), and then apply closure under equivalence before the inductive hypothesis can be used on the pointwise path spaces (line 184). The base case at line 178 is a separate input, and the statement itself says nothing about how the path space of a function type is to be rewritten.

items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.1.4 at source lines 68-73: if p : X -> Y is a retraction and X is an n-type then Y is an n-type. The author's proof (source lines 75-92) is an induction on n in which the step is a genuine construction: after fixing y, y' : Y one must exhibit the path space y = y' as a retract of s(y) = s(y') (source line 83), and this requires writing down both the section ap s and the retraction t(q) := opp(epsilon_y) `ct` ap p q `ct` epsilon_{y'} (source lines 85-87). The retraction identity is not definitional and is discharged at source line 91 by the naturality of the homotopy epsilon : p o s ~ 1, which is exactly the point where the chosen section and homotopy have to interact.

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 7.5.6 at source lines 1133-1136: if f : A -> B is n-connected then g : B -> C is n-connected if and only if g o f is. The author's proof (source lines 1138-1151) is a three-step chain of equivalences of truncations at a fixed c : C in which each step is a different input: the octahedron identity identifies the fiber of the composite with a total space of fibers (source lines 1141-1143), truncation inside a dependent sum moves the inner truncation inward (lines 1144-1145), and the hypothesis that f is n-connected contracts the inner truncated fibers (lines 1146-1147). items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.2.9 at source lines 423-426: A is an n-type if and only if Omega^{n+1}(A,a) is contractible for all a. The proof (source lines 427-445) is an induction whose inductive step is not formal: after reformulating with the loop-space criterion (line 431) and applying the hypothesis (line 432), the goal mentions Omega^{n+1}(Omega(A,a),refl a) while the available contractibility is at Omega^{n+1}(Omega(A,a),p), so one has to construct an explicit equivalence g between the two loop spaces at different basepoints (lines 435-437), define it by whiskering a path q : p = p with the concatenation composite refl a = p `ct` opp p = p `ct` opp p = refl a (lines 438-440), prove it is an equivalence as a composite of two named equivalences (lines 441-443), and check that it carries refl p to refl(refl a) (line 444). The statement says nothing about this basepoint comparison.

items.title: Higher functoriality of truncation: a homotopy induces a homotopy with a specified coherence square
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file hlevels.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 7.3.5 at source lines 569-578: a homotopy h : f ~ g induces a homotopy trunc n h : trunc n f ~ trunc n g whose composite with the naturality paths is required to equal ap(|.|_n)(h(a)) up to a specified square. The statement is a coherence requirement, and the proof (source lines 579-583) has to manufacture it: the naive candidate is only a homotopy between the two composites after composing with the naturality paths (source line 581), so one must first turn it into an equality by function extensionality, then use that precomposition with |.|_n is an equivalence (source line 582) to lift that equality to a path between the functors, and finally appeal to the coherence laws for function extensionality to obtain a homotopy with exactly the required composite. Nothing of this is visible from the statement, whose content is only the square.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:chow.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the multiplicity of a 2-periodic complex of finite-length modules as the alternating sum of the lengths of M and N, and deduces the vanishing of e_R for (2,1)-periodic complexes (statement lines 259-264). The proof does not compute the two remaining cases directly but instead observes that length_R(M) - length_R(N) is additive on the category of complexes with finite-length M and N, then splits off the displayed short exact sequence 0 -> (M, Im(phi), phi, 0) -> (M, N, phi, psi) -> (0, N/Im(phi), 0, 0) -> 0, which isolates exactly the cases where the assertion is immediate (proof lines 271-278). The author leaves those two cases to the reader and this is reproduced as written. The organisation of the reduction, not its execution, is the content, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Geometric connectedness is equivalent to connectedness of the base change to a separable algebraic closure
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma replaces the a priori testing field for geometric connectedness by a single one: for a scheme X over a field k and a separable algebraic closure kbar, X is geometrically connected exactly when X_{kbar} is connected (statement lines 793-797). The forward direction is built into the definition, so the work is the converse, where an arbitrary test extension k' has to be compared with kbar: a further extension kbar' of kbar containing k' is produced, the separably closed-field criterion gives connectedness of X_{kbar'}, and connectedness is then pushed down to X_{k'} because X_{kbar'} -> X_{k'} is surjective (proof lines 803-807). The claim is H2: one comparison field, one surjectivity, and a single cited criterion.

items.title: Gluing ring maps given at finitely many maximal ideals whose kernels and cokernels are killed locally
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:chow.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma reconstructs a single ring map phi : A -> B from finitely many local ring maps phi_i : A_{m_i} -> B_i at pairwise distinct maximal ideals, with the requirement that the kernel and cokernel of phi are killed by a power of the intersection m_1 cap ... cap m_r, and it asks that finiteness, injectivity or surjectivity of all phi_i pass to phi (statement lines 527-540). The non-formal step is the reduction: the product A' = prod A_i satisfies IA' = prod m_i A_i and A -> A' is flat with A/I isomorphic to A'/IA', which is exactly what allows more-algebra-lemma-application-formal-glueing to be invoked and then more-algebra-remark-formal-glueing-algebras to put an A-algebra structure on the glued module (proof lines 546-555). items.title: Every cohomology class on a ringed site is killed on a covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a sheaf F of O-modules on a ringed site, an object U, an integer n > 0 and a cohomology class xi in H^n(U, F), some covering {U_i -> U} of the site restricts xi to zero on every U_i (statement lines 716-721). The point that cannot be done by pure formalism is the passage from the class to a representative and from the representative to local primitives: the injective resolution must be used in two ways at once, first to present H^n(U, F) as a quotient of sections of I^n(U) and then, using exactness of the resolution in degree n, to know that the image sheaf of the differential equals the kernel sheaf, which is exactly what produces a covering over which the representative is a coboundary (proof lines 725-741). The class is then killed because restriction of a cohomology class is represented by the restricted section. The claim is H2: short, no citation, but with a genuine two-step use of the resolution.

items.title: A finite type module over an affine finite type scheme is pushed forward from its support by a finitely presented closed immersion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the algebraised existence statement behind the chapter's key technical lemma: given a finite type morphism of affine schemes with a finite type module F, it produces a finitely presented closed immersion i : Z -> X together with a finite type module G on Z whose pushforward is F and whose fibre Z_s is exactly Supp(F_s) (statement lines 451-454). The substance is the conversion of the fibre support, which is a priori only a closed subset of the fibre, into a finitely generated ideal inside the annihilator of M: finite generation of B tensor_A kappa(p) over kappa(p) is what supplies finitely many f_1, ..., f_m whose span already computes the support on the fibre, and only then can Z be defined by a finitely presented closed immersion (proof lines 476-488). The remaining steps are direct translations between modules and their associated sheaves, so the claim is H2. Note that the pinned author text writes the generating tuple once as (f_1, ..., f_m) and once as (f_1, ..., f_n); this is reproduced verbatim and not corrected.

items.title: Existence of a complete devissage at a point, by induction on the dimension of the fibre support
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition produces, for X locally of finite type over S and a point x over s, a pointed elementary etale neighbourhood diagram such that the pullback of F over X'/S' has a complete devissage at x, and the proof is an induction on d = dim_x Supp(F_s) whose step is a genuine construction rather than a citation (statement lines 1433-1443; proof lines 1447-1464). The dimension descent is driven by the free cover alpha_1 : O_{Y_1}^{\oplus r_1} -> pi_{1,*}G_1, whose cokernel on the fibre has support of strictly smaller dimension at y_1, so the induction hypothesis can be invoked either on Y_1 (non-vanishing stalk) or, after a shrinking that kills the cokernel, to give the length-zero case (proof lines 1466-1485). The part that cannot be done routinely is the final gluing: the one step devissage of F and the complete devissage of the cokernel produced over different elementary etale neighbourhoods S' and S'' have to be made to live over a single base, which is done by a two-stage shrinking in which X'_1 is first pushed inside Y_1 and then the one step devissage is shrunk so that Y''_1 = X'_1 x_S S'' with S'' contained in S' (proof lines 1548-1569); the author explicitly invites the reader to carry out this step independently rather than read it. This combination of a dimension-descending induction with a nested shrinking of two devissages is the independent technical content of the chapter's existence theorem.

items.title: The Calabi invariant of a Hamiltonian isotopy is twice the total Hamiltonian, under the normalisation
items.author: Alberto Abbondandolo; Christian Lange; Marco Mazzucchelli
items.work: Higher systolic inequalities for 3-dimensional contact manifolds
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.195
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:Calabi` at source lines 485-491: for a Hamiltonian isotopy generated by a normalised H_t, the integral of the action one-form a_{phi,nu} against omega equals twice the double integral of H_t over the surface. The author's proof (source lines 493-511) is an explicit computation in which three separate ingredients are consumed one after another: the identity a_{phi,nu} = a_{H,nu} and the invariance of omega to move the surface integral inside the time integral (lines 494-498), the rewriting of (X_t interior nu) omega as nu wedge dH_t (line 499), and Stokes theorem applied to H_t dnu - d(H_t nu) to produce the factor two together with a boundary term (lines 502-505). The last step is where the hypothesis enters, since the boundary term vanishes precisely because the Hamiltonian is normalised, and it is evaluated component by component on the boundary components (lines 506-508).

items.title: Normalised almost-Besse contact forms: boundary behaviour and C1-closeness of the Reeb field
items.author: Alberto Abbondandolo; Christian Lange; Marco Mazzucchelli
items.work: Higher systolic inequalities for 3-dimensional contact manifolds

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:nearly_Besse_normalized` at source lines 1289-1310, a four-part statement about the normalisation of an almost-Besse contact form: the pull-back of nu to the boundary agrees with nu_0, the two-form omega vanishes there, the normalised Reeb field extends smoothly and tangentially to the boundary, and it is C1-close to d/dt whenever the original Reeb field is C2-close to R_{lambda_0}. The author's proof (source lines 1198-1202) is an induction in which the two structural facts about the core and about insertions have to be combined correctly: the induction step removes one short chord (i_1,i_1+1), which requires knowing that an unstable matching contains a short chord, and then uses that removing a chord leaves the core unchanged so that the smaller matching has exactly k-1 unstable chords (line 1201). Only then can the induction hypothesis be applied to that smaller matching and the insertion prepended. The statement is a single sentence about a product of insertions and gives no hint that the core has to be tracked through the deletion.

items.author: Marmor, Avichai
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `prop:hook schur positive` at source lines 1334-1341: a set A has a hook-shaped non-negative Schur expansion if and only if the number |A(D = J)| depends only on |J|, with c_k the count on [k]. The author's proof (source lines 1343-1352) has two directions of different character. The forward direction is a bijective computation: it uses that a hook tableau of shape (N-k,1^k) has exactly k descents and that each k-subset arises from exactly one hook tableau (line 1344), which turns the uniform hypothesis into the displayed generating-function identity (lines 1345-1348) before the Schur-positivity criterion is applied (line 1349). The converse is not a computation at all: it rests on the uniqueness of the descent-set distribution of a generating function, cited from Adin and Roichman at line 1351. The statement is a two-way equivalence whose two halves are proved by completely different means.

items.author: Marmor, Avichai

The statement gives only the cardinality-free uniqueness clause.

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 8.8.1 at source lines 2378-2385: if trunc 0 f is surjective and ap f is an equivalence on all path spaces, then f is an equivalence. The author's proof (source lines 2386-2394) is short but it is a genuine exercise in truncation bookkeeping rather than a citation: the second hypothesis is first recognised as the statement that f is an embedding (line 2387), which lets the goal be reduced to surjectivity through the retained characterisation of equivalences (line 2388), and surjectivity is then produced in two stages. In each stage the point is that the goal is a mere proposition, so the merely existing data supplied by the first hypothesis may be assumed purely (lines 2389-2392); only after that does the inhabitation of the fiber follow (line 2393). Neither the reduction nor the two truncation strips are visible from the statement.

items.title: A uniform Beta integral estimate with a logarithmic-delta corollary
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia’s coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.317
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:beta estimate` at source lines 1460-1469: a uniform two-sided bound for sin(pi alpha) times the Beta-type integral over [u-delta,u+delta], together with the log-form corollary when delta >= 1/log x. The author's proof (source lines 1471-1496) is a full case analysis rather than an appeal to a standard Beta estimate: it starts with a symmetry reduction (line 1471), normalises the total mass to pi and thereby removes the case delta > 1/4 (lines 1472-1475), reduces the remaining claim to a pure power integral after bounding 1-t below (lines 1477-1481), and then splits into delta <= u/2, where t is bounded below by u/2 (lines 1483-1487), and delta >= u/2, where the integral is extended to [0,3delta] and evaluated to produce delta^alpha (lines 1489-1495). The exponent bookkeeping in the second case, including the comparison delta^alpha ~ delta/(u+delta)^{1-alpha}, is the step that the statement hides.

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:decomposition J neq J*` at source lines 842-848: if the three events E_1, E_2, E_3 hold then J_x = J_x^*, and consequently the probability that J_x differs from J_x^* is bounded by the sum of the three failure probabilities. The author's proof (source lines 850-882) is a two-stage argument in which the events are used for different purposes: E_1 alone gives the pinching inequalities J_x < x < J_x e^{h(Y_0)} through two separate estimates of log J_x from above and below (lines 852-864), while E_2 and E_3 are converted into the ordering inequalities for the index sets B_+ and B_- (lines 867-876) which are then used to identify the products indexed by the ordered process R^* with the two products built from J_x (lines 877-881). items.title: Colouring a Poisson--Dirichlet process recovers the Dirichlet distribution: a probabilistic proof
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia’s coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.317
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `prop:probabilistic dirichlet law` at source lines 1121-1128: colouring the points of a Poisson--Dirichlet process independently with probabilities alpha_j yields a random vector distributed according to Dir(alpha). The author's proof (source lines 1130-1148), repeated from Donnelly and Tavare because the Poisson representation is needed later, is a two-tool computation: the colouring theorem turns the single Poisson process into k independent processes of intensities alpha_m e^{-x}/x dx (lines 1131-1138), and Campbell's theorem evaluates the Laplace transform of each coloured sum, producing the integral of (e^{sx}-1)e^{-x}/x whose value -alpha_m log(1-s) identifies a Gamma(alpha_m,1) law (lines 1139-1143). The Dirichlet conclusion then follows by normalising the independent Gamma sums (lines 1144-1147). Both cited theorems are structural, and neither the colouring representation nor the generating-function computation is visible from the statement.

items.title: Two partial-summation bounds for the divisor function alpha^{omega(n)}
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia’s coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.317
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `prel:partial summation bounds` at source lines 1678-1685: two uniform bounds, sum over n <= x of alpha^{omega(n)} << x (log x)^{alpha-1} and sum over x/y < n <= xy of alpha^{omega(n)}/n << (log y)(log(xy))^{alpha-1}, for alpha in [0,1] and x, y >= 2. The author's proof (source lines 1687-1700) splits into two genuinely different regimes: when y >= sqrt(x) the second sum is enlarged to a sum over numbers with all prime factors at most y^3, factored as an Euler product and bounded with 1+t <= e^t along with the strong Mertens estimate (lines 1689-1693); when y <= sqrt(x) the interval is decomposed into dyadic blocks and each block is controlled by the first bound of the proposition, with the count of blocks producing the factor log y (lines 1695-1699). The statement is two inequalities and records neither the Euler product nor the dyadic splitting.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:chow.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the effect of multiplying one of the two structure maps of a (2,1)-periodic complex by an element x whose support condition dim Supp(M/xM) <= 0 forces x to behave like a parameter: e_R(M, x phi, psi) = e_R(M, phi, psi) - e_R(Im(phi), 0, x), and symmetrically for x psi (statement lines 465-475). The author proves only the first of the two formulas and says the second is proved in exactly the same manner; this is reproduced as written. The claim is H2.

items.title: A Cech complex over a covering containing the whole space is homotopy equivalent to zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if an open covering of a topological space contains the whole space as one of its members, then the extended Cech complex with F(U) placed in degree -1 is homotopy equivalent to zero (statement lines 950-959). The proof produces the contracting homotopy explicitly, by prefixing every tuple of indices with the distinguished index i and reading the resulting map as a projection onto the factors F(U_{i i_1 ...}) = F(U_{i_1 ...}); the verification is then a displayed cancellation of two sums of sections with opposite signs (proof lines 963-1003). The step that has to be seen rather than cited is that prefixing with the repeated index changes nothing on the intersections, so that the homotopy is well defined at all. The claim is H2: one explicit homotopy and one computation.

items.title: An open subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme is scheme theoretically dense if and only if it contains all embedded points, if and only if it contains all associated points
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states a three-way equivalence for an open subscheme U of a locally Noetherian X: scheme theoretic density, density plus containment of all embedded points, and containment of all associated points (statement lines 443-449). The work is a reduction plus an algebraic re-reading: the author first passes to X = Spec(A) with A Noetherian, uses quasi-compactness of U to write it as D(f_1) union ... union D(f_n), and then replaces the geometric conditions by statements about the single ring map A -> A_{f_1} x ... x A_{f_n} and about the associated primes of A (proof lines 453-462). The two non-obvious steps are reading density as containment of the minimal primes and invoking that the associated primes are exactly the minimal primes together with the embedded ones (proof lines 471-476), and closing the cycle by the injectivity of A into the product of its localisations at the associated primes (proof lines 479-484). This is H2: standard localisation machinery, but four separate implications, each needing its own translation rather than a citation.

items.title: A point outside the image of a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism is not weakly associated to the pushforward
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The claim is that if f : X -> S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and s is not in the image of f, then s is not weakly associated to f_* F (statement lines 721-724). The proof has two steps that are not routine. First a flat base change to Spec(O_{S,s}) reduces the problem to a local base (A, m) with s the closed point, using that base change by a morphism that is an isomorphism on the local ring at s does not change the stalk (proof lines 728-740). Second, the hypothesis that s is outside the image is converted into the open covering X = union over a in m of f^{-1}D(a), from which quasi-compactness extracts finitely many a_1, ..., a_n in the maximal ideal with M -> M_{a_1} + ... + M_{a_n} injective (proof lines 741-748). That injectivity is precisely what rules out an element of the stalk annihilated by a power of every a_i, i.e. what rules out weak associatedness (proof lines 748-753). This is H2: the covering indexed by the maximal ideal and its finite refinement are the non-formal content, but no Noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is needed and each step is short.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises formal unramifiedness of a morphism f : X -> S by the vanishing of its sheaf of differentials (statement lines 899-900). Both directions are organised around one construction: the first order neighbourhood X' of the diagonal inside X x_S X, cut out by the square of the ideal J of the diagonal, which is a square-zero thickening with Omega_{X/S} = J/J^2 generated by the local sections p_1^#(f) - p_2^#(f) (proof lines 904-922). The claim is H2: one construction and two short arguments, no citations beyond the recalled set-up.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a morphism of algebraic spaces f : X -> Y over a scheme S the sheaf of differentials Omega_{X/Y} is a quasi-coherent O_X-module (statement lines 1018-1019). The proof is a reduction to the scheme case along a presentation: the localisation lemma supplies a diagram with surjective maps from schemes U and V, the restriction of Omega_{X/Y} to U is identified with Omega_{U/V}, which is quasi-coherent by the scheme-theoretic statement, and quasi-coherence on X follows from the criterion phrased in terms of a presentation (proof lines 1023-1031). The two steps that carry the content are the identification on the presented piece and the appeal to the presentation criterion. The claim is H2: no construction beyond the diagram, three cited inputs.

items.title: Geometric reducedness at a point may be checked after an arbitrary field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that geometric reducedness of X over k at a point x is equivalent to geometric reducedness of the base change X_{k'} at every point x' over x, for an arbitrary field extension k'/k, and deduces the global statement (statement lines 492-502). The forward direction is by definition; the converse cannot be done by a single base change, because the definition tests all field extensions, so the proof replaces that by the finite purely inseparable ones and compares each of them with k' over a common extension k''', where the resulting local ring map is flat and local, hence faithfully flat, allowing reducedness to descend (proof lines 509-519). The two reduction devices, the finite inseparable criterion and faithful flatness descent, are the content. The claim is H2.

items.title: A nonzerodivisor in a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring is only boundedly divisible by a parameter in finite extensions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:chow.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring with nonzerodivisors a, b and a in the maximal ideal, the exponent m such that b = a^m c can be realised inside a finite ring extension is bounded independently of the extension (statement lines 606-609). The proof produces the bound by leaving the ring: a discrete valuation ring A dominating a minimal quotient R/q records v(a) > 0, and the bound n = v(b)/v(a) is then shown to hold for every finite extension R contained in R' by propagating the picture along A tensor_R R', cutting down by a prime over (0) and comparing valuations in a further discrete valuation ring A''' dominating a localisation, where the relation b = a^m c forces v'''(b) >= m v'''(a) and v''' = e v (proof lines 613-638). The non-formal content is this chain of base changes preserving the divisibility relation while keeping control of the ramification. The claim is H2.

items.title: Restriction of an injective module on a ringed space to a smaller open is surjective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma, whose slogan is that injectives are flasque, says that for open subspaces U' contained in U of a ringed space and an injective O_X-module I, the restriction map I(U) -> I(U') is surjective (statement lines 716-723). The proof is a three-step translation of the section functor into a representable functor: extension by zero of the structure sheaf represents F -> F(U) and F -> F(U'), Yoneda turns the canonical map between the two representing sheaves into the restriction map, injectivity of that canonical map is read off on stalks, and then the injectivity criterion for injective objects converts the monomorphism into a surjection on Hom groups (proof lines 727-762). The non-formal content is exactly this change of coordinates from sections to Hom groups. The claim is H2: one coordinate change, three cited inputs.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a family U = {U_i -> U} with all fibre products existing, the resulting chain complex of abelian presheaves Z^bullet_U is exact in every degree except zero (statement lines 1628-1638). The proof is a genuine computation in two stages: first the complex is evaluated at an object V and decomposed into a direct sum indexed by the composite morphisms V -> U, which reduces everything to the complex Z[S] <- Z[S x S] <- Z[S x S x S] <- ... for one set S; then an explicit chain map K : n_{(s_0, ..., s_p)} -> n_{(s, s_0, ..., s_p)} is written down and checked to be a nullhomotopy of the alternating-sum operator (proof lines 1687-1694). The author's proof carries a typographical slip in the displayed definition of delta, where the sign is written (-1)^p instead of (-1)^i; it is reproduced verbatim and not corrected. The claim is H2: a concrete homotopy, no citations beyond the definition.

items.title: Seven equivalent characterisations of geometric reducedness in positive characteristic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives seven equivalent formulations of geometric reducedness for a scheme X over a field of positive characteristic: via arbitrary base change, via finite purely inseparable extensions, via the two distinguished extensions k^{1/p} and k^{perf}, via the algebraic closure, and via the rings of affine opens (statement lines 419-432). The proof is a cycle (1) => (2) => (7) => (1) closing three genuinely different arguments — local rings on a base change, Spec of a tensor product, and gluing of spectra — and the remaining conditions are then attached by one algebraic statement applied to the rings O_X(U) (proof lines 436-459). What a reader cannot do routinely is see that the three directions are enough, i.e. that the cycle is closed and that the purely inseparable conditions follow from the same algebra lemma. The claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma passes from a point-wise hypothesis to an open neighbourhood: for a locally Noetherian scheme X over k that is geometrically reduced at a point x, there is an open neighbourhood U of x which is geometrically reduced over k (statement lines 600-605). The proof has three separate inputs in a fixed order: local Noetherianity produces an affine open U whose ring injects into the local ring O_{X,x}, the point-wise characterisation turns the hypothesis into geometric reducedness of that local ring, and the subalgebra criterion then descends geometric reducedness to the subring R = O_X(U) (proof lines 610-619). The step that is not automatic is the middle one, since the hypothesis is about a point while the conclusion is about a neighbourhood. The claim is H2.

items.title: Isomorphism classes of finite projective modules over a ring are detected modulo an ideal in the Jacobson radical
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the uniqueness companion of the lift lemma of the same section: for finite projective modules over a ring it asserts that an R-module map whose reduction modulo an ideal I contained in the Jacobson radical is an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism, and that isomorphism classes are detected modulo I (statement lines 146-155). The proof has to build the comparison map by hand twice: first a lift psi of the inverse of the reduction of phi, using the projectivity of P' against the surjection P -> P/IP (proof lines 159-161), then a lift phi of the composite P -> P/IP -> P'/IP', using the projectivity of P (proof lines 168-170). The decisive step is that Nakayama plus surjectivity of an endomorphism of a finite module converts surjectivity modulo I into invertibility of both composites, and it is applied twice with the roles of P and P' interchanged (proof lines 162-165). Both parts of the two-part statement live inside the counted span, and the only inputs are the two cited Algebra lemmas.

items.title: A finite stably free module modulo an ideal in the Jacobson radical lifts to a finite stably free module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma lifts a finite stably free module E over R/I to a finite stably free module over R itself when I lies in the Jacobson radical (statement lines 94-97). The proof first replaces E by an explicit isomorphism E + (R/I)^n = (R/I)^m, then has to choose two R-linear lifts phi and psi of the corresponding projection and injection (proof lines 101-106), and to prove that the composite phi o psi, which is only congruent to the identity modulo I, is actually invertible: this is done by inspecting its determinant, which lies in 1 + I and is therefore a unit by the hypothesis on I (proof lines 107-109). The last step reads the kernel of the split surjection phi off as a direct summand of a finite free module, hence stably free, and checks that it reduces to E (proof lines 110-111). The non-routine ingredient is the determinant argument, which upgrades a congruence modulo I to genuine invertibility without any locality or Nakayama input; nothing beyond the two reductions is cited.

items.title: Every quasi-inverse of a function can be corrected into a half adjoint equivalence
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file equivalences.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled theorem thm:equiv-iso-adj at source lines 215-217: every quasi-inverse of a map f can be promoted to a half adjoint equivalence. The author's proof (source lines 218-242) cannot follow the most obvious route, because the second homotopy of the given quasi-inverse has to be replaced by the corrected family epsilon-prime(b) built from the inverse of epsilon at f(g(b)) and the action of f on eta at g(b) (source lines 222-227), and only then can the coherence path tau(a) be stated (source lines 228-231). Producing that path needs two separate computations: the naturality of eta rewrites eta at g(f(a)) as the action of g on the action of f on eta at a (source lines 232-234), and the naturality of epsilon moves the action of f on that composite past epsilon(f(a)) (source lines 235-240), after which the common right factor is cancelled (source line 241). The statement indicates neither that the second homotopy must be modified nor which naturality squares close the coherence.
