items.title: The type of proofs that a type is a mere proposition, and the type of proofs that it is a set, are themselves mere propositions
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file logic.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma thm:isprop-isprop at source lines 334-336: for every type A the types of proofs that A is a mere proposition and that A is a set are mere propositions. The author's proof (source lines 337-346) has to extract level information from a witness that is only available hypothetically, and it does so twice at different levels. To compare two mere-proposition witnesses it applies function extensionality and then notices that the two values f(x,y) and g(x,y) are paths in A between the same endpoints, equal only because either witness already makes A a mere proposition, hence a set by the preceding result (source lines 338-341). The second half repeats the same manoeuvre for witnesses of sethood, which are functions of four arguments landing in an identity type (source lines 342-345). The statement does not show that equality of the two witnesses is obtained by first turning one of them into a level bound for A.

items.title: A family of sets over a type that is not a set refutes the truncated axiom of choice
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma thm:no-higher-ac at source lines 779-781: there is a type X and a family Y over it, each Y(x) a set, for which the truncated choice principle (3.8.3) fails. The author's proof (source lines 782-796) manufactures the counterexample instead of quoting one, and the two facts required of X pull in opposite directions: univalence together with the characterisation of paths in Sigma types makes the loop space at the base point equivalent to the equivalences of the two-element type with itself, which is what shows X is not a set (source lines 784-785), while truncation induction on the witness that A is merely equal to the two-element type shows that every A occurring in X is a set and hence that X is a 1-type (source lines 787-788). The statement shows neither that the family has to be the path type to the base point nor that the contradiction is reached by observing that an actual section would make X a mere proposition (source lines 793-795).

items.title: A type carrying the W-type rules with a propositional computation rule is precisely a homotopy-initial W-algebra
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file induction.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled theorem at source lines 700-702, printed as Theorem 5.5.5: a type satisfies the formation, introduction, elimination and propositional computation rules for W-types exactly when it is a homotopy-initial W-algebra. The author's proof (source lines 705-740) supplies the converse of the preceding homotopy-initiality theorem and does not merely cite it. Assuming that the polynomial functor has a homotopy-initial algebra (W,s_W), the elimination rule is obtained by equipping the Sigma type of pairs (w, c) with c in the assigned family over w with a structure map and applying homotopy-initiality to get a homomorphism whose composite with the first projection must be identified with the identity homomorphism, because the type of endohomomorphisms is contractible; the diagram of that composite is printed in the retained proof (source lines 712-727). The recursor itself is then manufactured by transporting the second component of that homomorphism along the resulting identity in a family of types depending on a function (source lines 729-737), and the computation rule is verified by a calculation with the naturality of those transports (source lines 738-739). The statement indicates neither that the recursor has to be built by transport nor that contractibility of the endohomomorphism type is what makes the two homomorphisms equal.

items.title: Weak function extensionality implies the full function extensionality axiom
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file equivalences.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled theorem wfetofe at source lines 980-983: weak function extensionality implies the full function extensionality axiom. The author's proof (source lines 985-1007) is a chain of reductions in which one link has to be weakened deliberately. Function extensionality is first reduced to the statement that the canonical map from identities of functions to homotopies induces an equivalence on total spaces (source lines 986-994); since the total space on the left is a type of pairs of a section with an identity, contractible by the characterisation of paths with one free endpoint, the goal becomes contractibility of the type of pairs of a section with a pointwise homotopy (source lines 995-999); transposing that type turns it into a product of contractible types, but the transposition result is proved using function extensionality for one of its two composites, so what survives is only a retraction, and the author records explicitly that a retract of a contractible type is contractible (source lines 1000-1006). The statement announces neither the retraction step nor the fact that the auxiliary transposition theorem has to be used one-sidedly.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives the relative Mayer-Vietoris sequence 0 -> f_*F -> a_*(F|_U) plus b_*(F|_V) -> c_*(F|_{U cap V}) -> R^1 f_*F -> ... for a morphism of ringed spaces f : X -> Y and a cover of X by two open subsets, functorially in F (statement lines 805-818). The proof works on the level of an injective resolution: the absolute Mayer-Vietoris proof is reused to see that the degreewise sequence of sections over f^{-1}(W) is short exact for every open W, which yields a short exact sequence of complexes of direct images, and the identification of the cohomology sheaves with the higher direct images rests on the separate statement that restrictions of the resolution are again injective resolutions (proof lines 822-846). The functoriality assertion is carried over from the absolute statement without proof. The claim is H2: one reduction to the absolute case plus one identification of resolutions.

items.title: A geometric point of an etale neighbourhood lifts to some member of any etale covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for an etale covering {phi_i : U_i -> U} of an etale neighbourhood (U, ubar) of a geometric point sbar of S, some U_i carries a geometric point ubar_i over sbar making phi_i a morphism of etale neighbourhoods (statement lines 3306-3312). The proof converts surjectivity of the covering into nonemptyness of one fibre product, and then exploits the special shape of a scheme etale over an algebraically closed field: the fibre product is a disjoint union of finite separable extensions of k, which are all trivial because k is algebraically closed, so a section of pr_1 exists and composing it with pr_2 gives the lift (proof lines 3328-3337). The non-formal step is precisely that appeal to triviality of the field extensions, which is what makes the covering-surjectivity statement into a lifting statement for geometric points. The claim is H2.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma compares two cohomology groups computed in different abelian categories: H^1(C, F_ab) for the underlying abelian sheaf and H^1(C, F) for the O-module (statement lines 423-434). The proof reduces the statement to a comparison of extension groups and then has to build the correspondence explicitly: one direction is a pullback along the map Z -> O of abelian sheaves, while the other is genuinely two steps, tensoring an extension of Z by F_ab with O and then pushing out along the O-linear multiplication map F tensor_Z O -> F, the legality of which rests on flatness of Z (proof lines 469-504). The author explicitly leaves the verification that the two constructions are inverse to the reader, and that sentence is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: two explicit constructions, one flatness input.

items.title: Varieties with dominant rational maps are equivalent to finitely generated field extensions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem asserts an equivalence between two categories: varieties over k with dominant rational maps, and finitely generated field extensions K/k (statement lines 166-168). The proof has to do two different jobs, and the difficulty is in seeing that they suffice: full faithfulness comes from reading a dominant rational map as the induced map of function fields k(Y) -> k(X) at the generic points and inverting it with the cited lemma on rational maps of finite presentation, while the essential image needs the separate observation that a finitely generated extension is the fraction field of a finite type k-algebra A, so that Spec(A) is a variety having K as its function field (proof lines 172-192). Neither direction is a computation; both are structural, which is why the claim is H2 and not lower.

items.title: Locality of cohomology: a cohomology class on a site dies on a covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for any site C, abelian sheaf F, object U, degree p > 0 and class xi in H^p(U, F) there is a covering of U over which xi restricts to zero (statement lines 2256-2260). The proof has to move once from the class to a representative and once from the representative to local primitives, and the second move is available precisely because p > 0 makes the resolution exact at I^p, so a section of the kernel sheaf becomes a coboundary after restriction to a covering (proof lines 2264-2271). The statement is then immediate from the fact that the restriction of a class is computed from the restriction of its representative. The claim is H2: the same two-step use of an injective resolution as in the ringed-site version, with its own self-contained proof in this chapter.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that tensoring the integral Cech chain complex of a family over a category with an arbitrary presheaf of rings yields a complex that is still exact in positive degrees, a statement whose slogan is that the integral Cech complex is a flat resolution of the constant presheaf of integers (statement lines 1151-1169). The proof is short because it reuses the structure of the integral complex: at each object the complex splits as a direct sum of complexes homotopic to Z in degree zero, and tensoring preserves that shape, the homotopy being preserved by an additive functor (proof lines 1173-1180). The author also records a second route through flatness of the terms and of H_0 (proof lines 1181-1185). The claim is H2: one reduction plus one preservation observation, with no new construction.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four consequences of the interaction of reducedness with field base change: reducedness of the product at points over a geometrically reduced point, global reducedness of a product with a reduced factor, geometric reducedness of a product of geometrically reduced factors, and reducedness of a product over a perfect field (statement lines 526-536). Each part is short but they are assembled differently: (1) and (2) reduce to an algebra lemma on tensor products, (3) is obtained by passing to the algebraic closure and applying (2) there, and (4) upgrades reducedness to geometric reducedness over a perfect field before applying (3) (proof lines 541-551). What keeps this at H2 rather than lower is that the reductions are one-way and the reader has to see which of the two chapter lemmas feeds which part. The author also left the placeholder item (5) 'Add more here.' in the statement; it is reproduced verbatim as the author's own text.

items.title: The presheaf of sections of a pullback of a quasi-coherent sheaf satisfies the fpqc sheaf condition
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that for a quasi-coherent sheaf F on S the presheaf F^a : (T -> S) -> Gamma(T, f^*F) on the category of schemes over S is an O-module satisfying the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology (statement lines 1333-1341). The work is to translate a sheaf-theoretic condition into algebra: after reducing to Zariski coverings and faithfully flat affine morphisms, the affine case is exactly the exactness of 0 -> M -> B tensor_A M -> B tensor_A B tensor_A M for a faithfully flat A -> B, which is the descent lemma for modules, and the Zariski case collapses because pullback along an open immersion has the same sections (proof lines 1350-1365). The reduction step and the identification of the Amitsur complex with the sheaf condition are what make the proposition non-immediate. The claim is H2.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a separably algebraically closed base field k and any extension k'/k, the base change X_{k'} -> X induces a bijection of connected components, so that X is geometrically connected exactly when it is connected (statement lines 772-777). Both the algebra statement and the two scheme-theoretic lemmas are quoted; what is contributed here is the assembly. The claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a scheme X locally of finite type over k with finitely many irreducible components, a single finite purely inseparable extension k'/k such that the reduction of X_{k'} is geometrically reduced over k' (statement lines 638-642). Three separate inputs are chained: the reduction lets one work with the generic points x_1, ..., x_n and their residue fields K_i; the purely inseparable base change is a homeomorphism, so the local rings of (X_{k'})_{red} at the points over the x_i are exactly the fields (K_i tensor_k k')_{red}; and one algebra lemma produces a single extension making all of them separable at once, after which the generic-point criterion closes the argument (proof lines 646-670). What is not routine is that one extension suffices for all components simultaneously. The claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is Krasner's lemma in the discretely valued case, stated for a complete local domain A of dimension one rather than for a complete field: for a polynomial P over A with a root alpha that is not a root of the derivative, every perturbation of the coefficients inside a sufficiently high power m_A^n of the maximal ideal produces a root beta of the perturbed polynomial with beta - alpha inside any prescribed m_A^c (statement lines 33749-33754). The proof is a Newton approximation that has to be run over a ring rather than a field, so the first move is to convert the dimension-one hypothesis into the statement that the maximal ideal is the radical of a principal ideal, which allows the inverse of P'(alpha) to be written as pi^{-m} a and fixes the two exponents c and n relative to each other (proof lines 33758-33762). The construction is an explicit sequence alpha_k with three simultaneous properties, whose limit is the required root; the induction step compares both summands of (P + Q)(alpha_k + delta) with their values at alpha_k through the Taylor expansion and through the congruence P'(alpha_k) equal to P'(alpha) modulo (pi^{m + 1}), yielding the explicit correction delta = -pi^{-m} a (P + Q)(alpha_k) and the verification that it lies in (pi^k) (proof lines 33782-33810). The argument consumes no cited result at all: the only inputs are the structure of a one-dimensional local domain, the Taylor expansion of a polynomial, and completeness of A.

items.title: Lowering the level of a degree p extension of discretely valued fields by a totally ramified separable base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the level-lowering step of the elimination-of-ramification argument: for discrete valuation rings A contained in B contained in C with fraction fields K contained in L contained in M, with A of mixed characteristic (0, p), A in B weakly unramified, B containing a primitive p-th root of 1 and the residue field of A equal to the intersection of the p-power residue fields of B, a degree p extension M/L of positive finite level l can be brought to level at most max(0, l - 1, 2l - p) after a finite separable base change of K that is totally ramified with respect to A, unless that base change is already a weak solution (statement lines 35166-35179). The argument is not a citation: it first converts the polynomial presenting M/L into the polynomial z^p - z modulo two explicitly computed error terms, one for the value and one for the multiplicative correction law, and chooses the exponent m so that those errors land exactly on the target level (proof lines 35190-35209). The core is an induction on the number of coefficients of xi that lie outside the residue field of A: pairs of indices related by a power of p are removed by an explicit correction of the generating element, and in the remaining case a base change of degree p^r obtained by extracting a p^r-th root of a uniformizer is performed and the computation is redone in the integral closure, so that the new level is read off from an expansion rather than from a general principle (proof lines 35282-35366). The degenerate case in which all coefficients lie in the residue field of A is closed by a contradiction with the minimality of n, using that the residue field of A is perfect, and then by an explicit degree p extension of K (proof lines 35234-35280); the level invariant, the p-power-orbit reduction and the p^r base change together are what put this beyond routine technique.

items.title: A complex is pseudo-coherent exactly when it is m-pseudo-coherent for all m, and then its finite free resolution can be chosen to vanish above the top cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes pseudo-coherence of a complex K over an arbitrary ring in three equivalent ways and appends a vanishing refinement: if the cohomology of K vanishes above b, then the quasi-isomorphism from a bounded above complex of finite free modules to K can be chosen with the same vanishing bound (statement lines 16049-16059). The direction (3) => (1) is not a citation but a construction: a bounded above complex of finite projective modules is rebuilt as one of finite free modules by the telescoping direct sum decompositions in the top degree and one degree lower, arranged so that the comparison map is even a homotopy equivalence (proof lines 16064-16076). The substantial part is (2) => (3) together with the vanishing bound, a descending induction on n in which finite free modules, their differentials and compatible maps to K are built so that the comparison map on cohomology is an isomorphism above n and surjective in degree n; the induction step passes through the cone on the partially built map, the long exact cohomology sequence, and the two cited lemmas lemma-cone-pseudo-coherent and lemma-finite-cohomology, and then needs a final correction of the module in degree n - 1 by a free summand in order to kill the cokernel there (proof lines 16086-16141). The bookkeeping of two cohomological properties plus a vanishing range at once, with the correction step at the end, is what keeps this out of the routine range; no step of the argument is replaced by a citation.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma attaches to a morphism of ringed spaces f : X -> Y, an f-map phi : f^*G -> F and coverings U of X refining f^{-1}V a commutative diagram in D^+(O_X(X)) between the Cech complexes and derived global sections, together with its consequence for cohomology groups (statement lines 2521-2552). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma exhibits a resolution of an arbitrary O_X-module F by the product-of-pushforwards complex C^p(U,F) = prod_{i_0...i_p} (j_{i_0...i_p})_* F_{i_0...i_p} attached to an open covering U : X = bigcup_{i in I} U_i, with the Cech differential of equation-d-cech (statement lines 4573-4594). items.title: The cup product gives a map of the Mayer-Vietoris distinguished triangles
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for X = U \cup V and objects K, M of D(O_X) the cup-product maps assemble into a map of distinguished triangles: the triangle of Lemma lemma-unbounded-mayer-vietoris for K \otimes^L M on the right, and the exact functor R\Gamma(X, K) \otimes_A^L - applied to the triangle for M on the left (statement lines 8328-8354). The proof cannot work with the abstract triangles alone. It first chooses a K-flat complex T^bullet of flat A-modules for R\Gamma(X, K), replaces the adjunction map T^bullet \otimes_A O_X -> K by a map into a K-flat complex K^bullet with flat terms (proof lines 8358-8379), chooses K-injective representatives I^bullet for M and J^bullet for K \otimes^L M, and only then writes the comparison maps Tot(T^bullet \otimes_A I^bullet(W)) -> J^bullet(W) for every open W (proof lines 8390-8404). The decisive step is the commutative diagram of complexes of A-modules whose columns are the Mayer-Vietoris short exact sequences, where flatness of the terms of T^bullet is exactly what makes Tot(T^bullet \otimes_A -) preserve short exactness (proof lines 8405-8424). What has to be supplied by hand is the choice of the four representatives and that diagram; the cited Mayer-Vietoris, K-flat and delta-functor results are standard prerequisites. The claim is H2.

items.title: For a big tt-category whose compacts are local, reducedness of the fibre of the comparison map over zero is equivalent to a nilpotence alternative for two composable maps of compacts with vanishing tensor product
items.author: Paul Balmer
items.work: Homological support of big objects in tensor-triangulated categories
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 7 (2020), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.135
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the theorem at source lines 881-893, label Thm:hom-local, printed as Theorem A.1: for a big tt-category whose compact-rigid subcategory is local, the assertion that the fibre of the comparison map from the homological to the triangular spectrum over zero is a single point is equivalent to a nilpotence alternative, namely that whenever two maps f and g of compacts satisfy f tensor g = 0, one of them is tensor-nilpotent on some non-zero compact. The proof at source lines 895-907 constructs the bridge between the two statements rather than observing it: in one direction it builds the Serre tensor-ideal B_0 of finitely presented modules admitting a non-zero compact that kills them, verifies closure under extensions from locality of the compacts, passes to the Gabriel quotient, and proves that a maximal tensor-ideal of the quotient has zero preimage in the compacts exactly when it contains B_0, which uses the embedding of the quotient unit into the dual of a compact tensored with itself; then it shows that both kernels of f and g would have to be contained in the unique maximal tensor-ideal, forcing a monomorphism into a tensor product of flat objects and contradicting f tensor g = 0. The converse direction uses E_B tensor E_C = 0 for distinct homological primes, finite presentability of the unit to factor the units of the pure-injectives through compacts, and the weak-ring property to convert nilpotence into E_B tensor z = 0. Neither implication is a formal consequence of the definitions, and the appendix theorem is the paper's only unconditional characterization of injectivity of the comparison map.

items.title: Surjectivity of the restriction map in Galois cohomology from an imaginary quadratic extension to the real place for a connected semisimple algebraic group over the rationals
items.author: Dave Witte Morris
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the lemma at source lines 245-249, label KneserHasse: for a connected semisimple algebraic group G over the rationals and any imaginary quadratic extension L, the natural restriction map from H^1(L/Q; G(L)) to H^1(R; G) is surjective. The proof retained at source lines 251-282 is the author's own argument rather than a citation: it represents an arbitrary real cohomology class by an element t of a maximal torus with t t^sigma = 1 and uses weak approximation for the variety of maximal tori to make that torus rational, then passes to the restriction of scalars R = Res_{L/Q} T, exhibits the L-isomorphism R = T x T that turns the norm-one condition r r^tau = 1 into an explicitly described subtorus, proves that this subtorus is defined over Q, and finishes by moving the class along a rational point produced by weak approximation at the infinite place. The non-routine content is exactly this combination: the cohomological representative has to be replaced by a rational point lying in the same connected component of a norm-one torus, which needs both the explicit model of the restriction of scalars and the archimedean density statement. Neither surjectivity nor the existence of such a representative follows from the definitions of Galois cohomology or from formal Hasse-principle arguments alone.

items.title: Every exact symplectomorphism of a compact surface with prescribed collar behaviour that is C1-close to the identity is generated by a quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian, with C1-small Hamiltonian and a collar expansion b_C + r^2 h_C
items.author: Alberto Abbondandolo; Christian Lange; Marco Mazzucchelli
items.work: Higher systolic inequalities for 3-dimensional contact manifolds

items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Theorem 2.8 at source lines 584-598, label t:quasi_autonomous: every exact symplectomorphism of a compact surface whose exact two-form satisfies the author's collar Assumption and which is sufficiently C1-close to the identity is generated by a Hamiltonian isotopy with a quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian, with C1-small H_t and phi_t and with the collar expansion H_t(r,s) = b_C + r^2 h_C(t,r,s) where |b_C| and the C0 norm of h_C are small. The retained proof is source section 2.3, which first has to build the tools it needs: it normalises a primitive in each collar to (a_C - r^2/2) ds, constructs the explicit map kappa_0(r,s,R,S) = (R, s, R(S-s), (r^2-R^2)/2) and proves a Weinstein tubular neighbourhood lemma for the diagonal of a surface with boundary, including the identity f(z_1,z_2) = -integral over the arc [z_1,z_2] of nu_0 on the boundary, and only then analyses the generating function on the cotangent bundle to produce the quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian and its boundary expansion. Neither the existence of a quasi-autonomous generator nor the boundary shape b_C + r^2 h_C follows from the usual C1-closeness theorem: the extremal points of H_t have to be produced from critical points of the generating function, and the collar expansion has to be read off from the explicit boundary formula for psi. The C1 estimates of items (i) and (ii) at source lines 589-597 are quantitative and are not restated anywhere else in the article.

items.title: Two nonzerodivisors in a one-dimensional local ring acquire a common factor after a finite blowup
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma turns a pair of nonzerodivisors in a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring into a pair with a common factor after a finite ring extension killed by a power of the maximal ideal (statement lines 567-572). The proof replaces the plausible algebraic argument by a geometric one: it blows up R in I = (a, b), shows the blowup is finite over Spec(R) by combining projectivity, the fact that all generic points lie over the punctured spectrum, and the finite-in-codimension-one criterion, and then uses that a locally principal ideal over the resulting semi-local ring is principal, which produces t with a = a't, b = b't (proof lines 578-601). The non-routine content is precisely this combination: finiteness of the blowup is what makes R' a ring of the required shape, and semi-locality is what upgrades locally principal to principal. The claim is H2.

The proof is short and complete, with the cited Limits lemma as its only external input, so H2.

items.title: The sheaf of differentials of a morphism of algebraic spaces restricts to the relative differentials along an etale commutative square
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a morphism of algebraic spaces f : X -> Y over a scheme S and a commutative square with etale vertical maps a : U -> X and b : V -> Y, and asserts the restriction formula Omega_{X/Y}|_{U_etale} = Omega_{U/V}, with the scheme case of the usual sheaf of differentials as a corollary (statement lines 980-996). The proof does not run through presentations of algebraic spaces at all: it identifies restriction to U_etale with pullback along a_{small} by the etale-topos equivalence, applies the localisation lemma for differentials on ringed sites, and then rewrites the coefficient sheaf of rings through the commutativity of the square (proof lines 999-1013). The step that carries the content is that last rewriting, because it is the only place where the hypothesis that the square commutes is used. The proof is short but has no gap and no omitted argument, so H2.

items.title: A Moser diffeomorphism pulling omega back to omega_0, fixing the boundary
items.author: Alberto Abbondandolo; Christian Lange; Marco Mazzucchelli
items.work: Higher systolic inequalities for 3-dimensional contact manifolds
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.195
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:pullback_to_nu0` at source lines 1501-1504: if lambda is C2-close enough to lambda_0 then there is a diffeomorphism kappa fixing the boundary with kappa^* omega = omega_0, and kappa is C1-close to the identity as lambda approaches lambda_0. The author's proof (source lines 1506-1580) is a complete Moser-trick construction on a surface with boundary: it first checks that the interpolating forms are symplectic with the right orientation and uniformly close (line 1507), sets up the isotopy equation d(X interior omega_t + nu - nu_0) = 0 and chooses the defining equation for X_t with a function f still to be determined (lines 1509-1523), computes in collar coordinates the structure functions h_1, h_2, h_3 together with the differential identity they satisfy (lines 1525-1539), chooses f explicitly as minus the integral of h_1 near the boundary and zero further out, and then estimates the two components of X_t, obtaining S_t = 0 and a formula for R_t with a C0-small numerator that makes X_t C1-small, smoothly extendable and boundary-vanishing (lines 1540-1577); the flow then gives the conclusion (lines 1578-1579). The statement contains only the existence and the convergence, and the whole quantitative part is invisible in it.

items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file reals.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 11.3.46 at source lines 1636-1646: squaring of rationals extends to a unique function on the Cauchy reals with the explicit Lipschitz bound |u^2 - v^2| <= 2 n |u - v| on [-n,n]. The author's proof (source lines 1648-1680) assembles four separate inputs rather than computing directly: the archimedean property makes the bounded-interval cover surjective onto RC (lines 1649-1658), the retained extension theorem turns squaring on each bounded rational interval, which is Lipschitz with constant 2n, into a map on that interval (lines 1658-1668), compatibility of these extensions on overlaps is deduced from continuity via the retained continuity lemma (lines 1668-1671), and uniqueness is obtained by factoring through the surjection using the retained factorisation result (lines 1671-1679). The statement is a single existence-and-uniqueness assertion with an estimate, and records none of the four steps.

items.title: Ell-adic completion preserves exactness of a short sequence of abelian groups under a finiteness hypothesis
items.author: Cyril Demarche; David Harari
items.work: Duality for complexes of tori over a global field of positive characteristic
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 7 (2020), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.129
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an exact sequence of abelian groups A -> B -> E -> 0 and states that the induced map B^(ell) -> E^(ell) on ell-adic completions is surjective, and that if the ell-torsion of E (or the quotient A/ell) is finite then A^(ell) -> B^(ell) -> E^(ell) -> 0 is again exact (statement lines 1074-1087). The proof first exploits right exactness of tensoring with Z/ell^m to get surjectivity of the maps on the kernels of the completed sequence, and then replaces A by the image I of A -> B so that the snake lemma can be applied and projective limits taken along the finite quotients _{ell^m}E (proof lines 1093-1125). The step that cannot be done by a single cited theorem is the middle one: passing to the projective limit requires the finiteness of the ell-power torsion for every m, which the author proves by an explicit induction using the short exact sequences _{ell}E -> _{ell^{m+1}}E -> _{ell^m}E. Both hypotheses of the second part are used in the proof, and the two cases are handled separately. H2.

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment following the lem (source lines 1090-1127)

items.title: Finiteness of the cohomology of tori and of finite multiplicative-type group schemes over a curve
items.author: Cyril Demarche; David Harari
items.work: Duality for complexes of tori over a global field of positive characteristic
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 7 (2020), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.129
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is about a curve U over a global field of positive characteristic: it claims that for a torus T the groups H^0(U, T) and H^1(U, T) are of finite type (finite when U is not X), and that for a finite group scheme N of multiplicative type both H^1(U, N) and H^2_c(U, N^D) are finite (statement lines 561-573). The proof splits T along a finite connected etale Galois covering, uses Dirichlet's theorem and the finiteness of the ideal class group to bound the two cohomology groups, and then embeds N into a sequence of two tori so that the finiteness reduces to an image computation plus a division by the order of N (proof lines 578-621). The step that is not a routine citation is the second one: the connecting map H^0(U, T_2) -> H^1(U, N) has to be controlled by factoring it through H^0(U, T_2)/n, and the author supplies that factorisation explicitly rather than invoking a general finiteness principle. The duality input at the end is a cited theorem, so the card is H2.

items.title: Monotonicity, positivity, edge direction and facet containment for the folding map of the associahedron
items.author: Naruki Masuda; Hugh Thomas; Andy Tonks; Bruno Vallette
items.work: The diagonal of the associahedra
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.142
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four properties of the folding map L that sends the vertices of the polytope P to the Boolean lattice: monotonicity along the lattice order, positivity of the scalar products with the coordinate vectors, the direction of the edges joining L-fibres, and the containment of every fibre in a facet (statement lines 1414-1425). The proof treats the four clauses separately, and the two that carry content are the third, where the edge vector between two neighbouring trees is computed explicitly as omega_i omega_{i+2} e_i on a single polytope K_omega, and the fourth, where an occurrence of the pattern (1,0) in the folding sequence produces the facet containing the fibre (proof lines 1434-1439). The second clause is dismissed by the author as straightforward from the definition of the vector; the first and fourth are argued in one sentence each but with the decisive observation stated. The proof is complete in the sense that every clause is addressed inside the span, so H2.

items.title: The Loday realization of the associahedron: its hyperplane, its facets and its face lattice
items.author: Naruki Masuda; Hugh Thomas; Andy Tonks; Bruno Vallette
items.work: The diagonal of the associahedra
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.142
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition collects five properties of the weighted Loday realization K_omega of the associahedron: the hyperplane containing it, its description by half-spaces with equality exactly on decomposable trees, the fact that this hyperplane-and-half-space system cuts the polytope out, the identification of the face lattice with the lattice of planar trees, and the product decomposition of any face (statement lines 670-691). The proof's substance is in clauses (3) to (5): clause (3) requires showing that the equations defining a vertex have nested or disjoint intervals, which is done by deriving a strict inequality that contradicts the defining half-spaces (proof lines 699-731), clause (4) then reads the face lattice off the facet description of clause (2), and clause (5) exhibits the explicit isomorphism Theta putting a product of two smaller Loday realizations onto a facet (proof lines 738-753). Clauses (1) and (2) are dismissed by the author as straightforward from the definition, and both dismissals are kept verbatim in the counted span; they are not where the item's obligation lies, since the decisive statement is the combinatorial description of the polytope, which is proved. H2.

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment following the proposition (source lines 693-755)

items.title: The tame symbol is well defined independently of the factorizations and of the chosen extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes that the displayed formula for the tame symbol gives a well-defined element of kappa(m)*, i.e. that the right-hand side is independent both of the local factorizations chosen and of the admissible extension B (statement lines 831-834). The two independence statements are proved by genuinely different arguments: the first turns the two factorizations into a unit identity by clearing powers and then settles the sign through a parity check on the exponents, while the second builds a third extension C dominating both, invokes transitivity of norms, and reduces everything to the numerical identity lambda^m = prod Norm(lambda)^{m_k}, which is then verified by comparing lengths using the comparison lemma and the pushdown lemma (proof lines 838-898). What is not routine is the bookkeeping that makes lambda^m match the product of the norms, in particular the identity m = sum m_k [kappa_k : kappa]. The claim is H2.

items.title: Sheafifying the differentials of a morphism of schemes on the small etale site gives the module of differentials of the morphism of etale sites
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma compares two objects attached to a morphism of schemes f : X -> Y, the sheaf (Omega_{X/Y})^a on the small etale site of X and the module Omega_{X_etale/Y_etale} defined on ringed sites, and asserts a canonical isomorphism compatible with universal derivations (statement lines 860-877). The proof builds the two comparison maps from opposite directions: c from etale-local identification of the values of (Omega_{X/Y})^a and the universal property of the module of differentials, c'' by restricting a derivation to the small Zariski site and taking an adjoint along id_{small,etale,Zar} (proof lines 880-936). The non-routine part is that the second direction has to pass through the Zariski site, where derivations are classical, and then back to the etale site by adjunction; the final check that the two composites are the identity is explicitly left to the reader (proof line 941) and is routine. Hence H2.

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 4.17 at source lines 1905-1912: for a < b and positive bounded increasing functions f, g on the interval, the mean of f g is at least the product of the means, with equality if and only if f or g is constant. The statement records the inequality and the equality case but neither the comparison of measures nor the reduction to indicators.

items.title: The action of a finite family of increasing kernels preserves the stochastic order and stabilises the decreasing-density class
items.author: Charles Boubel; Nicolas Juillet
items.work: The Markov-quantile process attached to a family of marginals

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 4.4 at source lines 1519-1530: for a finite set R and measures mu, nu in a class of measures, if mu <= nu then mu applied to the kernel l_R is again <= nu applied to it, and if mu has decreasing density then so does mu applied to l_R with mu <= that measure. items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is about thickenings X subset X' and Y subset Y' of algebraic spaces over a base B and a morphism f : X -> Y: given a map of O_B-algebras alpha from f_{spaces,etale}^{-1}O_{Y'} to O_{X'} that makes the square with f^sharp, i_Y^sharp and i_X^sharp commute, it produces a unique morphism of thickenings f' lifting f with (f')^sharp = alpha (statement lines 1600-1621). items.title: Triviality of the centre of a Lie superalgebra passes to the enveloping algebra of its polynomial current algebra
items.author: Maxim Nazarov
items.work: Yangian of the General Linear Lie Superalgebra
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 112, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.112; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition is about a Lie superalgebra a with trivial centre and claims that the centre of the enveloping algebra U(a[u]) of its polynomial current algebra is also trivial, that is equal to the scalars (statement lines 1239-1244). The proof passes to the invariants of the adjoint action on the supersymmetric algebra by the Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt theorem, takes an invariant A of maximal degree d in the generators f_i u^d, and expands it in the top-degree monomials (proof lines 1247-1276). The step that carries the content is the comparison at the end: the top-degree part of the invariance equation is a linear system whose coefficient matrix is the same as the one expressing triviality of the centre of a, after replacing the basis by (m'_q + 1) f_q (-1)^{h'_q}; triviality of the centre of a forces only the zero solution, and the coefficients of A in top degree therefore die one by one (proof lines 1317-1343). The degree argument then collapses d to zero. The whole proof is self-contained apart from the cited PBW reduction, so H2.

items.title: Stable vertices and the core of a matching do not depend on the reduction process
items.author: Marmor, Avichai
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 846-849: given a matching, its stable vertices and its core are well defined. The proof (source lines 850-853) is an exchange argument on two reduction processes run on the same matching: one compares the two lists of removed chords, takes the first position at which they differ, and uses the fact that the deviating chord had to become short before being removed in both processes to derive a contradiction, which forces the two lists to remove the same chords. The statement is a well-definedness claim for two constructions and records neither the process comparison nor the minimal-deviation argument, and the argument has to be carried through the vertex renumbering that each removal performs.

primary.label: prop:core well defined (statement, author label)

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled proposition, retained line for line

items.author: Marmor, Avichai

The author gave it no label, so its position in the article is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 861-869) first transfers well-definedness from the stable vertices and the core, and then has to check that the explicitly defined two-row tableau is standard: every letter occurs once, the rows increase, and each entry of the second row is matched to a smaller entry of the first row, which is what makes the columns increase; the count of unstable chords then identifies the shape. The statement records the map and none of the standardness verification.

items.title: Inserting a short chord at any two positions gives Knuth equivalent matchings
items.author: Marmor, Avichai
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1157-1160: for a matching m and any two insertion positions i and j, the matchings obtained by inserting a short chord at i and at j are Knuth equivalent. The proof (source lines 1161-1165) is an induction on the distance between the two positions, and its only non-formal step is the claim that inserting at i+1 is Knuth equivalent to inserting at i; that claim has to be read off the explicit vertex-shifting formula of the insertion definition rather than from the statement, and it is what makes the induction run. The statement records neither the induction parameter nor the appeal to the shifting formula.

items.title: Knuth equivalent matchings have the same core
items.author: Marmor, Avichai
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 1128-1130, the first of the two steps into which the author splits the proof of the theorem that two matchings are Knuth equivalent if and only if they have the same core. It states that two Knuth equivalent matchings have equal cores. The author gave it no label, so its position in the article is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 1131-1133) is short but requires a step that the statement hides: Knuth equivalence is generated by elementary Knuth transformations, so the invariant has to be checked on a single elementary transformation, and that check is done by comparing which chords the reduction process removes before and after the transformation. The statement mentions neither the reduction to one transformation nor the comparison of removed-chord sets.

items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia’s coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.317
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1266-1272: for every measurable subset A of the simplex, the probability that the empirical frequency vector lies in A differs from the probability that the Dirichlet limit lies in A by O(measure of the complements of the two exception events plus 1/log x). The proof (source lines 1274-1298) does not estimate the two probabilities separately but proves the stronger deterministic statement that on the intersection of the three events the two membership conditions coincide. The forward direction is a contradiction argument: one places a ball of an explicit radius around the empirical vector inside A and a ball around the limit inside the complement, uses the coupling distance bound to exhibit a point on the segment joining the two centres, and concludes by convexity of the simplex and of the two balls; the reverse direction is the symmetric variation of the same argument. Neither the deterministic reduction nor the convexity step appears in the statement.

items.title: The universal Askey-Wilson algebra maps onto the Askey-Wilson algebra, sending alpha, beta, gamma to a fixed central scalar
items.author: Paul Terwilliger
items.work: The Universal Askey-Wilson Algebra
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 7 (2011) article 069, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2011.069; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the universal Askey-Wilson algebra admits a unique F-algebra homomorphism onto the Askey-Wilson algebra Lambda taking A, B, C to the explicit combinations qA + q^{-1}A^{-1} and so on, and that this homomorphism sends alpha, beta and gamma to nu I with nu = (q^2+q^{-2})mu + mu^2 (statement lines 915-937). The proof substitutes the candidate images into the defining relations: two cited lemmas produce the three identities that A^vee, B^vee and C^vee satisfy, and because nu I is central these identities are recognised as the relations of the universal algebra (proof lines 940-971). The step that carries the content is that recognition, since the identities are obtained from a multiplication table rather than assumed; uniqueness and the images of alpha, beta, gamma are then immediate from generation and the defining relations. H2.

items.title: The monomials of degree at most n form a basis of the n-th filtration layer of the universal Askey-Wilson algebra
items.author: Paul Terwilliger
items.work: The Universal Askey-Wilson Algebra
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 7 (2011) article 069, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2011.069; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem states that the monomials A^i B^j C^k alpha^r beta^s gamma^t of total degree at most n form a basis of the n-th layer of the filtration of the universal Askey-Wilson algebra (statement lines 1349-1358). Independence is cited from the paper's own basis theorem, and the proof then establishes spanning by induction: the layer is generated by words in the seven generators, and the commutation lemma together with centrality of alpha, beta and gamma allows each word to be reordered modulo the previous layer, so only monomials of total degree exactly n have to be added at each step (proof lines 1361-1404). The step that carries the content is the reordering modulo Delta_{n-1}, since it is what converts an arbitrary word into the required monomial shape; the induction itself is then routine. H2.

items.title: The normalised gaps of the scale-invariant point process follow a GEM distribution
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia’s coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.317
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 706-709: the vector formed by one minus the first gap and the successive later gaps, all divided by the logarithm of x, follows a GEM distribution. The proof (source lines 711-713) is a single change of variables, but the step is not formal: the scale-invariant spacing process has to be transported by the map sending s to the base-two logarithm of x minus the logarithm of s, the mapping theorem has to be invoked to know that the image is again a Poisson process, now homogeneous of rate one on the whole real line, and the ordered points of that process have to be recognised as producing the geometric proportions that define the GEM distribution. The statement records only the resulting law.

items.title: The Dedekind-finite tree U_T falls into the definable cardinality class Delta_5
items.author: Supakun Panasawatwong, J K Truss
items.work: Dedekind-finite cardinals having countable partitions
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem is about the set U_T of nodes of a countable weakly 2-transitive tree together with its symmetric model with finite supports, and it pins the definable cardinality of U_T into the class Delta_5, with the sharper negative statement when the tree has infinitely many ramification orders (statement lines 307-308). The proof takes a surjection onto U_T union {*} with finite support A and shows that every point outside the definable closure of A is fixed, by analysing where an image point can sit relative to A: outside the closure the only possible obstruction is a cone at an exceptional ramification point created by a meet with an element of A, and iterating that obstruction for a preimage produces a contradiction (proof lines 310-341). The step that carries the content is the description of the closure [A union {x}] and the two-case analysis built on it, since it is what forces the fixed-point behaviour; surjectivity then fails against the finiteness of the support. H2.

items.author: Przemysław Berk; Frank Trujillo; Hao Wu

items.title: Every omega-tree with finite levels contains a leafless balanced subtree with omega levels
items.author: Supakun Panasawatwong, J K Truss
items.work: Dedekind-finite cardinals having countable partitions
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, inside any tree with omega finite levels, a subtree that is balanced, has no leaves and still has omega levels (statement lines 491-492). The proof schedules prunings according to a sequence in which every natural number occurs infinitely often, at each stage keeping only the nodes of the scheduled level that have infinitely many points above them and, among those, the minimum degree, and then takes the intersection of the resulting decreasing sequence of subtrees (proof lines 494-506). The two steps that carry the content are the choice of the minimum-degree pruning, which is what produces equal degrees on each level, and the argument that the levels of the intersection are eventually constant, which uses that each level is scheduled infinitely often and the levels are finite (proof lines 500-511). Leaflessness then follows because nodes survive with successors at every stage. H2.

items.title: Every template encodes a finitely branching omega-tree, uniquely up to local isomorphism, with branches controlled by branches of the template
items.author: Supakun Panasawatwong, J K Truss
items.work: Dedekind-finite cardinals having countable partitions
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma relates a template (T*, prec) to finitely branching omega-trees encoded by it: it produces one such tree, shows any two are locally isomorphic, links eventually singleton branches of the template to infinite branches of the tree, and proves that in a suitable finite-support model a template with no eventually singleton branch can encode a tree with no infinite branch at all (statement lines 588-595). The proof constructs the tree level by level while maintaining a bijection between the levels of the template and partitions of the levels of the tree (proof lines 597-608), then argues that the construction's freedom to leave the new points unordered is exactly what produces locally isomorphic but possibly non-isomorphic trees (proof lines 610-614), and finally runs a Fraenkel-Mostowski argument in which the group fixes the template and every would-be infinite branch lives inside a balanced subtree with infinitely many non-singleton entries (proof lines 619-625). The clause that carries the content is the last one, since it is the only place where the absence of choice is used; the first three clauses are a construction and two observations about it. H2.

items.title: Distinct infinite codes force the tree sets to be definably inequivalent inside Delta_5
items.author: Supakun Panasawatwong, J K Truss
items.work: Dedekind-finite cardinals having countable partitions
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem compares two countable weakly 2-transitive trees whose maximal chains in the one-point extensions are dense, and asserts that distinct infinite codes force the definable cardinalities of their node sets to be inequivalent, both lying in Delta_5 but not in Delta_4 (statement lines 377-379). The proof assumes an equivalence, which by the theory of definable cardinality gives a tree order on the first node set with a finite support and hence invariant under the pointwise stabiliser of that support, and then analyses that order on the pieces cut out by the support: it shows that on each piece the new order either agrees with the tree order or collapses to an antichain, using automorphisms that swap incomparable points inside the piece (proof lines 384-446). The decisive steps are the exclusion of the all-antichain case, which uses that the assumed order satisfies the same first order sentences and hence has only infinite chains, and the final recovery of the ramification orders above a point, which are first order definable and therefore equal to the codes (proof lines 448-466). items.title: The two-sided ideal generated by the commutators of the Askey-Wilson algebra coincides with the kernel of its polynomial quotient
items.author: Paul Terwilliger
items.work: The Universal Askey-Wilson Algebra
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 7 (2011) article 069, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2011.069; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition compares two objects attached to the universal Askey-Wilson algebra: the two-sided ideal generated by its commutators, and the kernel of the homomorphism onto the three-variable polynomial algebra (statement lines 2792-2808). The proof first observes that the commutator ideal sits inside that kernel because the target is commutative, then constructs a complement from the monomials A^i B^j C^k, which form a basis on the polynomial side, and finally shows that every word in the generators can be rewritten modulo the commutator ideal into that complement by successively swapping adjacent letters (proof lines 2811-2883). authors: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
items.work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem computes the non-minimality degree of a specific complete type: for the theory T_{r,k,mu} the type p given by the negation of the predicate P has nmdeg(p) = r - 1 (statement lines 2344-2351). The proof exhibits a tuple a_1, ..., a_r witnessing the relation R and analyses the successive types p_i = tp(a_i / A_{<i}): i-transitivity of the automorphism group on the complement of P makes each of the first r-1 a unique non-forking extension of p, while the last step forks because there are infinitely many choices of the final point producing distinct lines that meet the previous ones only in their common points (proof lines 2354-2368). The step that carries the content is the computation of the last step, since it is where the geometry of the lines is used to produce infinitely many forking extensions; the earlier steps are read off from the transitivity assumed in the construction. H2.

items.title: The probability that the second or the third event fails is of order one over the logarithm
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia’s coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 12 (2025), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.317
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 963-966: for x at least two, the sum of the probabilities that the second and that the third of the coupling events fail while the first holds is of order one over the logarithm of x. The proof (source lines 968-1041) is long and runs through four genuinely different steps: the failure of the second event is rewritten as an expectation of a double sum over pairs of points of the point process; the Mecke equation turns that expectation into a multiple integral against an exponential density; the density is then compared at the two levels so that the integrand depends on the two heights only through their sum, which collapses the number of integrations; and only after the exponential tail bound for the truncated weighted sum is inserted does the region split into two pieces whose evaluations give the stated order. The statement records the final order and none of the four steps.

items.title: The classifying space of the equivariant fundamental groupoid is universal for equivariant cellular maps
items.author: Massimiliano Puglisi; Thomas Schick; Vito Felice Zenobi
items.work: Stolz Positive Scalar Curvature Structure Groups, Proper Actions and Equivariant 2-Types
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 21 (2025) journal PDF and native TeX; acquired 2026-09-30; exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states the universal property of the classifying space B Pi of the equivariant fundamental groupoid: for every G-CW-complex Y and every natural transformation Phi from Pi_1(Y;G) to Pi there is a G-equivariant cellular map Y -> B Pi inducing Phi, unique up to G-equivariant homotopy (statement lines 1070-1077). The proof constructs the map skeleton by skeleton, choosing for each G-cell the ordinary cell inside the fixed point set of its isotropy group and prescribing the image through the transformation, and it extends over higher cells because the attaching maps become contractible through the vanishing of the higher homotopy groups of the fixed point sets (proof lines 1081-1117). The step that carries the content is the equivariant extension: the construction has to be checked to be independent of the chosen base cell, which uses naturality, and the extension over each cell uses both the groupoid structure of the transformation and the homotopy vanishing. Uniqueness is then the same induction for a homotopy between two maps. H2.

items.title: The argument principle turns a sign condition on the imaginary axis into the uniform Penrose condition
items.author: Marnie Smith
items.work: Phase mixing for the Hartree equation and Landau damping in the semiclassical limit
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 13 (2026), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.353
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1139-1146: if the imaginary part of the symbol vanishes only where its real part exceeds minus one, both for the symbol and for its low-frequency limit, then the uniform Penrose condition holds. The proof (source lines 1147-1189) first converts the pointwise sign condition into a statement about a curve in the complex plane and applies the argument principle to the symbol shifted by one, which is what produces a lower bound uniform in the parameter and the frequency; the positivity of the infimum in the condition is then established separately by rescaling the integral representation through an auxiliary function of the rescaled variables and bounding the tail of its defining integral with the third part of the boundedness and decay lemma. The statement records the two implications and the conclusion, and neither the curve argument nor the tail estimate.

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 1394-1399: for x beyond a universal threshold and for a level between two and the fourth power of the logarithm, the smooth part of the convolution sum is bounded by a constant times the logarithm of the level over the square root of the level, times an explicit factor in which the two weights appear. The author gave it no label, so its position in the article is part of its identity. The statement records only the final shape of the bound.

items.title: Non-minimality degree can be made arbitrarily large in an omega-categorical supersimple theory
items.author: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
authors: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
items.work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants
items.difficulty_reason: The fact asserts that for every n there is an omega-categorical supersimple theory with a type of non-minimality degree at least n (statement lines 1719-1723). The proof instantiates Evans's construction with a single k-ary relation, k = 3^{2n+1}, and the predimension delta(A) = 2|A| - |R(A)|/k!, verifying the two criteria on f(x) = log(x)/log(3) that make the generic theory simple (proof lines 1725-1733). The two steps that carry the content are then the n-transitivity computation, where an algebraic closure larger than n would have to be at least k in size and would violate the predimension bound through f, and the rank computation, which exhibits a k-element structure with exactly one instance of R to get SU(p) = 2 and hence the lower bound on the degree (proof lines 1733-1735). The construction is therefore explicit and the estimates are the substance. H2.

items.title: The closure of a generated subsystem is the subsystem itself
items.author: Silvia Barbina, Enrique Casanovas
items.work: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 358-360: for an HF-ordering of M, a subset A and the assumption that A equals its closure, the closure of the subsystem generated by A is that subsystem. The proof (source lines 361-363) replaces the generated subsystem by its presentation as a union of finite stages, reduces the claim to an induction on the stage, and the whole content of the induction step is the observation that a new element is a product of two elements of the previous union, so that the closure of that union already contains it because the closure is closed under forming blocks from elements already present. The statement records only the equality.

items.title: An HF-ordering over a partial subsystem exists exactly when that subsystem can be made an initial segment
items.author: Silvia Barbina, Enrique Casanovas
items.work: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 333-335: for partial Steiner triple systems A contained in B, there is an HF-ordering of B over A exactly when there is an HF-ordering of B in which A is an initial segment, and the author adds that one may in fact assume the given order is preserved. One direction is immediate from the definitions. In the other, the argument is not a definition chase: one has to take an element below an element of A that lies outside A, examine the block it produces in the ordering and extract four distinct elements, each of which is either below the chosen element or inside A, and only then does the defining condition of an HF-ordering over A deliver the contradiction. The statement records the equivalence and neither the block analysis nor the contradiction.

items.title: Forking independence coincides with tensor independence in the r-space theories of the paper
items.author: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
authors: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
items.work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies two independence relations in the r-space theories of the paper: forking independence over C and tensor independence, the latter being free amalgamation of the algebraic closures (statement lines 1089-1091). The proof disposes of one direction through invariant global types and reduces the other to the case where C is contained in an algebraically closed B, then finishes by the author's own claim about a C-indiscernible sequence of copies of B (proof lines 1111-1115 and the claim at 1124-1128). The step that carries the content is the proof of that claim, which splits according to the two ways tensor dependence can fail - either the algebraic closure is not larger than the union, or it is strictly larger - and in each case exhibits a finite set of neighbours witnessing the dependence of the next copy (proof lines 1133-1169). The author explicitly closes the main proof by pointing at the claim, so the claim and its proof are counted as the continuation of the same proof. H2.

items.title: A morphism of groupoids bijective on orbits and on isotropy groups is an equivalence
items.author: Massimiliano Puglisi; Thomas Schick; Vito Felice Zenobi
items.work: Stolz Positive Scalar Curvature Structure Groups, Proper Actions and Equivariant 2-Types
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 21 (2025) journal PDF and native TeX; acquired 2026-09-30; exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for a morphism of groupoids to be an equivalence: it is enough that the morphism induces a bijection between the orbit sets and, for every object, an isomorphism between the isotropy groups (statement lines 1261-1266). The proof is carried by an explicit commutative diagram that writes each groupoid as the disjoint union of the isotropy groups of representatives of its orbits; because the orbits correspond bijectively, the morphism becomes a disjoint union of isomorphisms of the summands, and a disjoint union of equivalences is an equivalence (proof lines 1267-1278). The substance is the decomposition: the diagram is what turns the two hypotheses into a summand-by-summand statement, and the remaining input is the standard closure of equivalences under disjoint unions. The proof is short but complete and contains no forward reference or omission. H2.

The proof first reduces to types without proper fibrations through the behaviour of F_ind along an analysis, then invokes the classification of such types into a locally modular case and a case internal to a non-locally-modular type (proof line 446-451). The step that carries the content is the second case: the proof has to move from generic 2-transitivity of the binding group to a definable isomorphism with a multiply transitive algebraic group action, where Knop's classification leaves only the affine and the projective actions, and then exhibit a Morley sequence on a line to obtain the value 2 for both invariants (proof lines 451-455). The first case is immediate, and the reduction is a citation plus one estimate. H2.

items.author: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
authors: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
items.work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem exhibits, for every n, an omega-categorical supersimple theory with a type whose fibre dimension strictly exceeds its non-minimality degree, the degree being exactly n (statement lines 1749-1754). The proof instantiates the same generic construction as the earlier existence result but with a piecewise f whose simplicity criteria only hold from n+2 onwards, so the finitely many amalgamation instances involving small structures have to be checked individually following the cited remark (proof lines 1758-1769). The two steps that carry the content are then the computation nmdeg(p) = n, which combines the rank with a predimension obstruction to the algebraic closure of n points having size n+1, and the strict inequality F_ind(p) > n, where the indiscernible-sequence analysis splits into the case where all (n+1)-tuples satisfy the relation - impossible because long sequences would have negative predimension - and the case where none does (proof lines 1769-1814). Both estimates are quantitative and are the substance of the proof. H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the degrees of a decomposition f = A(weierstrass_k) + weierstrass_k' B(weierstrass_k) for a function f in M_{k Lambda} with at most N poles counted with multiplicity: the numerator and denominator of A have degree at most 2N, those of B at most 2N+3 (statement lines 614-624). The proof reduces to the Lambda-periodic case by scaling, writes f through its even and odd parts, and reads the bounds off two pole counts: the even part has at most 2N poles and its reduced denominator contributes as many poles through the zeroes of Q(weierstrass), while the numerator is bounded by applying the same argument to the reciprocal and using that elliptic functions have equally many zeroes and poles; the odd part is handled the same way with the factor weierstrass' (proof lines 626-647). The step that carries the content is the passage from pole counts to degree bounds, which is the classical zero-pole bookkeeping for elliptic functions; the reduction and the odd part are then the same computation. H2.

items.title: The pi-adic completion of a localization of an integral perfectoid ring is again integral perfectoid
items.author: Juan Esteban Rodríguez Camargo
items.work: An integral model of the perfectoid modular curve
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.170
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for an integral perfectoid ring R with pseudo-uniformizer pi and any f in R, the pi-adic completion R<f^{-1}> = lim_n R/pi^n[f^{-1}] is again an integral perfectoid ring (statement lines 469-472). The proof computes the completion from the short exact sequences obtained by multiplying by pi^k - possible because pi is not a zero divisor - localizes them at f and passes to the inverse limit, which gives both pi-adic completeness and the non-zero-divisor property, and then localizes the Frobenius isomorphism at f to get surjectivity of the Frobenius on R<f^{-1}>/pi (proof lines 475-488). The step that carries the content is the passage from the level-wise sequences to the limit, since that is what identifies the completion of the localization with the localized completion and transfers both defining properties; the Frobenius check is then immediate by localizing an isomorphism. H2.

items.title: The upper shriek of the structure sheaf along an lci morphism is a shifted invertible sheaf
items.author: Juan Esteban Rodríguez Camargo
items.work: An integral model of the perfectoid modular curve
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.170
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the upper shriek of the structure sheaf along an lci morphism of relative dimension n between locally noetherian schemes of finite Krull dimension, showing it is the shift by n of an invertible sheaf (statement lines 689-692). The proof factors the morphism locally into a regular closed immersion followed by a smooth morphism, writes the upper shriek as the inverse image of a derived hom against the sheaf of m-differentials, and then replaces that derived hom by an explicit Koszul computation: the Koszul complex of the defining regular sequence is a flat resolution and its dual resolves the quotient shifted by the codimension (proof lines 694-707). The step that carries the content is the passage from the derived hom to the tensor product through the Koszul resolution, since it is what identifies the answer with the restriction of an invertible sheaf; the local factorization and the shift bookkeeping are then immediate. H2.
