items.title: A member of the family is covered by the coset determined by its own certificate
items.author: Gilad Chase, Neta Dafni, Yuval Filmus, Nathan Lindzey
items.work: Uniqueness for 2-Intersecting Families of \\ Permutations and Perfect Matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 568-572: for the characteristic function of a 2-intersecting family of permutations with common certificate size at most n minus two, each member implies that the whole family is covered by the coset determined by a minimal certificate for that member with one image fewer. The proof (source lines 573-577) takes a minimal certificate for the chosen member, forms the coset it determines with one image dropped, and then, for any other member of the family, invokes the representative lemma to find a representative whose certificate meets the first in exactly the intersection of the two; that intersection bound is precisely what forces the member into the coset. The statement records the covering and neither the choice of coset nor the use of the representative lemma.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a 2-out-of-3 statement for stably free modules over an arbitrary ring, inside a short exact sequence of finite projective modules, and its proof has to treat the three possible selections of the two stably free terms (statement lines 71-73). The case where the middle term P and the submodule P' are the stably free ones is the non-formal one: one has to display P'' as the complement of a free direct summand by rewriting P'' + (P' + R^m) + R^n in two different groupings and using the given freeness of P + R^n, rather than by cancelling free summands (proof lines 80-88). The remaining case is then dismissed by symmetry. The proof uses only that the sequence of projectives splits and the definition of stable freeness, both of which stay outside the counted span as standard prerequisites.

items.title: The base change of a dominant morphism along an open morphism is dominant
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The claim is that for a dominant f : X -> S and an open g : S' -> S, the base change f' : X times_S S' -> S' is again dominant (statement lines 1336-1338). The proof is a contradiction that has to move between three levels: it assumes f' is not dominant so that its image lies in a proper closed B, passes to the nonempty open U = S' minus B, uses openness of g together with density of f(X) to find x in X with f(x) in g(U), and then changes the base to W = Spec(kappa(f(x))). The step that carries the content is the last one: over the spectrum of a field the two nonempty pullbacks X_W and U_W must have a nonempty fibre product, which yields a point of X times_S S' landing in U and contradicts the containment in B (proof lines 1346-1351). This is H2: the argument is short and uses no hypothesis beyond dominance and openness, but the residue-field base change and the nonemptiness of a fibre product over a field are the non-formal moves, and neither is merely a citation in the author's text.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma transfers boundedness and tor amplitude from K tensor^L O/I to K tensor^L O/I^n uniformly in n (statement lines 12614-12630). Part (1) is an induction on n using the distinguished triangles coming from 0 -> I^n/I^{n+1} -> O/I^{n+1} -> O/I^n -> 0 and the base-change identification of K tensor^L I^n/I^{n+1} as (K tensor^L O/I) tensor^L_{O/I} I^n/I^{n+1}, which is what makes the bound independent of n (proof lines 12637-12660). Part (2) needs an additional reduction, since the test modules in the definition of tor amplitude are O/I^n-modules: one uses the finite filtration of such a module by the powers of I with O/I-module quotients, then rewrites (K tensor^L O/I^n) tensor^L_{O/I^n} G as (K tensor^L O/I) tensor^L_{O/I} G (proof lines 12666-12686). The claim is H2: two explicit reductions, each short once the right triangle and the right filtration are chosen.

items.title: The Brauer group of a C1 field is zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem computes the Brauer group of a C1 field as zero (statement lines 10833-10836). The argument passes through an explicit construction: a finite dimensional central division algebra D over K of degree d is split by the separable closure, D tensor_K K^sep being isomorphic to Mat_d(K^sep) uniquely up to inner isomorphism, so the determinant is Galois invariant and descends to the reduced norm N_red : D -> K, a homogeneous form of degree d on the d^2-dimensional K-space D (proof lines 10841-10849). The non-formal point is the C1 input: for d > 1 the form has more variables than its degree, so it has a nonzero zero, and a nonzero element with vanishing reduced norm is not invertible, contradicting divisionality (proof lines 10850-10852). The claim is H2: one descent construction and one application of the C1 hypothesis.

items.title: Cohomology of a profinite group in positive degrees is torsion and vanishes on Q-vector spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the cohomology of a profinite group in positive degrees: it is torsion, and it vanishes on Q-vector spaces (statement lines 8978-8986). The substantive step is the degree-one computation (proof lines 8989-8999): one represents a class in H^1(G, M) by an invariant element y of the quotient N of an injective I, lifts y to x in I, and then uses that the stabiliser U of x is open, hence of finite index r, so that the sum of the translates of x over representatives of G/U is invariant and maps to ry. The non-formal point is exactly this use of openness of the stabiliser in the profinite topology to manufacture the killing integer. The claim is H2: one explicit construction after a standard dimension-shifting reduction.

items.title: Every finitely branching level tree carries a sequence of ordered partitions with uniform successor numbers
items.author: Supakun Panasawatwong, J K Truss
items.work: Dedekind-finite cardinals having countable partitions
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem produces, for any tree with omega finite levels, a sequence of ordered partitions of its levels such that between consecutive levels the number of successors of a node inside a given piece is the same for all nodes of the piece (statement lines 527-530). The proof runs refinements of the partitions of each level along a schedule in which every level is treated infinitely often, refining one level at a stage by grouping nodes according to the vector of intersection sizes with the pieces of the next level, and ordering the pieces so that each previous piece splits into consecutive parts (proof lines 532-544). The step that carries the content is the limit argument: since each level is finite the refining sequences stabilise, and at the stable stage the grouping relation has become trivial on every piece, which is exactly what makes the successor counts uniform (proof lines 546-551). items.difficulty_reason: The lemma concerns an arbitrary ring map A -> B, complexes M of A-modules and N of B-modules, a map a : M -> N that becomes an isomorphism after the derived tensor product with B, and given subcomplexes M_1, N_1 compatible under a; the conclusion produces enlarged subcomplexes M_2, N_2 with an explicit cardinal bound max(kappa, |M_1 union N_1|) that kills one kernel and catches one image in every cohomological degree (statement lines 29894-29921). items.title: Lifting a bounded above acyclic complex of modules of the form P over IP to an acyclic complex whose terms lie in a class stable under summands and surjectivity modulo the ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement fixes a ring R, an ideal I, a class of R-modules closed under direct summands and stable under maps that are surjective modulo I, and asks that every bounded above acyclic complex whose terms are of the form P over IP with P in the class be lifted to a bounded above acyclic complex with terms in the class (statement lines 19342-19357). The proof is a downward induction on the degree under a vanishing bound: at each step the already lifted part is split as P^i = Z^i direct sum Z^{i+1} so that closure under summands keeps the cycles inside the class, and the next term is built from the projectivity of P^{n-1} together with the identification Z^n/IZ^n = Im(E^{n-1} -> E^n), after which property (3) upgrades the lifted map to a surjection (proof lines 19373-19383). What is not routine is maintaining three properties at once through the induction, namely the isomorphism modulo I, acyclicity in all degrees above the running index, and membership of every cycle in the class, which is why the two closure hypotheses are needed in exactly this form. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.

items.title: The content ideal of an element of a flat module is finitely generated
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma concerns the content ideal of an element x of a flat module over an arbitrary ring: whenever the set of ideals I with x in IM has a smallest element, that smallest element is finitely generated (statement lines 5712-5715). The author's proof is short and completely explicit (proof lines 5718-5721): it takes any ideal I with x in IM, writes x as a finite sum of f_i x_i with f_i in I and x_i in M, and observes that the finitely generated ideal (f_1, ..., f_n) already contains x. The point that has to be seen is the direction of the quantifier: it is not enough to exhibit one finitely generated ideal containing x, one must show that the assumed smallest ideal I cannot need more than the finitely many coefficients that occur in a single expression for x. Flatness of M enters only through the existence of such an expression for every ideal I, and the finitely generated ideal produced is contained in I, so it coincides with I by minimality.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four equivalent-looking descriptions of a finite module M of rank r over a domain: finiteness of the rank, the existence of a map to R^r with torsion kernel and cokernel, the existence of a single nonzero f making M_f free of rank r, and the existence of an injection R^r to M with torsion cokernel (statement lines 5083-5094). Its proof is the longest of the section (proof lines 5097-5137) and is the one that genuinely has to build objects rather than reduce to a definition. It starts by choosing generators of M and a basis of M tensor K and clearing all denominators with one element b, which makes the comparison map to R^r well defined and an isomorphism after tensoring with K (proof lines 5102-5116); then it shows the cokernel of that map is finite and torsion and chooses g annihilating it, splits M_g as N plus R_g^r, kills the remaining finite torsion module N by a further g', and concludes that M_f is free of rank r for f equal to gg' (proof lines 5119-5128); finally it writes a basis of M_f as m_j/f^{t_j} to produce the injection of (4) (proof lines 5131-5135). The last step is closed by the author with 'Details omitted.', which is reproduced verbatim; the three constructive steps before it are complete.

items.title: Torsion freeness survives base change along a flat homomorphism of domains
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is a base-change statement for torsion freeness along a flat map of domains, and the proof is a chain of three reductions that all have to be made in the correct order (statement lines 4824-4827, proof lines 4830-4837). One first sees that a torsion free M sits inside M tensor K and that flatness of R' over R keeps this injection after tensoring with R' (proof lines 4830-4833); the module M tensor K is then identified as a direct sum of copies of the fraction field so the problem is pushed to the single case K tensor R' (proof line 4834-4835), which is settled by recognising that module as a localisation of R' (proof line 4835-4836). What is not routine is the reduction step itself: it uses flatness of the ring map, not of the module, and it uses that torsion freeness is tested elementwise, so a reader cannot replace it by the (false) statement that an arbitrary tensor product of torsion free modules is torsion free.

items.title: Every flat module over a domain is torsion free
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is a one-line implication, flat implies torsion free over a domain, and the proof is a short but genuinely two-step argument (statement lines 4913-4915, proof lines 4918-4922). The decisive move is to test flatness on the principal multiplication maps x : R to R, which are injective because R is a domain with x nonzero; flatness transports that injectivity to x : M to M, and that is exactly what forbids a nonzero element of M from being killed by a nonzero ring element (proof lines 4919-4921). It is not a formal consequence of the definition of flatness alone: the domain hypothesis is what makes multiplication by x injective on the ring, and it is used at that single point. The proof reaches the conclusion directly, with no remaining verification.

items.title: The module of maps into a torsion free module is torsion free
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that Hom_R(M, N) is torsion free whenever N is, for arbitrary modules over a domain, and the author's proof is a two-line containment argument (statement lines 4995-4998, proof lines 5001-5004). It chooses a surjection from a direct sum of copies of R onto M and uses it to realise Hom_R(M, N) as a submodule of a product of copies of N (proof lines 5002-5003). The non-formal content is the choice of presentation and the direction of the induced map: the surjection on the first variable of Hom gives an injection into the product with Man itself, whereas the opposite arrow would be the wrong way. The reader also has to notice that the assertion is about torsion elements, which are tested elementwise, so a submodule of a product of torsion free modules is again torsion free.

items.title: Torsion kernel and cokernel do not change the rank of a module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma controls how far rank is from being an isomorphism invariant over a domain: a map M to M' whose kernel and cokernel are torsion modules has equal ranks at source and target (statement lines 5026-5030). The author's proof is a hint rather than a full argument (proof lines 5033-5035): one has to tensor the map with the fraction field K and observe that both the kernel and the cokernel die, because every torsion module has zero tensor product with K. The two steps that a reader must supply are that this vanishing holds for an arbitrary torsion module, not just for a module of the shape R/I, and that the resulting exactness of the tensor sequence identifies the induced map of K-vector spaces as an isomorphism. With that, the equality of ranks is just the definition of rank as a dimension.

items.difficulty_reason: The statement is Sylvester's determinant identity in the form det(id + a b) = det(id + b a) for two R-linear maps a : M -> N and b : N -> M between finite projective modules over an arbitrary ring R (statement lines 36419-36428). The proof is a three-stage reduction that is not a single routine computation: it first localizes at a prime to make the two modules finite free, then specializes to the universal polynomial ring in the matrix entries and passes to its fraction field so that the identity may be checked over a field of characteristic zero, and finally replaces the determinant by the traces of the powers of the matrix through a universal polynomial, leaving only the classical trace identity Trace((AB)^k) = Trace((BA)^k) (proof lines 36431-36454). The characteristic-zero input is what makes the passage from determinants to traces legitimate, since a determinant of size at most N is a polynomial expression in the traces of the powers there. The whole argument is inside the counted span, which refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects five properties of a coherent sheaf F on a proper scheme over a field whose support has dimension at most zero: global generation, a description of H^0 as the direct sum of the stalks at the support, vanishing of higher cohomology, the resulting formula for the Euler characteristic, and chi(X, F tensor E) = n chi(X, F) for locally free E of rank n. The proof realizes F as i_*G for the scheme-theoretic support Z, which is zero-dimensional and hence affine and a finite disjoint union of spectra of local Artinian rings, so that G is globally generated with vanishing higher cohomology and H^0(Z, G) is the direct sum of the stalks (proof lines 6225-6247). The last item uses the projection formula together with i^*E being trivial of rank n on the zero-dimensional Z (proof lines 6249-6256). H2: the reduction to the zero-dimensional support and the rank count via the projection formula are the substance.

items.author: Johan H{\aa}stad, Bj\"orn Martinsson, Tamio-Vesa Nakajima, Stanislav \v{Z}ivn\'y
authors: Johan H{\aa}stad, Bj\"orn Martinsson, Tamio-Vesa Nakajima, Stanislav \v{Z}ivn\'y
items.work: A logarithmic approximation of linearly ordered colourings
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the subprocedure lemma of the paper (author lemma at source lines 151-156, label lem:innerstep): for a {2,3}-uniform hypergraph that admits an LO 2-colouring and whose system Av = 1^m fixes no variable, produce a vertex set T of size at least n/2 that meets every 3-edge in zero or two vertices and every 2-edge in exactly one vertex, in O(n^3 + nm) time. The proof (source lines 158-182) is not a routine greedy step: it first reads the solution set of the linear system as an affine space and chooses a random solution to make the membership of each vertex in T a fair coin, with the odd-parity condition on every edge following from the parity of the right-hand side (proof lines 159-167), and then converts the randomised guarantee into a deterministic one by the method of conditional expectations, fixing the variables a_i one at a time so that at least half of the coordinates determined at that step become zero (proof lines 169-180). The bound |T| >= n/2 is exactly what the main algorithm needs from the subprocedure. H2.

items.title: A connected d-regular graph with second-largest eigenvalue at least d-1 has a perfect or nearly-perfect matching
items.author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
items.work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the spectral matching lemma of the paper (author Lemma at source lines 339-342, label lem:regular-matching): a connected d-regular graph with lambda(Gamma) >= d-1 has a perfect matching when the order is even and a nearly-perfect matching when it is odd. Its proof (source lines 344-366) cannot be done by the routine textbook argument that would apply when no spectral hypothesis is present: the parity upgrade from the expansion estimate e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) >= d-1 to e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) >= d is the step that makes the double counting work, and it uses d-regularity in the form d|Q_i| = 2 e_Gamma(Q_i) + e_Gamma(Q_i, Q_i^c) together with the oddness of |Q_i| (proof lines 353-359). The closing step appeals to the Tutte-Berge formula for maximum matchings rather than to Hall's condition in the bipartite form. H2.

items.title: A direct sum of simple Lie algebras over Q is R-universal exactly under four Brauer-theoretic conditions
items.author: Dave Witte Morris
items.work: A Cohomological Proof that Real Representations of Semisimple Lie Algebras Have Q-Forms
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 11 (2015) article 034, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2015.034; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the author's structure proposition for a direct sum of simple Lie algebras over Q (source lines 885-909): R-universality is equivalent to four simultaneous conditions on the simple factors, on the star-action, and on the Tits algebras of the factors. The proof (source lines 911-946) is not a routine assembly of earlier statements: condition (3) is a computation in the Brauer group, where the real division algebras attached to lambda_i and lambda_j are tensored, R-universality of the sum is used to force the tensor product to be Brauer equivalent to Q, and the conclusion that the two quaternion algebras are isomorphic uses that they are quaternion algebras (proof lines 921-932). Condition (4) needs the choice of an outer factor and a weight moved by the star-action before the restriction to the splitting field L, and it consumes the author's fourth description of R-universality through the division algebra D(Lie G, Q)(lambda) (proof lines 934-945). The two external lemmas it invokes, SameFixed and RunivIff, are navigation pointers only; the parts of the argument that use them are one-line appeals. H2.

items.title: Baire category theorem for a complete linearly topologized abelian group with a countable fundamental system
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Baire category theorem in the form this chapter needs: for a linearly topologized complete abelian group with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero, a countable intersection of open dense subsets is dense (statement lines 9037-9042). The proof is a full 31-line construction (proof lines 9045-9075): after replacing the U_n by their finite intersections it builds, for a prescribed point x and a prescribed neighbourhood M_k of zero, a sequence y_i with y_i in U_i and y_i - y_{i-1} in M_{k_{i-1}}, where the indices k_i are chosen increasing so that y_i + M_{k_i} sits inside U_i, then uses completeness to produce the limit y and shows x - y is in M_k and y is in every U_i. The two places where the topology is really consumed are the choice of each k_i, which needs openness of U_i, and the passage to the limit, which needs completeness of M; the proof closes with the telescoping identity for y - y_i, so no step is left as routine.

items.title: The first Koszul homology of a sequence with flat quotient maps onto its base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a base change statement for the first Koszul homology: if B over A is a ring map, f_1 to f_r is a sequence in B whose quotient B/(f_1, ..., f_r) is flat over A, and A to A' is any ring map, then the canonical map from H_1 of the Koszul complex of the sequence tensored with A' to H_1 of the Koszul complex of the base changed sequence is surjective (statement lines 7934-7945). The proof is a 42-line exactness computation (proof lines 7948-7989): it splits the four-term complex wedge^2(B^r) to B^r to B to B/J to 0 into three short exact sequences, tensors them with A' and uses flatness of B/J to keep the first one exact, then deduces J' = J tensor A' and the surjectivity of K tensor A' onto the kernel of the base changed map, and finally identifies H_1 tensor A' with a cokernel that maps onto the cokernel computing H'_1, which is the surjectivity asserted. The single place where the flatness hypothesis is consumed is the exactness of the first tensored sequence, and no step is left to the reader.

items.title: Totalisation of the tensor product is a functor on the homotopy category
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma makes the derived tensor product well defined: if two maps of complexes alpha and beta are homotopic, then their totalisations after tensoring with the identity of a fixed complex P are homotopic, so that L to Tot(L tensor P) descends to the homotopy category (statement lines 14103-14117). The proof is short but it is the standard construction rather than a citation (proof lines 14120-14136): from a homotopy h with alpha = beta + dh + hd in each degree one forms the total homotopy H given in degree n by the direct sum of the h^a tensor the identity on P^b over all decompositions n = a + b, and then verifies that Tot(alpha tensor id) equals Tot(beta tensor id) plus dH plus Hd. The verification is described by the author as a straightforward computation, and the only structural point is that summing the degreewise homotopies over the bigraded pieces of the total complex does produce a homotopy of the total complex, which is exactly why the total differential has the shape it has.

items.title: A monic polynomial over a ring is divisible by T minus each of its roots
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the first structural fact used in the section on descent of flatness along integral maps: a monic polynomial P over an arbitrary ring with a root alpha factors as (T - alpha) times a monic Q (statement lines 4551-4555). The author's proof is an 8-line induction on the degree which uses polynomial division by the monic linear factor T - alpha and evaluates the remainder at alpha (proof lines 4558-4565). What a reader has to supply is that division with remainder by a monic polynomial is available over an arbitrary ring, including over a ring with zero divisors, and that evaluating (T - alpha)Q + r at alpha leaves exactly r: the two steps are standard but they are what makes the argument work and the author does not spell them out beyond recording the division. Everything else in the proof is the induction, which is carried out for all degrees including the case where the ring is not a domain.

items.title: Juxtaposing an H1-regular sequence with an H1-regular sequence modulo the ideal it generates stays H1-regular
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the gluing statement for H_1-regularity: if I is generated by an H_1-regular sequence f_1 to f_n and the images of g_1 to g_m are H_1-regular in A/I, then the juxtaposed sequence f_1 to f_n, g_1 to g_m is H_1-regular in A (statement lines 7575-7582). Its proof is a 32-line argument built on a commutative diagram of the two Koszul complexes (proof lines 7585-7616) and it proceeds in two genuine correction steps: an element of A^{n+m} mapping to zero is first corrected by lifting an element of the exterior square from A/I to A so that its last m coordinates land in I, and then corrected along the images of the wedge elements (0, ..., g_j, 0, ..., f_i, 0, ...) so that those coordinates become zero; what remains lies in the first n coordinates and dies by the assumed H_1-regularity of f_1 to f_n. The case in which the two sequences interact is exactly the content of the lemma, and neither correction is bookkeeping.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the gluing statement for quasi-regularity, the analogue of the H1-regular gluing proved in the same section: if I is generated by a quasi-regular sequence f_1 to f_n and the images of g_1 to g_m are H_1-regular in A/I, then the juxtaposition is quasi-regular in A (statement lines 7522-7528). Both halves are genuine inductions and the second one needs the intermediate lemma to convert an intersection statement into a membership statement.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma sits inside a Situation with a fibre product of rings and describes the right adjoint of the functor that sends a pair (N, M') to the pair (N tensor B', N tensor A') equipped with its comparison map: the right adjoint is the fibre product N x_M M' over the common quotient M = M'/IM' (statement lines 643-655). It also asserts that the composition with the original functor is the identity, which is the part that has to be proved. The adjointness half alone is delegated to another lemma of the same chapter, while the identity statement is carried out completely inside the counted span.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma upgrades the previous descent statement to an invariance: for ring maps R to A to B with A to B faithfully flat and a complex K of A-modules, the tor amplitude of K over R equals the tor amplitude of K tensor over A with B over R (statement lines 17261-17266). The proof is a 16-line computation (proof lines 17269-17284): it reduces the claim to the identity of cohomology modules H^i of K tensor over R with M, base changed along A to B, and on the other side H^i of the derived tensor product over R of K tensor over A with B with M, then proves that identity by representing K by a complex, choosing a free resolution of M and comparing two total complexes that differ only in the order of the tensor factors. items.title: p-independent sets, p-bases and the differentials of a field extension of characteristic p
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the main structure theorem for a field extension K over a field k of characteristic p: p-independence of a subset is equivalent to linear independence of its differentials in the module of Kaehler differentials, every p-independent collection extends to a p-basis and p-bases exist, and a subset is a p-basis exactly when its differentials form a K-basis of the differential module (statement lines 11362-11377). The proof is a 36-line argument of four independent parts (proof lines 11380-11415): (2) implies (1) by applying the derivations theta_i dual to the x_j to a minimal relation and producing a relation of strictly smaller total degree, which is a contradiction; (a) implies (b) by presenting K as kK^p[X_i]/(X_i^p - x_i^p) and reading off the differentials; p-independence extends to a maximal p-independent set by Zorn's lemma, and a maximal p-independent set is shown to be a p-basis by adjoining a hypothetical element outside the subfield generated by kK^p and the x_i and contradicting maximality; finally (b) implies (a) closes the circle using the equivalence already proved. The two places where the reader has to bring in background are the existence of the derivations theta_i and the presentation of K over kK^p, both of which are standard for fields of characteristic p and neither of which is proved here.

items.title: Regular systems of parameters in power series rings over a field and over a Cohen ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma records the four standard consequences of choosing a regular system of parameters in a power series ring, once over a field and once over a Cohen ring: any two such systems present the ring as a power series ring on the system, any part of a system can be completed and the quotient is again a power series ring over the same base, and the same two statements hold for the system starting with p over a Cohen ring (statement lines 9736-9751). The proof is a 13-line argument (proof lines 9754-9766) which for (1) compares the two complete local rings by the surjections on the quotients by powers of the maximal ideal, for (2) extends the given partial system to a full one and reduces to (1), and then declares for (3) and (4) that the proofs are exactly the same. The decisive step is the passage from the identification of all the infinitesimal quotients to an isomorphism of complete rings, which is the completeness hypothesis doing real work; the author states it in one sentence and leaves the rest of the (3) and (4) cases by symmetry.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the basic comparison between reflexivity and torsion freeness over a domain (statement lines 5165-5174): a reflexive module is torsion free, and for a finite module M the natural map j to the double dual has torsion kernel and cokernel and is injective if and only if M is torsion free. items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a closure property for the near-projective modules of the section: in a short exact sequence 0 to K to P to M to 0 with P projective and M annihilated by the ideal I up to the near-projective condition, the kernel K is itself I-projective. The statement is stated for an arbitrary short exact sequence with P projective (statement lines 17809-17816). The proof is a 6-line argument (proof lines 17819-17824) which reads the class of the given extension as the image of the identity of K under the connecting map into Ext^1(M, K), uses the hypothesis that this class is annihilated by every a in I, and concludes that multiplication by a on K factors through P, which is the definition of I-projectivity. What has to be seen is the identification of the extension class with the image of the identity, and the translation of the annihilation statement into the factorisation property; both are standard but neither is spelled out.

items.title: The image of the spectrum map of a split algebra is the intersection of the closed sets cut out by the evaluation ideals
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the image of the spectrum map for a quotient S of a polynomial ring whose ideal contains, for each variable, a polynomial that is a product of linear factors with coefficients in the base ring (statement lines 4613-4628). For every choice of one root per variable one gets an evaluation map of R[T_1, ..., T_n] to R, hence an ideal J of the choice, and the assertion is that the image of Spec(S) to Spec(R) is exactly the closed subset defined by the intersection of all these ideals. The author's proof is one line plus a hint (proof lines 4631-4633): the hint is that the vanishing set of an intersection of ideals is the union of the individual vanishing sets. A reader has to combine that with the fact that a prime containing the intersection of finitely many ideals contains one of them, and with the identification of the fibre of the spectrum map over a prime with the evaluations that land in that prime. The lemma is used later in the section precisely to test set-theoretic properties of the map, so the identification is the content.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that m-pseudo-coherence is preserved by derived pullback along a morphism of ringed sites (statement lines 12109-12116). Its content is a two-stage localisation followed by one computation with a distinguished triangle (proof lines 12118-12174): the locality lemmas reduce to the case of final objects, a strictly perfect witness F^bullet -> E is localised to a single one, and after applying Lf^* the cone C with H^j(C) = 0 for j >= m must have H^j(Lf^*C) = 0 in the same degrees, which is the vanishing property of a left derived functor; strict perfectness of f^*F^bullet supplies the witness. H2: two reductions and one triangle computation, all written out.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces the cohomological descent distinguished triangle K -> Ri_*(K|_Z) + Rb_*(K|_{X'}) -> Rc_*(K|_E) for the blow-up square of a finite type quasi-coherent ideal and torsion coefficient complexes (statement lines 23314-23331). The proof (proof lines 23333-23385) represents the three derived pushforwards by explicit complexes — using exactness of i_*, an injective resolution for b and proper base change for c — and then verifies the resulting sequence of complexes is short exact by a stalk computation at a geometric point, with the two cases x not in Z (where the blow-up is an isomorphism nearby) and x in Z (where the comparison of complexes is an isomorphism). H2: an explicit choice of representatives followed by a two-case stalk check.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes finiteness of H^q_etale(X, underline M) for a constant coefficient sheaf on a separated finite type curve over an algebraically closed field, in the two cases named in the statement (statement lines 15817-15829). H2: several standard reductions, each written out, none of them a long construction.

items.title: Under the Zariskian section conditions of Gabber, sections of an etale sheaf over X agree with sections over the closed subscheme Z
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is Gabber's h^0 comparison: under the two Zariski section conditions (1) and (2) on Z subset X, the natural map Gamma(X, F) -> Gamma(Z, i^{-1}_{small}F) is bijective for every etale sheaf F (statement lines 14974-14987). The proof has two non-formal halves (proof lines 14989-15069): injectivity is a stalk computation in which the sheaf condition on the etale covering U -> U_0 gives injectivity of F(U_0) -> F(U), and surjectivity requires producing the etale local descriptions of t, refining the coproduct of the U_j to a finite surjective cover X' -> X, lifting the pullback t' by assumption (2), and descending along X' x_X X' via the finite-descent remark. H2: two explicit constructions with a finite cover and a descent step, all written out by the author.

items.title: Proper pushforward commutes with the k-cycle class of a coherent sheaf whose support has dimension at most k
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a proper f : X -> Y and a coherent F whose support has delta-dimension at most k, the cycle class of the pushforward equals the pushforward of the cycle class, in the form f_*[F]_k = [f_*F]_k, with the corresponding statement for a closed subscheme (statement lines 1991-2012, tag 02R6). The proof is a real reduction rather than a citation: it factors F through its support, reduces to a dominant proper morphism, shows that the generic fibre over any relevant component of Y is finite and shrinks to make f finite and affine, and then compares the multiplicities through the pushdown formula for a finite ring map. The reduction and the multiplicity comparison are both carried out in the span, so the claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the group of k-cycles of a scheme locally of finite type over S with K_0 of the quotient of the coherent sheaves of dimension at most k by those of dimension at most k-1 through two explicit maps (statement lines 3756-3779, tag 02S9). One direction is a formal additive-function argument, but the other needs real work: the proof reduces an arbitrary coherent F by cutting out the part supported in dimension at most k-1, filters the stalks at the generic points of the components of [F]_k, glues the resulting kernels back into coherent subsheaves, and then replaces each graded piece by an ideal sheaf inside O_{Z_i} so that two comparison quotients land in Coh_{<=k-1}(X). This multi-step gluing goes well beyond a routine citation, so the claim is H2.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for any coherent module F on projective n-space over an infinite field, a nonzero section s of O(1) such that multiplication F(-1) -> F is injective with cokernel of the form i_*G for the associated hyperplane i : H -> P^n. The proof first computes the map on D_+(T_0) as multiplication by a_0 + sum a_i x_i on the finite module M, then shows injectivity by choosing that element outside all associated primes of M, which is possible because Ass(M) is finite and each prime cuts out a proper k-subvector space, so a finite union of proper subspaces cannot exhaust the infinite field (proof lines 6513-6543). items.title: Surjectivity of flat pullback on Chow groups for a morphism whose restriction to a neighbourhood of every point is a product with affine space
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that pullback along a flat morphism of relative dimension r which is locally a product with A^r over the base is surjective on Chow groups in every degree (statement lines 5650-5660, tag 02TT). The proof is a genuine induction on two parameters: on the dimension of the base, using the product structure over a dense open together with the exact sequence of an open immersion, and then on the number r of A^1 factors, where the remaining case is that of a dominant integral hypersurface whose generic fibre is cut out by a monic irreducible polynomial, giving rational triviality after shrinking the base. Both reductions require the reader to track cycles through open immersions and infinite sums, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A proper morphism carries rationally equivalent cycles to rationally equivalent cycles
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the functoriality statement that a proper morphism preserves rational equivalence, p_* alpha rationally equivalent to p_* beta whenever alpha and beta are (statement lines 3216-3223, tag 02S2). Although the statement looks formal, the proof is a real reduction: it distributes the pushforward over the locally finite family, reduces to a single integral W and its image W', and then distinguishes three dimension cases, the delicate one being dim_delta(W') = k where one must observe that the fibre over the generic point of W' is a proper integral curve over a field, that its closed points correspond to the integral subschemes through which the divisor passes, and that the multiplicity of the image class equals the multiplicity of [Spec(K)] in the pushforward of the principal divisor, which vanishes. The identification of the multiplicities is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma packages the standard construction attached to a rational function on an integral X of delta-dimension n: the closure Y of its graph in X times_S P^1_S is proper over X, is an isomorphism over the open set where f is invertible, the two pullbacks of the standard sections are defined, and the divisor of f on Y and on X is the difference of the two cycle classes (statement lines 2700-2731, tag 02RQ). items.title: The top Chern class of a finite locally free module of rank r caps the fundamental class to the cycle of a regular section
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the top Chern class of a finite locally free module of rank r on a scheme X' of delta-dimension n as the class of the zero scheme of a section whose local ideals are generated by regular sequences of length r: c_r(E) cap [X']_n = [Z(s)]_{n-r} (statement lines 8749-8761, tag 0FA9). The auxiliary claim and the descent are the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Every finite set of elements of a bounded above complex of free modules lies in a bounded subcomplex of finite free modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement takes a bounded above complex F of free R-modules and a finite list of elements f_i in various degrees, and asserts the existence of a bounded subcomplex G of F containing all of them whose terms are finite free (statement lines 38552-38559). The proof is a descending induction on the minimal degree that occurs, and the induction step has to handle two degrees at once: a finite set of basis elements of F^a is chosen to capture the given elements of that degree, and a second finite set of basis elements of F^{a+1} is chosen so that the differentials of the first set land inside the span of the second, which is exactly what makes the glued object a subcomplex rather than just a family of submodules (proof lines 38564-38576). The finite rank and the boundedness of the result come from the finiteness of the two chosen sets and from the induction hypothesis. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012

The proof has to check two distinct and not obviously related conditions for the object N = M tensor^L K, namely the vanishing of the f-localized cohomology in negative degrees, which is computed through the factorization of the derived tensor product along R_f, and the vanishing of the cohomology of the cone of multiplication by f below degree -1, which is computed by writing the cone as a derived tensor product with the cone on K and using the triangle with K[f] and K over fK (proof lines 30054-30079). The two hypotheses on M are used in exactly one place each, and the argument is carried out for an arbitrary test module K, so the reduction is the substantive step. The counted span refers to one lemma and one section of this chapter; the computations themselves are inside the span.

items.title: Splitting a ring over the open pieces of a finitely generated ideal by adding one surjective component
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is a glueing lemma over the open pieces of a finitely generated ideal: given a ring map A -> C that becomes localization at an idempotent after inverting each element of a finitely generated ideal I, it produces a surjection A -> C' such that A_f -> (C times C')_f is an isomorphism for every f in I (statement lines 31983-31990). The proof is a concrete calculation with idempotents: it lifts the idempotents e_i of the localizations to elements a_i of A satisfying a_i^2 = f_i^n a_i for a common exponent, uses the compatibility of the idempotents over the pairwise localizations to force f_i^n a_j into the ideal of a_i after enlarging the exponent, defines C' as the quotient by the ideal generated by the a_i, and checks the splitting at each generator before transferring to all of I (proof lines 31992-32026). The non-routine part is exactly the exponent bookkeeping that makes all the a_i comparable at once. The final transfer uses a labelled lemma of another chapter as a pointer for the glueing of the local isomorphisms; the construction and all computations are inside the counted span.

items.title: Lifting an inverse system of objects of D(Ab) to a system of complexes whose transition diagrams commute strictly
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement compares an inverse system (K_n) of objects of the derived category D(Ab), which is not the same thing as a system of complexes, with a system of complexes whose transition diagrams commute strictly; it asserts that every such inverse system in D(Ab) can be represented by an object of D(Ab(N)) together with levelwise isomorphisms making the diagrams commute in D(Ab) (statement lines 23334-23348). items.title: Power torsion depends only on the closed subset: a module is I-power torsion exactly when its support lies in V(I)
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring R with a finitely generated ideal I, the subcategory of I-power torsion modules depends only on the closed subset Z = V(I) of Spec(R), and that a module is I-power torsion exactly when its support is contained in Z (statement lines 24085-24092). The proof is an elementwise computation that has to go through the localizations twice: an element annihilated by a power of I dies in the localizations at the elements of I and hence at the primes outside V(I), while conversely vanishing at all those primes must be lifted back to vanishing at the finitely many localizations M_{f_i}, which is where the finite generation of I is used, and only then do the annihilating exponents appear (proof lines 24095-24101). The last line identifies the power torsion submodule as the kernel of the map to the product of the localizations outside Z, and the dependence on the closed set rather than on the ideal follows from that description. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.

items.title: In the random subgraph of a high-dimensional product graph there is typically no component whose order lies in the interval from two to d to the twentieth
items.author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
items.work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the gap lemma for component orders (author lemma at source lines 514-516, label lem:component-gap): with high probability the random subgraph has no component whose order lies between 2 and d^20. The proof (source lines 518-532) is a first-moment computation whose content is the combination of two estimates: the expansion bound e_G(K,K^c) >= 0.9kd for sets of that size, coming from the author's displayed expansion estimate, and the rooted-tree bound that turns the event of K being a component into the product n(ed)^{k-1}(1-p)^{0.9kd}, after which the author substitutes 2 <= k <= d^20, n(1-p)^d <= d^{1/50} and d = Theta_M(log n) to reach n^{1-0.8k} and concludes with a union bound over k (proof lines 525-532). The estimates are quantitative and are the substance of the argument. H2.

items.title: A strict Hall inequality for the auxiliary bipartite graph of the Gallai-Edmonds decomposition
items.author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
items.work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the strict Hall inequality for the auxiliary bipartite graph of the Edmonds-Gallai decomposition (author lemma at source lines 1073-1079, label lem:strict-hall). The proof (source lines 1081-1090) is a self-contained matching argument: it extracts, for every vertex v of a component D of the D-part, a maximum matching that leaves v unmatched and therefore has no edge from A into that particular component (proof line 1082), uses the remaining edges to match A into the other components and so obtains a matching saturating A in the graph with one component deleted (proof lines 1083-1085), and then upgrades Hall's inequality to a strict one by noting that equality would break Hall after deleting any neighbour (proof line 1086). The closing count converts the strict inequality into the bound on the number of components of the auxiliary graph (proof lines 1088-1089). The argument is short but every step is used. H2.

items.title: The decomposition of the pushforward of the intersection cohomology sheaf of the regular part of a quiver variety
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.work: Quiver Varieties and Branching
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the branching theorem of the paper (author Theorem at source lines 2714-2731, label thm:branch): the pushforward of the intersection cohomology sheaf of the regular part of a quiver variety decomposes into a direct sum over v' of the Hom space between an irreducible integrable highest weight module of the Levi subalgebra and one of g, tensored with the IC sheaf of the regular part of M_0, plus IC sheaves of non-regular strata. The proof (source lines 2733-2803) is the paper's main technical argument: it first identifies the local-system decomposition of the top-degree homology of the fibre on the regular strata of both moduli spaces, using that the homology there is an irreducible integrable representation with a prescribed highest weight vector (proof lines 2734-2755), then rewrites an arbitrary stratum containing a given IC sheaf as a product stratum and pushes the exterior product through two finite birational morphisms, which is what forces all remaining summands to come from non-regular strata unless the second factor is trivial (proof lines 2757-2776), and finally reads off the restriction identity and identifies the multiplicities with the Hom spaces, using that the summands for different v^0 are non-isomorphic (proof lines 2777-2803). The argument is a chain rather than a single trick, and its middle step is the finite-birational-morphism computation. H2.

items.title: Stabilization of the dimension vectors by the stability parameter: the face structure of a zeta-bullet-stable module
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.work: Quiver Varieties and Branching
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the face lemma on the stabilization of dimension vectors for zeta-bullet-stable modules (author Lemma at source lines 999-1019, label lem:face), and its proof (source lines 1021-1150) is by far the longest of the paper's second section. The argument is organised as a double induction on the rank of a face of the stability parameter and on the dimension vector, with the reduction to the extremal points of the face relying on the author's monotonicity statement for dimension vectors along a wall, which the author attributes to section 5 of the cited paper (proof lines 1021-1150); at the extremal point the module is decomposed into polystable components and each component is matched against the author's earlier criterion for the non-vanishing of the regular part (label thm:Rudakov). The lemma is the technical device on which the author's later description of the strata rests, and its proof is a genuine multi-step induction rather than a citation. H2.

items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.work: Quiver Varieties and Branching
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the comparison of the homology of the fibre over a point for two different stability parameters, together with the identification of the top-degree homology with a specific weight space of V(w) (author Lemma at source lines 2966-2981). The proof (source lines 2986-3000) is short but depends on a precise reduction: both fibres are written as products of a factor over the origin in a smaller moduli space and a factor in the normalised moduli space that does not depend on the stability parameter (proof lines 2987-2991), and the remaining factor is handled by the homotopy equivalence of the inclusion of the fibre over the origin, together with the fact that the smooth structure of that moduli space is independent of the generic parameter zeta (proof lines 2993-2997). The last step uses that the top-degree homology is the weight space to reach the module statement. H2.

items.title: Description of the strata of the quiver variety for a generic stability parameter in the parabolic Levi example
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.work: Quiver Varieties and Branching
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the author's description of the strata of the quiver variety in the parabolic Levi-factor example (author Proposition at source lines 1656-1672, label prop:Levi): every stratum is the product of a regular part of a smaller quiver variety with a stratum of the W = 0 moduli space for the subgraph I^0, and the non-vanishing of that regular part forces the inequalities h_i . (w - v^0) >= 0 for i in I^0. The proof (source lines 1680-1708) has to pass from a closed point of the moduli space to a representative polystable module, use the constraint zeta^bullet . v' = 0 to locate the support of its W = 0 component, and then write down the explicit two-step complex built from the maps alpha_i and beta_i to extract the positivity statement of part (2) (proof lines 1702-1708). Part (2) is not proved from scratch but made apparent through that complex, which the author attributes to formula (4.2) of the earlier paper; the complex itself is displayed verbatim in the counted proof. H2.

items.title: The root spaces of the extended graph form the irreducible integrable highest weight module of highest weight w
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.work: Quiver Varieties and Branching
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the identification of the direct sum of the root spaces of the extended graph with an irreducible integrable highest weight representation and the resulting root-multiplicity formula (author Lemma at source lines 1184-1196, label lem:root). The proof (source lines 1198-1217) does two things: it reads off the commutation relations with the raising operators from the definition of the extended graph, and then shows that the prescribed root space is spanned by iterated brackets of the lowering operators with f_infinity, using a displayed bracket identity that moves f_infinity across the bracket up to a sign (proof lines 1203-1211). That spanning statement is what makes V a highest weight module with highest weight vector f_infinity; integrability and the translation of root multiplicities into weight multiplicities are attributed to two specific sections of Kac's book (proof lines 1213-1215). The step with content is the bracket identity and the spanning conclusion, not the citation. H2.

items.title: The fibre-dimension bound and the semismallness of the projective morphism between two quiver varieties
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.work: Quiver Varieties and Branching
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the pair of results that make the morphism between the two quiver varieties well behaved (author Proposition at source lines 1553-1575, label prop:semismall): the fibre over a point of a stratum has dimension at most half the difference of the dimensions of source and stratum, and the map restricted to its image is semismall for the stratification by the images of the strata. Part (1) is a strengthening of a result proved in the cited paper under the extra hypothesis that the regular part of the target moduli space is non-empty, and the content is the author's observation that the original proof works without it, the mechanism being that the fibre of the lifted map over the origin sits inside an affine algebraic manifold with the trivial factor removed (proof lines 1578-1586). Part (2) then combines the fibre-bundle property of the restrictions with the dimension bookkeeping forced by part (1) (proof lines 1588-1593). H2.

items.title: For a regular module the images of the moment maps fill the vertex spaces exactly when the module is zeta-stable
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.work: Quiver Varieties and Branching
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the criterion for the vanishing of the cokernels of the moment maps on a regular point of the quiver variety (author Lemma at source lines 2434-2438, Section 4). The proof (source lines 2445-2457) is short but not routine: after the forward direction is attributed to the author's lemma on the surjectivity of beta_i, the reverse direction has to build the Jordan-Holder filtration supplied by the author's Rudakov theorem, then argue on the associated graded object that the submodule V^{k_W+1} would contradict zeta-stability unless k_W = N, so that for N different from 0 the W-component of gr_0(B,a,b) vanishes and the graded object is a simple module for the subgraph I^0 extended by zero (proof lines 2451-2455); regularity then pins that simple module to some S_i, which makes the corresponding beta_i non-surjective. The statement is the technical heart of the author's description of the strata of M_{zeta^bullet} in the Levi-factor example. H2.

items.title: Partitioning the disjointness graph of the subtrees of a tree into two comparability graphs
items.author: Andr\'as Gy\'arf\'as, M\'arton Marits, G\'eza T\'oth
items.work: Partitioning perfect graphs into comparability graphs
items.difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2408.13523v2 的 Theorem co-triangulated（源 313-316 行，证明 319-373 行，共 55 行）：对共三角图的集合（即树 T 的子树系的互斥图）证明 c(G)<=p(G)<=2，也就是要把它的边集恰好剖成两个可比图。关键操作不是例行核验：作者必须先把结点按「离根最近」给每个子树定出根，再用「B 的根到 r 的路径是否含 A 的根」造出第一个偏序，并验证传递性时用到「B 的根把 A 与 C 分开因而二者互斥」这一几何事实（324-334 行）；随后还要处理第一个偏序下不可比的互斥对，为此引入 N^{<=N} 上的字典序与顶点标号 ψ，并证明第一个偏序恰好等于标号的前缀关系（337-351 行），再用前缀性质证明第二个偏序的传递性并推出结论的两棵子树互斥（353-371 行）。难点在于两个偏序必须互补地覆盖互斥图的所有边，这要求对同一树结构下的两类互斥对给出两套相容的序，任何一套的传递性都需要独立论证；原文位置在证明的 329-334 行与 358-371 行。

items.difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2408.13523v2 的 Theorem loglog（源 432-433 行，证明 438-453 行，共 16 行）：对 n 个基点确定的区间图 G_n 证明 c(n) >= (1/2) log log n。关键操作不是例行核验：必须先把覆盖 G_n 的 t 个可比子图各自取传递定向，再把每条相切边编码成「所在子图的编号 + 定向方向」这一类型，从而得到 2t 个类型（440-445 行）；关键一步是证明共享同一个中间区间的两条相切边 {[i,j],[j,k]} 与 {[j,k],[k,l]} 类型必定不同，否则单一子图的传递性会给出连接两个互斥区间 [i,j] 与 [k,l] 的边，而这条边在 G_n 中并不存在（447-449 行）；最后把类型读成双移位图 DS_n 的一个 2t 色正常着色，再用 χ(DS_n) >= log log n 收尾（451-453 行）。难点在于把「边集被可比子图覆盖」这一结构性质精确转译成一个着色的存在性，且类型数必须恰好是 2t；原文位置在证明的 440-445 行与 447-449 行。

items.title: An ideal in an absolutely integrally closed ring gives a henselian pair under two conditions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a sufficient condition for an ideal in an absolutely integrally closed ring to define a henselian pair: the ideal must lie in the Jacobson radical and the quotient map must induce a bijection on idempotents (statement lines 3619-3627). The proof is the longest of this batch at 41 lines (proof lines 3630-3670) and it is a real construction: from a factorisation of a monic polynomial modulo I into two monic factors generating the unit ideal, it produces the idempotent of the quotient A/I[T]/(f) corresponding to (1, 0), writes f as a product of linear factors with roots a_i in A using absolute integral closedness, evaluates the idempotent at each root to get idempotents e_i of A/I, lifts them to idempotents of A by the hypothesis on idempotents, decomposes A as a finite product of rings in which each e_i is 0 or 1, and then lifts the factorisation inductively using the fact that one factor becomes a unit at the roots in question. The decomposition into a product of rings is stated with the author's own note that some details are omitted, and the induction on the degree is carried out in full.

items.title: Finitely presented relative to the base survives an arbitrary base change of the base ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the base change permanence of the relative notion of finite presentation of the same section: if M is an A-module finitely presented relative to R and R to R' is an arbitrary ring map, then the base changed module M tensor over R with R' is finitely presented relative to R' (statement lines 21047-21055). The proof is a 13-line presentation (proof lines 21058-21070): it chooses a surjection from a polynomial ring over R onto A and a presentation matrix for M over that polynomial ring, tensors the whole presentation with R', and observes that a presentation over a polynomial ring over R remains a presentation over the polynomial ring over R' with the same number of generators and relations. The point that makes the argument short is that the base change of R[x_1, ..., x_n] is R'[x_1, ..., x_n] and that tensoring with R' is right exact, so nothing has to be added to the presentation; this is exactly why the relative notion is base change stable while the absolute notion is not.

items.title: A reformulation of the G-ring condition through the formal fibres of quotients
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma reformulates the G-ring condition for a Noetherian ring: instead of asking that every local ring have geometrically regular formal fibres, it is enough to check, for every pair of primes q inside p, that the algebra (R/q) at p completed, tensor over R/q with the residue field of q, is geometrically regular over that field (statement lines 12193-12201). The proof is eight lines (proof lines 12204-12211) and consists of the displayed identification of the two algebras over the residue field of q, together with the sentence that the result follows from it. The content is the base change computation: completing R at p and then reducing modulo q gives the same algebra as first dividing by q and then completing at the image prime, and the tensor factor over the residue field is the same on both sides, so testing one family of algebras is testing the other. The author leaves the identification itself to the reader; the surrounding discussion of the chapter is what fixes the meaning of G-ring and of geometric regularity used here.

items.title: Torsion freeness is detected on localisations at maximal ideals
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma replaces the global condition of being torsion free over a domain by a local one: a module is torsion free if and only if all of its localisations at maximal ideals are torsion free over the corresponding local rings (statement lines 4850-4855). The author's proof is a hint rather than a full argument (proof lines 4858-4861): it says to use that localisation at a multiplicative set preserves torsion freeness, together with a criterion of the Algebra chapter which states that a module is zero if and only if all its localisations at maximal ideals are zero. A reader has to combine the two: an element of M annihilated by a nonzero ring element survives as such after localising, so torsion freeness of all localisations forces there to be no such element and conversely torsion freeness of M passes to localisations by the preceding statement of the section. The proof is recorded here with its hint intact and no step added to it.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the transitivity statement for the relative notion of finite presentation: for finite type maps R to A to B, a B-module M that is finitely presented relative to A is finitely presented relative to R as soon as A is of finite presentation over R (statement lines 21101-21105). As in the base change statement of the same block, the work is the construction of the matrix and the claim that it presents M over a polynomial ring over R; the author states both without verifying the block computation.

items.title: Extending a derivation to a completion, to a localisation, and to a finite type extension after multiplying by a power
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma has two easy parts and one hard part: a derivation D of a ring extends canonically to the I-adic completion, extends uniquely to any localisation, and, for a finite type extension R inside R' with R_g isomorphic to R'_g for a nonzerodivisor g of R', some power g^N times D extends to R' (statement lines 11753-11765). The proof is a 28-line argument (proof lines 11768-11795). For (1) it uses the Leibniz rule to see that D maps I^n into I^{n-1}, which gives compatible maps on the quotients R/I^n and hence a limit derivation; the verification of the derivation axioms is explicitly omitted. For (2) it gives the standard formula D(r/s) = D(r)/s - rD(s)/s^2 and leaves the axiom check to the reader. The hard part (3) chooses generators x_i of R' over R, picks N with g^N x_i in R, extends g^{N+1}D first to R_g by (2), computes g^{N+1}D(x_i) by the Leibniz rule, shows the result lies in R' for every generator, and finishes by checking the formula on monomials, which is what turns a statement about generators into a statement about all of R'.

items.title: The dual of a finite I-projective module is I-projective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a closure property for the near-projective modules of the section: the dual of a finite I-projective module over a ring is again I-projective (statement lines 17826-17830). The proof is a 12-line argument (proof lines 17833-17844) which chooses a surjection from a finite free module onto M, dualises it to an injection of M dual into the free module, and then uses the description of I-projectivity through the Ext class of that surjection: since the class is annihilated by I, multiplication by a on M factors through the projection, and taking duals shows that multiplication by a on M dual factors through the inclusion of M dual into the free module, which is exactly I-projectivity of M dual. What has to be seen is the passage from the factorisation over M to the factorisation after dualising, and the choice of the presentation, both of which the author states in one sentence each.

The author closes with an induction on the number of generators whose details are omitted. The content is therefore the two-element case, which is carried out completely; the passage to an arbitrary finite set of generators is the part the author leaves out.

items.title: The evaluation map of a module into its double dual is injective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for an arbitrary module M over a ring the evaluation map into the double dual with respect to the Pontryagin dual by Q/Z is injective (statement lines 13803-13806). The proof is a 9-line argument (proof lines 13809-13817) which uses that Q/Z is an injective abelian group: for a nonzero x in M one takes the cyclic subgroup it generates, produces a nonzero homomorphism from that subgroup to Q/Z that does not annihilate x, extends it to all of M by injectivity, and reads off that the evaluation of x at that extended homomorphism is nonzero. The two steps that carry the content are the existence of a nonzero map on the cyclic subgroup, which is a statement about Q/Z being divisible with enough elements, and its extension along the inclusion, which is the injectivity of Q/Z in the category of abelian groups. Both are standard and neither is proved here, but the argument is complete and short.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes three facts for the inclusion i : Z -> X of a closed subset: that i_* lands in D_Z(O_X), that i_* : D(O_X|_Z) -> D_Z(O_X) is an equivalence with quasi-inverse i^{-1} = R-H_Z on D_Z, and that i_* composed with R-H_Z is right adjoint to the inclusion D_Z(O_X) -> D(O_X). items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves (f^*L_1 ... f^*L_d . Z) = deg(f|_Z : Z -> f(Z)) (L_1 ... L_d . f(Z)) for a morphism of proper schemes over k and an integral closed subscheme Z of dimension d. The proof computes the left side as the coefficient of n_1...n_d in an Euler characteristic, rewrites it as the alternating sum of the chi(X, R^i f_*O_Z tensor L^{n}) using a cited Euler-characteristic morphism lemma and the projection formula, and splits into two cases (proof lines 10492-10508). H2: the generic-finiteness and length identification together with the higher-direct-image vanishing are the non-routine steps.
