items.title: The top cohomology of a pseudo-coherent complex with bounded cohomology is finite type and finitely presented in the next degree
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma extracts finiteness statements from pseudo-coherence: if a complex K is m-pseudo-coherent and has no cohomology above m, then the module H^m(K) is of finite type, and if it has no cohomology above m+1 then H^{m+1}(K) is finitely presented (statement lines 15964-15974). The proof is a 24-line argument (proof lines 15977-16000) which uses the defining property of pseudo-coherence to replace K by a bounded complex E of finite projective modules agreeing with K in high degrees, and then argues by descending induction on the top degree n of E: when n = m the top cohomology of E is the cokernel of a map from E^{m-1} into E^m, and when n exceeds m the vanishing of H^n lets one split E^{n-1} as a direct sum of E^n and a smaller module E' and repeat. Part (2) then reads the finitely presented module off as a cokernel of a map between two finite projective modules. The splitting step is where the vanishing of the higher cohomology is really consumed, and the reduction to E is what makes the induction possible.

items.title: An abelian group is injective exactly when it is divisible
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the injective objects of the category of abelian groups: an abelian group is injective if and only if it is divisible, meaning that every equation n y = x is solvable (statement lines 13552-13556). The proof is the longest of the section at 46 lines (proof lines 13559-13604) and it has two halves. For the necessity, a failure of divisibility produces an element x and an integer n such that the map Z to J sending m to m x does not extend to the group Z[1/n], which exhibits the failure of injectivity. For the sufficiency, one applies Zorn's lemma to the set of partial extensions of a given map A to J, verifies that chains have upper bounds by glueing, and then shows that a maximal partial extension is defined on all of B by picking x outside its domain and treating the two cases: if no positive multiple of x lies in the domain, one extends by mapping x to any element; if a minimal n with n x in the domain exists, divisibility of J supplies z with n z = phi(n x), and the map on the direct sum of the domain with Z given by (a, m) to phi(a) + m z factors through the subgroup generated by the domain and x. Both halves are carried out completely, and the two case splits are where the divisibility hypothesis is consumed.

items.title: A subspace of K to the n meets the base field if and only if it meets every subfield of a filtering family
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a descent statement for linear algebra over a filtering family of subfields: given a family of subfields K_alpha of K with common intersection k, containing k, and filtering downwards, a subspace V of K to the n has nonzero intersection with k to the n exactly when it has nonzero intersection with K_alpha to the n for every alpha (statement lines 11417-11429). The proof is a 24-line induction on n (proof lines 11432-11455). The induction step is the real content: if some nonzero v lies in V cap K_alpha to the n and the last n-1 coordinates are not enough to win, one first chooses alpha with V cap 0 plus K_alpha to the n-1 equal to zero and then replaces v by a scalar multiple so that its first coordinate is 1, which forces V cap K_alpha to the n to equal K_alpha times v; applying the same argument to a subfield K_alpha' contained in K_alpha shows that the remaining coordinates of v lie in every such K_alpha', hence in k by the intersection and filtering hypotheses, and v itself is then a nonzero element of V cap k to the n.

items.title: Koszul regularity is preserved by a flat base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that both versions of Koszul regularity of a sequence of elements, the version relative to a module and the absolute one, survive base change along a flat ring map: if f_1 to f_r is M-H_1-regular or M-Koszul-regular over R and S is a flat R-algebra, then the images of the f_i are N-H_1-regular or N-Koszul-regular for N = M tensor over R with S (statement lines 7336-7347). The proof is eight lines (proof lines 7350-7357) and it is a two-step identification: the Koszul complex of the sequence over S is the base change of the Koszul complex over R, and this identity together with associativity of the tensor product rewrites (K(f) tensor M) tensor S as K(phi(f)) tensor N, which is exactly the complex whose homology has to vanish. What a reader has to check is the second identity, since the first is the definition of the base changed sequence; the author displays the conclusion of both steps and stops there.

items.title: An idempotent modulo an ideal is lifted by an etale ring map that is an isomorphism modulo the ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the second of the two lifting examples of the section: given a ring A, an ideal I and an idempotent ebar in A/I, there is an etale ring map A to A' inducing an isomorphism A/I to A'/IA' and carrying an idempotent e' lifting ebar (statement lines 1784-1789). The proof is a 12-line explicit construction (proof lines 1792-1803): it chooses any lift x of ebar, forms the ring A' obtained from A[t]/(t^2 - t) by inverting the element t - 1 + x, checks that A to A' is etale because the derivative 2t - 1 satisfies (2t - 1)^2 = 1 and so is invertible, identifies A'/IA' with A/I[t]/(t^2 - t) inverted at t - 1 + ebar, and shows that the map sending t to ebar is an isomorphism, which also proves that the class of t in A' is an idempotent lifting ebar. The construction of A' and the etale computation are both carried out in full; the only step a reader has to follow is the identification of the quotient of A' by IA' with the quotient of the polynomial ring.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the naive Koszul module of a finitely generated ideal: the module M generated by elements e_1 to e_n subject to the relations f_i e_j = f_j e_i maps onto the ideal I generated by the f_i, and the kernel of that map is annihilated by I (statement lines 24393-24402). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a dichotomy for a continuous map of topologized abelian groups: if the target is separated and the source is complete, linearly topologized with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero, then either the map is open or some open subgroup of the source has nowhere dense image (statement lines 9089-9099). The proof is a 21-line argument (proof lines 9102-9122): assuming the second alternative fails, the closures of the images of a nested fundamental system of subgroups are open and form a fundamental system in the target, one shows u(N_n) plus M_{n+1} equals M_n, chooses x_1 and then inductively elements y_i and x_{i+1} with u(y_i) + x_{i+1} = x_i, uses completeness of N to sum the y_i and separatedness of M to conclude that x_1 equals u(y), and then repeats the same argument to get M_i = u(N_i) for all i, which is openness. The two places where the topological hypotheses are really used are the formation of the sum of the y_i, which needs completeness, and the identification of the limit, which needs separatedness.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is one of the formal permanence properties of the relative notion of finite presentation introduced in this section: if M is finitely presented relative to R and A to A' is a ring map of finite presentation, then M tensor over A with A' is finitely presented relative to R (statement lines 21072-21077). items.title: Five equivalent characterisations of torsion freeness for a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian domain
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects five equivalent conditions for a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian domain: torsion freeness, being a submodule of a finite free module, having no associated prime other than the zero ideal, having the zero ideal in its support together with property (S_1), and having the zero ideal in its support with no embedded associated prime (statement lines 4883-4893). The proof is a 16-line web of implications (proof lines 4896-4911) which routes through the localisation lemma already proved in the section and through the theory of associated primes: (1) is equivalent to (2) by the preceding statement, (4) is equivalent to (5) by a lemma of the Algebra chapter, (3) is equivalent to (5) immediately from the definition, then localisation of a torsion free module is used to show (1) implies (5), and finally the reverse implication finds, under the negation of (5), an embedding of R/I for a nonzero ideal I into M and hence an embedded associated prime. The step that a reader has to follow is the last one, where a torsion element is converted into an associated prime of M and the embeddedness of that prime is what contradicts (5).

items.title: H1-regularity is inherited by a block of the sequence modulo the ideal generated by the earlier block
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the truncation statement for H_1-regularity: the images of the last m elements of an H_1-regular sequence in the quotient by the ideal generated by the first n elements form an H_1-regular sequence (statement lines 7618-7623). The proof is a 12-line argument (proof lines 7626-7637) whose strategy is to reduce H_1-regularity to the existence of a decomposition of every relation into trivial relations: a relation among the images in A/I is lifted to a relation among all n+m elements in A by using that I is generated by f_1 to f_n, and then the hypothesis that the long sequence is H_1-regular provides a decomposition of that lifted relation into trivial relations, whose image in A/I gives the required decomposition of the original relation. The point that has to be seen is that the lift exists at all, which is the content of choosing coefficients b_i for the f_i; the rest of the proof is taking images.

items.title: An Artin-Rees constant survives a flat base change of Noetherian rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a base change statement for the Artin-Rees lemma: if c works for a map f of finite modules over a Noetherian ring A, then c works for the base changed map over a flat Noetherian A-algebra B with respect to the extended ideal IB (statement lines 283-290). The proof is an 18-line computation with preimages and kernels (proof lines 292-309): it writes the intersection of the image of the base changed map with I^n N tensor B as the image of the preimage under the base changed map, identifies that preimage with the tensor product of the preimage f^{-1}(I^n N) with B by using that B is flat over A, and then applies the hypothesis on c over A. The whole content is the middle step, since flatness is exactly what allows kernels to be computed before tensoring, and the author states that commutation in one sentence.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the quasi-coherent objects of the derived category with the complexes whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent, for a category with chaotic topology whose restriction maps are flat (statement lines 11552-11561). items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies finite locally constant sheaves (of sets, of abelian groups, and of finite type Lambda-modules) on a limit of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with the colimit of the corresponding categories on the approximants (statement lines 12631-12649). The proof (proof lines 12651-12672) reduces to essential surjectivity, trivialises the pullback on a finite affine etale covering of X, approximates that covering at some stage by the affine-sites colimit lemma, and spreads the trivialisation to the approximant; the abelian and Lambda-module cases are identical. H2: one reduction and one spreading argument, written out.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that two natural formulations of the stalk comparison over the strict henselisations are equivalent (statement lines 16531-16548). The proof (proof lines 16550-16579) is a limit computation: separably closedness of K presents the relevant base change as a cofiltered limit of disjoint unions of copies of Spec(K), the compared fibre product is rewritten as the limit of the local fibre products, and the colimit theorem for cohomology of such limits finishes. H2: one limit presentation and one application of the colimit theorem.

items.title: Injectivity and K-injectivity survive restriction of abelian sheaves from the big etale site to a small one, but fail for modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma records that injective and K-injective abelian sheaves on the big etale site stay injective, respectively K-injective, when restricted to the small etale site or pulled back along an object, and that the corresponding statements for modules fail (statement lines 21101-21120). The positive parts (proof lines 21122-21149) are formal from right adjointness of exact functors, with two independent proofs for the pullback case; the negative part (proof lines 21151-21169) is an explicit counterexample over Spec(Z): multiplication by 2 is injective but its pullback is not, and the absence of the dotted arrow exhibits a non-injective restriction of an injective module. H2: formal adjunction arguments plus one explicit counterexample.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma makes a locally constant constructible complex on a connected scheme globally constant on an etale covering, over a finite complex of finite projective modules (statement lines 13849-13856). The proof (proof lines 13858-13878) trivialises the complex on an etale covering, separates the covering into the disjoint open pieces indexed by the isomorphism class of the local model — using that etale morphisms are open and that U_i x_X U_j is empty for non-isomorphic models — and then uses connectedness together with the perfectness criterion to replace the surviving model by a finite complex of finite projective modules. H2: the same grouping argument as for locally constant sheaves, with one extra perfectness input.

items.title: On an integral normal scheme with separably closed function field every separated etale morphism splits as a disjoint union of open immersions and all local rings are strictly henselian
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises integral normal schemes with separably closed function field: separated etale maps split into open immersions, and every local ring is strictly henselian (statement lines 14311-14320). The proof (proof lines 14322-14366) first settles the affine case, where normality forces the idempotents of A tensor_R K to lie in A and the radicial-etale criterion turns the resulting bijectivity of A tensor_R A -> A into an open immersion; the global statement follows by decomposing an affine piece of U along the generic points of its fibre and using separatedness for injectivity, and part (2) is read off from the description of strict henselisations. H2: an explicit affine argument followed by a two-step global reduction.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Zariski-topological companion of Gabber's comparison: sections of a sheaf on a proper scheme over a henselian pair agree with sections on the closed fibre (statement lines 18167-18173). H2: one reduction plus one connectedness argument, written out.

items.title: For a family of finitely generated ideals covering the punctured spectrum of a local domain, the intersection is zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: Let A be a local domain which is not a field and S a set of finitely generated ideals closed under products whose union of vanishing loci is the complement of the generic point; the lemma asserts that the intersection of all members of S is the zero ideal (statement lines 7343-7350). The proof is not a direct computation with the ideals but a compactness argument in the constructible topology: since the maximal ideal is not the generic point, some I in S is contained in the maximal ideal, so the intersection is contained in the maximal ideal; then for a nonzero f in the maximal ideal the closed set V(f) is covered by the V(I) with I in S, and quasi-compactness of V(f) in the constructible topology gives a finite subcover by V(I_1), ..., V(I_n) (proof lines 7353-7362). Because S is closed under products, the product I_1 ... I_n lies in S and V(f) is contained in V(I) for that single I; finite generation of I gives I^m contained in (f) for some m, closure under products gives I contained in (f^2) for some I in S, and then f cannot lie in that I (proof lines 7363-7367). Replacing a finite cover by one ideal through closure under products, and exploiting the two inclusions I^m subset (f) and I subset (f^2), is the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.

items.title: On an integral scheme a perfect complex becomes locally free with constant ranks on an open, and of tor dimension at most one after an admissible blowup
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a perfect complex E on an integral scheme X the lemma produces a nonempty open U on which every cohomology sheaf H^i(E|_U) is finite locally free of constant rank r_i, together with a U-admissible blowup b : X' -> X such that every H^i(Lb^*E) is perfect of tor dimension at most one (statement lines 13105-13113). The proof of the existence of U is genuinely written out despite the author's rhetorical remark: at the generic point eta the complex E becomes a finite complex of finite dimensional vector spaces with zero differentials, with dimensions r_i; the perfect object E' represented by the complex with terms O_X^{r_i} and zero differentials becomes isomorphic to E after pulling back to eta, and the relatively perfect descent lemma then gives an open neighbourhood U of eta on which E and E' agree (proof lines 13116-13127). The blowup assertion is then deduced from the first part and the earlier blowup lemma, using that any nonempty open is scheme theoretically dense in an integral scheme (proof lines 13127-13129). Building the model complex from the dimensions at the generic point and applying relative perfectness to spread it out is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Pullback of a perfect module of tor dimension at most one along a blowup is already derived and stays perfect of tor dimension at most one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts two things about a perfect O_X-module F of tor dimension <= 1 and an arbitrary blowup b : X' -> X: that the derived pullback Lb^*F coincides with the ordinary pullback b^*F, and that b^*F is again perfect of tor dimension <= 1 (statement lines 13223-13230). The proof is short but it is a genuine reduction rather than a citation: it passes to X = Spec(A), takes a two-term presentation 0 -> A^m -> A^n -> M -> 0 of the module M attached to F, recalls that the affine blowup algebra A[I/a] is a subring of the localization A_a, and then uses exactness of localization to transfer the injectivity of A_a^m -> A_a^n down to A[I/a]^m -> A[I/a]^n (proof lines 13233-13242). Locating the argument in the subring A[I/a] rather than in A_a, and noticing that the two-term presentation is what makes both assertions fall out at once, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Existence of a U-admissible blowup on which a perfect module of tor dimension at most one vanishing on U acquires two canonical filtrations with prescribed invertible Fitting divisors
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts the existence of a U-admissible blowup b : X' -> X, for a perfect O_X-module F of tor dimension <= 1 that vanishes on an open U, together with two canonical locally finite filtrations of F' = b^*F whose successive quotients F^i/F^{i-1} and F_i/F_{i+1} are finite locally free of rank i on an effective Cartier divisor D_i (statement lines 13265-13288). The proof has to construct the blowup and the divisors simultaneously: it blows up the product of all Fitting ideals Fit_k(F) (which is a finite product because Fit_k(F) = O_X for k past the number of generators in a local presentation), then uses the invertibility of Fitting ideals after blowing up to reduce to the case where each Fit_k(F) is invertible, where the divisors must satisfy the chain of equalities E_k = D_{k+1} + 2 D_{k+2} + 3 D_{k+3} + ... and are therefore determined uniquely (proof lines 13291-13317). The induction on the number n of generators then replaces the matrix A = f A' by A' with f a nonzerodivisor generating Fit_{n-1}, uses f^{n-k} Fit_k(F') = Fit_k(F)|_V, and finally produces the two filtrations from the two factorizations A = A'f = f A' as the kernel and cokernel of multiplication by f (proof lines 13319-13363). The simultaneous determination of the divisors by the Fitting ideals and the canonical kernel/cokernel description of the two filtrations are not a routine consequence of an existing theorem, so the claim is H3.

items.title: Chern classes, Chern character and Chern polynomials of the derived tensor product of two perfect objects whose Chern classes are defined
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes c_1, c_2 and the general Chern polynomial of a derived tensor product E tensor^L F of two perfect objects whose Chern classes are defined, together with the multiplicativity of the Chern character and the binomial formula P_p(E tensor^L F) = sum_{p_1+p_2=p} binom(p, p_1) P_{p_1}(E) P_{p_2}(F) (statement lines 9600-9622). The proof does not simply quote the vector bundle case: after an envelope reduces both objects to locally bounded complexes of finite locally free modules, the author sets up an abstract combinatorial model of a finite set S with a sign map and a function f into a commutative ring, defines P_p(S, f, epsilon) = sum_{s in S} epsilon(s) f(s)^p, and proves the binomial identity there by reducing to the polynomial ring on the disjoint union S amalg S' and comparing the coefficient of every monomial (proof lines 1024-1063 region, that is proof lines 9637-9653). The c_1 formula is then derived exactly from P_1 and r(E) = P_0(E), and the c_2 formula is checked by expanding P_2 in the same splitting-principle style (proof lines 9654-9676). Organising the computation through the polynomials P_p rather than through individual Chern classes is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Bivariant Chow cohomology of a scheme of finite type over a field with target the point is ordinary Chow homology in complementary degree
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts a canonical identification A^p(X -> Spec(k)) = CH_{-p}(X) for a scheme X locally of finite type over a field k and every p (statement lines 14182-14190). One direction is immediate from capping with the class of the point, but the converse must build a bivariant class out of an arbitrary cycle class alpha: writing alpha = sum n_i [X_i], the author forms the proper map g from the disjoint union of the X_i to X and the flat map f from that disjoint union to Spec(k) of relative dimension -p, multiplies by the integer n_i through a bivariant class nu on the disjoint union, and obtains the required class as g_* o nu o f^*, using that flat pullback and proper pushforward are bivariant operations (proof lines 14193-14224). The mutual inverses are then checked by reducing, through the bivariant-class axiom for the empty class, to integral X' for which the structure morphism is flat of relative dimension dim(X'), so that [X'] = (p')^*[Spec(k)] (proof lines 14227-14240). The construction of the converse class rather than the identification itself is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: After an admissible blowup of a compactification, a morphism of finite type separated over the base extends to a proper morphism from an open containing the original
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated base S, a scheme U of finite type and separated over S, a quasi-compact open V of U with a compactification V inside Y over S, the lemma produces a V-admissible blowup Y' -> Y and an open V inside V' inside Y' such that V -> U extends to a proper morphism V' -> U (statement lines 9761-9769). The proof forms the scheme theoretic image Z of the diagonal morphism V -> Y x_S U, and uses two inputs in sequence: that replacing Y by a V-admissible blowup replaces Z by the corresponding strict transform, which is exactly the strict transform comparison lemma proven just before, and then the Zariski-after-blowup lemma, which allows one to assume Z -> Y is an open immersion (proof lines 9772-9777). If V' denotes the image of Z in Y, then V' -> U is proper because the projection Y x_S U -> U is proper and V' is isomorphic to the closed subscheme Z of that fibre product (proof lines 9778-9781). Chaining the strict transform comparison with the Zariski-after-blowup input to make the image an open immersion is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The category of compactifications of a compactifyable scheme is cofiltered, with the scheme theoretically dense compactifications initial
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma has three parts: cofilteredness of the category of compactifications of a compactifyable X over a quasi-compact quasi-separated S; initiality of the full subcategory of compactifications whose image is dense and scheme theoretically dense; and the statement that a morphism of compactifications f : Xbar' -> Xbar with j'(X) dense in Xbar' satisfies f^{-1}(j(X)) = j'(X) (statement lines 9315-9330). The proof of (a) verifies the three conditions of the definition of a codirected set in the categorical form: a dominating compactification is built as the scheme theoretic image of X under the diagonal map into a fibre product over S (proof lines 9337-9346), and the equalizer of two morphisms between compactifications is shown to be a closed subscheme of the source, hence proper over S, using only separatedness of the target (proof lines 9347-9357). Part (b) replaces a compactification by the scheme theoretic closure of X inside it, and part (c) reduces to a scheme theoretic image statement for a partial section by replacing Xbar' with the closure of j'(X) (proof lines 9360-9377). The construction of the dominating compactification and the equalizer argument are the non-formal steps, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A compactifyable scheme mapping to a separated finite type scheme has a compactification over the target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a morphism f : X -> Y of schemes over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base S with Y separated and of finite type over S and X compactifyable over S, the scheme X has a compactification over Y (statement lines 9386-9392). The proof is short but it must choose the right ambient construction: starting from a compactification j : X -> Xbar over S, one takes the scheme theoretic image Xbar' of the pair (j, f) inside the fibre product Xbar x_S Y, which is proper over Y as a base change of the proper Xbar -> S (proof lines 9395-9400). The open immersion property needs the separatedness of Y: the diagonal-like map (1, f) : X -> X x_S Y is a closed immersion by the semi-diagonal lemma, so the partial-section lemma applied to s = (j, f) and to the projection Xbar x_S Y -> Xbar gives that X -> Xbar' is an open immersion (proof lines 9400-9406). Recognising that the two ingredients are the properness of the base change and the closedness of the semi-diagonal is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Computation of the alternating product of the Chern classes of the exterior powers of a locally free module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally free module E of rank r the lemma computes the alternating product of the total Chern classes of its exterior powers: the product over n = 0, ..., r of c(wedge^n E)^{(-1)^n} equals 1 - (r-1)! c_r(E) plus higher terms (statement lines 12499-12509). The proof applies the splitting principle to replace the computation by one in the polynomial ring on the Chern roots x_1, ..., x_r, writes c(wedge^n E) as the product over increasing multi-indices i_1 < ... < i_n of (1 + x_{i_1} + ... + x_{i_n}), and then takes the logarithm of the alternating product to obtain a double sum over p and n with the sign (-1)^{p+n}/p (proof lines 12512-12527). The key observation is the identity of the last display, namely that the corresponding sum with 1/p! equals the product of (1 - e^{-x_i}); the author notes explicitly that the minus sign in front must be kept, and deduces that the lowest nonzero degree of the alternating product is r, with the value predicted in the statement (proof lines 12528-12538). Setting up the logarithmic computation and matching the coefficients of the resulting exponential product is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The derived limit of the quasi-coherent approximations lies in bounded above quasi-coherent complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of the existence-of-hulls setup, the lemma states that the derived limit K = R-lim K_n = DQ_X(R-lim K_n) of the tower of pseudo-coherent complexes belongs to D^-_QCoh(O_X) (statement lines 8405-8413). The proof has three separate moves: the coherator DQ_X exists for a quasi-compact quasi-separated X and, being a right adjoint, commutes with products and hence with derived limits, which gives the displayed equality; since DQ_X has bounded cohomological dimension it suffices to show R-lim K_n lies in D^-(O_X); and finally one takes an affine open U and uses the exact sequence relating R^1-lim H^{m-1}(U, K_n) and lim H^m(U, K_n) to H^m(U, R-lim K_n), together with the comparison of the cohomology of a pseudo-coherent complex with the cohomology of its cohomology sheaves, to reduce to the boundedness statement (proof lines 8416-8443). That boundedness is proved by a Nakayama argument along the thickening tower: with a_n the largest degree in which H^{a_n}(K_n) is nonzero, the sequence a_1 <= a_2 <= ... is shown to be constant because H^{a_n}(K_{n-1}) = H^{a_n}(K_n) tensor O_{X_{n-1}} and the module H^{a_n}(K_n) is of finite presentation, so vanishing after the thickening forces vanishing (proof lines 8446-8458). The reduction to a boundedness statement and the Nakayama step are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The Chow group in dimension k is the image of the K-group of sheaves supported in dimension at most k inside the K-group of sheaves supported in dimensions k+1 and k
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the map CH_k(X) -> K_0(Coh_{<= k+1}(X)/Coh_{<= k-1}(X)) induced by the from-Chow-to-K construction is a bijection onto the image B_k(X) of the natural map from K_0(Coh_{<= k}(X)/Coh_{<= k-1}(X)) (statement lines 18508-18524). The proof translates rational equivalence into K-theory: it identifies Z_k(X) with K_0 of the quotient category of sheaves supported in dimension at most k compatibly with the map, then takes an element [A] - [B] representing a class that dies in the larger quotient, and unwinds that vanishing through the two parts of the Serre subcategory K-group lemma to produce sheaves A', B' supported in dimension at most k-1 such that [A + A'] - [B + B'] is zero in K_0(Coh_{k+1}(X)), and then a (2, 1)-periodic complex (F, phi, psi) in Coh_{<= k+1}(X) whose H^0 and H^1 are A + A' and B + B' (proof lines 18526-18553). The cycle-theoretic input is then the preceding lemma comparing the k-cycles of the two cohomology sheaves, which yields [A + A']_k ~ rat [B + B']_k and hence that [A] - [B] is rationally equivalent to zero (proof lines 18554-18568). The unwinding of the K-theoretic vanishing into an actual periodic complex is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A canonical isomorphism between the determinant of the outer terms and the determinant of the middle term of a short exact sequence of finite length modules, with three compatibility properties
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs a canonical map gamma from det_kappa(K) tensor det_kappa(M) to det_kappa(L) on nonzero symbols [e_1, ..., e_k] tensor [fbar_1, ..., fbar_m] -> [e_1, ..., e_k, f_1, ..., f_m] and asserts three properties: equivariance for isomorphisms of short exact sequences, a square with a Koszul sign (-1)^{cg}, and agreement with the usual determinant isomorphism for kappa-vector spaces (statement lines 16202-16295, with two commutative diagrams drawn in Xy-pic). The subtlety is well definedness on nonzero symbols: an admissible sequence in K and one in M need not concatenate to an admissible sequence in L, and the value must be independent of the chosen lifts; the author resolves this by observing that a nonzero symbol forces K = <e_1, ..., e_k>, and then transfers each admissible relation separately (proof lines 16298-16319). Surjectivity of gamma is obtained from the generation statement for det_kappa(L) of the previous lemmas rather than from a direct computation (proof lines 16322-16328), and property (2) is a genuine sign computation carried out by applying the admissible relation of type (c) a total of cg times in a prescribed order (proof lines 16340-16362). The claim is a nontrivial diagram-level consistency statement, so it is H2.

items.title: Canonical functorial isomorphism between the determinants of a finite length module over a local ring and over a local quotient-ring extension with the same residue field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a local homomorphism of local rings (R', m') -> (R, m) inducing an isomorphism on residue fields, the lemma asserts that the restriction M_{R'} of a finite length R-module is again of finite length and that there is a canonical isomorphism det_{R,kappa}(M) -> det_{R',kappa}(M_{R'}), functorial in M and compatible with the isomorphism gamma of the additivity lemma for short exact sequences (statement lines 16433-16447). The proof has three parts: the length is preserved, by the algebra lemma on pushdown of a module of finite length; an admissible sequence over R is again admissible over R' because m' maps into m, which is what makes the symbol comparison possible; and the isomorphism is defined by sending the symbol [x_1, ..., x_l] in det_{R,kappa}(M) to the corresponding symbol in det_{R',kappa}(M), after which functoriality and compatibility with gamma are immediate to verify (proof lines 16450-16462). Observing that admissibility is inherited along the map on maximal ideals, which is what makes the symbol-wise definition legitimate, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The determinant module of a finite length module over a local ring is at most one dimensional over the residue field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is short but it is not self-contained: it says 'with notations as above' and asserts that dim_kappa(det_kappa(M)) <= 1 for a finite length module M over a local ring (R, m, kappa), where det_kappa is the determinant module built out of admissible sequences of M modulo the three admissible relations (statement lines 15760-15763). The proof cannot be a formal manipulation of the definition: it must pick an admissible sequence f_1,...,f_l with length_R(<f_1,...,f_i>) = i, then show that an arbitrary admissible sequence e_1,...,e_l either has vanishing symbol [e_1,...,e_l] = 0 (when it does not generate M) or can be transformed into a scalar multiple of the chosen symbol by repeatedly locating the smallest index with f_1 in <e_1,...,e_i>, writing e_i = lambda f_1 + x with lambda a unit, and applying the second and third admissible relations i-1 times to move f_1 to the front, followed by an induction on j (proof lines 15766-15818). The order of the admissible sequences, the unit, and the sign (-1)^{i-1} are exactly the content of the argument, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The exterior product of cycle classes passes to rational equivalence in both variables
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is that the exterior product map CH_n(X) tensor CH_m(Y) -> CH_{n+m}(X x_k Y) is well defined (statement lines 14136-14141), which is not formal because the product is first defined only on cycles: for locally finite families of integral closed subschemes the author forms alpha x beta = sum n_i m_j [X_i x_k Y_j]_{n+m}, which is a cycle (proof lines 14144-14156). The substance is the compatibility with rational equivalence in each variable, and the proof obtains it by realising the product with a fixed class as a bivariant operation: for an integral closed subscheme i : X' -> X of dimension n the flat pullback along X' -> Spec(k) is a class (p')^* in A^{-n}(X' -> Spec(k)) and its composite with i_* is a class c' in A^{-n}(X -> Spec(k)), whose cap product sends an integral Y' of dimension m to [X' x_k Y']_{n+m}, so the construction factors through rational equivalence in the second variable, and symmetry gives the first variable (proof lines 14161-14179). Turning the compatibility into a statement about a bivariant operation rather than checking rational equivalence by hand is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Existence of a finitely generated ideal over which a finitely presented module has a pure spreadout
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of the reference equation, the lemma asserts that for every prime p of A there is a finitely generated ideal I inside pA_p such that over A_p/I the module in question has a pure spreadout (statement lines 7269-7274). The proof first replaces A by its localisation at p, then clears denominators to write N = S^{-1}N' for a finitely presented B-module N', uses that B/mB is Noetherian so that the kernel K of N'/mN' -> N/mN is finitely generated, and picks s in S annihilating K so that, after replacing B by B_s, the elements of S act injectively on N'/mN' (proof lines 7277-7286). The second half is a descent of finite presentation: one chooses a local subring A_0 of A essentially of finite type over Z, a finite type ring map A_0 -> B_0 with B = A tensor_{A_0} B_0, and a finite B_0-module N'_0 with N' = A tensor_{A_0} N'_0, and claims that I = m_{A_0} A works; indeed N'/IN' = N'_0/m_{A_0}N'_0 tensor_{k_{A_0}} A/I is free over A/I, and multiplication by elements of S stays injective after dividing out by the maximal ideal, which gives universal injectivity of N'/IN' -> N/IN (proof lines 7287-7299). Building the finite model over a subring of finite type and recognising that freeness plus one injectivity statement yields the pure spreadout is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A U-admissible blowup makes the strict transform flat and of finite presentation, for an over-S scheme flat over a quasi-compact open U and of finite type over S
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for X -> S of finite type and quasi-separated whose restriction to a quasi-compact open U is flat and locally of finite presentation, some U-admissible blowup S' -> S has strict transform flat and of finite presentation over S' (statement lines 9122-9135). The proof is a reduction: strict transforms remain quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so local finite presentation may be proved first; a finite affine open cover X = W_1 union ... union W_n allows the conclusion for X to be assembled from the conclusions for the W_i once a U-admissible blowup dominating all of them is chosen, using the existence of a common refinement of admissible blowups; and for affine X one embeds X as a closed subscheme of a quasi-compact open V of A^n_S and applies the flattening theorem to the pushforward i_*O_X, then uses that strict transform commutes with pushforward along an affine morphism, which converts flatness of the strict transform of i_*O_X into flatness of i'_*O_{X'} and hence of X' over S' (proof lines 9138-9169). items.difficulty_reason: In the flatness-in-dimension-n situation, assuming a complete devissage of F/X/S over a point s, finite presentation of X over S and of F over X, and flatness in dimensions at least d+1, the lemma asserts that after shrinking S the functor F_d is representable by a monomorphism Z_d -> S of finite presentation (statement lines 7805-7819). The proof runs an induction on the length n of the devissage, whose relative dimensions satisfy d_1 > d_2 > ... > d_n >= 0 because each alpha_k is an isomorphism at the generic point of (Y_k)_s. The key reductions are functorial: since F = i_{1,*}G_1 for a closed immersion i_1 and since pi_1 : Z_1 -> Y_1 is finite, flatness in dimensions at least d of F_T is equivalent to flatness in dimensions at least d of pi_{1,*}G_{1,T} (proof lines 7849-7862). When d_1 > d the author uses the induction-step lemma to make alpha_1 S-universally injective after shrinking, obtains the short exact sequence 0 -> O_{Y_{1,T}}^{r_1} -> pi_{1,T,*}G_{1,T} -> Coker(alpha_1)_T -> 0 with a universally injective first arrow, identifies the flatness loci of the two outer terms, and reduces to Coker(alpha_1), which carries a complete devissage of length n - 1 (proof lines 7864-7882); the case d_1 < d is represented by S itself, and the boundary case d_1 = d is quoted from two further lemmas (proof lines 7884-7891). The functorial reduction along a finite and a closed immersion, and the exact reduction of the flatness locus to the cokernel, are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A U-admissible blowup and a surjective open on which the strict transform of a finite type module becomes finite locally free
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: Under the assumptions that X -> S is affine of finite presentation and flat with geometrically integral fibres, F is of finite type and of finite presentation over U, and F is flat over S at the generic points of fibres over U, the lemma produces a U-admissible blowup S' -> S and an open V of X_{S'} whose preimage is surjective onto S' and on which the strict transform of F is finite locally free (statement lines 8781-8800). The proof is a reduction built on an invariance: the property 'flat at the generic points of the fibres' is preserved by strict transform and is local on S, so the standard successive-blowup reductions apply. The author then defines the rank function r(u) = dim_{kappa(xi_u)}(F_{xi_u} tensor kappa(xi_u)) at the generic point of the fibre over u, proves it locally constant by a fibrewise flat-and-free statement, separates the finitely many level sets U_0, ..., U_c by admissible blowups, reduces to r constant, and finally reduces to S affine with the complement of U cut out by a single nonzerodivisor, where the concluding case is quoted from the affine-space helper lemma (proof lines 8802-8846). The locally-constant-rank argument and the use of disjoint-union blowups to separate the level sets are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Acyclicity and square-zero kernel for the almost blowup square of an equation in two generators
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For an almost blowup square Z, X, X', E attached to two equations f_1, f_2 the lemma asserts that H^p(X', O_{X'}) vanishes for p > 0 and that the restriction Gamma(X, O_X) -> Gamma(X', O_{X'}) is surjective with kernel an ideal of square zero (statement lines 11781-11788). The proof computes first in the universal case A = Z[f_1, f_2], where X' turns out to be the effective Cartier divisor in P^1_X cut out by the global section f_2T_0 - f_1T_1, giving the resolution 0 -> O(-1) -> O -> O_{X'} -> 0 and hence the vanishing and the isomorphism of global sections from the standard cohomology of the projective line (proof lines 11791-11809). The passage to an arbitrary A is a base change argument that invokes the three fibrewise H^1 and H^0 vanishing lemmas (proof lines 11812-11820). The kernel computation is separate and concrete: an element a of A killed on X' is written on the two affine charts as (f_1x - f_2) times a polynomial in x and as (f_1 - f_2y) times a polynomial in y, which yields the chain a = f_2a_0, f_1a_0 = f_2a_1, ..., f_1a_r = 0 and the symmetric chain for the b's, and multiplying two such systems gives aa' = f_1f_2a_0b'_0 = f_1f_2a_1b'_1 = ... = 0 (proof lines 11823-11843). Recognising the two chart presentations as the source of the square-zero statement is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Existence of a generating sequence whose successive quotients are the residue field at a minimal prime of the support of a finite module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite module M over a local Noetherian ring R and a prime q that is a minimal prime of the support of M, the lemma produces elements x_1, ..., x_l of M such that the support of M/<x_1, ..., x_l> misses q while each successive quotient <x_1, ..., x_i>/<x_1, ..., x_{i-1}> is isomorphic to R/q, and it adds that necessarily l = length_{R_q}(M_q) (statement lines 17963-17977). The proof is a clearing-of-denominators argument rather than a citation: it takes a chain y_1, ..., y_l in the localisation M_q with the required successive quotients, lifts f_i y_i to elements z_i of M with f_i not in q, writes q = (g_1, ..., g_t) by Noetherianity, records that g_j y_i lies in <y_1, ..., y_{i-1}> after localising, and clears the finitely many denominators f_{ij} not in q to get f_{ij} g_j z_i in <z_1, ..., z_{i-1}> inside M; the products of the f's times z_i then have the required property because all cleared scalars are invertible at q, and each quotient is a one-generator R-module annihilated by q whose localisation at q is one dimensional over kappa(q), hence is R/q (proof lines 17980-18013). That last identification and the length statement are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The Gysin class at infinity commutes with every bivariant class pulled back from a locally finite type morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Extending the Gysin-at-infinity lemma, the statement says that for a morphism f : Y -> X locally of finite type and a class c in A^*(Y -> X), the class C of that lemma satisfies C o c = c o C in A^*(W_infinity x_X Y -> X) (statement lines 10155-10160). The proof builds the full cartesian diagram of W_Y over W over P^1_Y over Y and W_Y over P^1_X over X, picks beta in CH_{k+1}(W) restricting to the flat pullback of alpha on b^{-1}(A^1_X), observes that c cap beta restricts to the flat pullback of c cap alpha on b_Y^{-1}(A^1_Y), and then compares i_{Y,infinity}^*(c cap beta) with c cap i_infinity^* beta using that c is a bivariant class; this is exactly the identity C cap c cap alpha = c cap C cap alpha, and the same argument repeats after any base change by X' -> X locally of finite type (proof lines 10163-10188). Matching the two compatibilities, one for the class c and one for the defining property of C, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Intertwining of the Gysin-at-infinity class with the localized p-th Chern class under the further hypothesis that the rank of the quotient is less than p
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Building on the localized Chern class lemma, and adding the hypothesis that the restriction of Q to the complement T is finite locally free of rank less than p, the lemma asserts the two equalities C o c_p(Q|_{X x 0}) = C o (Z -> X)_* o c'_p(Q) = c_p(Q|_{W_infinity}) o C for the class C of the Gysin-at-infinity lemma (statement lines 10352-10362). The first equality is the preceding localized Chern class statement, and the second is reduced one cycle class at a time by the bivariant axiom, after assuming the construction compatible with base change; the author then verifies the identity by an explicit chain of eight displayed equalities inside A^*(X), each of which is justified separately: rewriting c'_p(Q) through its restriction to E, identifying the two routes E -> Z -> X and E -> W_infinity -> X, introducing beta with C cap alpha = i_infinity^* beta, using the key computation relating c'_p(Q|_E) to c_p(Q|_{W_infinity}) on i_infinity^* beta, and using twice that c_p(Q) is a bivariant class so that it commutes with i_infinity^* (proof lines 10365-10404). The bookkeeping that pairs each of the eight equalities with the exact lemma that justifies it, under the rank hypothesis, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Localizing the category of compactifications at the right multiplicative system recovers the category of compactifyable schemes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the forgetful functor (X, Xbar) -> X induces an equivalence between the localization of the category of compactifications at the right multiplicative system introduced in the preceding lemma and the category of compactifyable schemes over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base S (statement lines 9475-9484). The content is the third step of an equivalence check: essential surjectivity is immediate, full faithfulness on morphisms requires constructing, for an arbitrary morphism X -> Y of compactifyable schemes, a compactification of Y followed by a relative compactification of X over it, so that the localized morphism is represented (proof lines 9496-9503); and well definedness requires showing that two such representations producing the same morphism X -> Y are equal in the localized category, which uses the right-localization calculus to assume a common refinement and then takes the equalizer of the two proper maps Xbar' -> Xbar'' inside Xbar', a closed subscheme by separatedness of Xbar'' over S, to precompose with a map in the multiplicative system (proof lines 9504-9524). The equalizer trick is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Injectivity of a homomorphism of finite modules over a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring from the determinant at the prime, with the length of the cokernel given by an order
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the chapter's Key Lemma. Under the hypothesis that M and N each admit generating sequences x_1,...,x_l and y_1,...,y_l whose successive quotients are all isomorphic to R/q with dim(R/q) = 1, it asserts that phi : M -> N is injective if and only if phi_q is an isomorphism, and that then length_R(Coker(phi)) equals the order ord_{R/q}(f) of the residue-field element f defined by [phi(x_1),...,phi(x_l)] = f [y_1,...,y_l] in det_{kappa(q)}(N_q) (statement lines 17803-17828). The proof is a genuine double induction: the case l = 1 and the diagonal case phi(x_i) = f_i y_i with f_i not in q are disposed of first (proof lines 17831-17858); then for general l one lets i be minimal with phi(x_1) in <y_1,...,y_i>, rescales the x_j and y_j by a to reach a = 1 and computes length_R(M/M') = (l-1) ord(a) together with length_R(N/N') = (l-i+1) ord(a) to obtain length_R(Coker(phi')) = length_R(Coker(phi)) + i ord(a) while f' = a^i f, and finally uses the admissible relations of the determinant to replace y_1,...,y_l by the transposed sequence, which decreases the invariant i by one (proof lines 17861-17956). The coordination of the determinant condition with the length bookkeeping under a change of generating sequences is the crux of the argument and is not a routine exercise, so the claim is H3.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is stated for a cartesian square of schemes locally of finite type over a fixed base situation, under four hypotheses: f is a local complete intersection morphism for which the Gysin map exists, all four schemes satisfy the equidimensionality conditions of a preceding lemma, the numerical condition n_{x'} - n_{y'} = n_x - n_y holds pointwise, and the local rings of Y' at the images of generic points of X' are Cohen-Macaulay; the conclusion is f^![Y'] = [X'] (statement lines 13642-13668). The final case is a regular closed immersion, where the assertion is quoted from the easier Gysin lemma (proof line 13717). The reduction and the base-change verification of the Cohen-Macaulay condition are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The functor of points where a module is flat in dimensions at least n is unchanged by etale localisation on the source when the etale image contains the relative associated points
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: Inside the flatness-in-dimension-n setup, the lemma compares the functor F_n attached to (f : X -> S, F) with the functor F'_n attached to the etale base change h : X' -> X: F_n is always a subfunctor of F'_n, and the two agree as soon as h(X') contains the relative associated points of F over S (statement lines 7727-7736). The first part of the proof is a dimension comparison: after an arbitrary base change T -> S the non-flatness loci Z in the fibre X_t and Z' in X'_t satisfy Z' = h_t^{-1}(Z) by flatness permanence along the etale h_T, so Z' -> Z is etale and dim(Z') <= dim(Z), which gives F_n inside F'_n (proof lines 7739-7751). The converse is where the associated-points hypothesis is used: assuming F'_n(T) nonempty and a component of Z of dimension at least n, the author picks a generic point xi of that component and a generalisation x of xi that is an associated point of F_t, uses the relative associated points base change lemmas to place x in the image of h_T, and concludes from x not in Z' and flatness permanence that F_T is flat at x, which by the flatness-checking theorem contradicts dim(Z) >= n (proof lines 7753-7774). Locating the generalisation of xi in the image of h_T and turning flatness at x into flatness at xi is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Existence of the localized Chern class as a bivariant class on a closed subscheme, with the pushforward identity onto the zero fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Under assumptions (A0) that the Chern classes of the perfect object Q on W are defined, (A1) that b : W -> P^1_X is an isomorphism over A^1_X, and (A2) that there is a closed subscheme T of W_infinity containing all points over X setminus Z where Q restricts to zero or to a finite locally free module of rank less than p in degree 0, the lemma constructs canonical bivariant classes P'_p(Q) and c'_p(Q) in A^p(Z -> X) satisfying (Z -> X)_* o c'_p(Q) = c_p(Q|_{X x 0}) (statement lines 10203-10231). The proof splits W_infinity as T union E with E the preimage of Z, forms the class C of the Gysin-at-infinity lemma and the class c'_p(Q|_E) of the local construction lemma, defines c'_p(Q) = (E -> Z)_* o c'_p(Q|_E) o C, and then verifies the required identity by a chain of six equalities in the bivariant Chow groups, each justified by a named input: the equality of the composites E -> Z -> X and E -> W_infinity -> W -> X, the comparison of c'_p(Q|_E) with c_p(Q|_{W_infinity}), the commutation of the bivariant class c_p(Q) with i_{infinity,*}, the defining property of C, and finally the identification of W_0 with X (proof lines 10234-10272). items.title: For a cyclic two-periodic complex of a coherent sheaf with k-dimensional cohomology, the k-cycles of the two cohomology sheaves are rationally equivalent
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a coherent sheaf F on X with a two-periodic complex structure (F, phi, psi) as in the cyclic complex equation, assumes the support of F has delta-dimension at most k+1 and the supports of both cohomology sheaves have delta-dimension at most k, and concludes [H^0(F, phi, psi)]_k ~ rat [H^1(F, phi, psi)]_k as k-cycles (statement lines 18416-18445). The proof builds the rational equivalence explicitly: it lists the irreducible components W_j of the support of F of dimension k+1, which form a locally finite family, attaches to each generic point xi_j the determinant f_j of the two-periodic complex at the stalk, which is a unit in the function field R(W_j), and claims the exact cycle identity -[H^0]_k + [H^1]_k = sum (W_j -> X)_* div(f_j) (proof lines 18448-18468). The identity is then verified coefficient by coefficient: for an integral closed subscheme Z of dimension k with generic point xi, the local ring A = O_{X,xi} and the module M = F_xi give dim(Supp M) = 1, the components W_j through xi correspond to the minimal primes q_i of Supp(M), and the two coefficients are computed as -e_A(M, phi, psi) on the left and as the sum of ord_{A/q_i}(det_{kappa(q_i)}(M_{q_i}, phi, psi)) on the right (proof lines 18471-18504). The identification of the two coefficient formulas with the length-determinant proposition is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A locally finite type monomorphism into the spectrum of a limit ring that receives all finite stages is an isomorphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For A = lim A_n a limit of a system of rings with surjective transition maps and locally nilpotent kernels, the lemma states that a monomorphism T -> S = Spec(A) which is locally of finite type and through which every Spec(A_n) -> S factors must satisfy T = S (statement lines 8273-8280). The proof first reduces to a quasi-compact open T' of T containing the common image of the factorizations, so that T may be assumed quasi-compact, and then that T -> S is separated and quasi-finite (proof lines 8283-8294). Zariski's Main Theorem in the form of the quasi-finite separated factorization gives T -> W -> S with W -> S finite and T -> W an open immersion, and writing W = Spec(B) turns the unique factorizations S_n -> T into a diagram A -> B -> lim A_n = A (proof lines 8295-8304). The conclusion is then reduced to the statement that an open U of S containing the image of some S_n -> S must be all of S, which holds because the pair (A, Ker(A -> A_n)) is henselian, so every closed point of S lies in the image of S_n -> S (proof lines 8305-8315). The reduction to a henselian pair statement is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Multiplicativity of the determinant of a (2,1)-periodic complex under the factorization of one of the three endomorphisms
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Under the two kernel/image hypotheses I_alpha = K_{beta gamma} and K_alpha = I_{beta gamma} for every permutation of the three endomorphisms alpha, beta, gamma of a finite length module M over a local ring, the lemma asserts that three triples are exact (2, 1)-periodic complexes and that det_kappa(M, alpha, beta gamma) = det_kappa(I_gamma, alpha, beta) det_kappa(M/K_beta, alpha, gamma) (statement lines 16982-17010). The exactness parts are reductions through specifically constructed short exact sequences 0 -> I_{beta gamma} -> I_gamma -> I_{alpha gamma} -> 0 and 0 -> I_{alpha gamma} -> I_gamma -> I_{beta gamma} -> 0 (proof lines 17016-17030) together with the check alpha(K_beta) subset K_beta, gamma(K_beta) subset K_beta computed as alpha(I_{gamma alpha}) = I_{alpha gamma alpha} subset I_{alpha gamma} = K_beta (proof lines 17033-17041). The determinant identity itself is not a computation with the definition: the author chooses admissible sequences x, y, z generating K_alpha, K_beta, K_gamma together with lifts x-tilde, y-tilde, z-tilde, records the length bookkeeping length_R(I_alpha) = s + t, length_R(I_beta) = r + t, length_R(I_gamma) = r + s and length_R(M) = r + s + t, then characterizes each of the three determinants as the unique scalar in kappa^* in a displayed relation between two symbols and multiplies the three relations, keeping track of the signs (-1)^{r(s+t)}, (-1)^{rt} and (-1)^{rs} (proof lines 17044-17103). The construction of the admissible sequences and the sign bookkeeping are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.

The final identification with the two order functions is the cited additivity formula (proof lines 18641-18645). The manipulation of the length difference through the two injective rescalings is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: An F_p-algebra is absolutely weakly normal if and only if it is perfect
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises perfect F_p-algebras as exactly the absolutely weakly normal ones, which means that the two existence conditions on roots, x^3 = y^2 implies x is a square and y a cube, and l^l x = y^l implies a^l = x and l a = y for a prime l, hold in A (statement lines 12124-12128). One direction is immediate from condition (2)(b) of the seminormal-ring definition, but the converse is a case analysis on the prime p that uses perfectness in a genuinely arithmetic way: for p > 3 one writes p = 2n + 3m with n, m > 0, takes a^p = x and b^p = y, and checks c = a^n b^m satisfies c^{2p} = x^p hence c^2 = x and similarly c^3 = y; for p = 2 one writes x = a^2 and deduces a^3 = y from a^6 = y^2; and for p = 3 one writes y = a^3 and deduces x = a^2 from x^3 = a^6 (proof lines 12136-12146). The second condition is then disposed of by splitting on whether the prime l equals p (proof lines 12148-12152). The representation p = 2n + 3m and the reduction of the root-taking to taking p-th roots are the non-formal steps, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: In the base change situation for the cycle theory, the lemma states two things: for a closed subscheme Z of delta-dimension at most k with base change Z', the delta'-dimension of Z' is at most k + c and [Z']_{k+c} = g^*[Z]_k, and for a coherent sheaf F whose support has delta-dimension at most k the base change F' has support of delta'-dimension at most k + c and g^*[F]_k = [F']_{k+c} (statement lines 15192-15208). The proof reduces the dimension claims to the dimension base change lemma, deduces part (1) from part (2) by applying part (2) to O_Z, whose base change is O_{Z'}, and then proves part (2) coefficient by coefficient: for an integral closed subscheme W of delta-dimension k and an integral W' of delta'-dimension k + c mapping into W, with generic points xi and xi' and local rings A and B, one has F'_{xi'} = B tensor_A M for M = F_xi, so the coefficient of [W'] in g^*[F]_k is length_B(B tensor_A M) while the coefficient in [F']_{k+c} is length_A(M) length_B(B/m_AB), and the two agree by the algebra lemma on the length of a pullback module (proof lines 15210-15251). The reduction of the sheaf statement to a coefficient identity of lengths of a pullback is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Pushing a finite type ideal along an etale ring map into a product involving an ideal of the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For an etale ring map A -> B, a nonzerodivisor a in A facing a finite type ideal J of B whose vanishing locus sits inside V(aB), the lemma asserts that for every prime q of B there is a finite type ideal I of A with V(I) inside V(a) and an element g not in q such that IB_g = JJ' for some finite type ideal J' of B_g (statement lines 8875-8883). The proof localises at g to make B standard etale, hence a localisation C_h of C = A[x]/(f) with f monic of degree d, takes generators h_1, ..., h_n of J over B, uses the condition V(J) inside V(aB) to write a^m as a B-linear combination of the h_i, adds h_{n+1} = a^m, and takes I = Fit_0(C/(h_1, ..., h_{r+1})) as in the preceding fitting ideal trick (proof lines 8886-8897). The conclusion follows because C/(h_1, ..., h_{r+1}) is annihilated by a^m, so a^{dm} lies in I, which gives V(I) inside V(a) (proof lines 8898-8900). Reducing to the standard etale case and reading off the exponent dm from the monic equation are the non-formal steps, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The scheme theoretic image of a quasi-compact morphism after an admissible blowup is the strict transform of the original image
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For morphisms X -> S and Y -> S, an open U of X, a quasi-compact morphism V -> X x_S Y whose composite with the first projection lands in U, and the scheme theoretic image Z of V, the lemma states that for any U-admissible blowup X' -> X the scheme theoretic image of V -> X' x_S Y is the strict transform of Z (statement lines 9727-9737). The proof identifies the strict transform Z' with a closed subscheme of X' x_S Y, so that it suffices to show the scheme theoretic image Z'' of V -> Z' equals Z' (proof lines 9740-9745). Then it uses quasi-compactness, which passes to the base change because X' x_S Y -> X x_S Y is separated as a base change of a proper morphism, to conclude that Z'' and Z agree away from the exceptional divisor, and finishes by observing that the surjection O_{Z'} -> O_{Z''} must be an isomorphism because the structure sheaf of a strict transform has no nonzero sections supported on the exceptional divisor (proof lines 9746-9758). Replacing a comparison of images by an isomorphism criterion for a surjection of structure sheaves with no sections supported on the exceptional divisor is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Existence of the second Adams operation on K_0 of the vector bundles of a scheme, with additivity, pullback compatibility and multiplicativity
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the second Adams operation on K_0(Vect(X)) from the formula psi^2(E) = [Sym^2(E)] - [wedge^2(E)] and asserts three properties at once: well defined additivity on K_0, compatibility with pullbacks, and multiplicativity (statement lines 12752-12763). The additivity step is not a formal consequence of functoriality, because Sym^2 and wedge^2 are not additive on the nose: the author must compute the graded pieces of the filtrations induced by a two-step filtration on a short exact sequence on both Sym^2(F) and wedge^2(F) and observe that the common term E tensor F cancels (proof lines 12775-12800). The multiplicativity step likewise requires the two non-obvious exact sequences relating Sym^2(E tensor F) and wedge^2(E tensor F) to Sym^2/wedge^2 of the factors, with both maps given on elements (proof lines 12809-12828). The argument uses only standard multilinear algebra and quoted material, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Three equivalent conditions for a finitely presented closed subscheme of the source of an almost blowup square to contain the relevant pieces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: Given an almost blowup square and a closed immersion W -> X' of finite presentation, the lemma proves the equivalence of three conditions: that X' setminus E is scheme theoretically contained in W, that the blowup X'' of X in Z is scheme theoretically contained in W, and that the restricted square with E cap W and W is again an almost blowup square (statement lines 11026-11044). The proof is a cycle of implications: from (1) the surjection O_{X'} -> O_W is an isomorphism over the open complement of E, and since the ideal sheaf of X'' in X' is by definition the sheaf of sections of O_{X'} supported on E, this forces (2); (2) implies (3) directly from the definitions; and (3) implies (1) because X'' cap (X' setminus E) is isomorphic to X setminus Z, which is in turn isomorphic to X' setminus E (proof lines 11047-11054). Recognising that the defining property of an almost blowup square, the ideal sheaf supported on E, is exactly the bridge between conditions (1) and (2) is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Independence of the locally constructed bivariant class from the choice of the complementary closed subscheme
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement asserts that the bivariant class P'_p(E_2), respectively c'_p(E_2), constructed in the preceding local lemma does not depend on the choice of the closed subscheme X_1 complementary to X_2 (statement lines 9751-9756). The proof takes a second closed subscheme X'_1 satisfying the same two conditions, notes that X = (X_1 cap X'_1) union X_2 set theoretically, and therefore decomposes any cycle class alpha in CH_k(X) as i_*beta + i_{2,*}alpha_2 with beta supported on the intersection and alpha_2 on X_2; capping the two candidate classes with alpha then both reduces to P_p(E_2) cap alpha_2, or to c_p(E_2) cap alpha_2 in the other case, so the result is visibly independent of the chosen complementary piece, and the same reasoning applies after any base change (proof lines 9758-9771). The decomposition of a cycle class along a cover by two closed subschemes is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
