items.title: Existence of a bivariant class on a closed subscheme characterised by vanishing on the complementary component
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For two closed immersions i_1, i_2 covering X set theoretically, a perfect object E_2 on X_2 whose Chern classes are defined and whose restriction to X_1 cap X_2 is either zero or a finite locally free module of rank less than p in cohomological degree 0, the lemma produces a canonical bivariant class P'_p(E_2), respectively c'_p(E_2), in A^p(X_2 -> X) characterised by two capping properties: on i_{2,*}alpha_2 it returns P_p(E_2) cap alpha_2, respectively c_p(E_2) cap alpha_2, and on i_{1,*}alpha_1 it returns zero, with the same after any base change (statement lines 9694-9724). The proof writes an arbitrary class alpha' in CH_k(X') as i'_{1,*}alpha'_1 + i'_{2,*}alpha'_2 using the exact sequence for a cover by two closed subschemes, notes that alpha'_2 is well defined only up to an element in the image of the pushforward from X'_1 cap X'_2, and shows that setting P'_p(E_2) cap alpha' = P_p(E_2) cap alpha'_2 is independent of that ambiguity precisely because E_2 restricts to zero on the intersection (proof lines 9730-9742). In the rank case the same argument runs because c_p of the restriction vanishes by rank considerations (proof lines 9744-9748). Seeing that the only obstruction to well definedness is the ambiguity coming from the intersection, and that the two hypotheses are exactly what kills it, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The symbol of a discrete valuation ring equals the usual tame symbol
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K and nonzero x, y in K, the lemma identifies the symbol d_A(x, y) with (-1)^{ord_A(x) ord_A(y)} x^{ord_A(y)} / y^{ord_A(x)} modulo the maximal ideal (statement lines 17623-17634). The proof first uses multiplicativity of the symbol to reduce to x, y in A, writes x = t^a u and y = t^b v with t a uniformizer and u, v units, sets l = a + b, observes that t^{l-1}, ..., t^b is an admissible sequence in (x)/(xy) and t^{l-1}, ..., t^a is an admissible sequence in (y)/(xy), and invokes the characterisation of the symbol by a single comparison of two such symbols to obtain the equation defining d_A(x, y) with the sign (-1)^{ab} (proof lines 17637-17650). The last step evaluates the two symbols through the admissible relations to get d_A(x, y) = (-1)^{ab} u^a / v^b mod m_A (proof lines 17651-17654). Choosing the two admissible sequences in the quotients correctly and reducing the comparison to the unit parts is the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Multiplication by a unit acts on the determinant of a finite length module by the l-th power of the unit
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma determines the action of multiplication by a unit u of a local ring on the determinant of a finite length module M: it is multiplication by the image of u raised to the l-th power, where l = length_R(M) (statement lines 16504-16519). The proof is an induction on the length organised through the additivity of the determinant functor: writing det_kappa(u_M) = f_M id, the author takes a short exact sequence 0 -> K -> L -> M -> 0 of finite modules, observes that u_K, u_L, u_M form an isomorphism of short exact sequences, and applies the equivariance property of the determinant isomorphism to get the multiplicativity relation f_K f_M = f_L (proof lines 16522-16528). This makes f_M multiplicative in the length and reduces the claim to modules of length one, where it is trivial (proof lines 16529-16530). Recognising that the equivariance property of the determinant isomorphism is exactly the multiplicativity needed for the induction is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Frobenius-periodic vector bundles glue along the almost blowup square of a single equation, giving an equivalence of categories
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In characteristic p, for the almost blowup square X, X', Z, E attached to one equation f, the lemma states that the functor from F-periodic vector bundles on X to compatible pairs on Z and X' is an equivalence (statement lines 12234-12247). The proof is an algebraisation of the geometry: because all schemes are affine and vector bundles have internal Hom, full faithfulness reduces to the identity colim P tensor_{A, F^N} A = colim P tensor_{A,F^N} A/J x_{colim P tensor A/(fA+J)} colim P tensor_{A,F^N} A/fA for a finite projective A-module P, which is reduced to P finite free, then to P = A, and finally quoted from the fibre-product computation for the structure sheaf (proof lines 12250-12264). Essential surjectivity is turned into an explicit descent problem: given finite projective P_1 over A/J and P_2 over A/fA agreeing after inverting f and killing J, one uses the fibre-product identity A/(J cap fA) = A/J x_{A/(fA+J)} A/fA, the finitely-presented-module-over-a-fibre-product lemma, and the nilpotence of J cap fA to produce N and a finite projective A-module P with the required compatible isomorphisms (proof lines 12267-12299). Recognising that the Frobenius twist is exactly what makes the nilpotent thickening descend is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Frobenius-periodic vector bundles glue along the almost blowup square of an equation in two generators, giving an equivalence of categories
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In characteristic p, for the almost blowup square X, X', Z, E attached to two equations f_1, f_2, the lemma asserts that the functor G from the F-periodic vector bundles on X to the compatible pairs of F-periodic bundles on Z and X' is an equivalence (statement lines 12302-12316). Both directions need a genuine descent argument at the level of the colimit: full faithfulness requires choosing N large enough that maps on Z and X' agree over E, passing to a finite affine cover on which the bundles are free, replacing the colimit of global sections by the fibre product of the three colimits in the almost blowup square, and then gluing the resulting local maps after a further increase of N (proof lines 12319-12353). Essential surjectivity reduces first to the Noetherian case by descending the triple along a finitely generated subalgebra, then to X Noetherian and F = O_Z^{oplus r}, where the author uses that the ideal of E is globally generated by f_1 and f_2, that a globally generated quasi-coherent module on E = P^1_Z has vanishing H^1, and the theorem on formal functions to lift a compatible trivialisation of G along E to a map O_{X'}^{oplus r} -> G that is an isomorphism in a neighbourhood of E, and finally two Zariski glueing arguments (proof lines 12356-12437). The interaction of the Frobenius colimit with the three charts of the almost blowup square is the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The punctured spectrum of a Noetherian local ring is affine if and only if the dimension is at most one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma determines exactly when the punctured spectrum of a Noetherian local ring is affine: it is affine precisely in dimension at most one (statement lines 3348-3353). The counted proof is a real argument of moderate length whose substance is in the converse: the author reduces to a reduced ring, forms the quotient Q = B/A supported at the closed point, applies the snake lemma to multiplication by a well-chosen nonzerodivisor to see that the f-torsion in Q is finite of finite length, propagates that bound by induction to the lengths of the f^n-torsion, concludes that the quotient of Q by f is finite, and then converts the resulting finite ring map modulo f into closedness on spectra, which contradicts the punctured spectrum being an open subset unless the dimension drops all the way to zero (proof lines 3364-3405). It is H2: the author explicitly calls the argument somewhat nonstandard, but every step is carried out in the counted span and the only inputs are standard commutative algebra, so no independent research-level claim is made.

items.title: A closed subscheme is an effective Cartier divisor if and only if it is locally cut out by a single nonzerodivisor
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is the standard local characterization of effective Cartier divisors: for a closed subscheme D of a scheme S, being locally cut out by a single nonzerodivisor is equivalent to the ideal sheaf I_D being invertible (statement lines 2402-2413). The proof is short but runs both directions of the equivalence and needs the dictionary between an invertible ideal sheaf, a free generator f of its sections over an affine open, and the closed subscheme Spec(A/(f)); the passage from I_D restricted to U being O_U to the injectivity of multiplication by f, and the use of quasi-coherence of I_D to identify D cap U, are the non-formal moves (proof lines 2416-2421 and 2426-2432). It is H2: no hypothesis on S beyond being a scheme is used and the argument is a local computation, but no step is replaced by a citation.

items.title: A closed subscheme covered by effective Cartier divisors and a codimension two closed subset is, away from codimension two, an effective Cartier divisor supported on it
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if a closed subscheme Z of a Noetherian scheme is covered by integral effective Cartier divisors D_i together with a closed subset all of whose components have codimension at least two, then a nonnegative combination of the D_i is an effective Cartier divisor contained in Z and isomorphic to Z away from codimension two (statement lines 3075-3100). The counted proof is a genuine local argument: it defines the multiplicities a_i as valuations at the discrete valuation rings of the generic points, shows all but finitely many vanish, and then at an arbitrary point proves the delicate claim that the stalk of the ideal sheaf of Z is contained in the principal ideal generated by the product of the local equations of the relevant divisors, by an induction that peels off prime elements one at a time using that they are pairwise distinct (proof lines 3102-3143). It is H2: the arguments are carried out in full in the counted span and the only cited inputs are the discrete valuation ring property, local equations of Cartier divisors, and the UFD case used for the final existence sentence.

items.title: Depth and nonzerodivisor statements for the pushforward of a quasi-coherent module along a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six statements about the localised pushforward (f_*F)_s of a quasi-coherent module along a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism, at a point s outside the image of f: weak associatedness, associatedness, depth at least two, and then nonzerodivisor and depth statements under the extra hypothesis that F is flat over S (statement lines 938-961). The counted proof has real content in parts (3) to (6): part (3) is proved by the Ext criterion for depth, with flat base change reducing to the spectrum of the local ring and adjunction together with the pulled-back maximal ideal being the whole structure sheaf, and parts (4) to (6) are proved by pushing the short exact sequences cut out by a nonzerodivisor, and then by a regular sequence of length two, through the flat module F and out along the pushforward (proof lines 967-1031). It is H2: the arguments are local algebra of moderate length carried out in the counted span, but there is no independent research-level content, and the author's own parts (1) and (2) are citations rather than proofs.

items.title: For an affine morphism the pushforward is an equivalence from quasi-coherent modules on the source to quasi-coherent modules over the pushforward algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the module version of the affine equivalence: for an affine morphism f with pushforward algebra A, the pushforward gives an equivalence from quasi-coherent modules on X to quasi-coherent modules over A, and a module over A is quasi-coherent over the base exactly when it is quasi-coherent over A (statement lines 1895-1919). The counted proof constructs the quasi-inverse explicitly as a tensor product over the pulled-back algebra, then produces the unit and counit of the adjunction and reduces their verification to a single algebra identity (proof lines 1922-1965). It is H2: the construction is carried out in full and the argument is not a citation, but the last sentence of the statement is disposed of by the author with a citation to a same-chapter lemma, and the verification of the algebra identity is left to the reader with the author's phrase 'We omit the details'; the counted content is therefore the explicit construction of the equivalence and of its comparison maps.

items.title: The composition of two affine morphisms is affine
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The claim is that for affine morphisms f : X to Y and g : Y to Z the composite g composed with f is affine (statement lines 1969-1972). The proof is a four-line verification of the defining criterion: it takes an arbitrary affine open U of Z, uses affineness of g to make the preimage in Y affine, applies affineness of f to that affine open, and rewrites the result as the preimage under the composite (proof lines 1974-1979). It is H2: the argument is complete and self-contained and the only input is the standard affine criterion, so no H3 claim would be honest here, and the value of the item lies in the faithful short proof rather than in difficulty.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the canonical identification of the sheaf of relative differentials of f : X to S with the conormal sheaf of the diagonal immersion X to X times_S X (statement lines 6506-6511). The counted proof does two genuinely different things: it constructs the canonical map globally, by forming the square-zero thickening of the diagonal, exhibiting the conormal sheaf as the kernel of the resulting surjection, and then manufacturing the derivation as the difference of the two sections induced by the projections, which invokes the universal property of the module of differentials (proof lines 6515-6548); and it verifies the isomorphism over an affine chart U = Spec(A) over Spec(R), where the conormal sheaf becomes J/J^2 for the kernel of the multiplication of the tensor product algebra and the canonical map becomes the explicit formula sending a db to a tensor b minus ab tensor 1 (proof lines 6549-6593). It is H2: the final identification of the explicit formula is delegated to a cited algebra statement, but the construction of the map and the affine reduction are the author's own and are carried out in the counted span.

items.title: Dominance from a scheme with finitely many irreducible components is detected on generic points of the irreducible components of the target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that when X has finitely many irreducible components, dominance of f : X to S is equivalent to every irreducible component of S having its generic point in the image of f, and that S then has finitely many irreducible components as well (statement lines 1382-1390). The proof is a short but genuine topological argument: it decomposes X into components Z_i with generic points xi_i, uses that the image of an irreducible set is irreducible and that closure commutes with finite unions to obtain the display S = union of the closures of {f(xi_i)}, and then reads both conclusions off that display (proof lines 1392-1404). It is H2: the input is the generic-point dictionary for irreducible components, but the union-of-closures manipulation and the passage from generic points in the image to the statement about components are carried out inside the counted span.

items.title: Finite flat quasi-coherent modules are finite locally free exactly when every closed subset closed under generalizations is open
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts an equivalence between a module-theoretic condition on a scheme, that every finite flat quasi-coherent module is finite locally free, and a topological condition, that every closed subset closed under generalizations is open (statement lines 5068-5077). The proof is substantial in its second half: it uses flat closed immersions to get the easy direction, then for the converse shows that the support of a finite flat module is closed under generalization, applies the same reasoning to every exterior power, uses the nestedness of those supports to decompose the scheme into open and closed pieces U_i indexed by the rank, and finally produces a local surjection from a free module of the correct rank and proves it injective by applying the flat-closed-immersion characterisation to the top exterior power (proof lines 5079-5151). It is H2: the argument is a genuine scheme-level construction rather than a citation, but its individual inputs are standard local algebra and the author explicitly says the scheme case simply repeats the affine algebra argument, so no independent research-level claim is made for it.

items.title: Generic flatness over a reduced base: an open dense locus on which a finite type morphism and a finite type sheaf are flat and of finite presentation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition is the reduced-base form of generic flatness: for a finite type morphism f : X to S with S reduced and a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf F on X there is an open dense U of S over which X is flat and of finite presentation and F is flat over U and of finite presentation over O_X (statement lines 5246-5260). The counted proof has a real assembly layer of its own on top of the algebra input: it makes the base affine and reduced, covers X by finitely many affines with finite modules, introduces one auxiliary finite module M_ij for each pair of chart intersections so that those intersections can be controlled, intersects the finitely many dense opens produced by the algebra input, and then localises once more at a chosen point to read off the four flatness and finite presentation statements together with quasi-separatedness of X over S (proof lines 5262-5343). It is H2: the deep flatness input is the cited algebra lemma, while the contribution of this argument is the geometric assembly, which is carried out in the counted span and is not a citation.

items.title: The support of a quasi-coherent sheaf is closed under specialization
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is that for a quasi-coherent sheaf F on a scheme X the support is closed under specialization (statement lines 660-665). The counted proof is two lines long and its whole content is the observation that for a specialization x' of x the stalk of F at x' is a localization of the stalk at x, so the vanishing of F_x forces the vanishing of F_{x'}; the conclusion is then restated as closedness of the complement under generalization (proof lines 667-672). It is H2 by the rule that H3 is only given for genuinely independent research-level content: the argument is complete and uses no hypothesis beyond quasi-coherence being available for the notion of support, but it is a routine local argument and is deliberately not dressed up.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the additivity of the total Chern class, the Chern character and the Chern polynomials along a distinguished triangle of perfect objects under any of four increasingly weak hypotheses on X, from the existence of a representing map of complexes after an envelope up to quasi-compactness of X (statement lines 9426-9448, tag 0F9F). items.title: Corepresentability of the flat at a point functor in the henselian essentially finite type case
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem is the local flatterling statement: for a henselian local A, a B essentially of finite type over A and a finite B-module M, the functor of local homomorphisms along which the localisations of M are flat is corepresented by A/I for an ideal I, which is finitely generated when A -> B and M are of finite presentation (statement lines 6789-6807, tag 05PG). The counted proof is a genuine induction on the length of a complete devissage: it must transport corepresentability across the finite steps of the devissage, replace A by the quotient corepresenting the subfunctor coming from the cokernel, use that a flat such cokernel is free over A, and then recognise the remaining condition as the isomorphism condition for a presentation map via universal exactness before invoking the flatterling map theorem. The reduction chain is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: The theorem represents the functor of points where a surjection of modules becomes an isomorphism by a closed immersion Z -> S, in the finite presentation and flat and pure case, and makes Z of finite presentation when the target module is (statement lines 6670-6684, tag 05PF). The associated prime shrinking step is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The functor of points where a module is free at the generic points of the fibres is an fpqc sheaf and limit preserving
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the functor H_p assigning to a base change the property that the pullback of a module is free of rank p at every generic point of every fibre is an fpqc sheaf, and is limit preserving when the module is of finite presentation (statement lines 6178-6186, tag 05MS). The proof has two genuinely different halves: the sheaf half descends local freeness to the limit point through the flat local map of stalks and then has to upgrade a surjection from a free module to an isomorphism by checking the reduction fibre by fibre, using the induction step lemma; the limit preserving half descends the flat locus and its rank stratification to a stage and uses the open images in the base to find a stage at which the condition already holds. The second half is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The induction step for a finitely presented flat ring map with geometrically integral fibres
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the induction step of the flatterling theory over a finitely presented flat ring map with geometrically integral fibres: it produces a map from a finite free module to a finitely presented module that is an isomorphism on the special fibre, and shows that the flatness of the localisation at a prime over r is equivalent to five other conditions, one of which is the existence of localised elements making the map universally injective with flat cokernel (statement lines 3140-3169, tag 05IA). The proof constructs alpha from a basis of the fibre, then reduces the six conditions to one implication via the algebraic induction step, and that implication requires combining openness of the flat locus, openness of the isomorphism locus for a map of finitely presented modules, and openness of the image of a flat finitely presented ring map to produce the two localising elements. The openness argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The projective space bundle formula: the Chow group of a projective bundle as a direct sum over the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem is the projective space bundle formula: for a finite locally free sheaf E of rank r on X the map from the direct sum of the Chow groups CH_{k+i}(X), i from 0 to r-1, to CH_{k+r-1}(P) sending a tuple to the sum of the caps of the powers of c_1(O_P(1)) with the pulled back components is an isomorphism (statement lines 6931-6954, tag 02TX). The proof has genuinely different halves: injectivity is a pushforward computation using the fact that the pushforward of the powers of the first Chern class vanishes below the top power, while surjectivity requires reducing to an irreducible base, then to a trivial bundle by shrinking the base with an induction on its dimension, and finally descending a class through the affine space stratification of the projective space stratum by stratum. The stratification descent is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A criterion for purity along a fibre in terms of the relative associated primes inside the image of an etale neighbourhood
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the purity criterion used throughout the chapter: under the standing hypotheses it says that F is pure along the fibre if and only if the image of the etale morphism contains the relative associated points of the pullback that specialize into the fibre (statement lines 5196-5219, tag 05L4). The proof reduces the base to the etale neighbourhood and its localisation, proves the forward direction through the specialization of associated points and the openness of the image of g, and then proves the converse by base changing to the henselization, lifting a relative associated point along the etale morphism via the associated point lemma for etale maps, and using purity of the pulled back module to produce the required specialization inside the fibre. The henselization step is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: An impurity with a quasi-finite morphism can be replaced by one over an elementary etale neighbourhood
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if a module has an impurity above a point with a morphism that is quasi-finite at the specialisation, then it already has an impurity presented by an elementary etale neighbourhood of that point (statement lines 4644-4651, tag 05J0). The proof is a real construction: it applies the lemma that splits off a finite part of a quasi-finite morphism at a point over an elementary etale neighbourhood, lifts the specialisation along the resulting etale morphism, transports the relative associated point along the base changes, and then pushes the impurity down from the base change to the etale neighbourhood using finiteness of the relevant morphism. The lifting and pushing of the impurity are the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Purity, finiteness of the support and universal purity for a separated finite type module with finite fibres
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a separated finite type morphism whose module has finite support in every fibre, purity relative to the base, finiteness of the scheme theoretic support over the base and universal purity are equivalent (statement lines 5046-5059, tag 05K4). The proof reduces to the case where the support is all of X, then has to show that two easy implications plus one substantial one hold: assuming purity, the quasi-finite separated morphism is factored through a finite morphism and a quasi-compact open immersion, and the immersion is shown to be closed by lifting an arbitrary specialization using the etale splitting of the quasi-finite part, the identification of the lifted point as a relative associated point, and purity itself. That specialization lifting is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Flat pullback along a vector bundle is an isomorphism on Chow groups
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that pullback along the vector bundle associated to a finite locally free sheaf of rank r is an isomorphism from the Chow groups of the base onto the Chow groups of the bundle, shifted by r (statement lines 7061-7075, tag 02TY). Surjectivity is a citation of the affine space fibration lemma, but injectivity needs a real construction: the vector bundle is realised as the complement of the zero scheme of a carefully chosen section of the projective bundle of E direct sum the structure sheaf, a vanishing class is shown to come from the divisor, that divisor class is expanded through the projective space bundle formula, and the resulting expression is contradicted by the vanishing of the top cap on a bundle of one higher rank. The injectivity argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Weakly associated primes of a tensor product with a flat finitely presented module over a finitely presented ring map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the weakly associated primes of M tensor_R N, for a finite presentation R -> S and a finitely presented S-module N flat over R, as the primes lying over a weakly associated prime of M at which the fibre prime is associated to the fibre of N (statement lines 3749-3768, tag 05IG). The proof is long and genuinely reduction driven: an etale local model makes N projective over the base, the key observation on the associated primes of the fibre is extracted, the two forward implications are proved by universality of injectivity together with the fact that the localised module becomes a finite free direct summand, and the converse needs a five-condition reduction plus the determination of non injectivity of a map of projective modules over an auto-associated ring after tensoring with the residue field. That last step is not a routine citation, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A separated flat locally finite type morphism which is an isomorphism over a retrocompact scheme theoretically dense open is an open immersion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a Zariski main theorem style criterion: a separated flat locally finite type morphism which is an isomorphism over a retrocompact scheme theoretically dense open is itself an open immersion (statement lines 3072-3081, tag 081M). The proof does real work at each step: it upgrades local finite type to local finite presentation over the dense open, reduces to a quasi-compact flat morphism onto its image over an affine base, uses dimension zero fibres and the etale splitting of the quasi-finite part to write the base change as a finite piece plus a piece empty over the closed fibre, and then kills that second piece by scheme theoretic density, before descending finiteness and comparing the degree with one over the dense open. The density argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A tensor-square flat algebra over a field is weakly etale and a filtered colimit of etale algebras
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a K-algebra B over a field K and gives three equivalent conditions: that the multiplication B tensor_K B -> B be flat; that K -> B be weakly etale; and that B be a filtered colimit of etale K-algebras; it adds that every finitely generated K-subalgebra of B is etale over K (source lines 30503-30514). The equivalence of (1) and (2) is immediate because every K-algebra is flat over K, and (3) implies (1) and (2) is the direction supplied by an earlier lemma, so the substance is the converse. Assuming (1) and (2), the proof first notes that a field is absolutely flat, hence B is an absolutely flat ring, so B is reduced and every local ring of B is a field (proof lines 30521-30525). It then takes a prime q of B, observes that B -> B_q is weakly etale so that B_q is weakly etale over K, and concludes that B_q is a separable algebraic extension of K (proof lines 30528-30532). The final step is the substantive one: for a finitely generated K-subalgebra A of B, every minimal prime p of A is the image of a prime q of B, so kappa(p) viewed inside B_q = kappa(q) is separable algebraic over K; hence every generic point of Spec(A) is closed, so dim(A) = 0, so A is the product of its local rings, and since A is reduced those local rings equal their residue fields, which are finite separable over K, so A is etale over K (proof lines 30535-30552). The non-routine content is the dimension-zero argument together with the identification of the finite etale algebras over a field as reduced zero-dimensional rings with finite separable residue fields.

items.title: A solution containing a purely inseparable degree p step can be replaced by a separable solution
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a prime p, an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings with fraction field extension L/K, and a tower K_2/K_1/K of finite extensions, assumes K of characteristic p, L/K separable, B Nagata, K_2 a solution for A in B, and K_2/K_1 purely inseparable of degree p, and concludes the existence of a separable extension K_3/K_1 which is a solution (source lines 35774-35788). The proof is a substantial construction. It first records that L_1 and L_2 are reduced, that the integral closures A_1, A_2, B_1, B_2 are finite and Nagata, and that pi is a nonzerodivisor with the four fraction field identifications (proof lines 35791-35808). It then writes K_2 = K_1(alpha) with alpha^p = a_1 in A_1 after multiplying alpha by a power of pi, and introduces the presentation algebras A'_2 = A_1[x]/(x^p - a_1) and B'_2 = B_1[x]/(x^p - a_1), to which the extension-construction lemma is applied at f = pi^2, yielding an integer n that works for both (proof lines 35809-35822). The genuine content is the deformation: it replaces x^p - a_1 by the etale algebras K_3 = K_1[x]/(x^p - pi^{2n} x - a_1) and L_3 = L_1[x]/(x^p - pi^{2n} x - a_1) together with the subrings A'_3 and B'_3 defined by x^p - pi^n x - a_1, builds the displayed commutative diagram of quotient algebras, and transports the chosen n back to get finite extensions A'_3 in A_3 and B'_3 in B_3 with A_3 -> B_3 extending A'_3 -> B'_3 and an isomorphism of the pi^2-quotients (proof lines 35825-35862). It then shows A_3 and B_3 are finite products of Dedekind domains with pi in every maximal ideal, that every maximal ideal of A_3 becomes principal in its localization by Nakayama, and hence that A_3 and B_3 are the integral closures of A and B in K_3 and L_3 (proof lines 35865-35876). The last step verifies the formal smoothness criterion using the pi^2-quotient isomorphism and the hypothesis that K_2 is a solution, with the author noting that some details are omitted (proof lines 35877-35889). The etale deformation and the Dedekind-product analysis are independent research-level content.

items.title: The I-adic homology of a complex of finite modules is pro-isomorphic to the powers of its homology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: This is the companion of the Artin-Rees consequence for a complex of finite modules over a Noetherian ring, with the I-adic filtration applied to the terms rather than the quotients: for the induced complex I^nK -> I^nL -> I^nM with homology H_n the lemma produces canonical maps and a constant c such that the image of H_n -> H lies in I^{n-c}H, together with a canonical map I^nH -> H_{n-c} making the two displayed compositions canonical, so that the inverse systems (H_n) and (I^nH) are isomorphic as pro-objects (source lines 29431-29457). The proof rewrites H_n as (Ker(beta) cap I^nL)/alpha(I^nK), gets the comparison maps from the two inclusions, and again applies Artin-Rees twice to choose c_1 and c_2 so that Im(alpha) cap I^nL lies in alpha(I^{n-c_1}K) and Ker(beta) cap I^nL lies in I^{n-c_2}Ker(beta), setting c = c_1 + c_2 (proof lines 29460-29470). It then defines psi_n : I^nH -> H_{n-c} by choosing a representative y in I^n Ker(beta) and proves well-definedness using that a second representative differs by an element of Im(alpha), which by the choice of c_1 lies in alpha(I^{n-c}K) (proof lines 29477-29482 and following). The non-routine content is again the pair of Artin-Rees constants and the well-definedness check.

items.title: Flatness of a module over a glueing pair is detected by its two localizations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a glueing pair (R -> R', f) and an arbitrary R-module M that is not assumed glueable, and asserts that M is flat over R exactly when M tensor_R R' is flat over R' and M_f is flat over R_f (source lines 25707-25713). One direction is base change, but the other forces the proof to first reduce to the glueable case: it introduces the glued module M-tilde, and if that is flat it applies the flat Tors criterion to the sequence 0 -> Ker(M -> M-tilde) -> M -> M-tilde -> 0 to conclude that Ker(M -> M-tilde) tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) vanishes, whence M = M-tilde by the faithfulness lemma (proof lines 25716-25727). The substantive part is then the Tors computation. From the exact sequence 0 -> R -> R' oplus R_f -> (R')_f -> 0 the proof reads off that f is a nonzerodivisor on Tor_1^R(R', N) and invertible on Tor_i^R(R', N) for i >= 2 (proof lines 25733-25744), transfers that to Tor_i^R(M tensor_R R', N) using flatness of M tensor_R R' over R' together with the change-of-rings spectral sequence and the Lazard filtered-colimit description (proof lines 25745-25755), and finally feeds it into the long exact Tors sequence of the glueable sequence 0 -> M -> M tensor_R R' oplus M_f -> M tensor_R (R')_f -> 0 to force Tor_1^R(M, N) = 0 (proof lines 25756-25770). The non-routine content is the two-step comparison of the f-action on the two families of Tor modules, which is what makes the Tors criterion applyable.

items.title: In characteristic p, weak solvability for a degree p Galois step follows when the small residue field is the intersection of the p-power residue subfields
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma works with a tower A in B in C of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L in M, assumes A in B weakly unramified, characteristic of K equal to p, M a degree p Galois extension of L, and kappa_A equal to the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n}, and concludes the existence of a finite Galois extension K_1/K, totally ramified with respect to A, that is a weak solution for A -> C (source lines 34817-34830). The proof is a genuine multi-stage induction. It first uses that the characteristic p extension is Artin-Schreier, picks z with xi = z^p - z in L and chooses n minimal with pi^n xi in B, disposing of n = 0 as unramified (proof lines 34833-34839). It then invokes the perfectness of kappa_A together with the Cohen map to write xi as a sum over powers of pi with coefficients in kappa_B and splits the index set into the parts I and J according to whether the coefficient lies in kappa_A (proof lines 34842-34861). The proof then runs a first induction on the size of J: the case J empty is handled by a p-divisibility argument showing p does not divide n, then constructing K_1 with w^p - w = pi^{-n} a and tracking the extension through L_1, B_1, M_1 to conclude (proof lines 34864-34894); the induction step replaces the chosen z by an explicit z' that kills the coefficient of the offending index, shrinking J (proof lines 34898-34918). Finally it writes each remaining lambda_j as a proper p^{r_j}-th power, picks the unique maximal j p^{-r_j}, constructs a degree p^r extension with uniformizer controlled by (pi')^{p^r} = pi + pi^{n+1}a, recomputes xi in the integral closure B_1, performs a second explicit change of z, and reads the conclusion off case (C) of the characteristic p lemma (proof lines 34921-34973). The two nested inductions and the two explicit changes of the Artin-Schreier generator are independent research-level content, not routine bookkeeping.

items.title: Perfection of a pseudo-coherent complex can be checked on localizations at primes or at maximal ideals
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma lists five conditions on a pseudo-coherent complex K^bullet over a ring R: that it be perfect; that its localization at every prime be perfect; the same at every maximal ideal; the vanishing of H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa(p)) for all i much smaller than 0 at every prime; and the same at every maximal ideal; it asserts the implications (1) => (2) <=> (3) <=> (4) <=> (5), with all conditions equivalent when K^bullet is bounded below (source lines 20063-20086). The proof has real content beyond the formal implications. The localization implications come from applying the pullback-perfect lemma to the appropriate maps of local rings and residue fields, and the passage from primes to maximal ideals uses that every prime lies in a maximal ideal and then pulls back along R_m -> R_p (proof lines 20089-20097). The substantive direction is that (4) implies (2) and (5) implies (3): in the local case with vanishing below degree a, the proof invokes the cutting lemma at i = a - 1 to split K^bullet as the direct sum of tau_{<= a-1} and tau_{>= a} with the upper part perfect, and then shows the lower part vanishes by a contradiction: if not, the largest nonzero cohomology module M is finite by pseudo-coherence, so by Nakayama M tensor_R kappa is nonzero, which makes H^i((tau_{<= a-1}K^bullet) tensor^L kappa) = H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa) nonzero, contradicting the hypothesis (proof lines 20100-20122). The bounded below case is then finished by producing, at any given maximal ideal, an f outside it with K^bullet tensor R_f perfect, using the gluing and lift lemmas together with quasi-compactness (proof lines 20125-20132). The non-routine steps are the Nakayama contradiction and the final local-to-global promotion.

items.title: Artin-Rees controls the A-adic stabilisation of the homology of a complex of finite modules over a Noetherian ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: This is a six-part structure theorem. Starting from a complex K -> L -> M of finite modules over a Noetherian ring A with H = Ker(beta)/Im(alpha), and the complexes induced modulo I^n with homology H_n, the lemma produces canonical maps H -> H_n and H_n -> H_{n-1} and then asserts that the pro-systems (H_n) and (H/I^n H) are isomorphic, that their limits agree, that (H_n) is Mittag-Leffler, and three further exactness statements (source lines 28866-28903). The proof must first rewrite H_n as beta^{-1}(I^n M)/(Im(alpha) + I^n L) and build the comparison maps from the inclusions beta^{-1}(I^n M) in beta^{-1}(I^{n-1} M) and Im(alpha) + I^n L in Im(alpha) + I^{n-1} L (proof lines 28906-28913). The genuinely non-routine part is then the construction of the map psi_n : H_n -> H/I^{n-c}H, which depends on two Artin-Rees constants c_1 and c_2 chosen so that beta^{-1}(I^n M) is contained in Ker(beta) + I^{n-c_1} L and Ker(beta) cap I^n L is contained in I^{n-c_2} Ker(beta) (proof lines 28916-28920), together with a well-definedness argument that tracks a second set of choices through those two containments (proof lines 28927-28941). Parts (1) to (6) are then derived, with (5) proved by summing over generators of I^c H_n (proof lines 28971-28978) and (6) by splitting into the two annihilation bounds, one from each Artin-Rees constant, which is why the single exponent c = c_1 + c_2 is what makes the statement true (proof lines 28981-28990).

items.title: A vanishing cohomology group of a pseudo-coherent complex at a prime cuts the localized complex into an upper and a lower part
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a prime p, an integer i, and a pseudo-coherent complex K^bullet with H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa(p)) = 0, and asserts the existence of f not in p and a canonical direct sum decomposition of the localized complex into the truncations tau_{>= i+1} and tau_{<= i-1}, with the upper part perfect and of tor-amplitude in [i+1, infinity] (source lines 19866-19881). The proof, as the author notes, is a direct one rather than a citation: it reduces to a bounded above complex of finite free modules, inspects degree i, and writes the differentials there as matrices A and B (proof lines 19887-19895). The vanishing hypothesis is then unwound into the statement that A mod p has rank r and B mod p has rank m - r, which yields an r x r minor a of A and an (m - r) x (m - r) minor b of B both outside p (proof lines 19896-19899). Setting f = ab, the proof exhibits explicit summand decompositions of K^{i-1}, K^i and K^{i+1} after inverting f such that the two differentials kill off complementary summands and are isomorphisms on the others, so that K^bullet becomes quasi-isomorphic to the displayed two-piece complex (proof lines 19900-19914). The non-routine content is the extraction of the two minors from the rank statement and the explicit reblocking of the three free modules.

items.title: Ext groups before and after reduction modulo the powers of an ideal are pro-isomorphic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an ideal I in a Noetherian ring A and finite modules M and N, sets A_n = A/I^n, M_n = M/I^nM and N_n = N/I^nN, and asserts that for every i >= 0 the systems {Ext^i_A(M, N)/I^n Ext^i_A(M, N)} and {Ext^i_{A_n}(M_n, N_n)} are isomorphic in the category C of weird systems (source lines 29193-29210). The proof is a long comparison argument. It first chooses a presentation 0 -> K -> A^{oplus r} -> M -> 0, defines K_n = K/I^nK and K(n) = Ker(A_n^{oplus r} -> M_n), and uses the Artin-Rees consequence lemma to get a constant c and maps K(n) -> K_n/I^{n-c}K_n that are 'almost inverse', exhibiting an isomorphism of the systems (K(n)) and (K_n) in C (proof lines 29213-29229). It then proves the analogous statement for Ext groups: the surjections K_n -> K(n) have kernels annihilated by I^c, so the induced maps on Ext have kernel and cokernel annihilated by I^c, giving an isomorphism of the two Ext systems by the comparison lemma (proof lines 29232-29244). The proof then reduces to i = 0, 1 by the shift isomorphisms Ext^{i-1}_A(K, N) = Ext^i_A(M, N) and the analogous statement after reduction (proof lines 29247-29254). The substantive part is the final diagram chase for i = 0, 1: the proof writes down the commutative diagram comparing the two long exact sequences, uses the Mittag-Leffler comparison lemma to bound the kernel and cokernel of Hom(M, N)/I^n Hom(M, N) -> Hom(M_n, N_n) and of the analogous map for K by I^c-torsion, constructs maps delta_n between the I^c-saturated pieces, and finally makes a diagram chase (stated to be omitted) on the displayed solid diagram to define the dotted arrow and bound its kernel and cokernel (proof lines 29257-29304). The two-step reduction with Artin-Rees, the annihilation bookkeeping with a single constant c, and the final chase are independent research-level content.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules

items.difficulty_reason: The statement asks for a canonical isomorphism det(M') tensor det(M'') -> det(M) attached to a short exact sequence of finite projective R-modules (source lines 36282-36293). The difficulty is not in finding a map but in making it canonical: the proof first decomposes R into a product of rings indexed by the rank pairs (i, j) of the two outer modules, so that the ranks become constant (proof lines 36296-36301), and then has to produce a map between exterior powers that does not depend on the choices made. The construction uses chosen elements m'_1, ..., m'_i of M' and lifts m_{i+1}, ..., m_{i+j} of chosen elements of M'' (proof lines 36306-36316); the well-definedness and bijectivity of that rule is exactly the part the author states is omitted, and it is the substantive content of the lemma.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring map A -> B, a nonzerodivisor f in A, a bounded complex M^bullet of finite free A-modules, and assumes that f maps to a nonzerodivisor g in B; the conclusion is the equality I_i(M^bullet, f)B = I_i(M^bullet tensor_A B, g) of ideals (source lines 28012-28018). What makes the statement non-formal is that the ideal I_i is generated by the minors of an augmented map rather than of the differential alone, so the equality is not immediate from base change of a matrix; the author states the whole argument as the single observation that those minors map to those minors.

items.title: Annihilation of Ext one by an ideal is equivalent to the multiplication maps on the first term factoring through the differential
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an ideal I, and a complex K concentrated in degrees -1 and 0, and establishes the equivalence of three conditions: that Ext^1_R(K, N) be annihilated by I for all modules N; that K be representable by a two-term complex K^{-1} -> K^0 with K^0 free such that for each a in I the multiplication map a : K^{-1} -> K^{-1} factors through the differential; and the same factorization condition for every representation with K^0 projective (source lines 22451-22474). It then shows that when R is Noetherian and H^{-1}(K) and H^0(K) are finite, two further conditions involving only finite modules N and a representation with K^0 finite free and K^{-1} finite are equivalent to these (source lines 22465-22473). The proof is substantive. Assuming (1), it takes any two-term representation with K^0 projective, uses the description of maps out of K in the derived category, chooses N = K^{-1} and the element xi of Ext^1_R(K, K^{-1}) given by the identity on K^{-1}, and since xi is annihilated by a it obtains the dotted arrow h making the displayed square commute, which is exactly condition (3) (proof lines 22479-22493). The passage (3) implies (2) and (3) implies (5) invokes the two-term representation lemma, and (2) implies (1) is proved by taking an arbitrary xi in Ext^1_R(K, N) represented by a map varphi : K^{-1} -> N and computing a varphi = varphi o a = varphi o h o d_K^{-1}, which shows a xi = 0 (proof lines 22494-22502). The Noetherian part closes by observing that (5) implies (2) trivially, that (1) implies (4) trivially, and that the argument of (2) implies (1) applied with N = K^{-1} shows (4) implies (1) (proof lines 22505-22516). The non-routine content is the choice of the identity class in Ext^1_R(K, K^{-1}) that converts the annihilation hypothesis into the factorization condition.

items.title: Maps between modules over a flat covering that are I-power torsion in kernel and cokernel come from maps over the base ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R/I -> S/IS an isomorphism, and establishes two dual statements: given an R-module N and an S-module map M' -> N tensor_R S whose kernel and cokernel are I-power torsion, there is an R-module map M -> N and an isomorphism M tensor_R S = M' compatible with these; and symmetrically for a map out of M tensor_R S (source lines 24881-24899). The proof is a genuine application of the gluing equivalence rather than a citation of the conclusion. It writes I = (f_1, ..., f_t) and observes that the localizations at the f_i of the given map are isomorphisms, so that (M', N_{f_i}, varphi_{f_i}, can_{ij}) is an object of the gluing category (proof lines 24902-24906). The equivalence proposition then produces an R-module M with M' = M tensor_R S and N_{f_i} = M_{f_i} compatibly (proof lines 24907-24910). The remaining content is the functoriality step: the displayed morphism in the gluing category whose first component is varphi corresponds to an R-module map psi : M -> N under the equivalence of categories, and the composition of the base change of psi with the isomorphism M' = M tensor_R S is varphi, which is exactly the compatibility (proof lines 24911-24924). Part (2) is carried out as the dual argument with varphi_{f_i}^{-1} replacing varphi_{f_i} (proof lines 24927-24948), and the final kernel-and-cokernel statement is drawn from the neighbourhood equivalence lemma (proof lines 24951-24952). The non-routine content is the translation of a map of glued objects back to a map over R.

items.title: The automorphism group of a normal extension acts transitively on the maximal ideals of the integral closure
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A -> B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L, a normal extension K_1/K with automorphism group G, and asserts that G acts on the rings K_1, L_1, A_1 and B_1 and transitively on the maximal ideals of B_1 (source lines 34608-34615). The proof reduces immediately to the transitivity statement and argues by contradiction: if there are two or more orbits, one can find b in B_1 vanishing at all maximal ideals of one orbit and having residue 1 at all maximal ideals of another (proof lines 34618-34621). The substantive move is the construction of the G-invariant element b' = prod_{sigma in G} sigma(b), which lies in B_1 inside L_1 = (L tensor_K K_1)_red and lies in some but not all maximal ideals of B_1 (proof lines 34622-34625). The proof then has to lift b' back to L tensor_K K_1: in characteristic p > 0 it raises to a suitably large p-power q, which defines a canonical map (L tensor_K K_1)_red -> L tensor_K K_1, obtaining a G-invariant b'' mapping to (b')^N (proof lines 34626-34630). Since K = (K_1)^G one gets b'' in L, and since b'' maps to B_1 and B is normal one gets b'' in B; but then b'' must lie in the maximal ideal of B because b' lies in some maximal ideal of B_1, and simultaneously must not, because b' does not lie in all of them, a contradiction (proof lines 34631-34637). The non-routine step is the characteristic p lifting of a reduced-tensor element through a p-power Frobenius-type map.

items.title: For a flat ring map and a finite ideal the gluing category is abelian and the canonical functor is exact and commutes with colimits
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma works with the gluing category Glue(R -> S, f_1, ..., f_t) attached to a flat ring map varphi : R -> S and the ideal I = (f_1, ..., f_t) of R, and asserts that this category is abelian and that the canonical functor Can is exact and preserves arbitrary colimits (source lines 24742-24748). The proof has to work with an object of that category, namely a tuple (M', M_i, alpha_i, alpha_ij) consisting of an S-module, R_{f_i}-modules and gluing data, and to show that kernels and cokernels can be formed componentwise as Ker(varphi') and Ker(varphi_i), respectively, with the gluing maps induced (proof lines 24751-24760). The key point is that this componentwise construction is legitimate precisely because R -> S is flat, so that taking kernels and cokernels commutes with - tensor_R S (proof lines 24761-24762); exactness is then reduced to the R-flatness of the localizations R_{f_i} and of S, and commutation with colimits to the corresponding property of tensor products (proof lines 24763-24764).

items.title: An object of the derived category has a left dual precisely when it is perfect, and the dual is the dual of a perfect complex
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the perfect objects of D(R) as exactly those admitting a left dual, and identifies that dual with the object M^vee of the dual-perfect-complex lemma (source lines 38580-38591). One direction is structural: a bounded complex of finite projective modules has a left dual already in the category of complexes (proof lines 38594-38598). The converse is the hard direction and occupies the rest of the proof. From a left dual (N, eta, epsilon) one chooses a representative M^bullet and a K-flat complex N^bullet with flat terms, writes eta(1) as a finite sum of tensors m_{n,i} tensor n_{-n,i}, and builds the subcomplex K^bullet generated by the m_{n,i} and their differentials (proof lines 38601-38622). The key move is that eta factors through K tensor^L N and the identity on M therefore factors through K, which forces M to lie in D^-(R) (proof lines 38623-38641). One then re-represents M by a bounded above complex of free modules, uses the same finite-sum expression to cut out a bounded subcomplex K^bullet consisting of finite free modules, and again factors the identity through K; since K is perfect and a summand of M, M is perfect (proof lines 38642-38653). The non-routine content is the factoring-of-the-identity trick applied twice, once to bound M above and once to bound it below.

items.title: Eight equivalent conditions for the vanishing of Ext groups out of a localization at a single element
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, an element f, and a complex K in D(A), and establishes the equivalence of six genuine conditions (the seventh entry of the displayed list is the author's placeholder and contributes no mathematics): vanishing of Ext^n_A(A_f, K) for all n, vanishing of Hom in the derived category out of every object of D(A_f), the vanishing of T(K, f), the same condition degreewise on the cohomology, the pair of vanishings of Hom_A(A_f, H^p(K)) and Ext^1_A(A_f, H^p(K)), the vanishing of R Hom_A(A_f, K), and the invertibility of the explicitly displayed pro-product endomorphism (source lines 25849-25866). The proof runs three independent computations: it descends from Ext vanishing to Hom vanishing using a K-injective representative and the adjunction Hom_A(M, I) = Hom_{A_f}(M, Hom_A(A_f, I)) together with the fact that the resulting complex is K-injective and acyclic, hence homotopy equivalent to zero (proof lines 25869-25884); it writes down the explicit two-term free resolution of A_f with the displayed maps and identifies its Hom-dual with the pro-product endomorphism, which yields both the equivalence with condition (7) and the identification of T(K, f) with R Hom_A(A_f, K) (proof lines 25887-25906); and it uses the Ext spectral sequence of a two-term projective resolution, which degenerates at E_2 because the E_2 page then has only two nonzero columns, to obtain the short exact sequences comparing Ext^p_A(A_f, K) with Ext^1 and Hom of the cohomology (proof lines 25909-25932). The non-routine steps are the two-term resolution and the degeneration argument.

items.title: The obstruction to a split injection of finite projective modules being a direct sum of submodules is cut out by a finitely generated ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes finite projective A-modules M, N_1, N_2 and a split injection s : M -> N_1 oplus N_2, and asserts the existence of a finitely generated ideal J of A such that a ring map A -> B factors through A/J exactly when s tensor id_B identifies M tensor B with a direct sum of submodules of N_1 tensor B oplus N_2 tensor B (source lines 28126-28135). The proof chooses a splitting pi, defines the composite projectors p_i = pi o q_i o s with p_1 + p_2 = id_M, and observes that the desired direct-sum condition is equivalent to p_1 and p_2 being orthogonal projectors (proof lines 28138-28142). The real work is then encoding that equivalence as the vanishing of the four endomorphisms p_1 o p_1 - p_1, p_2 o p_2 - p_2, p_1 o p_2 and p_2 o p_1, which forces J to be the smallest ideal containing the entries of those endomorphisms under the identification J tensor End_A(M) (proof lines 28143-28145). The author leaves the remaining details omitted.

items.title: For a flat localized etale, unramified, quasi-finite, integral or generic-fibre-unique map of domains the contraction of any nonzero ideal is nonzero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes domains A and B with a ring map A -> B satisfying at least one of seven listable properties (localization of an etale map; flat and localization of an unramified map; flat and localization of a quasi-finite map; flat and localization of an integral map; flat with no nontrivial specializations between fibre points; generic point to generic point with no such specializations; or exactly one point over the generic point), and concludes that A cap J is nonzero for every nonzero ideal J of B (source lines 31701-31718). The proof is organized around case (7), the weakest hypothesis. For case (7) it uses that the unique point of Spec(B) over the generic point is the generic point, so that B tensor_A K has a unique prime with residue field L; for a nonzero b in J, the image of b is a unit of L and hence of B tensor_A K, and since B tensor_A K is the filtered colimit of the B_f for nonzero f in A, b becomes a unit in some B_f, giving b b' = f^n and hence f^n in A cap J (proof lines 31721-31736). The rest of the proof is a careful reduction showing each of the other hypotheses implies (7): assumptions (1) to (5) make A -> B flat, hence injective because flat local homomorphisms are faithfully flat, so the generic point of Spec(B) maps to that of Spec(A); the absence of nontrivial specializations between fibre points then forces it to be the unique such point, so (6) implies (7); and finally the absence of such specializations is established for the integral, quasi-finite, unramified and etale cases by reference to the corresponding standard facts (proof lines 31739-31759). The non-routine content is the colimit-and-unit argument in case (7) together with the systematic reduction ladder from the other six hypotheses.

items.title: The Fitting-type ideal attached to a bounded complex of finite free modules is well defined up to powers of the nonzerodivisor depending on the Euler characteristic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma fixes a nonzerodivisor f in a ring A and two bounded complexes M^bullet and N^bullet of finite free A-modules representing the same object of D(A), and asserts that f^m I_i(M^bullet, f) = f^n I_i(N^bullet, f) whenever the integers m, n satisfy a displayed Euler-characteristic condition (source lines 27892-27906). The proof localizes at every prime to reduce to comparing a complex with its sum with a trivial two-term complex (proof lines 27908-27917), and then splits into the three cases j not in {i-1, i, i+1}, j = i+1, j = i and j = i-1 (proof lines 27918-27998). The core is a minors computation: the generator sets of the two ideals are compared by exhibiting the relevant matrix in block form T with diagonal blocks T_1 and T_2 and invoking the formula for ideals generated by minors of a block matrix, which combined with I_0(T_2) = A, I_1(T_2) = A and I_p(T_2) = 0 for p >= 2 gives the required equality. This is the only candidate of the batch whose proof is a complete multi-case computation, and the author keeps the localization-and-induction reduction as an explicit step.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K, a finite Galois extension L/K, a maximal ideal m of the integral closure B of A in L, and the inertia group I of m, and asserts that B^I is the integral closure of A in L^I and that A -> (B^I)_{B^I cap m} is etale (source lines 33474-33482). The proof is a genuine index computation. It writes B' = B^I and m' = B' cap m, uses that m is the unique prime of B over m', and notes that since I acts trivially on kappa(m) the extension kappa(m)/kappa(m') is purely inseparable, so D/I acts faithfully on kappa(m'); then Galois theory gives [kappa(m') : kappa] >= |D/I| (proof lines 33485-33500). The substantive part is a numerical comparison of the two degree formulae: using that Norm_{L/K}(pi) = pi^{[L:K]} one gets |G| = [L:K] = |G/D| [kappa(m):kappa] ord_{B_m}(pi), and applying the same reasoning to L/L^I of degree |I| gives |I| ord_{B'_{m'}}(pi) = [kappa(m):kappa(m')] ord_{B_m}(pi) (proof lines 33502-33520 and following). Combining these with the Galois-theoretic bound on [kappa(m'):kappa] forces the ramification index of the local extension to be 1 and the residue extension to be separable, which is exactly etaleness. The non-routine content is the interplay of the ramification-index multiplicativity, the norm formula for the uniformizer and the bound coming from faithfulness of the action of D/I on the residue field.

items.title: An invertible module is the same thing as a finite locally free module of rank one, and its inverse is its dual
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of three conditions on a module M over a ring R: that M be finite locally free of rank 1, that M be invertible, and that there exist an R-module N with M tensor_R N isomorphic to R, together with the identification of the N in the third condition as Hom_R(M, R) (source lines 36117-36127). The proof is a three-way cycle of implications plus a rank argument. It first takes N = Hom_R(M, R) and the evaluation map, shows the evaluation map is an isomorphism by reducing to localizations at which M becomes free and invoking a cover argument (proof lines 36130-36135). The equivalence of invertibility with the existence of an inverse module is then a statement about tensor functors forming a quasi-inverse pair, with essential surjectivity for the converse (proof lines 36138-36141). The final and substantive part deduces finite local freeness: from an isomorphism psi : M tensor_R N -> R and an element xi = sum x_i tensor y_i with psi(xi) = 1, the proof exhibits the automorphism x -> sum psi(x tensor y_i) x_i of M and factors it through R^{oplus n}, so that M is a direct summand of a finite free module, hence finite locally free; applying the same to N by symmetry and using M tensor_R N isomorphic to R forces both to have rank 1 (proof lines 36144-36166). The non-routine content is the factoring of an automorphism through a finite free module, which is what produces the direct summand.

items.title: For a Noetherian ring the Koszul complexes of a sequence are pro-isomorphic to the quotients by the powers of the sequence
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of the Koszul construction, the lemma asserts that when A is Noetherian the pro-objects {K_n^bullet} and {A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)} of D(A) are isomorphic, with a footnote spelling out the consequence that for every n there is m >= n such that K_m^bullet -> K_n^bullet factors through K_m^bullet -> A/(f_1^m, ..., f_r^m) (source lines 27171-27178). The proof is a genuine pro-isomorphism argument. It writes down the inverse system of distinguished triangles with truncation tau_{<= -1}K_n^bullet and reduces, via the criterion for pro-isomorphisms, to showing that the inverse system of truncations is pro-zero (proof lines 27181-27190). Using that K_n^bullet is concentrated in degrees -r to 0, it further reduces to showing H^p(K_n^bullet) is pro-zero for p <= -1 (proof lines 27191-27195). The substantive step is the Artin-Rees input: since A is Noetherian each H^p(K_n^bullet) is a finite A-module; the transition map K_m^p -> K_n^p for p < 0 is given by a diagonal matrix with entries in the ideal (f_1^{m-n}, ..., f_r^{m-n}); H^p(K_n^bullet) is annihilated by J = (f_1^n, ..., f_r^n); and since (f_1^{m-n}, ..., f_r^{m-n}) is contained in J^t once m - n >= t n, Artin-Rees applied to the ideal J and the module K_n^p with submodule the kernel of K_n^p -> K_n^{p+1} shows that for m large enough the image of K_m^p -> K_n^p meets that kernel inside J times the kernel, yielding the zero map (proof lines 27196-27214). The non-routine content is the diagonal-matrix description of the transition maps and the Artin-Rees step that makes them vanish on cohomology.

items.title: Stabilization of the chain A[f^n] exhibits the pro-object A/(f^n) and the pro-object of the multiplication maps as isomorphic in the derived category
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma assumes a ring A and f in A such that the chain A[f^c] = A[f^{c+1}] = ... stabilizes from some c >= 1 on, and asserts that for every n >= 1 there are maps (A --f^n--> A) -> A/(f^n) and A/(f^{n+c}) -> (A --f^n--> A) in D(A) inducing an isomorphism of the pro-objects {A/(f^n)} and {(f^n : A -> A)} (source lines 26781-26793). The author then states that the calculation of the compositions needed to conclude the pro-object statement is omitted, which is where the actual verification of the isomorphism of pro-systems lies.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma fixes a field K and, for a K-algebra A, writes B_max(A) for the maximal weakly etale K-subalgebra, and then asserts a list of structural properties: functoriality under a K-algebra map A' -> A; agreement with the intersection B_max(A) cap A' when A' is a subalgebra of A; commutation with filtered colimits; invariance under reduction; and multiplicativity over finite products (source lines 30912-30930). The proof derives these from the defining property of B_max(A) as the subalgebra generated by the images of all weakly etale maps into A, checking in each case that the subalgebra produced on the left satisfies the universal property defining the right-hand side (proof span). The non-routine content is the colimit and reduction statements, where one must show that the relevant weakly etale maps factor through the appropriate intermediate algebra.
