items.title: The minimal primes of the strict henselization of a tensor product of strictly henselian local algebras correspond to pairs of minimal primes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an algebraically closed field k and strictly henselian local k-algebras A and B with residue field k, forms the strict henselization C of A tensor_k B at the maximal ideal m_A tensor_k B + A tensor_k m_B, and asserts that the minimal primes of C correspond one-to-one to pairs of minimal primes of A and B (source lines 31855-31863). The proof reduces the correspondence to a uniqueness statement. It first observes that a minimal prime r of C maps to minimal primes p of A and q of B because the ring maps A -> C and B -> C are flat, using going down for flat maps (proof lines 31866-31871). It then notes that it suffices to show the strict henselization of (A/p tensor_k B/q) at the corresponding maximal ideal has a unique minimal prime, and that A/p and B/q are again strictly henselian, so one may assume A and B are strictly henselian local domains and prove that C has a unique minimal prime (proof lines 31872-31881). The substantive step is the use of geometric unibranchness: the integral closures A' and B' of A and B in their fraction fields are normal local domains with residue field k, so that A' tensor_k B' is normal, hence its localization R at the corresponding maximal ideal is a normal local domain (proof lines 31882-31894). The proof then shows that A tensor_k B -> A' tensor_k B' is integral and that the maximal ideal of A' tensor_k B' over the given one is unique, so the displayed localization R can be rewritten with the smaller maximal ideal, and concludes that the localization of A tensor_k B is integrally closed in R, so R is its integral closure (proof lines 31895-31909). Applying geometric unibranchness once more gives that C has a unique minimal prime, completing the proof (proof lines 31910-31913). The non-routine content is the two-fold use of geometric unibranchness together with the normality of the tensor product of the integral closures.

items.title: In a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring the number of minimal primes is bounded by the length of the quotient by an element avoiding them
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension 1, an element x in m not contained in any minimal prime of R, and the number t of minimal primes, and asserts t <= length_R(R/xR) (source lines 38015-38021). The proof first reduces to the reduced case: putting R' = R/sqrt(0), the ring R' has the same number t of minimal primes and its quotient R'/xR' is a surjective image of R/xR, hence has smaller length (proof lines 38024-38030). For reduced R the proof uses the exact sequence 0 -> R -> prod_i R/p_i -> Q -> 0, computes that Q localized at any p_j vanishes, so that the support of Q is the single prime m, which makes Q of finite length and killed by a power x^n of x (proof lines 38033-38056). The substantive computation is then the snake lemma applied to the displayed square of multiplication-by-x^n maps: because x is not in any p_i, multiplication by x^n is injective on R and on M, and the snake sequence gives 0 -> Q -> R/x^nR -> M/x^nM -> Q -> 0, whence length_R(R/x^nR) = length_R(M/x^nM) for large n (proof lines 38057-38072). Splitting M as the product of the R_i = R/p_i and applying the one-dimensional polynomial-length lemma with x a nonzerodivisor gives n length_R(R/xR) = sum_i n length_{R_i}(R_i/xR_i), and since each term on the right is at least 1 the bound t <= length_R(R/xR) follows (proof lines 38073-38082). The non-routine steps are the support computation for Q and the snake-lemma length identity.

items.title: Extensions of modules over the base glue from I-power torsion extensions after a flat covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R/I -> S/IS an isomorphism, and says that for R-modules M and N with M being I-power torsion, every short exact sequence 0 -> N tensor_R S -> E-tilde -> M tensor_R S -> 0 descends to a commutative diagram of short exact sequences over R (source lines 24476-24501). The proof reformulates the statement as the assertion that the base-change map Ext_R(M, N) -> Ext_S(M tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) is an isomorphism, and it proves the stronger isomorphism statement. The reduction is a genuine chain: since M is I-power torsion one has M tensor_R S = M; the base-change map on Ext is functorial because R -> S is flat (proof lines 24504-24515). Choosing by the presentation lemma a surjection M' -> M with M' a direct sum of modules R/I^n, the six-term exact sequence together with the neighbourhood equivalence reduces the claim to M' and then, using compatibility of Ext with direct sums in a step the author states is omitted, to the single case M = R/I^n (proof lines 24518-24526). The case M = R/I^n is done by writing f_1, ..., f_t for generators of I^n and using the explicit description of Ext in terms of Koszul homology: the proof displays a commutative diagram with exact rows relating Ext_R(R/I^n, N) to H_1(N, f_bullet) and Hom_R(K, N), where K is the module of the naive Koszul complex, and reduces to showing the two right-hand vertical arrows are isomorphisms (proof lines 24529-24546). That is then verified directly: Hom_R(K, N) = Hom_S(K tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) because K is annihilated by I^n, and H_1(N, f_bullet) tensor_R S = H_1(N tensor_R S, f_bullet) = H_1(N, f_bullet) because R -> S is flat and H_1(N, f_bullet) is annihilated by I^n (proof lines 24547-24555). The non-routine content is the reduction to M = R/I^n and the Koszul-homology comparison that finishes it.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts the existence of a map c from perfect complexes over R to K_0(R) with three properties: sign behaviour under shifts, additivity on distinguished triangles, and agreement with the alternating sum of classes for a finite complex of finite projective modules (source lines 36490-36505). The proof defines c(K) = sum (-1)^n [M^n] and must show this is independent of the representative (proof lines 36507-36517). It does so in two stages: for a surjection of finite complexes of finite projective modules with kernel K^bullet, the degreewise short exact sequences split because each M^n is projective, giving additivity c(L) = c(K) + c(M) (proof lines 36519-36529); and for an acyclic M^bullet, the complex is broken into the displayed chain of short exact sequences and a descending induction shows each N^i is finite projective, the sequences split, and the alternating sum telescopes to zero (proof lines 36531-36549). Well-definedness and additivity on triangles then follow formally (proof lines 36551-36557). The non-routine step is the telescoping computation for acyclic complexes, which is what makes c well defined.

items.title: Unramified finite separable extensions of a discretely valued field are closed under subextension, Galois closure and compositum
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma has three parts for a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K: that in a tower M/L/K of finite separable extensions, if M is unramified with respect to A then so is L; that any unramified finite separable L/K is contained in a Galois M/K that is unramified; and that two unramified finite separable extensions are contained in a common unramified finite separable extension (source lines 33066-33081). Part (1) argues with the integral closures C/B/A: since C is finite over B, Spec(C) -> Spec(B) is surjective, so every maximal ideal m of B has a maximal ideal m' of C above it; multiplicativity of ramification indices together with the hypothesis gives that the ramification index of B_m over A is 1, and since kappa(m')/kappa_A is finite separable the same holds for kappa(m)/kappa_A (proof lines 33089-33099). Part (2) identifies 'L unramified with respect to A' with 'A -> B is etale' where B is the integral closure, takes M to be the normal closure of L over K, uses the surjection from a tensor power of L over K onto M, and applies permanence of etale maps to conclude that the tensor power of B over A is etale over A, hence a product of Dedekind domains, so M is unramified (proof lines 33102-33127). Part (3) is carried out 'in the same manner' and the author states that the details are omitted (proof lines 33130-33132). The non-routine content is the identification of unramifiedness with etaleness for the integral closure and the use of permanence of etale maps to reach the normal closure.

items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement fixes a ring A containing a primitive p-th root of unity zeta, sets w = 1 - zeta, and asserts two things about P(z) = ((1 + wz)^p - 1)/w^p: that it has the shape z^p - z + sum a_i z^i with all a_i in the ideal (w), and that it satisfies the addition formula P(z_1 + z_2 + w z_1 z_2) = P(z_1) + P(z_2) + w^p P(z_1)P(z_2) (source lines 34976-34989). The proof must first reduce to the cyclotomic integer ring Z[zeta] (proof lines 34992-34995), then use the factorization of t^{p-1} + ... + t + 1 into the factors (t - zeta^j) and the evaluation t = 1 to obtain p = (1 - zeta)...(1 - zeta^{p-1}) (proof lines 34996-35002). The substantive step is recognising that (p, w) = (w) is the unique prime above p, which forces p = u w^{p-1} for a unit u and yields the explicit formula for the a_i (proof lines 35003-35011); the addition formula is then left to a direct computation the author omits.

items.title: Adjoining an n-th root of a uniformizer gives a totally ramified degree n extension whose integral closure is A[root]
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with uniformizer pi and an integer n >= 2, sets K_1 = K[pi^{1/n}], and asserts six things: that the degree is n, that the integral closure A_1 is the ring A[pi^{1/n}], that A_1 is a discrete valuation ring, that the ramification index over A is n, that K_1 is totally ramified with respect to A, and that when n is prime to the residue characteristic K_1/K is tamely ramified with every subextension generated by pi^{1/d} for a divisor d of n (source lines 33953-33967). The first five parts are established through the auxiliary ring A' = A[x]/(x^n - pi): the proof observes that A' is finite free of rank n over A, so pi is a nonzerodivisor in A' and hence so is the image pi' of x; since A'/pi'A' is isomorphic to the field A/pi A, the ring A' is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer pi', its fraction field K' has degree n over K and is obtained by adjoining pi^{1/n}, and because A' is normal it is the integral closure A_1 (proof lines 33970-33979). The tameness assertion is then immediate from the definition and parts (3) and (4) (proof lines 33982-33984). The final statement about subextensions is the substantive part: it suffices to show every n-th root of unity zeta in K' lies in K, for which the proof notes zeta is a unit of A', writes zeta = a + b with a in A and b in the direct sum of the A(pi')^j for 1 <= j <= n-1, and argues by contradiction. If b were nonzero, writing b = u (pi')^t with t >= 1 and u a unit, the congruence 1 = zeta^n = a^n + n a^{n-1} u (pi')^t modulo (pi')^{t+1} would force b to be congruent to (1 - a^n)/(n a^{n-1}) in A modulo (pi')^{t+1}, which the direct sum decomposition A' = A oplus ... oplus A(pi')^{n-1} rules out because the image of multiplication by (pi')^{t+1} meets A(pi')^t in (pi A)(pi')^t (proof lines 33985-34002). The non-routine content is this congruence argument against the direct sum decomposition.

items.title: A quotient of an adic completion killing a square-zero ideal of the kernel is again the completion of a finite type algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian ring A, an ideal I, a finite type A-algebra B, and a surjection B-hat -> C with kernel J, and assumes J/J^2 is annihilated by I^c for some c >= 0; it concludes that C is isomorphic to the completion of a finite type A-algebra (source lines 32036-32043). The proof is a long chain of reductions rather than a single citation. It first uses that B-hat is Noetherian to make J finitely generated, then deduces from an idempotent criterion that C_f = ((B-hat)_f)_e for some idempotent e, and uses a gluing lemma to find a complementary surjection B-hat -> C' such that B-hat -> C x C' becomes an isomorphism after inverting any f in I (proof lines 32046-32060). Choosing generators f_1, ..., f_r of I, the proof exhibits the object (C x C', B_{f_i}, alpha_i, alpha_{ij}) of the gluing category Glue(B -> B-hat, f_1, ..., f_r), for which it states that the verification of conditions (1)(a) and (1)(b) is omitted (proof lines 32062-32074). Because B -> B-hat is flat and induces an isomorphism on B/IB, the equivalence proposition and the formal gluing remark apply, giving that C x C' is isomorphic to D tensor_B B-hat for some finite B-algebra D (proof lines 32075-32081). The rest is a Hensel-type lifting argument: the idempotent of D/ID corresponding to the factor C/IC is lifted after an etale base change B -> B' trivial modulo I, using that the pair (C x C', IC x IC') is henselian since C x C' is I-adically complete, and the henselian-pair criterion lets B -> C x C' factor through B'; replacing B by B' and D by D' splits D = D_e x D_{1-e} into a product of finite type A-algebras whose completions are C and C' (proof lines 32082-32096). The gluing formalism, the etale idempotent lifting and the Hensel pair argument are independent research-level content.

items.title: Over a catenary Noetherian local normal domain every radical ideal contains a nonzero element whose quotient is reduced
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition takes a catenary Noetherian local normal domain R of dimension d and a radical ideal J, and asserts the existence of a nonzero f in J with R/fR reduced (source lines 38386-38396). The proof spells out in full what the shorter radical-element lemma does, and the catenary hypothesis is used essentially: it makes every height one prime have dimension d - 1, so that the spectrum of R/(f + h) is equidimensional and the height-one-polynomial lemma applies (proof lines 38405-38409). The proof then sets up the divisor div(f) = sum m_j q_j over the height one primes containing f, observes that R/fR is reduced exactly when all m_j equal 1, and uses that R/fR embeds into the product of its localizations at those primes (proof lines 38414-38434). It introduces t(y) as the number of minimal primes over y and, using the catenary property together with the height-one-polynomial lemma, bounds t(f + h) independently of h in the power m^N (proof lines 38437-38459). Maximality of t over h in m^N cap J is then used to replace f so that t(f + h) <= s for all such h (proof lines 38462-38467), after which the desired h is manufactured: elements a_j in q_j cap J avoiding the other q_j' and elements b_j in J cap q_1 cap ... cap q_s outside the second symbolic power q_j^{(2)}, combined into c = sum b_j prod a_j', then multiplied by the a_j with m_j = 1 and by a suitable y (proof lines 38470-38512). The non-routine content is the boundedness of t, which is what makes the maximality argument possible, and the prime-avoidance construction of c with prescribed valuations.

items.title: A Noetherian regular ring of finite dimension is a strong generator for its perfect complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a Noetherian regular ring R of finite dimension d is a strong generator for the full subcategory of perfect objects of D(R) (source lines 20819-20824). The proof is a genuine induction on the projective dimension bound, using the characterisation of perfect objects as bounded complexes with finite cohomology and the definition of generation in a bounded number of steps. It first records that every finite R-module has projective dimension at most d, so that d + 1 is the generation bound, then proves by induction on i that if every H^n(K) has projective dimension at most i then K lies in the i + 1-fold generated subcategory of R (proof lines 20832-20840). The base case i = 0 uses that projective cohomology modules have vanishing higher Ext between them, so that K splits as the direct sum of the shifts of its cohomology, and each finite projective module is a summand of a sum of copies of R (proof lines 20843-20852). The induction step is the substantive part: it picks a surjection from a finite free module onto each cohomology module, lifts these to maps F^n[-n] -> K in the derived category, takes the associated distinguished triangle K' -> bigoplus F^n[-n] -> K -> K'[1], reads off the short exact sequences 0 -> H^n(K') -> F^n -> H^n(K) -> 0, and uses the projective-dimension subadditivity to bound the projective dimension of H^n(K') by max(0, i), so that K' lies in the i+1-fold generated subcategory and hence K lies in the i+2-fold one (proof lines 20855-20879). The non-routine content is the bookkeeping of the generation index through the distinguished triangle, together with the projective-dimension drop that makes the induction go through.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a tower A in B in C of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L in M, assumes the residue field k of A algebraically closed of characteristic p > 0, that A and B are complete, that A -> B is weakly unramified, that M is a finite extension of L, and that k is the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n}, and concludes the existence of a finite extension K_1/K which is a weak solution for A -> C (source lines 35369-35383). The proof is long and is where the surrounding theory is assembled: it first establishes that the integral closure of B in any finite extension of L is a complete discrete valuation ring, using that B is Nagata and that the relevant rings are dominated by maximal ones, which also shows that C is the integral closure of B in M (proof lines 35386-35395). It then reduces to the case where M/L is totally ramified with respect to B, and proceeds through the structure theory of the inertia and ramification subgroups, the algebraically closed residue field, and the p-power residue hypothesis. The proof is a research-level synthesis: at every stage a generous reduction is required before the characteristic p input can be applied.

items.title: Unramified and tamely ramified separable extensions stay so after tensoring with an extension of discrete valuation rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings with fraction field extension L/K and a finite separable extension K'/K, notes that K' tensor_K L is a finite product of fields, and asserts that if K' is unramified with respect to A then each factor is unramified with respect to B, and that if K' is tamely ramified with respect to A then each factor is tamely ramified with respect to B (source lines 34329-34345). The proof handles the two cases separately. Case (1) is short but real: the ring map A -> A' to the integral closure is finite etale, so B' = B tensor_A A' is finite etale over B and a finite product of Dedekind domains, hence is the integral closure of B in K' tensor_K L, and the conclusion follows (proof lines 34353-34359). Case (2) requires a reduction: one may replace K' by a larger extension already tame over A, and then the characterisation of tame extensions lets one assume K' contains K[pi^{1/e}] for some e invertible in kappa_A with K' unramified over A[pi^{1/e}] (proof lines 34362-34367). The proof then decomposes K[pi^{1/e}] tensor_K L into factors L_{e,j}, notes each L'_i is a finite separable extension of some L_{e,j_i}, and applies case (1) to conclude unramifiedness of L'_i over the localizations (B_{e,j_i})_m; this reduces the problem to showing that each L_{e,j} is tamely ramified over B (proof lines 34368-34381). The last computation is explicit and is where the tame hypothesis is consumed: writing the uniformizer of B and the e-th root relation, the proof exhibits A[pi^{1/e}] tensor_A B as a subring of B[y, z]/(y^{e'} - theta, z^e - u) with e' = e/gcd(e, t), which is a product of Dedekind domains each tamely ramified over B (proof lines 34384-34394). The non-routine content is the reduction step and the final explicit subring computation with the gcd exponent.

items.title: Epp's theorem: a finite weak solution exists for an extension of discrete valuation rings when the p-power core of the bigger residue field is separable over the smaller
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem (Epp) takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L and assumes that, when kappa_A has characteristic p > 0, every element of the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n} is separable algebraic over kappa_A; it concludes the existence of a finite extension K_1/K which is a weak solution for A -> B (source lines 35517-35528). The proof first dispatches the tame case: when the ramification index e is prime to p and the residue extension is separable, adjunction of an e-th root of a uniformizer produces A_1 whose maximal-ideal quotients are formally smooth over A by Abhyankar's lemma, hence weakly unramified (proof lines 35531-35543). The interesting case is residue characteristic p, and it is handled by a two-stage reduction followed by an explicit construction. First the proof uses the strict henselization lemma to assume the residue fields separably closed, which converts the theorem's hypothesis into the inclusion kappa_A containing the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n} (proof lines 35546-35555). Then it passes to completions: it shows that a finite M/K-hat that is a weak solution for A-hat -> B-hat and is a compositum of a separable extension with an extension obtained by adjoining a p-power root of pi descends to a finite K_1/K by the approximate-separable-extension lemma, and that formal smoothness of A -> A-hat propagates to A_1 -> A_1-hat, so that the two parts of the solutions-go-down lemma apply (proof lines 35557-35586). This leaves the complete case with separably closed residue fields, where the proof introduces k as the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n}, observes it is algebraically closed of characteristic p, builds a Cohen ring Lambda for k and a ring map Lambda -> A sending t to pi (proof lines 35588-35605), and proceeds to construct the weak solution explicitly. The reduction ladder (strict henselization, completion, descent, formal smoothness transfer) together with the Cohen-ring construction is independent research-level content.

items.title: The Picard group of a unique factorization domain is trivial
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that Pic(R) is trivial for a UFD (source lines 36183-36186). The proof is a genuine argument with a reduction and a prime-factorization comparison. It takes an invertible module L, uses that L is finite locally free hence torsion free and finite, and picks a nonzero element varphi of the dual so that I = varphi(L) is an invertible ideal of R (proof lines 36189-36193). Factoring a nonzero f in I as u p_1^{e_1} ... p_r^{e_r} into pairwise distinct primes, it then uses finite local freeness of L to find a_i not in (p_i) with I_{a_i} = (g_i), writes g_i = p_i^{c_i} g'_i with g'_i not divisible by p_i, and reads off e_i >= c_i (proof lines 36194-36203). The claim that I is generated by h = p_1^{c_1} ... p_r^{c_r} is then verified by the cover criterion: for any a with I_a principal, say I_a = (g), the set J of indices whose primes become nonunits in R_a is analysed, the prime factorizations of g and f are compared to get b_j <= e_j, and the compatibility I_{a a_j} = g R_{a a_j} = g_j R_{a a_j} together with uniqueness of factorization forces b_j = c_j (proof lines 36208-36218). The non-routine content is the two-level comparison of the same ideal after two different localizations.

items.title: Over a ring whose localizations satisfy the Warfield conditions every finitely presented module is a summand of a finite sum of quotients by principal ideals
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma assumes that every local ring of R at a maximal ideal satisfies the equivalent conditions of the generalized-valuation-ring lemma, and concludes that every finitely presented R-module is a summand of a finite direct sum of modules of the form R/fR (source lines 37736-37746). The proof is a genuine local-to-global argument. It reduces the conclusion to showing that Hom_R(M, B) -> Hom_R(M, C) is surjective for every short exact sequence with the property fA = A cap fB for all f, which is the characterisation established by the preceding module lemma (proof lines 37749-37757). Surjectivity is then checked after localization at maximal ideals, using that the localized sequences inherit the condition because an element of a localization can be written as a unit times an element of R and localization is exact, and using that the Hom modules localize for finitely presented M (proof lines 37758-37772). The conclusion at each maximal ideal is exactly the hypothesis, reduced through the localized modules lemma (proof lines 37773-37778). The final step is what makes the direct sum finite: since M is a finite R-module its image in the potentially infinite direct sum lies in a finite sub-sum (proof lines 37780-37785). The two non-routine moves are the localization of the condition fA = A cap fB and the finiteness bookkeeping at the end.

items.title: Differentials of the universal first order thickening restrict to the differentials of the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a formally unramified morphism h : Z -> X over S with universal first order thickening Z in Z', the lemma proves that the canonical map (h')^*Omega_{X/S} -> Omega_{Z'/S} becomes an isomorphism after restricting along Z. The proof computes the conormal sheaf of Z in Z' through the transitivity sequence and compares it with the differentials of the thickening, showing that the term contributing to the difference vanishes because h is formally unramified. The comparison of the two conormal and differential terms is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 1332-1342 statement, proof 1344-1357.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the category of schemes over a pushout with the category of pairs of schemes over the two factors glued along the image of the closed subscheme, which is the categorical content behind gluing along a closed immersion. items.title: Making several isolated fibre points finite by an etale neighbourhood of several points
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Given a locally finitely presented morphism and finitely many points of a fibre that are isolated in that fibre, the lemma produces an etale neighbourhood of the image point and, for each of the given points, finitely many open subschemes of the base change over which the morphism is finite and which separate the chosen points. The proof works point by point using the isolatedness of each point in its fibre to produce a finite piece, then assembles the pieces over a common etale neighbourhood so that the separation and finiteness conditions hold simultaneously. Making one etale neighbourhood serve all the points at once is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 12046-12091.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that base changing the normalization morphism along the henselization or strict henselization of the local ring at a point yields the normalization of that henselian local scheme. The proof first identifies the base change of the normalization to the local ring with the spectrum of the integral closure in the product of the residue fields of the generic points through the point, and then solves the resulting algebra problem by writing the henselization and strict henselization as filtered colimits of etale algebras, over which integral closure commutes. The reduction to a colimit statement about integral closure is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 5452-5496.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a formally smooth morphism of algebraic spaces the sheaf of differentials is locally projective and that its first cohomology vanishes on affine pieces. The proof chooses an etale chart, transports the statement to the chart using the compatibility of differentials with etale localisation, and then invokes the affine computation of the relevant cohomology. Passing the local projectivity and the cohomology vanishing through the etale chart is what the argument turns on rather than any single local computation. Retained author proof at lines 4768-4773 with the surrounding argument.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for quasi-coherent modules on the small etale site of an affine scheme, with the first module locally projective, the first cohomology of the internal hom sheaf vanishes. items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a bounded above complex of flat modules on a ringed site is K-flat (statement lines 3119-3123). The proof needs one reduction and one spectral-sequence computation: an arbitrary acyclic test complex is written as the termwise colimit of its truncations so that only bounded above test complexes have to be considered (proof lines 3126-3140), and in the bounded case the first quadrant spectral sequence of the double complex has E_1^{p,q} = H^p(L^bullet tensor K^q), which vanishes because K^q is flat and L^bullet is acyclic (proof lines 3141-3147). The non-formal content is the colimit reduction, which is also where boundedness of K^bullet is used. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one standard spectral-sequence identification.

items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for the unit f^*Rf_*K -> K to be an isomorphism for a flat morphism of ringed topoi and a bounded below K (statement lines 6343-6354). The proof is a reduction: one passes to cohomology sheaves, uses flatness of f so that pullback commutes with taking cohomology sheaves, H^j(f^*Rf_*K) = f^*H^j(Rf_*K), and the truncation identity H^j(Rf_*K) = H^j(Rf_* tau_{<= j}K) to reduce to a bounded K, after which hypothesis (3) puts each cohomology sheaf in the subcategory D' of the earlier upstairs lemma and boundedness plus stability under triangles puts K there (proof lines 6357-6364). The non-formal content is the combination of the truncation reduction with flatness; the claim is H2.

items.title: The sheaf condition is the bijectivity of the map to Cech H-0 for every covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises abelian sheaves among abelian presheaves on a site: the presheaf is a sheaf exactly when, for every covering, the natural map F(U) -> Cech H^0(U, F) is bijective (statement lines 850-864). The proof is the observation that Cech H^0 computes compatible families of local sections, so injectivity of the displayed map is the separation property and surjectivity is the gluing property, whose conjunction is the sheaf condition (proof lines 867-869). The content is the identification of the map, which is why the author can keep the proof to one sentence. The claim is H2: a definitional identification, stated rather than computed.

items.title: Cech cohomology computes cohomology when the covering has vanishing higher cohomology on all intersections
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives the standard criterion under which Cech cohomology of a covering computes cohomology: if the higher cohomology of F vanishes on every fibre product U_{i_0} x_U ... x_U U_{i_p} of members of the covering, then Cech H^p of the covering equals H^p(U, F) (statement lines 1505-1513). The proof identifies the hypothesis with the vanishing of the E_2 terms of the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence off the row q = 0, so the spectral sequence degenerates and the abutment is the E_2^{p,0} row (proof lines 1516-1520). The content is the correct reading of the hypothesis into the E_2 page. The claim is H2: one spectral-sequence degeneration, no further construction.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the relative cup product is associative, i.e. that the two bracketing composites of the displayed diagram agree in D(O') (statement lines 8421-8441). The proof does not compare the composites directly: it transposes them along the derived adjunction and computes the transposed source using monoidality of the derived pullback, Lf^*(Rf_*K tensor^L Rf_*L tensor^L Rf_*M) = Lf^*Rf_*K tensor^L Lf^*Rf_*L tensor^L Lf^*Rf_*M (proof lines 8444-8451), so that both sides are recognised as the same adjoint map into K tensor^L L tensor^L M. The non-formal move is this transposition and the resulting identification of two apparently different composites. The claim is H2: one adjunction computation, written out in a single display.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the standard Tor-criterion for flatness on a ringed site (statement lines 3359-3369). The forward direction is the author's one-line consequence of exactness and the vanishing of satellites (proof lines 3372-3373). The converse is the real content: given an injection G -> H with cokernel Q, one must use the long exact sequence of Tor to identify the kernel of F tensor G -> F tensor H as a quotient of Tor_1^O(F, Q), so the hypothesis kills it and tensorisation by F is seen to be exact (proof lines 3373-3381). The point is the exact-sequence bookkeeping that converts the vanishing for the cokernel into exactness at G, which is what makes the criterion usable. The claim is H2: one standard exact-sequence argument after an immediate first direction.

items.title: Higher direct images on a ringed site are the sheaf associated to the presheaf of cohomology of the inverse image
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the higher direct images of a module on a ringed site with the sheafification of the presheaf V -> H^i(u(V), F) (statement lines 746-757). The argument is a two-step unfolding of definitions: an injective resolution F -> I^bullet turns R^i f_* F into the i-th cohomology sheaf of f_* I^bullet (proof lines 760-765), and the cohomology sheaf of a complex of O_D-modules is the sheaf associated to the presheaf of kernels modulo images (proof lines 766-774), whose sections are then rewritten as sections of I^bullet over u(V), giving H^i(u(V), F) (proof lines 775-780). The non-formal content is the recognition that the sheafification step is what makes the naive presheaf equal to the derived pushforward. The claim is H2: two definitions unfolded in the right order, no additional construction.

items.title: A proper surjective morphism of locally quasi-compact spaces is a qc covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a proper surjective morphism f : X -> Y of locally quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces is a qc covering (statement lines 7584-7589). The proof has one genuine topological move: after covering the quasi-compact fibre X_y by finitely many opens U_{x_i} equipped with quasi-compact neighbourhoods E_{x_i}, one uses closedness of f to make Z = f(X minus the union of the U_{x_i}) a closed subset avoiding y, and surjectivity to place the resulting neighbourhood of y inside the finite union of the images f(E_{x_i}) (proof lines 7592-7603). The non-formal content is the choice of Z and the two properties of proper maps used to control it. The claim is H2: one finite covering argument with a standard closedness input.

items.title: Vanishing of Cech H1 on a cofinal system of coverings makes the map on sections surjective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for surjectivity of the map G(U) -> H(U) on sections of a short exact sequence of sheaves on a site (statement lines 1523-1536). The content is the combination of two coverings into one: the author must first take a covering on which the section lifts and then refine it, using cofinality, so that Cech H^1 of F vanishes (proof lines 1539-1545). The lifting defect on overlaps is then a Cech 1-cocycle with values in F (proof lines 1546-1552), whose triviality produces correction sections t_i in F(U_i) that make the corrected sections s_i - t_i glue (proof lines 1553-1561). The non-formal point is the cocycle computation and the gluing of the corrected sections. The claim is H2: one standard Cech-cocycle argument, written out in full.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the cohomological dimension of a one-dimensional affine scheme of finite type over a field K by 1 + cd(K) (statement lines 19650-19655). The proof routes everything through the Leray spectral sequence of f : X -> Spec(K) (proof lines 19658-19664): its E_2 terms involve the higher direct images R^q f_*F, whose stalks are identified with the cohomology of the pullback of F to the geometric fibre X_Kbar (proof lines 19665-19667), and the cited vanishing theorem for affine curves kills the row q at least 2, leaving only columns p at most cd(K) and hence no cohomology beyond 1 + cd(K) (proof lines 19668-19669). The non-formal content is the reading of the spectral sequence's vanishing region as a dimension bound. The claim is H2: one spectral-sequence bookkeeping argument with the cited vanishing as its only input.

items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma compares structure sheaves for two nested full subcategories C_1 subset C_2 of a big site: the inclusion is fully faithful, continuous and cocontinuous, and the canonical map g_!O_1 -> O_2 is an isomorphism (statement lines 7069-7099). Part (a) is immediate, but part (b) is a real computation of a colimit presheaf: surjectivity uses the affine line, which the hypotheses force to lie in C_1, to exhibit any section as a pullback (proof lines 7125-7131), while injectivity requires rewriting a finite sum of colimit generators as a single generator over a product of affine lines and then observing that a vanishing sum factors through a hyperplane, again an object of C_1 by the closure hypotheses (proof lines 7134-7153). The non-formal content is this use of the closure hypotheses, in particular products with affine space. The claim is H2: one serious colimit computation with both inclusions verified.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that constructibility of a sheaf on X_etale can be checked Zariski locally (statement lines 11788-11793). The proof is a short reduction with one non-formal step: for an affine open U one restricts the given open covering to U cap U_i, uses that restriction of a constructible sheaf to an open is constructible, and then invokes the same-chapter criterion producing a partition of U from constructible restrictions on a finite open covering (proof lines 11796-11804). The content is the reduction to the affine criterion, which is what makes the locality statement usable. The claim is H2: one reduction plus a cited criterion.

items.title: Finite locally free sheaves with isomorphic endomorphism algebras differ by an invertible twist
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma recovers a finite locally free sheaf from its endomorphism algebra: if SheafHom_O(F, F) and SheafHom_O(G, G) are isomorphic as O_S-algebras, then F and G differ by an invertible twist inducing that isomorphism (statement lines 9483-9495). The non-formal content is the construction: inside SheafHom(F, G) one takes the O_S-submodule L generated by the local isomorphisms whose conjugation is the given algebra isomorphism (proof lines 9501-9504), and then has to see that this L is invertible and that the evaluation F tensor L -> G is an isomorphism (proof lines 9505-9511). The author discharges both by an explicit reduction to the case of finite free modules over an affine base, where the two statements are direct matrix computations. The claim is H2: one construction plus two routine local verifications which the author delegates to the stated reduction.

items.title: Two morphisms of schemes with 2-isomorphic small morphisms of ringed topoi are equal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the small morphism of ringed topoi remembers the morphism of schemes: two morphisms a, b : X -> Y with 2-isomorphic small ringed topoi are equal (statement lines 5297-5304). The proof separates two layers. First, because the sheaves h_V are subsheaves of the final sheaf, the 2-isomorphism has to be the identity on each of them, which recovers a^{-1}(V) = b^{-1}(V) and hence equality on underlying topological spaces (proof lines 5309-5317). Second, a section f of O_Y(V) is a map h_V -> O_Y, and pulling back along the 2-isomorphism yields the displayed diagram whose commutativity, by definition of a 2-isomorphism of ringed topoi, forces the two structural maps to agree (proof lines 5318-5341). The non-formal content is the interplay of the two layers. The claim is H2: two short arguments, each ending in an equality of maps.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves base change for the pushforward along a proper morphism for arbitrary sheaves, with no finiteness hypothesis: g^{-1}f_*F = f'_*(g')^{-1}F (statement lines 18281-18287). The non-formal point is the stalk computation through the proper pushforward description, which is exactly where properness replaces the missing finiteness hypotheses. items.title: Relative Mayer-Vietoris sequence for the higher direct images along a morphism of schemes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces the relative Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence for the higher direct images along f : X -> Y when X is the union of two open subschemes U and V (statement lines 7222-7239). The proof is a short-exactness argument on complexes: after resolving F injectively on X_etale, one has to see that the complex-level sequence 0 -> f_* I^bullet -> a_* I^bullet|_U direct sum b_* I^bullet|_V -> c_* I^bullet|_{U cap V} -> 0 is short exact, which the author does by evaluating on sections over each object W of Y_etale, where the sequence becomes the Mayer-Vietoris sequence of the fibre products W x_Y X, W x_Y U, W x_Y V, W x_Y (U cap V) (proof lines 7252-7262). The remaining step is to recognise the restricted complexes as injective resolutions (proof lines 7263-7265), which is what converts cohomology sheaves into higher direct images of the restrictions. The claim is H2: one exactness check on sections plus one standard identification.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a flat quasi-compact morphism f : T -> S whose geometric fibres are connected, sections of an abelian sheaf on S_etale agree with sections of its inverse image over T (statement lines 5029-5038). The proof has three distinct parts: injectivity from surjectivity of f, a reduction of surjectivity to the equality of the two pullbacks to T x_S T via the fpqc description of pullbacks (proof lines 5047-5054), and the crux, the computation on a single geometric fibre where the restriction of F is a constant sheaf on the connected scheme T_{sbar}, so that every section is constant and both pullbacks correspond to the same element of F_{sbar} (proof lines 5055-5069). The non-formal content is this connectedness argument. The claim is H2: one descent reduction plus one geometric-fibre computation.

The claim is H2: three short but genuinely different arguments.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of ringed spaces f: X to Y with X the union of two open subsets, the lemma produces a distinguished triangle relating the derived pushforward of an arbitrary object of the unbounded derived category to the derived pushforwards of its restrictions along the three restrictions of f, and asserts functoriality in the object (statement lines 8249-8264). The proof follows the same pattern as the absolute case: represent E by a K-injective complex with injective terms, so that the four derived pushforwards are computed by the corresponding pushforwards of the restricted complexes, and identify the triangle with the one attached to a short exact sequence of complexes of sheaves on Y (proof lines 8266-8287). Exactness of that sequence is now derived from the relative Mayer-Vietoris lemma together with the vanishing of the first higher direct image of an injective module, rather than termwise as in the absolute case (proof lines 8288-8291). Functoriality is inherited from the functoriality of the K-injective construction (proof lines 8292-8294). The claim is H2: the same reduction as the absolute case with a different exactness input, plus a short functoriality argument.

items.title: Zero dimensional locally algebraic schemes are disjoint unions of spectra of local Artinian algebras
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally algebraic k-scheme X of dimension zero, the lemma shows that X is a disjoint union of spectra of local Artinian k-algebras of finite k-dimension and that in the algebraic case X is affine with X to Spec(k) finite (statement lines 3735-3742). The proof examines an affine open Spec(A): dimension zero of X gives dimension zero of A, Noether normalization then produces a finite injection k to A so that A has finite k-dimension, hence A is Artinian and therefore a product of finitely many Artinian local rings (proof lines 3745-3757). Since these are finite discrete spaces, X itself is discrete, so X is the disjoint union of its singleton connected components, each of which is the spectrum of such an algebra (proof lines 3759-3766). The algebraic case then uses quasi-compactness to write X as a finite disjoint union of such spectra, which is affine, and finiteness of X to Spec(k) was already seen (proof lines 3768-3775). The claim is H2: four standard algebra facts chained together, with no step referred to the reader.

items.title: The fibres of the canonical morphism to the spectrum of global functions are geometrically connected
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a proper scheme X over a field k with A = H^0(X, O_X), the lemma shows that the fibres of the canonical morphism X to Spec(A) are geometrically connected (statement lines 2012-2017). The proof first identifies A as a finite product of local Artinian k-algebras A_i finite over k, so that Spec(A) is the disjoint union of the singletons Spec(A_i) (proof lines 2020-2026), then reduces to an algebraically closed base field by base changing to the algebraic closure and using that the cohomology of the structure sheaf is preserved under flat base change (proof lines 2028-2052). In the algebraically closed case the argument is a clean local-ring computation: with X_i the inverse image of Spec(A_i), one has A_i = Gamma(X_i, O_{X_i}); if the fibre were disconnected then X_i would be disconnected, giving a nontrivial idempotent in the local ring A_i, a contradiction (proof lines 2054-2071). The claim is H2: standard inputs, but the reduction to the algebraically closed case and the idempotent argument are both written out and the local structure of A is what drives the proof.

items.title: Local rings under a ground field extension: faithful flatness and the residue field at a point of the base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a field extension K/k, a scheme X over k with Y = X_K, and a point y of Y over x in X, the four-part lemma describes the local map on local rings: it is faithfully flat, the residue field at y is the residue field of the kernel of the natural map kappa(x) tensor_k K to kappa(y), the local ring at y is a localization of the tensor product of the local ring at x with K, and the quotient by the maximal ideal of the local ring at x is the corresponding localization of kappa(x) tensor_k K (statement lines 237-253). The proof reduces to the affine case, where flatness is inherited from flatness of K over k and faithful flatness is then read off from the algebra lemma on local flat homomorphisms, and the residue field identification is quoted from the description of points of a fibre product (proof lines 255-261). The remaining two parts are proved by naming the relevant primes: the map of local rings factors through the tensor product with K localized at the contraction of the prime, and the second arrow is a localization at a prime that is the inverse image of the stated kernel (proof lines 262-279). Part (4) then follows by exactness of localization and of tensoring with K (proof lines 279-280). The claim is H2: a routine reduction with exactness bookkeeping, with no construction beyond identifying the relevant primes.

items.title: Free differentials, reducedness and a perfect base field force smoothness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k which is locally of finite type, has locally free differentials, is reduced, and has perfect base field, the lemma concludes that X to Spec(k) is smooth (statement lines 4556-4567). The proof works at an arbitrary point x: local Noetherianness gives finitely many irreducible components through x with generic points eta_i, reducedness identifies the local ring at each eta_i with the residue field, and perfection of k makes that finitely generated field extension separably generated, so its module of differentials is free of rank equal to the transcendence degree (proof lines 4570-4583). Comparing ranks along the components through x and using the dimension formula for the fibre at a point yields dim_x(X) = rank_x(Omega_{X/k}), which by the algebra criterion for smoothness over a field is exactly smoothness at x (proof lines 4584-4593). The claim is H2: five cited inputs assembled in the correct order, with the rank comparison across components through x as the step that makes the argument work at a non-generic point.

items.title: Geometric irreducibility can be tested over a separable algebraic closure
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k, the lemma shows the equivalence of geometric irreducibility, irreducibility of X_{k'} for every finite separable extension, and irreducibility of X over a separable algebraic closure (statement lines 1541-1556). The proof closes the three implications in a non-obvious order: assuming irreducibility over the separable closure, the author embeds an arbitrary extension k' into a larger field k-bar' over k-bar, uses that irreducibility is preserved by passing to the separable closure, and deduces irreducibility of X_{k'} by surjectivity of the projection, which gives geometric irreducibility (proof lines 1559-1566). For the converse direction the argument is more delicate: assuming X over the separable closure is reducible, the author exhibits an affine open covering and shows that if some member or some disjoint pair of members is already bad then X itself is reducible, so that one may assume the members meet after base change; then the algebra lemma on geometric irreducibility of finite type algebras produces a finite separable extension over which one member becomes reducible, hence X_{k'} is reducible (proof lines 1569-1588). The claim is H2: two standard inputs, but the reduction that forces a single affine member to be the culprit is a real step.

items.title: Galois action on irreducible components of a locally finite type scheme: continuity, finiteness of the defining extension, and orbits
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For X locally of finite type over k, the three-part lemma states that the action of the opposite absolute Galois group on the irreducible components of X over the separable closure is continuous for the discrete topology, that every such component is defined over a finite extension of k, and that for an irreducible component T of X the base change T over the closure is a finite union of components lying in one Galois orbit (statement lines 1788-1809). The proof is uniform: given a component of the base change, pick an affine open U meeting it, write U = Spec(A) with A a finite type k-algebra, and observe that the prime ideal cutting out the component is generated by finitely many elements of A tensor the closure, which therefore already lie in A_{k'} for a finite subextension k', so the stabilizer of the component contains an open subgroup; this gives (1) and (2) (proof lines 1811-1831). Part (3) then takes a component of the base change mapping to T, uses finiteness of its orbit, and applies the descent result for Galois invariant closed subsets to the union of the orbit (proof lines 1833-1844). The claim is H2: one finiteness observation reused three times plus a descent step, with no step left to the reader.

items.title: An invertible sheaf on an algebraic scheme over an infinite field is generated by dim(X) + 1 sections
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Over an infinite field k, for an algebraic k-scheme X and an invertible sheaf L generated by a linear map V to the global sections, the lemma produces a subspace W of V of dimension at most dim(X) + 1 which still generates L (statement lines 4259-4266). The proof is an induction on dim(X) driven by a nonvanishing condition: for every point x the composite of the given map with evaluation at x and reduction to the residue field is nonzero, and this is used twice. In the zero dimensional base case, X has finitely many points and infinitude of k allows a single vector on which none of the finitely many functionals vanishes (proof lines 4269-4282). In the induction step the author picks one point on each top dimensional irreducible component, chooses a vector nonvanishing at all of them, takes its zero scheme Z and observes that dim(Z) is strictly smaller than dim(X), applies the induction hypothesis to Z, and concludes that the span of the resulting subspace with that single vector generates L (proof lines 4285-4294). The claim is H2: a short induction whose content is the finite-avoidance choice of the vector and the strict dimension drop at the zero scheme.

items.title: Geometric reducedness from generic points: specialisation, the reduced local ring criterion and the function field case
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The four-part lemma relates geometric reducedness at a point to geometric reducedness at generic points of irreducible components: it is inherited by specialisations, it can be checked at a point with reduced local ring once it holds at all generic points specialising to it, it holds globally for a reduced scheme that is geometrically reduced at all generic points, and for a variety it is equivalent to separability of the function field (statement lines 554-573). Part (1) is immediate from the pointwise criterion and the permanence of geometric reducedness under localization (proof lines 576-581). Part (2) is the substantive translation: the hypotheses say that the local ring at x is reduced and that its localizations at minimal primes are geometrically reduced, which by the algebra criterion makes the whole local ring geometrically reduced, and the pointwise criterion lifts that to X (proof lines 584-590). Part (3) then follows trivially and part (4) is the separable function field criterion (proof lines 593-595). The claim is H2: one localization observation, one local-to-global passage through minimal primes and one field-theoretic equivalence.

The converse is the interesting half and runs by contradiction through the function field: after replacing X by its reduced structure one knows X is irreducible, hence integral; assuming there is a separably algebraic element alpha of the function field outside k, one chooses a nonempty affine open U with k contained in E = k(alpha) contained in O(U), so that E tensor_k E sits inside O(U times U) and one gets a dominant morphism to the spectrum of E tensor E; irreducibility of the self product then makes that spectrum connected (proof lines 1492-1512). But if E were bigger than k, its tensor square would be a product of at least two fields, since as a k-vector space it has dimension the square of dim_k(E), contradicting connectedness; hence E = k and the function field criterion gives geometric irreducibility (proof lines 1513-1520). The claim is H2: one reduction, one dominant-morphism argument and a short dimension count.

items.title: Geometric reducedness and geometric regularity of the normalization at a one dimensional point with separable residue fields
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally algebraic k-scheme X with normalization nu, and a point x whose local ring is reduced of dimension one and over which all residue fields of the normalization are separable over k, the lemma concludes that X is geometrically reduced at x and the normalization is geometrically regular at every point above x (statement lines 5101-5110). The proof first pins down the local structure upstairs: the local ring of the normalization at a point over x is again one dimensional by dimension theory, and being normal it is a discrete valuation ring, hence a regular local k-algebra with separable residue field; the author then invokes the formal smoothness criterion for regular local algebras with separable residue field and the theorem identifying formal smoothness with geometric regularity to conclude geometric regularity upstairs (proof lines 5112-5128). The second half transfers reducedness downward: injectivity of the local map from the reduced local ring at x into the geometrically reduced local ring upstairs forces the local ring at x to be geometrically reduced, and the pointwise criterion lifts that to geometric reducedness of X at x (proof lines 5130-5136). The claim is H3: the argument couples dimension theory, the discrete valuation ring structure of the normalization, formal smoothness over the residue field and the descent of geometric reducedness along an injective local map, none of which is a single citation.

The equivalence of the last two conditions then follows from the definition and the already proved equivalence of (3) and (4) (proof lines 2204-2206). The claim is H2: six conditions but a short cycle of implications, with the translation between the scheme statement and the algebra definition as the only step needing care.

items.title: A reduced locally finite type scheme over a field is geometrically reduced exactly when it contains a dense smooth open
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a reduced scheme X locally of finite type over a field k, the lemma proves that geometric reducedness is equivalent to the existence of a dense open subscheme smooth over k (statement lines 4693-4698). The forward implication uses that a dense smooth open contains the generic point of every irreducible component, where smoothness gives geometric reducedness, and then invokes the criterion that geometric reducedness can be checked at generic points (proof lines 4700-4707). The converse is a reduction: remove the nowhere dense union of the pairwise intersections of the irreducible components to make X a disjoint union of irreducibles, then use that an irreducible reduced scheme is integral, so that the structure sheaf at the generic point is the function field; geometric reducedness of that field makes it separable over k, and applying the separability-smoothness algebra lemma at the zero ideal shows that some principal localization of an affine chart is smooth, which is the required dense open (proof lines 4709-4726). The claim is H2: two standard input lemmas plus a reduction to the irreducible case, with the passage from a separable function field to smoothness of a localization as the key step.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'

items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X locally of finite type over a field k and a point x, the lemma proves that geometric regularity at x is equivalent to smoothness of X over k at x (statement lines 2543-2550). One direction is immediate: localizing to an affine chart, smoothness over k survives arbitrary field extensions and makes each of the Noetherian rings involved regular (proof lines 2559-2563). The converse is the substantive direction and is a purely inseparable trick: taking the residue field K at x, which is finitely generated over k, one finds a finite purely inseparable extension k' such that the compositum k'K is separable over k'; because the prime lifted to k' tensor A is the unique prime over the original one, its residue field is exactly that compositum, so regularity of the base changed local ring plus separability makes k' to A' smooth at the lifted prime, and smoothness descends back along the purely inseparable field extension (proof lines 2565-2582). The claim is H2: three cited algebra inputs, but the choice of the purely inseparable extension and the uniqueness of the prime above are what make the argument work.

items.title: Irreducible components of a base change map onto irreducible components, and the map is surjective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For an extension of fields K/k and a scheme X over k, the lemma shows that the image of every irreducible component of X_K is an irreducible component of X, so that there is a canonical surjective map on sets of irreducible components (statement lines 1621-1634). The proof first reduces to the case where K is the separable closure of k by using that the base change along separable algebraic closures induces a bijection on irreducible components (proof lines 1637-1651). The main step then uses the two structural properties of the projection: flatness makes generalizations lift, so generic points of components of the base change map to generic points of components of X, and integrality makes the projection universally closed, so the image of a component is closed; an irreducible closed subset containing a generic point of a component is that component (proof lines 1654-1664). Surjectivity is then read off from the fact that the inverse image of a component of X is a nonempty union of components of X_K, each of which maps onto it by the first part (proof lines 1665-1669). The claim is H2: a schematic reduction plus a two-property argument, with the correct combination of flatness and integrality being the point.

items.title: An irreducible scheme with a dense set of rational points is geometrically irreducible
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an irreducible scheme X over a field k with a dense set of k-rational points is geometrically irreducible (statement lines 1672-1677). By the finite separable characterization it suffices to show that X_{k'} is irreducible for every finite extension k'; so the author takes two irreducible components and proves they coincide. Both project onto X by the behaviour of components under base change, so if they were distinct their intersection would be a proper closed subset whose image under the finite projection is not dense by the standard result that finite morphisms send nowhere dense subsets to nowhere dense subsets (proof lines 1680-1690). Density of the rational points then supplies a k-rational point outside that image; its fibre consists of a single point with residue field k', which must lie in both components, giving the contradiction (proof lines 1691-1696). The claim is H2: a clean contradiction argument whose only inputs are the finite morphism property of the projection and the density hypothesis.

items.title: Finiteness, birationality and the reduced case for the normalization of a locally algebraic scheme
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally algebraic scheme X over a field k with normalization nu, the four-part lemma collects the expected properties: finiteness and dominance with a disjoint union of normal irreducible pieces, the factorization through the reduced scheme with the first map the normalization of the reduced scheme, birationality in the reduced algebraic case, and the variety case (statement lines 4902-4918). Part (1) is assembled in the proof: local Noetherianness gives finitely many irreducible components on quasi-compact opens so the definition of the normalization applies, the normalization is always a disjoint union of normal integral schemes with dominant morphism, and finiteness comes from the fact that a locally finite type scheme over a field is universally Nagata (proof lines 4920-4936). Part (4) then has a short argument of its own: separatedness of the normalization because it is finite over a separated scheme, combined with the previous parts (proof lines 4945-4946). Parts (2) and (3) are stated by the author as direct references to the Morphisms chapter (proof lines 4938-4942). The claim is H2: the content is the assembly in part (1) and the one-line argument for (4), with the rest being standard normalization facts.

items.title: Properness descends along an arbitrary field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: If X is a scheme over a field k and X_K is proper over K for some field extension K/k, the lemma concludes that X is proper over k (statement lines 2848-2853). The proof first extracts the finiteness conditions from the hypothesis: X_K is separated and quasi-compact, the morphism X_K to X is surjective, so X is quasi-compact, and separating affine opens upstairs shows X is quasi-separated (proof lines 2856-2865). The substantive step is a spreading-out argument: writing K as the colimit of its finitely generated k-subalgebras, the properness of X_K descends to some X_i over Spec(A_i), and a maximal ideal of A_i gives a finite extension k' of k by the Nullstellensatz; base change to k' is then proper, and since k'/k is finite both the projection X_{k'} to X and the composite to Spec(k) are proper, which yields separatedness and then properness of X over k (proof lines 2867-2889). The claim is H2: the descent through a filtered colimit plus the Nullstellensatz reduction to a finite extension is the part that cannot be read off formally.

items.title: The algebra of global functions of a proper scheme over a field and its connected components
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a proper scheme X over a field k, the eight-part lemma describes A = H^0(X, O_X): it is finite dimensional, a product of local Artinian k-algebras indexed by the connected components of X, a product of finite field extensions in the reduced case, a product of finite separable extensions in the geometrically reduced case, and A = k in the geometrically reduced and geometrically connected (or geometrically integral) cases, with the two irreducibility statements in between (statement lines 1932-1951). The proof pairs each part with one mechanism: finiteness from the finiteness of cohomology of a proper scheme over an affine base; the idempotent correspondence between product decompositions of A and decompositions of X, using that X is Noetherian so its connected components are open; reducedness to force the local factors to be fields; flat base change to the algebraic closure plus the separability criterion for finite extensions; and, in the last part, a counting argument with k_1 tensor k-bar being a product of [k_1 : k] copies of k-bar (proof lines 1953-2004). The claim is H2: eight parts, each settled by one standard input applied in the right way, with the idempotent correspondence as the only part that is not a one-line citation.

items.title: Quasi-affineness descends along an arbitrary field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: If X_K is quasi-affine for some field extension K/k, the lemma concludes that X is quasi-affine (statement lines 2782-2786). The proof is the same spreading-out pattern as for properness: surjectivity of X_K to X gives quasi-compactness of X, and the quasi-separatedness of X is deduced by separating affine opens upstairs, so that X may be assumed quasi-compact and quasi-separated (proof lines 2789-2797). Then K is written as the colimit of its finitely generated k-subalgebras, X_K is recognized as the limit of the base changes X_i, and quasi-affineness descends to some X_i; a maximal ideal of that finitely generated algebra gives a finite extension k' by the Nullstellensatz, and since X_{k'} is a closed subscheme of X_i it is quasi-affine, whence X is quasi-affine by descent along the finite locally free morphism X_{k'} to X (proof lines 2800-2813). The claim is H2: four cited inputs arranged so that quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are available before the limit argument is applied.

items.title: Quasi-projectivity descends along an arbitrary field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: If X_K is quasi-projective over K for some field extension K/k, the lemma concludes that X is quasi-projective over k (statement lines 2816-2821). The proof unpacks the definition into the three obligations and discharges them one at a time: for an affine open Spec(A) of X the base change is an affine open of X_K whose coordinate ring is a finitely generated K-algebra, so A is a finitely generated k-algebra by descent of finite generation; quasi-compactness descends by taking the image of the quasi-compact X_K; and the existence of a g-ample invertible sheaf for a finite type morphism is equivalent to having an ample invertible sheaf, which then descends along the field extension by the ample descent lemma (proof lines 2824-2841). The claim is H2: three bookkeeping steps, each resting on one cited result, with the equivalence between relative ampleness for a finite type morphism and the existence of an ample invertible sheaf as the organizing observation.
