items.title: The scheme theoretic image of a product of quasi-compact morphisms is the product of the scheme theoretic images
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For quasi-compact morphisms f: A to X and g: B to Y over a field k, the lemma shows that the scheme theoretic image of f times g is the product of the scheme theoretic images of f and g (statement lines 4480-4488). One inclusion is immediate from the universal property: the product morphism factors through Z times Z', so the scheme theoretic image W is contained in it (proof lines 4490-4494). The reverse inclusion is reduced to the affine case in two steps: scheme theoretic images are local on affine opens, so it suffices to treat X and Y affine, and quasi-compactness of f and g writes A and B as finite unions of affines, which may be replaced by their coproducts so that A and B are affine too (proof lines 4496-4507). In the affine case the three images are cut out by the kernels of the corresponding restriction maps on global functions, and the assertion follows from the identification of the global functions of A times_k B with the tensor product of the two coordinate rings (proof lines 4508-4517). The claim is H2: one universal-property inclusion and a localization-to-affine reduction, with the tensor product identification as the closing step.

items.title: Very ampleness from separating closed points and nonzero tangent vectors by sections
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Over an algebraically closed field, for a proper k-scheme X, an invertible sheaf L and a subspace V of H^0(X, L) that separates distinct closed points and separates nonzero tangent vectors from the vanishing locus, the lemma concludes that L is very ample and the canonical morphism to P(V) is a closed immersion (statement lines 4308-4324). The proof first notes that (1) makes V generate L, so the canonical morphism exists, and that it is proper; injectivity on closed points together with properness makes the morphism finite. The remaining and substantive step is surjectivity of O_{P(V)} to phi_*O_X, checked on stalks at closed points: condition (1) makes the fibre over p a singleton, so the stalk map is a finite module map between local rings, the residue fields are both k by the Nullstellensatz, and condition (2) makes the map on tangent spaces injective, i.e. the map on cotangent spaces surjective, which by the standard local criterion forces the stalk map to be surjective (proof lines 4326-4383). The claim is H2: the reduction to finiteness is quick, and the final local algebra step is the part that carries the content.

items.difficulty_reason: If X is smooth over the spectrum of a field k, the lemma shows that the closed points whose residue field is a finite separable extension of k form a dense subset (statement lines 4657-4666). The claim is H2: three standard inputs arranged so that the problem is transferred to affine space and back, with no step referred to the reader.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes f: X to S and a point x, the lemma exhibits a canonical isomorphism between the tangent space T_{X/S,x} and the kappa(x)-dual of the fibre of the relative differentials (statement lines 3013-3021). The forward map is constructed from a tangent vector theta, regarded as a map to the spectrum of the dual numbers over the residue field, by pulling back the differentials and taking the induced kappa(x)-linear map (proof lines 3024-3033). The rest is a chain of reductions: both sides only depend on the scheme theoretic fibre, and the local computation may be performed after replacing X by the spectrum of its local ring at x, which leaves both the tangent space and the fibre of the differentials unchanged (proof lines 3034-3044). The final step is the classical local statement: for a local ring over a field, a kappa-linear map from the module of differentials corresponds to a unique k-algebra map to the dual numbers agreeing with the residue map modulo epsilon, through the universal property of the module of differentials (proof lines 3046-3055). The claim is H2: one explicit construction, two harmless reductions and a standard universal-property argument.

items.title: The tangent space at a point with separable residue field extension as the dual of the cotangent space
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes f: X to S, a point x with s = f(x), and residue fields equal or related by a separable algebraic extension, the lemma identifies the fibre of the relative differentials with the cotangent space at x and consequently the tangent space with its dual (statement lines 3058-3077). The second identification is inherited from the previous duality lemma, so the content is the first: after reducing to the spectrum of the local ring of the fibre, the assertion becomes a purely algebraic statement about a local ring over a field k with separable algebraic residue field, where one must show that the canonical map from the cotangent space into the fibre of the module of differentials is an isomorphism (proof lines 3080-3093). The author rewrites the cotangent space as the first homology of the cotangent complex and reduces, by the transitivity exact sequence, to the vanishing of the differentials and of the first homology of the cotangent complex of the residue field over k; decomposing the separable algebraic extension as a filtered union of finite separable ones and using that a finite separable field extension is etale finishes the argument (proof lines 3094-3104). The claim is H2: three cited algebraic inputs with a clean transitivity reduction, but the passage through the cotangent complex is what makes the separability hypothesis do its work.

items.title: Disconnectedness descends along a morphism from a geometrically connected scheme over a Galois extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Let k-bar/k be a possibly infinite Galois extension, f: T to X a morphism of schemes over k; if T over the closure is connected and X over the closure is disconnected, the lemma concludes that X itself is disconnected (statement lines 1019-1025). The proof starts from a decomposition of X over the closure into two open and closed pieces and uses connectedness of T over the closure to place T entirely inside the preimage of one of them (proof lines 1028-1034). For each quasi-compact open W the two pieces descend to a finite Galois subextension k', and the author symmetrizes them over the finite Galois group to obtain Galois invariant open and closed pieces U'' and V'' of W_{k'}, which by the descent lemma come from open and closed subsets U_W and V_W of W (proof lines 1037-1053). The U_W are then glued over all quasi-compact opens using the compatibility supplied by a monotonicity statement that the author leaves as a verification, yielding a decomposition of X into two nonempty open and closed parts (proof lines 1055-1063). The claim is H2: the Galois symmetrization and the descent are the content, while the omitted compatibility is a bounded bookkeeping check.

items.title: Finiteness of the group of units modulo constants for an integral locally finite type scheme over an algebraically closed field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Over an algebraically closed field k, for an integral scheme X locally of finite type, the lemma shows that O^*(X)/k^* is a finitely generated abelian group (statement lines 5245-5250). The proof reduces the case at hand to the normal proper case by two moves that each need justification: since X is integral the restriction to a nonempty open is injective on functions, so one may assume X affine, and then X is realized as a nonempty open of a projective variety by taking the closure in projective space (proof lines 5253-5261). The normalization of that projective variety is finite, dominant and normal, and the author verifies that it stays a proper variety because properness is stable under finite morphisms and composition, and that it surjects onto the original variety because the image is closed and contains the generic point; since the inverse image of the affine open is then the scheme to which the previous normal case applies, the reduction is complete (proof lines 5263-5282). The claim is H2: the whole content is the reduction, with the previous normality lemma doing the actual counting.

items.title: Factorization through affine space of relative dimension r with unramified projection at a point
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism of affine schemes f: X to S and a point x, the lemma factors f as X to A^r_S to S with the first arrow unramified at x, where r is the dimension over kappa(x) of the fibre of the differentials (statement lines 3470-3485). The proof first makes sense of r: finiteness of the dimension comes from finite type of the differentials module, the identification with the fibre restricted module from base change of differentials, and the identification with the tangent space from the cotangent-space lemma (proof lines 3487-3495). The construction is then algebraic and explicit: write S = Spec(A), X = Spec(B), choose a surjection A[x_1,...,x_t] to B, renumber so that the images of dx_1,...,dx_r form a basis of the fibre of Omega_{B/A} at q, set P = A[x_1,...,x_r], and show Omega_{B/P,q} = 0 by Nakayama, since Omega_{B/P} is finite and its fibre at q vanishes by the choice of the variables; vanishing of the module of differentials is the criterion for unramifiedness (proof lines 3498-3517). The claim is H2: two standard identifications followed by an explicit renumbering-and-Nakayama argument.

items.title: Every finite separable extension of the completion of a discrete valuation field is obtained by base change from a finite separable extension of the field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K and completion, every finite separable extension of the completed fraction field arises by base change from a finite separable extension of K (statement lines 33813-33820). The proof combines three ingredients in one construction: a primitive element whose minimal polynomial is cleared into the completed ring, an approximation of that polynomial by a polynomial over A to within an arbitrarily high power of the maximal ideal, and Krasner's lemma, which turns the approximation into a root of the approximating polynomial inside the finite complete local algebra B, after which a Nakayama argument identifies the two quotients and the extension over K is read off (proof lines 33829-33851). The hypothesis of separability is used exactly where it is needed, namely to know that theta is not a root of the derivative so that Krasner applies. The counted span refers three times to earlier lemmas of this chapter, carried as navigation stubs.

items.title: Cutting a pseudo-coherent complex in two pieces after localizing, once a cohomology group is generated by its reduction at a prime
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is a local splitting result for a pseudo-coherent complex: if at a prime the natural map from the cohomology to the cohomology of the derived fibre is surjective in some degree, then after inverting one element outside the prime the upper truncation becomes perfect with amplitude starting at that degree and the complex splits as the direct sum of its two truncations (statement lines 19743-19763). The proof analyses the fibre in the critical degree through the image and kernel subspaces, lifts bases of the three pieces, and uses the surjectivity hypothesis precisely to lift the middle family, after which a localization makes the lifted elements a basis and the relevant quotient finite projective, so that the splitting statement can be applied (proof lines 19765-19818). The degree bookkeeping that identifies the quotient with the cokernel of the differential is what makes the upper truncation perfect. The counted span refers three times, once inside this chapter and twice to other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.

items.title: Three equivalent characterizations of tame ramification via adjoining a root of the uniformizer of exponent invertible in the residue field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement gives three equivalent characterizations of tame ramification of a finite separable extension of the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring: tameness itself, containment in an extension that is unramified after adjoining a root of the uniformizer of exponent invertible in the residue field, and the same with the exponent running through all multiples of a fixed invertible e_0 (statement lines 34184-34199). The proof closes the cycle by three steps: the equivalence of the second and third conditions is immediate, the second implies tameness by the composition and subextension statements, and tameness implies the third by a construction in which the ramification indices over the maximal ideals of the integral closure give the exponent e_0, the base is extended by a root of the uniformizer, the base change is decomposed into fields, and Abhyankar's lemma together with formal smoothness produces the unramified factor (proof lines 34202-34239). The least common multiple step and the passage from formal smoothness to unramifiedness are the two technical points. The counted span refers five times to earlier results of this chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.

primary.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-characterize-tame (canonical tag 0EXW), with the three equivalent conditions (source lines 34184-34199)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: the trivial implication (3) implies (2), the derivation of tameness from (2) through the compositum and subextension statements, and the construction starting from (1) with the ramification indices, the least common multiple e_0, the product decomposition of the base change and Abhyankar's lemma (source lines 34201-34240)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma relates I-adic completeness of a module to the vanishing of the torsion functors T(M, f) for f in I, and states the converse as surjectivity of the completion map when I is finitely generated (statement lines 25962-25970). Both directions are explicit: for the first, the proof reduces to the vanishing of Hom and Ext from A_f and then splits an arbitrary extension by an infinite series that converges precisely because M is complete, while for the second it builds, from an arbitrary sequence x_n, the extension of M by A_f whose relations are x_n - f e_{n+1} + e_n = 0, splits it using the vanishing assumption and finishes with the snake lemma (proof lines 25973-26014). The construction of the infinite series in part (1) and the construction of the universal extension in part (2) are the two substantive steps. The degree bookkeeping around the displayed sequence is what makes both assertions follow from the same computation. items.title: The derived tensor product with the quotients by the powers of an ideal agrees with the plain quotients as a pro-system
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a Noetherian ring, an ideal and a bounded complex of finite modules, the comparison between the derived tensor product with the quotients by the powers of the ideal and the plain quotients of the complex is an isomorphism of pro-objects (statement lines 29014-29023). The proof is a chain of three reductions: the quotient systems are replaced by Koszul systems, whose finite degree range makes the pro-isomorphism criterion applicable on cohomology in each degree, and the complex is then replaced by a bounded above complex of finite free modules so that the Artin-Rees consequence identifies both pro-systems with the quotients of the cohomology (proof lines 29025-29056). The degree bookkeeping and the last identification are what make the argument work. The counted span refers three times, twice to results of this chapter and once to a pro-isomorphism criterion of another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.

primary.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-derived-completion-plain-completion (canonical tag 0G9M), with the displayed inverse system of maps (source lines 29014-29023)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: the replacement of the quotients by the Koszul systems, the degree bound that allows the pro-isomorphism criterion to be applied on cohomology, and the conclusion through the Artin-Rees consequence after replacing the complex by a bounded above complex of finite free modules (source lines 29025-29057)

items.title: Every element of a projectively infinite-rank module over a ring with Noetherian radical quotient lies in a finite stably free direct summand
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement places a single element s of a projective module P inside a finite stably free direct summand, under the hypotheses that the quotient of the ring by its Jacobson radical is Noetherian and that the localizations of P at all maximal ideals have infinite rank (statement lines 39107-39114). The proof is a two-stage reduction rather than a formal consequence of the hypotheses: it first uses an auxiliary lifting result to reduce to the case where a finite stably free summand of R direct sum P contains (0, s), and then, inside that case, chooses a complement K' and splits off a free summand from it by a second auxiliary result, so that the kernel of the remaining projection is a direct summand of P containing s whose sum with R is finite free (proof lines 39116-39149). The two steps use the two auxiliary lemmas of the same section, which are carried as navigation stubs; all the bookkeeping with the complements and the final stable freeness argument are inside the counted span.

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: the reduction to R direct sum P through an auxiliary finite free module, the surjection onto a complement, the decomposition with the generated free summand and the final stably free identification (source lines 39116-39150)

items.title: When the Fitting ideal of a bounded complex with respect to a nonzerodivisor is principal, the shifted complex is locally free and its differential splits off
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement assumes that the Fitting ideal I_i(M, f) attached to a bounded complex of finite free modules and a nonzerodivisor is principal, and concludes that the shifted complex is locally free with explicit ranks and that its differential is the inclusion of a direct summand (statement lines 28049-28057). The proof works with the minors of the map (f, d^i): after localizing at f the rank is r_i, so the higher minors vanish, which makes the quotient by g-torsion finite locally free and f-torsion free, and the displayed complex of finite free modules is then used to identify the image of the second map with a projective module, after which the shifted term is recognised as a direct summand (proof lines 28059-28101). The subtle step is the passage from the cokernel to the cokernel modulo f-power torsion, which is what makes the projective module appear. The counted span refers twice, once to a fitting ideal statement of this chapter and once to the section in which the shifted complex is constructed, both carried as navigation stubs.

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: the generator g of the Fitting ideal and its divisibility, the vanishing of the higher minors after localizing at f, the split exact complex of finite free modules and the identification of the shifted term with the kernel of the second map (source lines 28059-28102)

items.title: The ideal of the Bockstein operators is finitely generated and its quotient makes the shifted complex have locally free cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement collects five facts about the ideal J of the Bockstein operators attached to a bounded complex of finite free modules over a nonzerodivisor, among them its finite generation, the finite presentation of the quotient C, the vanishing of J along a locus described in two equivalent ways, and the local freeness of the cohomology of the shifted complex after tensoring with C (statement lines 28197-28228). The proof identifies the two descriptions of the locus, then proves the finiteness from boundedness of the complex, then obtains the vanishing of J on the locus by localizing and using that the shifted terms are finite locally free, so that the localized reduction splits in a way compatible with the map (1, d^i) and the universal property of J_i applies (proof lines 28230-28259). The final part is proved by exhibiting two diagrams whose horizontal arrows are compatible with direct sum decompositions, which identifies the differential as an injection of a summand and makes the cohomology a quotient of finite projective modules (proof lines 28264-28305). The counted span refers three times to earlier lemmas of the same section, all carried as navigation stubs.

items.title: Equidimensionality and catenarity descend along a flat local map of Noetherian rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a flat local homomorphism A -> B of local Noetherian rings with B catenary and equidimensional, the fibres B over pB stay equidimensional and the source A is again catenary and equidimensional (statement lines 32388-32397). The proof reduces everything to one dimension computation: for a prime q minimal over pB the special fibre of A_p -> B_q is zero dimensional, so dim(A_p) equals dim(B_q), and equidimensionality plus catenarity of B make dim(B/q) independent of q (proof lines 32400-32413). The same computation applied to the quotients by a prime gives the dimension formula for A, and applied to an immediate specialization it shows that the dimension function drops by exactly one, which is the catenarity criterion (proof lines 32413-32434). The references to the dimension formula and to going down are pointers to standard results of another chapter; the argument that turns them into the two conclusions is inside the counted span.

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: the dimension computation through a minimal prime over pB, the equidimensionality of B over pB, the dimension formula for A and the catenarity argument (source lines 32399-32435)

items.title: The functors Can and H^0 are quasi-inverse equivalences for the glued category of a flat cover with a finitely generated ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is the main equivalence theorem for the glued category attached to a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R over I isomorphic to S over IS: the functor Can and the functor H^0 are quasi-inverse equivalences between modules over R and the glued category (statement lines 24812-24821). The proof has to exhibit the second composite as the identity, which it does by localizing the comparison morphism at each generator so that the kernel and cokernel become systems concentrated in the first component, deducing injectivity from left exactness of H^0, then turning the resulting exact sequence into a description of the local components and finally constructing a module E from an extension of the power torsion cokernel by the image of H^0 whose image under Can is the given object (proof lines 24823-24878). The two genuinely independent inputs, namely the identification of the comparison after localization and the extension lemma for power torsion modules along the flat cover, are what make the argument nontrivial, and the whole construction of E is inside the counted span. The proof refers four times to earlier lemmas of the same chapter, carried as navigation stubs.

primary.label: author proposition environment with its own label proposition-equivalence (canonical tag 05ER); statement at source lines 24812-24821

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the proposition: the comparison morphism Psi, the localization computation that makes it an isomorphism after inverting each f_i, the resulting exact sequence and the Xy-pic diagram exhibiting an object whose image is the given glued object (source lines 24823-24879)

items.title: Mittag-Leffler property and bounded kernels for the systems of homomorphisms and isomorphisms of the quotients M over I^n M
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement collects four facts about the systems obtained by reducing Hom and Isom groups modulo powers of an ideal: the Mittag-Leffler property, a uniform bound on the kernels and cokernels of the comparison maps, and the identification of the limits with Hom and Isom between the completed modules (statement lines 29059-29078). The proof replaces the Hom groups by the cohomology of a two-term complex obtained by dualizing a presentation of M, imports the Artin-Rees constant to get the Mittag-Leffler property and the uniform bound, and then identifies the limit with the completion of Hom, which is where the completeness of the completions is used (proof lines 29081-29109). The final part transfers the result to isomorphisms by applying the homomorphism case twice and invoking Nakayama, so the four assertions are proved in one coherent argument. The counted span refers four times, three of them to labelled results of another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs; the complexes, the limits and the isomorphism argument are inside the span.

items.title: The shifted-complex construction descends to an additive functor on the derived category for a nonzerodivisor
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement constructs the additive functor on the derived category that extends the shifted-complex construction, showing that on any object represented by a complex of torsion free modules it agrees with the shift of that complex, and warning in a footnote that the functor is not exact (statement lines 27531-27540). The proof is a localization argument: it isolates the subcategory of torsion free modules, invokes the localization criterion to reduce the construction to the existence of a resolution by torsion free complexes, obtains that from K-flat resolutions by flat modules, and then checks that the shifted construction on the subcategory sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms so that it factors through the localized category (proof lines 27542-27575). The reduction step is what makes the definition independent of the chosen representative. The counted span refers five times, three times to results of this chapter and twice to results of other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement assumes a domain as base, geometric unibranchness at the prime, unramifiedness of the map at the prime and injectivity of the localized map, and concludes that the map becomes etale after inverting one element outside the prime (statement lines 31762-31774). The proof first replaces the map by a standard etale cover with a surjection onto the given ring, then carries out a reduction to the case where that cover is a domain: it uses that the cover is reduced, that its fibre over the generic point is a finite product of fields so the minimal primes lie over the generic point, that a small number of them exist, and that geometric unibranchness makes the localization of an etale algebra at a prime a domain, after which an element separating the minimal primes produces the reduction (proof lines 31776-31797). The final step is a contradiction argument that invokes the previous lemma on ideals meeting the source domain, which is precisely why injectivity at the prime enters (proof lines 31799-31814). The counted span refers seven times, three times to results of this chapter and four times to other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.

items.title: Producing a totally ramified finite Galois extension that either solves the ramification weakly or puts the degree p extension on finite level
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a tower A inside B inside C of discrete valuation rings with A of mixed characteristic, A to B weakly unramified, B containing a primitive p-th root of unity and the top extension Galois of degree p, and concludes the existence of a finite Galois extension of K, totally ramified over A, that either is a weak solution for the tower or makes the top extension one of finite level (statement lines 35087-35100). The proof is a case analysis driven by Kummer theory and by the order of the element whose p-th root generates the top extension: in the case where that order is prime to p a totally ramified degree p extension is built so that the compositum has the required weak unramifiedness, and in the remaining case the base is replaced so as to reduce to a unit, after which either the residue class is not a p-th power and weak unramifiedness follows from the pre-purely-inseparable case, or the equation can be brought to the form y^p = 1 + pi b, which exhibits finite level with an explicit element (proof lines 35102-35139). Both alternatives of the conclusion are produced by explicit constructions. The counted span refers four times, three of them to earlier results of this chapter and one to Kummer theory in another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.

items.title: Residue field extensions of a finite group action are normal, and the decomposition group surjects onto the automorphism group
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a finite group acting on a ring and a prime lying over a prime of the invariant subring, and asserts first that the residue field extension is algebraic normal and then that the decomposition group maps onto its automorphism group (statement lines 32703-32716). The proof first reduces to the case where the prime below is maximal, which keeps the decomposition group and the residue fields unchanged, then exploits the single orbit of the primes over it: an element vanishing at all the other primes is chosen through the Chinese remainder theorem, the product of its translates splits completely and forces the required minimal polynomial to split, and the same element is reused after splitting the extension into a purely inseparable and a Galois part to realize every Galois conjugate by a translate under the decomposition group, the infinite case being excluded by a degree count (proof lines 32718-32773). The union of the normality argument and the conjugate realization is what makes the surjectivity statement work. The counted span refers seven times, twice to results of this chapter and five times to results of other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.

items.difficulty_reason: The statement is the local form of the perfectness criterion for a flat local ring homomorphism A -> B whose fibre B over m_A B is regular of dimension d, and it is content with a single cohomological input at the closed point of A, namely the vanishing of H^i(K tensor^L_A kappa(m_A)) outside [a, b] (statement lines 20228-20244). What makes the argument work is that everything is reduced to a single fibre, which is why only the closed point appears in the hypothesis. items.title: Over a regular ring perfect modules are exactly the finite modules and perfect complexes are those with bounded finite cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes perfect objects over a regular ring in two forms: a module is perfect exactly when it is finite, and a complex is perfect exactly when it is bounded with finite cohomology (statement lines 19114-19122). The proof of the first part is a covering argument: taking a finite free resolution of a finite module, the loci where the successive syzygies are free form an increasing sequence of opens because projectivity over a local ring is freeness, the local rings being regular have finite global dimension so a large syzygy is free at each prime, and Noetherianity of the spectrum makes the cover stabilize at some finite stage, after which the truncated resolution exhibits the module as perfect (proof lines 19124-19161). The second part is then deduced from the first by applying it to each cohomology module of a bounded complex. The counted span refers to six labelled results of another chapter and to one criterion of this chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.

items.title: A bounded above inverse system of derived objects with compatible reduction is derived complete and recovers each term by reduction
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement takes a ring A, an ideal I, objects K_n of the derived categories of the quotients A over I^n with compatible transition maps, and three hypotheses (Noetherianity, boundedness above, and the reduction isomorphisms), and concludes both that the derived limit K is derived complete and that reducing K modulo I^n recovers K_n (statement lines 28470-28483). The proof combines a general criterion with an explicit construction: derived completeness comes from the criterion on derived limits, while the second assertion requires choosing bounded above complexes of free modules over each quotient and lifting the transition maps so that the reductions are honest isomorphisms of complexes, after which K is the limit of the system and that limit is a bounded above complex of flat modules, so that the reductions can be computed termwise and the system stabilizes at the n-th term (proof lines 28485-28516). The stabilization step is what makes the reduction of K isomorphic to K_n, and it depends on the strictness of the lifted maps. The counted span refers three times to results of this chapter and twice more to items of the same chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.

items.title: Exactness of the Cech sequence of a module is equivalent to bijectivity of the comparison map on f-power torsion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes the exactness of the Cech sequence of an arbitrary module for a ring map inducing isomorphisms modulo all powers of a fixed element: exactness on the right always holds, exactness on the left is equivalent to injectivity of the comparison map on power torsion, and exactness in the middle is equivalent to its surjectivity, with the resulting characterization of glueability and its specialization to glueing pairs and to the completion (statement lines 25364-25385). The reduction to the universal case and the presentation step are the substantive moves. items.difficulty_reason: 命题是形式代数空间沿 I-进完备 Noether 基的代数化：给定逐层有限且 proper 的相容系统 {Y_n}，要造出有限 Y → X 使各层为 Y 的基变换且 Y 在 S 上 proper。证明的关键是把 Y_n 的前推结构层当作凝聚模的相容系统，用 Grothendieck 存在定理（及其重述形式）代数化，再用 completions 函子的完全忠实性把乘法映射拼成代数结构，最后取相对谱。不能一眼完成的是最后两步：代数结构不是自动的，需由完全忠实性从各层「拼」出来。原文位于第 10193–10236 行。

items.difficulty_reason: 命题要在给定整态射 f : X -> Y 与 Y 的一个闭点 y 之下，把 f 分解为 X -> X' -> Y，使 X -> X' 在 X'_y 外同构、且 X'_y 只有唯一一点、其剩余域恰为 k。证明的实质是构造 R-代数 C' 并控制纤维积的点：要证明纤维只剩一点，必须先把 k/R 写成有限可分扩张，再用纤维积代数的点论把「唯一性」从 k 搬到 k 的可分扩张上。不能常规完成的是唯一性那一步，它依赖对 C' 结构的精确控制。原文位于第 7273–7346 行。

items.difficulty_reason: 这条引理是 Grothendieck 存在定理证明里最重的一段：给定逐层系统 (F_n) 与额外对象 H，要造出整体凝聚模并同时控制其支集的 proper 性。关键操作有两处：一是用「核被 K 的幂零化」把核的支集压进 G_1 的支集；二是把核与 H 的支集相并，借助闭支集并集仍 proper 的引理得到结论。不能常规完成的是第一步——零化性必须从假设 (1) 的逐层等价与映射的构造中读出，而不是由定义直接给出。原文位于第 9827–9938 行。

items.title: The equivariant Stolz positive scalar curvature exact sequence is exact
items.author: Massimiliano Puglisi; Thomas Schick; Vito Felice Zenobi
items.work: Stolz Positive Scalar Curvature Structure Groups, Proper Actions and Equivariant 2-Types
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 21 (2025) journal PDF and native TeX; acquired 2026-09-30; exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that the three equivariant bordism groups defined earlier fit into a G-equivariant version of the Stolz positive scalar curvature exact sequence, with the three maps given by taking the boundary, forgetting the metric, and viewing a closed manifold as a manifold with empty boundary (statement lines 367-376). The proof is a complete case-by-case verification: it first checks that each composite of two consecutive maps vanishes, then constructs an explicit preimage for every class that lies in a kernel, the last case by gluing two bordisms along their common boundary and passing to the cylinder of the resulting closed manifold (proof lines 377-431). The step that carries the content is the last inclusion, since it requires building a bordism in the relative group out of two given ones; the other five verifications are direct consequences of the definitions. The argument is self-contained, the citation being only a pointer to the non-equivariant statement. H2.

items.title: Every connected semisimple Lie group with finite centre has a lattice whose finite-dimensional representations are integral
items.author: Dave Witte Morris
items.work: A Cohomological Proof that Real Representations of Semisimple Lie Algebras Have Q-Forms
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 11 (2015) article 034, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2015.034; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the arithmeticity corollary of the paper (author cor at source lines 115-125, label LattAppl): every connected semisimple Lie group with finite centre has a lattice Gamma such that G/Gamma has finite volume and every finite-dimensional real representation of G maps Gamma into a conjugate of the integral matrices. The proof (source lines 362-376) is the author's own, headed Proof of Corollary LattAppl, and it is short but it assembles three separate ingredients in the right order: the arithmetic lattice coming from the integral points of an adjoint group, the conjugation that makes the differential of an arbitrary real representation rational using the R-universal form, and the descent from the universal cover to a finite-index subgroup of the image (proof lines 367-375). The authors of the source cite this corollary as an application of the main theorem rather than as a new technique, and the card keeps the author's own level of detail. H2.

items.title: R-universality of the special linear Lie algebra over a central division algebra is exactly the split-or-quaternion condition
items.author: Dave Witte Morris
items.work: A Cohomological Proof that Real Representations of Semisimple Lie Algebras Have Q-Forms
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 11 (2015) article 034, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2015.034; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the classification of R-universality for the special linear Lie algebra over a central division algebra (author prop at source lines 541-545): it holds exactly when the division algebra is Q itself or a quaternion algebra that does not split over R. The proof (source lines 547-564) computes the Tits algebras at the powers of the highest weight of the standard representation as the tensor powers of the division algebra (proof lines 550-552), then reads the two implications off the author's division-algebra description of R-universality, using that the real Tits algebra is either R or the quaternions in the forward direction and that the square of a quaternion algebra is Brauer trivial in the converse (proof lines 554-563). The whole content is the Brauer-class computation and the parity split. H2.

items.title: R-universality of an odd-dimensional special orthogonal Lie algebra in terms of the even Clifford algebra
items.author: Dave Witte Morris
items.work: A Cohomological Proof that Real Representations of Semisimple Lie Algebras Have Q-Forms
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 11 (2015) article 034, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2015.034; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the R-universality criterion for an odd-dimensional special orthogonal Lie algebra (author prop at source lines 632-636): universality holds exactly when the even Clifford algebra of the symmetric matrix splits over Q or fails to split over R. The proof (source lines 638-641) is short and reduces the whole criterion to a single Brauer class: the oddness of n makes the centre of the spin group of order two, so only one Tits algebra occurs, and that algebra is Brauer equivalent to the even Clifford algebra, whose splitting behaviour over the two fields is exactly the stated alternative. The card keeps the author's own level of detail. H2.

items.title: A weight-splitting test for R-universality of a semisimple Lie algebra that splits over a quadratic extension
items.author: Dave Witte Morris
items.work: A Cohomological Proof that Real Representations of Semisimple Lie Algebras Have Q-Forms
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 11 (2015) article 034, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2015.034; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the splitting criterion for R-universality (author cor at source lines 203-216, whose own label is commented out in the author file and whose displayed hypothesis carries the label SplitOverQuadIff-weight): if an algebra that splits over a quadratic extension satisfies the stated invariance-and-vanishing test for every dominant weight, then it is R-universal. The proof (source lines 218-241) is the author's own and has a real mechanism: it uses the author's proposition on highest weights twice, once over R and once over Q, to reduce the hypothesis to irreducibility statements (proof lines 224-231), and then uses the quadratic-splitting dichotomy for the rational representation to count irreducible constituents on both sides and conclude that the rational representation is a Q-form of the real one (proof lines 233-240). The counting step is what makes the criterion sufficient. H2.

items.title: R-universality of the special unitary Lie algebra of a Hermitian form over a quaternion division algebra
items.author: Dave Witte Morris
items.work: A Cohomological Proof that Real Representations of Semisimple Lie Algebras Have Q-Forms
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 11 (2015) article 034, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2015.034; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the classification of R-universality for the special unitary Lie algebra of a Hermitian form over a division algebra with an anti-involution (author prop at source lines 566-575): universality holds exactly when the division algebra is an imaginary quadratic extension of Q and either the size is odd or the determinant condition on the Hermitian matrix is satisfied. The proof (source lines 577-609) is a case analysis driven by Tits algebras: it first shows the extension is imaginary using the author's lemma on inner forms (proof lines 578-580), identifies the Tits algebra of the natural representation with the division algebra and forces the division algebra to be the extension itself (proof lines 582-589), and then splits the remaining weights into those moved and those fixed by the star-action, which is where the parity and determinant conditions arise (proof lines 591-609). H2.

items.title: A sharp lower-bound construction for ordered hypergraph matchings along a fixed chain of ordered partitions
items.author: Lisa Sauermann, Dmitrii Zakharov
items.work: A Sharp Ramsey Theorem for Ordered Hypergraph Matchings
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the sharp lower-bound construction of the paper (author theorem at source lines 455-459, label thm-paramteters-lower-bound-stronger): for any chain of ordered partitions of r and any prescribed positive integers m_P, there is an ordered r-uniform hypergraph matching of the displayed product size whose every pair of edges forms a pattern in the union of the pattern families and whose pattern-cliques stay below m_P. The proof (source lines 575-593) is the author's own, headed Proof of Theorem thm-paramteters-lower-bound-stronger, and it iterates the author's partite construction along the chain while keeping the clique-size bounds, which is what produces the exact product size. The theorem is the statement whose maximisation over chains gives the paper's lower-bound theorem, as the author notes immediately after it. H2.

items.author: Lisa Sauermann, Dmitrii Zakharov

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the construction lemma that turns a monotone point set into an ordered hypergraph matching with prescribed clique-size bounds (author lemma at source lines 556-560, label obs-construction-partite). The proof (source lines 564-571) is the author's own, headed Proof of Lemma obs-construction-partite, and it is a clean correspondence argument: the patterns of the finest partition are parameterised by the monotone functions tau, the author's multi-dimensional Erdos-Szekeres theorem provides a point set with distinct coordinates whose tau-monotone sequences are bounded by the prescribed integers, and the coordinates of each point produce the edges of the matching, so that a P-clique corresponds precisely to a monotone sequence and the bounds transfer (proof lines 565-571). The lemma is the building block that the paper's lower-bound theorem iterates. H2.

The two steps with real content are the production of the idempotent of the quotient through the characteristic polynomial and the appeal to idempotent lifting, and both are displayed.

items.title: The inclusion of the big affine h site into the big h site is cocontinuous and induces an equivalence of topoi
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme S with a big h site containing it, the lemma asserts that the inclusion functor from (Aff/S)_h to (Sch/S)_h is cocontinuous and induces an equivalence of topoi from the sheaves on the affine big site to the sheaves on the big site (statement lines 10571-10579). The proof is an exhaustion of the five hypotheses of the criterion for a special cocontinuous functor: cocontinuity holds because every h covering of an affine T/S is refined by a standard h covering, by the approximate h cover lemma, which is condition (1); continuity is immediate because a standard h covering is an h covering, giving (2); conditions (3) and (4) follow from full faithfulness of the inclusion of affine schemes into schemes; and condition (5) follows because every scheme has an affine open covering, which is an h covering (proof lines 10582-10596). Deciding which of the five conditions carries real content - cocontinuity, via the standard covering refinement - and which are immediate is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: After a V-admissible blowing up a proper morphism becomes an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of the closure of a closed subset where it was already one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism f : X -> Y of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, a quasi-compact open V of Y with preimage U, and a closed subset T of V over a neighbourhood of which f|_U is an isomorphism, the lemma produces a V-admissible blowing up Y' -> Y such that the strict transform f' : X' -> Y' is an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of the closure of T in Y' (statement lines 9607-9617). The proof isolates the obstruction as the closed subset T' where f|_U fails to be an isomorphism, disjoint from T, and then separates the two by constructible approximations: since V is spectral one finds constructible closed T_c containing T and T'_c containing T' with empty intersection, explicitly via quasi-compact opens (proof lines 9620-9629). A disjoint-locally-closed separation lemma lets one blow up so that the two closures become disjoint, after which the complement Y_0 of the closure of T'_c carries a V_0-admissible blowing up making the strict transform an isomorphism by the Zariski-after-blowup lemma, and an extension result for admissible blowups lifts that local solution back to a V-admissible blowing up of Y (proof lines 9630-9643). Separating the obstruction from T by constructible approximations and then lifting the local solution is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: For a smooth affine morphism with geometrically irreducible fibres the functor of flatness in dimensions at least d is a finite disjoint union of the functors of fibrewise freeness of a given rank
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a smooth morphism X -> S of affine schemes with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension d and a quasi-coherent module F of finite presentation, the lemma asserts that the functor F_d defined by flatness in dimensions at least d is the disjoint union of the functors H_p of fibrewise freeness of rank p, for p running from 0 to some c (statement lines 7777-7786). The proof first bounds the ranks: since X is affine and F is of finite presentation, F is generated by c elements, so the dimension of F_x tensor kappa(x) never exceeds c and hence H_p is empty for p greater than c, which also shows the inclusion of the disjoint union into F_d (proof lines 7789-7794). The content is then identified precisely: for a base change F_T flat in dimensions at least d over T and a point t of T, one must show that F_T is free of some rank r on an open neighbourhood of the generic point of the fibre X_t, because then H_r contains the image of that neighbourhood, which is an open neighbourhood of t; this existence is quoted from the flat-and-free-at-a-point-of-the-fibre lemma (proof lines 7795-7802). Identifying the two functors through the generic point of the fibre is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The symbol of a one dimensional module is the product of the symbols of its minimal prime quotients raised to the local multiplicities
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite module M of dimension one over a Noetherian local ring A and nonzerodivisors a, b on M, the lemma computes the symbol d_M(a, b) as the product over the minimal primes q_i of the support of M of d_{A/q_i}(a, b) raised to length_{A_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}) (statement lines 17576-17591). The proof is an induction along a filtration rather than a direct computation: it takes a filtration 0 = M_0 in M_1 in ... in M_n = M whose successive quotients are A/p_j for primes p_j, uses that each p_j is either one of the minimal primes q_i of the support or the maximal ideal, and shows that for a fixed i the number of j with p_j = q_i equals the length of M at q_i (proof lines 17594-17606). The recurrence is then read off from the two structural lemmas: when p_j is a minimal prime the symbol multiplies by d_{A/q_i}(a, b), and when p_j is the maximal ideal the symbol is unchanged (proof lines 17607-17620). Setting up the filtration so that the multiplicities appear as the number of occurrences of each minimal prime is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: On a neighbourhood of the closed subset where the derived limit lives, the complex has a single cohomology sheaf of finite presentation reducing correctly along the thickenings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In the existence situation, with K as in the computation lemma and X_0 the closed subset of points lying over the common closed subset of Spec(A), the lemma asserts the existence of an open W containing X_0 with three properties: the cohomology of K vanishes on W except in degree 0, the resulting module F = H^0(K)|_W is of finite presentation, and F_n = F tensor O_{X_n} (statement lines 8180-8194). The proof is a pointwise reduction to an inductive statement about a complex of finite free modules: for a point x of X_0 it takes an affine open U = Spec(B), chooses a surjection P -> B with P smooth over A, and uses relative pseudo-coherence to represent Ri_*K by a bounded above complex F of finite free P-modules, after which tensoring with A_n computes the cohomology of F as M_n in degree 0 (proof lines 8203-8225). If the top nonvanishing index i is at most 0 the three properties hold outright; otherwise the rank of the differential F^{i-1} -> F^i is maximal at x, hence maximal on a neighbourhood, so after a principal localisation the map is surjective and splits, which replaces F by a shorter complex and closes by induction on i (proof lines 8226-8241). The truncation-by-splitting induction on the top index is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Independence of the Gysin-at-infinity class from the choice of the proper model, up to the induced morphism at infinity
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Extending the Gysin-at-infinity lemma, the statement says that for a proper morphism g : W' -> W which is an isomorphism over A^1_X, the classes C' in A^0(W'_infinity -> X) and C in A^0(W_infinity -> X) constructed there satisfy g_{infinity,*} o C' = C (statement lines 10107-10114). The proof sets b' = b o g, writes i'_infinity for the inclusion of W'_infinity, and compares the two constructions on a single cycle class: for alpha in CH_k(X) one chooses beta' in CH_{k+1}(W') restricting to the flat pullback of alpha on (b')^{-1}A^1_X, observes that its pushforward beta = g_*beta' restricts to the flat pullback of alpha on b^{-1}A^1_X, so beta is an admissible choice in the definition of C, and then invokes the compatibility of the Gysin map with the proper pushforward to get i_infinity^* beta = g_{infinity,*}(i'_infinity)^* beta' (proof lines 10116-10125). Since this holds after any base change by X' -> X locally of finite type, the two classes agree (proof lines 10126-10128). Choosing beta as a pushforward so that both constructions compute the same value is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The Gysin class of a virtual normal sheaf of rank r caps the fundamental class of a Cohen-Macaulay situation to the fundamental class of the intersection
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a virtual normal sheaf N of a closed subscheme Z of X, a morphism Y -> X locally of finite type, and integers r, n, the lemma asserts that under four hypotheses - N locally free of rank r, every component of Y of dimension n, dim(Z x_X Y) <= n - r, and Cohen-Macaulayness of O_{Y,xi} at every point xi of Z x_X Y of dimension n - r - the Gysin class c(Z -> X, N) caps [Y]_n to [Z x_X Y]_{n-r} (statement lines 12127-12142). The proof reduces the global statement to a local one: since the target has dimension at most n - r its Chow group is freely generated by the components W of dimension n - r, so it suffices to work at the generic point xi of such a W (proof lines 12145-12151). There, dim(O_{Y,xi}) = r by the dimension hypothesis and, because N has rank r and its dual surjects onto the conormal sheaf, the ideal of Z is locally cut out by r equations; combined with Cohen-Macaulayness this makes I_xi generated by a regular sequence, which spreads to an open neighbourhood V of xi (proof lines 12152-12165). On V the excess normal sheaf vanishes, so the fundamental-class lemma applies and gives the required identity (proof lines 12166-12170). Turning the four hypotheses into a regular sequence at the generic point of each top dimensional component is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Intersection product of two integral subschemes of a smooth integral scheme equals the fundamental class of their intersection under a dimension and Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a field k, an integral scheme X smooth over k, and integral closed subschemes Y, Z of dimensions summing to dim(X) + d, the lemma asserts that if dim(Y cap Z) <= d and O_{Y,xi} and O_{Z,xi} are Cohen-Macaulay at every point xi of the intersection of dimension d, then the intersection product [Y] . [Z] equals [Y cap Z]_d in CH_d(X) (statement lines 14522-14534). The proof identifies the intersection product with a higher codimension Gysin pullback: [Y] . [Z] = Delta^!([Y x Z]) where Delta^! is the Gysin map of the diagonal with respect to the tangent sheaf of X over k, which is locally free of rank dim(X) (proof lines 14537-14542). It then rewrites Y cap Z as the fibre product of Y x Z with X along the diagonal and notes dim(Y x Z) = dim(Y) + dim(Z), so that the first three hypotheses of the Gysin lemma are satisfied (proof lines 14542-14547). The fourth hypothesis is obtained by observing that the local map O_{Y,xi} -> O_{Y x Z,xi} is flat with fibre O_{Z,xi}, so Cohen-Macaulayness of both factors forces Cohen-Macaulayness of O_{Y x Z,xi}, after which the Gysin lemma applies (proof lines 14548-14559). Recognising the intersection product as a diagonal Gysin pullback and transporting Cohen-Macaulayness along the flat projection are the non-formal steps, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A two-periodic complex formed from two injective endomorphisms with commuting images over a one dimensional Noetherian local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite module M of dimension one over a Noetherian local ring A and two injective endomorphisms phi, psi with phi(psi(M)) = psi(phi(M)) - for instance commuting endomorphisms - the lemma asserts that M/phi psi M has finite length and that (M/phi psi M, phi, psi) is an exact (2, 1)-periodic complex (statement lines 17370-17380). The proof localises at a minimal prime q of the support of M, where M_q has finite length and both endomorphisms consequently become isomorphisms, so the support of M/phi psi M is concentrated at the closed point and hence has finite length (proof lines 17383-17389). Exactness is then checked directly: the kernel of phi on M/phi psi M is visibly psi M/phi psi M, so the kernel of phi is the image of psi, and the symmetric statement follows from the hypothesis M/phi psi M = M/psi phi M (proof lines 17390-17394). Recognising that injectivity plus the commuting-image condition is exactly what makes the two kernel computations match is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Proper pushforward of cycle and Chow groups commutes with the base change pullback in the shifted degrees
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In the base change situation, for a composite Y -> X -> S locally of finite type with base change Y' -> X' -> S' and f : Y -> X proper, the lemma asserts that f' is proper and that the two diagrams of cycle groups Z_k(Y) -> Z_k(X) -> Z_{k+c}(X') and of Chow groups commute with the pullback g^* (statement lines 15339-15360). The proof reduces to the level of cycles and to a single integral closed subscheme Z of Y of dimension k: by construction g^*[Z] = [Z']_{k+c}, and then both routes are computed by pushing forward the structure sheaf, using that f_*[Z] = [f_*O_Z]_k and (f')_*g^*[Z] = [f'_*O_{Z'}]_{k+c} and that g^*f_*[Z] = [(X' -> X)^* f_*O_Z]_{k+c} (proof lines 15363-15371). The whole reduction therefore turns on the isomorphism (X' -> X)^* f_*O_Z = f'_*O_{Z'} of coherent modules on X', which holds by flat base change because X' -> X is flat and O_{Z'} = (Y' -> Y)^*O_Z (proof lines 15372-15378). Reducing a commuting diagram of Chow groups to a single application of flat base change for coherent sheaves is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The sum of the orders of the tame symbols over the height one primes of a two dimensional Noetherian local domain vanishes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: This is the chapter's Key Lemma for the tame symbol, stated for a two dimensional Noetherian local domain A with fraction field K and f, g in K^*: the sum of ord_{A/q}(d_{A_q}(f, g)) over the height one primes q at which f or g fails to be a unit vanishes (statement lines 18339-18367). The statement is preceded by a reference block recording that for an excellent A this is Kato's Milnor K-theory proposition, which is why the result is genuinely research-level rather than a formal manipulation. The proof first uses the additivity of the tame symbols and of the order functions to reduce to the case f = a, g = b in A (proof lines 18370-18375). Then it rewrites the sum in terms of the determinant of the two-periodic complex, using the length-determinant proposition to convert the displayed sum into the condition e_A(A/(ab), a, b) = 0 (proof lines 18376-18382), and observes that this is immediate because the complex with terms A/(ab) and the alternating maps a, b is exact (proof lines 18386-18388). The reduction to the two specialisations of f and g, and the translation of an order-theoretic sum into the vanishing of an e-invariant, are the non-formal steps, so the claim is H3.

items.title: A section of a smooth morphism is a regular immersion and is a right inverse of the flat pullback bivariant class
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a smooth morphism p : P -> X of schemes locally of finite type over the base situation and a section s : X -> P, the lemma asserts two things: that s is a regular immersion, and that 1 = s^! o p^* in A^*(X), where p^* is the flat pullback bivariant class (statement lines 13434-13442). The first assertion is quoted, but the operator identity is proved by reducing to a single cycle class: since the assumptions are preserved by base change it suffices to show s^! cap p^*[Z] = [Z] for an integral closed subscheme Z of X (proof lines 13447-13450). After shrinking P to a neighbourhood of s(Z) one may assume p has fixed relative dimension r, so every component of p^{-1}(Z) has dimension n + r and p^*[Z] = [p^{-1}(Z)]_{n+r}; the key observation is that s(X) cap p^{-1}(Z) = s(Z) scheme theoretically and that this is a regularly embedded closed subscheme of codimension r, so the fundamental-class lemma for a regularly embedded divisor applies (proof lines 13451-13457). Recognising that the scheme theoretic intersection computes s^! on the class is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The zeroth Fitting ideal of a quotient along a finite locally free ring map factors as an ideal of the base times an ideal after localising
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite locally free ring map A -> C of rank d, an element h with C_h etale over A, and an ideal J of C, the lemma asserts that I = Fit_0(C/J), viewed as a finite A-module, satisfies IC_h = JJ' for some ideal J' of C_h, and that I and J' are finitely generated whenever J is (statement lines 8848-8855). The proof computes I after base change: IC is the Fitting ideal of C/J tensor_A C, using the basics of Fitting ideals, so it suffices to split the ring C tensor_A C_h along the multiplication section. The section shows that C -> C tensor_A C is etale at every prime in the image of Spec(C_h), hence the multiplication map C tensor_A C_h -> C_h is etale and in particular flat, and a finite locally free surjection with a section then splits the source as a direct sum of C_h-algebras (proof lines 8857-8868). Tensoring with C/J and reading off the zeroth Fitting ideal of each summand gives IC_h = JJ' with J' the Fitting ideal of the complementary summand, and finite generation is inherited from J (proof lines 8869-8872). Recognising that the section splits the base changed ring and thereby factors the Fitting ideal is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the relative associated points after an arbitrary base change for a morphism locally of finite type: a point upstairs is associated relative to the new base exactly when its image downstairs is associated relative to the old base and the point is a generic point of an irreducible component of the tensor product of the two residue fields (statement lines 1119-1138). The counted proof is a genuine reduction: it passes to the morphism between the fibres, which is flat because it is a base change along a field extension, applies the same-chapter decomposition of associated points over a locally Noetherian base to write the associated points of the fibre upstairs as a union indexed by those of the fibre downstairs, and then identifies the fibre of the fibrewise morphism at a point with the spectrum of the residue field tensor product, whose associated primes are its minimal primes by the cited Noetherian Cohen-Macaulay statement (proof lines 1140-1167). It is H2: the reduction is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard fibre, decomposition and algebra facts.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.title: For a glueing pair the first Tor of the bigger ring with the cokernel of localizing a module at the element vanishes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a glueing pair (R -> R', f) and asserts that for every R-module M one has Tor^R_1(R', Coker(M -> M_f)) = 0 (source lines 25498-25505). The proof proceeds in three stages. It first sets M-bar = M/M[f^infty], notes that Coker(M -> M_f) is isomorphic to Coker(M-bar -> M-bar_f), and therefore assumes f is a nonzerodivisor on M; in that case M is contained in M_f, M_f/M is the colimit of M/f^nM with multiplication transitions, and since Tor commutes with colimits it suffices to prove Tor^R_1(R', M/f^nM) = 0 (proof lines 25508-25515). The special case M = R/R[f^infty] is then done by an explicit diagram: the same-f-torsion lemma gives M tensor_R R' = R'/R'[f^infty], and from the short exact sequence 0 -> M -> M -> M/f^nM -> 0 the long exact Tor sequence produces the displayed commutative diagram in which the diagonal arrow is injective; since Tor_1^R(R', R/R[f^infty]) vanishes by the first-Tor-total lemma, the proof deduces Tor_1^R(R', M/f^nM) = 0 (proof lines 25518-25537). The general case reduces to this one: the proof chooses a surjection F -> M with F a free R/R[f^infty]-module and forms 0 -> N -> F/f^nF -> M/f^nM -> 0, which by the torsion-completion lemma stays exact after tensoring with R'; since Tor_1^R(R', F/f^nF) vanishes by the previous paragraph, so does Tor_1^R(R', M/f^nM) (proof lines 25540-25550). The non-routine content is the diagram in the special case and the reduction that removes the f-torsion from M.

items.title: Vanishing of the positive cohomology of the reduction modulo an ideal spreads to all power-torsion and bounded complexes with power-torsion cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an ideal I, and an object K of D(R) with H^i(K tensor^L_R R/I) = 0 for i > 0, and asserts three things: that H^i(K tensor^L_R R/I^n) = 0 for all n >= 1 and i > 0; that H^i(K tensor^L_R N) = 0 for any I-power torsion module N and i > 0; and that for any bounded complex M whose cohomology modules are I-power torsion and vanish in positive degrees one has H^i(K tensor^L_R M) = 0 for i > 0 (source lines 24109-24122). The proof works by reduction. For part (2) it writes N as the union of the submodules N[I^n] and uses that tensor products commute with colimits, in a step the author states is omitted with a hint, to reduce to the case where N is annihilated by some I^n (proof lines 24125-24129). It then introduces the square-zero extension R' = R/I^n oplus N and observes that it suffices to show the object K' = K tensor^L_R R' of D(R') has vanishing cohomology in positive degrees (proof lines 24130-24133). The substantive step is the passage along the surjection R' -> R/I with nilpotent kernel J: the proof computes K tensor^L_R R/I = (K tensor^L_R R') tensor^L_{R'} R/I = K' tensor^L_{R'} R/I, notes that by hypothesis this complex has tor amplitude in (-infinity, 0], and invokes the tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent lemma to conclude (proof lines 24134-24144). Part (1) is then immediate from part (2), and part (3) follows from part (2) by induction on the number of nonzero cohomology modules of M and the truncation distinguished triangles, in a final step the author again states is omitted (proof lines 24146-24151). The non-routine content is the square-zero extension trick and the transfer of the vanishing through the nilpotent quotient.

items.title: Fibres of the henselization of the normalization and the minimal primes over a local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a local ring A with finitely many minimal primes, lets A' be the integral closure of A in the total ring of fractions of A_red, and considers the two maps Spec(A') <- Spec((A')^h) -> Spec(A^h) attached to the henselization, where (A')^h = A' tensor_A A^h; it asserts that the left arrow is bijective on maximal ideals, that the right arrow is bijective on minimal primes, and that every minimal prime of (A')^h lies in a unique maximal ideal while every maximal ideal contains exactly one minimal prime (source lines 31154-31171). The proof runs the same three-part programme as the strict-henselization analogue counted separately: removal of nilpotents using (A/I)^h = A^h/IA^h, a computation identifying the fibres of the left arrow with spectra of residue field tensor products in the finite henselian case, the use of normality of the filtered colimit (A')^h to get uniqueness of the minimal prime inside each maximal ideal together with a henselian-pair connectedness argument for the converse, and a two-sided comparison of minimal primes via the total fraction ring. The arguments are independent of the geometric variant, which uses strict henselization and a separable algebraic closure and is counted at disjoint lines.
