items.title: A weakly etale algebra over a field is reduced, integral, a filtered colimit of finite separable products, and closed under subalgebras, quotients and tensor products
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six structural properties of a K-algebra B that is weakly etale over a field K: that B is reduced; that B is integral over K; that every finitely generated K-subalgebra of B is a finite product of finite separable extensions of K; that B is a field exactly when it has no nontrivial idempotents, in which case it is a separable algebraic extension of K; that every subalgebra or quotient algebra of B is again weakly etale over K; and that the tensor product of two such algebras is again weakly etale (source lines 30845-30859). The proof assembles these from the two preceding results and from the structure of etale algebras over a field. Part (1) is drawn from the absolutely-flat-over-absolutely-flat lemma. Part (3) follows from the absolutely-flat-over-field lemma together with the fact that etale K-algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions (proof lines 30861-30867). Part (3) implies (2), and part (4) follows from (3) because a product of fields is a field exactly when it has no nontrivial idempotents (proof lines 30868-30870). The substantive part is (5): for a subalgebra S of B the proof observes that S is the filtered colimit of its finitely generated subalgebras, each of which is etale over K by the above, and hence S is weakly etale by the absolutely-flat-over-field lemma; for a quotient B -> Q the proof uses that Q is the filtered colimit of quotients of finite products of finite separable extensions, and that any quotient of such a product is itself a sub-product, so the result follows by the same reasoning (proof lines 30873-30883). Part (6) is then obtained either similarly or by combining the base change and composition permanence lemmas (proof lines 30886-30888). The non-routine content is the filtered-colimit argument for subalgebras and the sub-product description of quotients of finite separable products.

items.title: The triangulated category of perfect complexes over a filtered colimit of rings is the colimit of the categories over the stages
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a filtered colimit of rings R = colim_{i in I} R_i and makes two assertions: first, that given a perfect K in D(R) there is a stage i and a perfect K_i in D(R_i) whose derived base change to R recovers K; and second, that for a fixed stage 0 and objects K_0 (perfect) and L_0 in D(R_0), the Hom group in D(R) between their base changes is the filtered colimit over i >= 0 of the corresponding Hom groups over R_i (source lines 19267-19285). The proof of part (1) is a descent argument: the cited colimit lemmas say that the category of finitely presented R-modules is the colimit of the categories of finitely presented R_i-modules, and since finite projective modules are characterised as summands of finite free modules the same holds for the category of finite projective modules, which by the definition of perfect objects gives (1) (proof lines 19287-19297). Part (2) is the substantive computation: the proof represents K_0 by a bounded complex K_0^bullet of finite projective R_0-modules and L_0 by a K-flat complex L_0^bullet, and uses the description of maps out of a projective complex to rewrite the Hom in D(R) as the Hom in the homotopy category between the two base-changed complexes (proof lines 19300-19310). Since only finitely many terms occur, and since each Hom_R(K_0^p tensor R, L_0^q tensor R) is the filtered colimit over i of Hom_{R_i}(K_0^p tensor R_i, L_0^q tensor R_i) by the cited lemmas, exactness of filtered colimits gives (2) (proof lines 19310-19321). The non-routine content is the two-step rewriting of the Hom group, first into the homotopy category and then into a filtered colimit of finite data.

items.title: The decomposition, inertia and wild inertia groups of a maximal ideal restrict surjectively along a Galois subtower
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K, a tower M/L/K with both extensions finite Galois, the integral closures C and B of A in M and L, a maximal ideal m' of C with m = m' cap B, and the chains of wild inertia, inertia and decomposition groups of m and m'; it asserts that the canonical surjection Gal(M/K) -> Gal(L/K) restricts to surjections P' -> P, I' -> I and D' -> D, and that these fit into two commutative diagrams, the second involving the ramification indices e' and e and the maps theta', theta into the groups of roots of unity of the residue fields (source lines 33619-33657). The first part is immediate from the definitions: the groups map into one another, and commutativity of the first diagram is clear because the residue extension kappa(m)/kappa_A is normal, so every automorphism of kappa(m') over kappa_A induces one of kappa(m) over kappa_A (proof lines 33660-33668). Surjectivity of I' -> I and D' -> D comes from the one-orbit geometric lemma, and surjectivity of P' -> P then follows because P' and P are Sylow p-subgroups of I' and I (proof lines 33671-33674). The substantive part is the commutativity of the second diagram: with uniformizers pi' of C_{m'} and pi of B_m one has pi = c' (pi')^{e'/e} for a unit c', and for sigma' in I' with image sigma in I, writing sigma'(pi') = c pi' and sigma(pi) = b pi, the proof computes b pi = sigma'(pi) = sigma'(c') c^{e'/e} (pi')^{e'/e} = (sigma'(c')/c') c^{e'/e} pi, so that this is sheer algebra with the ramification indices (proof lines 33677-33688 and following). The non-routine content is the uniformizer computation that identifies the two maps into the roots of unity up to the power e'/e.

items.title: The right derived functor of the inverse limit on N-indexed abelian groups has the standard two-term representation and vanishes above degree one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the existence of the right derived functor R lim : D(Ab(N)) -> D(Ab) of the inverse limit and then lists five properties: that R^p lim vanishes for p > 1; that R lim A_n is represented by the two-term complex prod A_n -> prod A_n with the displayed map sitting in degrees 0 and 1; that for a Mittag-Leffler system R^1 lim vanishes; that every object of D(Ab(N)) is quasi-isomorphic to a complex whose terms are right acyclic for lim; and that if each K^p is right acyclic then R lim K is represented by the complex of its limits (source lines 22942-22968). The proof constructs the acyclics by hand: for an arbitrary inverse system (A_n) it forms the system (B_n) with B_n = A_n oplus A_{n-1} oplus ... oplus A_1 and transition maps the projections, and embeds A_n into B_n by the displayed tuple built from the composites of the transition maps f_i, showing that every inverse system is a subobject of a Mittag-Leffler system (proof lines 22971-22980). Using the right-acyclic-subcategory criterion together with the Mittag-Leffler lemma it follows that every Mittag-Leffler system is right acyclic for lim, which is property (3), and this already defines RF on D^+(Ab(N)) (proof lines 22981-22986). The proof then sets C_n = A_{n-1} oplus ... oplus A_1 for n > 1 and C_1 = 0 with projection transitions, obtains the short exact sequence of inverse systems 0 -> (A_n) -> (B_n) -> (C_n) -> 0 where the map B_n -> C_n is the displayed difference map, and since (C_n) is also Mittag-Leffler concludes property (2), which implies (1) (proof lines 22987-22993). Finally, the unbounded right derived functor lemma gives that R lim is defined on all of D(Ab(N)), and its proof proceeds by establishing (4) and (5) (proof lines 22994-22999). The non-routine content is the explicit embedding of an arbitrary inverse system into a Mittag-Leffler one, which is what manufactures the acyclic objects.

items.title: For a derived complete object the vanishing above degree zero can be checked after tensoring with the Koszul complex
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finitely generated ideal I = (f_1, ..., f_r) of a ring A and a derived complete object K of D(A), and establishes the equivalence of three conditions: that H^i(K) vanish for i > 0; that H^i(K tensor^L_A A/I) vanish for i > 0; and that H^i(K tensor^L_A K_1^bullet) vanish for i > 0, where K_1^bullet is the Koszul object of the ambient situation (source lines 26436-26446). The implication (1) implies (2) is immediate, and (2) implies (3) is exactly the bounded-above-mod-I lemma (proof lines 26449-26450). The substantive direction is (3) implies (1). For s = 0, ..., r the proof considers the objects K(s) = K tensor^L_A K_bullet(A, f_1, ..., f_s) where K_bullet(A, f_1, ..., f_s) is the Koszul complex placed in cohomological degrees -s, ..., 0, and obtains distinguished triangles K(s-1) --f_s--> K(s-1) -> K(s) -> K(s-1)[1] from the cone-of-Koszul lemma (proof lines 26451-26461). Two inductions then run in opposite directions: an ascending induction on s from K(0) = K being derived complete shows every K(s) is derived complete (proof lines 26461-26463), and a descending induction shows that K(s) has no nonzero cohomology in degrees greater than 0, the case s = r being exactly assumption (3); if it holds for K(s) with s > 0, then the multiplication map f_s on H^i(K(s-1)) is surjective for i > 0, and the serre-subcategory and derived-complete-zero lemmas then force H^i(K(s-1)) to vanish (proof lines 26463-26468). The non-routine content is the interplay of the two inductions along the Koszul triangles, with the surjectivity of multiplication producing vanishing because the object is derived complete.

items.title: The determinant of a perfect complex of tor amplitude in two degrees is a functor to invertible modules, with a canonical element carrying isomorphisms
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma packages the determinant constructions of the surrounding section into a functor det from the category of perfect complexes with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] and isomorphisms as morphisms, to the category of invertible modules with isomorphisms as morphisms; it also asserts that a rank 0 perfect object L with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] carries a canonical element delta(L) in det(L) such that for every isomorphism a : L -> K in D(R) one has det(a)(delta(L)) = delta(K) (source lines 37123-37147). The proof is a substantial construction-and-verification. It first calls a two-term complex with finite projective terms good, notes that every object of the source category is represented by one, and that morphisms between good complexes in the derived category are homotopy classes of maps of complexes, so that the previously studied determinant det(L^bullet) = det(L^0) tensor det(L^{-1})^{tensor -1} can be used (proof lines 37150-37162). For a quasi-isomorphism a^bullet : L^bullet -> K^bullet it introduces the notion of a good diagram: a commuting-up-to-homotopy triangle through an auxiliary good complex M^bullet whose maps b^bullet and c^bullet satisfy the three conditions established earlier; det(a^bullet) is then defined as det(c^bullet) composed with det(b^bullet)^{-1}, and the proof must show that good diagrams always exist and that this definition does not depend on the diagram chosen (proof lines 37165-37182). Existence is constructive: choosing a surjection R^{oplus n} -> K^{-1}, the proof builds the good complex M^bullet = (L^{-1} oplus R^{oplus n}) -> (L^0 oplus R^{oplus n}) with the projection b^bullet and the map c^bullet using a^{-1} oplus p in degree -1 and a^0 oplus d o p in degree 0, and checks the conditions (proof lines 37185-37200). Independence for the identity is then immediate from the homotopic-surjections lemma, which gives det(c^bullet) = det(b^bullet) for a good diagram over the identity, so det(id^bullet) = id (proof lines 37203-37213). The proof continues by analysing composition of quasi-isomorphisms and good diagrams, and completes the independence, functoriality and the canonical element delta by the same diagrammatic machinery (rest of the counted proof span, source lines 37216-37290). The non-routine content is the existence construction for good diagrams, the use of the homotopic-surjections lemma to get independence over the identity, and the diagrammatic treatment of composition.

items.title: The dual of a perfect complex is perfect and refines the double dual and the tensor-Hom adjunction
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A and a perfect object K of D(A), and asserts that K^vee = R Hom_A(K, A) is perfect with K isomorphic to its double dual, and that for L in D(A) there are functorial isomorphisms L tensor^L_A K^vee = R Hom_A(K, L) and H^0(L tensor^L_A K^vee) = Ext^0_A(K, L) (source lines 19175-19186). The proof is explicit at the level of complexes. It represents K by a bounded complex K^bullet of finite projective modules, and by the Hom-out-of-projective lemma K^vee is then represented by E^bullet = Hom^bullet(K^bullet, A), whose terms E^n = Hom_A(K^{-n}, A) are again finite projective, so E^bullet is a bounded complex of finite projective modules and K^vee is perfect (proof lines 19189-19194). It then exhibits the canonical map from K^bullet, written as the total complex of Hom^bullet(A, A) tensor_A K^bullet, to Hom^bullet(Hom^bullet(K^bullet, A), A) which in each degree is the evaluation map up to sign, and concludes that this defines a canonical isomorphism (K^vee)^vee = K because the double dual of a finite projective module is itself (proof lines 19194-19204). The second displayed equality is derived from the first together with the internal Hom lemma, the description of maps from a projective complex, and the definition of Ext groups (proof lines 19207-19211). The first displayed equality — the tensor-Hom adjunction — is proved by exhibiting, for a complex L^bullet representing L, the canonical isomorphism from Tot(L^bullet tensor_A E^bullet) to Hom^bullet(K^bullet, L^bullet), which uses the sign rule asserting that E^bullet is the left dual of K^bullet in the category of complexes (proof lines 19212-19223). The non-routine content is the sign-compatible evaluation map and the identification of E^bullet as the left dual.

items.title: An extension obtained by adjoining a root of the prepared polynomial is Galois and falls into one of four cases according to the valuation of the parameter
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A of mixed characteristic (0, p) containing a primitive p-th root of 1, the polynomial P of the preparation lemma, and an element xi of the fraction field K, and considers the extension L obtained by adjoining a root of P(z) = xi; it asserts that L/K is Galois and that exactly one of four cases occurs — L = K; L/K unramified with respect to A of degree p; L/K totally ramified of ramification index p; or the integral closure B is a discrete valuation ring with A in B weakly unramified and a purely inseparable residue extension of degree p — and then, with pi a uniformizer of A, asserts three implications (A), (B) and (C) locating the case according to the shape of xi (source lines 35016-35042). The proof rewrites the adjunction of a root of P(z) = xi as the adjunction of a root of y^p = w^p (1 + xi), notes that K contains a primitive p-th root of 1 so the extension is Galois of order dividing p by Kummer theory, and reads the case list off the ramification discussion (proof lines 35045-35051). Case (A) is settled by observing that A -> A[x]/(P(x) - xi) is then a finite etale ring extension, so only cases (1) and (2) can occur (proof lines 35054-35055). Case (B) is settled by a valuation count: writing xi = pi^{-n} a with p not dividing n and letting B be the integral closure with C = B_m, one has p ord_C(z) = -n ord_C(pi), so the ramification index of A in C is divisible by p, hence equals p, and B = C (proof lines 35058-35063). Case (C) is the substantive one: writing k = n/p the proof rewrites the defining equation in the displayed form with (pi^k z) as the new variable, and concludes from the fact that A[y]/(y^p - pi^{n-k} y - sum a_i pi^{n-ik} y^i - a) is a discrete valuation ring weakly unramified over A (proof lines 35066-35071). The non-routine content is the Kummer rewriting together with the explicit discrete valuation ring in case (C).

items.title: For a flat local homomorphism the determinant of a base changed endomorphism is the m-th power of the original determinant
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat local homomorphism (R, m, kappa) -> (R', m', kappa') with m = length_{R'}(R'/mR') finite, and asserts that for an endomorphism varphi of a finite length module M over R as in the surrounding construction, the element det_kappa(varphi)^m maps to det_{kappa'}(varphi tensor 1) in kappa' (source lines 36721-36730). The proof first reduces to the case where (M, varphi) is a simple object of the ambient category: flatness of R -> R' ensures that the short exact sequences of the earlier lemma base change to short exact sequences over R', so the multiplicativity of the determinant along those sequences lets one descend to simple objects (proof lines 36732-36737). In the simple case M is annihilated by m, and the proof chooses a filtration of R'/mR' whose successive quotients are isomorphic to kappa' as R'-modules, of length m by the hypothesis (proof lines 36738-36743). Tensoring this filtration with M over kappa produces a filtration of M tensor_R R' = M tensor_kappa R'/mR' whose successive quotients are isomorphic to M tensor_kappa kappa', and the proof observes that the submodules are invariant under varphi tensor 1 (proof lines 36744-36754). Applying the multiplicativity lemma once more gives the displayed chain of equalities expressing det_{kappa'}(varphi tensor 1) as the m-th power of det_{kappa'}(varphi tensor 1) on M tensor_kappa kappa', which by compatibility of determinants with field extensions equals det_kappa(varphi)^m (proof lines 36755-36764). The non-routine content is the construction of the invariant filtration and its length count.

items.title: Faithfulness of base change on power-torsion modules characterises faithful flatness of the quotient map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring map R -> S and an ideal I of R, and establishes the equivalence of four conditions: that the map be flat with R/I -> S/IS faithfully flat; that the map be flat with Spec(S/IS) -> Spec(R/I) surjective; that the map be flat with base change faithful on modules annihilated by I; and that the map be flat with base change faithful on I-power torsion modules (source lines 24226-24239). The proof first notes that flatness of R -> S gives flatness of R/I^n -> S/I^nS for every n, so (1) and (2) are equivalent by the faithful flatness criterion (proof lines 24242-24245). The equivalence of (1) with (3) follows by identifying I-torsion R-modules with R/I-modules, using the identity M tensor_R S = M tensor_{R/I} S/IS for R-modules M annihilated by I, together with the easy faithful flatness lemma (proof lines 24246-24252). The implication (4) implies (3) is immediate. The substantive direction is (3) implies (4): assuming (3), the proof uses the previously established flatness of R/I^n -> S/I^nS and the induced surjection on spectra, which follows because Spec(R/I^n) = Spec(R/I) and similarly for S, to conclude that base change is faithful on modules annihilated by I^n; since an I-power torsion module is the union of the M_n annihilated by I^n, and tensor product commutes with colimits, faithfulness extends to all I-power torsion modules (proof lines 24253-24260). The non-routine content is the passage from bounded torsion to all power torsion via the colimit description.

items.title: Vanishing of cohomology on basis opens from vanishing Cech cohomology for a cofinal system of coverings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: Let X be a ringed space with a basis B, let F be an O_X-module and let Cov be a set of coverings whose members and finite intersections lie in B, which is cofinal among coverings of each basis open U, and for which all higher Cech cohomology of F vanishes; the lemma concludes H^p(U, F) = 0 for all p > 0 and all U in B (statement lines 1695-1714). The proof embeds F into an injective I, uses that I has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for the coverings of Cov, and observes that assumption (1) makes the Cech complex of any U in Cov a product of values over basis opens, so that the short exact sequence 0 to F to I to Q to 0 produces a short exact sequence of Cech complexes and hence Q again has vanishing higher Cech cohomology (proof lines 1720-1748). The proof then runs the long exact cohomology sequence: H^n(U, I) = 0 for n > 0, surjectivity of H^0(I) to H^0(Q) gives H^1(F) = 0, and the same argument applied to Q gives H^2(F) = 0 and so on by induction (proof lines 1751-1775). The claim is H2: a standard injective-and-induct argument, with the only subtlety being that the cofinality assumption is what makes the basis suffice.

items.title: Cohomology of a filtered colimit of pulled back sheaves as the colimit of the cohomologies
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of a directed system of ringed spaces X_i over X with sheaves F_i and transition maps, the lemma computes the cohomology of the colimit F = colim p_i^{-1}F_i on a quasi-compact open pulled back from some X_i as the colimit of the cohomologies H^p(f_a^{-1}(U_i), F_j), hence in particular H^p(X, F) = colim H^p(X_i, F_i) (statement lines 3359-3370). After disposing of p = 0 by the sheaf-theoretic colimit of sections, the author builds an embedding of the whole system (F_i, phi_a) into a system of injective sheaves (G_i, psi_a) by taking products of pushforwards of chosen injectives I_k, which requires checking that each G_i is injective and that the transition maps psi_a are well defined (proof lines 3376-3401). The reduction to the vanishing of H^p of G = colim f_i^{-1}G_i is then copied from the quasi-separated colimit lemma, and the vanishing is checked on Cech complexes of coverings of quasi-compact opens by finitely many quasi-compact opens, which descend to some X_i and where the Cech complex is a filtered colimit of acyclic complexes (proof lines 3403-3429). The claim is H2: no new idea, but three reductions that must be wired together, and the point where filtered exactness is applied is essential.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of a short exact sequence of complexes of sheaves with a compatible product, the lemma computes the boundary of a cup product: for a in H^n(X, F_3) and b in H^m(X, G_1) one has gamma_1(boundary(a) cup b) = (-1)^{n+1} gamma_3(a cup boundary(b)) (statement lines 5656-5669). The proof is a concrete cocycle computation: after fixing the notation that identifies F_1 as a subsheaf of F_2 with quotient F_3 and G_3 as a subsheaf of G_2 with quotient G_1 (proof lines 5672-5686), the author picks cocycles alpha_3 and beta_1 on a covering, lifts them to cochains alpha_2 and beta_2, observes that alpha_1 = d(alpha_2) and beta_3 = d(beta_2) represent the two boundary classes (proof lines 5689-5715), and then evaluates d(gamma_2(alpha_2 cup beta_2)) through a four-term chain that uses the Leibniz rule for the total complex and the compatibility of the products gamma_i with the boundary maps (proof lines 5716-5730). The claim is H2: nothing is left to the reader, but the content is bookkeeping of degrees and signs inside the total complex, and the final sign is remarked to depend on the sign conventions for the long exact sequence recorded in the author's footnote.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: For a ringed space (X, O_X), bounded below complexes K and M of O_X-modules and an open covering, the lemma asserts that a specific three-by-three diagram comparing the total Cech complexes, the tensor product, and the derived global sections commutes in D(A) (statement lines 7543-7578). The proof first replaces K and M by complexes K_1, M_1 for which the comparison maps of the Godement resolution type are available: since those maps are homotopy equivalences on stalks, the induced map on the total tensor products is a homotopy equivalence on stalks and hence a quasi-isomorphism, so the two targets agree in D(A) (proof lines 7581-7606). The claim is H2: two explicit reduction steps plus a diagram chase whose individual inputs are all standard, with no new construction.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is an eleven-part collection for a locally algebraic k-scheme X: catenarity of the underlying space, dim_x(X) = dim(O_{X,x}) at closed points, invariance of the dimension under nonempty open subsets and at every point when X is irreducible, extendability of chains of irreducible closed subsets to maximal chains of length dim(X), the max-min formula for dim_x(X), dim(X) = trdeg_k(kappa(x)) at the generic point, the drop of the transcendence degree by exactly one along an immediate specialization, dim(X) as the supremum of the transcendence degrees of generic points, the monotonicity of dim_x and dim(O_{X,x}) along specializations together with the length formula for maximal chains, the formula dim_x(X) = trdeg_k(kappa(x)) + dim(O_{X,x}), and the increment of dim(O) by one along an immediate specialization in the irreducible or equidimensional case (statement lines 3782-3845). The author announces that instead of using the more general results proved earlier he will reduce everything to finite type k-algebras and cite the commutative algebra chapter (proof lines 3847-3851). Each part is then routed separately, mostly by replacing X by an affine neighbourhood Spec(A) with A a finite type k-algebra; the steps that are not formal are the reductions themselves, for instance the use of the Jacobson property of X to produce a closed point inside U cap U' in part (3) (proof lines 3876-3883), the use of the rule Z to Z cap U to compare irreducible components pointwise in part (5) (proof lines 3894-3902), and the maximal chain argument in part (7) (proof lines 3911-3918). The claim is H2: no new construction is introduced, but eleven statements each have to be routed to the correct algebra input.

items.title: Finiteness of the group of units modulo constants for a normal open subscheme of a proper variety
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For an algebraically closed field k, a proper variety X-bar over k and an open subscheme X which is normal, the lemma shows that O^*(X)/k^* is a finitely generated abelian group (statement lines 5156-5163). The proof has three real moves: first replace X-bar by its normalization, using that the normalization morphism is finite and is an isomorphism over the normal X, so that X-bar may be assumed normal (proof lines 5166-5177); then let xi_1, ..., xi_r be the generic points of the complement of X and single out the indices j for which the local ring O_j is one dimensional, so that O_j is a discrete valuation ring and yields a valuation v_j on k(X-bar)^* (proof lines 5190-5206); finally show that the kernel of O(X)^* to the product of the Z over j in J is k^*, by proving that an element of the kernel lies in every height one localization of every affine piece, hence extends to a global function on the proper X-bar and therefore lies in k. The claim is H2: every input is standard, but the assembly of the height one localization criterion with properness into the finiteness statement is the non-formal part.

items.difficulty_reason: For f: X to Y locally of finite type and a point y whose local ring is Noetherian of dimension at most one, the lemma gives five alternative hypotheses at generic points of X under which f is quasi-finite at every point of X lying over y (statement lines 3187-3206). The proof first linearises the hypotheses: (4) implies (3) because the quasi-finite locus is open and a dense open of a locally Noetherian scheme contains all generic points of irreducible components, (3) implies (1) by the equivalence between quasi-finiteness at a point and finiteness of the residue field extension there, and (1) implies (2) trivially (proof lines 3209-3218). The non-formal part is the main case: after replacing Y by Spec(O_{Y,y}) and X by one of its irreducible components (proof lines 3221-3237), the author distinguishes whether the generic point of X maps to y or to the other point of Spec(B), and in the second case applies the dimension formula to force the transcendence degree trdeg_{kappa(y)} kappa(x) to vanish, which makes every point of the fibre closed in the fibre (proof lines 3240-3265). The claim is H2: the reduction steps are standard, while the dimension formula computation is the substantive part.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For schemes X and Y over a field k and subsets A and B, the lemma identifies the closure of the set of points of X times_k Y whose projections lie in A and B with the product of the closures of A and B (statement lines 4424-4439). One inclusion is immediate. For the other the author reduces to the case where X and Y are the closures themselves, and then argues by density: given a nonempty open W of the product, the projection of W to X is nonempty open because a scheme over a field is universally open over the base, so it meets A, and then the fibre over the chosen point a is a nonempty open subset of W whose image in Y is nonempty open, hence meets B (proof lines 4441-4459). The claim is H2: a clean density argument in which the base change of the universally open morphism to the residue field of a is what makes the second projection open as well.

items.title: Presentation of a complete local ring of a locally Noetherian scheme as a quotient of a power series ring, and when it is a k-algebra isomorphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally Noetherian scheme X over a field k and a point x with residue field kappa, the lemma produces an isomorphism kappa[[x_1, ..., x_n]]/I to the completion of the local ring at x inducing the identity on residue fields, and determines exactly when it can be chosen as a k-algebra isomorphism (statement lines 4043-4057). The first half is an application of the Cohen structure theorem, with the author's own footnote explaining how the mixed characteristic form of the theorem reduces to the displayed one (proof lines 4060-4067). The second half is where the lemma acquires independent content: the author exhibits an explicit example over k = F_p(t), namely A = k[x,y]/(y^2 + x^p - t) completed at the maximal ideal (y), whose completion is isomorphic to k(t^{1/p})[[z]] as a ring but not as a k-algebra, because no element of the completion has p-th power t, as one sees modulo y^2 (proof lines 4069-4078). The positive direction for separable kappa/k is then a separate construction: lift kappa to a k-algebra homomorphism into the completion, send x_i to generators of the maximal ideal, and use that both sides are adically complete and that the map is surjective modulo the ideal, hence surjective (proof lines 4080-4097). The claim is H3: the lemma carries a counterexample construction and a separability criterion of its own, not merle restating the structure theorem.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'

items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k, a k-algebra A and a quasi-compact open V of X_A, the lemma produces a finitely generated k-subalgebra A' of A and a quasi-compact open V' of X_{A'} whose base change to A is V (statement lines 811-820). The proof is an explicit descent through standard opens: choose finitely many affine opens U_i of X covering V, write each as the spectrum of a ring R_i, express V as a finite union of standard opens D(f_{ij}) inside the base changed charts, and then observe that finitely many elements of the rings R_i tensor_k A are involved, so a single finitely generated subalgebra A' contains all of them (proof lines 822-835). Setting V' to the union of the corresponding standard opens of X_{A'} gives the descent, and the equality V = pi^{-1}(V') is checked pointwise using that the f_{ij}' map to the f_{ij} (proof lines 836-841). The claim is H2: a finite-presentation bookkeeping argument carried out concretely, with the pointwise verification written out.

The proof replaces Y by Spec(O_{Y,y}) and X by an affine neighbourhood, reduces to X integral by handling the irreducible components separately, and then splits on whether the generic point of X maps to y (proof lines 3605-3622). The claim is H2: the reductions are standard, while the dimension formula computation and the strict inequality between the local rings are the substantive steps.

items.title: Upper bound for the fibre dimension at a point whose generic specialisations lie outside the image point
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f: X to Y locally of finite type, a point x whose image y has Noetherian local ring, and an integer d equal to the fibre dimension at every generic point of an irreducible component of X through x which does not map to y, the lemma bounds dim_x(X_y) by d + dim(O_{Y,y}) - 1 (statement lines 3670-3678). The proof copies the reduction of the codimension one case to reduce to X = Spec(A) with A a domain and Y = Spec(B) with B a Noetherian local domain contained in A (proof lines 3681-3685). The dimension formula then gives an inequality between dim(O_{X,x}) plus a transcendence degree on the left and dim(B) plus the transcendence degree of A over B on the right, where the latter is exactly d by hypothesis; since the local ring at x maps onto the local ring of the fibre with a nonzero kernel and is a Noetherian domain, its dimension is strictly larger than the fibre dimension upstairs, and the two comparisons produce the stated strict bound (proof lines 3686-3706). The claim is H2: the same two ingredients as the codimension one case with the strict inequality now bounding rather than identifying the fibre dimension.

items.title: Dimension of fibres of a morphism of locally algebraic schemes: bounds, openness and the generic value
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism f: X to Y of locally algebraic k-schemes, the lemma records that fibres are locally algebraic over the residue field, and for X irreducible with Z the closure of the image and d = dim(X) - dim(Z), it bounds the fibre dimension below by d, asserts that equality holds on a dense open, gives an upper bound in terms of the dimension of the local ring of Z at f(x), and identifies the fibre dimension with d when that local ring has dimension one; a final part bounds the fibre dimension at an arbitrary point by dim_x(X) - dim_y(Y) (statement lines 3952-3972). The proof first computes d as a transcendence degree of the extension of the function field of Z inside the function field of X at the generic point, which identifies d with the fibre dimension at the generic point of X (proof lines 3983-3990). The lower bound and the density of equality are then the openness of bounded fibre dimension, and the two refined bounds come from the codimension one and higher codimension lemmas of the same chapter (proof lines 3991-3995). The last part reduces to an irreducible component of X through x of dimension dim_x(X) and applies the irreducible case to it (proof lines 3998-4000). The claim is H2: one transcendence degree computation plus a careful routing of four statements to the appropriate earlier results.

items.title: Geometric normality of the normalization is reached after a finite purely inseparable field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For an algebraic k-scheme X, the lemma produces a finite purely inseparable extension k' such that the normalization of X_{k'} is geometrically normal over k' (statement lines 4993-4998). The proof spreads the statement out over the perfect closure of k: normalizing X over the perfect closure gives a morphism, which descends to a finite presentation morphism over some finite subextension, and the descended morphism is already geometrically normal (proof lines 5001-5008). The remaining work is to keep increasing k' until the descended morphism has the two properties that make it a normalization: finiteness, by descending the finiteness of the normalization morphism, and closed-immersion behaviour over a dense open, by descending a dense open on which the normalization is an isomorphism onto the reduced fibre and then descending the closed immersion property (proof lines 5009-5021). The author then reads off that the descended morphism is the normalization (proof lines 5022-5023). The claim is H2: no new construction, but three successive descents along a filtered colimit that must be ordered correctly, with the finite subextension chosen at each step.

items.title: Finiteness and continuity of the Galois action on the connected components of a quasi-compact base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over k with separable algebraic closure, assuming X quasi-compact and the connected components of X over the closure open, the lemma states that there are finitely many such components and that the Galois action on them is continuous, and it observes that both hypotheses hold when X is of finite type over k (statement lines 1283-1300). The proof of finiteness is immediate: open components cover, the space is quasi-compact, so only finitely many appear (proof lines 1303-1306). Continuity comes from the descent of quasi-compact opens: each connected component is a quasi-compact open of the base change, hence defined over a finite subextension, so its stabilizer contains an open subgroup, which for the discrete topology is exactly continuity (proof lines 1307-1309). The last paragraph verifies the finite type case through Noetherianness giving finitely many irreducible, hence connected, components (proof lines 1310-1318). The claim is H2: three short steps, with the descent of the quasi-compact opens as the only input requiring care.

items.title: A formally catenary Noetherian local ring is universally catenary
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a formally catenary Noetherian local ring A is universally catenary (source lines 32437-32441). The proof is a chain of reductions followed by a flatness argument. It first replaces A by A/p for a minimal prime p, so that the spectrum of the completion A-hat may be assumed equidimensional; then it reduces the universal catenarity assertion to showing that every local ring essentially of finite type over A is catenary, and further to showing that A[x_1, ..., x_n]_m is catenary for a maximal ideal m lying over the maximal ideal of A (proof lines 32444-32455). The substantive step introduces the unique maximal ideal m' of A-hat[x_1, ..., x_n] lying over m and uses that the displayed map A[x_1, ..., x_n]_m -> A-hat[x_1, ..., x_n]_{m'} is local and flat because completion is flat; it then observes that it suffices to prove the ring on the right is catenary with equidimensional spectrum, which is where formal catenarity enters (proof lines 32456-32463 and following). The non-routine content is the reduction to a single flat local extension of the polynomial ring and the appeal to equidimensionality of the completed spectrum.

items.title: Fibres of the strict henselization of the normalization and the minimal primes over the algebraic closure of the residue field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a local ring (A, m, kappa) with finitely many minimal primes, lets A' be the integral closure of A in the total ring of fractions of A_red, and considers the maps Spec(A') <- Spec((A')^{sh}) -> Spec(A^{sh}) where (A')^{sh} = A' tensor_A A^{sh}, the strict henselization being taken with respect to a separable algebraic closure kappa^{sep} of kappa inside an algebraic closure; it then asserts three things: that for a maximal ideal m' of A' the residue field kappa' is algebraic over kappa and the fibre of c over m' can be canonically identified with Hom_kappa(kappa', kappa-bar); that the right arrow is bijective on minimal primes; and that every minimal prime of (A')^{sh} lies in a unique maximal ideal and every maximal ideal contains a unique minimal prime (source lines 31338-31362). The proof first removes nilpotents: since (A/I)^{sh} = A^{sh}/IA^{sh} for the ideal I of nilpotents and the spectra involved agree, one may assume A is reduced (proof lines 31364-31373). Part (1) is then a computation: kappa'/kappa is algebraic because A' is integral over A, and by going up every maximal ideal of A' or (A')^{sh} lies over the corresponding maximal ideal; the proof computes (A')^{sh} tensor_{A^{sh}} kappa^{sep} = (A' tensor_A kappa) tensor_kappa kappa^{sep}, so the fibre of c over m' is the spectrum of kappa' tensor_kappa kappa^{sep}, and that spectrum is in bijection with Hom_kappa(kappa', kappa-bar) via the map sending sigma to the kernel of sigma tensor 1 (proof lines 31376-31396). Part (3) argues that A' is a finite product of normal domains, that (A')^{sh} is a filtered colimit of etale A'-algebras and hence normal, so every local ring of (A')^{sh} is a normal domain and every maximal ideal contains a unique minimal prime; then the integral-over-henselian-pair lemma makes ((A')^{sh}, m(A')^{sh}) a henselian pair and the connectedness lemma shows the intersection of V(q) with V(m (A')^{sh}) is connected, while V(m (A')^{sh}) = Spec((A')^{sh} tensor kappa^{sh}) is profinite, giving the unique maximal ideal above q (proof lines 31399-31422). Part (2) compares minimal primes of A' with those over minimal primes of A, uses flatness and quasi-finiteness of the filtered colimit to identify them, and finishes with the computation (A')^{sh} tensor_A Q(A) = A^{sh} tensor_A Q(A), where Q(A) is the total fraction ring, observing that the spectra of these two rings are exactly the minimal primes of (A')^{sh} and of A^{sh} respectively (proof lines 31425-31450). The non-routine content is the fibre computation in part (1), the henselian-pair connectedness argument in part (3), and the two-sided minimal-prime comparison in part (2).

items.title: A Noetherian local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres is Nagata and has the same number of branches as its completion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (A, m) whose formal fibres are geometrically normal (as happens for excellent or quasi-excellent rings) and concludes both that A is Nagata and that the number of (geometric) branches of A and of its completion A-hat agree (source lines 32230-32239). The proof is a multi-stage reduction. Since a normal ring is reduced, A is Nagata by the Nagata-local-ring lemma; the rest of the proof then establishes that A is a P-ring for the property 'geometrically normal over k' using the formal-fibres lemma, the finite-type-over-a-P-ring proposition and the criterion on maximal ideals, together with the corresponding statement for essentially finite type A-algebras (proof lines 32242-32249). It then reduces to the case where A is a domain: for a minimal prime q one has A-hat/q A-hat = (A/q)-hat and A^h/q A^h = (A/q)^h, so the number of branches of A is the sum over q of the numbers of branches of the quotients, and the same for A-hat (proof lines 32252-32259). The substantive part is the domain case. Letting A' be the integral closure of A in its fraction field K, finiteness of A -> A' follows from Nagata; the number of branches of A is the number of maximal ideals of A', and A'-hat decomposes as A' tensor_A A-hat, which in turn is the product over the maximal ideals m' of A' of the completions (A'_{m'})-hat (proof lines 32262-32271). Because each A'_{m'} is a local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres, each such completion is normal, so the minimal primes of A' tensor_A A-hat are in bijection with the factors of that product (proof lines 32272-32278). Finally, flatness of A -> A-hat gives the inclusions A-hat subset A' tensor_A A-hat subset K tensor_A A-hat, and since the outer rings have the same minimal primes so does the middle one, in a step the author states is a small detail omitted, which finishes the proof (proof lines 32278-32284). The geometric-branches statement is then obtained by applying the branch result to A^{sh}, using that its formal fibres are geometrically normal and that (A^{sh})-hat = ((A-hat)^{sh})-hat (proof lines 32287-32293). The non-routine content is the P-ring reduction and the minimal-prime comparison in the domain case.

items.title: Every object of the derived category of an inverse system of rings is represented by a system of K-flat complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for an inverse system of rings (A_n), every object K of the derived category of the module-valued inverse systems can be represented by a system of complexes (K_n^bullet) with each K_n^bullet K-flat (source lines 23815-23821). The proof is an induction that resolves the compatibility problem between the two structures. It first uses the preceding lemma to represent K by a system of complexes (M_n^bullet) all of whose transition maps M_{n+1}^bullet -> M_n^bullet are surjective (proof lines 23824-23826). It then chooses a quasi-isomorphism K_1^bullet -> M_1^bullet with K_1^bullet K-flat, possible by the K-flat resolution lemma (proof lines 23827-23829). The inductive step is the substantive part: assuming K_n^bullet -> ... -> K_1^bullet and maps psi_e : K_e^bullet -> M_e^bullet have been constructed so that the displayed squares commute for all e < n, the proof forms a diagram in D(A_{n+1}) and, because M_{n+1}^bullet -> M_n^bullet is termwise surjective, constructs the complex C^bullet fitting in the upper left corner with terms the fibred products C^p = M_{n+1}^p times_{M_n^p} K_n^p, which is quasi-isomorphic to M_{n+1}^bullet in a step the author states is omitted (proof lines 23830-23852). Choosing a quasi-isomorphism K_{n+1}^bullet -> C^bullet with K_{n+1}^bullet K-flat then completes the induction (proof lines 23853-23855). The non-routine content is the termwise surjectivity reduction and the fibred-product construction that makes the induction step possible.

items.title: Finite presentation relative to a base ring can be glued along a finite cover by principal opens
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite type ring map R -> A, an A-module M, and elements f_1, ..., f_r of A generating the unit ideal, and asserts the equivalence of two conditions: that each localization M_{f_i} be finitely presented relative to R, and that M itself be finitely presented relative to R (source lines 21130-21139). One implication is the localize-relative-finite-presentation lemma. For the converse, the proof writes 1 = sum f_i g_i in A and chooses a surjection from a polynomial ring in the x's and two sets of y's and z's onto A mapping y_i to f_i and z_i to g_i; this yields a surjection P = R[x, y, z]/(sum y_i z_i - 1) -> A with P a finitely presented R-algebra (proof lines 21141-21153). By the relatively-finitely-presented lemma each M_{f_i} is a finitely presented A_{f_i}-module, so by the cover criterion M is a finitely presented A-module, hence a finite P-module (proof lines 21154-21159). The substantive part is the verification that the kernel K of a surjection P^{oplus t} -> M is finite: since P_{y_i} surjects onto A_{f_i}, the lemmas cited show that each localization K_{y_i} is a finitely generated P_{y_i}-module; the proof chooses finitely many elements k_{i,j} of K generating all these localizations, lets K' be the P-submodule they generate, and concludes that K/K' has all localizations at the y_i equal to zero, whence K/K' = 0 because the y_i generate the unit ideal of P (proof lines 21160-21174). The non-routine content is the introduction of the auxiliary algebra P, which encodes the cover generators and their unit relation, and the final vanishing argument.

items.title: The evaluation map on internal Hom is an isomorphism for perfect first argument or for pseudo-coherent first argument with bounded below second and finite injective dimension third
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and objects K, L, M of D(R) and asserts that the evaluation map R Hom_R(L, M) tensor^L_R K -> R Hom_R(R Hom_R(K, L), M) of the preceding lemma is an isomorphism in two cases: when K is perfect, and when K is pseudo-coherent with L in D^+(R) and M of finite injective dimension (source lines 28561-28575). The proof works at the level of complexes rather than abstractly. It chooses a K-injective complex I^bullet representing M, a K-injective complex J^bullet representing L, and a bounded above complex of finite projective modules K^bullet representing K, then considers the explicit map of complexes from Tot(Hom^bullet(J^bullet, I^bullet) tensor_R K^bullet) to Hom^bullet(Hom^bullet(K^bullet, J^bullet), I^bullet) given by the evaluate-and-more lemma (proof lines 28578-28588). The substantive point is that this map decomposes into the component maps c_{p,r,s} : Hom_R(J^{-r}, I^p) tensor_R K^s -> Hom_R(Hom_R(K^s, J^{-r}), I^p), each of which is an isomorphism because K^s is finite projective; the product formula used to write the left-hand side is also justified by finiteness and projectivity of K^s (proof lines 28589-28600). The remaining difficulty is the finiteness bookkeeping: an element alpha of degree n on the left has only finitely many nonzero components alpha^{p,r,s} with n = p + r + s, whereas on the right one must verify that the same vanishing is forced on the components beta^{p,r,s} of an element beta. The proof does this in two cases: if K^bullet is a bounded complex of finite projective modules this is clear, and if instead I^bullet is bounded and J^bullet bounded below then beta^{p,r,s} vanishes for p outside a fixed range, for s large and for r large, so again only finitely many s values occur (proof lines 28601-28613). The non-routine content is this case split on the boundedness hypotheses, which is what converts the componentwise isomorphisms into a complex isomorphism.

items.title: The diagonal tensor-internal-Hom map is an isomorphism for a perfect argument or for a pseudo-coherent argument with bounded below second object and tor amplitude condition
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and objects K, L, M of D(R) and asserts that the map K tensor^L_R R Hom_R(M, L) -> R Hom_R(M, K tensor^L_R L) is an isomorphism in three cases: when M is perfect; when K is perfect; and when M is pseudo-coherent, L lies in D^+(R), and K has tor amplitude in [a, infinity] (source lines 28652-28667). The proof treats the first two cases by a generator reduction and the third by an explicit complex computation. In case M perfect, both sides of the arrow transform distinguished triangles in M into distinguished triangles and commute with direct sums, so by the check-on-a-generator remark and the classical-generator lemma it suffices to verify the statement for M = R[n], where it is obvious; case K perfect is settled by the same argument with the roles of the two arguments interchanged (proof lines 28670-28679). Case (3) is the substantive computation: the proof represents K and L by bounded below complexes K^bullet and L^bullet, may take K^bullet K-flat with flat terms by the tor amplitude lemma, and represents M by a bounded above complex M^bullet of finite free modules as pseudo-coherence allows (proof lines 28682-28688). It then identifies the object on the left as Tot(K^bullet tensor_R Hom^bullet(M^bullet, L^bullet)) and the object on the right as Hom^bullet(M^bullet, Tot(K^bullet tensor_R L^bullet)), using the Hom-out-of-projective lemma, and observes that both complexes have in degree n the same module, namely the direct sum over p + q + r = n of K^p tensor Hom_R(M^{-r}, L^q), identified with the direct sum of Hom_R(M^{-r}, K^p tensor_R L^q) because M^{-r} is finite free and the sums are finite (proof lines 28689-28703). The map of the lemma is then the one induced by the explicit map of complexes whose components are these canonical isomorphisms (proof lines 28704-28707). The non-routine content is the generator reduction in the perfect cases and the degreewise identification in case (3).

items.title: An object of the derived category is invertible exactly when it is locally a shift of the ring, and then its cohomology is finite projective in a single degree per factor
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and an object M of D(R) and gives two equivalent conditions: that M be invertible with respect to the tensor product in D(R); and that for every prime p there exist f not in p and an integer n with M_f isomorphic to R_f[-n]. It then asserts four consequences in the invertible case: that M is perfect; that M is the direct sum of its shifted cohomology objects; that each H^n(M) is a finite projective module; and that R decomposes as a product over a range of degrees on which the corresponding cohomology module is invertible (source lines 38656-38675). The proof is a real local-to-global argument. For (2) implies (1) it forms R Hom_R(M, R) and the composition map R Hom(M, R) tensor^L_R M -> R, sees by local checking that this is an isomorphism in a step stated to be omitted, and concludes that M is invertible because D(R) is symmetric monoidal (proof lines 38678-38683). For (1) implies (2) it observes that an invertible object of a monoidal category has a left dual, namely its inverse, so M is perfect by the duals-and-perfection lemma; then for a prime p with residue field kappa it uses that M tensor^L_R kappa is an invertible object of D(kappa), which forces dim H^i(M tensor^L_R kappa) to be nonzero for exactly one i and equal to 1 there, and the lift-perfect-from-residue-field lemma then produces the required n (proof lines 38686-38695). The last part is the global assembly: the proof defines U_n as the union of the opens D(f) with M_f isomorphic to R_f[-n], notes U_n and U_{n'} are disjoint for n not equal to n', and if M has tor amplitude in [a, b] then U_n is empty for n outside that range; hence there is a product decomposition R = prod_{a <= n <= b} R_n with U_n corresponding to Spec(R_n), and since D(R) decomposes as the product of the D(R_n) the remaining assertions (b), (c) and (d) follow (proof lines 38698-38707). The non-routine content is the residue-field argument that forces the single-degree shape, and the product decomposition that promotes it to a global statement.

items.title: The number of top-dimensional minimal primes of a Noetherian local ring is bounded by the length of the quotient by a system of parameters
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension d, lets t be the number of minimal prime ideals of dimension d, and lets (g_1, ..., g_d) be a system of parameters, and asserts t <= length_R(R/(g_1, ..., g_n)) (source lines 38296-38302). The proof reduces to the already established one-dimensional case and then uses Hilbert-polynomial asymptotics. After disposing of d = 0 and reducing d = 1 to the one-dimensional lemma, it assumes d > 1, lists the minimal primes p_1, ..., p_s with the first t of dimension d, and reduces to the case where R is reduced, arguing 'in exactly the same way as in the proof' of the one-dimensional statement (proof lines 38305-38310). For reduced R it forms the exact sequence 0 -> R -> prod_{i=1..t} R/p_i -> Q -> 0 and sets M equal to the product (proof lines 38313-38321). Localizing at p_j shows R_{p_j} -> M_{p_j} = (R/p_j)_{p_j} is surjective, so Q_{p_j} = 0 for all j, hence no height zero prime lies in the support of Q; consequently the numerical polynomial n -> length_R(Q/I^n Q) has degree dim(Supp(Q)) < d (proof lines 38322-38332). The substantive step is the Hilbert-function comparison: by the length additivity lemma — applicable since R does not have finite length — the polynomial n -> length_R(M/I^nM) - length_R(R/I^n) - length_R(Q/I^nQ) has degree less than d (proof lines 38333-38338). Since M is a product of the R/p_i and n -> length_R(R/p_i + I^n) is a numerical polynomial of degree exactly d for i = 1, ..., t, the leading coefficient of n -> length_R(M/I^nM) is at least t/d!; the multiplicity lemma then gives the bound (proof lines 38339-38344). The non-routine content is the support computation for Q together with the leading-coefficient comparison that converts the Hilbert polynomials into the numerical bound.

items.title: For a four-term inverse system of complexes the zeroth cohomology of the limit is the limit of the zeroth cohomologies under two vanishing hypotheses
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an inverse system of four-term complexes of abelian groups, denotes its limit and the inverse systems of cohomologies, and assumes that (A^{-2}_n) and (A^{-1}_n) have vanishing R^1 lim and that (H^{-1}_n) has vanishing R^1 lim; it concludes that H^0 = lim H^0_n (source lines 23022-23038). The proof is a spectral sequence computation carried out on both sides. It represents the system as an object K of the derived category of inverse systems of abelian groups, and computes H^0(R lim K) using both spectral sequences of the two-variable spectral sequence lemma, adding a footnote explaining that the use of these spectral sequences requires Ab(N) to have enough injectives, that an inverse system of abelian groups is injective exactly when each term is injective and the transition maps are split surjections, and that every system embeds in one of these, with the details stated to be omitted (proof lines 23041-23050). The first spectral sequence has the displayed E_1 page with terms R^1 lim A^0_n and R^1 lim A^1_n in the top row and A^{-2}, A^{-1}, A^0, A^1 in the bottom row, with horizontal differentials and all higher differentials zero (proof lines 23051-23058). The second has the displayed E_2 page whose bottom row consists of the limits of the cohomology systems and whose top row consists of their first derived limits, and it degenerates there (proof lines 23059-23068). Comparing the two computations of the single group H^0(R lim K) under the stated vanishing hypotheses gives the conclusion (proof lines 23068-23069). The non-routine content is the double spectral sequence comparison together with the injectivity remark that legitimises it.

items.title: Every finite module over a principal ideal domain is a finite free module plus a sum of quotients by nonzero elements
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that every finite module M over a principal ideal domain R is isomorphic to R^{oplus r} oplus bigoplus_{i=1..n} R/f_iR for some r, n >= 0 and nonzero f_i in R (source lines 37886-37894). The proof is a multi-stage reduction. Since a PID is a Noetherian Bezout ring, the splitting lemma applied there reduces the problem to the case where M is torsion; being finite, M then has nonzero annihilator, say fM = 0, so M may be viewed as a module over R/fR (proof lines 37896-37900). The substantive part is the structure of R/fR: since it is Noetherian of dimension zero — a fact the author states is a small detail omitted — it is a finite product of Artinian local rings R_j by the dimension-zero proposition, and each R_j, being a local quotient of a PID, is a generalized valuation ring in the sense of the earlier lemma, again with a small detail omitted (proof lines 37901-37907). Writing M = prod M_j with M_j = e_j M for the idempotents e_j corresponding to the factors, the structure lemma for modules over a generalized valuation ring gives M_j = bigoplus_{i=1..n_j} R_j/\overline{f}_{ji} R_j (proof lines 37908-37911). The final step lifts the quotients back to R: choosing lifts f_{ji} in R and elements g_{ji} with (g_{ji}) = (f_j, f_{ji}) where f_j is a lift of the uniformizer, the proof concludes M = bigoplus R/g_{ji}R as an R-module (proof lines 37912-37918). The non-routine content is the decomposition of R/fR into Artinian local factors and the lifting of the resulting cyclic quotients back to elements of R.

items.title: Over a flat neighbourhood covering the I-power torsion modules on both sides are equivalent and Hom does not change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R/I -> S/IS an isomorphism, and asserts three things: that the natural map on I-power torsion submodules is an isomorphism; that Hom_R(M, N) -> Hom_S(M tensor_R S, N tensor_R S) is an isomorphism whenever either M or N is I-power torsion; and that base change is an equivalence between I-power torsion modules and IS-power torsion modules (source lines 24300-24318). The proof gives each part. Part (1) sets M' = M/M[I^∞] and uses the exact sequence 0 -> M[I^∞] -> M -> M' -> 0 together with M[I^∞] = M[I^∞] tensor_R S to reduce to showing (M' tensor_R S)[(IS)^∞] = 0; writing I = (f_1, ..., f_t), it uses the divide-by-torsion lemma to get M'[I^∞] = 0, so the map x -> (f_1^n x, ..., f_t^n x) into the direct sum of t copies of M' is injective for every n > 0, and flatness of S keeps it injective after base change, giving (M' tensor_R S)[I^n] = 0 as required (proof lines 24325-24342). Part (2) splits into two cases: if N is I-power torsion then N tensor_R S = N and the map is an isomorphism by the adjoint tensor-restrict lemma; if M is I-power torsion then any map M -> N lands in N[I^∞] and any map after base change lands in (N tensor_R S)[(IS)^∞], so part (1) lets one replace N by N[I^∞] and reduce to the previous case (proof lines 24345-24354). Part (3) argues that the functor is fully faithful by (2) and checks essential surjectivity for IS-power torsion modules (proof lines 24357-24358 and following). The non-routine steps are the injection-into-a-direct-sum argument in part (1) and the reduction of part (2) to the case already handled.

items.title: Every one-dimensional minimal prime of the completion of a Noetherian local ring is the radical of the extension of a minimal prime of the henselization
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (A, m) with henselization A^h and a minimal prime q of the completion A-hat with dim(A-hat/q) = 1, and asserts the existence of a minimal prime q^h of A^h with q = sqrt(q^h A-hat) (source lines 32099-32106). The proof is a two-stage descent. Since A and A^h have the same completion, one may assume A is henselian; then one applies the quotient-by-idempotent lemma to the surjection A-hat -> A-hat/J with J = Ker(A-hat -> (A-hat)_q), which requires proving that a power of m annihilates J/J^2: the proof obtains q^n contained in J because dim((A-hat)_q) = 0, chooses a power of m annihilating J/J^2 using that (J/J^2)_q = 0 and that m is the only associated prime of J/J^2, and concludes that A-hat/J is the completion of a finite type A-algebra C (proof lines 32109-32121). The second stage identifies C: since C/mC = A/m, the ideal m_C = mC is maximal and A -> C is unramified there; after a principal localization C is a quotient of an etale A-algebra B by the structure proposition for unramified maps, and because the residue field extension of A -> C_{m_C} is trivial and A is henselian one gets B = A after a localization, so C = A/I for some ideal I (proof lines 32124-32134). Finally the proof shows J = IA-hat by exactness of completion in this situation and I = J cap A by flatness of A -> A-hat, so with q^n contained in J contained in q one gets p = q cap A satisfying p^n contained in I contained in p, and hence sqrt(p A-hat) = q (proof lines 32134-32141). The non-routine content is the two-step annihilation of J/J^2 that makes the quotient lemma applicable, and the henselian rigidity that forces the unramified algebra to be A itself.

items.title: The length of the quotient by powers of an element avoiding the minimal primes is at most n times the length modulo the element itself
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring (R, m) and an element x in m contained in no minimal prime of R, and asserts that the function P(n) = length_R(R/x^n R) satisfies P(n) <= n P(1) for all n >= 0, with equality for all n when x is a nonzerodivisor (source lines 37978-37988). The proof first notes that since the dimension is one, each R/x^nR has dimension zero and hence finite length, so P is defined (proof lines 37990-37993). It then argues by induction on n: P(0) = length_R(0) = 0 and the case n = 1 is immediate, and for n >= 2 the proof uses the exact sequence R/x^{n-1}R -> R/x^nR -> R/xR -> 0, where the first map is multiplication by x (proof lines 37994-38002). Additivity of length in this sequence gives P(n) <= P(n-1) + P(1), and the induction hypothesis P(n-1) <= (n-1)P(1) then yields P(n) <= n P(1), completing the induction step (proof lines 38003-38007). The equality statement is the substantive sharpening: when x is a nonzerodivisor the displayed sequence is also exact on the left, so one gets the exact recursion P(n) = P(n-1) + P(1) for all n >= 1, hence P(n) = n P(1) (proof lines 38009-38012). The non-routine content is the exactness of the short sequence and the resulting two-sided length computation.

items.title: For a field of characteristic p an Artin-Schreier extension of a discretely valued field falls into one of four cases located by the valuation of the parameter
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K of characteristic p > 0, an element xi of K, and the extension L obtained by adjoining a root of z^p - z = xi; it asserts that L/K is Galois and that one of four cases occurs — L = K; L/K unramified of degree p; L/K totally ramified with ramification index p; or the integral closure B of A in L is a discrete valuation ring with A in B weakly unramified and a purely inseparable residue extension of degree p — and then, with pi a uniformizer, asserts the three implications (A), (B), (C) locating the case from the shape of xi (source lines 34764-34787). The proof uses Artin-Schreier theory to get that the extension is Galois of order dividing p, and reads the four cases off the ramification discussion (proof lines 34790-34794). Case (A) is settled at once: for xi in A the ring A[x]/(x^p - x - xi) is finite etale over A, so only cases (1) and (2) can occur (proof lines 34797-34798). Case (B) is settled by a valuation count: writing xi = pi^{-n} a with p not dividing n and letting C = B_m for a maximal ideal, one has p ord_C(z) = -n ord_C(pi), so the ramification index of A in C is divisible by p and therefore equals p, and B = C (proof lines 34801-34806). Case (C) is the substantive case: setting k = n/p the proof rewrites the defining equation as (pi^k z)^p - pi^{n-k} (pi^k z) = a, and concludes from the fact that A[y]/(y^p - pi^{n-k} y - a) is a discrete valuation ring weakly unramified over A (proof lines 34809-34814). The non-routine content is the Artin-Schreier rewriting in case (C) and the valuation count in case (B).

items.title: A levelwise quasi-isomorphism of complexes of complexes induces a quasi-isomorphism of product totalizations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a map between two complexes of complexes of abelian groups, reinterprets them as double complexes via A^{p,q} = A_p^q and B^{p,q} = B_p^q, forms the product total complexes, and asserts that if each levelwise map A_p^bullet -> B_p^bullet is a quasi-isomorphism then the induced map of product totalizations is a quasi-isomorphism (source lines 30130-30147). The proof is a cone reduction. It recalls that the product totalization in degree n is the product over p + q = n of A^{p,q}, and forms the levelwise cones C_p^bullet, obtaining by functoriality a complex of complexes C_0^bullet -> C_1^bullet -> ... (proof lines 30150-30158). The substantive step is the degreewise computation of Tot_pi(C^{bullet,bullet}): its degree n part is the product over p + q = n of C^q_p, which the proof rewrites as the product of B^q_p and A^{q+1}_p and splits into two products, concluding that Tot_pi(C^{bullet,bullet}) is the cone of the map Tot_pi(A^{bullet,bullet}) -> Tot_pi(B^{bullet,bullet}), with the author stating that the verification that the differentials agree is omitted (proof lines 30159-30169). It therefore suffices to show that Tot_pi(A^{bullet,bullet}) is acyclic whenever each A_p^bullet is acyclic, which follows from the vanishing lemma for product totalizations of acyclic complexes (proof lines 30169-30172). The non-routine content is the degreewise identification of the totalization of the levelwise cones with the cone of the totalizations, which is what reduces the statement to the acyclicity criterion.

items.title: A product of valuation rings has weak dimension at most one, and its fraction field product is a localization
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a set J, a valuation ring A_j with fraction field K_j for each j, and sets A = prod A_j and K = prod K_j, asserting that A has weak dimension at most 1 and that A -> K is a localization (source lines 30647-30654). The proof reduces flatness to finitely generated ideals: by the weak-dimension-one criterion it suffices to show that any finitely generated ideal I of A is flat (proof lines 30657-30659). It then exploits the product structure. Letting I_j be the image of I in A_j, the proof observes that I_j = I tensor_A A_j, so the natural map I -> prod I_j is surjective by the finitely generated tensor proposition, whence I = prod I_j (proof lines 30660-30664). Since each A_j is a valuation ring, each I_j is principal, say I_j = (f_j), so I is generated by f = (f_j) (proof lines 30665-30668). The substantive step identifies I with a principal ideal generated by an idempotent: taking e to be the idempotent with coordinate 0 or 1 in A_j according to whether f_j is zero, the proof writes f = g e with g a nonzerodivisor, namely with g_j = 1 where f_j = 0 and g_j = f_j otherwise (proof lines 30669-30672). Hence I is isomorphic to the ideal (e), which is flat because (e) is a direct summand of A, giving weak dimension at most 1 (proof lines 30673-30674). The final statement follows because K = S^{-1}A for S = prod (A_j minus {0}) (proof lines 30674-30675). The non-routine content is the idempotent factorisation that turns a principal ideal of the product into a direct summand.
