items.title: For a degree p purely inseparable step over a weakly unramified extension one of three explicitly described alternatives holds
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a tower A in B in C of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L in M, a uniformizer pi of A, and assumes B is Nagata, A in B is weakly unramified, and M is a degree p purely inseparable extension of L; it concludes that one of three alternatives holds: that A -> C is weakly unramified; that C = B[pi^{1/p}]; or that there exists a degree p separable extension K_1/K totally ramified with respect to A such that L_1 = L tensor_K K_1 and M_1 = M tensor_K K_1 are fields and the maps of integral closures A_1 -> B_1 -> C_1 are weakly unramified extensions of discrete valuation rings (source lines 34675-34695). The proof is a case analysis controlled by a p-adic expansion. Letting e be the ramification index of C over B, the proof disposes of e = 1 immediately, and otherwise observes that e = p by the inequality and ramification-index lemmas, which implies that the residue fields of B and C agree; choosing a uniformizer pi_C of C one writes pi_C^p = u pi for a unit u of C, and since pi_C^p lies in L one gets u in B^*, as well as M = L[pi_C] (proof lines 34698-34704). The first substantial case is when there is an integer m >= 0 with u expanded as the displayed sum of p-th powers of elements of B times powers of pi plus a term b pi^m whose coefficient b has image in kappa_B which is not a p-th power; the proof then chooses an extension K_1/K from the degree-q construction with n = m + 2, denotes pi' the corresponding uniformizer with pi = (pi')^p + (pi')^{np} a, notes that A_1 -> B_1 is weakly unramified, and computes in B_1 the displayed identity expressing u pi as a p-th power plus b (pi')^{(m+1)p} plus (pi')^{np} b_1, a computation the author states is omitted (proof lines 34707-34726). From that identity the proof concludes that M_1 is obtained from L_1 by adjoining a p-th root of b + (pi')^{n-m-1} b_1, and since the residue field of B_1 equals that of B, the pre-purely-inseparable-case lemma gives that M_1/L_1 has degree p and C_1 is weakly unramified over B_1, which is the third alternative (proof lines 34727-34736). The second case is the complement: if no such m exists, then u is a p-th power in the pi-adic completion of B_1, and since B is Nagata this makes u a p-th power in B_1 itself, so the second alternative C = B[pi^{1/p}] holds (proof lines 34739-34743). The non-routine content is the p-adic expansion dichotomy and the explicitly computed identity in B_1.

items.title: Along a flat ring map inducing an isomorphism modulo a finitely generated ideal, restriction is an equivalence of derived complete derived categories
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring map A -> B and a finitely generated ideal I contained in A, assumes that A -> B is flat and that A/I is isomorphic to B/IB, and concludes that the restriction functor D(B) -> D(A) induces an equivalence D_comp(B, IB) -> D_comp(A, I) (source lines 26634-26640). The proof exhibits an explicit inverse. It chooses generators f_1, ..., f_r of I and uses the quasi-isomorphism of extended alternating Cech complexes C^bullet_A -> C^bullet_B; for K in D_comp(A, I) represented by a K-injective complex I^bullet of A-modules, it uses the vanishing of Ext^n_A(A_f, K) and Ext^n_A(B_f, K) for all f in I and all n to conclude that both C^bullet_A -> A and C^bullet_B -> B induce quasi-isomorphisms, in a step the author states is omitted (proof lines 26643-26662). Since C^bullet_A -> C^bullet_B is a quasi-isomorphism and I^bullet is K-injective, the proof concludes that Hom_A(B, I^bullet) -> I^bullet is a quasi-isomorphism, and because Hom_A(B, I^bullet) is a complex of B-modules this shows K is in the image of the restriction functor, i.e. essential surjectivity (proof lines 26663-26669). The argument in fact exhibits F : D_comp(A, I) -> D_comp(B, IB), K -> Hom_A(B, I^bullet), as a left inverse to restriction (proof lines 26671-26672). The final step shows F is also a right inverse: for L in D_comp(B, IB) represented by a K-injective complex J^bullet of B-modules, J^bullet is also K-injective as a complex of A-modules, so F applied to the restriction of L gives Hom_A(B, J^bullet), and there is a map J^bullet -> Hom_A(B, J^bullet) of complexes of B-modules whose composite with Hom_A(B, J^bullet) -> J^bullet is the identity (proof lines 26673-26683). The non-routine content is the systematic use of Cech complexes and K-injectivity to build the two-sided inverse.

items.title: A separable algebraic base change with separably closed residue fields, in which solutions descend, exists for any extension of discrete valuation rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for any extension A -> B of discrete valuation rings there is a commutative square of such extensions with three properties: the induced fraction field extensions K'/K and L'/L are separable algebraic; the residue fields of A' and B' are separable algebraic closures of those of A and B; and if a solution, weak solution or separable solution exists for A' -> B' then one exists for A -> B (source lines 34554-34574). The proof constructs the square and then proves the descent. Construction: the colimit-finite-etale lemma gives a filtered colimit A' of finite etale extensions of A whose residue field is a separable algebraic closure of that of A, and taking B' to be a strict henselization of B gives the square with parts (1) and (2) clear (proof lines 34577-34590). The substantive part is the descent: given a (weak) solution K'_1/K' for A' -> B', the proof uses that A' is a colimit to find a finite etale extension A subset A'_1 and a finite extension K_1 of its fraction field F with K'_1 = K' tensor_F K_1; since A subset A'_1 is finite etale and B' is strictly henselian, B' tensor_A A'_1 is a finite product of rings isomorphic to B', so that L' tensor_K K_1 = L' tensor_K F tensor_F K_1 is a finite product of rings isomorphic to L' tensor_{K'} K'_1; hence K_1/K is a (weak) solution for A -> B', and therefore also one for A -> B by the solutions-go-down lemma (proof lines 34593-34605). The non-routine content is the combination of the colimit description of A' with the strict henselianness of B' to make the tensor products split into copies of B'.

items.title: Over a Bezout domain every finite submodule of a free module is free and every finitely presented module splits as free plus torsion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma has two parts for a Bezout domain R: that every finite submodule of a free module is finite free; and that every finitely presented R-module M is the direct sum of a finite free module and a torsion module M_tors which is a summand of a module of the form bigoplus R/f_iR with the f_i nonzero (source lines 37846-37856). Part (1) is an induction on the rank: one reduces to F = R^{oplus n} because M is finite in a few lines the author states are omitted, treats n = 1 using that a finitely generated ideal in a Bezout domain is principal, and for n > 1 examines the image I of M under the projection onto the last summand: if I = 0 then M sits inside R^{oplus n-1} and induction applies, and if I is nonzero then I = (f) is isomorphic to R so M is isomorphic to R oplus Ker(M -> I) and induction applies again (proof lines 37858-37868). Part (2) uses the local structure: the localizations of R at maximal ideals are valuation rings, so the Warfield decomposition lemma applies and M is a summand of R^{oplus r} oplus bigoplus R/f_iR with f_i nonzero (proof lines 37871-37876). The final step is functoriality of the torsion submodule: M_tors is then a summand of bigoplus R/f_iR and M/M_tors is a summand of R^{oplus r}, which is finite free by part (1), so M is the direct sum of M_tors and M/M_tors (proof lines 37877-37883). The non-routine content is the induction in part (1) together with the observation that the two summands produced by the Warfield decomposition can be separated by taking the torsion submodule.

items.title: Injectivity of an Ext group along injective module maps forces a splitting of the truncation triangle
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an object K of D^-(R), and an integer a, assumes that for every injective R-module map M -> M' the map Ext^{-a}_R(K, M) -> Ext^{-a}_R(K, M') is injective, and concludes that there is a unique direct sum decomposition K = tau_{<= a}K oplus tau_{>= a+1}K with tau_{>= a+1}K of projective-amplitude in [a+1, b] for some b (source lines 19917-19926). The proof starts from the truncation distinguished triangle for K and computes the two Ext groups of tau_{<= a}K: it observes that Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{<= a}K, M) = Hom_R(H^a(K), M) and that Ext^{-a-1}_R(tau_{<= a}K, M) = 0, so the long exact sequence of Ext yields a short exact sequence 0 -> Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, M) -> Ext^{-a}_R(K, M) -> Hom_R(H^a(K), M), functorial in M (proof lines 19928-19947). The substantive step is the vanishing: for an injective module I one has Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, I) = 0, and since every module injects into an injective module the hypothesis forces Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, M) = 0 for every R-module M; the projective-amplitude lemma then gives that tau_{>= a+1}K has projective-amplitude in [a+1, b] for some b, which is where boundedness above is used (proof lines 19948-19956). The splitting then follows from the unique-splitting lemma (proof lines 19956-19957). The non-routine content is the computation of the two Ext groups of the lower truncation and the passage from the vanishing at injective modules to all modules.

items.title: An element avoiding the minimal primes extends to a system of parameters stable under small perturbations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension d and an element f in m contained in no minimal prime of R, and asserts the existence of g_1, ..., g_{d-1} in m and an integer N such that f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1} is a system of parameters and such that for every h in m^N the sequence f + h, g_1, ..., g_{d-1} is again a system of parameters with the same length quotient (source lines 38347-38360). The proof is an explicit computation. By the preceding existence lemma there are g_1, ..., g_{d-1} making f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1} a system of parameters, so that m = sqrt((f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1})); by the Noetherian power lemma there is n with m^n contained in (f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}), and the proof claims N = n + 1 works (proof lines 38363-38369). The verification is a direct ideal computation: for h in m^N one writes h = a f + sum b_i g_i with a, b_i in m, and then the displayed chain of equalities shows that (f + h, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}) = ((1 + a) f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}) = (f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}) because 1 + a is a unit of R, which gives both the system-of-parameters claim and the equality of lengths (proof lines 38370-38383). The non-routine content is the choice N = n + 1 that makes the perturbation absorbable into the first ideal generator.

items.title: Over a ring with finite-dimensional Noetherian maximum spectrum a finitely presented module with a large free summand locally splits off a free summand globally
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem takes a ring R whose maximum spectrum Omega is a Noetherian topological space of dimension d < infinity, and a finitely presented R-module M such that for every maximal ideal m the localization M_m has a free direct summand of rank greater than d; it concludes that M is isomorphic to R oplus M' (source lines 38919-38930). The proof reduces the local hypothesis to a global dimension bound and then invokes the splitting proposition. The reduction is a spreading-out argument: for m in Omega with R_m^{oplus r} a direct summand of M_m, the colimit lemmas for localization and for finitely presented modules give an f not in m with R_f^{oplus r} a direct summand of M_f, so the hypothesis means precisely that the dimension of the closed set V(x) exceeds d for every x in Omega, where V(x) is the set of elements that split (proof lines 38933-38940). The substantive step is the application of the splitting proposition with F empty, h = 0, no s_i, n = 0 and no x_i or v_i, and k = d + 1, which produces an element s in M and a closed subset F' of Omega such that every irreducible component of F' has codimension at least d + 1 and Z(s) is contained in F' (proof lines 38941-38945). Since d equals the dimension of Omega this forces F' to be empty, so the map s : R -> M is the inclusion of a direct summand at every maximal ideal (proof lines 38945-38947). It follows that s is universally injective by the stalk-wise criterion, and hence s is split injective by the universally-exact-splitting lemma, which gives the required decomposition M = R oplus M' (proof lines 38947-38951). The non-routine content is the codimension bookkeeping that converts the local rank bound into the emptiness of F' and the final passage from universal injectivity to split injectivity.

items.title: A local ring is unibranch exactly when its henselization has a unique minimal prime
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for a local ring A with henselization A^h, A is unibranch if and only if A^h has a unique minimal prime (source lines 31248-31259). The proof notes that this follows from the branch count but supplies a direct argument anyway, and the direct argument is what is counted. Assume (2) and let p^h be the unique minimal prime of A^h: flatness of A -> A^h makes p = A cap p^h the unique minimal prime of A by going down, and since A^h/pA^h = (A/p)^h is reduced by the reducedness lemma, one gets p^h = pA^h (proof lines 31268-31276). Then with A' the integral closure of A/p in its fraction field, unibranchness amounts to A' being local; the proof argues by contradiction, noting that A -> A' is integral so every maximal ideal of A' lies over m, and that if A' had two distinct maximal ideals m_1 and m_2 one could choose f_i in m_i outside m_{3-i} and pass to the finite subalgebra B = A/p[f_1, f_2] with the two distinct maximal ideals B cap m_i (proof lines 31277-31286). The substantive step is the tensor comparison: the inclusions A/p in B in kappa(p) become after tensoring with the flat map A -> A^h the chain A^h/p^h in B tensor_A A^h in kappa(p) tensor_A A^h in kappa(p^h), the last inclusion because kappa(p) tensor_A A^h = kappa(p) tensor_{A/p} A^h/p^h is a localization of the domain A^h/p^h (proof lines 31287-31301 and following). The contradiction is then produced from the two distinct maximal ideals of B tensor_A A^h lying over the single maximal ideal of the domain A^h/p^h. The non-routine content is this flat base change comparison, which converts a statement about A' into one about the tensor product over A^h.

items.title: Over a Bezout domain any unimodular row of length n is the first row of an invertible matrix
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Bezout domain R, an integer n >= 1, and elements f_1, ..., f_n generating the unit ideal, and asserts the existence of an invertible n x n matrix over R whose first row is f_1 ... f_n (source lines 37925-37930). The proof notes that this follows from the earlier splitting lemma but supplies a direct inductive construction. For n = 1 the result holds. For n > 1, after renumbering so that f_1 is nonzero, the proof uses the Bezout hypothesis to choose f with (f) = (f_1, ..., f_{n-1}), takes an (n-1) x (n-1) matrix A whose first row is f_1/f, ..., f_{n-1}/f — which exists by the induction hypothesis, since those quotients generate the unit ideal — and chooses a, b with af - b f_n = 1, possible because 1 lies in (f, f_n) (proof lines 37933-37941). The explicit answer is then the product of the two displayed matrices, the left one having determinant 1 and hence being invertible, whose product therefore has the required first row and is invertible (proof lines 37942-37962). The non-routine content is the reduction of length n to length n - 1 by factoring out the generator of the ideal spanned by the first n - 1 entries, together with the determinant-one matrix that supplies the last column.

items.title: An essentially finite type injective local homomorphism out of a geometrically unibranch local domain with separable residue extension is the localization of an etale map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a geometrically unibranch local domain (A, m) and an injective local homomorphism A -> B of local rings, essentially of finite type, such that mB is the maximal ideal of B and the induced residue field extension is separable, and concludes that A -> B is the localization of an etale ring map (source lines 31817-31828). The proof is a reduction-and-descent argument. It writes B = C_q with A -> C of finite type and q a prime over m, and uses the unramifiedness criterion to see that A -> C is unramified at q (proof lines 31831-31835). The structure proposition for unramified maps then supplies, after replacing C by a principal localization, a standard etale ring map A -> C' with a surjection C' -> C; taking q' the inverse image of q and B' = C'_{q'} gives a surjection B' -> B, and it remains to show it is also injective (proof lines 31836-31842). That is the substantive step: since A is a domain the rings C' and B' are reduced, and since A is geometrically unibranch B' is a domain, using the invariance of the number of branches under smooth maps and the branch-count-one criterion (proof lines 31845-31849). If B' -> B were not injective, then A cap Ker(B' -> B) would be nonzero by the nonzero-contraction lemma, contradicting the injectivity of A -> B (proof lines 31850-31852). The non-routine content is the recognition that geometric unibranchness forces the standard etale cover to be a domain, which is what upgrades surjectivity to an isomorphism.

items.title: Five equivalent formulations of regularity for a morphism of schemes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma records five equivalent formulations of the regularity of a morphism: the morphism itself, flatness with geometrically regular fibres, the ring-map condition on every compatible pair of affine opens, the same condition on an open cover, and the condition on an affine open cover. The proof reconciles the global formulations with the ring-theoretic one by localising and using that regularity is checked on affine opens, so the content is the assembly of the local conditions into the global ones. Retained author proof at lines 5701-5733.

items.title: A finitely locally free module trivial on every fibre comes from the base over a reduced base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a flat proper finitely presented family whose structure sheaf pushes forward to the structure sheaf of the base, stably under base change, a finite locally free module that is trivial on every fibre is pulled back from the base when the base is reduced. The proof uses the diagonal representability result to obtain a locally closed immersion parameterising the triviality locus, observes that the hypothesis makes it bijective, and then concludes it is an isomorphism because the base is reduced. Combining the locally closed immersion with bijectivity and reducedness is the content. Retained author proof at lines 9326-9331.

items.title: The action of a derivation on a thickening exists and is unique for algebraic spaces over a base space
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of first order thickenings of algebraic spaces over a base algebraic space B and a linear map from the pullback of the differentials to the conormal sheaf, the lemma produces a unique morphism of the thickening pairs obtained by acting with the derivation, and identifies its effect on the structure sheaves. The proof uses the square-zero structure of the conormal sheaf to define the modified map on structure sheaves, verifies the resulting map is a morphism of thickenings over B by checking the algebra structure, and proves uniqueness by comparing two such maps through the difference construction. The construction and its uniqueness via the difference are the substance. Retained author proof at lines 3764-3800.

items.difficulty_reason: The algebraic-spaces criterion for the Gorenstein property, structured exactly as the Cohen-Macaulay criterion: three chartwise conditions using surjective etale charts by schemes, plus a pointwise equivalence comparing the strict local rings of a point and its image. The descent step together with the strict-local-ring comparison is the substance. Retained author proof at lines 6562-6609.

items.title: Filtered colimits of abelian sheaves commute with cohomology under a generating set of quasi-compact sheaves
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the commutation of cohomology with filtered colimits for a site carrying a set S of sheaves satisfying five conditions, including quasi-compactness of its members (statement lines 2629-2653). The proof is an induction on the cohomological degree with two substantial parts. The base case is reduced to the corresponding statement on colimits of global sections, whose hypotheses are checked through (1)-(3) and quasi-compactness (proof lines 2656-2675). The induction step reduces the assertion to the vanishing of H^{p0+1} on a filtered colimit of injective sheaves and computes with the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence E_1^{p,q} = H^q(K^{p+1}, I) = H^q(C/K^{p+1}, j^{-1}I), where commutation of j^{-1} with filtered colimits and the induction hypothesis in the localized topoi give the vanishing (proof lines 2687-2725). The delicate part, which the author writes out separately, is the check that the localized topoi themselves admit a set satisfying (1)-(5), without which the induction could not be applied (proof lines 2728-2785). The claim is H2: a long but fully written-out induction.

items.title: Filtered colimits commute with cohomology for a collection of finite coverings cofinal in each object
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that filtered colimits of abelian sheaves commute with cohomology, uniformly over the objects of a subset B, provided a collection Cov of finite coverings of those objects is cofinal (statement lines 2517-2541). The proof is an induction on the cohomological degree. It first records that finiteness of the coverings in Cov makes the objects of B quasi-compact in the relevant sense (proof lines 2543-2550); then it replaces an arbitrary filtered diagram by one of injective sheaves using functorial injective embeddings, which reduces the statement to the vanishing of H^p on a filtered colimit of injectives (proof lines 2553-2602); finally the vanishing is obtained from the same-chapter criterion for filtered colimits of injective sheaves, whose hypothesis is precisely the cofinality of Cov, with the degree zero case supplying the input (proof lines 2605-2627). The non-formal content is the reduction to the vanishing claim together with the verification that the criterion applies. The claim is H2: a three-step proof, each step written out.

items.title: A filtered colimit of K-flat complexes is K-flat
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a filtered colimit of K-flat complexes of O-modules on a ringed site is K-flat (statement lines 3151-3157). The proof is a two-step reduction: because the colimit of complexes is taken termwise, the total tensor product commutes with it, colim_i Tot(F^bullet tensor K_i^bullet) = Tot(F^bullet tensor colim_i K_i^bullet) (proof lines 3160-3167), and testing against an acyclic F^bullet each member of the system is acyclic by K-flatness, so exactness of filtered colimits gives acyclicity of the colimit (proof lines 3167-3169). The content is the termwise commutation of the tensor product with the colimit together with exactness of filtered colimits. The claim is H2: one displayed identity plus one standard exactness property.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects the comparison results between the Zariski topoi of the big site of locally quasi-compact spaces and the small Zariski topoi of a space, in seven numbered items covering cohomology, exactness of the pushforward, the unit of the adjunction, the derived statement, the commutativity of the square induced by a morphism f : X -> Y, and the base change identities for a proper f (statement lines 7769-7804). The claim is H2: seven short arguments of the same flavour, each written out, with the derived case as the most technical.

items.title: Compact objects in the derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category are summands of finite complexes built from generators
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma describes compact objects of D(A) for a Grothendieck abelian category with a generating set S satisfying two conditions: every compact object is a direct summand of a finite complex of finite direct sums of elements of S (statement lines 13933-13946). The proof has three substantial parts: compactness is used twice to replace infinite constructions by finite ones, first to make K bounded below through the canonical truncations (proof lines 13949-13961) and then to factor the identity through a bounded complex L with terms in direct sums of S (proof lines 13967-13989); the technical heart is the improvement claim, where assumption (2) on the functor Hom_A(E, -) and compactness of K cut a direct sum L^c down to a finite subsum through which the differential factors and whose remaining projection becomes zero after composing with varphi (proof lines 14001-14017); finally the kernel of that projection gives a distinguished triangle from which a new factorisation is extracted using the homological behaviour of Hom_{D(A)}(K, -) (proof lines 14018-14031), and the idempotent so obtained is split to display K as a direct summand (proof lines 13990-13998). The claim is H2: a long but completely written-out argument whose only inputs are the two displayed assumptions and standard results of the derived-category chapters.

items.title: The pullback of a sheaf along the projection of the qc site of locally quasi-compact spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the sheaf (f : Y -> X) maps to Gamma(Y, f^{-1}F) on the qc site of locally quasi-compact spaces as the pullback of F along the projections to the Zariski and qc topologies (statement lines 7674-7686). The proof has three genuinely different parts. The Zar-sheaf property is immediate (proof lines 7689-7693), but the qc-sheaf property is not: by the sheaf criterion one must prove injectivity, which uses surjectivity of qc coverings and detection of equality at stalks, and then gluing after refinement via the plus construction (proof lines 7696-7711). The gluing itself requires two steps, first manufacturing a compatible family of stalk values from local sections over opens W_i of the base (proof lines 7713-7732) and then showing that family is a global section by covering a neighbourhood of an arbitrary point with finitely many quasi-compact pieces and shrinking until finitely many local sections agree (proof lines 7734-7745). Finally the identification with the pullbacks follows by comparing with the explicit colimit description of the pullback and its sheafification (proof lines 7747-7760). The claim is H2: three separate arguments, of which the second is a real topological gluing argument.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the induction step (V_n) implies (V_{n+1}) in the comparison of two topologies on a site carrying the data of the situation, namely a set of arrows P and weak Serre subcategories A'_X of the tau'-sheaves (statement lines 7147-7150, with the situation delivered verbatim as a context span from lines 6840-6879). The proof has four stages: an arbitrary class in degree n+1 is replaced, using locality of cohomology, by the target of an arrow of P that is a tau-covering (proof lines 7152-7172); the degree-n comparison result produces the corresponding tau'-class and the induction hypothesis kills it locally after pullback along an arrow of P (proof lines 7184-7194); finally the hypothesis that the class dies under the canonical map F -> Rf_{tau,*}f_tau^{-1}F, together with the cited Leray-type lemma and a distinguished-triangle argument, kills the original class on a tau'-covering, which is the assertion (proof lines 7205-7289). The non-formal content is the bookkeeping that lets the degree-n statement be applied to the twisted data and then lifted back. The claim is H2: a long reduction, written out in full, with each step attributed to a named result of the same section.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that having a left dual in D(O) forces an object to be perfect and forces the dual to be the canonical one (statement lines 13185-13192). The proof is a long technical development with a clear architecture: the duality identities are converted into factorisation statements for the identity through suitable subcomplexes of any chosen representative (proof lines 13210-13256); applying these to dumb truncations yields boundedness and then a bounded above representative of a controlled shape (proof lines 13259-13275); the same machinery, under the extra hypothesis of tor amplitude, gives m-pseudo-coherence and finally a strictly perfect representative on the members of a covering (proof lines 13278-13413); the dual computed from that representative is then identified with the abstract left dual using the identities of the first paragraph. items.difficulty_reason: The lemma upgrades a failure of base change in degree q to a counterexample over the spectrum of a field: assuming BC(f, n, q-1) holds but BC(f, n, q) does not, it produces a commutative diagram with T = Spec(K) and a sheaf on Spec(K) annihilated by n for which the base change map in degree q is not an isomorphism (statement lines 17078-17094, with the standing notation delivered as a context span from lines 16847-16866). The non-formal content is concentrated in that last verification. The claim is H2: a long but fully written-out verification, assembled by an explicitly cited formal principle.

The non-formal content is the reduction of the general case to the smooth situation together with the two interludes. The claim is H2: a long argument, entirely written out, with Noether normalization and the curve bound as its only inputs.

items.title: A frobenius linear endomorphism of a finite dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field has surjective F minus one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a frobenius linear endomorphism F of a finite dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p has F - 1 surjective, with kernel of dimension at most dim_k(V) over F_p (statement lines 9640-9648). The proof combines three arguments: a reduction to the case of injective F via F-stable filtrations and the case F = 0 (proof lines 9651-9654), the inversion of the matrix of F to turn surjectivity into the system of p-power equations lambda_j^p minus sum b_{ij}lambda_i = sum b_{ij}mu_i (proof lines 9657-9675), and the construction of the algebra A defined by those equations, which is standard smooth because the partial derivatives of the x_j^p vanish and whose monomial basis shows dim_k(A) = p^n (proof lines 9676-9685). Surjectivity then follows by counting the p^n points of Spec(A) through algebraic closedness of k (proof lines 9686-9688). The claim is H2: three explicit steps, each short, with the algebra construction as the non-formal core.

The non-formal content is the combination of the two reductions with the dimension induction. The claim is H2: a long but completely written-out argument whose only external input is the vanishing statement for curves.

items.difficulty_reason: The proposition, attributed by the author to Serre, deduces the vanishing of Galois cohomology from the vanishing of the Brauer groups of all finite extensions of K: H^q(Gal(K^sep/K), (K^sep)^*) = 0 for q at least 1 and H^q(Gal, M) = 0 for torsion M and q at least 2 (statement lines 10693-10707, whose commented reference block is excluded from the counted spans as explained in the notes). items.title: Extension by zero along an etale morphism commutes with base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma records that extension by zero along an etale morphism commutes with base change, j'_!f'^{-1} = f^{-1}j_! (statement lines 11492-11504). The proof is an adjointness argument: the two composite functors are identified as left adjoints of f'_*(j')^{-1} and j^{-1}f_* respectively, and commutation of pushforward with etale localization makes those right adjoints equal, so the left adjoints agree (proof lines 11507-11513). The content is the choice of adjunctions and the one identification of right adjoints. The claim is H2: a short categorical argument, with the author noting that it works for any morphism of sites.

items.title: Cech cohomology in degree one agrees with cohomology on every topological space
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a topological space X and an abelian sheaf F, the lemma shows that the comparison map from the first Cech cohomology group to the first cohomology group is an isomorphism (statement lines 2642-2647). The proof uses the exact sequence relating the Cech group of a fixed covering to cohomology and to the zeroth Cech cohomology of the sheafified first cohomology presheaf, which gives injectivity immediately (proof lines 2650-2657). For surjectivity one must show that any section of the presheaf of first cohomology over a covering becomes zero after refinement, which the author reads off from the vanishing of the sheafification of that presheaf by locality of cohomology (proof lines 2657-2663). The claim is H2: a two-line reduction to the low degree terms of a spectral sequence, with the locality of cohomology as the single input doing the work.

items.title: K-flatness of a complex of modules is checked on stalks
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a ringed space X and a complex K of O_X-modules, the lemma shows that K is K-flat if and only if every stalk of K is K-flat over the corresponding local ring (statement lines 5872-5879). One direction is a stalkwise argument: tensor products and direct sums commute with taking stalks and exactness is checked on stalks, so exactness of the relevant total complexes follows from exactness of their stalks (proof lines 5882-5886). The converse is more substantial: given an acyclic complex M over the local ring at a point, its pushforward by the skyscraper functor is an acyclic complex of O_X-modules, so tensoring it with the K-flat K gives an acyclic total complex, and taking stalks at the point recovers the total complex of M with the stalk of K, which is therefore acyclic (proof lines 5887-5894). The claim is H2: one direction is bookkeeping with stalks, while the converse requires inventing the skyscraper pushforward to transfer acyclicity from the local ring to the space.

primary.label: author Lemma environment, source label lemma-check-K-flat-stalks (statement, source lines 5872-5879)

items.title: Cohomology is unchanged by pushing forward along a closed immersion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a closed immersion of topological spaces i: Z to X and an abelian sheaf F on Z, the lemma shows that the cohomology of F on Z agrees with the cohomology of the pushforward on X (statement lines 3446-3451). The proof names the mechanism: the pushforward along a closed immersion is exact, hence its higher derived functors vanish, so the Leray spectral sequence for the composite of the global section functor with the pushforward degenerates and gives the equality (proof lines 3453-3458). The claim is H2: a short but complete chain of reasoning whose content is the exactness of the pushforward and the resulting degeneration of Leray.

items.title: Cohomology on the set of specialisations of a quasi-compact subset as a colimit over its neighbourhoods
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a spectral space X, an abelian sheaf F and a quasi-compact subset E, the lemma expresses the cohomology on the set W of points specializing to a point of E as a colimit of the cohomologies of the quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of E, and gives the analogous statement for the complement when E is constructible (statement lines 3869-3881). The proof identifies W as the inverse limit of the quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of E, notes that each of those is a spectral space, and applies the colimit formula for cohomology on spectral spaces to obtain the first statement (proof lines 3884-3888). The second statement is obtained by the same argument with the variant of the structure theorem for the complement of a constructible subset (proof lines 3889-3890). The claim is H2: one structure theorem plus one colimit formula, applied twice, with no additional construction.

items.title: Higher direct images as the sheaf associated to the presheaf of cohomology on inverse images
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of ringed spaces f: X to Y and an O_X-module F, the lemma identifies the higher direct images with the sheaves associated to the presheaves sending an open V to the cohomology of F on the inverse image of V, with the restriction maps coming from the displayed equation, and notes that the same holds for a bounded below complex (statement lines 591-603). The proof resolves F injectively and recalls that the higher direct image is by definition the cohomology sheaf of the pushed forward complex; because cohomology sheaves in the category of O_Y-modules are computed as associated sheaves of the presheaves of kernels modulo images, the presheaf in question is computed termwise, and identifying f_*I(V) with I(f^{-1}(V)) makes it exactly the cohomology of F on the inverse image (proof lines 605-626). The claim is H2: the content is the passage from the cohomology sheaf of a complex of modules to the associated presheaf, which the author writes out explicitly.

items.title: Flasque modules have vanishing higher Cech cohomology for every open covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a ringed space, a flasque sheaf of modules F and an open covering, the lemma shows that all higher Cech cohomology groups of the covering vanish (statement lines 1963-1970). The proof applies the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence: the presheaves of higher cohomology appearing in its low degree terms vanish because F is flasque and hence acyclic for the global section functors, and the spectral sequence then degenerates to give both the equality of Cech and ordinary cohomology and the vanishing (proof lines 1972-1977). The chapter text immediately before the lemma warns that the statement fails for flasque presheaves, which is why the sheaf hypothesis is essential. The claim is H2: one spectral sequence applied with a vanishing input, with the two steps (vanishing of the presheaves, then degeneration) explicitly named.

items.title: The constant sheaf on an irreducible topological space has no higher cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For an irreducible topological space X and any abelian group A, the lemma shows that the cohomology of the constant sheaf vanishes in positive degrees (statement lines 3461-3466). The proof computes the values of the constant sheaf: any nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is itself irreducible and hence connected, so the constant sheaf takes the value A on every nonempty open and the value zero on the empty open, which is precisely the flasqueness condition (proof lines 3469-3474). Vanishing of higher cohomology for flasque sheaves is a previous lemma, and the conclusion follows immediately (proof lines 3475-3476). The claim is H2: a one-line computation of values plus one cited vanishing result, with nothing left to the reader.

items.title: Stalk of a higher direct image along a spectral map as cohomology on the set of specialisations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a spectral map of spectral spaces f: X to Y, a point y, the set E of points specializing to y and an abelian sheaf F on X, the lemma identifies the stalk at y of the p-th higher direct image with the cohomology of F on the inverse image of E (statement lines 3893-3899). The proof observes that E is the intersection of the quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of y, so its inverse image is the filtered intersection of the inverse images, which are spectral spaces because f is spectral; hence the inverse image of E is a spectral space and its cohomology is the colimit of the cohomologies of the inverse images of the neighbourhoods, by the colimit lemma for spectral spaces (proof lines 3901-3911). The other side of the identity is exactly that colimit, since stalks of higher direct images are computed as colimits over the quasi-compact open neighbourhoods (proof lines 3912-3913). The claim is H2: the identification of the two colimits is the content, with the spectrality of the pieces as the input that makes the colimit lemma applicable.

items.title: Pushforward of an injective module is acyclic for the global section functors of the target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of ringed spaces f: X to Y and an injective O_X-module I, the lemma shows that the Cech cohomology of the pushforward vanishes in positive degrees for every open covering of Y, that its cohomology vanishes on every open of Y, and hence that the pushforward is right acyclic for the global section functors of Y (statement lines 1778-1794). The proof is a termwise identification: the Cech complex of the pushforward with respect to a covering of Y equals the Cech complex of I with respect to the inverse image covering of X, because the value of the pushforward on an intersection is the value of I on the inverse image of that intersection (proof lines 1797-1809). The vanishing for I is a previous lemma, and the passage from Cech vanishing to cohomological vanishing is the vanishing criterion already established (proof lines 1810-1812). The claim is H2: one termwise computation plus two cited inputs, with the identification of the complexes written out in full.

items.title: Local Noetherianness is unchanged by base change along a finitely generated field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k and a finitely generated field extension k'/k, the lemma shows that X is locally Noetherian exactly when its base change is (statement lines 2314-2321). The proof reduces to the affine case using locality of the Noetherian property, arriving at the statement that A is Noetherian if and only if k' tensor_k A is; the forward direction is the standard behaviour of Noetherian rings under a field extension, and the converse is descent of Noetherianness along the faithfully flat map to the tensor product (proof lines 2323-2332). The claim is H2: a locality reduction plus the two directions of the tensor product statement, each a single cited input, with the finite generation hypothesis used precisely for the forward direction.

items.title: A sufficiently large base field extension makes a scheme Jacobson and makes residue fields at closed points algebraic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k, the lemma asserts that for every field extension K/k of sufficiently large cardinality, the residue field at every closed point of X_K is algebraic over K and X_K is a Jacobson scheme (statement lines 2699-2710). The proof covers X by affine opens, uses the algebra base change result for Jacobson rings and the affine criterion to attach to each member U_i a cardinal kappa_i beyond which the base change U_{i,K} has both properties, takes the maximum of the finitely many cardinals, and then applies the local criterion for Jacobson schemes to conclude for X_K (proof lines 2712-2723). The statement about residue fields is inherited from the affine members (proof lines 2724-2726). The claim is H2: a compact argument whose content is the passage from the affine pieces to the global scheme, with the cardinal threshold bookkeeping written out.

items.title: Noether normalization over the fibre: factorization through affine space with finite fibre map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism of affine schemes f: X to S and a point s with fibre dimension d, the lemma produces a factorization of f through affine space of relative dimension d over S such that the induced morphism on the fibres over s is finite (statement lines 3415-3424). The proof is a direct transcription of the situation into rings: writing S = Spec(A), X = Spec(B) and choosing a surjection onto B from a polynomial ring, Noether normalization supplies elements y_1 to y_d in the subalgebra generated by the chosen variables such that the induced A-algebra map from A[t_1,...,t_d] to B becomes finite after tensoring with the residue field at s (proof lines 3426-3437). The same elements define the required factorization and the finiteness statement is exactly the fibrewise one. The claim is H2: one algebra input applied in the relative setting, with the transcription between the geometry and the rings carried out explicitly.

items.difficulty_reason: For an extension of fields k'/k with k separably algebraically closed and a scheme X over k, the lemma shows that the base change morphism induces a bijection between irreducible components (statement lines 1523-1529). The proof is a two-step reduction: separably closedness of k makes the extension k' geometrically irreducible over k, hence the spectrum of k' is geometrically irreducible as a scheme, and then the base change is recognized as the product of X with that geometrically irreducible factor, so the general bijection statement for products with a geometrically irreducible factor applies (proof lines 1531-1538). The claim is H2: two cited inputs with the identification of the base change as a product as the connecting observation, and nothing referred to the reader.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a smooth morphism X to Spec(k) with k a field, the lemma concludes that X is geometrically regular, geometrically normal and geometrically reduced over k (statement lines 4616-4621). The proof reduces the three properties simultaneously to a statement about a single smooth scheme over a field: by the purely inseparable characterizations already available it suffices to show that the base change along any finite purely inseparable extension is regular, normal and reduced, and the base change of a smooth morphism is smooth (proof lines 4626-4634). There it is enough to prove the three properties for a scheme smooth over a field, which the author does in two steps: smoothness over a field implies regularity by the specialized lemma, and a regular scheme is normal by the standard criterion (proof lines 4635-4639). The claim is H2: the reduction is a shared one for three properties, with two cited inputs finishing the job.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Over an algebraically closed field k, for a proper k-scheme X with an invertible sheaf L, the lemma concludes that L is very ample provided the restriction map on global sections surjects onto the sections of L over every zero dimensional closed subscheme of degree two (statement lines 4385-4396). The proof is a reformulation: given two distinct closed points, their union viewed as a closed subscheme of degree two gives the first hypothesis of the separation lemma, and given a nonzero tangent vector, the associated morphism from the spectrum of the dual numbers is a closed immersion whose image is a zero dimensional subscheme of degree two giving the second hypothesis (proof lines 4398-4407). The separation lemma then yields very ampleness. The claim is H2: a clean translation between two formulations, with the identification of the image of a tangent vector as a degree two subscheme as the only step needing care.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a variety over k possessing a k-rational point at which it is smooth is geometrically integral (statement lines 4775-4780). The proof replaces X by its smooth locus U, which is nonempty, hence dense and scheme theoretically dense, and remains dense and scheme theoretically dense after base change to the algebraic closure; it therefore suffices to prove geometric integrality of U (proof lines 4783-4787). The claim is H2: three standard inputs combined in a short argument, with the reduction to the smooth locus as the step that makes the geometric connectedness hypothesis available.

items.difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a cocartesian square of rings and says that if the algebra is flat over the base then the base change of its naive cotangent complex is a quasi-isomorphism onto the naive cotangent complex of the base changed algebra, and that the derived version holds as well when the naive cotangent complex has tor amplitude in the interval from minus one to zero (statement lines 22809-22823). items.title: Noetherianity, surjectivity and finite residue extensions for the integral closure in a base field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement concerns an extension of discrete valuation rings with the larger ring essentially of finite type over the smaller one, and an algebraic extension of the fraction field whose integral closure in the base is required to be Noetherian; it concludes that the integral closure in the reduced base change is Noetherian, that the induced map of spectra is surjective and that the residue field extensions are finitely generated (statement lines 35925-35935). The proof presents the larger ring as a localization of a finite type algebra, base changes along the integral extension to obtain a one dimensional Noetherian ring integral over the original one, lists its finitely many minimal primes, and applies Krull-Akizuki to the finitely many resulting one dimensional domains to get Noetherianity, with the finiteness of the residue extensions coming from the one dimensional case (proof lines 35937-35958). The degreewise reduction argument is the technical heart of the uniqueness half. items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that a complex that is m-pseudo-coherent relative to the localization of a ring at an element stays so after localizing the algebra at a further element, now relative to the original ring (statement lines 21498-21505). The proof is a two-step transfer: it first expresses the localized base ring as a quotient of a polynomial ring so that relative pseudo-coherence can be moved to a polynomial algebra over the base, then localizes at a lift of the element using the pullback statement, and finally presents that second localization as one more quotient and transfers relative pseudo-coherence once more (proof lines 21507-21539). The two transfers and the two presentations are what make the change of base from the localization to the original ring work. The counted span refers twice to earlier results of this chapter, both carried as navigation stubs.

items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a pair satisfying the equivalent conditions of the preceding characterization of flatness on torsion, the natural map from every power torsion module to its base change is an isomorphism exactly when the quotient of the base by the ideal is isomorphic to the corresponding quotient of the target (statement lines 24263-24273). The induction with the outer terms is what makes the statement sharp. The counted statement depends on the preceding characterization, which is delivered as a context span so that its label resolves inside the package, and there is no further reference, so the card carries no navigation stub.

items.difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes exactness of the Cech sequence of the ring itself for a map inducing isomorphisms modulo all powers of a fixed element: exactness on the right always holds, left exactness is equivalent to injectivity of the comparison map on power torsion and middle exactness to its surjectivity, whence the pair is a glueing pair exactly when that comparison is bijective, with a specialization to the completion (statement lines 25254-25270). The companion statement for a general module and the faithfulness statement for the pair are the neighbouring results of the same section, and the completion case is obtained by specialization. items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that in the Koszul setup of the section, over a Noetherian ring, the inverse system of powers of the ideal is pro-isomorphic to the inverse system of Koszul complexes, as objects of the derived category (statement lines 29647-29652, formulated inside the situation of the section). The proof replaces the powers by the system generated by the powers of the chosen generators, forms the inverse system of distinguished triangles with the cone of the comparison, and reduces to pro-zero-ness of the cones: the cones are bounded because the Koszul complex sits between degrees minus r plus one and zero, their cohomology vanishes in nonnegative degrees and agrees with the Koszul cohomology below, and the pro-zero property of the latter was established earlier, which is where the Noetherian hypothesis is used (proof lines 29654-29673). The reduction to a statement about cones is what makes the argument short. The counted statement depends on the situation of the section, which is delivered as the context span, and refers three times to earlier results, which are carried as navigation stubs.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a smooth ring map R -> S stays smooth after localizing the source (S_g over R) and after inverting in the base (R_f -> S) (statement lines 37329-37335). The proof does not compute with presentations: it uses the naive cotangent complex, transports it along the localization through the cited localisation lemma, and observes that finite projectivity - which is what smoothness of R -> S supplies - is preserved by base change (proof lines 37338-37343); the second assertion is the same argument with the base-localisation lemma (proof lines 37345-37346). The step that carries the content is the transport of the complex, since it is what turns the assumption on S into the corresponding statement for S_g and R_f. Both cited inputs are same-chapter lemmas. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project — Topology
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file topology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the description of the topology of a cofiltered limit of spaces (author lemma at source lines 2590-2601, label lemma-describe-limits): every open of the limit is a union of projection-preimages of opens, and every quasi-compact open is a single projection-preimage. The proof (source lines 2603-2642) computes with the standard basis of the product topology: it observes that only finitely many factors of a basis element can be proper, writes the intersection with the limit as a finite intersection of projection-preimages, and then uses quasi-compactness to collapse the finite union in the second assertion (proof lines 2604-2641). The distinction between arbitrary and quasi-compact opens is the point of the lemma and is what the later results on limits of spectral spaces use. H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement collects the basic properties of irreducible components (author lemma at source lines 1102-1113, label lemma-irreducible): closures of irreducible subsets are irreducible, components are closed, every irreducible subset lies in an irreducible component, and the space is the union of its irreducible components. items.title: Alexander's subbase theorem: a finite-refinement test on a subbase implies quasi-compactness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project — Topology
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file topology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is Alexander's subbase theorem in the form the chapter uses (author lemma at source lines 2182-2187, label lemma-subbase-theorem, bearing the author's own bracketed name): a subbase whose coverings always have finite refinements forces the space to be quasi-compact. The proof (source lines 2189-2210) is the classical Zorn argument, complete in the author's own presentation: it chooses a maximal covering without a finite refinement (proof lines 2190-2196), shows that the members lying in the subbase already cover the space (proof lines 2196-2204), applies the hypothesis to obtain a finite refinement, and uses maximality a second time to turn that refinement into a finite subcovering of the original covering, giving the contradiction (proof lines 2204-2210). The theorem is the tool by which the chapter verifies quasi-compactness of spectral spaces and of limits. H2.

items.title: Construction of the canonical functorial map from the alternating Cech complex of a finite covering to derived global sections
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the canonical map from the total complex of the alternating Cech complex of a finite open covering into RGamma(X, F^bullet), functorially in the complex and compatible with the previously constructed map on global sections. The proof chooses a quasi-isomorphism from F^bullet into a K-injective complex with injective terms, uses that derived global sections are represented by the complex of global sections of any such K-injective representative, and obtains the map by composing the comparison of the alternating Cech complexes along the quasi-isomorphism with the map already built in the bounded setting (proof lines 10171-10199). The author explicitly omits only the verification of functoriality and of the compatibilities, which are routine checks (proof line 10200). H2: the K-injective reduction that makes the construction possible is the substance.

items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the commutativity of an explicit square relating the cup product H^0(K tensor E^vee) x H^0(E) -> H^0(K tensor E^vee tensor E), the evaluation contraction E^vee tensor E -> O_X, the identification of H^0(K tensor E^vee) with Hom_X(E, K) for perfect E, and the composition of morphisms. The proof identifies the objects with internal homs, shows that the cup product corresponds to the tensor product of the representing maps, and then checks that the morphism E -> K obtained from a section via the duality lemma is exactly the composition of the tensor product map with the evaluation (proof lines 13426-13405 region, i.e. lines 13346-13404). H2: the identification of the two constructions of the map E -> K is the substance, and it uses the explicitness of the evaluation map.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma extends the projection formula Rf_*E tensor K = Rf_*(E tensor Lf^*K) from a finite locally free twist to an arbitrary perfect module K. The proof reduces to the case where K is represented by a finite complex of finite free modules, using that a perfect module is locally of that form; a simple argument with stupid truncations then reduces to K represented by a single finite free module, and invariance of the statement under finite direct summands in the K variable reduces further to K = O_Y[n], where the statement is trivial (proof lines 12922-13938 region, i.e. lines 13922-13938). H2: the truncation and direct-summand reductions are short but each is a genuine step, and together they give the full statement from the finite locally free case.

items.title: Base change for the internal hom: pullback of R-Hom is R-Hom of the pullbacks in three cases
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the canonical comparison map Lh^* R-Hom(K, M) -> R-Hom(Lh^*K, Lh^*M) is an isomorphism in three separate situations: K perfect; h flat with K pseudo-coherent and M bounded below; and finite tor dimension of O_X over h^{-1}O_Y with K pseudo-coherent and M bounded below. The proof of the first case reduces locally to a strictly perfect representative of K and a K-flat representative of M, computes R-Hom(K, M) as the single complex of Homs between them, and compares the pullback with the internal hom of the pullbacks using the description of pullback of finite free modules (proof lines 13426-13480). The remaining cases require the flatness and tor dimension hypotheses to make the same computation valid. H3: the local computation and the three-way case analysis are independent research-level work, not a citation chain.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the canonical maps RGamma_Z(X, K) -> RGamma_Z(X, K_ab) and R-H_Z(K) -> R-H_Z(K_ab), where K_ab is the image of K in the derived category of abelian sheaves, are isomorphisms. The proof builds the first map from the functoriality of Gamma_Z on abelian sheaves and shows that it fits with the canonical maps of the abelian-comparison lemma into a morphism of distinguished triangles coming from the sections-with-support triangle; since two of the three arrows are known isomorphisms, the five lemma in the derived category gives the third (proof lines 8724-8757). The sheaf-level statement is then deduced in the same manner. H2: the triangle comparison and the conclusion by the five lemma are the substance.

items.title: Vanishing of the higher direct images along the inclusion of a quasi-compact open in a one-dimensional affine Noetherian case
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the vanishing of the higher direct images R^p j_* F for the inclusion j of a quasi-compact open U into a scheme whose local rings are Noetherian of dimension at most one, which is the key input for the affineness criterion for such opens. The proof reduces the vanishing to a stalk computation and uses flat base change to assume that X is the spectrum of a Noetherian local ring of dimension at most one (proof lines 7755-7763). In that case X has a closed point x and finitely many other points specializing to it and to no other point, so U is either all of X or the finite set of the remaining points, which is affine; the argument then concludes the vanishing (proof lines 7764-7794). H2: the flat-base-change reduction to the local case and the resulting explicit description of U are the substance.

items.title: An invertible sheaf on a proper curve is ample exactly when its degree is positive
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes ampleness of an invertible sheaf on a proper curve by positivity of its degree. For the forward direction the proof uses that an ample sheaf has a power with a section whose nonvanishing locus is affine, that the curve is not affine, hence the section vanishes somewhere, so the degree of that power is positive, and multiplicativity of the degree gives positivity of the degree of L (proof lines 10005-10013). The converse uses that dim_k H^0(X, L^{tensor n}) is at least chi(X, L^n) = n deg(L) + chi(X, O_X), which grows linearly, so for any finite collection of closed points one can find sections separating them; this yields the ampleness criterion (proof lines 10016 onwards to line 10067). H2: the two directions each combine a degree computation with a section-existence argument, and the growth estimate is the key step of the converse.

items.title: Bertini: the general member of a family of divisors cut by a generating system on a smooth projective immersion is smooth
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Bertini smoothness theorem in the form used by the Stacks Project: for a smooth X over k, a generating system of sections of an invertible sheaf L whose associated morphism to P(V) is an immersion, the general member H_v of the resulting family of divisors is smooth over k'. The proof sets up the universal divisor H_univ inside A^r_k times X, considers the singular locus Sigma of the projection q : H_univ -> A^r_k, argues that Sigma is closed because the smooth locus of a morphism is open, and reduces to proving that the image q(Sigma) is contained in a proper closed subset of A^r_k; since Sigma is of finite type over k it suffices to bound its dimension by r - 1 (proof lines 10966-10987 and the remainder of the proof to line 11057). H3: the dimension count for the singular locus of the universal family is a genuine research-level argument and is the heart of the theorem.

items.title: Faithful flat descent for a line bundle whose pullback is trivial: the sections form invertible modules and multiply isomorphically
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a faithfully flat ring map A -> B and a quasi-compact quasi-separated A-scheme X, a line bundle on X whose pullback to X_B is trivial has globally invertible modules of sections in both directions, and the multiplication map between them is an isomorphism. The proof lets M and R be the modules of sections of L and of O_X, computes H^0(X_B, L_B) as M tensor_A B by flat base change, identifies it with R tensor_A B because the pullback of L is trivial, and concludes that M is invertible over R by faithful flat descent for finite projective modules (proof lines 5757-5780). H2: the descent step and the tensor-product comparison are the substance, and both are written out.

items.title: The degree of a locally free module on a proper scheme of dimension at most one is the multiplicity-weighted sum of its degrees on the one-dimensional components
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma expresses the degree of a locally free module on a proper scheme of dimension at most one as the sum over the one-dimensional irreducible components of the multiplicity times the degree of the restriction. The proof isolates each component by taking the complement of the union of the others and the scheme theoretic closure X_i of that open piece, uses the birational-invariance lemma for the coproduct morphism, and so reduces to the irreducible case (proof lines 9726-9741). There it must show deg(E) = m deg(E|_C) for the reduced structure C of multiplicity m, which it does by induction on the nilpotency index e of the ideal of C, using the short exact sequence 0 -> I^e -> O_X -> O_{X'} -> 0 and an additivity computation of lengths at the generic point (proof lines 9744-9781). H3: the reduction to components together with the nilpotency induction and the length computation is independent research-level work.

items.title: Degree of an effective Cartier divisor on a proper scheme of dimension at most one and the degree shift by that divisor
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the degree of an effective Cartier divisor D on a proper scheme of dimension at most one as the dimension of its global sections, and shows that twisting a locally free module of rank n by O_X(D) shifts the degree by n deg(D). The proof uses the definition of an effective Cartier divisor to write the short exact sequence 0 -> O_X -> O_X(D) -> i_*i^*O_X(D) -> 0 for the closed immersion i : D -> X, tensors it by the locally free module E so that exactness is preserved, and then applies additivity of the Euler characteristic together with the finite-support lemma to obtain the degree formula (proof lines 9845-9869). H2: the exact-sequence computation together with the two cited inputs is the substance, and the argument is written out.

items.title: Enriques-Severi-Zariski: vanishing of H^1 of sufficiently negative twists of an ample invertible sheaf under depth at least two
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma, attributed by the author to Enriques-Severi-Zariski, proves that for a proper scheme X over a field, an ample invertible sheaf L and a coherent F whose stalks have depth at least two at all closed points, one has H^1(X, F tensor L^{tensor m}) = 0 for m sufficiently negative. The proof embeds X into projective space so that L becomes a power of the restriction of O(1), reduces to a coherent module G on projective space built from the e twists of F, checks that G again has depth at least two at closed points and infinite depth off the image, and then carries out the projective-space case (proof lines 11168-11290). H3: the reduction step that packages the e twists into a single sheaf with controlled depth, followed by the projective-space vanishing argument, is independent research-level work.
