items.title: A finite set of points whose traces on each irreducible component lie in an affine open lies in an affine open
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma assembles the per-component affine containment hypotheses into a single affine open containing the whole finite set T. The proof proceeds by induction on the number of irreducible components: given an affine open U meeting the first r-1 components in the desired way and an affine open V inside the r-th component containing T cap Z_r, one shows that Delta = (U cap Z_r) minus (U cap V) is closed in U and contains no point of T, and then uses prime avoidance to replace U by a standard open U' containing T cap U and disjoint from Delta, so that U cap V becomes closed in U; a symmetric argument handles the remaining components (proof lines 9094-9135). H2: the two prime-avoidance steps that make the intersections closed are the substance.

items.title: Existence of an element of the maximal ideal whose radical is the maximal ideal, matching an element of an integral extension inside the product of localizations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring A with product of minimal-prime localizations L and an integral ring map K -> L, there are a in the maximal ideal and x in K with the same image in L and with the maximal ideal equal to the radical of (a). The proof reduces A via the power-works lemma to the reduced case, replaces K by its image so that K is reduced and Spec(K) is a finite discrete space, hence K is a finite product of fields (proof lines 7639-7645). It then lists the minimal primes of A, sets A_j to be the normalization of A/p_j (a semi-local Dedekind domain), and proceeds to construct the required element by summing the numbers of maximal ideals and choosing a and x accordingly (proof lines 7648 onwards). H2: the reduction to a finite product of fields and the subsequent construction through the normalizations are the substance; the author marks two auxiliary steps as 'some details omitted', which concern only the reduction and the closedness of Spec(L) -> Spec(K).

items.title: The Euler characteristic of the twists of a coherent sheaf on projective space is a polynomial in the twist
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the function d mapping to chi(P^n, F(d)) is a polynomial for a coherent sheaf on projective n-space. The proof inducts on n using the hyperplane section sequence: after enlarging the base field so that a suitable section exists, it obtains the identity chi(P^n, F(d)) - chi(P^n, F(d-1)) = chi(H, G(d)) and notes that H is projective (n-1)-space, so by induction the right-hand side is a polynomial (proof lines 6779-6798). The conclusion then uses that a function whose first difference is a polynomial is itself a polynomial; the author states that arithmetic fact without proof and points to the corresponding algebra lemma (proof lines 6799-6803). H2: the induction through the hyperplane sequence is the substance, and the omitted arithmetic fact is routine and explicitly identified.

items.title: Nonempty closed subsets of projective space whose dimensions sum to at least n intersect, with a dimension bound for the intersection
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that nonempty closed subsets X and Y of projective n-space with dim(X) + dim(Y) at least n meet, and that every component of the intersection has dimension at least r + s - n. The proof pulls the situation back along the surjective smooth morphism from punctured affine (n+1)-space to projective space, which has irreducible fibres of dimension one, so that the preimages have dimensions r+1 and s+1 (proof lines 6374-6393). It then chooses irreducible components V and W of the preimages of those dimensions, observes that they contain every fibre they meet, and passes to their closures in affine (n+1)-space, which contain the origin because the origin lies in the closure of every fibre; the affine intersection bound then gives the result (proof lines 6394-6410). H2: the cone construction and the fibre-containment observation are the substance.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves surjectivity of the multiplication map H^0(F(m)) tensor H^0(O(1)) -> H^0(F(m+1)) for an m-regular coherent sheaf on projective n-space. H2: the field reduction and the two-stage lifting through the exact sequence are the substance.

items.title: Finite generation of the units modulo constants under any one of three additional hypotheses
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition proves finite generation of O(X)^*/k^* for a connected reduced locally finite type scheme with finitely many irreducible components, provided at least one of three conditions holds: the integral closure of k in the global sections is k, X has a k-rational point, or X is geometrically integral. The proof passes to a connected component Y of the reduced geometric base change, applies the algebraically closed case to Y, and uses it to produce, under the failure of finite generation, an element f of O(X) not in k whose image under O(X) -> O(Y) lies in the algebraic closure (proof lines 5363-5383). It then shows that conditions (2) and (3) each imply condition (1): a k-rational point gives a section of the inclusion k -> O(X), forcing the integral closure to be k, and geometric integrality gives the same conclusion through the integral closure being a field (proof lines 5384-5403). H3: the passage to the geometric base change and the comparison of the three hypotheses is independent work.

items.title: Any h sheaf turns an almost blowup square into a cartesian diagram of sets
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a sheaf F on one of the big h sites and any almost blowup square in that category, the lemma asserts that the resulting square with entries F(E), F(X'), F(Z) and F(X) is cartesian in the category of sets (statement lines 11215-11228). The proof does not test the sheaf condition directly but substitutes a covering: since Z coproduct X' -> X is a surjective proper morphism of finite presentation, the singleton family is an h covering, and the sheaf condition for it computes F(X) as the equalizer of the two maps to F(Z coprod X') (proof lines 11231-11233). The author then expands the fibre product (Z coprod X') x_X (Z coprod X') = Z coprod E coprod E coprod (X' x_X X'), uses that a Zariski sheaf sends disjoint unions to products, and rewrites the sheaf condition concretely as: pairs (t, s') with t|_E = s'|_E and s' in the equalizer of the two maps F(X') -> F(X' x_X X') (proof lines 11234-11246). The remaining step removes condition (b) by observing that E x_Z E coprod X' -> X' x_X X' is again a surjective proper morphism of finite presentation, because b is an isomorphism away from E, so F(X' x_X X') -> F(E x_Z E) x F(X') is injective and (a) implies (b) (proof lines 11247-11255). Choosing the covering Z coproduct X' and then eliminating the second sheaf condition is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The exterior product over a base of dimension one is well defined on Chow groups in degree shifted by one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is that the exterior product map CH_n(X) tensor_Z CH_m(Y) -> CH_{n+m-1}(X x_S Y) over a base of dimension one is well defined (statement lines 14657-14661). The proof first defines the product on cycles: among the pairs (i, j) one keeps only those where X_i or Y_j dominates an irreducible component of S, and shows that these form a locally finite family of closed subschemes of delta-dimension n + m - 1, so that the sum of n_i m_j [X_i x_S Y_j] makes sense (proof lines 14664-14681). Compatibility with rational equivalence is then obtained by splitting the case distinction between components that do and do not dominate S: for an integral X' of dimension n dominating an irreducible component of S, the projection X' -> S is flat of relative dimension n - 1 by the Dedekind domain input, so the composite of the flat pullback with the proper pushforward is a bivariant class whose cap product sends [Y'] to [X' x_S Y']_{n+m-1} (proof lines 14684-14698). For the complementary case, where X' -> X -> S factors through a closed point s of S, the point s is an effective Cartier divisor with trivial normal bundle, so composing the Gysin class of s in S with the flat pullback along the now flat X' -> s of relative dimension n gives a bivariant class whose cap product sends [Y'] to the correct cycle precisely when Y' dominates a component of S and to zero otherwise, matching the definition on cycles (proof lines 14701-14722). Splitting the cycle definition along the two kinds of components and building the matching bivariant class in each case is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Comparison of the determinants of two exact two-periodic complexes joined by a morphism vanishing on kernel and cokernel
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of exact (2, 1)-periodic complexes of finite length modules over a local ring whose maps induce zero on both the kernel K and the cokernel Q, the lemma asserts that det_kappa(M, phi, psi) equals det_kappa(alpha_0^{-1} o alpha_1) times det_kappa(M', phi', psi'), where the two isomorphisms Q -> K come from the boundary maps of the two short exact sequences of complexes displayed in the statement (statement lines 17107-17139). The proof is a long and explicit computation rather than a formal manipulation: the author first identifies the two boundary maps concretely as composites through the intermediate quotients I_{phi'}/alpha(I_phi) and I_{psi'}/alpha(I_psi) (proof lines 17149-17210), then does a length bookkeeping with k = length(K), a = length(I_phi) and b = length(I_psi) showing length(M) = length(M') = a + b while length(N) = a + b - k and length(Q) = k (proof lines 17163-17173), and finally chooses admissible sequences generating K, I_phi and I_psi together with preimages under phi and psi, compares the two determinants through the characterisation by admissible sequences, and tracks the scalar obtained (proof lines 17212 onward). The author explicitly notes that an alternative enormous commutative diagram exists and chooses the admissible-sequence route instead, which is why the argument is a delicate bookkeeping computation. Coordinating the boundary maps with the admissible sequences and their preimages is not a routine exercise, so the claim is H3.

items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme S and a big h site as in the definition, the lemma identifies the rule X -> Gamma(X^{awn}, O_{X^{awn}}) as the sheafification of the structure sheaf, and asserts the same for the ph topology (statement lines 12076-12086). The proof already knows from the preceding ph-sheaf lemma that this rule is a ph sheaf, hence a fortiori an h sheaf, and that there is a canonical map O -> F of presheaves of rings (proof lines 12089-12093). It then reduces the sheafification statement to the two standard conditions: that an element mapping to zero is killed by an h covering, and that an element of F(X) is locally in the image of an element of O (proof lines 12094-12100). The first is dispatched by noting that f vanishing on X^{awn} means f is locally nilpotent, so the closed subscheme cut out by f is a surjective closed immersion of finite presentation, which is exactly an h covering; the second by passing to affine X = Spec(A), using that an element of F(X) lies in the absolutely weakly normal quotient A^{awn}, and spreading it out to a finitely presented universal homeomorphism A -> B by the universal-homeomorphism limit lemma, whose singleton family is an h covering (proof lines 12101-12115). Converting the sheafification statement into the two local-surgery conditions and sourcing each from a different input is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A finite locally free morphism of degree d carries a canonical norm of degree d compatible with base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a canonical norm map of degree d for a finite locally free morphism and asserts its compatibility with base change (statement lines 3788-3793). The counted proof is a complete construction: over an affine chart it trivializes the pushforward, represents multiplication by a section by a matrix, defines the norm as its determinant, checks independence of the trivialization so that the local definitions glue, and then verifies the degree and vanishing properties, the latter after base change to the spectrum of a field where a vanishing section gives a non-surjective endomorphism of a finite dimensional algebra (proof lines 3795-3823). It is H2: the construction and both verifications are carried out in the counted span, with the inputs being standard linear algebra over rings.

items.title: The denominators of a regular meromorphic section form a quasi-coherent ideal whose quotients of the structure sheaf and the line bundle are nowhere dense
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma defines the ideal of denominators of a regular meromorphic section and asserts that it is a quasi-coherent ideal whose two natural inclusions into the structure sheaf and into the line bundle have cokernels supported on nowhere dense closed subsets (statement lines 6172-6194). The counted proof reduces the statement to an affine chart with trivial bundle and a section equal to a quotient of two nonzerodivisors, proves quasi-coherence by an explicit localization computation, and then shows that the principal ideal generated by the denominator lies in the ideal of denominators, which bounds both supports by the vanishing locus of a nonzerodivisor and hence makes them nowhere dense (proof lines 6196-6217). It is H2: the reduction and both arguments are carried out in the counted span, with no independent research-level content.

It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the standard relative associated prime comparison and the affine description of associated points.

The reduction to the preimage and the pushforward comparison are the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the cycle of the zero scheme of a global section with the sum over the components of Y of the multiplicities times the cycles of the restricted sections, under the hypothesis that the section is injective at every generic point of the k-dimensional part of its zero scheme (statement lines 4357-4379, tag 0EPI). The proof is a local computation: it chooses a generator at the generic point of an integral Z so that the section becomes an element f of the local ring A, splits off the zero-dimensional case where injectivity forces f to be a unit, and in the one-dimensional case matches the length of A/(f) with the sum over the minimal primes of the local length times the length of A/(f, q_i). That matching is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Characterisations of absolutely flat rings by weak dimension, reducedness with all primes maximal, and field local rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of four conditions on a ring A: that A have weak dimension at most 0; that A be absolutely flat; that A be reduced with every prime maximal; and that every local ring of A be a field (source lines 30249-30258). The equivalence of (1) and (2) is immediate. The substantive part is (1) implies (3): assuming A absolutely flat, every ideal of A is pure, so every finitely generated ideal is generated by an idempotent by the finitely-generated-pure-ideal lemma; for f in A one then has (f) = (e) for an idempotent e, so D(f) = D(e) is open and closed, which makes every prime ideal maximal by the criterion on rings with only minimal primes, and if f is nilpotent then e = 0 and hence f = 0, so A is reduced (proof lines 30264-30275). The implication (3) implies (4) is immediate from the description of local rings of a reduced ring whose primes are all maximal, and (4) implies (2) because if every local ring is a field then every module is flat (proof lines 30278-30285). The non-routine content is the passage from purity of ideals to idempotent generation and the resulting open-and-closed structure of the spectrum.

items.title: Finite projectivity over a glueing pair is detected by the two pieces of the pair
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a glueing pair (R -> R', f) and an R-module M not assumed glueable, and asserts that M is a finite projective R-module exactly when M tensor_R R' is finite projective over R' and M_f is finite projective over R_f (source lines 25777-25784). The proof establishes the non-trivial direction by assembling earlier results. Assuming the two pieces are finite projective, the proof notes it will use the finite-projective criterion without further mention, and applies the flatness criterion of the glueing pair to conclude that M is flat (proof lines 25786-25792). It then uses the faithful descent lemma for the pair to conclude that M is finite (proof lines 25793). The substantive step is the finiteness of a kernel: choosing a short exact sequence 0 -> K -> R^{oplus n} -> M -> 0, and using that a finite projective module is finitely presented while the sequence remains exact after tensoring with R' (by the Tor-vanishing property for flat maps) and with R_f, the proof concludes that K tensor_R R' and K_f are finite modules, whence K is finitely generated by the previous statement of this series (proof lines 25794-25800). Therefore M is finitely presented and hence finite projective (proof lines 25800-25801). The non-routine content is the reduction of finite projectivity of M to finite generation of a kernel, using the two-piece hypotheses.

items.title: The quotient by the power-torsion submodule has no I-torsion, and power-torsion modules are closed under extensions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and a finitely generated ideal I of R and asserts two things: that for any R-module M the quotient M/M[I^infinity] has no I-torsion, i.e. (M/M[I^infinity])[I] = 0; and that an extension of I-power torsion modules is again I-power torsion (source lines 24041-24048). The proof of the first statement is an explicit exponent computation. Given m in M whose image lies in (M/M[I^infinity])[I], one has I m contained in M[I^infinity]; writing I = (f_1, ..., f_t), this gives f_i m in M[I^infinity], so that I^{n_i} f_i m = 0 for some n_i > 0, and taking N = sum_i n_i + 2 yields I^N m = 0 (proof lines 24051-24055). Hence m maps to zero in M/M[I^infinity], which is the first statement (proof lines 24056-24057). The second statement is settled by a quotient argument: for a short exact sequence 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 with M' and M'' both I-power torsion, one has M[I^infinity] containing M', so M/M[I^infinity] is a quotient of M'' and is therefore I-power torsion; combined with the first statement and the torsion-free criterion this forces it to be zero, so M is I-power torsion (proof lines 24060-24065). The non-routine content is the exponent bookkeeping in the first statement and the two-sided use of the first statement in the second.

items.title: Power-torsion Ext groups are essentially constant along the quotients by powers of the ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian ring A, an ideal I, a pseudo-coherent object K of D(A), and an integer a, and assumes that for every finite A-module M the modules Ext^i_A(K, M) are I-power torsion for i >= a; it concludes that for i >= a and M finite the system Ext^i_A(K, M/I^nM) is essentially constant with value Ext^i_A(K, M) = lim Ext^i_A(K, M/I^nM) (source lines 29781-29793). The proof begins with finite generation: since K is pseudo-coherent, each Ext^i_A(K, M) is a finite A-module, so for i >= a it is annihilated by I^t for some t >= 0 (proof lines 29796-29798). The substantive step is a vanishing of images: the induced-topology lemma shows that the image of Ext^i_A(K, I^nM) -> Ext^i_A(K, M) is zero for some n > 0 (proof lines 29799-29801). The proof then applies the long exact sequence of Ext to the short exact sequence 0 -> I^nM -> M -> M/I^nM -> 0, obtaining the displayed four-term exact sequence Ext^i_A(K, I^nM) -> Ext^i_A(K, M) -> Ext^i_A(K, M/I^nM) -> Ext^{i+1}_A(K, I^nM) (proof lines 29802-29807). Since the systems Ext^i_A(K, I^nM) and Ext^{i+1}_A(K, I^nM) are essentially constant with value 0 by the preceding vanishing applied to the finite modules I^m M, a diagram chase completes the proof (proof lines 29808-29812). The non-routine content is the systematic use of the long exact sequence with a two-sided vanishing to force the middle system to be essentially constant.

items.title: Boundedness above of the cohomology of the cone of multiplication by f forces boundedness above of the source
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an element f, an object M of D(R), and the cone C of the multiplication map f : M -> M; assuming that H^i(M)_f = 0 for i < 0 and that H^i(C) = 0 for i < -1, it concludes that H^i(M) = 0 for i < 0 (source lines 30011-30017). The proof is a triangle argument. It denotes M_f = M tensor^L_R R_f and chooses a distinguished triangle F -> M -> M_f; by hypothesis H^i(M_f) = H^i(M)_f = 0 for i < 0, so it suffices to show that H^i(F) = 0 for i < 0 (proof lines 30020-30022). The proof then records the structural fact that H^i(F) is f-power torsion for every i (proof lines 30023). The substantive observation is that, since f : M_f -> M_f is an isomorphism, C is isomorphic to the cone of f : F -> F, which the proof draws from the octahedral-type statement (proof lines 30024-30026). The conclusion is then a contrapositive: if H^i(F) were nonzero, the kernel of f on H^i(F) would be nonzero, which forces H^{i-1}(C) to be nonzero; the hypothesis H^i(C) = 0 for i < -1 therefore rules out the cases i - 1 < -1, finishing the proof (proof lines 30027-30029). The non-routine content is the identification of C with the self-cone of F, which converts the hypothesis on C into information about the kernel of multiplication by f.

items.title: For a finite map of finite type algebras relative pseudo-coherence is detected after restriction of scalars
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a finite map A -> B of finite type R-algebras, an integer m, and a complex K^bullet of B-modules, and asserts that K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent (respectively pseudo-coherent) relative to R if and only if K^bullet viewed as a complex of A-modules is so (source lines 21359-21366). The proof reduces the comparison to a single polynomial presentation. It chooses a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and elements y_1, ..., y_m generating B over A; since A -> B is finite each y_i satisfies a monic equation over A, so one finds monic polynomials P_j(T) in R[x_1, ..., x_n][T] with P_j(y_j) = 0 in B (proof lines 21369-21373). These data assemble into the displayed commutative diagram whose corners are the polynomial rings in the x's and in the x's and y's, the quotient by the P_j(y_j), and the algebras A and B (proof lines 21374-21382). The substantive observation is that the top horizontal arrow and the top right vertical arrow of that diagram satisfy the hypotheses of the finite-pushforward lemma for pseudo-coherent complexes, so that K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent (respectively pseudo-coherent) as a complex of R[x_1, ..., x_n]-modules exactly when it is so as a complex of R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m]-modules (proof lines 21383-21389). The two outer comparisons then give the stated equivalence. The non-routine content is the construction of the monic polynomials realising the finite algebra map as a quotient of a polynomial extension.

items.title: A module with a complete devissage that is flat at the point is finitely presented, free over the base and a direct sum of smooth pieces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma draws concrete consequences from the existence of a complete devissage: for a module flat at a prime over the maximal ideal of a local base, it concludes that the module is finitely presented, free over the base, and a direct sum of powers of smooth algebras (statement lines 2425-2440, tag 05I4). The proof runs an induction on the length of the devissage: it first replaces the pair by the first step using the identification of localisations, then applies the induction step to see that the first map is universally injective with flat cokernel so that the induction hypothesis applies to the tail, and finally assembles finite presentation from the extension lemma and freeness from projectivity over the local base. The induction and the assembly are the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Every object of the derived category of an inverse system of rings is represented by a system of complexes with surjective transition maps
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for an inverse system of rings (A_n), every object K of the derived category of the module-valued inverse systems can be represented by a system of complexes (M_n^bullet) all of whose transition maps M_{n+1}^bullet -> M_n^bullet are surjective (source lines 23779-23786). The proof is an induction replacing the transition maps one at a time. If K is represented by the system (K_n^bullet), the proof sets M_1^bullet = K_1^bullet and assumes surjective maps M_n^bullet -> ... -> M_1^bullet together with homotopy equivalences psi_e : K_e^bullet -> M_e^bullet making the displayed squares commute for all e < n (proof lines 23789-23799). The inductive step is the substantive part: considering the displayed diagram K_{n+1}^bullet -> K_n^bullet and K_n^bullet -> M_n^bullet, the proof invokes the make-a-map-surjective lemma to factor the composite K_{n+1}^bullet -> M_n^bullet as K_{n+1}^bullet -> M_{n+1}^bullet -> M_n^bullet with the first arrow a homotopy equivalence and the second a termwise split surjection (proof lines 23800-23811). The lemma then follows by induction (proof lines 23811-23812). The non-routine content is the choice of the factoring lemma, which supplies simultaneously the homotopy equivalence needed for compatibility and the surjectivity needed for the conclusion.

items.title: The Hom complex from a bounded above projective complex representing a perfect object to a K-flat complex is again K-flat
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a bounded above complex P^bullet of projective R-modules, and a K-flat complex K^bullet of R-modules, and asserts that if P^bullet represents a perfect object of D(R) then Hom^bullet(P^bullet, K^bullet) is K-flat and represents R Hom_R(P^bullet, K^bullet) (source lines 28710-28717). The second assertion is immediate from the Hom-out-of-projective statement (proof line 28720). The substantive part is the K-flatness. Since P^bullet represents a perfect object, the proof chooses a finite complex F^bullet of finite projective R-modules isomorphic to it in D(R) (proof lines 28721-28724). Because both are complexes of projectives, they are in fact homotopy equivalent, by the description of maps from a projective complex, so Hom^bullet(P^bullet, K^bullet) and Hom^bullet(F^bullet, K^bullet) are homotopy equivalent, and hence the first is K-flat exactly when the second is, using the definition of K-flatness and the homotopy-invariance of derived tensor product (proof lines 28725-28733). The proof then computes Hom^bullet(F^bullet, K^bullet) as the total complex Tot(E^bullet tensor_R K^bullet), where E^bullet is the dual complex of F^bullet with terms E^n = Hom_R(F^{-n}, R), using the dual-perfect-complex lemma and its proof (proof lines 28734-28742). Finally, since E^bullet is a bounded complex of projectives it is K-flat, and the tensor product of K-flat complexes is K-flat, which gives the conclusion (proof lines 28743-28745). The non-routine content is the replacement of P^bullet by the finite complex F^bullet together with the identification of the Hom complex with a tensor product of the dual complex.

items.title: The set of elements for which the obstruction to derived completeness vanishes is a radical ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A and an object K of D(A) and asserts that the set I of elements f in A with T(K, f) = 0 is a radical ideal of A (source lines 25935-25939). The proof uses the characterisation of the condition T(K, f) = 0 in terms of the vanishing of Ext^n_A(A_f, K) for all n, which is the content of the preceding lemma and is invoked without further mention (proof lines 25942-25943). The three ideal axioms are then checked. Closure under multiplication is immediate: if f lies in I and g is arbitrary, then A_{gf} is an A_f-module, so Ext^n_A(A_{gf}, K) = 0 for all n and hence gf lies in I (proof lines 25944-25945). Additivity is the substantive step: for f and g in I the proof exhibits the short exact sequence 0 -> A_{f+g} -> A_{f(f+g)} oplus A_{g(f+g)} -> A_{gf(f+g)} -> 0, which holds because f and g generate the unit ideal in A_{f+g}, using the standard covering lemma and the surjectivity of the last arrow (proof lines 25946-25952). Applying the long exact sequence of Ext and the vanishing of the three Ext groups appearing in the outer positions for all n then gives the vanishing of Ext^n_A(A_{f+g}, K) for all n, so f + g lies in I (proof lines 25952-25957). Finally the radical property is immediate because T(K, f) = T(K, f^n), or equivalently because A_f is isomorphic to A_{f^n}, so f^n in I implies f in I (proof lines 25958-25959). The non-routine content is the standard covering short exact sequence that makes additivity work.

items.title: Composition of internal Hom admits a canonical functorial morphism in the derived category
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and objects K, L, M of D(R) and asserts the existence of a canonical morphism R Hom_R(L, M) tensor^L_R R Hom_R(K, L) -> R Hom_R(K, M) in D(R), functorial in all three variables (source lines 18758-18765). The proof constructs the map at the level of complexes. It chooses a K-injective complex I^bullet representing M, a K-injective complex J^bullet representing L, and an arbitrary complex K^bullet representing K (proof lines 18768-18770). The composition statement for complexes then supplies a map of complexes from Tot(Hom^bullet(J^bullet, I^bullet) tensor_R Hom^bullet(K^bullet, J^bullet)) to Hom^bullet(K^bullet, I^bullet) (proof lines 18771-18778). The proof records that these three Hom complexes represent R Hom_R(L, M), R Hom_R(K, L) and R Hom_R(K, M) respectively (proof lines 18779-18781). The substantive step adapts the source to the derived tensor product: choosing a K-flat complex H^bullet with a quasi-isomorphism H^bullet -> Hom^bullet(K^bullet, J^bullet), the proof obtains the displayed map from Tot(Hom^bullet(J^bullet, I^bullet) tensor_R H^bullet) to the previous total complex, whose source represents R Hom_R(L, M) tensor^L_R R Hom_R(K, L) (proof lines 18782-18793). Composing the two displayed arrows gives the desired morphism, and the author states that the proof of functoriality is omitted (proof lines 18794-18795). The non-routine content is the insertion of the K-flat replacement so that the source actually computes the derived tensor product.

items.title: Left duals in the monoidal category of complexes are degreewise left duals with a sign-twisted differential
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma analyses a left dual (N^bullet, eta, epsilon) of a complex M^bullet in the monoidal category of complexes of R-modules, asserting four things: that M^bullet and N^bullet are bounded; that their terms are finite projective; that writing epsilon and eta as finite sums of degreewise components, each (N^{-n}, eta_n, epsilon_n) is the left dual of M^n in the sense of the one-module statement; and that the differential d_N^n equals -(-1)^n times the map induced by d_M^{-n-1} under the identification of N^n with Hom_R(M^{-n}, R). It also gives the converse construction (source lines 18461-18491). The proof unwinds the two triangle identities of a dual pair: from (1 tensor epsilon) o (eta tensor 1) = id and (epsilon tensor 1) o (1 tensor eta) = id it immediately extracts the degreewise identities (1 tensor epsilon_n) o (eta_n tensor 1) = id_{M^n} and (epsilon_n tensor 1) o (1 tensor eta_n) = id_{N^{-n}}, which proves part (3) (proof lines 18494-18500). Part (2) then follows from the one-module statement, and part (1) from the finiteness of the sum eta = sum eta_n (proof lines 18500-18501). The substantive part is (4): since eta is a map of complexes R -> Tot(M^bullet tensor_R N^bullet), the proof writes down the identity (d_M^{-n-1} tensor 1) o eta_{-n-1} + (-1)^n (1 tensor d_N^{-n}) o eta_{-n} = 0, which is exactly the sign rule for the total complex differential, and unwinding the definitions gives the claimed formula for d_N^n (proof lines 18502-18509). The converse is then obtained by reading the same computation backwards (proof lines 18510-18511). The non-routine content is the sign bookkeeping in the total complex that produces the twisted differential on the dual.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension d, a system of parameters g_1, ..., g_d with I = (g_1, ..., g_d), and asserts that if e_I/d! is the leading coefficient of the numerical polynomial n -> length_R(R/I^{n+1}), then e_I <= length_R(R/I) (source lines 38260-38267). The proof first records the two structural inputs: the function is a numerical polynomial by the Hilbert-function proposition, and it has degree d by the dimension proposition (proof lines 38270-38273). It disposes of d = 0 as trivial and reduces d = 1 to the earlier one-dimensional statement (proof lines 38274-38275). The general case is the substantive computation. The proof exhibits the surjection from the direct sum of copies of R/I indexed by the tuples i_1, ..., i_d >= 0 with sum n, onto I^n/I^{n+1}, sending the basis element to the class of the monomial g_1^{i_1} ... g_d^{i_d} (proof lines 38276-38283). This yields the inequality length_R(R/I^{n+1}) - length_R(R/I^n) <= length_R(R/I) binom(n + d - 1, d - 1) (proof lines 38284-38288). The proof then compares leading coefficients: for d >= 2 the numerical polynomial on the left has degree d - 1 with leading coefficient e_I/(d-1)!, and the polynomial on the right has degree d - 1 with leading coefficient length_R(R/I)/(d-1)!, which gives the bound (proof lines 38289-38293). The non-routine content is the surjection onto the graded pieces of I^n with its binomial index count, and the leading-coefficient comparison.

items.title: Nagata passes down along a separable extension of discrete valuation rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings and asserts that if B is Nagata and the extension L/K of fraction fields is separable, then A is Nagata (source lines 35666-35671). The proof first recalls the criterion that a discrete valuation ring is Nagata exactly when it is N-2, so it suffices to show that for a finite purely inseparable extension K_1/K the integral closure A_1 of A in K_1 is finite over A (proof lines 35674-35677). The substantive step is the field-theoretic observation: since L/K is separable and K_1/K is purely inseparable, the algebra L tensor_K K_1 is a field, by the reducedness and radicial-integrality lemmas (proof lines 35678-35681). Letting B_1 be the integral closure of B in that field, Nagata-ness of B makes B_1 finite over B; since B tensor_A A_1 is contained in B_1 and B is Noetherian, that subring is finite over B (proof lines 35682-35685). The final step is descent: because A -> B is faithfully flat, finiteness of B tensor_A A_1 over B implies finiteness of A_1 over A, by the descent lemma for properties of modules (proof lines 35685-35687). The non-routine content is the field-theoretic identification of the base change as a field, which is what allows Nagata-ness of B to be tested there, together with the faithful flat descent at the end.

items.title: Weakly etale algebras over a normal domain are integrally closed in the base change to the fraction field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a normal domain A with fraction field K and a weakly etale ring map A -> B, and asserts that B is integrally closed in B tensor_A K (source lines 30727-30732). The proof reduces the statement to a computable situation by choosing a diagram as in the product-of-valuation-rings lemma and base changing it along A -> B. Since A -> B is flat, the base change of that cartesian diagram gives the displayed cartesian square with corners B, B tensor_A K, B tensor_A V and B tensor_A L (proof lines 30734-30742). The substantive observations are three: that V -> B tensor_A V is weakly etale by base change of weakly etale maps, so that B tensor_A V has weak dimension at most 1 by the weak-dimension-goes-up lemma; that B tensor_A V -> B tensor_A L is a flat, injective epimorphism of rings because it is a flat base change of such; and therefore, by the weak-dimension-one integrated-closedness lemma, that B tensor_A V is integrally closed in B tensor_A L (proof lines 30743-30751). The final step transfers integrated closedness back along the cartesian square: the cartesian property of the diagram shows that B is integrally closed in B tensor_A K (proof lines 30752-30753). The non-routine content is the choice of the valuation-ring presentation of the fraction field and the transfer of integral closedness across the cartesian square.

items.title: For a flat map of Noetherian rings the completed Ext agree with the Ext of the reduced modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat homomorphism A -> B of Noetherian rings, an ideal I of A, A-modules M and N, and sets B_n = B/I^nB, M_n = M/I^nM, N_n = N/I^nN; assuming M is flat over A it asserts the displayed equality of inverse limits relating the completed Ext^i_B(M, N) to Ext^i_{B_n}(M_n, N_n) for all i (source lines 29370-29385). The proof is an explicit comparison of two complexes computing the two families. It chooses a resolution ... -> P_2 -> P_1 -> P_0 -> M -> 0 by finite free B-modules P_i and sets P_{i,n} = P_i/I^nP_i; flatness of M and B over A makes the reduced sequence ... -> P_{2,n} -> P_{1,n} -> P_{0,n} -> M_n -> 0 exact (proof lines 29388-29396). The proof then observes that the complex Hom_B(P_0, N) -> Hom_B(P_1, N) -> ... computes Ext^i_B(M, N), while the complex Hom_{B_n}(P_{0,n}, N_n) -> Hom_{B_n}(P_{1,n}, N_n) -> ... computes Ext^i_{B_n}(M_n, N_n) (proof lines 29397-29406). The substantive step is the termwise identification Hom_{B_n}(P_{i,n}, N_n) = Hom_B(P_i, N)/I^n Hom_B(P_i, N) (proof lines 29406-29409). Applying the second part of the Artin-Rees consequence to the two complexes gives the asserted equality of limits (proof lines 29410-29411). The non-routine content is the exactness of the reduced resolution, which is what makes the second complex compute the reduced Ext, together with the termwise identification feeding into Artin-Rees.

items.title: A finite group acts transitively on the primes of an integral extension lying over a fixed prime of the invariant subring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite group G acting on a ring R and asserts that any two primes q and q' of R lying over the same prime of the invariant subring R^G are conjugate under the action of G (source lines 32679-32684). The proof first observes that the extension R^G in R is integral, because every x in R is a root of the monic polynomial prod_{sigma in G} (T - sigma(x)) with coefficients in R^G[T]; consequently there are no inclusion relations among the primes lying over a given prime p, by the no-inclusion criterion for integral extensions (proof lines 32687-32691). The argument is then by contradiction and is the substantive part: if the lemma fails one can choose x in q' with x not in sigma(q) for every sigma in G, by the prime avoidance lemma; then y = prod_{sigma in G} sigma(x) lies in R^G and in p = R^G cap q', while the condition x not in sigma(q) for all sigma means sigma(x) not in q for all sigma, so y is not in q because q is prime — contradicting y in p contained in q (proof lines 32692-32700). The non-routine content is the construction of the invariant element y and the use of primality to place it on both sides of the contradiction.

items.title: The Picard group of the generic fibre vanishes for a flat essentially finite type local algebra over a valuation ring with regular special fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a valuation ring R with fraction field K and residue field kappa, and a ring homomorphism R -> A such that A is local and R -> A is local, A is flat and essentially of finite type over R, and A tensor_R kappa is regular; it concludes that Pic(A tensor_R K) = 0 (source lines 36845-36856). The proof is a long descent. Starting with an invertible A tensor_R K-module L, it uses that L is finite and the construct-finite-module lemma to find a finite A-module M with M tensor_R K isomorphic to L, which may be taken torsion free as an R-module and hence flat over R by the valuation-ring criterion (proof lines 36859-36865). From the flat finite type statement over a valuation ring the proof deduces that M is finitely presented as an A-module and that A is essentially of finite presentation as an R-algebra (proof lines 36866-36868). The structure of relatively perfect modules then shows M is perfect relative to R, in particular pseudo-coherent as an A-module, and the perfect-over-a-regular-local-ring statement upgrades this to M being perfect, so that M has a finite free resolution F_bullet over A (proof lines 36869-36874). It follows that L is quasi-isomorphic to a finite complex of free A tensor_R K-modules, so the Euler characteristic map gives [L] = n[A tensor_R K] in K_0(A tensor_R K) for some integer n (proof lines 36875-36879). Applying the determinant map then shows L is trivial, which is the conclusion (proof lines 36880-36881). The non-routine content is the chain of upgrades from a finite torsion free module to a perfect module with a finite free resolution, and the final use of the determinant on K_0.

items.title: Relative finite presentation of a module is independent of the presentation and passes to finitely presented quotients of the algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite type ring map R -> A and an A-module M, and establishes the equivalence of three conditions: that for some presentation alpha : R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A the module M be finitely presented over R[x_1, ..., x_n]; that the same hold for all presentations; and that for any surjection A' -> A with A' a finitely presented R-algebra, M be finitely presented as an A'-module; it adds that in this case M is a finitely presented A-module (source lines 20922-20936). The proof of the first equivalence is a comparison of presentations: given alpha and beta, the proof chooses f_j and g_i realising the two compositions and assembles the displayed commutative diagram, after which the equivalence of (1) and (2) follows from the finitely-presented-over-a-subring and finite-finitely-presented-extension lemmas (proof lines 20938-20954). The third condition is then related to the second in the substantive step: choosing a presentation A' = R[x_1, ..., x_n]/(f_1, ..., f_m), the proof uses the finite-finitely-presented-extension lemma again to show that M is finitely presented as an A'-module exactly when it is finitely presented as an R[x_1, ..., x_n]-module (proof lines 20955-20959), which gives the equivalence of (2) and (3). The non-routine content is the uniform use of the finite-extension criterion to relate the module-theoretic conditions across the two presentations and across the surjection A' -> A.

items.title: Relative pseudo-coherence is independent of the chosen polynomial presentation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite type ring map R -> A, a complex K^bullet of A-modules, and an integer m, and establishes the equivalence of two conditions: that for some presentation alpha : R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A the complex K^bullet be an m-pseudo-coherent complex of R[x_1, ..., x_n]-modules, and that the same hold for all presentations; it adds that the same equivalence holds for pseudo-coherence (source lines 21290-21305). The proof is a comparison-of-presentations argument. Given two presentations alpha and beta, the proof chooses f_j in R[x_1, ..., x_n] with alpha(f_j) = beta(y_j) and g_i in R[y_1, ..., y_m] with beta(g_i) = alpha(x_i), and assembles the displayed commutative diagram whose corners are the polynomial ring in both sets of variables, the two polynomial rings, and A (proof lines 21307-21320). The substantive step is the normalisation: after a change of coordinates, the ring homomorphism R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m] -> R[x_1, ..., x_n] becomes isomorphic to the one mapping each y_i to zero, and similarly for the left vertical map of the diagram; hence by induction on the number of variables the lemma follows from the add-a-variable statement for pseudo-coherence (proof lines 21321-21326). The pseudo-coherent case is then obtained from this together with the passage between m-pseudo-coherence and pseudo-coherence (proof lines 21327-21328). The non-routine content is the coordinate change that normalises an arbitrary comparison map to one killing the extra variables.

items.title: The derived limit of an inverse system of perfect complexes along surjections with locally nilpotent kernels is perfect
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes A = lim A_n a limit of an inverse system of rings, objects K_n of D(A_n) with compatible maps K_{n+1} -> K_n, and assumes that the transition maps A_{n+1} -> A_n are surjective with locally nilpotent kernels; that either all K_n are perfect or there is n_0 beyond which K_{n_0} is perfect and the kernels are nilpotent; and that the maps induce isomorphisms K_{n+1} tensor^L_{A_{n+1}} A_n -> K_n; it concludes that K = R lim K_n is perfect in D(A) with K tensor^L_A A_n -> K_n an isomorphism for all n (source lines 28400-28419). The proof begins from the pseudo-coherent statement, which already gives that K is pseudo-coherent and that the base change maps are isomorphisms (proof lines 28422-28424). The substantive part is the reduction to a residue field computation. For a surjection A -> kappa with kernel a maximal ideal m, the proof uses that any element mapping to a unit in A_1 is a unit in A to conclude that Ker(A -> A_1) lies in the Jacobson radical of A, so that A -> kappa factors through A -> A_1 (proof lines 28425-28431). Hence the displayed chain gives K tensor^L_A kappa = K tensor^L_A A_1 tensor^L_{A_1} kappa = K_1 tensor^L_{A_1} kappa (proof lines 28432-28437). Since K_1 is perfect by assumption (2), it has finite tor dimension, so there are integers a and b with H^i(K tensor^L_A kappa) = 0 for all i outside [a, b] (proof lines 28438-28441); the pointwise perfection criterion then gives that K is perfect (proof lines 28442-28443). The non-routine content is the radical argument that descends the residue field through A_1 and the use of the pointwise criterion.

items.title: Vanishing of a pro-system is equivalent to the vanishing of the limit and first derived limit of it and of its countable direct sum
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an inverse system of abelian groups (A_n) and establishes the equivalence of two conditions: that (A_n) be zero as a pro-object; and that both lim A_n and R^1 lim A_n vanish and the same holds for the countable direct sum of (A_n) (source lines 23526-23535). One direction is drawn from the pro-isomorphism statement: (1) implies (2) (proof lines 23538-23539). For the converse the proof first applies Emmanouil's criterion to conclude that (A_n) is Mittag-Leffler (proof lines 23540). The substantive part is then a direct analysis of the images: defining A_{n,m} = Im(A_m -> A_n) for m >= n, so that A_n = A_{n,n} contains A_{n,n+1} contains ..., the proof records the two translations of the hypotheses — that (A_n) is zero as a pro-object exactly when for every n there is m >= n with A_{n,m} = 0, and that (A_n) is Mittag-Leffler exactly when for every n there is m_n >= n with A_{n,m} = A_{n,m+1} = ... (proof lines 23541-23546). In the Mittag-Leffler case the proof observes that lim A_n = 0 forces A_{n,m_n} = 0, because the maps A_{n+1,m_{n+1}} -> A_{n,m} are surjective in that case, which completes the argument (proof lines 23546-23549). The non-routine content is the translation of pro-zeroness into the vanishing of the images at some later stage and the surjectivity used to descend it.

items.title: Over a separable fraction field extension a solution can be replaced by a separable solution
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings and assumes that the fraction field extension L/K is separable, that B is Nagata, and that there exists a solution for A in B; it concludes that there exists a separable solution (source lines 35892-35902). The proof is an induction on the inseparable degree. The characteristic zero case is trivial, so the proof assumes characteristic p > 0 (proof lines 35905-35906). Given a solution K_2/K, the proof inducts on the inseparable degree [K_2 : K]_i of K_2/K: if that degree is 1 then K_2 is separable over K and one is done (proof lines 35909-35912). Otherwise there exists a subfield K_2/K_1/K with K_2/K_1 purely inseparable of degree p, by the separability-first and finite-purely-inseparable statements (proof lines 35913-35916). The substantive step applies the approximate-solution lemma to produce a separable extension K_3/K_1 which is a solution for A in B (proof lines 35917-35919). Then the multiplicativity of inseparable degrees gives [K_3 : K]_i = [K_1 : K]_i = [K_2 : K]_i / p, which is smaller, so the induction hypothesis applies and finishes the proof (proof lines 35919-35922). The non-routine content is the choice of the purely inseparable degree p step and the degree computation that makes the induction decrease.

items.title: Derived complete modules form a weak Serre subcategory and the derived completion identifies the corresponding derived subcategory
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an ideal I of a ring A and asserts two things: that the derived complete A-modules form a weak Serre subcategory C of the category of A-modules, and that the full subcategory spelled with C of D(A) is exactly the full subcategory of derived complete objects (source lines 26067-26076). Part (2) is immediate from the Ext characterisation of derived completeness and the definitions (proof lines 26078-26079). Part (1) is the substantive verification of the weak Serre axioms. First, for a map M -> N of derived complete modules with K the corresponding object of D(A), the proof uses that Ext^n_A(A_f, M) and Ext^n_A(A_f, N) vanish for all n and every f in I to conclude that Ext^n_A(A_f, K) vanishes for all n, hence that K is derived complete; then part (2) shows that the kernel and cokernel of M -> N lie in C (proof lines 26080-26086). Second, for a short exact sequence 0 -> M_1 -> M_2 -> M_3 -> 0 with M_1 and M_3 derived complete, the long exact sequence of Ext shows that M_2 is derived complete (proof lines 26087-26090). The conclusion that C is a weak Serre subcategory follows from the characterisation of weak Serre subcategories (proof lines 26091-26092). The non-routine content is the arrangement of the long exact Ext sequences so that the two weak Serre axioms are satisfied.

items.title: In a two-dimensional Noetherian local ring an element avoiding the minimal primes extends to a system of parameters stable under small perturbations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension two and an element f in m contained in no minimal prime of R, and asserts the existence of g in m and an integer N such that f and g form a system of parameters and such that for every h in m^N, the pair f + h and g again forms a system of parameters with length_R(R/(f, g)) = length_R(R/(f + h, g)) (source lines 38107-38119). The proof is an explicit computation parallel to the higher-dimensional statement. By the system-of-parameters existence lemma there is g in m making f, g a system of parameters, so that m = sqrt((f, g)); the Noetherian power lemma then gives n with m^n contained in (f, g), and the proof claims N = n + 1 works (proof lines 38122-38127). The verification is a direct ideal computation: for h in m^N one writes h = a f + b g with a and b in m, and the displayed chain (f + h, g) = (f + a f + b g, g) = ((1 + a) f, g) = (f, g) follows because 1 + a is a unit of R, which gives both the system-of-parameters claim and the equality of lengths (proof lines 38128-38134). The non-routine content is the choice N = n + 1 that lets the perturbation be absorbed into the first generator.

items.title: An explicit complex-level map realises the adjunction between derived base change and restriction
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring map R -> R' and objects K of D(R) and M of D(R'), and asserts a canonical isomorphism R Hom_R(K, M) = R Hom_{R'}(K tensor^L_R R', M) (source lines 28762-28769). The proof is an explicit comparison at the level of complexes. It chooses a K-injective complex J^bullet of R'-modules representing M, a quasi-isomorphism J^bullet -> I^bullet with I^bullet a K-injective complex of R-modules, and a K-flat complex K^bullet of R-modules representing K (proof lines 28772-28775). It then considers the map from Hom^bullet(K^bullet tensor_R R', J^bullet) to Hom^bullet(K^bullet, I^bullet) (proof lines 28776-28780). The substantive part is the degreewise description: on degree n terms the map is the product over n = p + q of Hom_{R'}(K^{-q} tensor_R R', J^p) -> Hom_R(K^{-q}, I^p) obtained by precomposing with K^{-q} -> K^{-q} tensor_R R' and postcomposing with J^p -> I^p (proof lines 28781-28787). To conclude, the proof observes that it suffices to show the induced maps on cohomology are isomorphisms, namely that Hom_{D(R)}(K, M) = Hom_{D(R')}(K tensor^L_R R', M), which is true because derived base change is left adjoint to restriction by the tensor-Hom adjunction lemma (proof lines 28788-28795). The non-routine content is the degreewise formula for the comparison map together with the identification of its cohomology with the adjunction comparison.

items.title: Weak unramifiedness is preserved by a totally ramified separable base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A -> B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L, assumes A -> B weakly unramified, and asserts that for any finite separable extension K_1/K totally ramified with respect to A one has that L_1 = L tensor_K K_1 is a field, that A_1 and B_1 = B tensor_A A_1 are discrete valuation rings, and that the extension A_1 in B_1 is weakly unramified (source lines 34489-34498). The proof works with uniformizers and the minimal polynomial. Writing pi in A and pi_1 in A_1 for uniformizers, total ramifiedness gives pi_1^e = u_1 pi for a unit u_1 of A_1, so that A_1 is generated over A by pi_1 and the minimal polynomial P(t) of pi_1 over K has the displayed Eisenstein shape t^e + a_{e-1} t^{e-1} + ... + a_0 with all a_i in (pi) and a_0 = u pi for a unit u of A (proof lines 34501-34509). The proof records that e = [K_1 : K] (proof line 34510). The substantive step is the base change: since A -> B is weakly unramified, pi is a uniformizer of B, so B_1 = B[t]/(P(t)) is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer the class of t, from which all three assertions follow (proof lines 34510-34513). The non-routine content is the reduction of the weak unramifiedness of the base change to the statement that B[t]/(P(t)) is a discrete valuation ring with the evident uniformizer.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma extends the standard classification of locally constant sheaves to irreducible geometrically unibranch schemes, and the point of the extension is that a finite Lambda-module need not have a finite underlying set, so the proof of the companion lemma does not apply as written (statement lines 10199-10219, with the author's remark at proof lines 10221-10224 recording exactly that failure). The proof has three steps: the reduction to the normal case through the normalization morphism and the invariance of the etale site under universal homeomorphisms (proof lines 10227-10236); the construction of the functor from finite type locally constant sheaves to finite modules with continuous fundamental group action in the integral normal case (proof lines 10239-10263); and the converse construction together with the verification that the two are inverse (proof lines 10266-10291). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings

The proof is a long sequence of reductions that each remove a hypothesis: from arbitrary R -> S to finite presentation by writing S as a quotient and using that the ideal is a union of finitely generated ideals, then to R of finite type over Z by a filtered colimit argument with a dimension bound descending along the colimit, and finally an induction on dim(R) that peels off a component of the complement of a distinguished open and applies the inductive hypothesis to R/I -> S/IS. The final assembly takes the maximum of the two thresholds. What makes this non-routine is that the dimension condition must be transported through each of these reductions in the correct direction, and the induction needs the complement to be cut out by an ideal so that dim(R/I) < dim(R). items.difficulty_reason: The theorem asserts that for an integral, universally injective and surjective f : X -> Y, pullback along f is an equivalence between the small etale topoi. The proof is organised as a three-part verification. Faithfulness is settled first by exhibiting a pair of distinct morphisms and separating them after base change. What is not routine is that the reduction to schemes must respect the etale sites on both sides, and that both fullness and essential surjectivity depend on the same descent construction. items.title: Tensoring an injective module by a finite locally free module yields an injective module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the tensor product of an injective O_X-module I with a finite locally free O_X-module E is again injective. The proof uses the adjunction Hom(F, E tensor I) = Hom(F tensor E^vee, I) for the dual E^vee = SheafHom(E, O_X), which is again finite locally free, and then concludes by the standard criterion: since tensoring with a finite locally free sheaf is exact, the functor Hom(-, E tensor I) is exact and hence E tensor I is injective (proof lines 13827-13839). H2: the adjunction identification with the dual, combined with exactness of tensoring by a finite locally free sheaf, is the whole content, and neither step is a citation-only reduction.

items.title: Finiteness and torsion freeness of the limit of the global sections of an inverse system of sheaves over a complete principal ideal ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a Noetherian ring A complete with respect to a principal ideal (f), an inverse system of sheaves whose first term has finite global sections and which satisfies the f-divisibility condition has M = lim Gamma(X, F_n) finite over A with f a nonzerodivisor and M/fM the image of M in Gamma(X, F_1). The proof derives the containment M/fM inside H^0(X, F_1) from a cited result, gets finiteness of M/fM from that containment, observes that the intersection of the f^nM is zero by construction, and concludes finiteness of M from the cited complete-ring criterion (proof lines 9316-9322). The final claim is a one-line kernel computation: if fs = 0 then s_{n+1} lies in the kernel of F_{n+1} -> F_n by the divisibility condition (proof lines 9323-9328). H2: combining the two cited finiteness criteria with the explicit description of the kernel is the substance.

items.title: The locus where all cohomology sheaves of a perfect complex are finite free is open and is the maximal such open subset
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the set of points where all cohomology sheaves of a perfect complex are finite free at the stalk as an open subset and shows it is the maximal open set on which all cohomology sheaves are finite locally free, assuming the local rings of the structure sheaf are local. The proof replaces X by an open neighbourhood so that E is represented by a strictly perfect complex concentrated in degrees [a, b], then runs an induction on b - a: the top cohomology is finitely presented, freeness at the stalk spreads to a neighbourhood, and a direct sum decomposition of E^b and then of E^{b-1} is arranged so that the truncated complex represents a perfect object with the same cohomology outside degree b (proof lines 12728-12754). H2: the induction on the length of a strictly perfect representative together with the two direct sum splittings is the non-routine content.

items.title: Adjunction and vanishing for cohomology with support of a sheaf pushed forward from a closed subset
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves three facts about R-H_Z for the inclusion i : Z -> X of a closed subset: it is right adjoint to i_* on the derived level, it recovers K from i_*K, and its higher cohomology sheaves vanish on sheaves pushed forward from Z. The proof derives the adjunction from exactness of i_* together with the derived adjunction criterion applied to the abelian adjunction of sections with support (proof lines 8513-8517), and proves the second statement by representing K by a K-injective complex whose pushforward stays K-injective, so that H_Z(i_*I^bullet) computes R-H_Z(i_*K) and equals I^bullet; the third statement is then the special case of a single sheaf (proof lines 8518-8525). H2: the K-injective bookkeeping is short but is exactly what makes the derived statement follow, and it is not spelled out anywhere else in the section.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the nonvanishing of degree n cohomology with l-power torsion coefficients is the same on S and on the limit X of a directed system of finite etale S-schemes of constant degree prime to l (statement lines 10542-10560). The non-formal content is the descent of a cohomology class from the limit to a stage. The claim is H2: two applications of the same transfer argument.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma generalises the filtration statement from F_l-vector spaces to finite type locally constant Lambda-modules annihilated by l^n, over an irreducible geometrically unibranch scheme: after a finite etale cover of degree prime to l the pullback admits a finite filtration with successive quotients constant sheaves attached to finite Lambda-modules (statement lines 10478-10489). The proof translates the sheaf into a module with continuous fundamental group action (proof lines 10491-10505), realises the relevant finite quotient by a cover of the required degree (proof lines 10505-10518), and filters the pullback using the structure of modules over the group algebra of a finite group of order prime to l (proof lines 10518-10524). The non-formal content is the same as in the F_l case, now with the annihilator hypothesis supplying the bounded torsion. The claim is H2: one translation plus one filtration argument.

items.title: Vanishing of higher Cech cohomology for all open coverings implies vanishing of cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a module F on a ringed space whose Cech cohomology vanishes in positive degrees for every open covering of every open, the lemma concludes the vanishing of ordinary cohomology in positive degrees on every open (statement lines 1630-1644). The proof embeds F into an injective I, uses that injectives have trivial higher Cech cohomology, and observes that the short exact sequence then remains exact as a sequence of presheaves by the hypothesis, so that the quotient Q inherits the Cech vanishing (proof lines 1647-1665). The long exact cohomology sequence then gives the vanishing by induction: H^n(U, I) = 0 for n > 0 makes H^1(U, F) vanish, the same argument applied to Q gives H^1(U, Q) = 0 and hence H^2(U, F) = 0, and the argument repeats (proof lines 1668-1692). The claim is H2: a standard injective-and-induct argument whose only non-formal step is the recognition that the hypothesis makes the sequence of presheaves exact.

primary.label: author Lemma environment, source label lemma-cech-vanish (statement, source lines 1630-1644)

items.title: Cohomology of a quasi-compact Hausdorff subset as the colimit of the cohomologies of its open neighbourhoods
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a topological space X and a quasi-compact subset Z whose points admit disjoint open neighbourhoods, the lemma shows that the canonical map from the colimit of the cohomology over the open neighbourhoods of Z to the cohomology of the restriction of a sheaf to Z is an isomorphism (statement lines 2847-2863). The proof is long and has genuine content. Degree zero is handled by hand: injectivity is immediate, and surjectivity requires gluing local lifts, for which the author finds opens W_ij inside the pairwise intersections on which two lifts agree and then applies a covering-lifting lemma for quasi-compact Hausdorff subsets to shrink the U_i so that the lifts glue (proof lines 2866-2880). For positive degrees the argument reduces to injective sheaves, then rewrites a Cech class of a covering of Z as a class of the presheaf of sections that extend to X, refines the covering so that every cocycle is such a section, lifts the cocycles to X using flasqueness of injectives, and finally shrinks the covering so that the lifted cochain becomes a cocycle, at which point triviality of the higher Cech cohomology of an injective finishes the proof (proof lines 2883-2947). The claim is H3: the presheaf of extendable sections, the refinement producing cocycles of that presheaf, and the two shrinkage steps using the covering-lifting lemma are an original assembly, not a citation chain.

primary.label: author Lemma environment, source label lemma-cohomology-of-closed (statement, source lines 2847-2863)

items.title: Flatness of a module is equivalent to the vanishing of the first Tor functor against every module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a ringed space and a module F, the lemma shows that flatness of F is equivalent to the vanishing of the first Tor functor of F against every module (statement lines 6204-6217). One direction is immediate because flatness makes the tensor functor exact, so the satellites vanish. The converse is where the argument lies: given an injection of modules with cokernel Q, the long exact sequence of Tor identifies the kernel of the induced map on tensor products as a quotient of the first Tor of F against Q, which vanishes by hypothesis, so the tensor functor is exact and F is flat (proof lines 6219-6229). The claim is H2: a two-line application of the long exact Tor sequence, with the direction that requires the sequence written out in full.

items.title: Filtration of a finitely generated subsheaf of the constant sheaf Z by extensions of extensions by zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: On a space where the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact, the lemma shows that a subsheaf of the constant sheaf Z generated by finitely many sections over quasi-compact opens admits a finite filtration whose successive quotients sit in short exact sequences involving extensions by zero of the constant sheaf Z along inclusions of quasi-compact opens (statement lines 3479-3501). The proof is a real normalisation argument: after decomposing the generating opens so that the generators become constant sections, removing zero generators and flipping signs, the author enlarges the list by adding, for every subset of indices, the intersection of the corresponding opens together with the greatest common divisor of the corresponding integers, so that at every point the gcd of the generators active there is attained by one of them (proof lines 3504-3516). The filtration is then indexed by the positive integers, with the n-th piece generated by the generators not exceeding n, and the successive quotient is generated by the single value n over the union of the opens where the generators are at most n while its kernel is generated by the same value over the smaller union, which produces exactly the required short exact sequence (proof lines 3518-3527). The claim is H2: the gcd-enlargement device and the filtration by values are both written out in full.
