items.title: Vanishing above the dimension from the vanishing on extensions by zero of basis opens
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: Under four hypotheses on a topological space X, namely quasi-compactness, quasi-compact opens forming a basis, stability of intersections of quasi-compact opens, and the vanishing of the cohomology of the extensions by zero of the constant sheaf Z along quasi-compact opens above the degree d, the lemma concludes that the cohomology of every abelian sheaf vanishes above d (statement lines 3530-3545). The proof has three genuinely different stages. First the author writes an arbitrary sheaf as a filtered colimit of subsheaves generated by finitely many local sections over quasi-compact opens and uses the colimit formula for cohomology, reducing to the finitely generated case (proof lines 3548-3571). Second, an induction on the number of generators via a short exact sequence reduces to sheaves generated by at most one section, which are exactly the quotients of the extensions by zero of Z along quasi-compact opens (proof lines 3574-3587). Third, the kernel of such a quotient is controlled by the filtration of a subsheaf of the constant sheaf Z by extensions of extensions by zero, which transfers the hypothesis to the successive quotients and finishes by induction along the long exact sequence (proof lines 3589-3615). The claim is H3: three linked reduction stages, each of which is an argument of its own, ending in a transfer of the vanishing hypothesis along a filtration.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'

items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism f: X to Y of schemes locally of finite type over a base S, a point x with y = f(x) and equal residue fields, the lemma shows that injectivity of the differential on tangent spaces is equivalent to unramifiedness of f at x (statement lines 3148-3157). The proof is a short chain of translations: the differential is injective exactly when the induced map on the fibres of the relative differentials is surjective, which is the tangent-cotangent duality statement; the transitivity exact sequence for differentials then identifies that surjectivity with the vanishing of the fibre of the relative differentials of f; and vanishing of that fibre is the pointwise criterion for unramifiedness (proof lines 3159-3170). The claim is H2: three cited inputs chained, but the chain is what produces a usable tangent-space criterion, and each step is a different statement rather than a repetition.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement concerns an inverse system of rings with surjective transition maps having locally nilpotent kernels, objects over each ring compatible under reduction, and asks that the derived limit be pseudo-coherent and be recovered by reduction (statement lines 28335-28351). The proof represents the first object by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, propagates pseudo-coherence along the system through the nilpotent kernel statement, lifts the system to complexes of finite free modules whose reductions are isomorphisms of complexes, and then identifies the derived limit with the limit complex, whose terms are finite free of the same bounded ranks (proof lines 28353-28374). The strictness of the reductions is what makes the limit complex computable and hence pseudo-coherent. The counted span refers five times, four times to results of this chapter and once to a remark of this chapter accompanying the computation of derived limits, all carried as navigation stubs.

items.title: A linear combination of elements defining an injective map is a nonzerodivisor in the polynomial ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that if the map sending x to the tuple (x a_1, ..., x a_n) is injective, then the linear form sum a_i t_i is a nonzerodivisor in the polynomial ring, and the proof is a 29-line argument in two cases. The case of a Noetherian ring works with the associated primes of the base: for each associated prime one of the a_i is not a unit and the symmetric powers involved are free, so localising at that prime makes the multiplication injective and the injectivity follows because a map that is injective at all associated primes is injective. The general case writes the ring as a filtered union of Noetherian subrings containing the a_i and applies the result to each of them. The localisation argument at associated primes is the substance, and the reduction to the Noetherian case is displayed.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the Tor groups of a base changed pair of algebras with the base change of the Tor groups of the original pair, under three flatness hypotheses, and the proof is a 31-line argument in three stages. It first constructs the canonical comparison map from the functoriality of Tor, then computes one of the intermediate Tor groups by a free resolution and uses flatness to identify it with a base change of Tor over the original ring, and finally uses Lazard's theorem to write the outer algebras as filtered colimits of finite free modules so that Tor commutes with the colimit and the identification becomes an isomorphism. Each of the three stages uses exactly one of the hypotheses, and all three are carried out in the source.

items.title: The zero scheme of a regular section of an ample invertible sheaf on a connected proper scheme of depth at least two is connected
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the zero scheme of a regular section s of an ample invertible sheaf on a connected proper scheme whose local rings have depth at least two is connected. The proof argues by contradiction: the vanishing schemes Z(s^n) have the same underlying topological space as Z(s), so a disconnected Z(s) would give a nontrivial idempotent in R_n = Gamma(X, O_{Z(s^n)}), hence the map Gamma(X, O_X) -> R_n is not an isomorphism; reading that off the canonical short exact sequence 0 -> L^{-n} -> O_X -> O_{Z(s^n)} -> 0 forces either H^0(X, L^{-n}) or H^1(X, L^{-n}) to be nonzero for infinitely many n, contradicting the two vanishing theorems for negative twists (proof lines 11308-11328). H3: the idempotent-to-cohomology transfer and the use of both vanishing theorems in one contradiction are independent research-level moves.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that (L_1 ... L_d . Z) is positive when L_1, ..., L_d are ample on a proper scheme X over a field and Z is a closed subscheme of dimension d. The proof inducts on d: the zero-dimensional case follows from the finite-support Euler characteristic lemma, and in the inductive step one reduces to Z integral and then to Z = X a proper variety, replaces L_1 by a positive tensor power so that a section with affine nonvanishing locus exists, observes that X is not affine so the section has a nonempty vanishing scheme Z(s) which is a regular effective Cartier divisor of dimension d - 1, rewrites the intersection number as (L_2 ... L_d . Z(s)) using the effective-Cartier-divisor lemma, and concludes by induction (proof lines 10586-10618). items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a domain A with fraction field K and finitely many Noetherian one-dimensional semi-local domains B_i inside K whose tensor products with A surject onto K, an element x of A whose inverse lies in the Jacobson radical of every B_i. The proof first replaces each B_i by its integral closure, using the conductor lemma to descend back after raising x to a power, then replaces semi-local Dedekind domains by their local rings, and finally reformulates the problem in terms of the associated discrete valuations v_i: one must find a nonzero x in A with v_i(x) < 0 for all i (proof lines 7546-7566). The existence is then proved by induction on the number of valuations, with the crucial step replacing x by a power so that v_i(x) < v_i(y) for i < r and taking x + y (proof lines 7568-7578). H2: the reduction chain and the weighted induction combining two elements are the non-routine content.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects five criteria relating the sign of the degree of an invertible sheaf L on a proper curve to the existence and vanishing behaviour of its sections, and concludes that a nonzero map N -> L forces deg(L) at least deg(N) with equality only for an isomorphism. H2: the realization of the section as an effective Cartier divisor and the reduction of the general case to the degree-zero criterion are the substance.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the degree of a locally free module E/X/k of constant rank equals the degree of its base change E_{k'}/X_{k'}/k'. The proof sets X_{k'} equal to the base change of X and E_{k'} equal to the pullback along the projection, then applies flat base change for cohomology to identify H^i(X_{k'}, E_{k'}) with H^i(X, E) tensor_k k' and similarly for the structure sheaf (proof lines 9579-9586). Since the Euler characteristics are therefore unchanged, so is the degree (proof lines 9587-9588). H2: the reduction of the claim to two flat-base-change identifications is short but complete, and the constant-rank hypothesis is exactly what the degree formula needs.

items.title: The degree of a finite locally free sheaf of constant rank is invariant under pullback along a birational morphism of schemes of dimension at most one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves deg(f^*E) = deg(E) for a birational morphism f : X' -> X of proper schemes of dimension at most 1 over a field and a finite locally free E of constant rank, and notes that the hypothesis can be weakened to f inducing a bijection on one-dimensional components and isomorphisms at the corresponding generic points. The proof first shows f is proper with fibres of dimension at most zero, hence finite, so that Rf_*f^*E = E tensor f_*O_{X'} by the projection formula; it then uses the exact sequence 0 -> K -> O_X -> f_*O_{X'} -> Q -> 0 whose kernel and cokernel have zero-dimensional support, and telescopes the difference of Euler characteristics through additivity and the rank-linear behaviour of chi on zero-dimensional support (proof lines 9621-9665). H2: the identification of the kernel and cokernel of O_X -> f_*O_{X'} as zero-dimensional and the Euler characteristic telescoping are the substance.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves chi(X, E tensor F) = r deg(E) + n chi(X, F) for a locally free E of rank n and a coherent F of rank r on a proper curve. The proof applies the general criterion for a property of coherent sheaves to hold on all of them: it verifies that the property P(F) expressed by the formula is additive in short exact sequences, because both the Euler characteristic and the rank are additive, and that it holds for the two test sheaves required by the criterion, namely O_X (where it is the definition of the degree) and i_*O_Z for a closed point (where r = 0 and the claim reduces to the finite support lemma) (proof lines 9681-9692). H2: setting up the property and verifying the two test cases of the criterion is the substance.

items.title: The degree of a pulled-back locally free module along a nonconstant morphism of proper curves is multiplied by the degree of the morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves deg(f^*E) = deg(X/Y) deg(E) for a nonconstant morphism of proper curves and a locally free E on the target. The proof recalls that the degree of X over Y is the rank of f_*O_X as a coherent sheaf on Y, namely the dimension of its stalk at the generic point, and then telescopes the Euler characteristic: chi(X, f^*E) = chi(Y, f_*f^*E) = chi(Y, E tensor f_*O_X) = deg(X/Y) deg(E) + n chi(Y, f_*O_X) = deg(X/Y) deg(E) + n chi(X, O_X) (proof lines 9906-9922). Each equality is then justified by finiteness of f, the projection formula, and the rank formula for the degree (proof lines 9923-9927). H2: the telescoping computation and the identification of the degree with the generic rank of f_*O_X are the substance.

items.title: The delta-invariant dominates the number of geometric branches minus one for strictly henselian one-dimensional reduced Nagata local rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the inequality delta-invariant >= number of geometric branches - 1 in the strictly henselian one-dimensional reduced Nagata case. The proof works with the normalization A' of A and its local factors: it shows that the canonical map A/m -> A'/m A' is an isomorphism, that A' is a product of local rings because A is henselian and A -> A' is finite, that these factors are discrete valuation rings because A' is normal, and concludes that A is the wedge of these local rings (proof lines 8709-8737). The number of geometric branches is then read off from the number of local factors and compared with the length of A'/A, giving the inequality. H3: the wedge decomposition and the transfer from the number of local factors of the normalization to the branch count are independent arguments, not a routine assembly.

items.title: Powers of an element of the Jacobson radical of the integral closure of a one-dimensional semi-local domain land back in the domain
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma records that the integral closure B' of a semi-local Noetherian one-dimensional domain B in its fraction field is a semi-local Dedekind domain, and that for a nonzero x in the Jacobson radical of B' and any y in B' some power x^n y lies in B. The proof builds the subring A generated by B, x and y inside B', shows it is finite over B, observes that the finite module A/B is supported on the closed points of B so that a power of the Jacobson radical of B lands in B, notes that Spec(B') -> Spec(A) is surjective and hence A is semi-local with x in its Jacobson radical, and finishes with x^m y in m_B A for some m, giving x^{nm} y in B (proof lines 7427-7443). H2: the intermediate ring A and the two-step use of the conductor to absorb y are the substance.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves chi(Y, G) = sum (-1)^i chi(X, R^i f_* G) for a morphism f : Y -> X of proper schemes over a field and a coherent G on Y. The proof first checks that the formula makes sense, using coherence and finiteness of the higher direct images, then applies the Leray spectral sequence with E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, R^q f_* G) converging to H^{p+q}(Y, G) (proof lines 6286-6295). Finiteness of cohomology on X makes all E_2 terms finite dimensional and almost all zero, so the alternating sum of dimensions is independent of the page; since E_r stabilizes and convergence means a filtration on H^n(Y, G) with graded pieces E_infty^{p,q}, the alternating sums agree and the formula follows (proof lines 6296-6309). H2: the spectral-sequence bookkeeping through the alternating sum of dimensions is the substance and is a genuinely non-trivial assembly of cited machinery.

items.title: Lifting an element modulo an ideal while avoiding finitely many primes that do not contain the ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for an ideal I of a ring A and finitely many primes p_1, ..., p_r none of which contains I, every element of A/I lifts to an element of A avoiding all the p_i. The proof first removes inclusion relations among the primes, picks an arbitrary lift f, and lets S be the set of indices with f in p_s. If S is nonempty it forms the ideal J = I times the product of the p_i with i not in S, verifies that J is not contained in any p_s for s in S (using that there are no inclusions among the primes and that I is in none of them), invokes the avoidance lemma to find g in J outside all the p_s with s in S, and produces the solution f + g (proof lines 9069-9080). H2: the construction of the auxiliary ideal J and the avoidance step are the substance.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the number of geometric branches of a locally algebraic k-scheme X at a point equals that of its base change X_K at any point lying above it. The proof compares the normalizations of X and Y = X_K in the commutative square of X^nu, Y^nu and X^nu_K, uses the cited normalization-and-change-of-fields lemma to see that one arrow is a universal homeomorphism and hence induces purely inseparable residue field extensions, and then rewrites both branch numbers as sums of separable degrees of residue field extensions over the normalizations (proof lines 8617-8633). H2: the reduction to the algebra fact and the connected-component interpretation are the non-routine steps, and the proof contains a commutative diagram.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a connected reduced scheme X over a field k, the integral closure k' of k inside Gamma(X, O_X) is a field. The proof observes that X -> Spec(k) factors through Spec(k'), that k' is reduced because X is, and that by integrality of k -> k' every prime of k' is both minimal and maximal so Spec(k') is totally disconnected (proof lines 5327-5335). H2: the route from total disconnectedness of Spec(k') through constancy of the map to the locality of k' is the substance.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that an m-regular coherent sheaf on projective n-space is also (m+1)-regular. H2: the induction on n combined with the long exact sequence comparison across the two shifts is the substance.

items.title: The relative Frobenius of a locally finite type morphism in characteristic p is finite
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a scheme X over S in characteristic p with X -> S locally of finite type, the relative Frobenius F_{X/S} is finite. The proof translates to algebra: for a finite type homomorphism A -> B of characteristic p rings with B' = B tensor over (A, F_A) with A and F_{B/A} : B' -> B given by b tensor a maps to b^p a, the assertion is that F_{B/A} is finite (proof lines 7161-7165). Choosing generators x_1, ..., x_n of B over A, one has x_i^p = F_{B/A}(x_i tensor 1), so each generator is integral over B', and the integrality criterion for finite ring maps gives finiteness (proof lines 7166-7169). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves H^1(X, L) = 0 for every invertible sheaf of degree at least 2g - 1 on a proper curve over an algebraically closed field, where g = dim_k H^1(X, O_X). The proof takes the invertible module N supplied by the general degree lemma for line bundles, computes its degree as chi(X, N) - chi(X, O_X) = g - 1, and hence finds deg(L tensor N^{-1}) >= g, so that its Euler characteristic is at least one (proof lines 8160-8167). H2: the degree bookkeeping through the auxiliary line bundle and the short exact sequence computation are the substance.

items.title: Pseudo-coherence is unchanged by adjoining a variable and killing it
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a complex K^bullet of R-modules and an integer m, and considers the R-algebra map R[x] -> R sending x to zero; it asserts that K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules if and only if it is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R[x]-modules (source lines 21258-21265). The proof first records that this is a special case of the pushforward pseudo-coherence statement, then gives a second, independent argument (proof lines 21268-21270). In the second argument, the exact sequence 0 -> R[x] -> R[x] -> R -> 0 shows that R is pseudo-coherent as an R[x]-module, so one implication follows from the pushforward statement (proof lines 21273-21276). For the other implication, assuming K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent over R[x], the pullback statement gives that K^bullet tensor^L_{R[x]} R is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules; the pull-push statement then gives that K^bullet oplus K^bullet[1] is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules; and finally the summands statement gives that K^bullet itself is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules (proof lines 21277-21287). The non-routine content is the reduction of the two-term base change complex to the direct sum K^bullet oplus K^bullet[1], which converts a question about a shift-and-sum into one about summands.

items.title: Projective dimension is additive along a quotient ring of finite projective dimension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring R, an ideal I, and a nonzero finite module E over R/I, and assumes that R/I has finite projective dimension and that E has finite projective dimension over R/I; it concludes that E has finite projective dimension over R and that pd_R(E) = pd_R(R/I) + pd_{R/I}(E) (source lines 29860-29869). The proof proceeds through the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula. It first recalls that for a finite module, finiteness of projective dimension over R, respectively over R/I, is the same as being perfect (proof lines 29872-29874). It then uses the cohomology-of-perfect statement to conclude that E has finite projective dimension over R (proof lines 29875-29876). The substantive step applies Auslander-Buchsbaum three times, obtaining pd_R(E) + depth(E) = depth(R) with depth taken over R, pd_{R/I}(E) + depth(E) = depth(R/I) with depth taken over R/I, and pd_R(R/I) + depth(R/I) = depth(R) (proof lines 29877-29886). The proof then records that the two depths of E, computed over R and over R/I respectively, agree — a fact the author calls trivial and which also follows from the depth-goes-down statement (proof lines 29887-29890). Adding the second and third equations and comparing with the first yields the stated additivity (proof lines 29890-29891). The non-routine content is the correct bookkeeping of which depth is being used in each Auslander-Buchsbaum instance.

items.title: The factorization property for Ext one annihilation is preserved by base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an ideal I of a ring R, an object K of D(R) concentrated in degrees -1 and 0, and a ring map R -> R', and asserts that if K satisfies the equivalent conditions of the Ext-one-annihilation statement with respect to (R, I) then tau_{>=-1}(K tensor^L_R R') satisfies the same conditions with respect to (R', IR') (source lines 22552-22561). The proof works with the explicit representing complex. By the equivalent conditions one may assume K is represented by a two-term complex K^{-1} -> K^0 with K^0 free such that for every a in I the multiplication map a : K^{-1} -> K^{-1} equals h_a composed with the differential d_K^{-1}, for some map h_a : K^0 -> K^{-1} (proof lines 22564-22566). The two-term base change statement then shows that tau_{>=-1}(K tensor^L_R R') is represented by K^bullet tensor_R R' (proof lines 22567-22569). The substantive step is the base change of the factorization: for every a in I one has a tensor 1 = (h_a tensor 1) composed with (d_K^{-1} tensor 1), so the required factorization holds after base change (proof lines 22569-22571). Since the collection of maps K^{-1} tensor_R R' -> K^{-1} tensor_R R' factoring through d_K^{-1} tensor 1 forms an R'-module, and IR' is generated by the images of the elements of I, the conclusion follows for the ideal IR' (proof lines 22572-22574). The non-routine content is the observation that the factorization condition is preserved verbatim by base change, together with the module structure that promotes it from the generators of I to the whole ideal IR'.

In the special case where each inverse system (K_n^p) is right acyclic for lim, the computation lemma gives a short exact sequence 0 -> lim_n K^p_n -> prod_n K^p_n -> prod_n K^p_n -> 0 for every p, and since the complex with terms lim_n K^p_n computes R lim K, the lemma holds in that case (proof lines 23283-23291). The substantive step is the reduction: for general K, the computation lemma provides a quasi-isomorphism K -> L in D(Ab(N)) such that each (L_n^p) is acyclic, and because products are exact in the category of abelian groups the product prod K_n^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to prod L_n^bullet; hence the result for L, already proved, implies the result for K (proof lines 23294-23299). The non-routine content is the passage from the acyclic case to the general one using the existence of a suitable replacement and the exactness of products.

items.title: The first Ext of a quotient by a finitely generated ideal fits into a canonical short exact sequence with the Koszul homology and the Hom of the naive Koszul module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a finitely generated ideal I = (f_1, ..., f_n), and an R-module N, and defines the explicit module H_1(N, f_bullet) as the quotient of the n-tuples satisfying the Koszul relations by those of the form (f_1 x, ..., f_n x); it asserts that for every N there is a canonical short exact sequence 0 -> Ext_R(R/I, N) -> H_1(N, f_bullet) -> Hom_R(K, N), where K is the module of the naive Koszul complex (source lines 24412-24427). The proof first records the convention that the Ext groups here are those of the category of modules as defined earlier (proof lines 24429-24432). It then computes Ext_R(R/I, N) by applying the six-term exact sequence to the short exact sequence 0 -> I -> R -> R/I -> 0 and using Ext_R(R, N) = 0, obtaining Ext_R(R/I, N) = Coker(N -> Hom(I, N)) (proof lines 24433-24440). The substantive second step uses the short exact sequence of the naive Koszul complex to produce a complex N -> Hom(M, N) -> Hom_R(K, N) whose middle homology is canonically isomorphic to Ext_R(R/I, N) (proof lines 24441-24448). Since the cokernel of the first map of that complex is canonically isomorphic to H_1(N, f_bullet), the displayed short exact sequence follows and the proof is complete (proof lines 24448-24450). The non-routine content is the identification of Ext_R(R/I, N) with the middle homology of the explicit three-term complex, which is what places it in the displayed sequence.

items.title: For a Noetherian ring the completion and localization along an element exhibit finitely generated modules as a fibre product
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition takes a Noetherian ring R, an element f, and the f-adic completion R-hat, and asserts that the functor M -> (M-hat, M_f, can) defines an equivalence between finitely generated R-modules and the fibre product of finitely generated R-hat-modules and R_f-modules over finitely generated (R-hat)_f-modules (source lines 24998-25012). The proof identifies this functor with one already treated. It records that R -> R-hat is flat and that R/fR = R-hat/fR-hat, and that the completion of a finite R-module M equals M tensor_R R-hat, so that the displayed functor coincides with the functor of the formal gluing theorem; in particular it is fully faithful (proof lines 25015-25024). The substantive step is essential surjectivity: given an object (M_1, M_2, psi) of the right-hand category, the formal gluing theorem produces an R-module M with M_1 = M tensor_R R-hat and M_2 = M_f, and then the proof argues that M is finitely generated (proof lines 25024-25028). That last step uses that R -> R-hat x R_f is faithfully flat together with the cover criterion (proof lines 25028-25031). The non-routine content is the reduction of the equivalence statement for finitely generated modules to the unrestricted formal gluing theorem plus faithful flatness of the pair of maps.

items.title: Flatness of the tensor square and weak etaleness descend along a faithfully flat extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes ring maps A -> B -> C and asserts two descents: that if B -> C is faithfully flat and C tensor_A C -> C is flat, then B tensor_A B -> B is flat; and that if B -> C is faithfully flat and A -> C is weakly etale, then A -> B is weakly etale (source lines 30374-30383). The proof of the first part is a descent along the displayed commutative square with corners C tensor_A C, C, B tensor_A B and B. The proof notes that the vertical arrows are flat and the top horizontal arrow is flat, whence C is flat as a B tensor_A B-module (proof lines 30385-30395). The substantive step is the descent: since B -> C is faithfully flat and C = B tensor_B C, the flatness of C over B tensor_A B descends to flatness of B over B tensor_A B, by the general descent lemma for flatness (proof lines 30395-30398). The second part then follows from the first together with the fact that A -> B is flat whenever A -> C is flat and B -> C is faithfully flat, again by the same descent lemma (proof lines 30399-30401). The non-routine content is the arrangement of the base-changed square so that the flatness of the top arrow plus faithful flatness of B -> C gives the conclusion by descent.

items.title: The zeroth cohomology functor is right adjoint to the canonical functor out of the gluing category
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that in the gluing setup the functor H^0 from the gluing category Glue(R -> S, f_1, ..., f_t) to R-modules is right adjoint to the canonical functor Can in the other direction (source lines 24701-24707). The proof constructs the adjunction comparison map explicitly: for an object bold M = (M', M_i, alpha_i, alpha_ij) of the gluing category and an R-module N, the proof exhibits the map from Hom(Can(N), bold M) to Hom_R(N, H^0(bold M)) sending psi to H^0(psi) composed with the obvious map N -> H^0(Can(N)) (proof lines 24709-24718). It then notes that by construction this map is an isomorphism for N = R, even though R -> H^0(Can(R)) need not be an isomorphism in general (proof lines 24719-24720). The substantive step extends this from N = R to all N: the proof observes that the gluing category has direct sums and cokernels, that Can commutes with direct sums and cokernels, and hence that the displayed map is bijective because N can be written as a cokernel of a map between free R-modules (proof lines 24721-24724). The author states that the details are omitted (proof line 24725). The non-routine content is the reduction from the single case N = R to all modules by presenting N as a cokernel of free modules, using the exactness properties of Can.

items.title: An integral domain extension of a henselian local ring is henselian local, and strict henselianness forces a purely inseparable residue extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring homomorphism A -> B assuming that A is a henselian local ring, that A -> B is integral, and that B is a domain, and asserts that B is a henselian local ring with A -> B a local homomorphism; it adds that if A is strictly henselian then B is strictly henselian and the residue field extension is purely inseparable (source lines 30756-30769). The proof reduces the integral case to the finite case. It writes B as a filtered colimit of finite A-subalgebras B_i and observes that it suffices to prove the statements for each B_i, by the colimit-of-henselian-rings lemma (proof lines 30771-30774). For a finite A -> B the proof uses that B is a product of local henselian rings, whence B is local because B is a domain (proof lines 30775-30777). The maximal ideal of B lies over that of A by going up for integral maps, which gives both the locality of the homomorphism and, with the domain hypothesis, the henselian property (proof lines 30778-30779). The substantive final step concerns the strictly henselian case: the residue field extension being algebraic, it has to be purely inseparable, and consequently kappa(m_B) is separably algebraically closed and B is strictly henselian (proof lines 30780-30784). The non-routine content is the reduction from the integral to the finite case and the purely inseparable conclusion for strictly henselian A.

items.title: Isomorphisms in the category of weird inverse systems are detected by bounded torsion kernels and cokernels
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes isomorphisms in the category of the weird systems remark: a morphism (c, phi_n) is an isomorphism if and only if there is c' >= 0 such that the kernel and cokernel of phi_n are I^{c'}-torsion for all sufficiently large n (source lines 29167-29174). The proof is an explicit construction of an inverse. It first assumes, without loss of generality, that c' >= c and that the kernel and cokernel of every phi_n are I^{c'}-torsion (proof lines 29177-29179). For n >= c' and x in I^{c'}E'_n it chooses y in I^cE_n with x congruent to phi_n(y) modulo E'_n[I^c], possible because the cokernel is annihilated by I^{c'}, and sets psi_n(x) to be the class of y in E_n/E_n[I^{c'}] (proof lines 29180-29183). The substantive step is well-definedness: for another choice y' with the same congruence the difference y - y' maps to zero in E'_n/E'_n[I^c] and hence is annihilated by I^{c'} in I^cE_n, so psi_n is independent of the choice (proof lines 29183-29188). The author then omits the verification that (c', psi_n) is the inverse of (c, phi_n) in the category (proof lines 29189-29190). The non-routine content is the lifting step and the well-definedness argument, both of which depend on reading the torsion conditions at the correct exponents; note that the author leaves the final composition check to the reader.

items.title: A ring map is perfect exactly when the target has a finite resolution by finite projectives over a polynomial algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises a perfect ring map A -> B by the existence of a presentation B = A[x_1, ..., x_n]/I together with a finite resolution of B by finite projective A[x_1, ..., x_n]-modules (source lines 21773-21778). The proof runs the two implications. For a perfect A -> B, the proof uses that B is pseudo-coherent as an A[x_1, ..., x_n]-module and has finite tor dimension as an A-module; the perfect-over-a-polynomial-ring lemma then makes B perfect as an A[x_1, ..., x_n]-module, which by the perfect-module statement means it has a finite resolution by finite projective A[x_1, ..., x_n]-modules (proof lines 21781-21787). Conversely, given such a resolution, B is pseudo-coherent as an A[x_1, ..., x_n]-module, hence A -> B is pseudo-coherent; and the given resolution over A[x_1, ..., x_n] is in particular a finite resolution by flat A-modules, so B has finite tor dimension as an A-module (proof lines 21788-21794). The two conditions together are exactly the definition of a perfect ring map, which closes the equivalence. The non-routine content is the pairing of relative pseudo-coherence with finite tor dimension over the base in each direction.

items.title: Projective amplitude of a pseudo-coherent complex is equivalent to perfection with bounded tor amplitude and to Ext vanishing against finitely presented modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a pseudo-coherent object K of D(R), and integers a and b, and establishes the equivalence of five conditions: that K have projective-amplitude in [a, b]; that K be perfect of tor-amplitude in [a, b]; that Ext^i_R(K, N) vanish for all finitely presented N and all i outside [-b, -a]; that H^n(K) vanish for n > b with Ext^i_R(K, N) vanishing for all finitely presented N and all i > -a; and that H^n(K) vanish outside [a-1, b] with Ext^{-a+1}_R(K, N) vanishing for all finitely presented N (source lines 20135-20150). The proof is organized in two halves. First, (2) implies (1) by the final statement of the perfect-complex lemma; conversely, if (1) holds then K is represented by a complex of projectives P^i vanishing outside [a, b], and since projective modules are flat being summands of free modules, K has tor-amplitude in [a, b], so (2) holds (proof lines 20153-20158). The substantive second half reduces the Ext conditions against finitely presented modules to conditions against all modules: the proof observes that in (3), (4) and (5) the assumed vanishing of Ext^i_R(K, M) for M of finite presentation is equivalent to the vanishing for all R-modules M, by the colimit statement for pseudo-coherent objects together with the description of an arbitrary module as a filtered colimit of finitely presented ones (proof lines 20161-20165). The equivalence of (1), (3), (4) and (5) then follows from the projective-amplitude criterion (proof lines 20166-20167). The non-routine content is the reduction of the Ext vanishing hypotheses from finitely presented to arbitrary modules, which is what brings the three numerical conditions into the range of the existing criterion.

items.title: Objects of D(R) with cohomology only in degrees minus one and zero have two-term free representations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and an object K of D(R) whose cohomology vanishes outside degrees -1 and 0, and asserts two things: K can be represented by a two-term complex K^{-1} -> K^0 with K^0 free, and if R is Noetherian with H^{-1}(K) and H^0(K) finite, then K can be represented by such a complex with K^0 finite free and K^{-1} finite (source lines 22303-22314). Both halves are constructive. For (1), the proof replaces a representing complex of modules M^bullet by its truncation tau_{<=0}M^bullet, so that M^i vanishes for i > 0; chooses a free resolution P^bullet -> M^bullet with P^i = 0 for i > 0, quoting the existence of left resolutions in the derived category; and sets K^bullet = tau_{>=-1}P^bullet (proof lines 22317-22322). For (2), it uses the pseudo-coherence statement to choose a quasi-isomorphism F^bullet -> M^bullet with F^i = 0 for i > 0 and all F^i finite free, and again truncates, setting K^bullet = tau_{>=-1}F^bullet (proof lines 22325-22328). The non-routine content is the choice of truncation window: truncating above degree 0 and below degree -1 leaves exactly a two-term complex, and the freeness of K^0 is read off from the resolution, while in the Noetherian finite case the finiteness of K^{-1} comes from the finite free resolution.

items.title: The derived tensor product of two perfect complexes is perfect
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for a ring R, if K and L are perfect objects of D(R) then so is K tensor^L_R L (source lines 19050-19054). The proof gives an elementary argument via the definition: representing K and L by bounded complexes K^bullet and L^bullet of finite projective R-modules, the derived tensor product is represented by the bounded total complex Tot(K^bullet tensor_R L^bullet) (proof lines 19056-19061). The substantive observation is that the terms of that complex are direct sums of the modules M^a tensor_R L^b, and since M^a and L^b are direct summands of finite free R-modules, so is their tensor product; hence the terms of the total complex are finite projective, which makes it a bounded complex of finite projective modules and therefore perfect (proof lines 19062-19066). The proof then records a second route: the characterisation of perfect complexes together with the corresponding statements for pseudo-coherent complexes and for tor amplitude, the latter applied with A = B = R (proof lines 19068-19073). The non-routine content is the closure of finite projectivity under tensor products of summands of finite free modules, which is what makes the total complex eligible.

items.title: Naive derived completion and derived completion agree exactly when the f-power torsion is bounded
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: With I = (f), the lemma compares the naive derived completion K' = R lim (K tensor^L_A A/f^nA) with the derived completion K^wedge = R lim (K tensor^L_A (A -> f^n -> A)) of the Koszul-complex statement, and asserts that the natural transformation K^wedge -> K' is an isomorphism for all K if and only if the f-power torsion of A is bounded (source lines 26810-26822). The forward implication is short: if the f-power torsion is bounded, the pro-objects {(f^n : A -> A)} and {A/f^nA} are isomorphic by the lifting statement, hence the functors are isomorphic by the equality of R lim on pro-equal pro-objects (proof lines 26825-26828). The converse is the substantial direction. From the exactness statement for tensor and R lim one gets that the condition is exactly that R lim (K tensor^L_A A[f^n]) vanishes for all K in D(A), the maps of the system (A[f^n]) being multiplication by f (proof lines 26829-26834). Taking K = A and K = bigoplus over N of A, the R lim of direct sums statement forces (A[f^n]) to be zero as a pro-object, that is f^{n-1}A[f^n] = 0 for some n, which is equivalent to A[f^{n-1}] = A[f^n], that is, bounded f-power torsion (proof lines 26835-26840). The non-routine content is the design of the converse: the two test complexes are chosen so that the vanishing of R lim on their tensor products detects the pro-triviality of the system of f-power torsion modules.

items.title: Localizations, etale maps and filtered colimits of weakly etale algebras are weakly etale
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma lists three cases in which a ring map A -> B is weakly etale: when B is a localization of A; when A -> B is etale; and when B is a filtered colimit of weakly etale A-algebras (source lines 30453-30462). The proof treats the etale case first: an etale ring map is flat and the multiplication B tensor_A B -> B is again etale as a map between etale A-algebras, which is exactly the conjunction defining weak etaleness (proof lines 30465-30468). The colimit case is the substantive part: for a directed system B_i of weakly etale A-algebras, the colimit B is flat over A by the colimit-of-flat-maps statement; the transition maps B_i -> B_{i'} are flat by permanence of weak etaleness, so B is flat over each B_i and hence flat over B_i tensor_A B_i by composition of flat maps; and therefore B is flat over B tensor_A B = colim (B_i tensor_A B_i) by the colimit-of-rings-flat statement (proof lines 30471-30480). The localization case is then obtained directly or as a combination of the other two (proof lines 30483-30484). The non-routine content is the systematic use of flatness permanence to transport flatness of the multiplication maps along the colimit.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a proper scheme over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p the mod p etale cohomology is finite in each degree and unchanged under extension of algebraically closed fields (statement lines 9862-9874). The non-formal content is the use of the Artin-Schreier description in both parts. The claim is H2: one description plus two consequences.

items.difficulty_reason: The theorem states the fundamental exact sequence of etale sheaves on a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field (statement lines 10943-10953, with the set-up delivered verbatim as a context span from lines 10937-10941). The proof reduces to a connected etale U over X, where the sequence for U is a product of the sequences for the components (proof lines 10955-10961), identifies the classical exact sequence of the structure sheaf, its units and the divisor group with the sequence of sections of the sheaves in the statement (proof lines 10961-10980), and then uses that divisors on a nonsingular curve are Zariski locally principal to obtain surjectivity (proof lines 10981-10985). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for the spectrum S of a strictly henselian local ring with closed point sbar the global sections functor on abelian sheaves is exact, indeed the global sections of any sheaf of sets are the stalk at sbar, and consequently the higher etale cohomology of every abelian sheaf vanishes (statement lines 8206-8218). The proof identifies the global sections with the stalk at the closed point, using that every etale neighbourhood of the closed point admits a section (proof lines 8220-8232), and then uses exactness of the stalk functor to obtain exactness of global sections and the vanishing (proof lines 8232-8242). The non-formal content is the identification of sections with the stalk. The claim is H2: one identification plus one exactness argument.

items.title: An exponential upper bound on the number of large sets with a small edge boundary in a product graph
items.author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
items.work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the counting lemma for large sets with a small edge boundary (author lemma at source lines 714-716, label lem:small-boundary-sets): for a in the stated range, at most exp(2a/log d) sets of size a have an edge boundary below a log^2 d. The proof (source lines 718-743) has genuine content: it restricts to a sub-product on a set I of m = log_2(log^5 d) coordinates, applies the author's isoperimetric inequality on that sub-product to force any set with a small boundary to interact non-trivially with few of the fibres, converts that into a binomial-product bound on the number of admissible sets, and then optimises over m and over the choice of I to reach the exponential bound (proof lines 719-742). The lemma is one of the two counting inputs to the size bound on obstructions. H2.

The lemma is used in this chapter and in the Stacks treatment of morphisms to propagate irreducibility. H2.

items.title: The bivariant group of a morphism between disjoint unions is the product of the bivariant groups of its pieces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the bivariant group of a morphism of disjoint union decompositions as the product of the bivariant groups of the pieces, over an arbitrary index set (statement lines 6622-6634, tag 0FDZ). The proof builds both maps explicitly and then has to check the non-trivial composite: for a fixed piece of the target it uses that a bivariant class commutes with flat pullback to move the restriction of the cap into the pullback, and that it commutes with proper pushforward to identify the pushed forward restricted cap with the cap of the pushed forward class. Because the indices are arbitrary, the argument has to be phrased through the product decompositions of the Chow groups rather than finitely many cases, which is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that tor amplitude of an object over a local ring, over its henselization and over its strict henselization are equivalent conditions, with the expected variant when the object is pulled back from the local ring or from the henselization (statement lines 243-270, tag 0DK0). Faithful flatness disposes of the easy implications and of the descent equivalences, but the remaining direction needs a real argument: one represents the object by a bounded above complex of free modules, uses flatness over the local ring of the cokernel of the last differential below the interval, transports that flatness through the flat up and down lemma, and thereby exhibits a complex of flat modules over the strict henselization. That transport is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Chern classes of a finite locally free sheaf which is an extension of a sheaf of one lower rank by the structure sheaf: the top Chern class vanishes and all the lower ones agree with those of the quotient (statement lines 7862-7878, tag 02UG). The proof is a real comparison through projective bundles: it reduces to an integral base, embeds the projective bundle of the quotient into the projective bundle of the extension, realises the smaller one as an effective Cartier divisor cut out by the constant section so that its normal bundle is trivial, and then pushes the characterising relation of the quotient forward to obtain the relation of the extension, whose uniqueness forces the claimed identifications. The pushforward of the relation is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that being a weakly associated point of a quasi-coherent module is equivalent to the maximal ideal being a weakly associated prime after pulling the stalk back to the henselization or to the strict henselization (statement lines 379-395, tag 0CTU). One direction is the definition and the flat pullback statement, but the converse needs real work: it descends a witnessing element from the strict henselization to some etale neighbourhood using the colimit description of the strict henselization, uses faithful flatness to identify the annihilator downstairs as an inverse image so that its radical is the maximal ideal, and then applies the up and down lemma for etale neighbourhoods. The descent of the witnessing element is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Absolute flatness and reducedness transfer along a ring map whose tensor square is flat
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Let A -> B be a ring map such that B tensor_A B -> B is flat. The lemma asserts two things: if A is absolutely flat then so is B; and if A is reduced and A -> B is weakly etale then B is reduced (source lines 30322-30329). Part (1) the author disposes of in one line, as an immediate consequence of the key lemma and the definitions (proof line 30332). For part (2), the proof assumes A reduced and produces an injection A -> A' = product over the minimal primes of A of A_p into an absolutely flat ring, quoting the Algebra statement that a reduced ring embeds into the product of its residue fields at minimal primes together with the lemma that a product of fields is absolutely flat (proof lines 30333-30337). If A -> B is flat then the induced map B -> B' = B tensor_A A' is injective too (proof lines 30338-30339). By the base change statement the map A' -> B' is weakly etale (proof lines 30339-30340). Part (1) then shows B' is absolutely flat, and the absolutely flat statement shows B' is reduced (proof lines 30341-30342). Since B injects into the reduced ring B', B is reduced, completing the proof (proof lines 30342-30343). The non-routine content is the reduction of reducedness of B to that of the base changed ring B', which is legitimate only because the base change stays injective, a fact that uses flatness of A -> B.

items.title: Perfectness with tor amplitude in a range can be checked on residue fields at maximal ideals
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, integers a and b, and a pseudo-coherent complex K^bullet of R-modules, and proves the equivalence of three conditions: K^bullet is perfect with tor amplitude in [a, b]; for every prime p the cohomology H^i(K^bullet tensor^L_R kappa(p)) vanishes for i outside [a, b]; and the same vanishing for every maximal ideal m (source lines 20031-20045). The proof omits the implications (1) => (2) => (3) (proof line 20048), so the substantive content is (3) => (1). Assuming (3), fix i outside [a, b]; the cut-complex statement shows the assumption implies H^i(K^bullet)_m = 0 for all maximal ideals, hence H^i(K^bullet) = 0 (proof lines 20049-20053). The cut-complex statement is then used again to show that for every maximal ideal m there is an element f not in m such that K^bullet tensor_R R_f is perfect with tor amplitude in [a, b] (proof lines 20054-20059). The conclusion follows from the two gluing statements for perfectness and for tor amplitude (proof lines 20059-20060). The non-routine content is the two-step use of the cut-complex statement: first to kill the individual cohomology modules locally, then to produce a localizing element on which the amplitude condition holds.

items.title: Two bounded finitely projective representatives of one perfect object agree after localization up to trivial summands
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a prime p, and bounded complexes M^bullet and N^bullet of finite projective R-modules representing the same object of D(R), and asserts that there is f not in p and an isomorphism of complexes M^bullet_f oplus P^bullet = N^bullet_f oplus Q^bullet, where P^bullet and Q^bullet are finite direct sums of trivial complexes of the form ... -> 0 -> R_f -> R_f -> 0 -> ... placed in arbitrary degrees (source lines 19627-19641). The proof first localizes: if an isomorphism of the described type exists over R_p, then since R_p = colim R_f one can descend it to R_f for some f (proof lines 19644-19647). This reduces to the case where R is local and p is the maximal ideal (proof lines 19648-19648). In that case the result follows from the uniqueness of a minimal complex representing a perfect object, quoted as the lifting-from-the-residue-field statement, together with the fact that any complex is a direct sum of a trivial complex and a minimal one, quoted from the Algebra chapter (proof lines 19649-19653). The non-routine content is entirely in the reduction step: the localization argument converts a statement invoked at a prime into an isomorphism that exists on a Zariski neighbourhood, and the local case itself is delegated to the minimal-complex uniqueness theorem.

items.title: A derived complete module whose reduction modulo the ideal is finite is the completion of a finite module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Let I be an ideal of a Noetherian ring A and M a derived complete A-module. The lemma asserts that if M/IM is a finite A/I-module then M = lim M/I^nM and M is a finite A^wedge-module (source lines 27291-27297). The proof picks x_1, ..., x_t in M mapping to generators of M/IM and obtains a map A^{oplus t} -> M sending the i-th basis vector to x_i (proof lines 27300-27302). By the Noetherian proposition on naive completion, the derived completion of A is A^wedge = lim A/I^n (proof lines 27302-27305). Because M is derived complete, the map factors through a map q : (A^wedge)^{oplus t} -> M (proof lines 27305-27306). The cokernel Coker(q) is zero by the statement that a derived complete module annihilated by I is zero (proof lines 27307-27308), so M is a finite A^wedge-module (proof line 27309). Finally, since A^wedge is Noetherian and complete with respect to IA^wedge, it follows that M is I-adically complete, quoting three results from the Algebra chapter on completion of Noetherian rings, finite modules over complete rings and Artin-Rees (proof lines 27310-27314). The non-routine content is the factorization of the generator map through the completion, which is what converts a statement about M/IM into a statement about finite generation over the completion.

items.title: A derived complete module annihilated by a finitely generated ideal is zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finitely generated ideal I of a ring A and a derived complete A-module M, and asserts that if M/IM = 0 then M = 0 (source lines 26099-26104). The proof is a reduction to a single element. Write I = (f_1, ..., f_r) and let i < r be the largest integer such that N = M/(f_1, ..., f_i)M is nonzero; if no such i exists then M = 0 and the proof is done (proof lines 26107-26110). Then N is derived complete, being a cokernel of a map between derived complete modules, quoting the statement that the derived complete modules form a Serre subcategory (proof lines 26110-26112). By the choice of i, the map f_{i+1} : N -> N is surjective, so the inverse limit of the constant system (... -> N -> N -> N) is nonzero, contradicting the derived completeness of N (proof lines 26113-26118). The non-routine content is the choice of the maximal index at which the partial quotient survives: it converts the vanishing of M/IM into the surjectivity of a single multiplication map, whose derived limit is then forced to be nonzero.

items.title: Derived completion of a complex with finite cohomology computes the adic completions of its cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Let A be a Noetherian ring and I an ideal. The lemma takes an object K of D(A) whose cohomology modules H^n(K) are finite for all n, and asserts that the cohomology modules H^n(K^wedge) of the derived completion are the I-adic completions of the cohomology modules H^n(K) (source lines 27265-27272). The proof works by truncation. For every m the complex tau_{<= m}K is pseudo-coherent by the Noetherian pseudo-coherence statement, hence represented by a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite free A-modules (proof lines 27275-27278). Then tau_{<= m}K tensor^L_A A/I^n = P^bullet/I^nP^bullet, so the derived completion of tau_{<= m}K is R lim P^bullet/I^nP^bullet, by the Noetherian naive-completion proposition (proof lines 27279-27281). Since that R lim is computed termwise by the computation statement, and since I-adic completion is exact on finite A-modules by the Algebra flatness statement, the result holds for tau_{<= m}K (proof lines 27282-27286). The result for K then follows because derived completion has finite cohomological dimension (proof lines 27286-27288). The non-routine content is the reduction to bounded-above truncations: it converts a statement about an arbitrary K into a statement about a bounded above complex of finite free modules, where the termwise R lim and exactness of completion can be applied.

primary.label: author Lemma environment, source label lemma-derived-completion-pseudo-coherent (statement, source lines 27265-27272)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma (source lines 27274-27289)

items.title: Derived completion commutes with tensoring by a finite module or a pseudo-coherent complex
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Let I be an ideal in a Noetherian ring A and let ^ denote derived completion with respect to I. The lemma takes K in D^-(A) and asserts two identities: (K tensor^L_A M)^ = K^ tensor^L_A M for a finite A-module M, and (K tensor^L_A L)^ = K^ tensor^L_A L for a pseudo-coherent L in D(A) (source lines 27346-27357). The proof proves (2) and derives (1) as its special case. Represent K by a bounded above complex P^bullet of free A-modules and L by a bounded above complex F^bullet of finite free A-modules (proof lines 27360-27363). Since Tot(P^bullet tensor_A F^bullet) represents K tensor^L_A L, the derived completion (K tensor^L_A L)^ is represented by Tot((P^bullet)^ tensor_A F^bullet), where (P^bullet)^ is the complex whose terms are the ordinary i.e. derived completions (P^n)^, quoting the Noetherian naive-completion proposition and the statement on when derived completion is completion (proof lines 27364-27373). Part (1) is then a special case of (2) (proof line 27374). The non-routine content is the passage from the derived completion of a total complex to the total complex of the completed free resolution: it is what allows the completion to be moved inside the tensor product, at the cost of requiring libreeness of the representing complex and finite freeness of the second factor.

items.title: Free cohomology makes the eta ideals principal, generated by powers of the nonzerodivisor
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, a prime p, a nonzerodivisor f, and a bounded complex M^bullet of finite free A-modules, and assumes that H^i(M^bullet)_p is free for all i; it concludes that I_i(M^bullet, f)_p is a principal ideal, in fact generated by a power of f, for all i (source lines 28026-28033). The proof reduces along two axes. First, by the base change statement one may assume A is local with maximal ideal p (proof lines 28036-28037). Second, by the well-definedness statement one may replace M^bullet by a quasi-isomorphic complex (proof lines 28037-28038). The key step uses the freeness hypothesis: by the freeness of the cohomology modules, M^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to the complex whose term in degree i is H^i(M^bullet) with vanishing differentials, quoting the Derived Categories statement (proof lines 28039-28043). In other words one may assume all differentials in M^bullet vanish (proof lines 28044-28045). With vanishing differentials it is clear that I_i(M^bullet, f) = (f^{r_i}) is principal, completing the proof (proof lines 28045-28046). The non-routine content is the recognition that free cohomology over a local ring splits the complex into its cohomology modules, after which the invariants are visibly principal.

items.title: Finiteness of a module descends along a ring map inducing isomorphisms on quotients by powers of an element
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an element f, and a ring map R -> R' inducing isomorphisms R/f^nR -> R'/f^nR' for n > 0, and asserts that an R-module M is finitely generated if and only if the (R' oplus R_f)-module M tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) is finitely generated; a special case with the completion is recorded as an example (source lines 25189-25201). The proof begins by noting that the 'only if' direction is clear, so it assumes M tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) is finitely generated (proof line 25204-25205). The substantive step is a manipulation of generators: writing each generator as a sum of simple tensors, the module M tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) admits a finite generating set consisting of elements of M (proof lines 25205-25208). That is, there is a morphism from a finite free R-module to M whose cokernel is killed by tensoring with R' oplus R_f; applying the Beauville-Laszlo faithful statement to this cokernel gives that M is finitely generated (proof lines 25209-25212). The final sentence observes that the completion example is a special case of the first statement by the same-quotients statement (proof lines 25213-25214). The non-routine content is the observation that the generating set can be chosen inside M itself, which turns the hypothesis into a statement about the cokernel of a finite free presentation of M.

items.title: Relative finite presentation is insensitive to a finite map of finite type algebras
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a finite map A -> B of finite type R-algebras, and a B-module M, and asserts that M is an A-module finitely presented relative to R if and only if it is a B-module finitely presented relative to R (source lines 20979-20986). The proof is a presentation argument. It chooses a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and elements y_1, ..., y_m of B generating B over A (proof lines 20989-20990). Since A -> B is finite, each y_i satisfies a monic equation with coefficients in A, so there are monic polynomials P_j(T) in R[x_1, ..., x_n][T] with P_j(y_j) = 0 in B (proof lines 20991-20993). The proof then exhibits the commutative square from R[x_1, ..., x_n] to R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m]/(P_j(y_j)) over A -> B (proof lines 20994-21001). Since the top arrow is a finite and finitely presented ring map, the conclusion follows from the Algebra statement on finite finitely presented extensions together with the definition of relative finite presentation (proof lines 21002-21005). The non-routine content is the construction of a presentation of B over a polynomial ring by killing monic equations, which is what makes the top arrow finitely presented as well as finite.

items.title: A flat ring map of finite presentation is perfect
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts in one line that a ring map which is flat and of finite presentation is perfect (source lines 21814-21817). The proof is a Noetherian-approximation argument. Let A -> B be flat and of finite presentation; it is clear that B has finite tor dimension (proof lines 21820-21821). By the Algebra approximation statement there exists a finite type Z-algebra A_0 contained in A and a flat finite type ring map A_0 -> B_0 such that B = B_0 tensor_{A_0} A (proof lines 21821-21825). By the Noetherian relative pseudo-coherence statement, A_0 -> B_0 is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 21825-21827). Since A_0 -> B_0 is flat, B_0 and A are tor independent over A_0, so the base change statement for relative pseudo-coherence applies and gives that A -> B is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 21828-21831). Together with finite tor dimension this is perfectness. The non-routine content is the reduction to the Noetherian case: every flat finitely presented map is a base change of a flat finite type map of finite type Z-algebras, and pseudo-coherence descends along tor independent base change.

items.title: Formal smoothness of an extension of discrete valuation rings is inherited by finite extensions of the fraction field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A -> B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L, assumes A -> B formally smooth in the m_B-adic topology, and asserts that for any finite extension K_1/K, with L_1 = L tensor_K K_1, B_1 = B tensor_A A_1, and the extensions (A_1)_{m_i} in (B_1)_{m_ij} of the construction remark, each such extension is formally smooth in the m_ij-adic topology (source lines 34005-34014). The proof works through the equivalence of the formally smooth characterisation for extensions of discrete valuation rings, used without further mention (proof lines 34016-34017). Let pi in A and pi_i in (A_1)_{m_i} be uniformizers. Because kappa_A in kappa_B is separable, the ring (B tensor_A (A_1)_{m_i}) / pi_i (B tensor_A (A_1)_{m_i}), rewritten as B/piB tensor_{A/piA} (A_1)_{m_i}/pi_i(A_1)_{m_i}, is a product of fields each separable over kappa_{m_i} (proof lines 34018-34024). Hence pi_i is a nonzerodivisor in B tensor_A (A_1)_{m_i} and the quotient by it is a product of fields (proof lines 34025-34026). It follows that B tensor_A A_1 is a Dedekind domain, in particular reduced, so the inclusion B tensor_A A_1 in B_1 is an equality, which is what was to be shown (proof lines 34027-34028). The non-routine content is the rewriting of the residue ring as a tensor product of residue fields and the use of separability of the residue extension to read off the nonzerodivisor property; the final step is the identification of B_1 with the tensor product via the Dedekind property.

items.title: The ideal of divisible elements in a derived complete ring is nilpotent with an explicit bound
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A derived complete with respect to an ideal I, sets J equal to the intersection of the ideals I^n, and asserts that if I can be generated by r elements then J^N = 0 where N = 2^r (source lines 27106-27111). The proof is an induction on the number of generators. The case r = 1 is the square-zero statement (proof line 27114). For r > 1 write I = (f_1, ..., f_r); by the Serre subcategory statement the ring A_t = A/f_r^t A is derived complete with respect to I, hence a fortiori derived complete with respect to I_t = (f_1, ..., f_{r-1})A_t (proof lines 27115-27119). The map A -> A_t sends J into J_t = intersection of the ideals I_t^n (proof lines 27119-27120). By induction on r one has J_t^{N/2} = 0, where N = 2^r (proof lines 27120-27121). Finally the ideal given by the intersection of the kernels of A -> A_t, which is the intersection of the ideals f_r^t A, has square zero by the case r = 1, which finishes the proof (proof lines 27121-27122). The non-routine content is the doubling bookkeeping: the induction gives the exponent 2^{r-1} on the quotient, the square-zero statement contributes exponent 2 on the kernel, and the product of the two exponents is 2^r. The proof is terse and does not spell out the filtration argument combining J_t^{N/2} = 0 with the square-zero statement.

items.title: The kernel of the map to the f-adic completion of a derived complete module has square-zero intersection with the ideal of divisible elements
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an element f of a ring A, sets J equal to the intersection of the ideals f^nA, and lets M be an A-module derived complete with respect to f; it asserts that JM' = 0, where M' is the kernel of M -> lim M/f^nM, and in particular that if A is derived complete then J is an ideal of square zero (source lines 27066-27072). The proof is a direct element chase. Take x in M' and g in J; for every n >= 1 one may write x = f^n x_n, and since g lies in f^nA the element y_n = g x_n of M' is independent of the choice of x_n (proof lines 27075-27077). One may therefore take x_n = f x_{n+1}, which yields y_n = f y_{n+1}; this compatible system defines a map A_f -> M sending 1/f^n to y_n (proof lines 27078-27079). The author then invokes the derived completeness of M in the form of the statement that there are no maps from A_f to a derived complete module, so that this map must be zero and hence every y_n vanishes (proof lines 27080-27081). Finally gx = g f x_1 = f y_1 = 0, completing the proof (proof lines 27082-27083). The non-routine content is the construction of the compatible family y_n and the recognition that the derived completeness of M forces the resulting localization map to vanish.

items.title: The cotangent complex of a local complete intersection is perfect with tor amplitude in degrees minus one and zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a local complete intersection A -> B in the sense of the local complete intersection definition and asserts that the naive cotangent complex NL_{B/A} is a perfect object of D(B) with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] (source lines 22855-22861). The proof exhibits the standard two-term presentation: write B = A[x_1, ..., x_n]/I, so that NL_{B/A} is represented by the complex I/I^2 -> bigoplus B dx_i with I/I^2 in degree -1 (proof lines 22864-22869). Since the degree 0 term is finite free, the amplitude statement is equivalent to flatness of I/I^2 as a B-module, by the lemma on the last term being flat (proof lines 22869-22872). By definition I is a Koszul regular ideal and hence quasi-regular (proof lines 22872-22873). It follows from the quasi-regular ideal statement that I/I^2 is a finite projective B-module, so NL_{B/A} is both perfect and of tor amplitude in [-1, 0] (proof lines 22874-22877). The non-routine content is the reduction of the amplitude question to flatness of the conormal module via the freeness of the degree 0 term, and the conversion of quasi-regularity into finite projectivity of I/I^2.
