items.title: A bounded-above finitely projective complex over a henselian quotient lifts to the ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an ideal I, a complex E^bullet of R/I-modules, and an object K of D(R), under four hypotheses: E^bullet is a bounded above complex of finite projective R/I-modules; K tensor^L_R R/I is represented by E^bullet in D(R/I); K is pseudo-coherent; and (R, I) is a henselian pair. It concludes that there is a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite projective R-modules representing K in D(R) with P^bullet tensor_R R/I isomorphic to E^bullet, and moreover that P^i is free wherever E^i is (source lines 19656-19669). The proof applies the general lifting lemma for complexes with respect to the class of all finite projective R-modules (proof lines 19671-19674). Its five hypotheses are checked in turn: properties (1) and (2) are immediate; property (3) follows from Nakayama's lemma; property (4) follows from the liftability of finite projective modules over a henselian pair; and property (5) holds because a pseudo-coherent complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free R-modules (proof lines 19674-19682). The general lemma then produces P^bullet, and the final freeness assertion follows from the statement on isomorphism classes of finite projective lifts (proof lines 19682-19684). The non-routine content is entirely in the verification that the class of finite projective modules satisfies the five hypotheses of the abstract lifting lemma, with Nakayama and henselian lifting doing the substantive work.

items.title: Every algebra over a field contains a maximal weakly etale subalgebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a field K and a K-algebra A and asserts the existence of a maximal weakly etale K-subalgebra B_max of A (source lines 30891-30895). The proof is a directed-colimit argument. Given two weakly etale K-subalgebras B_1, B_2 of A, the tensor product B_1 tensor_K B_2 is weakly etale over K by the class statement, and so is the image of B_1 tensor_K B_2 -> A, again by the class statement which is closed under quotients (proof lines 30898-30901). Hence the collection of weakly etale K-subalgebras of A is directed (proof lines 30902-30903). Taking the colimit B_max over this directed collection, the characterization statement shows that a filtered colimit of weakly etale algebras is weakly etale, so B_max is weakly etale over K (proof lines 30903-30905). The image of B_max -> A is then weakly etale over K by the preceding lemma (proof lines 30906-30907). It follows that this image belongs to the collection and hence the collection has a maximal element, which is the image and equals B_max (proof lines 30908-30909). The non-routine content is the recognition that the union-of-two-subalgebras operation, which is what directedness requires, is supplied by tensoring over K and taking the image in A.

items.title: For a Noetherian ring the naive completion functor is left adjoint to the inclusion of derived complete objects
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Let A be a Noetherian ring and I an ideal. The proposition asserts that the functor sending K in D(A) to the derived limit K' = R lim(K tensor^L_A A/I^n) is the left adjoint to the inclusion functor D_comp(A) -> D(A) constructed in the derived completion statement (source lines 27217-27224). The proof reduces the naive completion along a different presentation of the ideal to the Koszul presentation. Write I = (f_1, ..., f_r) and let K_n^bullet be the Koszul complex with respect to f_1^n, ..., f_r^n (proof lines 27227-27228). By the derived completion Koszul statement it suffices to prove the displayed three-term chain of equalities identifying R lim(K tensor^L_A K_n^bullet) with both R lim(K tensor^L_A A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)) and R lim(K tensor^L_A A/I^n) (proof lines 27229-27235). By the sequence of Koszul complexes statement the pro-objects {K_n^bullet} and {A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)} in D(A) are isomorphic, and the pro-objects {A/(f_1^n, ..., f_r^n)} and {A/I^n} are visibly isomorphic (proof lines 27236-27239). The map from left to right is therefore an isomorphism by the statement on tensor products and R lim respecting pro-isomorphisms (proof lines 27240-27241). The non-routine content is the choice of presentation: replacing the naive system A/I^n by the Koszul system K_n^bullet puts the computation in the framework of the Koszul-derived completion statement, and the two pro-isomorphism statements then transport the adjunction.

items.title: Perfect modules are exactly the modules with a finite projective resolution
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a module M over a ring R and proves the equivalence of two conditions: M is a perfect module, and there exists a resolution 0 -> F_d -> ... -> F_1 -> F_0 -> M -> 0 with each F_i finite projective (source lines 18916-18927). Part of the proof is immediate: assuming (2), the complex E^bullet with E^{-i} = F_i is quasi-isomorphic to M[0], hence M is perfect (proof lines 18930-18931). The substantive direction is (1) implies (2). By the perfect-complex statement and the statement on pseudo-coherence of modules, one can find a resolution E^bullet -> M with each E^{-i} finite free (proof lines 18932-18935). By the last-term-flat statement, the cokernel F_d = Coker(E^{d-1} -> E^d) is flat for d sufficiently large (proof lines 18936-18938). The Algebra statement on finitely presented flat modules then gives that F_d is finite projective (proof lines 18938-18940). The desired resolution is then the truncated one 0 -> F_d -> E^{-d+1} -> ... -> E^0 -> M -> 0 (proof lines 18941-18945). The non-routine content is the choice of d large enough that the cokernel becomes flat, which converts a possibly infinite free resolution into a finite projective one.

items.title: Perfect complexes are exactly the pseudo-coherent complexes of finite tor dimension, with a bounded projective model
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an object K^bullet of D(R) and proves the equivalence of two conditions — K^bullet is perfect if and only if it is pseudo-coherent and has finite tor dimension — and further asserts that when these hold and K^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b], then K^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to a complex E^bullet of finite projective R-modules with E^i = 0 for i outside [a, b] (source lines 18888-18899). The proof notes that (1) implies (2) is clear, quoting the pseudo-coherence and tor-amplitude statements (proof lines 18902-18903). Hence assume (2) and tor amplitude in [a, b]; in particular H^i(K^bullet) = 0 for i > b (proof lines 18904-18905). Choose a complex F^bullet of finite free R-modules with F^i = 0 for i > b and a quasi-isomorphism F^bullet -> K^bullet (proof lines 18906-18908). Set E^bullet = tau_{>=a}F^bullet, so that E^i is finite free except at E^a, which is a finitely presented R-module (proof lines 18909-18910). By the last-term-flat statement E^a is flat, and by the Algebra statement on finitely presented flat modules E^a is finite projective (proof lines 18911-18913). The non-routine content is the cohomological bound H^i = 0 for i > b, which allows a bounded-above finite free model to be chosen, and the truncation at a, which isolates the single term E^a whose projectivity follows from flatness plus finite presentation.

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma (source lines 18901-18914)

items.title: The Picard group of a localization of a regular local ring is trivial
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a regular local ring R and an element f, and asserts that Pic(R_f) = 0 (source lines 36779-36783). The proof is a K-theoretic argument. Let L be an invertible R_f-module; in particular L is a finite R_f-module, so there is a finite R-module M with M_f isomorphic to L, quoting the Algebra statement on constructing finitely presented modules realizing a given localization (proof lines 36786-36789). By the Algebra proposition on the finite global dimension of a regular local ring, M has a finite free resolution F_bullet over R (proof lines 36790-36791). It follows that L is quasi-isomorphic to a finite complex of free R_f-modules (proof lines 36792-36793). Hence by the statement relating perfect complexes to the K-group, [L_f] = n[R_f] in K_0(R_f) for some integer n (proof lines 36793-36795). Applying the determinant map then shows that L is trivial, which is the conclusion (proof lines 36796-36797). The non-routine content is the route: a line bundle on R_f is realized by a finite module over R, finite global dimension of the regular local ring gives a finite free resolution, and the resulting vanishing in the reduced K_0 together with the determinant map forces triviality. Note that the author leaves the final determinant step to be read off from the cited map.

items.title: Tameness of a finite separable extension of a discrete valuation ring passes to intermediate subextensions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K and finite separable extensions M/L/K, and asserts that if M is tamely ramified with respect to A then so is L (source lines 34159-34165). The proof proceeds by the standard integral-closure argument. Let C/B/A be the integral closures of A in M/L/K and use the discussion of the finite separable extension remark without further mention (proof lines 34167-34171). Since C is a finite ring extension of B, the map Spec(C) -> Spec(B) is surjective, so for every maximal ideal m of B there is a maximal ideal m' of C lying over it (proof lines 34172-34175). By multiplicativity of ramification indices and the hypothesis, the ramification index of B_m over A is prime to the residue characteristic (proof lines 34176-34179). Since kappa(m')/kappa_A is finite separable, the same holds for kappa(m)/kappa_A (proof lines 34180-34181). The non-routine content is the use of multiplicativity of ramification indices to transfer tameness downwards along the tower, together with the corresponding descent of the separability of the residue extension.

items.title: A flat injective epimorphism out of a ring of weak dimension at most one lands in an integral extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A of weak dimension at most one and a flat, injective epimorphism of rings A -> B, and asserts that A is integrally closed in B (source lines 30705-30710). The proof is a cancellation argument. Let x in B be integral over A and set A' = A[x], a subring of B; then A' is a finite ring extension of A by the Algebra characterization of finiteness in terms of integrality (proof lines 30713-30715). To show A = A' it suffices to show that A -> A' is an epimorphism, by the Algebra statement that a finite epimorphism is surjective (proof lines 30716-30717). The key input is that A' is flat over A, which follows from the hypothesis on A together with the flatness of B over A (proof lines 30718-30719). The proof then exhibits the composition A' tensor_A A' -> B tensor_A A' -> B tensor_A B -> B and concludes it is injective (proof lines 30720-30724), which says A' tensor_A A' is isomorphic to A' and hence A -> A' is an epimorphism, completing the proof (proof line 30724). The non-routine content is the flatness of the intermediate ring A' over A, which is what supplies the injectivity of the tensor product map, and the reduction of the integrality claim to the surjectivity of a finite epimorphism.

items.title: Weak dimension does not increase along a weakly etale ring map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a weakly etale ring map A -> B and asserts that if A has weak dimension at most d then so does B (source lines 30230-30234). The proof is a resolution argument split by the value of d. Let N be a B-module. If d = 0, then N is flat as an A-module, hence flat as a B-module by the key lemma (proof lines 30237-30238). Assume d > 0: choose a resolution F_bullet -> N by free B-modules (proof lines 30239-30240). The hypothesis on A implies that the image K of F_d -> F_{d-1} is A-flat, by the last-term-flat statement (proof lines 30240-30242). Hence K is B-flat by the key lemma (proof lines 30242-30243). Then 0 -> K -> F_{d-1} -> ... -> F_0 -> N -> 0 is a flat resolution of length d, so N has tor dimension at most d (proof lines 30244-30246). The non-routine content is the choice of the truncation point: the syzygy at position d is A-flat by the weak dimension hypothesis, and weak etaleness of A -> B, used through the key lemma, upgrades that A-flatness to B-flatness.

primary.label: author Lemma environment, source label lemma-weak-dimension-goes-up (statement, source lines 30230-30234)

items.title: Derived adic completion agrees with usual completion for finite modules tensored with a flat module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Let I be an ideal in a Noetherian ring A. The lemma asserts two things: if M is a finite A-module and N is a flat A-module, then the derived I-adic completion of M tensor_A N is the usual I-adic completion of M tensor_A N; and if M is finite and f in A, then the derived I-adic completion of M_f is the usual I-adic completion of M_f (source lines 27317-27328). The proof introduces the notation M^wedge for the derived completion and lim M/I^nM for the usual completion, and assumes M is finite (proof lines 27330-27332). The key input is that the system Tor^A_i(M, A/I^n) is pro-zero for i > 0 (proof lines 27333-27335). Since Tor_i^A(M tensor_A N, A/I^n) equals Tor_i^A(M, A/I^n) tensor_A N by flatness of N, the same pro-zero statement holds for the tensored system (proof lines 27336-27338). The computation statement for the Noetherian case then shows that R lim ((M tensor_A N) tensor^L_A A/I^n) has cohomology only in degree 0, given by the usual completion lim (M tensor_A N)/I^n(M tensor_A N), which proves (1) (proof lines 27339-27342). Part (2) follows from (1) and the identification M_f = M tensor_A A_f, using that A_f is flat (proof line 27343). The non-routine content is the transfer of the pro-zero property across the flat base change and the recognition that the degree-0 cohomology of the derived limit is exactly the usual completion.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies Cech cohomology with the right derived functors of Cech H-0 on the category of abelian presheaves and produces a functorial quasi-isomorphism between the Cech complex and the derived functor (statement lines 1188-1217). The proof is complete and has three parts: it first verifies that Cech cohomology of an injective presheaf vanishes in positive degrees through the exactness of the representable complex and of hom into an injective, which makes the Cech delta-functor effaceable and hence universal (proof lines 1228-1248); it then identifies it with the universal delta-functor of the right derived functors (proof lines 1250-1258); and finally it resolves the presheaf injectively and compares the two maps into the total complex of the resulting double complex, whose rows and columns are exact in positive degrees, obtaining the quasi-isomorphism of the statement (proof lines 1262-1301). The author marks the middle of the proof as skippable and omits only the functoriality verification at the end; both are retained verbatim inside the counted span.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a morphism of ringed topoi whose source has enough points, the pullback of a K-flat complex is K-flat (statement lines 3833-3839). The non-formal content is the reduction to points. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one computation at a point.

items.title: Finite locally constant sheaves on a connected scheme are finite representations of the etale fundamental group
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies finite locally constant sheaves of Lambda-modules on a connected scheme with finite Lambda-modules carrying a continuous action of the etale fundamental group (statement lines 10117-10168, a long statement with two displayed categories). items.title: The descent lemma: tensoring the equalizer diagram by a universally injective map keeps it an equalizer

The proof is an explicit diagram chase of real substance: the author first splits the map C(N tensor_R S) to C(N) functorially in N, which produces the upper vertical arrows of a three-by-three commutative diagram whose column composites are identities, then reads off a dashed arrow because the second row is a coequalizer diagram, and deduces from the top right square that the first row is a split coequalizer (proof lines 1448-1479). The claim is H3: the split-coequalizer bookkeeping across a three-by-three diagram together with the functorial splitting and the adjunction step is an original assembly, not a citation chain.

items.difficulty_reason: For a surjective finite etale morphism X to Y with a group G acting compatibly, the lemma identifies quasi-coherent modules on Y with systems consisting of a quasi-coherent module on X together with isomorphisms to its pullbacks along the group elements satisfying the cocycle relation (statement lines 2067-2080). The proof reduces the statement to ordinary descent: the morphism is an fpqc covering, the maps from G times X to the double fibre product and from the triple product of G with X to the triple fibre product are isomorphisms, and using those identifications the systems of the lemma are recognized as exactly the descent data for that covering (proof lines 2083-2091). The general fpqc descent theorem for quasi-coherent modules then gives the equivalence (proof lines 2092-2093). The claim is H2: the reduction is a precise but standard translation between two descriptions of the same data, with the identifications written out.

items.title: Seven equivalent formulations of etale localness on the source-and-target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a property of morphisms of schemes which is etale local on the source-and-target, the lemma collects seven equivalent formulations: the property itself, the existence of etale local models, the pullback condition along every etale commutative square, the same for one surjective such square, the two etale-covering conditions on the target and on the source, and the two-step covering condition (statement lines 7468-7499). The proof pairs the formulations off: the first two are part of the definition, two more are parts (2) and (1) of the equivalence lemma, the two-step condition follows because the property is now known to be equivalent to both one-step conditions, and the remaining square condition is handled in both directions by applying clause (1) to transfer the property to the composite and clause (4) to descend it, with the surjectivity of the first component turning the single arrow into an etale covering for the converse (proof lines 7501-7524). The claim is H2: no new construction, but seven formulations must each be routed to the correct clause of the definition, and the route is written out for every one of them.

items.title: Cohomology of a module sheaf on the fppf site agrees with the cohomology of its small-site restriction
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a sheaf of modules G on the big fppf site of a scheme S which is quasi-coherent on the small site and invariant under pullback along flat locally finitely presented morphisms, the lemma shows that the cohomology of G on a flat locally finitely presented U agrees with the cohomology of its small-site restriction (statement lines 4056-4070). The proof is a comparison of two short exact sequences: the author pulls back the small-site restriction to the big site to get a quasi-coherent F together with a comparison map which is an isomorphism on every small site of a flat locally finitely presented morphism, by the two hypotheses, and therefore has parasitic kernel and cokernel for the fppf topology (proof lines 4072-4089). The parasitic cohomology lemma makes the comparison map an isomorphism on cohomology, and the known result for the quasi-coherent F finishes (proof lines 4089-4095). The claim is H2: the notion of parasitic sheaves and the reduction to the quasi-coherent case are both cited, but the construction of the comparison map and the check that its kernel and cokernel are parasitic are written out in the span.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a ring R and a morphism f: M to N of modules, the lemma shows that f is universally injective exactly when the induced map C(N) to C(M) is a split surjection (statement lines 1218-1222). The proof uses the adjunction identity to replace the induced map on Hom groups by the base changed map inside C, exhibiting a commutative square whose vertical arrows are isomorphisms (proof lines 1224-1233). The forward direction then reads surjectivity of the rows at P equal to C(M), which lets the identity of C(M) be lifted to a splitting of C(f); the converse uses surjectivity of the rows for arbitrary P together with faithfulness of C to conclude that every base change of f is injective (proof lines 1234-1242). The claim is H2: a short but complete argument whose content is the correct choice of the test object P and the two one-line transfers.

items.title: Eilenberg's swindle: a module whose sum with a nonfinitely generated free module is free is itself absorbed by that free module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is Eilenberg's swindle for modules over an arbitrary ring: if a module summed with a complement is a nonfinitely generated free module, then the module summed with that free module is isomorphic to the free module (statement lines 38970-38985). The proof is a displayed chain of isomorphisms in which the free module is first identified with a countable direct sum of copies of itself, the two summands are then interleaved inside that sum, and the result is regrouped as the module plus a copy of the free module (proof lines 38987-38993). The proof is deliberately brief, but it is a complete computation rather than an omission: the chain exhibits the required isomorphism, and no step is deferred. The counted statement contains the author's slogan, history and reference environments; the retained preamble defines all three as comment-type, so their bodies, including the two citations they carry, are discarded when the document is typeset, which is why the card needs no bibliography.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: 命题说：若有效 Cartier 除子 D_1,…,D_m 的交为空、且每个 L_i 限制到 X \ D_i 上 ample，则 X 有 ample family of invertible modules。证明的关键操作是「把局部截面延拓成整体截面」：先在补集上用 ample 性取到非零点集仿射的截面 s，再借 U_i 恰是 O_X(D_i) 典范截面的非零点集这一点，用延拓引理把 s 延拓为 L_i^{\otimes n} ⊗ O_X(N D_i) 的截面；最后把 N 增大 1，使新截面在 D_i 上消失而不改变非零点集。不能一眼完成的是最后这一步：扭动与消失必须同时成立，才能保证 X_{s'} = (U_i)_s 仍仿射。原文位于第 23360–23389 行。

items.difficulty_reason: Derived Chow 引理是 Chow 引理的导出版本：除几何部分（存在闭子空间 Z ⊂ X x_A P^n_A 与开 V，使 Z 在 V 上是闭浸入并给出 X 上的同构）之外，还要给出一个对象 E ∈ D(O_{X x_A P^n_A}) 满足所列性质。证明先把情形降到 Noetherian（用极限小节的有限展示与分离性下降），再用部分截面的概型论像构造 Z，最后取 E=(b,c)_*O_Z 并用伪凝聚判别引理验证。不能一眼完成的是导出部分：E 的选择与伪凝聚性必须与 Z、V 的几何构造配合。原文位于第 12012–12112 行。

items.title: Finiteness and finiteness of the quotient by the integral closure for a reduced one-dimensional Nagata local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the three properties of the integral closure A' of a reduced one-dimensional Nagata local ring A that make the delta-invariant well defined: A' is a normal Nagata ring, A -> A' is finite, and the quotient A'/A has finite length as an A-module. The finiteness of A -> A' is the Nagata hypothesis, and the length statement is obtained by choosing an element f of the maximal ideal satisfying the equivalent conditions of the preceding lemma, so that A_f equals A'_f; hence the support of the finite module A'/A is contained in the maximal ideal, and the module has finite length by the support-point lemma (proof lines 8301-8315). H2: the reduction of the length statement to the support of A'/A and the use of the element f are the substance, and the argument is short but complete.

items.title: Equivalent characterizations of an element of the maximal ideal that cuts out the maximal ideal up to radical
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section 'Geometrically connected schemes'
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of three conditions on an element f of the maximal ideal of a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring - that the maximal ideal is the radical of (f), that f lies in no minimal prime, and that A_f is the product of the localizations at the minimal primes - proves such an f exists, and, under the depth-one (for instance reduced) hypothesis, adds the equivalences with f being a nonzerodivisor and A_f being the total ring of fractions, and under reducedness further with A_f being the product of the residue fields at the minimal primes. The proof identifies the prime spectrum as the minimal primes together with the maximal ideal, derives the equivalence of (1) and (2) from the Zariski topology criterion, shows (2) implies (3) by describing Spec(A_f) as the finite discrete set of minimal primes and applying the dimension-zero structure theorem, and then treats the depth-one and reduced cases through associated primes and total rings of fractions (proof lines 8253-8291). H2: the assembly of these conditions is a real argument, with the identification of Spec(A_f) as the discrete set of minimal primes as its core.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a flat morphism with integral fibres from a locally Noetherian source onto a locally Noetherian integral normal base, an invertible module whose restriction to the generic fibre is trivial is the pullback of an invertible module on the base (statement lines 6967-6981). The counted proof is long and has three distinct layers: it produces a regular meromorphic section from a trivializing section of the generic fibre, defines the candidate module of meromorphic functions on the base and states the isomorphism claim, settles the affine case with a substantial symbolic-power computation over the normal base in which the product of the two ideals is shown to be principal so that both factors become invertible, and then glues over the target by comparing local generators along fibres, which is where the irreducibility of the fibres and the case hypothesis on the morphism are used to make the exceptional set closed (proof lines 6983-7090). It is H2: the argument is a complete author proof with real substance and the cited inputs are standard commutative algebra, but the author leaves 'some details omitted' in the glueing step, so no independent research-level claim is made.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)

The counted proof is long and organized by cases: it computes the ideal of the immersion explicitly in the case of an affine space over an affine base and proves that the associated conormal sequence splits, which reduces that case to a cited permanence statement; it then handles the H1-regular case by embedding the smooth total space regularly into an affine space, and the quasi-regular case by factoring the smooth morphism through an étale map to an affine space and identifying the graded pieces of the two ideals through formal étaleness (proof lines 5755-5846). items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the locus of points of the base-changed family whose fibre is geometrically reduced with the inverse image of the corresponding locus for the original family, for an arbitrary base change. items.title: Conormal algebras of the fibres induced by a formal local map are controlled by one finite type modification
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: This is the graded companion of the Artin approximation control step. Over a composable pair Y -> T -> S of finite type Noetherian schemes and a local O_{S,s}-algebra map sigma : O_{T,t} -> O_{S,s}^, the lemma produces a single finite type modification (T',t') -> (T,t) through which sigma factors, such that every other sigma' factoring through it induces closed immersions Y_sigma <- Y_t -> Y_sigma' with isomorphic conormal algebras. The proof has to compare two base changes of Y along two different formal maps that agree through the modification, then transport the conormal algebra across the comparison; the uniformity in sigma' is what carries the content, since a single modification must serve all competitors at once. The graded statement is not implied by the ungraded control lemma in any routine way, because conormal algebras of the two closed immersions, not just the maps, must match. Retained author proof at lines 11592-11718.

items.difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism to the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring, assuming every irreducible component of the total space dominates the base and the special fibre is reduced, the lemma proves that both the total space and the generic fibre are reduced. The proof uses properness and the dominance hypothesis to control the components, compares the special fibre with the total space through the local structure over the valuation ring, and concludes reducedness of the total space and hence of the generic fibre by restriction. Using properness to prevent components from being supported on the special fibre is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 7313-7339.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence between etaleness and the pair of conditions locally of finite presentation plus formally etale. items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes two properties of the category of etale neighbourhoods of a point: any two neighbourhoods admit a common refinement, and two morphisms inducing the same map on residue fields are equalised by a further etale neighbourhood. Constructing the equaliser from the residue-field condition is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 10172-10200.

items.difficulty_reason: The theorem compares two ways of testing flatness at a point of the support: flatness over the base together with flatness of the fibre module over the fibre of the intermediate morphism, versus flatness of the intermediate morphism at the image together with flatness of the module over it. The proof establishes the equivalence by reducing to the local situation and comparing the two associated graded pieces, and then shows the locus where the conditions hold is open in the support by exhibiting it as the complement of a closed condition on a finitely presented module. The comparison of the two flatness conditions together with the openness argument is the substance. Retained author proof at lines 4612-4655.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For locally finitely presented schemes over a locally Noetherian base whose local ring at the base point is a G-ring, the lemma approximates a local algebra map from the local ring of the target into the completion of the local ring of the source, modulo the N-th power of the maximal ideal, by an actual S-morphism from an elementary etale neighbourhood of the source. The proof reduces to the algebra statement about the two completions, produces the morphism through the approximation of the induced map, and then verifies the commutativity modulo the power by comparing the induced maps on completions. Realising the formal data by an honest morphism on an etale neighbourhood is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 11041-11068.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism over an irreducible base, if a closed subset is nowhere dense in the generic fibre then it is nowhere dense in every fibre over a nonempty open. The proof passes to the closure of the complement of the subset, spreads that closure to a neighbourhood using finite type and the irreducibility of the base, and then shows that the spread closure does not swallow any fibre over the open. Keeping the spread closure off the fibres is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 6532-6560.

items.difficulty_reason: For a finitely presented morphism, the level sets of the function counting geometric connected components of the fibres are locally constructible. items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a directed colimit of rings whose transition maps are faithfully flat, the lemma shows that the number of minimal primes of the colimit, as an element of the natural numbers with infinity, is the supremum of the numbers of minimal primes of the stages. The proof compares the minimal primes of the colimit with those of the stages using the faithful flatness of the transition maps, which lets minimal primes descend and ascend, and then takes the supremum. Descending minimal primes along faithfully flat maps is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 10311-10331.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma, attributed in the author's reference to SGA 1, proves that an unramified morphism with connected source, at least one component dominating the target, over an integral geometrically unibranch base, is etale and has irreducible source. The proof uses the unibranch hypothesis to control the local structure of the target, shows that every component of the source must dominate, and then concludes etaleness from unramifiedness plus flatness over the whole source. Using geometric unibranchness to force flatness is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 10510-10527.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma compares two topologies at the level of derived categories: under the covering and vanishing conditions for a family of objects, the given subcategory is a weak Serre subcategory of the modules on the finer site and the pullback and derived pushforward give an equivalence of triangulated categories (statement lines 6550-6570). The proof is a complete argument: the identification of the subcategory with its image and the quasi-inverse equivalences are established (proof lines 6574-6592); the vanishing of the positive higher direct images is deduced from the two assumptions through the description of those sheaves (proof lines 6594-6600); the image is shown to be a weak Serre subcategory by a comparison diagram and the five lemma (proof lines 6600-6652); and the five conditions of the comparison criterion are checked, yielding the equivalence (proof lines 6654-6666). The non-formal content is the verification of the weak Serre property and of the criterion. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-cohomology.tex (Cohomology on Sites), section Cech cohomology of presheaves
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file sites-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the two notions of derived limit available for a complex on a product site: the derived functor of the limit and the homotopy limit of the inverse system of its pullbacks to the terms (statement lines 5066-5075). The proof is a complete computation: after choosing a K-injective representative with injective terms the derived limit is computed termwise (proof lines 5078-5088); surjectivity of the transition maps is deduced from the fact that the structure morphisms are monomorphisms (proof lines 5091-5098); and exactness of the left adjoints together with the identification of products with derived products exhibits the derived limit as the homotopy limit (proof lines 5101-5122). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two limit notions. The claim is H2: a computation whose inputs are named and whose steps are written out.

The non-formal content is the passage from a trivialized comparison to a descent datum through the cohomological obstruction. The claim is H2: a structured descent argument with every input named.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves whose colimit is constructible is essentially constant, in the three settings of sheaves of sets, abelian sheaves and modules over a Noetherian ring (statement lines 11902-11919). items.title: The stalk at a geometric point gives an equivalence from abelian sheaves on the etale site of a field to modules over the absolute Galois group
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for S = Spec(K) with K a field and a geometric point fixed, the stalk functor is an equivalence between abelian sheaves on S_etale and modules over the absolute Galois group (statement lines 9077-9088). The proof is a short but complete formal transport: the equivalence between sheaves of sets and Galois sets is already available (proof lines 9091-9093), and the author explains that an abelian sheaf is precisely a sheaf of sets with a commutative group law while a Galois module is precisely a Galois set with a commutative group law, so the equivalence restricts (proof lines 9094-9096). The non-formal content is the recognition that both sides are categories of commutative group objects. The claim is H1: a one-step formal transport whose reason is written out.

items.title: Morphisms of locally ringed topoi on small etale topoi come from morphisms of schemes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem is the fully faithfulness statement that the construction sending a scheme to its small etale topos with structure sheaf is fully faithful: every morphism of locally ringed topoi comes from a unique morphism of schemes, up to a 2-isomorphism (statement lines 5552-5571). The proof is a long gluing argument: the author first treats the case of an affine target, composing with localization morphisms and applying the affine case over an affine open covering of the source (proof lines 5584-5620); then covers the target by affine opens and observes that the local morphisms agree on overlaps by rigidity, producing a global morphism of schemes (proof lines 5620-5688); finally the 2-isomorphisms are glued by the same rigidity and uniqueness is recorded (proof lines 5688-5693). The non-formal content is the gluing both of the morphisms and of the 2-isomorphisms. The claim is H2: a structured construction carried out in two stages with the rigidity input named.

items.difficulty_reason: The proposition treats the pushforward along a morphism that is integral and universally injective: on sheaves of sets it is fully faithful with essential image described by the complement of the image, and on abelian sheaves it is fully faithful with essential image the sheaves supported in the image, the inverse image being a left inverse in both cases (statement lines 6764-6791). The proof is a complete reduction: the author factors f into an integral, universally injective surjective morphism followed by a closed immersion (proof lines 6793-6801) and then applies the established closed immersion proposition to the second factor and topological invariance to the first (proof lines 6802-6806). items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the pushforward along a finite etale morphism of schemes preserves (finite) locally constant sheaves of sets, and likewise of abelian groups and of Lambda-modules, on the small etale sites (statement lines 9972-9980). The proof is short but genuine: the author first removes the geometry by observing that f_* commutes with etale localization, and that a finite etale morphism is etale locally a disjoint union of isomorphisms (proof lines 9983-9986), which reduces the assertion to the statement that a finite product of locally constant sheaves is locally constant; the author states that reduced assertion and closes it directly (proof lines 9987-9990), the other two categories being the same argument. items.title: The comparison morphism from the etale site to the Zariski site is flat
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the morphism of ringed sites from the small etale site of S to the small Zariski site of S is flat (statement lines 3220-3224). Flateness here is a statement about the structure sheaf of the etale site viewed as a module over the pullback of the Zariski structure sheaf, so the proof must first identify that pullback: using that etale morphisms are open, it computes it as the sheafification of the presheaf sending an etale V over S to the sections of the Zariski structure sheaf over the image of V (proof lines 3227-3236). It then checks flatness on the members of a suitable covering of each etale V: if both V and its image are affine, the map corresponds to an etale ring map, and etale ring maps are flat, so the comparison map between the two structure sheaves is flat there (proof lines 3237-3242). The remaining point is that every etale V does admit an affine open cover by pieces whose images are affine open in S, which the author proves in a footnote by intersecting with a suitable affine and taking a fibre product; flatness then descends from the covering by the sheafification-and-refinement criterion (proof lines 3243-3252). The claim is H2: three separate verifications are needed, the computation of the pullback sheaf, the flatness of the affine case through the corresponding ring map, and the affineness of the covering used to globalise, and all three are carried out rather than cited.

items.title: Descent along a faithfully flat ring map of finite type, finite presentation, formal unramifiedness, unramifiedness and etaleness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem states that if the S-algebra A tensor over R with S is of finite type, of finite presentation, formally unramified, unramified or etale, then the corresponding property holds for A as an R-algebra, with the converse being the easy direction (statement lines 1662-1678). The proof is not one argument but a sequence of independent ones. Part (a) chooses a finite system of generators of the base changed algebra, writes each as a finite sum of decomposable tensors, builds the polynomial R-algebra on the resulting variables together with the evident map to A, and concludes that the cokernel vanishes because it vanishes after tensoring with the faithfully flat S (proof lines 1681-1687). Part (b) is the substantive one: finite type over R is taken from part (a), a surjection from a polynomial algebra onto A is chosen, finite generation of the kernel after base change is obtained from an Algebra lemma, generators are lifted from the base changed kernel back to the kernel itself, and the quotient by the ideal they generate is a finitely presented R-algebra which becomes isomorphic to A after base change and therefore already is A (proof lines 1690-1703). Part (c) identifies the module of relative differentials of the base changed algebra with the base change of the module of relative differentials of A, and descends the vanishing (proof lines 1706-1711). Parts (d) and (e) are deductions from (a) and (c) together with the standard criteria for unramifiedness and etaleness (proof lines 1714-1717 and 1720-1724). The claim is H3: at least three of the five items are independent arguments rather than steps of one, and part (b) additionally requires the lifting construction for finite presentation together with the external algebra criterion that finite generation of a kernel can be checked after faithfully flat base change, which is precisely the extra criterion that separates this from a routine derivation.

items.title: Functoriality of the equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on a scheme and on its big and small sites
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes f : T to S the proposition has three parts: the equivalences of categories identifying quasi-coherent modules on S with those on the big and small sites are compatible with pullback, in the sense that pulling back the sheaf associated to a quasi-coherent module is the sheaf associated to the pulled back module; the corresponding compatibility with pushforward fails, and not even the statement can be made precise in general; and when f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and the topology is Zariski or etale, pushforward of quasi-coherent modules along f and along the induced morphism of small sites stays quasi-coherent and the square comparing pushforward with the association F to F^a commutes (statement lines 3108-3135). The claim is H3 for two reasons. First, part (2) is carried by an explicit counterexample, the quasi-compact open immersion of the punctured plane into the plane, where the pushforward of the structure sheaf of the punctured plane is the structure sheaf of the plane but becomes zero after base change to the origin; the author also explains why no precise statement is available, namely that compatibility over the big sites would force pushforward to commute with arbitrary base change (proof lines 3140-3150). Second, part (3) is a separate argument that turns the asserted equality of sheaves into a statement about sections over an etale morphism into S and identifies the two sides by flat base change (proof lines 3153-3161). What keeps this below a routine derivation is precisely that a counterexample has to be exhibited for one part and a flat base change identification carried out for another.

items.title: Properties of the functor from quasi-coherent modules to modules on a big or small site
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a topology tau among Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic and fppf, the lemma collects ten properties of the functors sending a quasi-coherent module to the associated module on the big and on the small tau-site: full faithfulness, commutation with direct sums and colimits, right exactness, exactness for the small etale site, failure of exactness for the big site in general, compatibility with tensor products, compatibility with internal hom for etale and Zariski in the small case, failure of that compatibility in the big case, and quasi-coherence of the middle term of a short exact sequence between associated modules (statement lines 3255-3307). The proof is a genuine assembly: colimit compatibility comes from recognizing the construction as a pullback of ringed sites, left exactness for the small etale site from flatness of etale morphisms, and the two failures are established by explicit counterexamples over the spectrum of the integers, where multiplication by two is injective but not so on the big site, and where the internal hom of a cokernel is a nonzero torsion sheaf on one side and zero on the other (proof lines 3309-3375). The most substantial part is the last one, which reduces to affine opens, uses the vanishing of the first cohomology of the associated module to get right exactness on the small site, and then proves universal injectivity of the map on sections by testing against square-zero algebras (proof lines 3377-3423). The claim is H3: two independent counterexample constructions and a genuinely original reduction in the last part, none of which is a citation chain.

items.title: Finite type descends along a surjective flat open morphism of locally ringed spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a morphism of locally ringed spaces that is open on underlying spaces and surjective and flat, a sheaf of modules on the target is of finite type as soon as its pullback is (statement lines 2126-2137). The proof is a stalkwise argument carried out with explicit bookkeeping. It chooses a point of the target and a preimage, picks finitely many sections generating the pullback over an open neighbourhood of that preimage, and then uses the description of the pullback as a tensor product of the inverse image sheaf with the structure sheaf to rewrite those generators as finite sums of tensors (proof lines 2140-2146); after shrinking it may assume the inverse image sections come from sections of the original sheaf over an open set of the target, which produces a map from a finite direct sum of the structure sheaf to the original sheaf (proof lines 2147-2153). The pullback of that map is surjective by construction, and the substance of the argument is the step from surjectivity after tensoring with the stalk of the structure sheaf to surjectivity of the original stalk map, which uses that the local ring map is flat and hence faithfully flat (proof lines 2154-2164). Openness of the morphism then promotes the neighbourhood on which the generators live back to a neighbourhood of the chosen point of the target (proof lines 2165-2166). The claim is H2: the tensor rewriting is bookkeeping, but the faithfully flat descent of the surjectivity of a stalk map is the real step, and it is displayed rather than cited.

items.title: Effectivity and full faithfulness of fpqc descent for quasi-coherent sheaves
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an fpqc covering of a scheme, the proposition asserts that every descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves is effective and that the comparison functor from quasi-coherent modules to descent data is fully faithful (statement lines 1800-1810). The proof is a three-part argument. It begins by reducing to coverings that are standard affine over the members of an affine open covering of the base, exhibiting for each member a standard affine covering refining the given one (proof lines 1812-1835). Faithfulness is then a stalkwise argument using faithful flatness of the local ring maps induced by the covering morphisms (proof lines 1842-1851). Fullness and essential surjectivity are handled together: a morphism of descent data pulls back to the standard coverings and glues over the affine pieces, the agreement on overlaps being checked through a common refinement and the faithfulness just proved (proof lines 1853-1880), while a descent datum pulls back to the standard coverings, is realized there, and the resulting local modules are glued after checking the cocycle condition again by faithfulness (proof lines 1882-1904). The author closes by stating that the verification that the canonical descent datum of the glued module is isomorphic to the one started with is omitted (proof lines 1905-1907). The claim is H3: three genuinely different arguments, with the gluing and the refinement bookkeeping being original work.

items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012

The claim is H2: one genuine sub-claim is proved from a recognition criterion and the remainder is a commutative diagram whose commutativity is taken from the cited construction, so this is a complete but not multi-front argument.

items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that a Noetherian local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres has universally catenary henselization, and that the ring itself is universally catenary when it is unibranch (statement lines 32497-32509). items.title: Descent morphisms, effective descent morphisms and universal injectivity for modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a ring map f the theorem asserts the equivalence of three conditions: that base extension along f on modules is fully faithful, that it is an equivalence of categories, and that f is universally injective (statement lines 1506-1514). Two of the three implications carry real work and they are of different kinds. The implication from full faithfulness to universal injectivity is proved by contraposition and requires a construction: if f is not universally injective then some module M has an element killed by the base change map, and the quotient by the submodule generated by such elements is not isomorphic to M although its image under base extension is an isomorphism, so base extension is not fully faithful (proof lines 1517-1522). The implication from universal injectivity to effectiveness is an adjunction argument: the counit of the adjunction between base extension and its right adjoint is an isomorphism on descent data by two earlier lemmas, and then the composite of the unit followed by the image of that counit is the identity by adjunction, which forces the unit on the image of base extension to be an isomorphism, whereupon a criterion for base change along a universally injective ring map upgrades this to the unit itself (proof lines 1525-1536). The claim is H3: the two directions rest on independent mechanisms, one a counterexample construction at the level of modules and one a formal adjunction computation whose final step needs an outside criterion.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property of a scheme that every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components is local in the fppf topology (statement lines 5069-5073). The proof works through a locality criterion, and the substance is two verifications of how the property behaves under a flat finitely presented morphism of affines. For the property of having finitely many irreducible components, generic points of the source map to generic points of the target, so it suffices to bound the generic points of each fibre, and each fibre is an affine scheme of finite type over the residue field, hence Noetherian and in particular with finitely many irreducible components (proof lines 5079-5090). For the target, the corresponding statement under a surjective flat finitely presented morphism is reduced to the topological fact that a surjective continuous map lifts a finite set of irreducible components (proof lines 5091-5094). Together with Zariski locality these are exactly the hypotheses of the criterion, so the conclusion follows (proof lines 5077-5078 and 5095-5096). The claim is H2: two distinct geometric inputs, generic points under flat maps and Noetherianness of the fibres, are used in addition to one topological input, and all three are stated with their source rather than being hidden in a single citation.

Given a descent datum over U, one fixes a member V_j of the target family, considers the subfamily of U mapping to it, and pulls the transition isomorphisms back along the canonical morphism from the fibre product over V_j to the fibre product over S, producing a descent datum relative to a Zariski covering of V_j (proof lines 9050-9060). Because the transition isomorphisms are isomorphisms between opens, the pieces over this Zariski covering can be glued into a scheme over V_j (proof lines 9061-9066), and the transition isomorphisms over U glue to transition isomorphisms between these schemes satisfying the cocycle condition, which the author marks as omitted details (proof lines 9066-9069). The claim is H2: one comparison morphism has to be recognised, one pullback of a datum computed, and one glueing performed, and the only step left to the reader is the cocycle verification, which is routine once the glueing is in hand.

It is H2: the argument is fully carried out in the counted span and its inputs are standard algebra theorems of the openness and approximation type.

items.title: Parasitic modules have vanishing cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a presheaf of modules on the big site of a scheme for one of five topologies, the lemma asserts that if the presheaf vanishes on the objects of the topology which are flat over the base then all its cohomology vanishes on those objects, and that a presheaf parasitic in the stronger sense has vanishing cohomology on every flat object (statement lines 4004-4019). The proof is carried out in the fppf case, the other cases being parallel. The hypothesis is unwound to say that the presheaf takes the value zero on every object flat and locally of finitely presented over the base, and then the Cech vanishing criterion is applied to the subset of the site consisting exactly of those objects and the collection of all coverings of its members (proof lines 4021-4028). The claim is H2: the proof is short, but it consists of exhibiting the precise input the cited vanishing criterion needs -- a subset of the site and a collection of coverings for it, with the hypothesis checked on that subset -- and that choice is the content of the argument rather than a restatement of the conclusion.

items.title: Dominance is unchanged by a field extension of the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a field extension E over k, the lemma asserts that a morphism over k is dominant if and only if its pullback to the base change to E is dominant (statement lines 5861-5866). The proof splits the equivalence. For the forward direction it uses that the morphism from the spectrum of E to the spectrum of k is universally open, so the projection from the base change of the target to the target is open, and then a cited lemma gives that dominant morphisms are preserved by open base change (proof lines 5869-5875). For the converse it uses that the same projection is surjective, so composing the dominance of the base changed morphism with it gives dominance of the composite, which is also the composite of the projection to the source with the original morphism, whence the original morphism is dominant (proof lines 5876-5880). The claim is H2: the two directions rest on different properties of the field extension -- openness in one and surjectivity in the other -- and both are used explicitly, with a short compositeness argument at the end.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property of a morphism of being quasi-compact and dominant is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 5835-5838). The proof dispatches the easier direction first: preservation under flat base change is a cited property of dominant morphisms, and quasi-compactness is fpqc local on the base by an earlier lemma of the chapter, while being dominant is Zariski local on the base (proof lines 5842-5847). items.title: Being proper over the base descends along an fpqc covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes of locally finite type, a closed subset Z of the source is proper over the base as soon as its inverse image in the base change along some fpqc covering is (statement lines 6726-6734). The proof begins with a choice that makes the rest work: Z is endowed with the reduced induced closed subscheme structure, which is what turns a statement about a closed subset into a statement about a morphism of schemes (proof lines 6737-6738). For each member of the covering, the base change of Z is identified as a closed subscheme of the base changed source whose underlying closed subset is the given inverse image, and the definition of being proper over the base, by way of a cited lemma, gives that the projections from these base changes to the members of the covering are proper (proof lines 6739-6743). Properness of the morphism from Z to the base then descends by the earlier lemma on descending properness, and the conclusion for the closed subset follows from the definition (proof lines 6744-6746). The claim is H2: the reduction from a closed subset to its reduced induced scheme structure is a real step, the identification of the base changes has to be made, and the descent lemma is then applied to the resulting morphisms.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes T to S and a parasitic module on the big site of T, the lemma asserts that the pushforward and all higher direct images are parasitic modules on the big site of S (statement lines 4031-4037). The proof computes the higher direct images as the sheafification of the presheaf sending U to the cohomology of the base change of T along U, and then shows that this presheaf vanishes on every U flat over S: the base change of the structure morphism along a flat morphism is flat, so the hypothesis that the module is parasitic makes the cohomology vanish by the preceding lemma of the chapter (proof lines 4039-4049). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)

items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme S, a topology among Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic and fppf, and one of the listed properties of modules -- free, finitely free, generated by global sections, generated by r global sections, generated by finitely many global sections, having a global presentation, having a global finite presentation, locally free, finite locally free, locally generated by sections, locally generated by r sections, finite type, finitely presented, coherent or flat -- the lemma asserts that a quasi-coherent module has the property if and only if its associated module on the big site or on the small site does, with a possible exception for locally free and coherent, and with the coherent case holding for the small site when S is locally Noetherian and the topology is Zariski or etale (statement lines 2829-2866). The claim is H2: the division of fifteen named properties into the global ones and the local ones, the identification of the covering statement each local property reduces to, and the separate treatment of the two exceptions are the content of the card, and the author marks the last reduction as having omitted details, which is recorded as an obligation.

items.title: The induced morphism on fibres in a cartesian square with etale vertical arrows is etale
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Given a commutative square of schemes whose two vertical arrows are etale, and a point of the upper right scheme mapping to a point of the lower right one, the lemma asserts that the induced morphism of fibres over those points is etale (statement lines 8185-8196). The proof proceeds in three steps, each using a different standard fact. The base change of the upper left vertical arrow to the fibre of the lower right vertical arrow is etale because etale morphisms are stable under base change (proof lines 8198-8200); the fibre of an etale morphism over a point is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions, and the chosen point of the upper right scheme is one of those summands, which makes the fibre over that point an open and closed subscheme of the previous one (proof lines 8200-8205); the composite of an open immersion with an etale morphism is etale, giving the conclusion (proof lines 8205-8208). The claim is H2: no step is a restatement of the conclusion, and in particular the middle step requires identifying the relevant fibre as one of the summands of a disjoint union of spectra of separable extensions, which is the point of the lemma.

items.title: Base change along a surjective flat morphism is faithful
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a surjective flat morphism h : S' to S, the lemma asserts that the base change functor from schemes over S to schemes over S' is faithful (statement lines 8723-8731). The proof reduces faithfulness to a cancellation property. Given two morphisms over S between the same pair of S-schemes whose base changes agree, one writes down the resulting commutative diagram, and the assertion that the two morphisms are equal is seen to follow as soon as the projection from the base change of the source to the source is an epimorphism (proof lines 8734-8749). That projection is the base change of h, hence is itself surjective and flat, so the preceding lemma of the chapter, that a surjective flat morphism is an epimorphism, applies and the proof ends (proof lines 8749-8754). The claim is H2: the two steps are short but the first is a real reduction -- recognising that faithfulness of base change is equivalent to a statement about one particular projection -- and the second consists in checking that the hypotheses of the epimorphism lemma are inherited by the base change, with the diagram displayed.

items.title: The extended cochain complex of a faithfully flat ring map is exact
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for a faithfully flat ring map R to A and any R-module M the extended cochain complex, that is the complex obtained by putting M in degree minus one in front of the complex of the cosimplicial module associated to A over R, is exact (statement lines 773-779). The proof first reduces to a smaller problem: it suffices to find a faithfully flat ring map R to R' such that the statement holds for R' to R' tensor A, because the cosimplicial module computing the bigger complex is obtained from the smaller one by tensoring with R', and faithful flatness of R to R' lets the vanishing of cohomology descend (proof lines 781-793). The author marks the parallel treatment of the two extra degrees of the extended complex as omitted, which is why the proof is shorter than the statement suggests. The reduction is then discharged by the cheapest possible choice, namely R' equals A, since the ring map A to A tensor A over R has a section given by multiplication and the section case has already been handled (proof lines 795-800). The claim is H2: the reduction step is a real argument in which the two cosimplicial modules are identified and faithful flatness is used to descend the vanishing, and the choice of the cover is then justified by exhibiting the section.

items.title: Finite type descends along a faithfully flat finitely presented algebra map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For ring maps R to A to B with R to B of finite type and A to B faithfully flat and of finite presentation, the lemma asserts that R to A is of finite type (statement lines 4568-4573). The proof is a small approximation argument. A cited algebra result produces a commutative diagram whose bottom row is the given sequence and whose top row R to A_0 to B_0 has R to A_0 of finite presentation, A_0 to B_0 faithfully flat of finite presentation and B equal to the tensor product of A and B_0 over A_0 (proof lines 4577-4590). Because R to B is of finite type, one may add finitely many elements to A_0 in such a way that B_0 to B becomes surjective, which is the step where the finite type hypothesis enters (proof lines 4590-4592). In that situation the base change of the map A_0 to A along A_0 to B_0 is isomorphic to the surjective map B_0 to B, and faithful flatness lets surjectivity descend, so A_0 to A is surjective; composing with the finite presentation of R to A_0 gives finite type for R to A (proof lines 4593-4598). The claim is H2: the approximation diagram, the enlargement of A_0 to force surjectivity and the descent of surjectivity along a faithfully flat map are three separate steps that have to be carried out, and the display of the isomorphism of the two base changed maps is the crux.

items.title: The pullback functor on descent data for schemes is fully faithful when the covering is fpqc over the same base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation where descent data for schemes relative to a morphism X to S are compared along a morphism X' to X, the lemma asserts that the pullback functor is fully faithful provided that the single morphism X' to X is an fpqc covering and the base is unchanged (statement lines 8777-8787). Faithfulness is immediate from the surjectivity and flatness of the morphism together with the preceding lemma, so the substance is the essential surjectivity on morphisms (proof lines 8790-8792). Given a morphism of descent data over X', one has to produce a morphism of descent data over X pulling back to it, and this takes three separate steps. The first is a pointwise computation: the two composites from the fibre product of the source with itself over the source to the target agree, which the author proves by chasing scheme points through the two descent isomorphisms, writing the descent isomorphism on points, transporting the points along the given morphism of descent data and concluding that the two images agree after applying the second descent isomorphism, which is legitimate because that isomorphism is invertible (proof lines 8813-8852). The author explicitly advises the reader to prove this step rather than read it, which signals that it is not a formal consequence of the definitions. The second step is the descent of the morphism itself, which uses that the base change of the source along the covering is an fpqc covering and that fpqc coverings are universal effective epimorphisms, so that the morphism over X' factors through a unique morphism over X (proof lines 8855-8863). The third step closes the argument for morphisms of descent data rather than merely morphisms of schemes: the relevant square commutes because after base change to the fibre product of X' with itself over S it commutes, and the morphism between the two fibre products is surjective and flat, so that base change along it is faithful (proof lines 8863-8875). The claim is H3: three independent mechanisms -- a pointwise calculation, a descent along an effective epimorphism, and a faithfulness test after base change -- are needed, and the first of them is the kind of step the author himself flags as non-obvious.

The proof is a numerical criterion argument. items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter descent.tex (Descent)

items.title: A root of a function in a weakly unramified extension of normal local domains descends to the smaller ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules

items.difficulty_reason: statement 是「平坦局部 Noether 正规整环之间、在高度 1 素理想处弱非分歧的扩张中，若 f 在 B 中是某个 h 的 n 次幂乘单位，则 f 在 A 中也是某个 g 的 n 次幂乘单位」。证明是一段扎实的估值论证：把 f 的极小素理想（都是高度 1）列出来，用弱非分歧性得到 v_i(f) 被 n 整除；再用局部商构造理想 I 的短正合列；然后要**自己证明一个单射性 claim**——把 (A_p/p^{w})⊗B 映到各 B_q/q^{e·w} 的乘积里是单射，靠正规整环「在每个高度 1 素理想处可除即在环内」的性质；由此把 I⊗B 认成由 h 生成的秩 1 自由模，沿忠实平坦下降回 A 得到 g，最后再用同一性质把 g^n 与 f 的差写成单位。承重演算全在 span 内；5 处引用里 1 处同章定义（使 statement 有意义）、4 处跨章，均为导航桩。
