items.title: Regularity of a generating sequence does not depend on the chosen generators of the ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the three regularity notions of a sequence depend only on the ideal generated, provided the sequence has the minimal possible length, and the proof is a 32-line argument built on the comparison of Koszul complexes. It first observes that a quasi-regular generating sequence of minimal length has free conormal module, which forces the given generators to form a basis and hence the maps from symmetric powers of the conormal module to be isomorphisms, so the given sequence is quasi-regular; then it compares the two Koszul complexes by a change-of-basis matrix, uses the invertibility of the determinant modulo the ideal and the annihilation of the cohomology by the ideal to upgrade an isomorphism after inverting the determinant to a quasi-isomorphism; finally the H1-regular and Koszul-regular cases are reduced to the quasi-regular one by the equivalence of the notions for such sequences. Each of the three steps uses one named statement of the chapter.

items.title: A formal algebraic space satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a formal algebraic space over a scheme is a sheaf for the fpqc topology (statement lines 7052-7059). The proof is organised as the equalizer condition for a surjective flat morphism of affine schemes, and it discharges the two halves of that condition by different mechanisms. Uniqueness is a fibre product argument: given two morphisms agreeing after composition with the covering, their difference is measured by the fibre product of the source with the graph of the diagonal, which is a monomorphism of schemes because the diagonal of a formal algebraic space is a representable monomorphism; the covering factors through it, whence the projection from the base change of this monomorphism to the source is a monomorphism with a section and therefore an isomorphism, and descent of the property of being an isomorphism makes the monomorphism itself an isomorphism, which is exactly the equality of the two morphisms (proof lines 7071-7100). Existence is a descent argument of a different kind and is the bulk of the proof: an etale cover of the target by a formal affine is chosen so as to contain the image of the given morphism, the base change of this cover along the given morphism is an etale separated surjective morphism of schemes, the cocycle condition for the given morphism is turned by an explicit chain of identifications into a descent datum on it, effectivity of that descent datum is obtained from the fact that the morphism is ind-quasi-affine because it is etale and separated, the descended morphism is checked to be surjective and etale by descent, a morphism into the chosen formal affine is produced and descended, and finally uniqueness from the first half upgrades the etale local solution to a global one because the space is an etale sheaf (proof lines 7102-7165). The claim is H3: at least four independent mechanisms are used -- fibred products with the diagonal, effectivity of an ind-quasi-affine descent datum, descent of surjectivity and etaleness, and the etale sheaf property -- and each has its own criterion.

items.title: Every formal algebraic space carries a structure sheaf of topological rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that every formal algebraic space has a structure sheaf (statement lines 7664-7667). The proof has four distinct parts. First it reduces the problem to constructing the structure sheaf as a sheaf of topological rings on the small etale site of the space, using the identification of that topos with the site of affine formal algebraic spaces etale over it (proof lines 7669-7674). Second it sets up the category of affine formal algebraic spaces etale and representable over the space, observes that reduction is an equivalence from that category to the small etale site, so that the structure sheaf exists as a presheaf and only the sheaf condition remains (proof lines 7672-7680). Third it analyses a covering: a covering corresponds to a finite family whose reductions form an etale covering, and each member is representable hence affine, and etale by permanence, so that after writing the base as a filtered colimit of its defining affine schemes one obtains an exact sequence for each index, and taking the filtered colimit of these exact sequences -- which is legitimate because limits commute with limits -- produces an exact sequence computing the sections of the structure sheaf (proof lines 7682-7727). Fourth, and separately, it must be checked that the topology on the sections is the one induced from the product, which is done by comparing the fundamental systems of open submodules on the two sides (proof lines 7728-7748). The claim is H3: the category-theoretic reduction, the finiteness and affineness analysis of a covering, the limit of exact sequences, and the compatibility of the limit topology are independent pieces of work, and the last of them is a genuine subtlety about topological rings rather than a formality.

items.title: Fibre products of formal algebraic spaces preserve countable indexedness, classicity, weak adicness, adic* and local Noetherianness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For two morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over a scheme, the lemma has five parts: the fibre product inherits local countable indexedness; it inherits local countable indexedness together with classicity; it is weakly adic when the factors are; it is locally adic* when the factors are; and it is locally Noetherian when the factors are and the induced morphism between the reductions is locally of finite type (statement lines 4799-4815). The proof begins with a reduction that is used for all five parts: a covering of the target and coverings of the two sources over it are chosen as in the definition of a formal algebraic space, the fibre products of the members of those coverings are affine formal algebraic spaces, and the resulting family covers the fibre product, so that it suffices to treat the case where all three objects are affine (proof lines 4817-4832). The first part then requires a genuine construction: writing the two sources as colimits of their defining systems and the target as a filtered colimit, one shows that each stage of each source factors through some stage of the target, and then chooses an increasing cofinal sequence of stages of the target through which both sources factor, which lets the target be replaced by the corresponding sub-object without changing the fibre product (proof lines 4834-4856). Once all three are countably indexed they are formal spectra of weakly admissible topological rings, the fibre product is the formal spectrum of the completed tensor product, and part (1) follows from the corresponding statement for completed tensor products (proof lines 4858-4874). Parts (2), (3) and (4) are then read off from the other parts of the same tensor product lemma (proof lines 4876-4900). Part (5) is a separate argument: transferring the hypothesis from the reductions of the original morphisms to the reductions of the members of the coverings uses that the vertical morphisms in the resulting square are etale and that reductions commute with the relevant fibre products, the replacement of the target by the cofinal sub-object is checked not to change the reduction, and the finite type hypothesis is finally translated into a condition on the two rings modulo the ideals of topologically nilpotent elements (proof lines 4902-4956). The claim is H3: the covering reduction, the cofinality construction, the four tensor product transfers and the hypothesis matching in part (5) are independent pieces of work, and part (5) in particular requires an extra criterion to move the finite type hypothesis to the coverings where the tensor product lemma applies.

items.title: A birational morphism between schemes with finitely many components is an isomorphism over the local ring of a generic point of the target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a birational morphism between schemes with finitely many irreducible components, the base change to the local ring at a generic point of the target is an isomorphism (statement lines 13236-13243). The counted proof is a short but genuine commutative algebra reduction: it passes to an affine irreducible situation, identifies the generic point with a minimal prime, uses birationality to know that the corresponding local rings are isomorphic and that there is a unique minimal prime upstairs, and then shows that the localized source ring has exactly one prime by exhibiting the extension of the minimal prime as both minimal and maximal, from which the identification with the base change follows (proof lines 13245-13260). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the standard dictionary between points, minimal primes and local rings.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the normalization of the base in a disjoint union of two schemes is the disjoint union of the normalizations in the two pieces (statement lines 14312-14318). The counted proof reduces the geometric statement to the algebraic statement about the integral closure of a ring in a product of rings, and then gives the key reason why the statement holds, namely that the standard idempotents of the product are integral over the base ring and hence belong to the integral closure, which forces it to be a product whose factors are the individual integral closures (proof lines 14320-14330). items.title: A refined valuative criterion with a dense subscheme implies universal closedness, and separatedness when the morphism is quasi-separated
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a refined valuative criterion: if a quasi-compact morphism has a quasi-compact dense subscheme through which every valuation ring diagram admits a unique filler, then the morphism is universally closed, and separated as well when it is quasi-separated (statement lines 10219-10234). The counted proof is long and technically dense: it reduces to reduced schemes and an affine base, passes to a flat polynomial algebra cover so that the base changed dense open has the whole spectrum as scheme theoretic image, applies the existence statement for valuation diagrams to produce an auxiliary valuation ring, then invokes the existence of a dominating valuation ring inside a residue field and a sandwich construction to put the situation into the shape required by the hypothesis, and finally pulls the dotted arrow back to the original valuation ring by maximality for the domination order (proof lines 10236-10302); the separatedness half is deduced by running the same argument for the quasi-compact diagonal (proof lines 10304-10327). It is H2: the argument is a complete author proof with several genuinely distinct reduction steps, and the cited inputs are standard criteria and algebra facts.

items.title: Four characterisations of an identity system over a pointed type are logically equivalent
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file induction.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 1152-1160 (book Theorem 5.8.2): four conditions on a pointed predicate over a pointed type, namely being an identity system, having a contractible type of pointed maps into every pointed predicate, having all the transport maps out of the loop space be equivalences, and having a contractible total type, are logically equivalent. The statement lists the four conditions and nothing else, while the proof (source lines 1167-1193) runs the cycle in one direction only and must construct, for each implication, the auxiliary pointed predicate and the two pointed maps that make the argument go through: for the first implication it turns the identity-system elimination into inhabitation and then into a mere proposition by applying elimination to the equality of any two pointed maps; for the second it uses (a_0 = b) as the auxiliary family and gets the composites to be identities from the contractibility of the pointed-map types ppmap(R,R) and ppmap(S,S); the third goes through the equivalence of \Sigma-types; the fourth has to transport the given element along a uniform path family of the contractible total type and check the base-point computation. Only the derived direction of each implication is proved, so the chapter's observation that the four conditions are also logically equivalent as propositions is used, not proved.

items.title: The localized Chern classes of the structure sheaf of a regular closed immersion vanish below the codimension and equal a factorial multiple of the class of the normal sheaf in top degree
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a regular closed immersion i : Z -> X of codimension r between schemes locally of finite type over a base (S, delta) as in Situation labelled situation-setup, the lemma states that c_t(Z -> X, i_* O_Z) = 0 for t = 1, ..., r - 1 and that c_r(Z -> X, i_* O_Z) = (-1)^{r - 1} (r - 1)! c(Z -> X, N) in A^r(Z -> X), where N is the conormal sheaf of Z in X and the c_t are the localized Chern classes of Definition labelled definition-localized-chern (statement lines 12612-12628). The proof begins by making the statement meaningful: locally on X one writes Z as V(f_1, ..., f_r) for a regular sequence, the Koszul complex is a resolution of A/(f_1, ..., f_r) by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-regular-koszul-regular, hence F = i_* O_Z is a perfect object of D(O_X) with zero restriction off Z, so the localized classes exist under the quasi-compactness assumption (proof lines 12630-12648). The main body uses the blowing up b : W -> P^1_X in infinity(Z): the closed immersion i' : P^1_Z -> W is shown to give a perfect Q = i'_* O_{P^1_Z}, the claim that F and Q satisfy the hypotheses of Lemma labelled lemma-independent-loc-chern-bQ is proved by exhibiting the r + 1 affine charts of the blowing up as global complete intersections and reading off the regular sequence y_1, ..., y_r, sy_1 - f_1, ..., sy_r - f_r (proof lines 12650-12698). Granting the claim, the defining property of the localized classes in Lemma labelled lemma-independent-loc-chern-bQ converts the assertion into the corresponding one for c'_p(Q|_E), which is Lemma labelled lemma-compute-section, and the identification of c(Z -> X, N) via j^* o C = p^* o c(Z -> X, N) finishes the comparison (proof lines 12700-12705). The author marks one step of the regularity verification with 'Some details omitted' (proof line 12700) while the complete-intersection computation around it is written out. Recognising that the blown-up situation reduces the local statement to the fiber case handled by Lemma labelled lemma-compute-section is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Chow groups and cycle groups commute with a filtered limit of affine base changes in the c = 0 situation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-setup-base-change with c = 0 and S' = colim_{i in I} S_i a filtered limit of schemes affine over S satisfying the three listed situation conditions, the lemma states that for a quasi-compact X of finite type over S with base changes X' and X_i one has Z_k(X') = colim Z_k(X_i) and CH_k(X') = colim CH_k(X_i) (statement lines 15482-15498). The proof first reduces to the Noetherian case by replacing S by a quasi-compact open over which X -> S factors, so that all schemes in the proof become Noetherian (proof lines 15500-15506). Surjectivity of colim Z_k(X_i) -> Z_k(X') is proved by descending an integral closed subscheme Z' of delta'-dimension k along Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-finite-presentation and Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, replacing Z_i by the scheme theoretic image of Z' -> X_i, and matching dimensions with Lemma labelled lemma-dimension-base-change (proof lines 15508-15528). Injectivity is proved by testing a cycle alpha_i whose base change to X' vanishes: since each base change Z'_j -> Z_j is flat and dominant, the coefficient of a dominating component is nonzero, so every Z'_j must be empty, and then Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-limit-nonempty kills alpha_i at some transition map (proof lines 15530-15549). The Chow group statement follows by the same strategy: surjectivity from the cycle level result, and injectivity by descending the integral subschemes W'_l and the rational functions f'_l that exhibit alpha' as a sum of divisors, using Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-opens and Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-section, with the comparison of the divisor coefficients n_{l,j} = n_{i,l,j} reduced to the order comparison along the flat local ring map O_{W_{i,l},xi} -> O_{W'_l,xi'} and Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-pullback-module (proof lines 15551-15618); one step in that comparison is dismissed as 'for some i' >= i by an easy argument we omit' (proof line 15592), while the rest of the argument is written out. Descending cycles, divisors and rational functions through a filtered limit and matching the orders along a flat local ring map is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: For a finite length module over a local ring the determinant is one-dimensional and generated by the symbol of any spanning admissible sequence
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a local ring R with residue field kappa and a finite length R-module M, the lemma asserts that det_kappa(M) is a one-dimensional kappa-vector space and is generated by the symbol [f_1,...,f_l] of any admissible sequence with <f_1,...,f_l> = M (statement lines 15849-15857). The proof does not recompute the relations: that det_kappa(M) has dimension at most one and is generated by the symbol of a spanning admissible sequence is quoted from Lemma labelled lemma-dimension-at-most-one together with its proof (proof lines 15859-15862), and the new content is nonvanishing, proved by induction on the length l. The induction step picks a nonzero f with m f = 0 and constructs a surjection psi from det_kappa(M) onto det_kappa(M/<f>) by an explicit rule on symbols: send [e_1,...,e_l] to zero if f is not in <e_1,...,e_l>, and otherwise choose the minimal i with f in <e_1,...,e_i>, write e_i = lambda f + x with lambda a unit, and map to (-1)^i lambda-bar times the symbol with the i-th entry deleted (proof lines 15863-15885). The bulk is checking that this rule kills each of the three families of admissible relations: type (a) (proof lines 15887-15897), type (b) with the nontrivial subcase i = a resolved by the rewrite e'_a = lambda^{-1}(mu f + y - x) (proof lines 15899-15965), and type (c) split into four cases according to the position of i relative to a (proof lines 15967-16060); surjectivity then follows by lifting an admissible sequence from M/<f> (proof lines 16062-16066). Carrying the induction through every relation family with the correct signs and indices is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Etale local flatness after admissible blowups globalises to one admissible blowup making the strict transform flat
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated S, a morphism X -> S, a quasi-coherent F on X and a quasi-compact open U of S, the lemma states that if there are finitely many diagrams with quasi-compact etale e_i : S_i -> S covering S, etale j_i : X_i -> X covering X and e_i^{-1}(U)-admissible blowups S^*_i -> S_i over which the strict transform of j_i^* F is flat, then some U-admissible blowup S' -> S makes the strict transform of F flat over S' (statement lines 8903-8928). The proof first checks that the hypotheses survive a U-admissible blowup: after base changing S' -> S and blowing S'_i up in the pulled back ideal one compares the resulting square with the given one through Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-blowing-up-two-ideals, and the strict transform computation of Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-strict-transform-flat together with Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups identifies the new transform as the pullback of the flat F^*_i, hence flat (proof lines 8930-8972). Remark labelled remark-successive-blowups then lets one assume S minus U is the support of an effective Cartier divisor D, and Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-characterize-effective-Cartier-divisor reduces further to S = Spec(A) and D = Spec(A/(a)) with a a nonzerodivisor (proof lines 8974-8980). The heart is Lemma labelled lemma-push-ideal, which produces finitely many opens W_i inside each S_i and finite type ideals I_i on S with I_i O_{S_i} = J_i J'_i and V(I_i) contained in V(a); blowing S up in the product I_1 ... I_n is U-admissible, and Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-blowing-up-two-ideals shows that its base change to S_i factors through the given blowup S^*_i -> S_i, so after replacing S one has j_i^* F flat over S_i, hence over S by Lemma labelled lemma-etale-flat-up-down, and finally F flat over S by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-flat-permanence (proof lines 8982-9014). Reducing the etale local hypothesis to a single blowup whose base change dominates all prescribed local blowups is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The locus where a quasi-coherent module is free of a given rank at the generic fibre point is representable by a locally closed immersion, of finite presentation when the module is
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-free-at-generic-points the lemma asserts that for each p >= 0 the functor H_p of equation labelled equation-free-at-generic-points is representable by a locally closed immersion S_p -> S, and that S_p -> S is of finite presentation when F is of finite presentation (statement lines 7630-7637). The proof treats all p concurrently for a fixed S: H_p is an fppf sheaf by Lemma labelled lemma-free-at-generic-points, so by Descent, Lemma labelled descent-lemma-descent-data-sheaves, More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-morphisms-fppf-descend and Descent, Lemma labelled descent-lemma-descending-fppf-property-immersion the question is etale local, hence Zariski local, on S (proof lines 7639-7647). Writing xi_s for the generic point of the fibre X_s, generic flatness gives that F_s is locally free of some rank p(s) near xi_s, and p(s) is computed as the dimension of the fibre of F at xi_s, so H_{p(s)}(s) is nonempty and H_q(s) is empty for q different from p(s) (proof lines 7649-7663). Because f is smooth hence open, one may replace X by any open U without changing H_p, and after shrinking to a neighbourhood where F is generated by p(s) elements via a surjection O_X^{p(s)} -> F, the functor H_{p(s)} is identified with the functor F_iso of equation labelled equation-iso, which Theorem labelled theorem-flattening-map represents by a closed immersion (proof lines 7665-7698). The global representability then follows formally by induction on the maximum of p(s): representability for the maximum is a closed immersion, and removing S_p lowers the maximum by at least one (proof lines 7700-7709). The finite presentation statement is obtained by redoing the induction and checking that each complement stays quasi-compact, which uses that S_p -> S is a closed immersion of finite presentation (proof lines 7711-7725). Converting the local closed-immersion statement into a global locally closed immersion by induction on the maximal rank is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A composite of localized Chern classes equals the pushforward of the restricted classes along the intersection of the W_i
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for X locally of finite type over a base (S, delta) as in Situation labelled situation-setup, a proper b : W -> P^1_X, closed subschemes Z_i with W_i = b^{-1}(P^1_{Z_i}), perfect objects Q_i and integers p_i >= 0 satisfying the assumptions of Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre, the vanishing of Q_i off W_i up to a rank bound, and assumption (3) of Situation labelled situation-loc-chern, the composite c'_{p_n}(Q_n) o ... o c'_{p_1}(Q_1) equals the pushforward from W_{n,infinity} cap ... cap W_{1,infinity} to Z_n cap ... cap Z_1 of the products of the restricted classes composed with the class C of Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-at-infinity (statement lines 11025-11059). The proof is an induction on n. The case n = 1 is the construction of c'_{p_1}(Q_1), using that W_{1,infinity} is the inverse image of Z_1 in W_infinity (proof lines 11061-11067). The induction step applies Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-localized-chern-pre to compute the restriction of c'_{p_n}(Q_n) to Z_{n-1} cap ... cap Z_1 through the closed subset Z_n cap ... cap Z_1 and the restriction of Q_n, observes (b')^{-1}(Z_n) = W_n cap ... cap W_1 and rewrites the restriction with the class C_{n-1} of Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-at-infinity, then reorders the composite (proof lines 11068-11106). The decisive move is Lemma labelled lemma-homomorphism-pre, which makes C_{n-1} composed with the pushforward equal to the identity on elements in the image of the Gysin map, so it suffices to show that every element in the image of the composite of the restricted classes is such a Gysin image; this is done by writing each c'_{p_i}(Q_i|_{W_{i,infinity}}) through Lemma labelled lemma-loc-chern-agree as the restriction of the bivariant class c_{p_i}(W_i -> W, Q_i) and using that bivariant classes commute with i_infinity^* (proof lines 11108-11158). Managing the induction, the base change of the localized class and the identification of the image of the composite with the Gysin image is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Existence and defining property of the canonical bivariant localized Chern classes attached to a perfect object in the localized Chern situation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that in Situation labelled situation-loc-chern there are canonical bivariant classes P_p(Z -> X, E) and c_p(Z -> X, E) in A^p(Z -> X) characterised by i_* o P_p(Z -> X, E) = P_p(E), resp. i_* o c_p(Z -> X, E) = c_p(E), as bivariant classes on X (statement lines 10700-10717). The proof constructs them from the blowing up b : W -> P^1_X and the perfect object Q in D(O_W) produced by More on Flatness, Section labelled flat-section-blowup-complexes-III and Lemma labelled flat-lemma-graph-construction: with T in W_infinity the given closed subscheme and T' the open and closed piece on which Q is zero or of rank < p, condition (2) of the situation makes T' -> T -> W_infinity -> X isomorphisms over X minus Z, so an application of Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre with the data W, b, Q, T' yields P'_p(Q) and c'_p(Q); using Q|_{X x {0}} = E by construction gives the classes and their defining property (proof lines 10719-10748). The second half is a separate verification that the Chern classes of Q are defined, and it is exactly where the four alternatives of condition (3) of the situation are consumed: in cases (3)(a) and (3)(b) one passes to W, which is proper over X, and applies Lemma labelled lemma-chern-classes-defined; in case (3)(c) the object Q is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules by part (5) of the graph construction lemma; in case (3)(d) one compares with the analogous construction over a base X' with quasi-compact irreducible components using More on Flatness, Lemma labelled flat-lemma-complex-and-divisor-blowup-base-change (proof lines 10750-10784). The author marks that paragraph with 'we suggest the reader skip this' (proof line 10756), but the argument is written out. Disentangling the four cases of condition (3) so that Lemma labelled lemma-chern-classes-defined applies, and seeing that the definition of the classes does not depend on the chosen data, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A presheaf on the big h site is a sheaf iff it is a Zariski sheaf, satisfies the equalizer condition for surjective flat proper finitely presented maps to affine targets, and turns both almost blowup squares into cartesian diagrams
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises sheaves on one of the big h sites (Sch/S)_h: a presheaf F is a sheaf if and only if it is a Zariski sheaf, F(Y) is the equalizer of F(X) => F(X x_Y X) for every surjective flat proper finitely presented f : X -> Y with Y affine, and F turns the two almost blowup squares of Example labelled example-one-generator and Example labelled example-two-generators into cartesian diagrams of sets (statement lines 11500-11519). By Proposition labelled proposition-check-h it suffices to show the cartesian property for an almost blow up square with X affine (proof lines 11521-11528), and the proof opens with a Zariski descent reduction: if the cartesian property holds on the members U_i of an open cover and on the double overlaps U_{ijk}, it holds for the square on X (proof lines 11530-11558). The core is an induction on the number r of generators of the ideal defining Z. For r <= 2 the square may be chosen as in Example labelled example-two-generators, so assumption (4) applies (proof lines 11584-11590); for the induction step one takes Z_1 = Spec(A/(f_1,f_2)) with its almost blow up square from Example labelled example-two-generators, uses Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-almost-blow-up to obtain the two almost blow up squares (I) and (II) whose ideals are generated by fewer elements, applies the induction hypothesis to Y and Z_1, and glues the three fibre product descriptions through assumption (4) (proof lines 11592-11689). The argument also isolates a preliminary reduction that decides when b is a closed immersion and Z locally principal, and uses Lemma labelled lemma-almost-blow-up-unique to show that the truth of the fibre product condition is independent of the chosen almost blow up square (proof lines 11560-11582). The proof concludes by omitting the routine verification that the constructed s maps to s' and t, with the hint to use uniqueness of s and work affine locally (proof lines 11690-11693). Building the induction on the number of generators so that both assumptions (3) and (4) apply after base change is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The Steinberg relation for the symbol of a one-dimensional module over a Noetherian local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian local ring A, elements a, b and a finite A-module M of dimension one on which a, b and b - a are nonzerodivisors, the lemma asserts the relation d_M(a, b - a) d_M(b, b) = d_M(b, b - a) d_M(a, b) in kappa^* (statement lines 17659-17670). The proof reduces in three stages: by Lemma labelled lemma-compute-symbol-M it suffices to treat M = A/q of dimension one (proof lines 17672-17675); then A may be replaced by A/q because the determinants over A and over A/q are canonically identified by Lemma labelled lemma-determinant-quotient-ring, so A may be taken to be a one-dimensional local Noetherian domain (proof lines 17677-17685); and the cases where a or b is a unit are dispatched by Lemma labelled lemma-symbol-when-one-is-a-unit and Lemma labelled lemma-symbol-when-equal, so both may be assumed to lie in the maximal ideal (proof lines 17687-17691). The core then chooses the extension A subset A' together with the factorizations a = t a', b = t b' supplied by Lemma labelled lemma-Noetherian-domain-dim-1-two-elements, works with the relative symbols d^A_{A'}(-,-) of Lemma labelled lemma-pre-symbol, relates them to the absolute symbols by Lemma labelled lemma-symbol-compare-modules, and evaluates them using the decompositions of A'/(a'(b' - a')), A'/(b'(b' - a')) and A'/(a'b') as products of cyclic modules together with Lemma labelled lemma-periodic-determinant-easy-case and Lemma labelled lemma-periodic-determinant (proof lines 17693-17752). Carrying the sign (-1)^{length_A(A'/(b'))} produced by the identification of multiplication by b' - a' with multiplication by minus a' and closing with Lemma labelled lemma-periodic-determinant-sign is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A finite type separated scheme covered by two opens with compactifications and dense intersection has a compactification
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian S and a scheme U of finite type and separated over S written as U = U_1 cup U_2 with U_1 and U_2 admitting compactifications over S and U_1 cap U_2 dense in U, the lemma asserts that U itself has a compactification over S (statement lines 9790-9796). The proof chooses compactifications U_i in X_i which are scheme theoretically dense, uses Lemma labelled lemma-compactification-dominates to have proper morphisms psi_i : V_i -> U extending the identifications, and sets Z_i = U  minus U_j (proof lines 9798-9808). It then blows up X_i in a V_i-admissible way so that the closures of Z_{i,i} and Z_{i,j} become disjoint (Lemma labelled lemma-separate-disjoint-locally-closed-by-blowing-up, and the disjointness condition is preserved by further admissible blowups), forms V_{12} = V_1 x_U V_2, and takes X_{12} to be the scheme theoretic image of V_{12} in X_1 x_S X_2, whose projections are proper; a further admissible blowup makes p_1 an isomorphism near the closure of Z_{1,2} by Lemma labelled lemma-blowup-iso-along, from which the emptiness of X_{12} cap (closure Z_{1,2} x_S closure Z_{2,1}) follows (proof lines 9810-9868). This is the point of the construction: it is exactly what allows the glued schemes W_i = U coprod_{U_i} (X_i  minus closure Z_{i,j}) to satisfy the valuative criterion. Separatedness of W_i -> S is checked with Lemma labelled lemma-check-separated by verifying that the immersion U_i -> U x_S (X_i  minus closure Z_{i,j}) is closed, using unique lifting of specializations along the proper psi_i (proof lines 9870-9890), and the extension property of the valuative criterion for the W_i is proved by applying properness of X_i -> S and excluding the bad case via the emptiness above (proof lines 9892-9904). The final diagram of Lemma labelled lemma-find-common-blowups is then filled by lifting along the proper W'_i -> W_i, and Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-refined-valuative-criterion-universally-closed plus finiteness and separatedness of W -> S finish the proof (proof lines 9906-9947). Building the auxiliary X_{12} with its controlled intersection and running the valuative criterion through the glued W_i is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A failure of base change is witnessed by an algebraically closed field over a normal affine base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma makes the failure of the base change property concrete: if the property holds in degree q - 1 but fails in degree q, then there is a cartesian diagram with an affine, integral, normal base with algebraically closed function field, a dominant map from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field, and a cyclic coefficient sheaf of order dividing n whose higher direct image in degree q does not vanish (statement lines 17295-17317). The proof is a complete chain of named reductions: it starts from the diagram and sheaf prepared by the companion lemma (proof lines 17325-17327), makes the base affine (proof lines 17328-17329), makes the field algebraically closed through the integral top lemma (proof lines 17330-17331), replaces the coefficients by a constant cyclic sheaf using the decomposition of modules over the cyclic group (proof lines 17332-17335), and replaces the base by its normalization in that field through the integral bottom lemma (proof lines 17336-17338). The non-formal content is the sequence of reductions, each attributed. The claim is H2: a structured reduction with every input named.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:etale-cohomology.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file etale-cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the Cech complex construction, for a fixed family of morphisms with a fixed target, is an exact functor on the category of abelian presheaves (statement lines 1503-1508). The proof is short but complete: it reduces exactness of sequences of abelian presheaves to exactness of the sequences of values at every object, using that this category is a functor category (proof lines 1521-1528), and then observes that each degree of the Cech complex is a product of those values, so the sequence of complexes is a product of short exact sequences in every degree (proof lines 1528-1529). The non-formal content is the identification of the Cech complex with products of values. The claim is H1: a short reduction plus a direct verification.

items.title: An anti-equivalence between systems of finite type algebras and finite type maps of affine formal algebraic spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space X over a scheme with associated weakly admissible topological ring A, the lemma establishes an anti-equivalence between the category of inverse systems of finite type algebras over the quotients of A, with compatible transition maps inducing isomorphisms modulo the earlier quotients, and the category of finite type maps of affine formal algebraic spaces into X (statement lines 6404-6415). The proof constructs both functors and then checks that they are quasi-inverse. From a map into X it takes the fibre products with the quotients of A, notes that they are affine and that the resulting ring maps are of finite type, so that the system of their coordinate rings is an object of the first category (proof lines 6417-6424). In the other direction it takes the colimit of the spectra of the members of a system, which is an affine formal algebraic space, and verifies that its fibre product with a quotient of A is the corresponding member of the system by evaluating on quasi-compact test objects: a morphism from such a test object into the fibre product factors through one of the stages by two applications of the factorization lemma, and the second axiom on the system identifies that stage (proof lines 6426-6445). The same evaluation then shows that the resulting map into X is of finite type, since any quasi-compact test object over X factors through a quotient of A (proof lines 6445-6458). Finally the two composites are seen to be the identity, once by the computation just made and once by evaluating on quasi-compact test objects and writing X as the colimit of its quotients (proof lines 6460-6478). The claim is H2: it is one coherent construction, but each of the three verifications -- that the colimit computes the expected fibre products, that the map obtained is of finite type, and that the composites are identities -- is carried out rather than assumed.

items.title: Properties of the completed tensor product of linearly topologized rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For continuous homomorphisms of linearly topologized rings from B to A and from B to C the lemma lists five properties of the completed tensor product: it is weakly admissible when the two rings are weakly pre-admissible, admissible when they are pre-admissible, countably generated as a topological ring when they are, adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition when they are pre-adic with finitely generated ideals of definition, and adic Noetherian in the Noetherian pre-adic case under a finite type hypothesis between the quotients by the ideals of topologically nilpotent elements (statement lines 1186-1207). The proof fixes the common setup once: the completed tensor product is the limit of the tensor products of the quotients by fundamental systems of open ideals, the kernels of the structure maps form a fundamental system of open ideals and are the closures of the ideals generated by the two systems, and there is a ring map from the ordinary tensor product with dense image (proof lines 1209-1221). Each part is then a short verification on that setup: part (1) transfers topological nilpotence to those kernels, part (2) shows that a suitable power of one kernel lies inside any other so that the kernel at ideals of definition is an ideal of definition, part (3) is the countability of a product of countable sets, part (4) identifies the completed tensor product with a completion with respect to a finitely generated ideal and invokes the corresponding algebra statement, and part (5) uses part (4) and computes the quotient by the finitely generated ideal of definition as a finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring, to which the completion-Noetherian statement applies (proof lines 1223-1282). The claim is H2: five statements are proved, but they are parallel consequences of one shared setup and each is a short computation, with the single genuinely external input being the two algebra lemmas invoked in parts (4) and (5).

items.title: The structure sheaf of a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space has no higher cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space X the lemma asserts that the higher cohomology of the structure sheaf on the small etale site vanishes (statement lines 7764-7768). The proof first reduces the site to the affine etale site and, since finite disjoint unions are available, applies the Cech vanishing criterion to reduce the claim to the exactness of the Cech complex of a covering by a single arrow, which for the base object one writes out explicitly in terms of the values of the structure sheaf on the reductions of the iterated fibre products; the general member of the site is then dismissed as being treated in exactly the same way (proof lines 7770-7788). The computation of those values is the second step: writing X as the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological ring with a countable fundamental system of weak ideals of definition, the objects of the site correspond to etale algebras over it, the values of the structure sheaf are their completions, and the values on iterated fibre products are the completions of the corresponding tensor powers (proof lines 7790-7807). The third step supplies the input for exactness: the morphism from the base to the cover is faithfully flat because the cover is a covering, so the complex before completion is not merely exact but universally exact, by the descent lemma identifying that notion (proof lines 7808-7813). The fourth and last step transfers exactness through completion: the complex is split into short exact sequences, universal exactness gives that each submodule meets every ideal of the base in the image of the intersection, so the two topologies on the submodules agree, and the countable fundamental system of ideals of definition makes the completed short exact sequences exact (proof lines 7814-7838). The claim is H3: the reduction to a single-arrow Cech complex, the identification of the values of the structure sheaf as completions of tensor powers, the use of universal exactness, and the comparison of topologies through a countable system are four independent pieces of work rather than one.

items.title: Maps from the spectrum of a complete local Noetherian algebra agree with maps from its formal spectrum
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a complete local Noetherian algebra R over a scheme S and an algebraic space X over S, the lemma asserts that the natural map from morphisms of the spectrum of R into X to morphisms of the formal spectrum of R into X is bijective (statement lines 7226-7236). The proof rewrites the target as the inverse limit of the morphism sets over the quotients of R by powers of the maximal ideal and then proves the two halves by different mechanisms. Injectivity measures the difference of two morphisms by the fibre product with the diagonal: what results is a scheme, locally of finite type, separated and locally quasi-finite over the spectrum of R, hence locally Noetherian, and the point over the closed point has a local ring whose quotients by the powers of the maximal ideal agree with those of R; since the local ring embeds in its completion, the local ring is R and the two morphisms agree (proof lines 7240-7262). Surjectivity is a lifting argument: a surjective etale cover of the space is chosen, the fibre of that cover over the residue field is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions so that a suitable finite separable extension and a compatible point are available, the corresponding finite etale extension of complete local rings is formed, formal etaleness of the cover lifts the given compatible family to the extension, the scheme case of the statement produces a morphism from the extended spectrum, and descent along the resulting fppf covering produces a morphism from the spectrum of R (proof lines 7264-7309). The claim is H3: injectivity rests on a completion argument through a fibre product with the diagonal, surjectivity on an etale lifting combined with fppf descent, and the compatibility needed to make the descent work is obtained by invoking the injectivity half again for the tensor square of the extension -- three separate ingredients rather than one.

items.title: Topologically of finite type over a complete Tate ring: equivalent formulations and locality
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an arrow of complete weakly admissible topological rings B to A, the lemma asserts the equivalence of four conditions -- tautness together with finite type of B/J to A/I for every weak ideal of definition, the same with a cofinal system of weak ideals of definition, tautness together with A being topologically of finite type over B, and A being isomorphic as a topological B-algebra to a quotient of a restricted power series algebra by a closed ideal -- and adds that these conditions define a local property, that is, they satisfy the three locality axioms (statement lines 6559-6580). Three of the implications are immediate from the definitions, and the substance is the implication from the cofinal-system formulation to the first one. That argument is a genuine construction: an inverse system of quotients A_n with A_{n+1} modulo the image of J_n equal to A_n and with A its limit is produced, finite generation is transferred downwards along the system, generators of the first stage are lifted to A, the universal property of the restricted power series algebra produces a continuous map to A, surjectivity of the induced maps on the quotients is obtained from a local nilpotence criterion, and the exactness of the inverse limit of the resulting short exact sequences -- using that the transition maps between the kernels are surjective -- shows that the map from the restricted power series algebra to A is surjective and open, with closed kernel (proof lines 6583-6620). The locality axioms (1) and (2) are then treated by a second, independent argument, in which the induced diagram between the quotients is shown to have etale horizontal maps and the two directions are read off from an algebra lemma and from the descent lemma for finiteness along a faithfully flat etale extension (proof lines 6622-6655). The claim is H3: the equivalence and the locality verification rest on different mechanisms, and the first of them requires an inverse-limit construction with an explicit Mittag-Leffler step.

items.title: A formal algebraic space has a reduced algebraic space with a representable thickening onto it
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a formal algebraic space X over a scheme, a reduced algebraic space X_red together with a representable morphism to X which is a thickening, and asserts that morphisms from a reduced algebraic space into X factor uniquely through it (statement lines 2832-2838). The proof has three parts. The affine case is settled by writing the affine formal algebraic space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes whose transition morphisms are thickenings, so that all stages have isomorphic reductions; representability and the thickening property follow from the covering-by-thickenings lemma and from closure of thickenings under composition, and the author explicitly leaves the verification of the universal property to the reader, pointing at the four statements that make it routine (proof lines 2840-2854). The global case is a glueing construction: for the chosen affine presentation of X one takes the reductions of the members, observes that the fibre products of a reduction with a member are etale over that reduction and therefore reduced, so that the projections factor through the reductions of the members, identifies the resulting fibre products in three ways, and concludes that the two projections form an etale equivalence relation whose quotient is an algebraic space by the presentation theorem; the comparison diagram with the presentation is cartesian, and representability and the thickening property of the resulting morphism are then transferred along a surjective etale morphism by a bootstrap lemma and a descent lemma for representable transformations (proof lines 2856-2890). The third part proves the universal property in general: for a morphism from a reduced algebraic space, the fibre products with the members of the presentation are etale over the source and hence reduced, so each factors through the corresponding reduction, and since those fibre products form an etale covering of the source, the morphism itself factors through X_red (proof lines 2892-2907). The claim is H3: the affine computation, the equivalence-relation glueing with its three-way identification, the transfer of representability and of the thickening property along a cover, and the general universal property are four independent pieces of work.

items.title: Tautness of an arrow of complete weakly admissible rings is a local property
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an arrow of complete weakly admissible topological rings, the lemma states the equivalence of tautness with the existence of a compatible inverse system of quotients whose limit is the target, and adds that this condition satisfies the three locality axioms (statement lines 5465-5487). The proof is notable for giving the locality twice by different means. The first is geometric: by an earlier lemma the equivalent conditions translate into representability of the corresponding morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces by algebraic spaces, and since that condition is etale local on source and target all three axioms follow at once (proof lines 5489-5498). The second is algebraic and is carried out for two of the three axioms. For the first axiom the closures of the ideals generated by a weak ideal of definition of the base are traced through the two arrows, and the observation that as the chosen ideal runs over a fundamental system so do its closures is what gives the axiom (proof lines 5504-5519). For the second axiom the argument is a genuine computation: assuming faithful flatness of the extension and the condition for the composite, the intersection of the target with the closed ideal is rewritten in three steps -- using the description of a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero by kernels, and then faithful flatness -- to become the intersection of the ideals generated by the chosen ideal of the base with a system of ideals of definition, which is exactly the closure of the ideal generated by the chosen one; openness of that closure then gives the axiom (proof lines 5521-5548). The claim is H3: the geometric route and the algebraic route are independent arguments, and within the algebraic route the second axiom needs a three-step identification whose middle step rests on faithful flatness.

items.title: A pointed map of pointed spaces yields a long exact sequence of homotopy groups
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file homotopy.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 1080-1093 (book Theorem 8.4.6): a pointed map f : X \to Y with fiber F gives a long exact sequence of homotopy groups, which are groups except in the last three terms and abelian except in the last six. The statement records only the sequence and the algebraic structure, while the proof (source lines 1100-1129) has to establish exactness at every term: it reduces the theorem to exactness of the 0-truncation of a fiber sequence, proves the inclusion im \subseteq ker from functoriality together with f \circ g = 0, and then has to show ker \subseteq im for an element given only as a truncated equality, which forces two successive truncation inductions: one to lift the element of the 0-truncation to an element w of W, and one that uses the path-truncation equivalence to turn \tproj0{f(w)} = \tproj0{z_0} into a genuine path p : f(w) = z_0, after which (w,p) is the required preimage. The identification of the later maps with the negative of the induced maps on homotopy groups, and the resulting group and abelian-group structure, are then read off with thm:fiber-of-the-fiber and the Eckmann-Hilton argument; nothing of this reduction is visible in the statement.

items.title: The localized Chern classes are compatible with base change of finite type
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-loc-chern, for a morphism f : X' -> X locally of finite type with E' = f^*E and Z' = f^{-1}(Z), the lemma states that the class P_p(Z' -> X', E'), resp. c_p(Z' -> X', E'), constructed as in Lemma labelled lemma-independent-loc-chern from the base changed data is the restriction, in the sense of Remark labelled remark-restriction-bivariant, of P_p(Z -> X, E), resp. c_p(Z -> X, E) (statement lines 10823-10839). The proof unfolds the construction: b : W -> P^1_X and b' : W' -> P^1_{X'} come from More on Flatness, Lemma labelled flat-lemma-complex-and-divisor-blowup-pre applied to the triples (P^1_X, (P^1_X)_infinity, p^*E) and its base change, Q and Q' are the derived twist L eta of the pulled back perfect objects along the ideals of W_infinity and W'_infinity, and the base change lemma of More on Flatness, Lemma labelled flat-lemma-complex-and-divisor-blowup-base-change supplies a commutative square whose morphism g identifies W' with the strict transform and gives Q' = (q o g)^*Q (proof lines 10841-10866). It then recalls that P_p(Z -> X, E) = P'_p(Q) is built from b, Q and a closed subscheme T' of W_infinity with the two properties (a) and (b), that the precise choice of T' is immaterial by Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre-independent, and that Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-localized-chern-pre exhibits the restriction of P'_p(Q) to X' as the class constructed from the base changed blowing up r, the complex q^*Q and the inverse image q^{-1}(T') (proof lines 10868-10895). The second statement of Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre-independent gives P'_p(Q') = P'_p(q^*Q), and the identification P_p(Z' -> X', E') = P'_p(Q') closes the proof (proof lines 10897-10903). Seeing that the two constructions of the base changed class agree, and that the choice of T' does not matter, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A perfect complex whose cohomology is locally free on a dense open becomes of tor dimension at most one after a suitable admissible blowup
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X, a perfect object E of D(O_X) and a scheme theoretically dense open U such that every H^i(E|_U) is finite locally free of constant rank r_i, the lemma asserts the existence of a U-admissible blowup b : X' -> X with H^i(Lb^*E) a perfect O_{X'}-module of tor dimension at most 1 for all i (statement lines 13035-13044). The proof works affine locally: representing E|_V by a complex of free modules and setting k_i = r_{i+1} - r_{i+2} + ... + (-1)^{b-i+1} r_b, an explicitly omitted computation gives the rank rho_i of d_i over U cap V as -k_i + n_{i+1} - n_{i+2} + ... + (-1)^{b-i+1} n_b, and the ideal of rho_i by rho_i minors of d_i is introduced (proof lines 13046-13065). The proof then observes that this ideal agrees with the global ideal Fit_{i,k_i}(E), which is independent of the chosen complex by Lemma labelled lemma-fitting-ideals-complex, and also realises it as a Fitting ideal of the cokernel of d_i (proof lines 13067-13075). Blowing X up in the product of the ideals Fit_{i,k_i}(E) dominates each individual blowup b_i by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-blowing-up-two-ideals, each b_i is U-admissible by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-blowup-fitting-ideal, and one further small detail, explicitly omitted and compared with Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-dominate-admissible-blowups, shows that the product blowup is U-admissible (proof lines 13077-13086). After this reduction one may assume the Fitting ideals are invertible; choosing a finite free complex representing E|_V, the cokernels have tor dimension at most 1 by the blowup-of-fitting-ideal lemma, hence both the images and the kernels are finite locally free, and the short exact sequences 0 -> Im(d_{i-1}) -> Ker(d_i) -> H^i(E)|_V -> 0 give the conclusion (proof lines 13088-13103). Locating the right Fitting ideals whose blowup forces tor dimension at most one is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the two omitted details are recorded verbatim in the editorial notes.

items.title: Existence and universal property of the blowup making a complex and divisor into a good triple
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-complex-and-divisor the lemma produces a morphism b : X' -> X which is unique with the properties that the pullback D' = b^{-1}D is defined with (X', D', Lb^*M) a good triple, and that every h : Y -> X for which h^{-1}D is defined and (Y, h^{-1}D, Lh^*M) is a good triple factors uniquely through b; moreover on an affine chart (U, A, f, M^bullet) the restriction of b is the blowing up in the product of the ideals I_i(M^bullet, f), and on a quasi-compact open W it is a W minus D-admissible blowing up (statement lines 13587-13603). The construction blows up each affine chart U in the finitely generated product ideal I = prod_i I_i(M^bullet, f), notes that b_U^{-1}(U cap D) is defined by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-blow-up-pullback-effective-Cartier, that f^{r_i} lies in I_i hence b_U is U minus D-admissible, and that b_U factors through each individual blowup in I_i by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-blowing-up-two-ideals, so that the pullbacks of the I_i become invertible and (U', b^{-1}D, Lb^*M|_U) is a good triple by Lemma labelled lemma-pullback-triple-ideals-good (proof lines 13605-13636). The universal property over U is then checked by covering Y by affine charts where the ideals I_i(N^bullet, g) are invertible, using that the images of f and g differ by a unit and More on Algebra, Lemmas labelled more-algebra-lemma-eta-change-unit and more-algebra-lemma-ideal-well-defined to identify the ideals, after which the classical universal property of a blowup (Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-universal-property-blowing-up) gives the unique factorization (proof lines 13638-13662). The charts glue: the local morphisms agree on overlaps by the universal property, satisfy the cocycle condition, and descend to b : X' -> X by Constructions, Lemma labelled constructions-lemma-relative-glueing (proof lines 13664-13685); the final assertion on a quasi-compact W is proved by a finite affine cover, gluing the corrected ideals I_{t,i} = f_t^{N_i - sum_{j >= i} (-1)^{j - i} rk(M_t^j)} I_i(M_t^bullet, f_t) into finite type ideals I_i on W (proof lines 13687-13714). Two routine steps are dismissed as 'details omitted' (proof lines 13665 and 13681). Gluing the local blowups through their universal property and correcting the ideals so that they patch is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Two open immersions of finite type separated schemes over a common open can be made part of one separated finite type scheme by admissible blowups
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated S with open immersions U -> X_1 and U -> X_2 of schemes of finite type and separated over S, the lemma asserts the existence of a commutative diagram whose arrows X_i' -> X_i are U-admissible blowups, whose arrows X_i' -> X are open immersions, and whose X is separated and of finite type over S (statement lines 9646-9661). The proof works throughout with separated finite type schemes, so that the scheme theoretic image of an immersion is a closed subscheme containing the source as a dense open, and starts from X_12, the scheme theoretic image of U in X_1 x_S X_2, whose projections induce isomorphisms over U by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-of-partial-section (proof lines 9663-9680). It chooses U-admissible blowups X_i^i -> X_i making the strict transform X_12^i an open subscheme of X_i^i via Lemma labelled lemma-zariski-after-blowup with ideal I_i, observes that X_12^i -> X_12 is the blowup in p_i^{-1}I_i O_{X_12} by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-strict-transform, blows X_12 up in the product of the two pulled back ideals so that both transforms appear in one commutative square, and extends the resulting blowup to X_i^i using Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-extend-admissible-blowups (proof lines 9682-9708). The key point is that X'_12 -> X_1' x_S X_2' is an immersion which is proper, hence a closed immersion by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed, so glueing X_1' and X_2' along the common open X'_12 produces a scheme X which is finite type and separated over S by Lemma labelled lemma-check-separated; compositions of U-admissible blowups are again U-admissible by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-composition-admissible-blowups (proof lines 9710-9725). Producing one blowup of X_12 dominating both strict transforms and then gluing along it is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: After a suitable principal affine blowup a module that is free of rank r at the generic points of the closed fibres becomes free of rank r locally on the blowup
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an element f, an integer r, a finitely presented flat ring map R -> S with geometrically integral fibres, and a finite S-module M with M_f finitely presented which is free of rank r over S_q for every q = pS with f not in p, and it asserts that some finitely generated ideal I with V(f) = V(I) has the property that for all a in I and R' = R[I/a] the module M' = (M otimes_R R')/a-power torsion is locally free of rank r over S' = S otimes_R R', in the sense that at every prime p' of R' some g outside p'S' makes M'_g free of rank r (statement lines 8667-8691). The proof is announced as a generalisation of More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-blowup-module and first reduces to M finitely presented: a finite submodule K of the kernel of a surjection S^{oplus n} -> M with S^{oplus n}/K iso to M after inverting f is produced from hypothesis (4), and the comparison map between the two a-power torsion quotients is an isomorphism because a is a nonzerodivisor on the modified module (proof lines 8693-8718). It then uses the Fitting ideal J = Fit_r(M), writes S as a direct summand of a free R-module by Lemma labelled lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective-nonnoetherian, defines I' as the ideal generated by the coefficients of the elements of J and sets I = f I' (proof lines 8720-8732). The verification that V(f) = V(I) uses hypothesis (5) together with More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally (proof lines 8734-8744), and for a in I with a = f a' the Algebra lemmas on affine blowup and blowup with a principal generator give I'R' = a'R' with a' a nonzerodivisor, whence JS' is locally principal and More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-principal-fitting-ideal generates M' by r elements locally (proof lines 8746-8762). The proof closes by killing the Fitting ideal Fit_{r-1}(M') using More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-fitting-ideal-finite-locally-free and the containment S'_a inside a product of localisations supplied by Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-universally-flat (proof lines 8764-8779). Realising the right ideal I through coefficients of the Fitting ideal and then descending freeness from the Fitting ideal computation is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The localized class computed from a blowing up equals the localized Chern class of the perfect object it restricts to
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Assume (S, delta), X, Z, b : W -> P^1_X, Q, T and p satisfy the assumptions of Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre, and let F be a perfect object of D(O_X) such that Q restricts to the pullback of F over b^{-1}(A^1_X), F is zero or finite locally free of rank < p off Z in degree 0, and Q and F satisfy assumption (3) of Situation labelled situation-loc-chern; the lemma asserts that P'_p(Q), resp. c'_p(Q), equals P_p(Z -> X, F), resp. c_p(Z -> X, F) (statement lines 11164-11182). The proof first notes that the assumptions are stable under base change along X' -> X locally of finite type, reducing to the equality after capping with an arbitrary alpha in CH_k(X), and chooses beta in CH_{k+1}(W) restricting to the flat pullback of alpha as in the construction of C in Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-at-infty (proof lines 11184-11198). The body is a chain of eight equalities for c'_p(Q) cap alpha: the construction of c'_p(Q) in Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre, the replacement of the localized class by c_p(E -> W_infinity, Q|_{W_infinity}) by Lemma labelled lemma-loc-chern-agree, the base change identification of E = W'_infinity -> W_infinity with the pullback of W' -> W using Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-loc-chern, commutation with i'_infinity^*, the observation that c_p(W' -> W, Q) and c_p(Z' -> X, F) restrict to the same class over b^{-1}(A^1_X) so that (i'_infinity)^* annihilates the difference, the replacement of W'_infinity by W'_0 using that both are pullbacks of rationally equivalent divisors as in Lemma labelled lemma-support-cap-effective-Cartier, another use of bivariance, and finally W'_0 = Z with i_0^* beta = alpha (proof lines 11200-11244). Tracking which of the eight steps is base change, which is the defining property of C, and which is rational equivalence of the special and generic fibres is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Localized Chern classes of a derived tensor product are given by the universal polynomial formula in the two localized classes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-setup, for closed subschemes Z_1, Z_2 of X locally of finite type over S and perfect objects F_i with F_i zero off Z_i and satisfying assumption (3) of Situation labelled situation-loc-chern, the lemma with r_i = P_0(Z_i -> X, F_i) computes c_1 and c_2 of F_1 otimes^L F_2 on Z_1 cap Z_2 as the universal polynomials r_1 c_1(F_2) + r_2 c_1(F_1) and r_1 c_2(F_2) + r_2 c_2(F_1) + C(r_1,2) c_1(F_2)^2 + (r_1 r_2 - 1) c_1(F_1) c_1(F_2) + C(r_2,2) c_1(F_1)^2, together with the corresponding statements for the total Chern character and for P_p (statement lines 11524-11564). The proof first chooses the data b_i : W_i -> P^1_X with Q_i and T_i representing the localized classes, builds a common W as the closure of the graph of the isomorphism between b_1^{-1}(A^1_X) and b_2^{-1}(A^1_X), and uses Lemma labelled lemma-independent-loc-chern-bQ to replace both b_i by the common b with the pullbacks Lg_i^*Q_i (proof lines 11566-11592). It then records the resulting normalised situation (b an isomorphism over A^1_X, E_i the inverse image of Z_i, Q_i with the stated properties) and writes both c_p(Z_i -> X, F_i) and P_p(Z_i -> X, F_i) as (E_i -> Z_i)_* o c'_p(Q_i|_{E_i}) o C via the same lemma (proof lines 11594-11618). Since Q_1 otimes^L Q_2 satisfies the corresponding conditions for F_1 otimes^L F_2 with T_1 cup T_2, the same description applies on E_1 cap E_2, and Lemma labelled lemma-silly-tensor-product expands c'_p(Q|_{E_1 cap E_2}) and P'_p(Q|_{E_1 cap E_2}) in terms of the summands, after which Lemma labelled lemma-homomorphism-final turns polynomials in the restricted classes into polynomials in the unrestricted ones (proof lines 11620-11638). Reducing to a common blowing up through the graph closure and then transporting the polynomial identity from E_1 cap E_2 back to Z_1 cap Z_2 is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The total localized Chern class of a direct sum is the product of the total classes of the summands
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In the setting of Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre the lemma assumes that Q|_T is finite locally free of rank < p, takes a second perfect object Q' whose Chern classes are defined with Q'|_T finite locally free of rank < p' in cohomological degree 0, and with the truncated total classes c^{(p)}(Q) of Remark labelled remark-ring-loc-classes asserts c^{(p + p')}(Q oplus Q') = c^{(p)}(Q) c^{(p')}(Q') in A^{(p + p')}(Z -> X) (statement lines 10498-10517). The proof first disposes of the degrees below p + p': the image of c'_i(Q) in A^p(X) is c_i(Q|_{X x {0}}) by Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre, so those degrees follow from the additivity stated in Lemma labelled lemma-additivity-on-perfect (proof lines 10519-10527). For degrees at least p + p' it writes E for the inverse image of Z in W_infinity, invokes the equality c^{(p + p')}(Q|_E oplus Q'|_E) = c^{(p)}(Q|_E) c^{(p')}(Q'|_E) of Lemma labelled lemma-silly-sum-c, and uses the description c'_p(Q oplus Q') = (E -> Z)_* o c'_p(Q|_E oplus Q'|_E) o C to reduce to the identity (E -> Z)_* o c^{(p)}_i(Q|_E) c^{(p')}_j(Q'|_E) o C = c^{(p)}_i(Q) c^{(p')}_j(Q') for i + j = n (proof lines 10529-10547). It then splits into the three position cases i >= p and j >= p', i >= p and j < p, and i < p and j >= p', which are settled by Lemma labelled lemma-silly, the second part of Lemma labelled lemma-homomorphism and the commutation of capping with bivariant Chern classes in Lemma labelled lemma-cap-commutative-chern respectively (proof lines 10549-10600). Matching the two different products on the localized classes through the three cases and the insertion of the pushforwards is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
