items.title: The Gysin pullback of the normal cone of Z in X is the normal cone of Z in Y
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: With the notation of the surrounding section, for closed subschemes Z contained in Y inside X the lemma asserts o^*[C_Z X]_n = [C_Z Y]_{n-1} in CH_{n-1}(Y x_{o, C_Y X} C_Z X) (statement lines 12259-12266). The proof compares the two blowups W -> P^1_X in infinity(Z) and W' -> P^1_X in infinity(Y); since infinity(Z) is contained in infinity(Y) the inclusion of ideal sheaves gives a map of graded algebras and hence a canonical rational map U -> W' with U open in W, by Constructions, Lemma labelled constructions-lemma-morphism-relative-proj (proof lines 12268-12278). Two local calculations, both explicitly omitted, identify U as containing the complement of the fibre over infinity together with C_Z X, and identify the induced morphism U_infinity -> W'_infinity with the canonical morphism C_Z X -> C_Y X of normal cones (proof lines 12280-12287). The proof then takes W'' the strict transform of P^1_Y in W, which is the blowup of P^1_Y in infinity(Z) by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-strict-transform, so that (W'' cap U)_infinity = C_Z Y, and compares the two ways of applying the Gysin maps: on the one hand (i'_infinity)^* i^* [U]_{n+1} = i_infinity^* i^* [U]_{n+1} = i_infinity^* [(W'' cap U)_infinity]_{n+1} = [C_Z Y]_n using that i_infinity^* kills classes supported over infinity and that i^*[U] and [W''] agree over A^1, while on the other hand the same expression equals i^* i_infinity^* [U]_{n+1} = i^* [U_infinity] = o^* [C_Y X]_n using that (i'_infinity)^* and i^* commute by Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-commutes-gysin and the factorization of the fibre over infinity as o followed by the open immersion C_Y X -> W'_infinity (proof lines 12289-12322). Comparing the two evaluations of the same Gysin pullback is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; note that the two local calculations are left to the reader by the author, which we record verbatim in the editorial notes.

items.title: Computing the pullback of a sheaf along a morphism from a colimit of sites
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites.tex (Sites and Sheaves)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file sites.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the pullback of a sheaf along the morphism of sites from a colimit of sites: for an object at a finite level the value of the pullback is the filtered colimit, over the stages mapping to that level, of the pullbacks of the sheaf along the transition morphisms (statement lines 4075-4087). The proof is a complete argument: continuity is taken from the companion construction and exactness is reduced to left exactness because the pullback is a left adjoint (proof lines 4089-4098); the author builds a presheaf with the displayed values, checks functoriality and the sheaf condition by reducing coverings to a finite level and commuting filtered colimits with finite limits (proof lines 4101-4130); identifies it with the pullback through the universal property of the adjunction (proof lines 4135-4168); and deduces left exactness from the formula (proof lines 4171-4179). The non-formal content is the construction of the sheaf and its universal property. The claim is H2: a construction with the verification carried out in stages.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites.tex (Sites and Sheaves)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file sites.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four statements about the canonical map from the filtered colimit of the global sections of a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets into the global sections of its colimit: injectivity under injective transition maps, injectivity over a quasi-compact topos, bijectivity when both hold, and bijectivity under an additional hypothesis on a set of objects of the topos (statement lines 3731-3760). The proof treats each part: part (1) via separated presheaves and the plus construction (proof lines 3763-3772); part (2) by forming the equalizers of two compatible families and using that the equalizer of the colimit maps is the filtered colimit of the stagewise equalizers together with quasi-compactness of the final sheaf (proof lines 3775-3793); part (3) by pulling the stages back along a map into the colimit and using quasi-compactness (proof lines 3797-3802); and part (4) by producing a quasi-compact object surjecting onto the final sheaf, factoring a lift through finitely many stages, and repeating the equalizer argument for its square (proof lines 3805-3869). The non-formal content is the equalizer bookkeeping with the quasi-compactness input. The claim is H2: several written-out arguments with each input named.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that pullback along a morphism of ringed topoi preserves seven local properties of modules: locally free, finite locally free, locally generated by sections, locally generated by r sections, finite type, quasi-coherent, and finite presentation. H2: the reduction to the left exact continuous case and the transfer through the diagram of localizations are the substance.

items.title: The diagonal of a formal algebraic space is representable, a monomorphism, locally quasi-finite, locally of finite type and separated
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts five properties of the diagonal of a formal algebraic space over a scheme: representability, monomorphism, local quasi-finiteness, local finite typeness and separatedness (statement lines 2666-2671). The proof produces the first by testing against a pair of morphisms from schemes: for such a pair the fibre product is a sheaf, and applying the presentation of the space and base changing gives a jointly surjective family of representable etale morphisms from schemes onto that fibre product, so the fibre product is an algebraic space by the bootstrap theorem (proof lines 2673-2690). The same computation shows that the morphism from that fibre product to the fibre product of the two schemes over the base is a monomorphism, and that it is locally quasi-finite because after precomposing with the family it becomes a composition of a closed immersion and an etale morphism; a proposition on locally quasi-finite separated algebraic spaces then makes the fibre product a scheme, which is representability of the diagonal (proof lines 2683-2695). The remaining four properties are then deduced from that: the same computation shows the diagonal is a monomorphism and locally quasi-finite, and the principle allowing properties of representable transformations to be checked on schemes identifies the diagonal with a monomorphism of schemes, hence separated, and with a locally quasi-finite morphism of schemes, hence locally of finite type (proof lines 2697-2712). The claim is H2: the first part is a genuine argument with a base-change family and a reduction from algebraic spaces to schemes, and the rest is a two-step transfer, with each step named rather than assumed.

items.title: Formal schemes are sheaves for the fpqc topology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the functor of points of a formal scheme satisfies the sheaf condition for fpqc coverings (statement lines 646-652). The proof reduces the topology to the case of a Zariski covering together with a covering by a single faithfully flat ring map, and uses that the sheaf condition for Zariski coverings was already observed when the functor of points was introduced (proof lines 654-660). The substance is the descent of a morphism along a faithfully flat ring map, and it is carried out in three steps. First, a morphism from the spectrum of the faithfully flat extension whose two pullbacks to the tensor square agree is shown to come from a set-theoretic map on the base, by a descent statement for maps of sets; continuity of that map is then deduced from the corresponding quotient topology statement and continuity of the given morphism (proof lines 662-671). Second, the problem is localised: an affine formal open subscheme containing the image of a chosen point is selected, a standard affine open neighbourhood of the point on which the image stays inside that subscheme is chosen, and the restriction of the morphism above it is converted into a continuous ring map into a localisation of the extension, whose two further localisations agree by hypothesis (proof lines 673-684). Third, the ring map is descended: since the localisation of the faithfully flat extension is still faithfully flat, the equalizer statement for a faithfully flat ring map identifies the fixed ring, so the ring map factors uniquely through a ring map to the localisation of the base, which has the same open kernel and hence is continuous, and therefore defines a morphism on the chosen open (proof lines 684-692). The conclusion that the local morphisms glue is left to the reader (proof lines 694-700). The claim is H2: one descent argument is carried through three stages -- set-theoretic, topological and algebraic -- and each stage is displayed, with the single omitted step being the routine glueing of morphisms that have already been constructed locally.

items.title: Three equivalent formulations of a local property of morphisms of complete weakly admissible rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of locally countably indexed formal algebraic spaces and a local property P of morphisms of complete weakly admissible topological rings, the lemma states the equivalence of three formulations: that every commutative square of representable etale affine formal algebraic spaces over the two sides corresponds to a morphism with the property; that there is a covering of the target and, over each member, a covering of the base change such that the corresponding ring morphisms all have the property; and that there is a covering of the source with a factorisation of each member through an affine formal algebraic space etale and representable over the target such that the corresponding ring morphism has the property (statement lines 5103-5129). Two of the three implications are immediate, and the substance is the step from the third formulation to the first, which is a finite chase through the locality axioms. Given a square as in the first formulation, coverings of the relevant fibre products are chosen, quasi-compactness of the source of the square is used to select finitely many members of one of them so that the resulting disjoint union surjects onto it, and then the three axioms are applied in turn: the first to transport the property along the completions of etale ring maps appearing in the diagram, the second twice, once with identities standing in for the surjective flat map and once at the end with a degenerate extension, and the third to pass to the finite disjoint union, after which the surjectivity of the covering morphism is converted into a faithfully flat etale ring map whose completion carries the property back to the morphism of the square by the second axiom (proof lines 5131-5189). The claim is H2: the argument is a single chase, but each of its four moves -- choosing the finite refinement by quasi-compactness, and applying the three axioms at the points where their hypotheses hold -- has to be justified against the statements of the axioms.

items.title: Formal completion of an affine formal algebraic space along a closed subset keeps its type
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an affine formal algebraic space X and a closed subset T of its reduction, the lemma asserts five things about the formal completion of X along T: that it is an affine formal algebraic space, that it is McQuillan when X is, that it is countably indexed when X is and the complement of T in the reduction is quasi-compact, that it is adic* under the same quasi-compactness assumption when X is, and that it is Noetherian when X is (statement lines 8093-8120). The first part is a citation, and the second follows by recognising the completion as a morphism to the spectrum of the ring satisfying the second defining property of a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 8122-8128). The substance is the third part: since X is countably indexed it is the formal spectrum of a ring with a countable fundamental system of weak ideals of definition, quasi-compactness of the complement of T produces a finitely generated ideal of the first quotient cutting T out, lifts of its generators are chosen, and then the universal property of the completion is used to show that the completion is the formal spectrum of the limit of the quotients of the ring by the ideals generated by the powers of the chosen ideal together with the members of the fundamental system -- an explicit computation in which the nilpotence of the images of the chosen generators is the key observation (proof lines 8130-8147). The fourth part repeats that computation verbatim in the adic case, where the fundamental system may be taken to be the powers of a single finitely generated ideal, and the author marks some details as omitted (proof lines 8149-8156). The fifth part observes that in the Noetherian case quasi-compactness of the complement is automatic, and then applies the same description together with the corresponding algebra statement on completions of Noetherian rings (proof lines 8158-8165). The claim is H2: one computation is carried out in full and its two variants are then read off in the same way, with the McQuillan and Noetherian cases reduced to cited statements.

items.title: A Borel reduction that eventually satisfies push-forward preserves Scott sentence complexity above a threshold
items.author: David Gonzalez, Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled proposition at source0.tex lines 696-704: if a Borel reduction Phi between the model classes of two vocabularies has Borel image and eventually satisfies push-forward, then above a threshold on the Scott rank the Scott sentence complexities of A and Phi(A) agree. The statement gives no bound and no construction, while the proof (source lines 706-718) has to manufacture one from three independent pieces of data: the measurability rank lambda of the reduction, the rank beta of a formula describing its image, and the rank delta from which the push-forward property starts to hold. It pushes a Scott sentence of A forward to one for Phi(A) by conjoining the pushed formula with the description of the image, pulls a Scott sentence of Phi(A) back with the pull-back theorem to get one for A of rank lambda plus epsilon, and then reads off the threshold at which the two bounds meet. The interaction of the three ranks is the whole content and it is invisible in the statement.

items.title: Linear orders of successor Scott sentence complexities exist in all three complexity classes
items.author: David Gonzalez, Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled corollary at source0.tex lines 1361-1368: there are linear orders of Scott sentence complexity S_infinity(alpha plus n) for every countable alpha and n at least 4, of complexity dS_infinity(alpha plus n) for n at least 1, and of complexity P_infinity(alpha plus n) for n at least 1. The statement lists nine families and gives no examples, and the proof (source lines 1370-1392) has to produce each family by combining a base example with the shift by Z^alpha, and in each case the optimality of the resulting rank must be secured: for the first family by the ranked lower bound between the order and its companion, for the second and third by the known back-and-forth analysis of well-orderings, which the author invokes for omega^alpha times two and for omega^alpha. Which base example produces which successor rank, and where the optimality comes from in each of the three classes, is exactly what the statement omits.

items.title: Formulas over a structure translate to formulas over its labelled tree at the same quantifier complexity, and back
items.author: David Gonzalez, Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 234-249: for every structure A and every infinitary formula over its vocabulary there is a formula of the same quantifier rank over the labelled tree of A that holds at every node above a tuple exactly when the original holds at that tuple, and conversely every formula over the tree has an equivalent formula over A of the same rank. The statement contains no construction, and the proof (source lines 250-286) has to build both directions: the push-forward direction by disjunctive normal form for the quantifier-free case, then an induction whose existential step replaces a quantifier by a quantifier over successor nodes, with the height and label conditions read off the tree; the pull-back direction is a different kind of argument, constructing a parameterised Turing computable embedding by choosing, for a fixed tuple of nodes, the lexicographically least finite tuples whose subtrees are isomorphic to the ones described by that tuple, and then invoking the pull-back theorem along it. Neither the disjunctive normal form reduction nor the embedding construction is visible in the statement.

items.title: Operational Chow cohomology of a scheme over a base of dimension one is Chow homology in complementary degrees
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a base (S, delta) of dimension one and a scheme X locally of finite type over S, the lemma asserts a canonical identification A^p(X -> S) = CH_{1-p}(X) for all integers p (statement lines 14733-14741). The proof constructs both directions: sending a bivariant class c to c cap [S]_1 gives a map A^p(X -> S) -> CH_{1-p}(X), and conversely an element alpha of CH_{1-p}(X) defines c_alpha by c_alpha cap alpha' = alpha times alpha' in CH_{n-p}(X x_S X') (proof lines 14743-14748 and 14780-14784). To see that c_alpha is a bivariant class the proof writes alpha = sum n_i [X_i] as in Definition labelled definition-cycles, so that g : coprod_i X_i -> X is proper, and builds the class componentwise: if X_i dominates an irreducible component of S then p_i : X_i -> S is flat and xi_i = p_i^*, while if p_i factors through a closed point s_i then xi_i = (p'_i)^* o c_i with c_i the Gysin homomorphism of s_i in S; since A^p(coprod_i X_i -> S) is the product of the A^p(X_i -> S), the sum xi = sum n_i xi_i makes sense and g_* o xi is bivariant by Lemma labelled lemma-push-proper-bivariant, and the proof states that the reader easily verifies that c_alpha equals this class (proof lines 14750-14778). The two constructions are then shown to be mutually inverse: one direction is c_alpha cap [S]_1 = alpha, and for the other, with alpha = c cap [S]_1, it suffices by Lemma labelled lemma-bivariant-zero to prove c cap [X'] = c_alpha cap [X'] for integral X' locally of finite type over S, where either p' : X' -> S is flat of relative dimension dim_delta(X') - 1 and [X'] = (p')^*[S]_1 or X' -> S factors through a closed point and [X'] = (p')^*(s -> S)^*[S]_1, after which commutation of bivariant classes with flat pullback and Gysin maps finishes the argument (proof lines 14786-14804). Splitting the construction of the class along the two kinds of components, and then reducing the inverse identity to the two cases for an integral test scheme, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the step called easy by the author is recorded verbatim in the editorial notes.

items.title: The top localized Chern class of the section of a projective bundle vanishes below the rank and is a factorial multiple of the vector bundle pullback
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally free sheaf C of rank r on X, the lemma considers the morphisms X -> E = Proj_X(Sym^*(C)[T]) -> X and asserts that c_t(i_* O_X) = 0 for t = 1, ..., r - 1 and that p^* o pi_* o c_r(i_* O_X) = (-1)^{r - 1} (r - 1)! j^* in A^0(C -> E), where j : C -> E and p : C -> X are the structure maps of the vector bundle C (statement lines 12541-12563). The proof first resolves i_* O_X by the Koszul complex on the map pi^*C otimes O_E(-1) -> O_E, which vanishes exactly along i(X), so that i_* O_X is perfect with defined Chern classes; the vanishing for t < r comes from Lemma labelled lemma-compute-koszul, which also gives c_r(i_* O_X) = -(r-1)! c_r(pi^*C otimes O_E(-1)) (proof lines 12565-12580). Lemma labelled lemma-chern-classes-dual rewrites the latter as (-1)^r c_r(pi^*C^vee otimes O_E(1)), a bundle with a section s vanishing exactly along i(X) (proof lines 12582-12586). After replacing X by a scheme locally of finite type over X, the proof reduces the equality to the effect of both sides on an element alpha in CH_*(E): since C -> X is a vector bundle every cycle class on C is p^* beta by Lemma labelled lemma-vectorbundle, so Lemma labelled lemma-restrict-to-open lets alpha be written as pi^* beta + gamma with gamma supported on E minus C, and it suffices to check p^*(pi_*(c_r(pi^*C^vee otimes O_E(1)) cap [W])) = j^*[W] for integral W either disjoint from C or of the form pi^{-1}Y, where the section s and Lemma labelled lemma-top-chern-class give 0 in case (a) and [i(Y)] in case (b) (proof lines 12588-12610; the author ends with 'The result follows easily from this; details omitted'). Recognising that the cycle class on the projective bundle decomposes into a pulled back part and a part supported off the vector bundle, and then reading off the two cases from the zero locus of the section, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The virtual normal sheaf construction is well defined as a bivariant class and is compatible with base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the construction of the surrounding section defines a bivariant class c(Z -> X, N) in the completion A^*(Z -> X)^wedge, that this construction is compatible with base change as in Lemma labelled lemma-pullback-virtual-normal-sheaf, and that c lies in A^r(Z -> X) when N has constant rank r (statement lines 11911-11924). The proof defines the class by the displayed equation i_* o j^* o C = p^* o c(Z -> X, N), which is legitimate because both i_* o j^* o C and p^* are bivariant classes by Lemmas labelled lemma-flat-pullback-bivariant and lemma-push-proper-bivariant and because p^* is bijective on Chow groups by Lemma labelled lemma-vectorbundle (proof lines 11926-11934). For compatibility with base change it writes c and c' for the two classes, reduces by a formal argument to checking c' cap alpha' = c cap alpha' for alpha' in CH_k(X'), and compares the two computations of the class attached to alpha': the commutative diagram of W's, W_infinity's and normal cones induces closed immersions W' -> W x_{P^1_X} P^1_{X'}, W'_infinity -> W_infinity x_X X' and C_{Z'} X' -> C_Z X x_Z Z', and Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-at-infty-independent plus Lemma labelled lemma-flat-pullback-proper-pushforward show that the classes obtained from the two morphisms agree after pushforward and pullback along C_{Z'} X' -> N' (proof lines 11936-11991). Seeing that the defining equation determines a class and that the diagram comparison reduces the base change statement to a pushforward identity is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the reduction step is called formal by the author and is recorded verbatim in the editorial notes.

items.title: The colimit of the structure sheaf along the Frobenius is a sheaf for the h topology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a prime p and a scheme S over F_p, the lemma states that on the big h site (Sch/S)_h there is a unique sheaf F with F(X) = colim_F Gamma(X, O_X) for every quasi-compact and quasi-separated object X, the colimit being along the Frobenius action (statement lines 11854-11863). The proof takes the Zariski sheafification of the functor X -> colim_F Gamma(X, O_X), notes that on quasi-compact and quasi-separated X the sections are unchanged by Sheaves, Lemma labelled sheaves-lemma-directed-colimits-sections, and reduces the sheaf property to conditions (1), (2), (3) and (4) of Lemma labelled lemma-refine-check-h (proof lines 11865-11877). Condition (1) is immediate from the sheafification; condition (2) is reduced to the fact that O is an fppf sheaf (Descent, Lemma labelled descent-lemma-sheaf-condition-holds) together with the commutation of colim_F with equalizers of F_p-algebras (proof lines 11879-11884). Condition (3) is turned into an explicit algebra problem: given a', a'' with F^n(a' - a'') in fA + J one must produce a and m with a - F^m(a') in J and a - F^m(a'') in fA, uniquely up to the replacement (a, m) going to (F(a), m + 1), and the proof does this by writing F^n(a' - a'') = fh + g and taking a = F^n(a') - g with m = n, then proving uniqueness by showing a - a_1 is nilpotent and hence killed by a large power of F (proof lines 11886-11910). Condition (4) follows from Lemma labelled lemma-funny-blow-up and the fact that E = P^1_Z in that example (proof lines 11912-11920). Turning the two sheaf conditions into the concrete algebra problem with a uniqueness statement modulo Frobenius is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The injectivity lemma holds over a henselian local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if in Situation labelled situation-mod-injective the ring A is henselian, then the conclusion holds, namely that N is A-flat and finitely presented over B and that u is universally injective (statement lines 7072-7076; the statement refers back to the situation rather than repeating the three assertions). The proof first reduces to B essentially of finite presentation over A and N of finite presentation over B by Lemma labelled lemma-reduce-finite-type-injective-into-flat-mod-m, and handles the extra assumption that N is flat over A: then N is a filtered colimit of free A-modules F_i with transition maps injective modulo the maximal ideal by Lemma labelled lemma-flat-finite-type-local-colimit-free, each composition F_i -> M is A-universally injective by Lemma labelled lemma-universally-injective-local, and a colimit of universally injective maps is universally injective (proof lines 7078-7092). In the general case, Theorem labelled theorem-flattening-local produces a finitely generated ideal I of A such that N/IN is flat over A/I and N/I^2N is not flat over A/I^2 unless I = 0; the previous paragraph applies to u modulo I, and the proof writes the commutative diagram with exact rows relating M otimes_A I/I^2, M/I^2M, M/IM and their N counterparts, uses right exactness of the tensor product and flatness of M over A (proof lines 7094-7112). The left vertical arrow is identified as N/IN otimes_{A/I} I/I^2 -> M/IM otimes_{A/I} I/I^2, hence injective, and a diagram chase shows that the lower left arrow is injective, which by Algebra, Remark labelled algebra-remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal says that Tor^1_{A/I^2}(I/I^2, M/I^2) vanishes; Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-what-does-it-mean then makes N/I^2N flat over A/I^2, contradicting the choice of I unless I = 0 (proof lines 7114-7122). Turning the failure of flatness into the vanishing of a Tor group by a diagram chase over I/I^2 is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: When the object vanishes over T the localized P classes are the universal polynomials in the localized Chern classes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In the setting of Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre with the additional assumption that Q|_T is zero, the lemma asserts the explicit polynomial relations P'_1(Q) = c'_1(Q), P'_2(Q) = c'_1(Q)^2 - 2c'_2(Q), P'_3(Q) = c'_1(Q)^3 - 3c'_1(Q)c'_2(Q) + 3c'_3(Q) and P'_4(Q) = c'_1(Q)^4 - 4c'_1(Q)^2c'_2(Q) + 4c'_1(Q)c'_3(Q) + 2c'_2(Q)^2 - 4c'_4(Q), and so on, with the multiplication of Remark labelled remark-ring-loc-classes (statement lines 10435-10447). The proof first notes that the statement makes sense because the zero sheaf has rank less than 1 so all c'_p(Q) are defined, and recalls that P'_p(Q) and c'_p(Q) were built from the class C and the restricted classes on E, so that Lemma labelled lemma-silly-compose already gives the desired relation between P'_p(Q|_E) and c'_p(Q|_E) (proof lines 10449-10462). Since P'_p(Q) = (E -> Z)_* o P'_p(Q|_E) o C and c'_p(Q) = (E -> Z)_* o c'_p(Q|_E) o C, it suffices to show that the products of the a_p = c'_p(Q) agree with the pushforward-composed products of the b_p = c'_p(Q|_E), and for r > 1 the proof unwinds the multiplication of Remark labelled remark-ring-loc-classes as insertions of the pushforwards between factors (Remark labelled remark-res-push), uses (E -> W_infinity)_* o b_{p_i} = c_{p_i}(Q|_{W_infinity}) from Lemma labelled lemma-silly and C o (Z -> X)_* o a_{p_i} = c_{p_i}(Q|_{W_infinity}) o C from Lemma labelled lemma-homomorphism for i >= 2, and observes that both sides of the desired equality reduce to (E -> Z)_* o c'_{p_1}(Q|_E) o c_{p_2}(Q|_{W_infinity}) o ... o c_{p_r}(Q|_{W_infinity}) o C (proof lines 10464-10496; the author inserts 'Some details omitted' before handling r > 1 while the reduction itself is written out). Controlling the nested insertions of the pushforwards in the product to make the two expressions coincide is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The injectivity lemma holds over a valuation ring: the module is flat and finitely presented and the map is universally injective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if in Situation labelled situation-mod-injective the ring A is a valuation ring, then the conclusion of the situation holds, namely that the module N is A-flat and of finite presentation over B and that u is universally injective (statement lines 7157-7161; the statement refers back to the situation instead of repeating the three assertions). The proof first recalls that over a valuation ring an A-module is flat exactly when it is torsion free by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat, lets T be the A-torsion of N, notes u(T) = 0 and that N/T is A-flat, hence finitely presented over B by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, so that T is a finite B-module by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-extension (proof lines 7163-7176). Since N/T is A-flat one has T/m_A T contained in N/m_A N by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-flat-tor-zero, and the injectivity of the induced map u-bar forces T/m_A T = 0, whence T = 0 by Nakayama's lemma, giving the flatness and finite presentation assertions (proof lines 7178-7184). For universal injectivity the proof invokes Algebra, Theorem labelled algebra-theorem-universally-exact-criteria to reduce to the injectivity of N otimes_A Q -> M otimes_A Q for finitely presented Q, uses More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-generalized-valuation-ring-modules to reduce to Q = A/(a) with a a nonzero element of the maximal ideal, and then takes x in N with u(x) in aM: by Lemma labelled lemma-flat-finite-type-local-valuation-ring-has-content the element x has a content ideal I, which is finitely generated by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-content-finitely-generated and hence principal, say I = (b), because A is a valuation ring; More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-equal-content shows u(x) has the same content ideal, so (b) is contained in (a) by More on Algebra, Definition labelled more-algebra-definition-content-ideal, and x in bN gives x in aN, which is the required injectivity (proof lines 7186-7203). Reducing universal injectivity to a content ideal computation for a principal ideal in a valuation ring is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The absolutely weakly normal structure sheaf is a sheaf for the ph topology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For the big ph site (Sch/S)_{ph} the lemma asserts that the rule X -> Gamma(X^{awn}, O_{X^{awn}}) is a sheaf (statement lines 11990-11999). The proof checks conditions (1) and (2) of Topologies, Lemma labelled topologies-lemma-characterize-sheaf: condition (1) holds because the formation of X^{awn} commutes with open coverings by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-seminormalization and its proof (proof lines 12001-12008). For condition (2) it lets pi : Y -> X be a surjective proper morphism and takes f in the equalizer of the two maps Gamma(Y^{awn}, O_{Y^{awn}}) -> Gamma((Y x_X Y)^{awn}, O_{(Y x_X Y)^{awn}}); viewed as a morphism f : Y^{awn} -> A^1_X, its scheme theoretic image Z is closed in A^1_X, proper over X, and Z -> X is finite and surjective by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-is-proper and Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-finite-proper (proof lines 12010-12028). The proof then shows Z -> X is injective on field valued points: two k-points z_1, z_2 of Z equalized by Z -> X are first lifted through the surjectivity of Y^{awn} -> Z to K-points y_1, y_2, then tested against k-algebra maps K -> Omega for an algebraically closed extension of very large cardinality, where the universal homeomorphism (Y x_X Y)^{awn} -> Y^{awn} x_X Y^{awn} lets the compositions be lifted to (Y x_X Y)^{awn} and the equalizer property gives sigma_1(lambda_1) = sigma_2(lambda_2); a standard lemma on field extensions yields lambda_1 = lambda_2 (proof lines 12030-12058, where the field-theoretic step is dismissed with 'details omitted'). Consequently Z -> X is universally injective by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-universally-injective and hence a universal homeomorphism by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-universal-homeomorphism, and the map g : X^{awn} -> Z obtained from the universal property satisfies g o pi^{wan} = f, so f comes from an element of Gamma(X^{awn}, O_{X^{awn}}) (proof lines 12060-12074). Turning condition (2) into a statement about the scheme theoretic image and then proving it is a universal homeomorphism by a large-cardinality field argument is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A universally closed morphism of schemes is quasi-compact
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a universally closed morphism of schemes is quasi-compact, so that universal closedness cannot hold for a morphism that fails to be quasi-compact (statement lines 9985-9991). The counted proof is a contrapositive argument of real substance: after reducing to an affine base it builds an auxiliary affine space with one coordinate per affine chart of the source, cuts out a closed subset of the fibre product encoding the failure of the charts to cover, produces a point over a strategically chosen bad point of the base that escapes the image on that fibre, and then uses a polynomial vanishing on the image together with the invertibility of one coefficient to construct a point of the closed subset whose image avoids the zero locus of that polynomial, contradicting closedness (proof lines 9993-10047). It is H2: every step is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are standard criteria for quasi-compactness and for points of fibre products.

items.difficulty_reason: The Artin-Tate lemma states that if R is Noetherian, S is a finitely generated R-algebra and T is an R-subalgebra over which S is finite, then T is of finite type over R (statement lines 12513-12519). The construction of S' so that it is visibly finite over T' is the substance of the argument. H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for an ideal I and a multiplicative subset S of a ring R, every finite module over the localised quotient lifts to a finite R-module, and every finitely presented module lifts to a finitely presented R-module, in both cases with the localised quotient by I recovering the given module (statement lines 31706-31718). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map from R to S and S-modules L, M, N, the composite of a differential operator D of order k with one D' of order k' is again a differential operator, of order at most k + k' (statement lines 34900-34906). The splitting trick is the substance and the author displays it explicitly. H2.

items.title: On a vector space of dimension below the cardinality of the field some monic polynomial in any operator is not invertible
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a nonzero vector space V over a field k whose dimension as a cardinal is smaller than the cardinality of k, the lemma produces, for any linear operator T, a monic polynomial P with P(T) not invertible (statement lines 7089-7096). The proof is a contradiction from the opposite assumption: if every monic polynomial in T were invertible then V would carry a k(t)-vector space structure, whose dimension over k is at least the cardinality of k because the elements 1/(t - lambda) are k-linearly independent, contradicting the bound on the dimension of V (proof lines 7098-7103). The cardinal comparison rather than an algebraic computation is what settles the statement. H2.

The pigeonhole step choosing the bad factor is what drives the construction, and the author spells it out. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if R to S is faithfully flat and the base change M tensor S is countably generated, then M itself is countably generated (statement lines 22601-22606). The proof does not use the isomorphism criterion for descent in general: it writes each of countably many generators of the base change as a finite sum of pure tensors, takes the submodule generated by the resulting countable family of coefficients, observes that the induced map on base changes is surjective because the image contains the generators, and applies faithful flatness to upgrade surjectivity to equality (proof lines 22608-22617). Using faithful flatness to detect equality of submodules is the step that carries the argument, and countability is preserved because each generator uses only finitely many coefficients. H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a graded ideal I contained in the positive-degree part and not contained in any of finitely many homogeneous primes contains a homogeneous element of positive degree avoiding all of them (statement lines 13846-13853). The proof does not reduce to the general prime avoidance lemma: it inducts on the number of primes, and in the critical case where the previously chosen homogeneous element lies in the last prime it uses that I times the product of the other primes is not contained in the last prime, takes a homogeneous witness, and combines the two witnesses as x to the degree of y plus y to the degree of x (proof lines 13855-13865). That swap of exponents is the step that makes the result homogeneous, and the author displays it. H2.

items.title: Choosing a p-power exponent that brings a sum of two variables into a prescribed subring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a prime p and positive integers n, m the lemma produces an exponent a such that both the p^a-th power of x+y and p^a(x+y) lie in the subring generated by p^n-th powers and p^n-multiples of x and of y (statement lines 11030-11035). The proof does not invoke a general binomial congruence: it expands the power, decomposes the exponents against p^n and p^m, reduces the claim to the divisibility of a multinomial coefficient by a p-power determined by the remainders, and then estimates the p-adic valuation of those coefficients using the identity expressing a multinomial coefficient as p^a over i times a smaller one (proof lines 11037-11062). The valuation estimate that yields the explicit choice of a is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.

items.title: Separating finitely many multi-indices by a rapidly decreasing weight vector
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finite set of multi-indices in n variables one can choose a weight vector, rapidly decreasing in its entries, such that the weighted sums separate the multi-indices (statement lines 28144-28157). The proof does not invoke a generic linear functional: it defines the coordinatewise spreads A_i, selects the weights so that each dominates the weighted sum of all later coordinates, and then, from a vanishing weighted difference, looks at the first coordinate where the multi-indices differ and derives a contradiction unless that difference is zero, descending through the coordinates (proof lines 28159-28177). The choice of how fast the weights decrease is exactly what makes that first coordinate decisive, and the author writes the inequality chain out. H2.

items.title: The Hilbert-Samuel function for one ideal of definition is bounded by that for another after rescaling
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For two ideals of definition I and I' of a Noetherian local ring R and a finite module M, the lemma produces a constant a with the Hilbert-Samuel function for I at n bounded by that for I' at a n (statement lines 14351-14357). The proof does not compare the two functions term by term through their polynomial behaviour or the dimension theory behind them: it uses that ideals of definition contain powers of one another to find c with (I')^c contained in I, converts this into a surjection M/(I')^{c(n+1)}M onto M/I^{n+1}M, and then takes a = 2c - 1 (proof lines 14359-14363). Choosing the constant and turning the containment into the surjection is the whole content, and the author records exactly those steps. H2.

items.title: An idempotent splits the spectrum into the two basic open pieces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an idempotent e of a ring R the lemma states that the spectrum decomposes as the disjoint union of the two basic opens D(e) and D(1-e) (statement lines 3991-3998). The proof does not argue with the Zariski topology directly: it rewrites each of the two basic opens as the set of primes where the image of the idempotent in the residue field takes the value 1, respectively 0, using that an idempotent in a domain is 0 or 1, and then observes that these two conditions are complementary (proof lines 4000-4036). Passing to residue fields is what makes the two pieces visibly disjoint and covering, and the author writes both chains out. H2.

items.title: Injectivity into a product of localisations is equivalent to injectivity of the map multiplying by the elements
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For elements f_1, ..., f_n of a ring R and an R-module M, the lemma states that the map into the product of the localisations M_{f_i} is injective exactly when the map multiplying m by the tuple (f_1 m, ..., f_n m) is injective (statement lines 4621-4632). The proof does not compute with fractions: it rewrites the first condition as the statement that an element killed by powers of all the f_i vanishes, gets one direction immediately, and proves the converse by induction on the sum of the exponents, reducing in the induction step to a smaller total exponent by multiplying the element by one of the f_i (proof lines 4634-4648). The induction on the total exponent is the substance, and the author writes each step out. H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map from A to B and a multiplicative subset S of A, the integral closure of S^{-1}A in S^{-1}B is the localisation of the integral closure of A in B (statement lines 7813-7819). The clearing of denominators is the substance, and the author displays both relations in full. H2.

items.title: Integrality over an ideal is equivalent to integrality of st over a Rees algebra
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a ring map from R to S, an ideal I of R and the subring A of R[t] generated by R plus It, the lemma states that an element s of S is integral over I exactly when st is integral over A (statement lines 8582-8592). The proof does not pass to a Rees-algebra filtration: it takes a monic relation for st with coefficients in A, replaces each coefficient by its homogeneous part of the complementary degree, argues by degree to discard the other components, and reads off integrality of s over I; the converse is the explicit multiplication of coefficients by powers of t (proof lines 8594-8613). Choosing the complementary degree so that the two gradings match is the step carrying the argument. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Given a ring map from R to S and an element t of S satisfying a polynomial relation with R-coefficients a_0, ..., a_n the lemma produces an integral element, namely a_n t (statement lines 30697-30703). The exact bookkeeping of that rescaling, especially that the top term becomes the n-th power of a_n t, is the content, and the author writes the whole computation out. H2.

Finding the two stages, first for the map and then for the element, is the content, and the author writes both steps out. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps

items.difficulty_reason: For a ring R with a locally nilpotent ideal I, the lemma states that an element x is a unit exactly when its class in R/I is a unit (statement lines 6496-6502). items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian ring R and ideals I, J with J contained in the radical of I, the lemma asserts the existence of an exponent n with J^n contained in I, and consequently that locally nilpotent ideals are nilpotent in the Noetherian case (statement lines 6516-6527). The finite generation of J is what makes this possible, and that is exactly where the Noetherian hypothesis enters; the author writes the whole argument out in three sentences. H2.

items.title: Tensor relators along generating sets of two modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma rewrites the vanishing of a finite tensor sum, along chosen generating sets of M and N, as the existence of a coefficient matrix satisfying two systems of relations (statement lines 26239-26258). The proof does not work with the universal property of the tensor product directly: it presents N as a quotient of a direct sum of copies of the ring by a kernel K, tensors the presentation with M using right exactness, lifts the given element to K tensor M, and then reads the entries of the lifted elements as the required coefficients (proof lines 26260-26275). Deciding to present N and then lift is the substance, and the author records both systems of relations exactly as they come out. H2.

items.title: Generating a graded ring over its degree-zero part equals generating the positive part as an ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that homogeneous elements of positive degree generate a graded ring over its degree-zero part as an algebra exactly when they generate the positive-degree part as an ideal (statement lines 13998-14003). The proof does not compare the two filtered pieces abstractly: one direction reads polynomial generation without constant term, and the other inducts on the degree of a homogeneous element, writing it as a sum of multiples of the generators and using gradedness to replace each coefficient by its homogeneous component of the complementary degree before applying the induction hypothesis (proof lines 14005-14017). That degree bookkeeping on the coefficients is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.

items.title: Avoiding finitely many prime ideals while staying in a fixed coset of an ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if the coset x + I is not contained in any of finitely many primes, then there is an element y of I with x + y outside all of them (statement lines 2813-2820). The proof does not use the general prime avoidance lemma in the form it is usually quoted: it removes inclusions among the primes, splits them by whether they contain x, finds an element of I outside the first bad prime together with a multiplier lying in all the earlier primes but not in that one, and adds their product to x, concluding by induction on the number of primes already avoided (proof lines 2822-2830). The construction of the adjusting element is the substance and the author writes out each step. H2.

items.title: The homogeneous ideal generated by the homogeneous elements of a prime is prime
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a graded ring S and a prime p, the lemma states that the ideal q generated by the homogeneous elements of p is again prime (statement lines 13867-13874). The proof does not study the graded structure of p or compare components: it reduces primality to the case of a product of two homogeneous elements, uses that q is generated by homogeneous elements of p to place the product in p, applies primality there, and then upgrades membership in p of a homogeneous element to membership in q (proof lines 13876-13884). The two passage steps, both resting on homogeneity, are what the argument turns on. H2.

items.title: Surjectivity onto each one-generator completion implies surjectivity onto the ideal-adic completion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a finitely generated ideal I = (f_1, ..., f_r) the lemma states that if M surjects onto each completion with respect to a single generator, then M surjects onto the I-adic completion (statement lines 22972-22977). The proof does not argue with the I-adic filtration directly: it replaces it by the filtration cut out by the separate powers of the generators, using I^n contained in (f_1^n, ..., f_r^n) contained in I^{rn}, writes an element of the resulting limit as a symbolic series in the f_i, and matches the series term by term using the hypotheses for the individual generators (proof lines 22979-22990). The substitution of one tower by the other is the step that makes the term-by-term matching possible. H2.

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma (source lines 22979-22990)

items.title: A surjective endomorphism of a Noetherian ring is an isomorphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a surjective endomorphism of a Noetherian ring is automatically injective and therefore an isomorphism (statement lines 6435-6438). The proof does not use the module-theoretic statement that a surjective endomorphism of a finitely generated module is injective, nor Nakayama: it assumes a nonzero kernel and exhibits the chain of iterated kernels of f, which strictly increases, as a contradiction to the ascending chain condition (proof lines 6440-6447). The observation that a non-injective endomorphism has strictly growing iterated kernels is the step carrying the content, and the author writes the chain out explicitly. H2.

items.title: A symbolic power of a prime in a Noetherian ring has that prime as its only associated prime
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian ring R, a prime p and n greater than zero, the lemma states that the associated primes of R modulo the n-th symbolic power of p consist of p alone (statement lines 15776-15781). The proof does not use the theory of primary decomposition: it first gets p contained in every associated prime directly from the quotient, then shows that each x outside p is a nonzerodivisor on that quotient by writing the symbolic power as R intersected with p^n R_p and observing that xy in the symbolic power forces y into p^n R_p and hence back into the symbolic power (proof lines 15783-15792). The use of the localised description to run the divisibility test is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma (source lines 15783-15792)

items.title: The localisation of a module is the base change of the ring of fractions tensored with it
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the localisation of a module is canonically isomorphic to the tensor product of the ring of fractions with it, with the isomorphism given on pure tensors by (a/s) tensor m going to am/s (statement lines 2304-2313). The proof does not invoke flatness or adjunction: it builds the map from a bilinear pairing via the universal property, reduces every tensor to the shape one over s tensor m by putting the summands over a common denominator, and proves injectivity by exhibiting an element of the multiplicative subset that annihilates the relevant numerator (proof lines 2315-2338). Reducing a general tensor to a single common denominator is the step that makes both checks possible. H2.

items.title: Flatness after a base change makes the natural map on Tor one surjective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For ring maps R to R' to R'' and an R-module M whose first base change is flat over R', the lemma states that the natural map from Tor_1(M, R') tensor R'' to Tor_1(M, R'') is surjective (statement lines 24062-24069). The proof does not compute Tor with a resolution over R'': it takes one free resolution over R, identifies both Tor groups as quotients of the kernels after the two base changes, tensors the exact sequence for the first base change with R'', and uses flatness to keep it exact, which makes the map on kernels surjective (proof lines 24071-24095). Using a single resolution for both computations, so that the comparison becomes a map of kernels, is the content of the argument. H2.

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma (source lines 24071-24095)

items.title: The natural comparison map on Tor one for a quotient by an extended ideal is surjective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map R to R', an ideal I with extension I', and an R-module M, the natural comparison map from Tor_1 over R of the quotient by I' to Tor_1 over R' of the base change is surjective (statement lines 24097-24104). The proof does not compute either Tor group with an explicit resolution over the target ring: it notes that the base change of a free resolution need not remain exact, completes it by an extra free module, identifies the two complexes computing the Tor groups modulo the extended ideal, and exhibits a vertical map of complexes that is visibly surjective on cohomology (proof lines 24106-24135, with the diagram drawn in Xy-pic). Supplying the extra free module so that the comparison becomes a map of complexes is the content, and the author writes the diagram out. H2.

items.title: Inverting a multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors does not change the total ring of fractions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that inverting a multiplicative subset S of R made of nonzerodivisors does not change the total ring of fractions, Q(R) being isomorphic to Q(S^{-1}R), and that consequently Q(R) agrees with Q(Q(R)) (statement lines 4809-4815). The proof isolates the one step that could fail, namely the passage from a nonzerodivisor of S^{-1}R to its numerator: if x = r/f with f in S is a nonzerodivisor, then r must be a nonzerodivisor in R, and this is exactly what the hypothesis on S is for (proof lines 4817-4820). The author leaves the assembly of the two rings of fractions to the reader once that step is in hand. H2.

items.title: A unique factorization domain satisfies the ascending chain condition for principal ideals
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a unique factorization domain satisfies the ascending chain condition for principal ideals (statement lines 29759-29763). The proof does not argue with divisor chains or invoke Noetherianity of any kind: it factors the first element of a given ascending chain as a product of primes, then uses the containment of principal ideals to see that every later element is an associate of a product of the same primes with exponents bounded by those of the first element, so only finitely many possibilities arise (proof lines 29765-29771). The finiteness of the exponent bookkeeping, driven entirely by unique factorization, is the content. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a unique factorization domain is normal, that is, integrally closed in its fraction field (statement lines 29817-29820). The proof does not use the theory of Dedekind domains or a minimal polynomial: it writes an integral element as a unit times a product of powers of pairwise non-associate irreducibles with integer exponents, assumes one exponent is negative, and raises the integrality equation into an identity that exhibits a product of primes as divisible by the offending irreducible, contradicting uniqueness of factorization (proof lines 29822-29836). The choice of exponent N to clear denominators is the substance, and the author writes the resulting identity out. H2.

items.title: A sufficiently divisible Veronese subring of a finitely generated graded algebra is generated in degree one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a graded ring S finitely generated over S_0, the lemma states that for all sufficiently divisible d the Veronese subring in degree d is generated in degree one over S_0 (statement lines 13499-13504). The proof does not use Hilbert functions or asymptotic generation theorems: after making the generators homogeneous it describes the monomials of a given degree, takes m to be a common multiple of the generator degrees, and uses a pigeonhole argument to show that every monomial of degree N m with N at least r already contains a monomial of degree m as a factor, which gives generation in degree one for the Veronese subring in degree r m (proof lines 13506-13522). The pigeonhole step and the choice of r m are the content, and the author writes both out. H2.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a Z-graded ring with a homogeneous invertible element of positive degree, the lemma states that the set of graded primes maps homeomorphically onto the spectrum of the degree-zero part (statement lines 13627-13633). The proof does not cite a general result on group-graded localisations: it builds an inverse by taking, for a prime of the degree-zero part, the radical of its extension, checks primality by rescaling a product of homogeneous elements with powers of the invertible element so that its degree-zero part appears, and then upgrades the bijection to a homeomorphism by computing the image of a basic open through the decomposition of an element into homogeneous parts (proof lines 13635-13654). The rescaling trick is what makes the homogeneous case collapse to the degree-zero case. H2.

items.author: David Gonzalez, Dino Rossegger

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 795-798: if a class K_0 is alpha-universal for a class K_1, then K_0 contains every structure of K_1 that has a P_infinity alpha Scott sentence. The proof (source lines 799-804) is short but it is not a formality: it has to pick a counterexample, obtain a comparison partner from the universality hypothesis, and then convert that comparison into an isomorphism by the defining property of a Scott sentence of that class, which is what puts the structure back into K_0. The statement records only the containment and hides that the whole content is the interaction between the universality relation and the isomorphism characterisation supplied by the Scott sentence.

items.author: David Gonzalez, Dino Rossegger

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 809-812: the class consisting of the natural numbers and the rationals is two-universal for all countable linear orders, and in particular the rationals alone are two-universal for the infinite ones. The statement gives no witness and no rank bookkeeping, and the proof (source lines 813-818) has to supply both: it separates the finite orders, which are already members, from the infinite ones, for which the comparison at rank two has to be produced through a rank one comparison of intervals, using that every interval of the rationals is infinite while an interval of an arbitrary countable order need not be. The reduction of a rank two comparison to a single interval comparison is the whole argument and it is invisible in the statement.

items.title: Noetherian filtered colimits of etale algebras have finitely many separable fibres
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the fibre over a prime of a Noetherian filtered colimit of etale algebras: finitely many primes lie over it, the fibre splits as a product of their residue fields, and each field extension is separable algebraic. The proof is a 22-line argument that goes through the presentation of the colimit: the fibre is a filtered colimit of etale algebras over the residue field, each of which is a finite product of finite separable extensions, so no nontrivial specialisations occur between its primes; combined with Noetherianness this forces the fibre to be a finite product of fields, and the separability statement follows from the description of each factor as a colimit of finite separable extensions. The specialisation argument and the splitting are the substance and both are displayed.

items.title: The modules admitting the standard cokernel presentation form a weak Serre subcategory under a hypothesis on kernels
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-modules.tex (Modules on Sites)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file sites-modules.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that in the quasi-compact objects situation the full subcategory A of modules isomorphic to a cokernel presentation by direct images j_{U!}O_U along basis members is a weak Serre subcategory, provided the kernel of every map between finite direct sums of such objects already lies in A. The proof uses the characterization criterion for weak Serre subcategories and the section's closure results for cokernels and extensions, reducing the verification to the kernel of a map between two objects of A; it then chooses presentations of both objects and refines them, so that the kernel can be exhibited as an object of A by the assumed hypothesis (proof lines 5690-5731). H2: the reduction chain to the single kernel case and the refinement of the two presentations are the substance, and the argument is written out.

items.title: Every h cover of an affine scheme is refined by a finite affine cover of a surjective proper finitely presented morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme X and an h covering {X_i -> X}, the lemma asserts that there is a surjective proper morphism Y -> X of finite presentation, with a finite affine open covering Y = Y_1 cup ... cup Y_m whose members refine the given covering (statement lines 10302-10312). The proof begins with the definition of an h covering: there is a proper surjective Y -> X with a finite affine open covering refining {X_i -> X}, say with morphisms h_j : Y_j -> X_{i_j} over X, and the whole problem is that Y -> X need not be of finite presentation (proof lines 10314-10325). By Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation the morphism Y -> X is a directed limit of schemes Y_lambda proper and of finite presentation over X with closed immersion transition maps, and each Y_lambda -> X is still surjective (proof lines 10327-10333). Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-opens then spreads the cover to quasi-compact opens Y_{lambda,j} covering Y_lambda and restricting to Y_j, and after increasing lambda the Y_{lambda,j} may be assumed affine by Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-limit-affine (proof lines 10335-10341). Finally the functorial characterisation of morphisms locally of finite presentation (Limits, Proposition labelled limits-proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation) applies because the X_i -> X are locally of finite presentation, giving morphisms h_{lambda,j} : Y_{lambda,j} -> X_{i_j} restricting to h_j for a suitable lambda, so the approximating cover refines the given one (proof lines 10343-10353). Descending the cover and the refinement maps through the directed limit, and using the finite presentation of the targets to make the descent work, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The exterior product over a base of dimension one is associative
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: With (S, delta) as in the situation of this section, X smooth over S and Y, Z, W locally of finite type over X, the lemma asserts that the product defined above on Chow groups satisfies (alpha . beta) . gamma = alpha . (beta . gamma) in CH_*(Y x_X Z x_X W) (statement lines 14917-14925). The proof starts from the associativity of the exterior product over S, (alpha x beta) x gamma = alpha x (beta x gamma) in CH_*(Y x_S Z x_S W), which is Lemma labelled lemma-exterior-product-associative-dim-1 (proof lines 14927-14929), and then introduces the closed immersions Delta_12, Delta_23 : X x_S X -> X x_S X x_S X, with bivariant classes Delta_12^! and Delta_23^! that are the restrictions of Delta^! along pr_12 and pr_23 (proof lines 14931-14948). The observation that restricting Delta_12^! along Delta_23 and Delta_23^! along Delta_12 both give Delta^! is converted by Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-commutes into Delta^! o Delta_12^! = Delta^! o Delta_23^! (proof lines 14950-14957). The lemma itself is then a six term chain of equalities expanding (alpha . beta) . gamma through Delta^!, replacing Delta^! by Delta_12^! and Delta_23^! using the commutation relation, and pulling Delta^! past the exterior factors using Remark labelled remark-commuting-exterior (proof lines 14959-14976). Controlling the two restriction equalities for the diagonal classes and using them to swap the order of the two Delta^! operations is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The blow up formula: the restriction of the Gysin map of a blowup in a regular center is the top Chern class of the kernel of the conormal comparison
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a regular closed immersion i : Z -> X of schemes locally of finite type over a base (S, delta) and b : X' -> X the blowing up in Z with exceptional divisor E, the lemma asserts that, assuming the Gysin map for b exists, res(b^!) = c_top(F^vee) o pi^* in A^*(E -> Z), where F is the kernel of the canonical map pi^* C_{Z/X} -> C_{E/X'} (statement lines 13807-13825). The proof notes that b is a local complete intersection morphism by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-blowup-regular-sequence, so the statement makes sense, and that regularity of Z -> X makes C_{Z/X} finite locally free with Sym^*(C_{Z/X}) isomorphic to the conormal algebra by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-quasi-regular-immersion, whence E = Proj(C_{Z/X,*}) = P(C_{Z/X}) is a projective space bundle over Z, in particular smooth and a local complete intersection morphism (proof lines 13827-13840). Lemma labelled lemma-compare-gysin-base-change then gives res(b^!) = c_top(C^vee) o pi^! for the kernel C occurring there, and Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-flat lets pi^! be replaced by pi^* (proof lines 13842-13848). What remains is the identification of the two kernels: since E -> Z is smooth, H^{-1}(NL_{E/Z}) vanishes by More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-NL-smooth, and the exact sequences of More on Morphisms, Lemmas labelled more-morphisms-lemma-get-triangle-NL and more-morphisms-lemma-NL-immersion, both for E -> X' -> X and for E -> Z -> X, identify F with H^{-1}(j^* NL_{X'/X}) and hence with C (proof lines 13850-13865). Identifying the abstract kernel from the base change comparison with the concrete kernel of the conormal map, using the two exact sequences of the normal cone, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The blowup making a complex and divisor into a good triple is compatible with base change, where the new scheme is the strict transform
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-complex-and-divisor, for a morphism h : Y -> X such that the pullback E = h^{-1}D is defined, the lemma compares the blowups b : X' -> X and c : Y' -> Y constructed by Lemma labelled lemma-complex-and-divisor-blowup-pre for the two data, asserts that Y' is the strict transform of Y with respect to b, and gives the identification L eta_{J'} L(h o c)^*M = L(Y' -> X')^*Q with Q = L eta_{I'} Lb^*M (statement lines 13730-13747; the strict transform assertion has a precise formulation only in the proof). The proof notes that (Y', E', L(h o c)^*M) is a good triple with E' = c^{-1}E, so the universal property of Lemma labelled lemma-complex-and-divisor-blowup-pre produces a unique morphism h' : Y' -> X' with b o h' = h o c, hence a morphism (h', c) : Y' -> X' x_X Y (proof lines 13749-13758). The strict transform claim is reduced to a local statement on a quasi-compact open W of X; over an affine chart (U, A, f, M^bullet) the restriction of b to U is the blowup in the product of the ideals I_i(M^bullet, f), while for an affine open V = Spec(B) inside h^{-1}(U) the chart (V, B, g, M^bullet otimes_A B) of Lemma labelled lemma-pullback-triple-ideals-good shows that c over h^{-1}(U) is the blowup in the pullback of that product ideal, which is exactly the description of the strict transform (proof lines 13760-13782). With that in hand the identification of the two derived twists follows from Lemma labelled lemma-complex-and-divisor-eta-pull, and the final statement is the special case c = id_Y (proof lines 13784-13789). Comparing the two blowups through their affine charts to recognise the strict transform, and then transferring the derived twist by the eta pull lemma, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
