items.title: Base change shifts the delta-dimension of every irreducible component by the constant c
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-setup-base-change, for X -> S locally of finite type and X' -> S' the base change, the lemma asserts that if X is integral with dim_delta(X) = k then every irreducible component Z' of X' has dim_{delta'}(Z') = k + c (statement lines 15138-15144). The proof uses that X' -> X is flat, being a base change of the flat S' -> S (Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-base-change-flat), so every generic point x' of an irreducible component of X' maps to the generic point x of X by lifting of generalizations along flat morphisms (Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-generalizations-lift-flat) (proof lines 15146-15153). Writing s for the image of x in S, it views x' as a point of S'_s x_s x, which is a monomorphism into S' x_S X, and applies flatness of Spec(kappa(x)) -> Spec(kappa(s)) again to see that x' maps to a generic point s' of an irreducible component of g^{-1}(s), so delta'(s') = delta(s) + c by the assumption of the base change situation (proof lines 15155-15167). The fibre dimensions at x and x' agree by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change, both are generic points of the corresponding fibres, and the transcendence degrees of kappa(x) over kappa(s) and of kappa(x') over kappa(s') agree by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point, which gives the displayed equality delta_{X'/S'}(x') = delta(s') + trdeg = delta(s) + c + trdeg = delta_{X/S}(x) + c and hence the claim by Definition labelled definition-delta-dimension (proof lines 15169-15179). Transporting the generic point through the two flat maps and comparing fibre dimensions and transcendence degrees is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The fundamental computation of the class of the virtual normal sheaf against the fundamental class of a regularly embedded subvariety
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation described just above the lemma, assuming dim_delta(Y) = n and that the conormal sheaf of Y x_X Z in Z has constant rank r, the lemma asserts c(Z -> X, N) cap [Y]_n = c_top(E) cap [Z x_X Y]_{n - r} in CH_*(Z x_X Y), where c_top(E) is the bivariant class of Remark labelled remark-top-chern-class (statement lines 12075-12085). The proof first uses Lemma labelled lemma-construction-gysin to replace X by Y, so that Z -> X becomes a regular closed immersion of codimension r with dim_delta(X) = n and the goal becomes c(Z -> X, N) cap [X]_n = c_top(E) cap [Z]_{n - r} (proof lines 12087-12095). Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-decompose then reduces further to the case where the normal sheaf and the conormal sheaf are identified, so it suffices to show c(Z -> X, C_{Z/X}^vee) cap [X]_n = [Z]_{n - r} (proof lines 12097-12104). The proof traces the definition of the class: with b : W -> P^1_X the blowing up of infinity(Z), the class C cap [X]_n equals i_infinity^*[W]_{n+1} because the restriction of [W]_{n+1} to A^1_X is the flat pullback of [X]_n, and since W_infinity is an effective Cartier divisor this is [W_infinity]_n by Lemma labelled lemma-easy-gysin; restricting to the open C_Z X inside W_infinity gives [C_Z X]_n (proof lines 12106-12118). Regularity of the embedding makes the conormal sheaf algebra the symmetric algebra by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-quasi-regular-immersion, so p : N = C_Z X -> Z is the structure morphism of the vector bundle of the finite locally free conormal sheaf of rank r, whence p^*[Z]_{n - r} = [C_Z X]_n and the proof is complete (proof lines 12120-12125). Tracing the definition of the localized class through the blowing up and identifying the normal cone with the total space of a vector bundle is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The flat pullback map on cycles descends to a map on Chow groups with the expected degree shift
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-setup-base-change, for X -> S locally of finite type and X' the base change along S' -> S, the lemma asserts that the map g^* : Z_k(X) -> Z_{k+c}(X') factors through rational equivalence to give a map CH_k(X) -> CH_{k+c}(X') (statement lines 15254-15264). The proof takes a k-cycle alpha rationally equivalent to zero and uses Lemma labelled lemma-rational-equivalence-family to write alpha = sum ([(W_i)_0]_k - [(W_i)_infinity]_k) for a locally finite family of integral closed subschemes W_i of X x P^1 of delta-dimension k not contained in the fibres over 0 or infinity (proof lines 15266-15278). It therefore suffices to prove two things for such an integral W with base change W' in X' x P^1: that W' satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma labelled lemma-closed-subscheme-cross-p1 with k replaced by k + c, and that g^*[W_0]_k = [(W')_0]_{k+c} and similarly at infinity (proof lines 15280-15288). items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated X with a quasi-compact open U, the lemma asserts that closed subschemes Z_1, Z_2 of finite presentation whose intersection with U is empty can be made to have disjoint strict transforms by a U-admissible blowup, and that disjoint constructible closed subsets T_1, T_2 of U can be separated in the same way (statement lines 9553-9566). For part (1) the proof notes that finite presentation of Z_i means the ideal sheaves I_i are of finite type by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, forms Z cut out by the product I_1 I_2, observes that Z cap U is the disjoint union of Z_1 cap U and Z_2 cap U, and applies Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-separate-disjoint-opens-by-blowing-up to get a (U cap Z)-admissible blowup Z' -> Z with disjoint strict transforms (proof lines 9568-9579). If Y is the center of that blowup, then Y -> X is a closed immersion of finite presentation by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-composition-finite-presentation, so the blowing up X' -> X of Y is U-admissible, and the strict transforms of Z_1 and Z_2 with respect to X' -> X agree with those with respect to Z' -> Z by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-strict-transform (proof lines 9581-9605 in part (1), and the same computation gives part (1)). For part (2) one writes each T_i as V(J_i) for a finite type ideal J_i on U by Properties, Lemma labelled properties-lemma-quasi-coherent-finite-type-ideals, extends J_i to a finite type ideal I_i on X by Properties, Lemma labelled properties-lemma-extend, and applies part (1) to Z_i = V(I_i) (proof lines 9593-9605). Reproducing the blowup on Z as a blowup on X so that the strict transforms agree is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Five equivalent descriptions of a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states the equivalence of five descriptions of a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space: the definition, being the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological algebra with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero, with one given by a sequence of weak ideals of definition, with one given by a sequence of ideals whose successive quotients are locally nilpotent, and finally being the formal spectrum of a limit of quotients of an algebra by such a sequence (statement lines 2492-2513). The proof first derives every other description from the definition: the space is the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible algebra by an earlier lemma on the types of affine formal algebraic spaces, and any presentation as a filtered colimit gives the algebra as the limit of its quotients by weak ideals of definition, which by a further earlier lemma form a countable fundamental system of open neighbourhoods of zero (proof lines 2515-2534). The converse direction from the last description is an argument about nilpotence: an element of the algebra dying in the first quotient has a power dying in the second because its image there is nilpotent, and so on inductively, so the kernel of the first projection is a weak ideal of definition and the algebra is weakly admissible (proof lines 2536-2549). Two of the remaining descriptions are immediate special cases, and the final step closes the cycle: from a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods one chooses open ideals inside them and intersects with a weak ideal of definition, obtaining a countable fundamental system of weak ideals of definition and hence a presentation of the space as a colimit (proof lines 2551-2565). The claim is H2: four implications are proved and each of them is a short but real manipulation, one of them an induction on the successive quotients in a filtered system of nilpotent ideals.

The proof first records the consequence of the monomorphism and factorisation assumptions, namely that the reductions of the two sides coincide (proof lines 6206-6208). It then reduces to an affine target: the assumptions are preserved by etale base change, so the etale-local characterisation of closed immersions lets the target be assumed affine (proof lines 6210-6214). Writing that affine formal algebraic space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, the base changes of the morphism are algebraic spaces carrying monomorphisms that induce isomorphisms on reductions, and a statement on limits of spaces makes them affine schemes; it therefore suffices to treat the case of a monomorphism of affine schemes inducing an isomorphism on reductions (proof lines 6216-6225). That case is where the last assumption enters: the author notes that without it the conclusion is false, referring to a published counterexample, and then observes that either the morphism is of finite type or the target is Noetherian, so that the corresponding ring map has the property that its reduction modulo the nil radical is an isomorphism and is either of finite type or has a Noetherian source; surjectivity then follows from the criterion for a surjection modulo a locally nilpotent ideal in the first case and from Nakayama's lemma, applied because the nil radical is finitely generated and therefore nilpotent, in the second (proof lines 6227-6247). The claim is H2: one reduction and one case split are carried out, the counterexample in the general case is acknowledged, and the two case analyses each invoke a distinct named criterion.

The proof is a cycle of implications. From the definition one obtains the taut map by equipping the ring itself with the topology induced by a chosen ideal, and the closures of its powers are then the fundamental system required by the definition (proof lines 1654-1661). From the taut map one reads off the open closures of the powers of the closure of the image of an ideal of definition, which gives the third formulation (proof lines 1663-1674). The third formulation returns to the definition, and also implies the fourth because any other ideal of definition is open and therefore contains a power of the chosen one, whence the closures of its powers are open too, while the fourth implies the third trivially (proof lines 1676-1690). The two additional statements are then short consequences: for a weakly pre-adic ring a taut map to the completion is produced by composing the taut map of the second formulation with the completion map, so the completion is weakly pre-adic and, being complete, weakly adic (proof lines 1692-1698); and a weakly adic ring is complete and pre-admissible hence admissible, and has a countable fundamental system of open ideals by definition (proof lines 1700-1704). items.title: Inserting an order into a shuffle sum lowers its back-and-forth rank by two
items.author: David Gonzalez, Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 1024-1027: for a shuffle sum A and an order B of the form L times Q, a rank alpha comparison between A and B upgrades to a rank alpha plus two comparison between A plus L plus B and A plus B. The statement is a rank shift that says nothing about how the extra two moves are spent, and the proof (source lines 1028-1056) has to exhibit the strategy explicitly: the existential player first copies the opponent tuple through isomorphisms of the outer parts, which leaves exactly one non-isomorphic interval, then uses that the remainders of a shuffle sum are again shuffle sums to move the comparison onto the two orders themselves, then on the following turn answers inside the inserted order by identifying its initial segment with the remainder of the first order, and finally reduces the goal to the hypothesis through the self-similarity of a shuffle sum. The whole argument is a two-move strategy in the back-and-forth game, and the statement contains none of it.

The statement is a rank bookkeeping assertion, and the proof (source lines 621-645) has to earn it from both sides: the forward implication rests on the label and predecessor relations of the tree being definable in the order at rank three, while the converse is a two-turn strategy in the back-and-forth game in which the existential player first has to find elements with the same label and the same position inside their block that restore the tree isomorphism, and then has to match the sizes of all intervals at once, which uses that between two elements in different blocks there are blocks coding paths of arbitrarily large size. items.title: Multiplying by Z to the alpha preserves back-and-forth relations with a doubled shift
items.author: David Gonzalez, Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 1275-1278: for any two countable linear orders, a rank beta comparison between them yields a comparison of rank twice alpha plus beta between their products with Z^alpha. The statement is a rank arithmetic assertion with no witness, and the proof (source lines 1280-1301) has to run an induction on beta in which the successor step is the real work: the product is rewritten as an ordering of pairs, the opponent plays a tuple of pairs, the answer is produced coordinatewise by the winning strategy of the original comparison, and the interval that remains to be compared is identified with a concatenation of two zeta blocks around the product of the corresponding interval, after which the induction hypothesis applies. Neither the coordinatewise strategy nor the interval computation is visible in the statement, and the doubled shift in the rank comes out of the second factor.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition characterises finitely generated modules by the surjectivity of the canonical map from M tensor a direct product of modules to the product of the tensored modules, in four equivalent forms (statement lines 21532-21545). The proof does not estimate cardinalities of generating sets: it reduces the first implication to a finite free presentation whose square has an isomorphism on top by commutation of tensor products with finite direct sums, and proves the reverse implication by feeding in the diagonal element of M indexed by M, whose finiteness as a sum in the image directly produces a finite generating set (proof lines 21547-21573). Deciding to use the diagonal element is the step that carries the reverse implication. H2.

items.title: A good element is a nonzerodivisor and its quotient is Cohen-Macaulay with a shorter maximal regular sequence
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a good element g with respect to a tuple (M, f_1, ..., f_d) is a nonzerodivisor on M and that M/gM is Cohen-Macaulay with maximal regular sequence f_1, ..., f_{d-1} (statement lines 25201-25207). The proof does not rework the definition of goodness: in the case d = 1 it bounds the support of the kernel of multiplication by g to the closed point, so that the kernel has finite length and Nakayama kills it; in general it observes that g stays good on M/f_1M, applies the induction hypothesis, and permutes the resulting regular sequence with f_1 (proof lines 25209-25232). Recognising that the hypothesis descends to the quotient by f_1 is what makes the induction work. H2.

items.title: Finitely many maximal ideals with locally nilpotent Jacobson radical make a ring a product of its localisations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a ring with finitely many maximal ideals whose Jacobson radical is locally nilpotent is the product of its localisations at those maximal ideals, and that all its primes are maximal (statement lines 12974-12979). The proof does not invoke the classification of Artinian rings: it uses local nilpotence to show every prime contains the intersection of the maximal ideals and hence one of them, making the spectrum discrete, then splits the ring by a disjoint-support decomposition applied finitely many times and identifies the factors as the localisations (proof lines 12981-13001). The first step, which turns local nilpotence into discreteness of the spectrum, is the content, and the author writes it out. H2.

items.author: Quentin Le Hou\'erou, Ludovic Levy Patey, Keita Yokoyama
items.work: Conservation of Ramsey's theorem for pairs\\ and well-foundedness
items.difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2402.11616v3 的 Lemma lem:sem-wf-finite-tree-forcing（源 893-897 行，证明 898-912 行）：给定条件、Σ⁰₁ 公式与一棵 M-有限极大泛树，存在扩展 (τ,c)≤(σ,a) 与 q 使 (τ,c) 同时强制 φ(G,q−1) 与 ¬φ(G,q)。关键操作不是例行核验：先从有效叶出发取其给出扩展 (π(ν),b)（899-901 行）；再把「极大性」翻译成对每个高度存在的二分划，使任何合法块都不能在保持 φ 为真的前提下延拓该叶，从而得到逐高度的性质 (P)（903-909 行）；随后必须用紧致性把逐高度性质提升为 X_b 的整个二分划，并注意到该分划类是非空的 Π⁰₁(Y⊕X_b) 类，借定义 X 族的性质把它实现为两个 X_c、X_d 对 X_b 的分划（911 行），最后由 G ⊆* X_b 得 G 落在其中一侧，才得到所宣称的强制关系。难点在于两次跨「有限/无穷」的过渡（极大性→逐高度、逐高度→紧致性）与把抽象分划类落到模型内具体集合；原文位置在证明的 903-911 行。

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for presheaves of modules the internal hom functor commutes with arbitrary limits in either variable, and that the same holds for sheaves of modules. items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-modules.tex (Modules on Sites)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a covering {U_i -> U} with U quasi-compact, some finite subfamily I' already gives an exact sequence presenting j_!O_U by the extensions by zero along the members of the subfamily and their pairwise fibre products. The proof first reduces to the case where U satisfies a stronger quasi-compactness condition, then in general uses the definition of quasi-compactness to find a refinement V of the covering U whose index image I' is finite, and checks exactness of the resulting sequence by applying Hom into an arbitrary module and using the standard sequence coming from the lower shriek construction (proof lines 5306-5334). H2: the reduction to a finite-index refinement and the Hom-test for exactness are the substance; the author explicitly says the reader may skip the general case, which is nonetheless written out.

items.title: The second Adams operator multiplies the Chern classes and the Chern character by powers of two
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For X locally of finite type over (S, delta), with psi^2 as in Lemma labelled lemma-second-adams-operator and c and ch as in Remarks labelled remark-chern-classes-K and remark-chern-character-K, the lemma asserts c_i(psi^2(alpha)) = 2^i c_i(alpha) and ch_i(psi^2(alpha)) = 2^i ch_i(alpha) for all alpha in K_0(Vect(X)) (statement lines 12901-12910). The proof observes that multiplying by 2^i in degree i is a ring map of the product of the A^i(X), so since psi^2 is also a ring map it suffices to check the formulas on additive generators, i.e. on classes [E] of finite locally free modules, and by the construction of the Chern classes one may assume E has constant rank r by Remark labelled remark-extend-to-finite-locally-free (proof lines 12912-12922). The splitting principle, Lemma labelled lemma-splitting-principle, then supplies a projective smooth p : P -> X with A^*(X) -> A^*(P) injective such that p^*E has a finite filtration with invertible graded parts L_j; writing x_j = c_1(L_j) the proof computes c(alpha) = prod (1 + x_j) and c(psi^2(alpha)) = prod (1 + 2x_j), and ch(alpha) = sum exp(x_j) with ch(psi^2(alpha)) = sum exp(2x_j), from which the two formulas follow (proof lines 12924-12942). Recognising that the multiplicative structure reduces the statement to line bundles, and then reading the effect of psi^2 off the splitting of E, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Base change of a Gysin map of a local complete intersection morphism is the top Chern class of the kernel of the conormal comparison
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a cartesian square of schemes locally of finite type over (S, delta) with both f and f' local complete intersection morphisms and with the Gysin map existing for f, the lemma asserts that C = Ker(H^{-1}((g')^* NL_{X/Y}) -> H^{-1}(NL_{X'/Y'})) is a finite locally free O_{X'}-module, that the Gysin map exists for f', and that res(f^!) = c_top(C^vee) o (f')^! in A^*(X' -> Y') (statement lines 13737-13761). The proof gets finite local freeness of C from More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-base-change-lci-bis, then chooses a factorization f = h o i with h smooth and i an immersion, so that f' = h' o i' with h' and i' the base changes, which also shows the Gysin map exists for f' (proof lines 13763-13782). Using the presentation NL_{X/Y} = (C_{X/P} -> i^* Omega_{P/Y}) of More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-get-NL and its primed analogue, together with the identifications (g')^* i^* Omega_{P/Y} = (i')^* Omega_{P'/Y'} by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-base-change-differentials and the surjectivity of (g')^* C_{X/P} -> C_{X'/P'} by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial-flat, the proof identifies C with the kernel of that surjection between finite locally free modules (proof lines 13784-13794). Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-excess then gives res(i^!) = c_top(C^vee) o (i')^! in A^*(X' -> P'), and since f^! = i^! o h^*, (f')^! = (i')^! o (h')^* and (h')^* = res(h^*) the conclusion follows (proof lines 13796-13805). Recognising the abstract kernel from the definition of the normal cone as the kernel of the conormal surjection, so that the excess lemma applies, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: For a good triple there is a finite presentation closed subscheme of the divisor on which the derived twist has locally free cohomology of the expected ranks
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: Letting X, D, I, M be as in Situation labelled situation-complex-and-divisor with (X, D, M) a good triple, the lemma produces a closed immersion i : T -> D of finite presentation such that T scheme theoretically contains D cap W for the maximal open W where the cohomology sheaves of M are locally free, the cohomology sheaves of Li^*L eta_I M are locally free, and the ranks of H^i(M)_x and H^i(Li^*L eta_I M)_t agree for t in T with image x in W (statement lines 13809-13829). On an affine chart (U, A, f, M^bullet) where all the ideals I_i(M^bullet, f) are principal, the proof defines T cap U inside D cap U by the ideal J(M^bullet, f) = sum_i J_i(M^bullet, f) of A/fA studied in More on Algebra, Lemmas labelled more-algebra-lemma-eta-vanishing-beta-plus-pre and more-algebra-lemma-eta-vanishing-beta-plus, the second of which also identifies the morphism T cap U -> D cap U with the ring map A/fA -> C (proof lines 13831-13842). Since the triple is good, such charts cover X and the first of the two lemmas shows that the construction glues, giving a closed subscheme T of D cut out by the ideals J(M^bullet, f) on good charts, and then properties (1) and (2) follow from the second lemma (proof lines 13844-13849; the author writes 'Details omitted' here and adds an observation that since eta_f M^bullet is a complex of locally free modules the restriction Li^*L eta_I M over T cap U is represented by eta_f M^bullet otimes_A C, after which property (3) follows from Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-eta-cohomology-locally-free at proof lines 13851-13857). Gluing the local ideal construction and matching ranks through the locally free representative of the twist is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A finite presentation morphism that is flat over a quasi-compact open becomes flat after an almost blowup square
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated Y, X of finite presentation over Y and a quasi-compact open V of Y over which X_V -> V is flat, the lemma produces a commutative diagram whose left and right squares are almost blow up squares, whose lower and top squares are cartesian, with Z cap V empty, and with X' -> Y' flat and of finite presentation (statement lines 11161-11179). The proof first disposes of the Noetherian case by quoting Lemma labelled lemma-flat-after-blowing-up, since blow up squares are almost blow up squares and strict transforms are blowups (proof lines 11181-11187). The general case is reduced to the Noetherian one by absolute Noetherian approximation: Y is written as a directed limit of Noetherian schemes with affine transition morphisms by Limits, Proposition labelled limits-proposition-approximate, then X -> Y is descended to some finite presentation X_i -> Y_i by Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-finite-presentation, V is descended to an open V_i by Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-opens, and flatness of X_{i,V_i} -> V_i is imposed by Limits, Lemma labelled limits-lemma-descend-flat-finite-presentation (proof lines 11189-11203). The Noetherian case applied to X_i -> Y_i with V_i produces a diagram whose base change by Y -> Y_i is the desired one, using preservation of properness, finite presentation, closed immersions and flatness under base change by Morphisms, Lemmas labelled morphisms-lemma-base-change-proper, morphisms-lemma-base-change-finite-presentation, morphisms-lemma-base-change-closed-immersion and morphisms-lemma-base-change-flat, together with the base change stability of almost blow up squares in Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-almost-blow-up (proof lines 11205-11213). Descending the whole configuration to a Noetherian approximation and transporting the almost blowup diagram back along the base change is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Every bivariant class commutes with the class of a virtual normal sheaf
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For X locally of finite type over (S, delta), a closed subscheme Z with virtual normal sheaf N, a morphism Y -> X locally of finite type and c in A^*(Y -> X), the lemma asserts that c and c(Z -> X, N) commute in the sense of Remark labelled remark-bivariant-commute (statement lines 12205-12212). The proof uses Lemma labelled lemma-bivariant-zero to reduce to X integral, where the assertion becomes c cap c(Z -> X, N) cap [X] = c(Z -> X, N) cap c cap [X] in CH_*(Z x_X Y) (proof lines 12214-12221). Two cases follow. If Z = X then c(Z -> X, N) = c_top(N) by Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-fundamental, and Chern classes commute with any bivariant class by Lemma labelled lemma-cap-commutative-chern (proof lines 12223-12228). Otherwise Lemma labelled lemma-bivariant-zero allows a further reduction after blowing X up in a nonzero ideal, and blowing up in the ideal sheaf of Z brings one to the case where Z is an effective Cartier divisor by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor (proof lines 12230-12236). In that case c(Z -> X, N) = c_top(E) o i^* with i^* the Gysin homomorphism of the divisor and E the dual of the kernel of N^vee -> C_{Z/X} by Lemmas labelled lemma-gysin-decompose and lemma-gysin-agrees, and the claim follows because Chern classes are central in the bivariant ring in the strong sense of Lemma labelled lemma-cap-commutative-chern and c commutes with the Gysin homomorphism by the definition of bivariant classes (proof lines 12238-12248). The two step reduction, first to an integral base and then to a Cartier divisor after a blowup, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a prime p and a scheme S over F_p, the lemma asserts that the rule F(X) = lim_F Gamma(X, O_X) on the big h site (Sch/S)_h defines a sheaf (statement lines 11930-11939). The proof checks conditions (1), (2), (3) and (4) of Lemma labelled lemma-refine-check-h: condition (1) holds because limits of sheaves are sheaves and O is a Zariski sheaf, and condition (2) because O is an fppf sheaf by Descent, Lemma labelled descent-lemma-sheaf-condition-holds and because lim_F of an equalizer of F_p-algebras is the equalizer of the limits (proof lines 11941-11949). Condition (3) is turned into the bijectivity of lim_F A -> lim_F A/(fA cap J): the right hand side is identified with the fibre product of the two limits, and since J is annihilated by a power of f the ideal a = fA cap J is nilpotent, so lim_F A -> lim_F A/a is bijective (proof lines 11951-11967). Condition (4) follows from Lemma labelled lemma-funny-blow-up together with the E = P^1_Z identification, as in the previous paragraph (proof lines 11969-11983). Reducing condition (3) to the nilpotence of fA cap J and the bijectivity of the limit along a nilpotent quotient is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The Gysin map of a morphism of smooth schemes over a field is multiplicative and exists
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a field k and a morphism f : X -> Y of schemes smooth over k, the lemma asserts that the Gysin map exists for f and that f^!(alpha . beta) = f^!alpha . f^!beta (statement lines 14436-14441). The proof first notes that X -> X x_k Y is an immersion of X into a scheme smooth over Y, so the Gysin map exists by Definition labelled definition-lci-gysin, then reduces to the case where X and Y are smooth and equidimensional of dimensions d and e by decomposing into connected components (proof lines 14443-14452). With f^![Y]_e = [X]_d from Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-easy and the identifications alpha = c cap [Y]_e, beta = c' cap [Y]_e given by Lemma labelled lemma-identify-chow-for-smooth, the proof notes that alpha . beta = c cap c' cap [Y]_e and that f^! commutes with c and c' by Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-commutes, then runs a six term chain of equalities moving f^! onto the fundamental class and back (proof lines 14454-14476). An alternative proof via (f x f)^!(alpha x beta) = f^!alpha x f^!beta and Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-composition is also recorded (proof lines 14478-14479). Representing Chow classes of smooth schemes as caps of bivariant classes and using commutation of f^! with them is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The Gysin class of a local complete intersection morphism is independent of the chosen factorization
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y a local complete intersection morphism of schemes locally of finite type over (S, delta), the lemma asserts that the bivariant class f^! is independent of the choice of a factorization f = g o i with g smooth, provided such a factorization exists (statement lines 13484-13492). The proof reduces an arbitrary second factorization to a comparison diagram: given f = g' o i' as well one first passes to the smooth morphism g'' : P x_Y P' -> Y and the immersion i'' : X -> P x_Y P', so that it suffices to treat a diagram X -> P -> Y and X -> P' -> Y with p : P' -> P smooth, and then, because (g')^* = p^* o g^* by Lemma labelled lemma-compose-flat-pullback, to show that i^! = (i')^! o p^* in A^*(X -> P) (proof lines 13494-13509). The proof considers the cartesian diagram with X x_P P' and the section s = (1, i'), notes that s and j are regular immersions by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-section-smooth-regular-immersion and Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-flat-base-change-regular-immersion, and that i' = j o s, so that (i')^! = s^! o j^! by Lemma labelled lemma-composition-regular-immersion (proof lines 13511-13519). Since the square is cartesian, j^! is the restriction of i^! to P' by Lemma labelled lemma-construction-gysin, and because bivariant classes commute with flat pullbacks one has j^! o p^* = p-bar^* o i^!, so it remains to show s^! o p-bar^* = id, which is Lemma labelled lemma-section-smooth (proof lines 13521-13527). Reducing an arbitrary pair of factorizations to a single smooth comparison via the fibre product and then splitting the immersion through a section is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The category of standard h coverings of an affine limit is the colimit of the categories of standard h coverings of the approximating schemes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme T written as a directed inverse limit of affine schemes T_i, the lemma asserts three approximation statements: a standard h covering of T descends to a standard h covering of some T_i, morphisms of standard h coverings descend after increasing the index, and two morphisms with equal base change to T become equal at some index; equivalently the category of standard h coverings of T is the colimit over I of those of T_i (statement lines 10767-10795). The proof reduces the first statement to a single assertion: if a finite family of finitely presented morphisms with affine sources becomes an h covering after base change to T, then it is already an h covering after base change to some T_i (proof lines 10797-10809). For this it uses Lemma labelled lemma-approximate-h-cover to choose a finitely presented proper surjective Y -> T together with a finite affine open covering refining the given family, and then Limits, Lemmas labelled limits-lemma-eventually-proper, limits-lemma-descend-surjective and limits-lemma-descend-opens to descend Y -> T, the cover and the refinement to some T_{i'}, so that the descended family is an h covering (proof lines 10811-10827). Descending the approximating proper cover and reading the h covering property off the descended refinement is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The projection formula for a proper morphism of smooth schemes over a field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a field k and a proper morphism f : X -> Y of schemes smooth over k, the lemma asserts that the Gysin map exists for f and that f_*(alpha . f^!beta) = f_*alpha . beta (statement lines 14481-14486). The proof shows existence as in the multiplicative case, by exhibiting X -> X x_k Y as an immersion into a scheme smooth over Y and quoting Definition labelled definition-lci-gysin, then reduces to X and Y smooth equidimensional of dimensions d and e by decomposing into connected components (proof lines 14488-14497). Using f^![Y]_e = [X]_d from Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-easy and writing alpha = c cap [X]_d and beta = c' cap [Y]_e by Lemma labelled lemma-identify-chow-for-smooth, the proof runs a seven term chain: pull f^! inside the product, use its value on the fundamental class, swap the two cappings by the commutativity of the intersection product, move the bivariant class c' past f_*, and read the result back as beta . f_*alpha (proof lines 14499-14520). The commutation of f^! with c' is Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-commutes, and the passage of c' through f_* is the definition of a bivariant class. Recognising that the identity reduces to bookkeeping with bivariant classes against a single fundamental class is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Grothendieck existence: a compatible system of modules over the thickenings comes from a finitely presented flat module with proper support
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-existence the theorem asserts the existence of a finitely presented O_X-module F, flat over A and with support proper over A, whose reductions F_n agree with the given system compatibly with the maps phi_n (statement lines 8318-8326). The proof assembles the module first: Lemmas labelled lemma-compute-what-it-should-be, lemma-compute-against-perfect, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence, lemma-compute-over-affine, lemma-finitely-presented and lemma-proper-support together produce an open subscheme W of X containing all points lying over Spec(A_n) and a finitely presented O_W-module F whose support is proper over A with F_n = F otimes O_{X_n} for all n (proof lines 8328-8338). Lemma labelled lemma-proper-pure then shows F is universally pure relative to Spec(A), so Theorem labelled theorem-flat-dimension-n-representable, explained by Lemma labelled lemma-when-universal-flattening, gives a universal flattening S' -> Spec(A) which is a monomorphism of finite presentation (proof lines 8340-8346). Since the base change of F to Spec(A_n) is F_n, each Spec(A_n) -> Spec(A) factors uniquely through S', and Lemma labelled lemma-monomorphism-isomorphism forces S' = Spec(A), which means F is flat over A (proof lines 8348-8354). Finally the scheme theoretic support Z of F is proper over Spec(A), hence Z -> X is closed, so the pushforward of F along W -> X has all the desired properties (proof lines 8356-8358). Turning the formal existence of the module into flatness through the universal flattening and the monomorphism criterion is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A map of flat modules injective on every residue field fibre is universally injective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In equation labelled equation-star the lemma assumes N is A-flat, M is a flat A-module and u : N -> M is an A-module map with u otimes id_{kappa(p)} injective for every prime p, and concludes that u is A-universally injective (statement lines 7302-7308). By Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-check-universally-injective-into-flat it suffices to check injectivity of N/IN -> M/IM for every ideal I, and replacing A by A/I reduces this to injectivity of u (proof lines 7310-7316). For that, the proof takes a nonzero x in the kernel of u, chooses a weakly associated prime p of the module Ax by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-weakly-ass-zero, passes to the localisation at p and picks a nonzero y in Ax whose annihilator has radical the maximal ideal by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-weakly-ass-local, so that the support of y lies in the closed fibre of Spec(S^{-1}B) -> Spec(A) (proof lines 7318-7327). Choosing a finitely generated ideal I inside the maximal ideal so that there is a pure spreadout over A/I by Lemma labelled lemma-find-pure-spreadout, one has I^n y = 0, and flatness gives Ann_M(I^n) = Ann_A(I^n) otimes_R N; the desired contradiction therefore follows once Ann_A(I^n) otimes_R N -> Ann_A(I^n) otimes_R M is injective, which since Ann_A(I^n) is annihilated by I^n and both modules are flat reduces to the injectivity of Q otimes_A N -> Q otimes_A M for every A-module Q annihilated by I, and that is exactly Lemma labelled lemma-properties-pure-spreadout part (2) (proof lines 7329-7341). Producing the pure spreadout ideal through a weakly associated prime and turning the counterexample into a tensor computation is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the right exactness of the Chow group sequence of two closed subschemes whose union is the whole scheme, with the first map the difference of the two pushforwards from the scheme theoretic intersection (statement lines 2990-3006, tag 0F94). Surjectivity is a citation, but exactness in the middle requires a real argument: one writes the vanishing sum as a locally finite family of principal divisors, splits that family according to which closed subscheme each integral component lies in, and rearranges the equation so that the two given classes become the two pushforwards of one cycle supported on the intersection. The splitting and rearrangement are the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Four equivalent characterisations of a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states the equivalence of four descriptions of an affine formal algebraic space: being Noetherian; being adic* with every closed subscheme Noetherian; being adic* with the stages of one presentation Noetherian; and being weakly adic with the stages of one presentation Noetherian (statement lines 2557-2572). The proof closes the cycle. From the definition one writes the space as the formal spectrum of a Noetherian adic ring, and a closed immersion from a scheme into it is seen to be affine and to be a closed immersion into the spectrum of that ring, hence Noetherian, which gives the second description (proof lines 2574-2582). Two further implications are immediate from the implications between the types of affine formal algebraic spaces (proof lines 2584-2587). The step from the third description back to the definition writes the space as the formal spectrum of an adic ring with a finitely generated ideal of definition, uses openness of that ideal to find one of the given Noetherian quotients inside it, and concludes that the ring is Noetherian by the corresponding algebra statement on completions (proof lines 2589-2597). The step from the fourth to the third works with a weakly adic ring, uses that its ideal of definition has an open second power closure, finds a given Noetherian quotient inside that closure, deduces that the quotient by the second power is Noetherian and hence that the quotient of the ideal by its second power is a finite module, and concludes that the ideal of definition may be taken finitely generated (proof lines 2599-2609). The claim is H2: four implications are proved and, while two are immediate, each of the other two is a short argument combining a presentation with an algebra statement about completions or about finite generation of ideals.

items.title: A directed colimit of formal algebraic spaces glued by closed immersions is a formal algebraic space
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a directed system of formal algebraic spaces whose transition maps are closed immersions inducing isomorphisms on the reductions, the colimit, taken in fppf sheaves, is again a formal algebraic space (statement lines 7902-7910). The proof constructs the presentation explicitly. A member of the system is fixed and one of its affine etale coverings is chosen, so that the covering is an etale covering by affine schemes after passing to reductions (proof lines 7912-7917). The covering is then extended to the whole system: since the reductions of all members agree, the etale covering of the reduction of the fixed member corresponds to an affine formal algebraic space etale over every other member, and the identification lemma for the affine etale site shows both that base changing it back gives the original piece and that the pieces are compatible along the system (proof lines 7917-7938). Taking the colimits of the pieces over the system produces a morphism into the colimit of the members, which is etale because any morphism into the colimit from a quasi-compact scheme factors through a member, so it remains to see that each collected piece is an affine formal algebraic space; this follows because the transition maps between the pieces are closed immersions, as base changes of the given ones, and induce isomorphisms on reductions, which is the situation of the auxiliary statement on colimits of affine pieces (proof lines 7938-7951). The claim is H2: the argument is a construction carried along a directed system, and its three ingredients -- extending the covering along the system, showing the resulting morphism is etale by testing on quasi-compact schemes, and reducing each piece to the affine case -- are each stated with their reason.

items.title: The type of an affine formal algebraic space is inherited by an affine morphism over it
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a representable affine map of fppf sheaves from X to an affine formal algebraic space Y, the lemma asserts that X is an affine formal algebraic space and that it inherits countable indexedness, countable indexedness together with classicity, weak adicness, the adic* property, and -- when Y is Noetherian and the map is locally of finite type -- Noetherianness (statement lines 4315-4336). The proof of the first part is a colimit argument: writing the target as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, the fibre products with X are affine because the map is representable and affine, and they present X as a colimit, which is exactly the shape required of an affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 4338-4345). The second part reads off countable indexedness because the index set may then be taken countable (proof lines 4347-4351). Parts (3), (4) and (5) are grouped: in each case the assumptions already imply that the target is countably indexed and weakly admissible, so the source is, and after writing both as formal spectra the map corresponds to a continuous algebra homomorphism, which the representability and affineness of the map make taut; the three properties are then transported by the three corresponding ascent statements for taut maps (proof lines 4353-4368). The last part combines the third with an implication between types to get the adic* property for the source, then applies the criterion for Noetherian affine formal algebraic spaces twice, once to learn that the stages of a presentation are Noetherian and once, after the fibre products are seen to be Noetherian because the map is locally of finite type, to conclude for the source (proof lines 4370-4385). The claim is H2: the parts are parallel consequences of one colimit description and of the tautness of the induced ring map, but each transfer is named and the Noetherian case requires a two-step use of a criterion.

items.title: A morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces is of finite type exactly when the ring map is taut and topologically of finite type
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a continuous map of weakly admissible topological rings over a scheme, the lemma states that the induced morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces is of finite type if and only if the ring map is taut and the target ring is topologically of finite type over the source (statement lines 6342-6350). The proof fixes a common framework: tautness corresponds to representability, and both spaces are written as filtered colimits of the spectra of their quotients by weak ideals of definition, the target's quotients being the closures of the images of the source's (proof lines 6352-6358). For the direction from the ring-theoretic condition, one chooses a ring map from a polynomial algebra with dense image, notes that it remains dense after passing to any of the quotients and hence is surjective there, and then for a quasi-compact test scheme over the source -- which factors through one of the quotients -- identifies the base change of the morphism with the base change of the corresponding map of affine schemes, which is of finite type (proof lines 6360-6374). For the converse one picks a quotient of the source, uses the hypothesis to see that the corresponding maps of quotients are of finite type, lifts images of generators back to the target ring, and shows the resulting polynomial map has dense image by comparing two quotients and applying the criterion for surjectivity modulo a locally nilpotent ideal (proof lines 6376-6391). The claim is H2: two implications are proved, each resting on a different observation -- the first on the compatibility of the presentations and the second on the comparison of two quotients through a surjectivity criterion.

items.title: Splitting of the conormal sequence for a composite of immersions detects regularity of both factors over a locally Noetherian base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a composite of two immersions over a locally Noetherian base, regularity of both factors, regularity of the composite together with regularity of the first factor, and regularity of the composite together with split exactness of the conormal sequence are equivalent (statement lines 5144-5163). The counted proof is a compact local algebra argument: it reduces to local rings where all notions of regular immersion agree, cites two implications, and then proves the remaining one by choosing a minimal generating system of the larger ideal whose first part minimally generates the smaller ideal, using the assumed splitting, observing that this system is a regular sequence and splitting it according to the definition of a regular sequence to obtain the two shorter sequences (proof lines 5165-5197). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the standard criteria for regular sequences and conormal sequences.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps

items.difficulty_reason: The acyclicity lemma states that for a complex of finite modules over a local Noetherian ring whose i-th term has depth at least i, the cohomology at the largest index where exactness fails has depth at least one (statement lines 25009-25023). The proof does not use spectral sequences or a resolution argument: it breaks the complex into a chain of short exact sequences exposing that cohomology group, then propagates depth bounds along the chain using the depth lemma, starting from the given bounds on the top terms (proof lines 25024-25048). The bookkeeping of which sequence yields which bound is the content, and the author writes every step out. H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a map M to N, any resolution of N and any free complex mapping to M, there is a map of complexes lifting the given square, and any two such maps are homotopic (statement lines 17716-17737). The proof does not use a general lifting theorem for projective complexes: it lifts degree by degree using freeness of the terms, and repeats the same device for the difference of two comparison maps, correcting each degree so that the next lift lands in a kernel (proof lines 17739-17763). Seeing that the homotopy is the same lifting argument applied to the difference is the content, and the author writes the induction steps out in both parts. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if R to S is faithfully flat and the base change of M is Mittag-Leffler over S, then M is Mittag-Leffler over R (statement lines 22558-22565). The proof does not argue with the definition directly: it reduces the claim through the characterisation to producing an index over which one comparison map dominates another, rewrites that domination as universal injectivity of the map from the approximating module to a pushout, transports the picture along the flat base change, and then uses faithful flatness to bring the universal injectivity back down (proof lines 22567-22599). Choosing the pushout formulation so that faithful flatness applies is the step that carries the argument. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a local Noetherian ring and a finite module, any permutation of a regular sequence is again regular (statement lines 16855-16862). The proof does not use the Koszul complex or a dimension count: it treats the case of two elements directly by analysing the kernel of multiplication by the second element and concluding by Nakayama, then handles the general case by writing a permutation as a product of adjacent transpositions and applying the two-element case to the quotient by the preceding elements (proof lines 16864-16890). The reduction to adjacent transpositions on a quotient is what makes the general case follow from the two-term one. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a module over a local ring which is a direct sum of finite modules, no associated prime of a tensor product with an arbitrary module can generate the unit ideal together with the extended maximal ideal (statement lines 4378-4386, tag 05IU). The identity and the Nakayama step are the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves exactness of the functor j_{U!} taking a module on an object U to a module on the whole ringed site. items.title: Flatness of a sheafification from flatness of a cover of the presheaf of modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-modules.tex (Modules on Sites)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file sites-modules.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a presheaf of modules whose values admit a covering on which they are flat over the corresponding rings has a flat sheafification. The proof starts from an inclusion of modules and has to prove injectivity of the induced map on tensor products with the sheafification; using that both sides are sheafifications of the presheaf tensor products, and that the presheaf tensor product is computed sectionwise on objects where the module is flat, it reduces the claim to a statement about maps of presheaves which is then handled by the same covering argument (proof lines 4536-4556). The proof takes Q^bullet = eta_I M^bullet, which represents L eta_I M by Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-Leta, and reduces the boundedness and local freeness checks to the affine local case, where boundedness is clear (proof lines 13546-13552). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for f : X -> Y a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over (S, delta) with both X and Y quasi-compact, regular, of affine diagonal and finite dimension, f is a local complete intersection morphism, and that if moreover the Gysin map exists for f and f is proper then f_*(alpha . f^!beta) = f_*alpha . beta in CH^*(Y) otimes Q for the intersection product of the regular section (statement lines 13912-13926). The first assertion is More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-morphism-regular-schemes-is-lci; the proof notes f^![Y] = [X] by Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-easy, writes alpha = ch(alpha') cap [X] and beta = ch(beta') cap [Y] with alpha', beta' in K_0(Vect) otimes Q as in the construction of that intersection product, and sets c = ch(alpha'), c' = ch(beta') (proof lines 13928-13940). Recognising that the regularly embedded situation admits the same bivariant bookkeeping as the smooth case, with the Chern character providing the bridge to K-theory, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

For the first part the proof chooses U and N' as in the definition of a pure spreadout: every element of N' has a content ideal because N' is A-projective, which follows either directly or from More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-content-exists-flat-Mittag-Leffler together with Algebra, Example labelled algebra-example-ML (proof lines 7240-7250). For the second part the proof reduces to A local at a maximal ideal, and for each s in S considers the composition N' -> N -> N -> M; each map is injective modulo the maximal ideal, so the composition is A-universally injective by Lemma labelled lemma-universally-injective-local, and since N is the colimit of the (1/s)N' one concludes that u is a colimit of universally injective maps and hence universally injective (proof lines 7257-7267; the localization reduction is marked 'small detail omitted'). items.title: Adic morphisms into a formal completion come from morphisms meeting the closed subset only at the closed point
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an algebraic space X with a closed subset T whose complement is quasi-compact, and a complete local Noetherian algebra R, the lemma asserts that an adic morphism from the formal spectrum of R into the formal completion of X along T corresponds to a unique morphism from the spectrum of R into X whose preimage of T is exactly the closed point (statement lines 7314-7321). That the statement makes sense uses that the completion is adic* by an earlier result on the types of formal completions, so that adicness of morphisms is available (proof lines 7323-7326). The proof first applies the statement comparing morphisms from the spectrum and from the formal spectrum of a complete local Noetherian ring to produce a unique morphism g into X lifting the composition of the given adic morphism with the comparison map (proof lines 7327-7330). It then studies the fibre product of the formal spectrum with the reduced induced structure on T: since the given morphism is adic it is representable, the fibre product is an algebraic space with a closed immersion into the formal spectrum, and because the comparison map is a monomorphism this fibre product can also be computed over X (proof lines 7331-7340). It is therefore the spectrum of a quotient of R by an ideal containing a power of the maximal ideal, and comparing that quotient with the fibre product of the spectrum of R with the reduced subspace over successive thickenings gives two ideals with the same images modulo every sufficiently high power of the maximal ideal; Krull's intersection theorem then forces the two ideals to be equal, which is exactly the assertion about the preimage of T (proof lines 7340-7351). The claim is H2: the argument combines a lifting statement with a computation of two fibre products and closes it by an intersection theorem, each step named and displayed.

items.title: The affine etale site of an affine formal algebraic space is the category of representable etale affine formal algebraic spaces over it
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the affine etale site of an affine formal algebraic space with the category of morphisms from an affine formal algebraic space into it which are representable by algebraic spaces and etale (statement lines 7479-7491). The proof constructs the equivalence in both directions. The functor takes such a morphism to its fibre product with the reduction of the base, and the first observation is that the morphism is in fact representable by schemes and affine, so that this fibre product is an affine scheme, giving an object of the affine etale site (proof lines 7493-7503). For the quasi-inverse the base is written as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, each of which receives the reduction as a thickening; since etale affine schemes over a scheme depend only on the reduction in this situation, an etale morphism from an affine scheme to the reduction extends to a compatible system of etale morphisms at every stage, whose colimit is an affine formal algebraic space over the base (proof lines 7505-7520). The author then observes that the construction has the expected fibre products along the stages, which shows the resulting morphism is representable and etale, and leaves the verification that the two constructions are mutually inverse to the reader (proof lines 7520-7526). The claim is H2: both functors are built and their required properties -- affineness of the fibre product in one direction, representability and etaleness in the other -- are proved, with only the final round-trip verification omitted.

items.title: A directed colimit of algebraic spaces glued by thickenings is a formal algebraic space
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a directed system of algebraic spaces whose transition maps are thickenings, the colimit taken in fppf sheaves is a formal algebraic space (statement lines 2972-2979). The proof builds the required covering explicitly. The colimit is a sheaf by construction; a member of the system is fixed and an etale covering of it by affine schemes is chosen, which exists by a general statement on coverings of algebraic spaces by affines (proof lines 2981-2987). The covering is then propagated along the system: for each later member there is a cartesian diagram with etale vertical arrows whose existence is the topological invariance of the etale site under thickenings, and these diagrams are unique up to unique isomorphism, so the pieces are compatible along the system, the transition maps between them are thickenings as base changes of thickenings, and each piece is an affine scheme because the fibre product of an affine scheme over a thickening is again affine (proof lines 2987-3003). Taking the colimit of the pieces yields an affine formal algebraic space, and the resulting morphism to the colimit of the members is etale because any morphism from an affine scheme into the colimit factors through a member -- a step the author marks as omitted (proof lines 3003-3011). The claim is H2: two constructions are used in earnest, the propagation of an etale covering along a system of thickenings with its uniqueness, and the reduction of the affineness of the pieces to a statement on limits of spaces, with only the factorisation step left unproved.

items.title: Countable indexedness ascends and descends along a representable surjective flat morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable, surjective and flat, the lemma asserts that the source is countably indexed if and only if the target is (statement lines 4548-4553). One direction is a citation; the other is a real argument. Assuming the source countably indexed, one writes both spaces as filtered colimits, and for each stage of the source finds a stage of the target through which it factors; conversely, for each stage of the target, the fibre product with the source is an affine scheme and therefore factors through some stage of the source (proof lines 4555-4568). The author then displays the resulting diagram and observes that the proof is complete once the dotted arrow -- a factorisation of one stage of the target through a later one -- exists (proof lines 4568-4574). That existence is established by choosing a stage above the two in question, translating the two closed subschemes into ideals of its coordinate ring, and using the hypothesis: the relevant fibre product is faithfully flat over the stage of the target, so the containment of the two ideals after extending along the source morphism descends to a containment of the ideals themselves (proof lines 4574-4589). Since the stages selected form a cofinal countable subsystem, the target is countably indexed (proof lines 4571-4576). The claim is H2: the argument builds a cofinal countable subsystem of a presentation and the single nontrivial step -- descent of an inclusion of ideals along a faithfully flat morphism -- is displayed with its reason.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives three equivalent criteria for a bivariant class to vanish: vanishing of the class itself, vanishing of its cap with the fundamental class of every integral locally finite type base, and the existence of a proper birational cover on which that cap vanishes (statement lines 6584-6599, tag 02UC). items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a scheme whose weakly associated points are generic points of components and whose components are locally finite, the sheaf of meromorphic functions is simultaneously the direct sum and the product of the skyscrapers at the generic points, with consequences for meromorphic sections of quasi-coherent modules, the description of nonzerodivisors, the total quotient rings of local rings and of affine coordinate rings, and the identification of rational with meromorphic functions (statement lines 6034-6073). items.title: The axiom of choice implies the law of excluded middle
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file setmath.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 614-619 (book Theorem 10.1.14, Diaconescu theorem): the axiom of choice implies the law of excluded middle. The statement is a global implication between principles and gives no construction, and the proof (source lines 621-646) has to build the whole argument around one mere proposition A: the two-point map into the suspension of A has to be shown surjective, which needs a fibre over each pole and the fact that truncated fibres are mere propositions; choice then supplies a section merely, whose existence is used together with decidable equality of the booleans to produce a disjunction; and that disjunction has to be transported along the injectivity of the section and the identification of the equality of the two poles with A. Which form of choice is used, why the suspension of a proposition is the right type, and where decidability enters are all invisible in the statement.

items.title: A composition of standard smooth ring maps is standard smooth
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that composing two standard smooth ring maps gives a standard smooth ring map (statement lines 37589-37592). items.title: Symbolic powers are preserved by a flat extension along which the prime stays prime
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a flat ring map R to S and a prime p whose extension q is prime, the lemma states that the extension of the n-th symbolic power of p is the n-th symbolic power of q (statement lines 15794-15799). The proof does not compare primary decompositions: it rewrites both symbolic powers as kernels of maps to localised quotients, reduces to injectivity of the localised comparison, and then obtains that injectivity from the existence of a filtration whose subquotients are tensor products of a vector space with the localised residue ring, which makes elements outside q act invertibly (proof lines 15801-15829). Producing that filtration from flatness is the step carrying the argument. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts existence and uniqueness of the tensor product as the module representing bilinear maps, with the commuting diagram drawn in the statement (statement lines 1932-1953). The proof builds the module as a quotient of the free module on the product by the bilinearity relations, extends a bilinear map along the basis to get the universal arrow, and then produces the unique comparing isomorphism between two solutions by evaluating the two composites on generators (proof lines 1960-1993). Quotienting the free module by exactly the relations needed for well-definedness is the step that carries existence. H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if there is a unique prime of S over p and either going up holds, or going down holds with at most one prime over every prime of R, then the localisation of S at p equals the localisation at that prime (statement lines 10013-10029). Reading the two hypotheses as two ways of closing the same cube is the content. H2.

items.title: Transport in the circle code along the generating loop adds one to the integer
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file homotopy.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 447-450 (book Lemma 8.1.2): transporting an integer in the circle code along the generating loop yields its successor, and along the inverse loop its predecessor. The statement is arithmetic about a transport, and the proof (source lines 451-460) has to carry it out through three rewrites: the composition rule for transport, the computation of the action of the code family on the loop as the successor equivalence, and the computation of transport along the univalent image of that equivalence; only then does the arithmetic appear. The second equation is then obtained by the general fact that transports along a path and its inverse are mutually inverse, which is exactly why the second half costs no computation. Which rewrite supplies which factor is the whole content and the statement shows none of it.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement gives an explicit presentation of the level one Demazure module D(1, k theta) by one generator and four families of relations, including the annihilation by the positive part, the action of the Cartan part, and two families for the negative root vectors (author proposition at source lines 396-425, label WvsD). The proof (source lines 426-442) uses a root system observation to see that one family of known relations does not occur, simplifies the other family using the relation labelled w2', and identifies the remaining relations with the defining relations of the local Weyl module (proof lines 427-441). The comparison of the listed relations with the known ones is the content. H2.

items.title: Annihilation in a fusion product from annihilation in the factors
items.author: Bhimarthi Ravinder
items.work: Demazure Modules, Chari-Venkatesh Modules and Fusion Products
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 10 (2014) article 110, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2014.110; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that if a fixed element of the Lie algebra twisted by a high enough power of the parameter annihilates each generator of the factors, then the element twisted by the sum of the exponents annihilates the fusion product (author lemma at source lines 559-565, label f2). The proof (source lines 566-576) passes to the associated graded of the tensor product, uses the article's lemma f1 to compute the action of the twisted operator on the class of the tensor of the generators, and reads the conclusion off the definition of the fusion product (proof lines 567-575). The computation in the associated graded is the content. H2.

items.title: Two relations in the local Weyl module attached to a multiple of the highest root
items.author: Bhimarthi Ravinder
items.work: Demazure Modules, Chari-Venkatesh Modules and Fusion Products
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 10 (2014) article 110, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2014.110; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement records two relations in the local Weyl module W((k+1)theta): a power of the lowering operator times a twisted vector annihilates the highest weight vector, and a product of two twisted vectors lies in the submodule generated by a higher one (author lemma at source lines 323-338, label g). The proof (source lines 340-368) proves the first relation by a complete commutator computation: it replaces a raising operator applied to a high power of a lowering operator by the commutator, expands it as a sum, substitutes the explicit commutator with the Cartan element, simplifies to a non-zero multiple of the desired vector and uses the vanishing of a high power (proof lines 341-364); the second relation is obtained by specialising the article's labelled commutation relation (proof lines 365-367). The commutator computation is the content. H3.

items.title: The forcing question for split pairs is decided Y-prime computably
items.author: Quentin Le Hou\'erou, Ludovic Levy Patey, Keita Yokoyama
items.work: Conservation of Ramsey's theorem for pairs\\ and well-foundedness
items.difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2402.11616v3 的 Lemma lem:sads-forcing-question-sigma01（源 1149-1156 行，证明 1158-1166 行）：在 SADS 的 split-pair 力迫下，forcing question 成立与否两种情况都能 Y′-可计算地判出，并各自给出扩展使某一侧强制收敛或发散。关键操作不是例行核验：第一种情况必须用「split pair 的两半必有一半落在 U 或 V 内」这一核心性质把收敛搬到某一侧（1159 行）；第二种情况要造一个 Y-可计算的下降序列枚举、利用「模型内不存在解」假设断定它有限，再用最小/最大性把见证找出来并判定属于哪一侧（1161-1163 行），最后用 forcing question 失败排除两个见证同时落在正确侧，再补一个元素得到发散（1165 行）。难点在于两种情况的对称处理与「用最小性保证发散」的验证；原文位置在证明的 1159、1161-1163 与 1165 行。
