items.title: Criteria forcing the pushforward of abelian sheaves along a morphism of topoi to be exact
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-modules.tex (Modules on Sites)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file sites-modules.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives four alternative hypotheses on a morphism of topoi - preservation of surjections of sheaves of sets or of abelian sheaves, commutation with coequalizers, or with pushouts - each of which forces the pushforward of abelian sheaves to be exact. Since f_* is a right adjoint, it is already left exact, so only the preservation of surjections has to be checked; the proof shows that each of the four hypotheses implies the corresponding statement about surjections or coequalizers needed to conclude right exactness, and then assembles the conclusion (proof lines 1723-1741). H2: the reduction of the four hypotheses to the single right-exactness statement is the substance.

items.title: The localization of a ringed topos at a sheaf is a ringed topos with a canonical morphism to the original
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter sites-modules.tex (Modules on Sites)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file sites-modules.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma endows the localization of a topos at a sheaf F with a structure sheaf O_F, making it a ringed topos, and produces the canonical morphism of ringed topoi to the original, together with the expected descriptions of the functors involved. The proof imports from the sites-level localization lemma that the localized category is a topos and the basic properties, identifies the pullback of the structure sheaf with O_F using that lemma, and hence may take the structure map j_F^sharp to be the identity; it further reduces to the case where the site has finite limits with a subcanonical topology and F is representable, where the remaining description follows from the explicit description of the lower shriek functor (proof lines 2764-2782). H2: the identification of the structure sheaf and the reduction to the representable case are the substance.

items.title: Composition of two flat base changes is a flat base change and the pullbacks compose
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For flat morphisms g : S' -> S and g' : S'' -> S' with constants c and c' as in Situation labelled situation-setup-base-change, and X -> S locally of finite type with base changes X' and X'', the lemma asserts that the composite data is again of that form, that g^* and (g')^* compose on cycles to the pullback along g o g', and that the same holds on Chow groups with the map of Lemma labelled lemma-pullback-base-change (statement lines 15437-15460). For the first part the proof takes a generic point s'' of a component of (g o g')^{-1}(s), sets s' = g'(s''), notes that s'' is a generic point of a component of (g')^{-1}(s') and, because g' is flat so generalizations lift by Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-base-change-flat, that s' is a generic point of a component of g^{-1}(s); the assumed shifts delta'(s') = delta(s) + c and delta''(s'') = delta'(s') + c' then give delta''(s'') = delta(s) + c + c' (proof lines 15462-15476). For the second part, an integral closed subscheme Z of delta-dimension k has base changes Z' and Z'' with g^*[Z] = [Z']_{k+c} and, by Lemma labelled lemma-pullback-coherent-base-change, (g')^*[Z']_{k+c} = [Z'']_{k+c+c'}, which is exactly the composition statement on cycles and hence on Chow groups (proof lines 15478-15480). Tracking the generic points of the iterated fibres to add the shifts is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

primary.label: author Lemma environment, source label lemma-compose-base-change (statement, source lines 15437-15460)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the statement (source lines 15462-15480)

items.title: Global sections and derived Hom against a perfect object in the existence situation are perfect and compute the reductions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-existence with K as in Lemma labelled lemma-compute-what-it-should-be, the lemma asserts for every perfect object E of D(O_X) that M = RGamma(X, K otimes^L E) is perfect over D(A) with a canonical isomorphism RGamma(X_n, F_n otimes^L E|_{X_n}) = M otimes_A^L A_n, and dually that N = RHom_X(E, K) is perfect over D(A) with RHom_{X_n}(E|_{X_n}, F_n) = N otimes_A^L A_n (statement lines 8078-8096). The proof of (2) writes E_n = E|_{X_n} and N_n = RHom_{X_n}(E_n, F_n), recalls that RHom_{X_n}(-, -) is RGamma(X_n, RSheafHom(-,-)) by Cohomology, Section labelled cohomology-section-global-RHom, and uses Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-base-change-RHom-perfect to see that each N_n is perfect over D(A_n) with base change compatible formation (proof lines 8098-8110). Hence the transition maps N_n otimes^L A_{n-1} -> N_{n-1} are isomorphisms, so More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-Rlim-perfect-gives-perfect shows Rlim N_n is perfect and recovers N_n after base change; since the exact functor RHom_X(E, -) commutes with products and hence with derived limits, RHom_X(E, K) = Rlim RHom_X(E, F_n) = Rlim N_n, giving (2) (proof lines 8112-8123). Statement (1) is translated into (2) with Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex (proof lines 8123-8125). Recognising that the system of perfect complexes is Mittag-Leffler enough for its derived limit to be perfect, and identifying the derived limit with the Hom against K, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Vector bundles for the colimit along Frobenius form a stack in groupoids for the h topology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For a prime p and a scheme S in characteristic p, the proposition asserts that the category fibred in groupoids over (Sch/S)_h whose fibre category over U is the category of finite locally free colim_F O_U-modules is a stack in groupoids, and that for quasi-compact and quasi-separated U the fibre category is colim_F Vect(U) (statement lines 12439-12450). The proof disposes of the final assertion by Lemma labelled lemma-colim-F-Vect, then verifies conditions (1), (2) and (3) of Lemma labelled lemma-refine-check-h-stack (proof lines 12452-12458). Condition (1) is immediate because glueing for the Zariski topology holds by definition; condition (2) is reduced, for a surjective flat proper finite presentation f : X -> Y with Y affine, to the equivalence Vect(Y) -> Vect(X) x_{Vect(X x_Y X)} Vect(X) obtained from fppf descent of finite locally free modules by Descent, Proposition labelled descent-proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent and Lemma labelled descent-lemma-finite-locally-free-descends, since the four schemes involved are quasi-compact and quasi-separated so that the description of fibre categories applies (proof lines 12460-12476). Condition (3) is the content of Lemmas labelled lemma-vector-bundle-I and lemma-vector-bundle-II (proof lines 12478-12483). Recognising that colimits of vector bundles are computed after fppf descent and that the remaining conditions are exactly the two almost blowup computations is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: For a smooth equidimensional scheme over a field the bivariant Chow ring is Chow homology and composition becomes intersection
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a field k and a smooth scheme X over k equidimensional of dimension d, the lemma asserts that c -> c cap [X]_d is an isomorphism A^p(X) -> CH_{d-p}(X) and that under it composition of bivariant classes becomes the intersection product (statement lines 14402-14412). The proof writes the map as a composition of two isomorphisms A^p(X) -> A^{p-d}(X -> Spec(k)) -> CH_{d-p}(X), the first being c -> c o g^* from Proposition labelled proposition-compute-bivariant and the second c -> c cap [Spec(k)] from Lemma labelled lemma-chow-cohomology-towards-point (proof lines 14414-14422). It then reads the inverses off the proofs of those two results: the inverse of the second sends alpha to the class c_alpha acting by beta -> alpha x beta in CH_*(X x_k Y), and the inverse of the first sends c_alpha to the class acting by beta -> Delta^!(alpha x beta) = alpha . beta, which identifies composition with the intersection product (proof lines 14424-14434). Chasing the two explicit inverses to see that composition corresponds to the diagonal product is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: A finite locally free module trivial at all codimension one points of a normal base is pulled back from the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> S flat and proper with O_S = f_* O_X, S normal Noetherian, and a finite locally free E on X whose pullback to X x_S Spec(O_{S,s}) is free at every codimension one point s of S, the lemma asserts that E is isomorphic to the pullback of a finite locally free O_S-module (statement lines 12640-12653). The proof shows that the canonical map Phi : f^*f_* E -> E is an isomorphism: by flat base change, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma labelled coherent-lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, together with assumptions (1) and (3), the pullback of Phi to X x_S Spec(O_{S,s}) is an isomorphism at every codimension one point s (proof lines 12655-12663). Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-check-isomorphism-via-depth-and-ass then reduces the claim to depth((f^*f_*E)_x) at least 2 for every x mapping to a point s of codimension at least 2; flatness identifies (f^*f_*E)_x with (f_*E)_s otimes O_{X,x}, so it suffices to bound depth((f_*E)_s) below by 2, which follows from Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-apply-grothendieck together with the depth at least 2 of O_{S,s} for a normal Noetherian scheme of dimension at least 2 by Properties, Lemma labelled properties-lemma-criterion-normal and the pushforward depth bound of Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-depth-pushforward (proof lines 12665-12679). Reducing triviality to the isomorphism of the canonical map and then controlling depth at codimension two through normality is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file sites.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for any set-valued functor the direct image on presheaves is right adjoint to the stalk functor (statement lines 8174-8179). The proof is a short but complete argument: a morphism from a presheaf into the direct image of a set is a compatible system of maps from the values times the values of the functor into the set, and the description of the stalk shows that a morphism out of the stalk into the set is the same kind of compatible system (proof lines 8182-8192), which gives the asserted bijection. The non-formal content is the comparison of the two descriptions. The claim is H1: a one-step comparison with its inputs named.

items.title: The map from a linearly topologized ring to its completion is taut
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for any linearly topologized ring the canonical map to its completion is taut (statement lines 1341-1344). The proof is short and complete: it fixes a fundamental system of open ideals of the ring, recalls that the completion is the limit of the quotients with the limit topology so that the kernels of the structure maps form a fundamental system of open ideals of the completion, and then identifies each of those kernels with the closure of the extension of the corresponding ideal of the ring, which is exactly the condition defining tautness (proof lines 1346-1354). The claim is H2: the argument is brief, but it is a complete derivation in which the relevant system of open ideals of the completion is produced and each member of it is identified with the closure required by the definition, so nothing is left to the reader and no step is a restatement.

items.title: Etale morphisms onto a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space are formal spectra of completions of etale algebras
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space Y, that is the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological algebra B, the lemma establishes an equivalence between the category of representable etale morphisms of affine formal algebraic spaces into Y and the category of topological B-algebras obtained as completions of etale B-algebras, the equivalence sending such an algebra to its formal spectrum, and deduces that every such source is McQuillan (statement lines 4441-4456). The proof first checks that the functor is well defined, because an etale algebra over B induces etale maps of the quotients and hence a representable etale morphism of formal spectra, and that the formal spectrum functor is fully faithful by an earlier statement (proof lines 4458-4466). The substance is that every representable etale morphism lies in the essential image: fixing a weak ideal of definition and base changing the morphism to the corresponding affine scheme gives an etale morphism of affine schemes, and the lift of that etale map along the quotient supplies an etale B-algebra whose quotient reproduces it (proof lines 4468-4477). One then compares this algebra with the algebras obtained from the other ideals of definition: both are etale lifts of the same etale map over the fixed quotient, and the uniqueness statement for etale lifts along a locally nilpotent ideal produces a unique isomorphism between them compatible with the identification at the fixed quotient, so that the isomorphisms are compatible as the ideal varies (proof lines 4477-4488). This identifies the given space with the formal spectrum of the completion of the constructed algebra, which completes the proof (proof lines 4488-4489). The claim is H2: after the preliminary well-definedness and full faithfulness, the argument has two genuine steps -- lifting an etale map along a quotient and gluing the resulting lifts by a uniqueness statement -- and both are displayed rather than cited away.

items.title: Weak pre-adicness descends along a taut map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of the taut descent statements of the chapter, the lemma asserts that if the target ring B is weakly pre-adic then so is the source A (statement lines 1856-1860). The proof works directly with the characterisation of weak pre-adicness rather than with its definition. It first obtains pre-admissibility of A from the corresponding descent statement for admissibility, so that it remains to show that the closure of a power of an ideal of definition is open (proof lines 1862-1870). Fixing an ideal of definition of A and an exponent, the proof chooses a fundamental system of open ideals of A and passes to the closures of their extensions to B; since B is weakly pre-adic the closure of the power of the extension of the chosen ideal is open, so one of the extended open ideals lies inside the intersection which computes that closure, an identification supplied by the lemma describing closures as intersections of quotients (proof lines 1870-1882). Rewriting that containment modulo each member of the fundamental system, using that every element of the closure agrees with an element of the extension of the chosen ideal modulo that member, gives a containment of the images of the two ideals in the quotient of B; faithful flatness of the maps between the quotients then descends the containment to A, and one reads off that the chosen open ideal lies in the closure of the power of the ideal of definition, which is therefore open (proof lines 1882-1890). The claim is H2: a single descent is carried out, but it requires the reduction to a topological statement, the identification of a closure by an intersection, and a faithfully flat descent of an inclusion of ideals, each displayed with its reason.

items.title: A weakly adic ring whose ideal of definition has finite dimensional square quotient is adic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a weakly adic topological ring is adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition as soon as some ideal of definition has the property that its quotient by the closure of its square is a finitely generated module (statement lines 1713-1718). The proof uses the characterisation of weakly adic rings and proceeds by an induction on powers: generators of that quotient are chosen and lifted to elements of the ideal, and the identity expressing the ideal as the sum of the ideal they generate and the square closure is iterated, using the description of the square of a sum of ideals, to show that the ideal they generate together with the closure of every higher power is the whole ideal (proof lines 1720-1729). Consequently the closure of the ideal generated by the chosen elements is the ideal of definition itself, so that the closures of the powers of that finitely generated ideal are exactly the closures of the powers of the given one and therefore form a fundamental system of open ideals; the auxiliary statement on finite generation then gives the conclusion (proof lines 1729-1734). The claim is H2: the induction is carried out explicitly and its consequence -- that the closures of the powers of the finitely generated ideal agree with those of the given ideal -- is what makes the definition of adicness apply.

items.title: The norm of an ample invertible sheaf along a finite morphism with a degree d norm is ample on the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if a finite morphism admits a norm of degree d and its source carries an ample invertible sheaf, then the base carries one too, namely the norm of that sheaf (statement lines 3737-3742). The counted proof is short but complete: it obtains quasi-compactness of the base from ampleness on the source and surjectivity of the morphism, then at an arbitrary point uses the ample sheaf to find a section of a high power whose nonvanishing locus sits between the fibre over the point and a chosen affine neighbourhood, takes its norm, and applies the cap criterion for ampleness using that the nonvanishing locus of a section inside an affine open is affine (proof lines 3744-3767). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the standard ampleness criterion and the properties of the norm map.

items.title: Computing the restriction of the Chern classes of a perfect object after a proper birational modification
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a perfect object whose Chern classes are defined, any locally finite type morphism from an integral scheme can be replaced by an integral proper birational model on which the pulled back object is represented by a bounded complex of locally free modules of constant rank, with the p-th Chern class of that complex equal to the restriction of the Chern class of the object (statement lines 9355-9372, tag 0GUE-adjacent). The proof base changes the trivialising envelope, chooses a suitable point over the generic point, cuts out an integral closed subscheme through it so that the projection becomes proper and birational, and pulls back the representing complex, using integrality to conclude boundedness and constant rank. The construction of the model is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the projection formula for an arbitrary Chern class against a proper pushforward (statement lines 7393-7405, tag 02SJ). The proof is a real argument through projective bundles: it records the characterising relation for the classes obtained by capping with the Chern classes of the pulled back sheaf on the projective bundle of the sheaf, pushes that relation forward along the morphism between the projective bundles using compatibility of the cap with a first Chern class, with flat pullback and with proper pushforward, and then identifies the pushed forward classes by the uniqueness part of the characterisation. The pushforward of the relation is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a local criterion for universal injectivity: for a map from a projective module to a flat module over a local ring whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal is injective, the map is universally injective (statement lines 1945-1951, tag 05FX-adjacent). The proof reduces to a finite free source, writes the flat target as a directed colimit of finite free modules and factors the map through one of them, observes that injectivity of the reduction persists so that the map into each late piece is a split injection, and concludes by compatibility of tensoring with colimits. The splitting step is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: 命题是泛平坦性的分层形式：有限展示态射与有限展示模 F 之下，存在由有限型理想层切出的下降闭环链 S = S_0 ⊃ … ⊃ S_t = ∅，使链的每段差集上 F 的拉回平坦。证明先把情形化到 Noetherian 底（此时「有限型理想」条件自动成立），再用约化底上的泛平坦性取稠密开、以其补集为下一步，最后由 Noether 性保证链终止。不能一眼完成的是「先降条件再迭代」的次序：有限型理想条件必须靠 Noether 化处理掉，否则链的每一环都要额外验证。原文位于第 15565–15612 行。

The proof notes that Z coproduct X' -> X is a surjective proper morphism, hence a ph covering by Topologies, Lemma labelled topologies-lemma-surjective-proper-ph, so the singleton family computes F(X) as an equalizer of two maps out of F(Z coproduct X') (proof lines 10892-10896). Finally the morphism E x_Z E coproduct X' -> X' x_X X' is surjective and proper because b induces an isomorphism X' minus E -> X minus Z, so F(X' x_X X') -> F(E x_Z E) x F(X') is injective and the equalizer condition follows from the diagonal one (proof lines 10914-10918). items.title: Global sections of the twisted object are pseudo-coherent and compute the reductions in the derived existence situation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-existence-derived with K as in Lemma labelled lemma-compute-what-it-should-be-derived, the lemma asserts for every perfect E of D(O_X) that M = RGamma(X, K otimes^L E) is pseudo-coherent over D(A) with a canonical isomorphism RGamma(X_n, K_n otimes^L E|_{X_n}) = M otimes_A^L A_n (statement lines 8461-8474). The proof writes E_n = E|_{X_n} and M_n = RGamma(X_n, K_n otimes^L E|_{X_n}), and uses Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general to see that each M_n is pseudo-coherent over D(A_n) with base change compatible formation, so the transition maps M_n otimes^L A_{n-1} -> M_{n-1} are isomorphisms (proof lines 8476-8486). items.title: The splitting principle: a projective flat modification making finitely many bundles filtrations by invertible sheaves
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for finitely many finite locally free modules on a locally finite type scheme, a projective flat morphism of some relative dimension along which the pullback is injective on Chow groups after any base change and under which each module acquires a filtration by invertible sheaves, with the corresponding injectivity on the bivariant theory (statement lines 8428-8443, tag 0F5F-adjacent). The proof is an induction on the sum of the ranks minus one: at each step it passes to the projective bundle of a bundle of rank greater than one, where an invertible quotient splits off and pullback is injective, and applies the induction hypothesis to the kernel and the remaining bundles. The induction with its bookkeeping of injectivity is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: 命题是形式代数空间的代数化定理在「相对维数 ≤ 1」情形下的形式化：给定相容的形式系统 X_n（方图笛卡尔、dim(X_1) ≤ 1），要造出射影概型态射 X -> S 使各层为基变换。证明的实质是把形式层当作概型 X_1 的加厚，用可逆层的障碍理论把逐层提升化归为 H^2 障碍类消失，再靠「X_1 是维数 ≤ 1 的 Noetherian 概型」使该群为零，最后调用 Grothendieck 代数化定理。不能一眼完成的是把几何维数条件翻译成障碍群消失。原文位于第 10338–10393 行。

items.work: Conservation of Ramsey's theorem for pairs\\ and well-foundedness
items.difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2402.11616v3 的 Lemma lem:sads-wf-forcing-wf-jump（源 1250-1259 行，证明 1261-1292 行）：对两种公式的任意组合与任意条件，存在扩展在两侧强制指定实例并使某一侧的下一实例被否定。证明的关键不是例行核验：作者先把问题化归为「证明那张极大树是 M-有限的」（1262 行），再假设树 M-无穷、取递增的有限树逼近（1270 行），然后为每棵树定义序数秩 ζ_s——在每个结点取 ω 的（f_0 ⨭ f_1）次幂乘（2 − 后继数）再对后继求和（1272-1277 行）；核心是验证 ζ_s 严格下降：两棵相邻树只差一个结点，秩恒等式归结为 ω^{f_0+f_1} > 2·ω^{f_0(ρι)+f_1(ρι)}，而这需要分 Φ_k 与 Ψ_k 四种组合逐一核对 f_0、f_1 在两个后继上的取值行为（1281-1287 行）。难点在于把「树在长」翻译成序数严格下降，且四种公式组合的不等式都必须成立；原文位置在证明的 1272-1277 行与 1281-1287 行。

items.difficulty_reason: For a triple (L, s, i : D -> X) as in Definition labelled definition-gysin-homomorphism over a base (S, delta), the lemma asserts that the Gysin homomorphism i^*, viewed in A^1(D -> X) by Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-bivariant, equals the bivariant class c(D -> X, N) built from the virtual normal sheaf N = i^*L (statement lines 12173-12183). The proof uses the criterion of Lemma labelled lemma-bivariant-zero to reduce to X integral, where it must show i^*[X] = c cap [X], and then splits into two cases (proof lines 12185-12193). If X = D both classes are represented by c_1(N) cap [X]_n with n = dim_delta(X), by Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-fundamental and Definition labelled definition-gysin-homomorphism; if D is not X then D -> X is an effective Cartier divisor, in particular a regular closed immersion of codimension one, and Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-fundamental gives c(D -> X, N) cap [X]_n = [D]_{n-1}, which is also the definition of the Gysin homomorphism (proof lines 12195-12203). Reducing to an integral base and then matching the two cases with the fundamental computation is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: For a smooth quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal the two intersection products agree after tensoring with the rationals
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a field k and a smooth scheme X over k which is quasi-compact and has affine diagonal, the lemma asserts that the intersection product on CH^*(X) constructed in the regular section agrees, after tensoring with Q, with the one constructed in the smooth section (statement lines 14586-14593). The proof takes alpha in CH^i(X) and beta in CH^j(X), writes both as chern characters capped against [X] with alpha', beta' in K_0(Vect(X)) otimes Q as in the regular section, sets c = ch(alpha') and c' = ch(beta'), and observes that the regular intersection product produces c cap c' cap [X] (proof lines 14595-14603). This is the same as alpha . beta by Lemma labelled lemma-identify-chow-for-smooth, or rather by the obvious generalisation of that lemma to smooth schemes that are not assumed equidimensional, namely that c -> c cap [X] is an isomorphism; the author notes the generalisation explicitly in the proof (proof lines 14604-14606). Recognising that both products are computed as caps of Chern characters against the fundamental class, with the identification supplied by the bivariant-to-homology isomorphism, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the invoked generalisation is recorded verbatim in the editorial notes.

Tracking the two degree shifts c and r and matching the base changes of the fibre product is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable by algebraic spaces is in fact representable by schemes and affine (statement lines 4208-4213). For the converse the proof builds the presentation explicitly: the category of representable thickenings from affine schemes is shown to be directed, which uses that the coproduct of two such thickenings can be factored through a third and that between any two objects there is at most one arrow, and the sheaf is written as the colimit over that category, which by hypothesis is a filtered colimit of affine schemes (proof lines 2108-2122). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for formal algebraic spaces X and Y over a sheaf Z whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, the fibre product of X and Y over Z is a formal algebraic space (statement lines 3487-3493). The proof first chooses presentations of the two spaces and observes that the induced family of fibre products is a family of representable etale morphisms onto the fibre product, so that by locality of the definition it suffices to treat the case where both spaces are affine (proof lines 3495-3505). The conclusion follows from the statement that a filtered colimit of algebraic spaces glued by thickenings is a formal algebraic space (proof lines 3514-3518). The claim is H2: the reduction to the affine case is a locality argument with a covering whose members are representable and etale, and the affine case requires writing the colimit and verifying the thickening property of the transition maps.

items.title: The type of a formal algebraic space can be checked on any one presentation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a formal algebraic space and one of the five types -- countably indexed, countably indexed and classical, weakly adic, adic*, Noetherian -- the lemma asserts the equivalence of two formulations: that every representable etale affine formal algebraic space over it has the type, and that the members of some presentation have the type (statement lines 4681-4695). One implication is immediate; the substance is the other. Given a representable etale affine formal algebraic space over the space and a presentation, the fibre products of the given object with the members of the presentation are formal algebraic spaces, so coverings of them may be chosen, and quasi-compactness of the given object allows finitely many members of these coverings to be selected so that their coproduct covers it and is etale over it (proof lines 4697-4712). Each selected member inherits the type from the corresponding member of the presentation by the statement on affine morphisms over an affine formal algebraic space, and the finite coproduct of them does too -- a step the author marks as a small detail omitted concerning finite disjoint unions (proof lines 4712-4718). The conclusion then follows from the corresponding two-way statement for each of the five types (proof lines 4718-4729). The claim is H2: the argument combines a finite refinement by quasi-compactness with two transfers of the type, and it collects the five cases into one statement by citing the five corresponding equivalence results.

items.title: Base change for the right adjoint of pushforward under Tor independence, in three cases
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In diagram labelled equation-base-change, with g : Y' -> Y a morphism of affine schemes, f : X -> Y proper, and f and g Tor independent, the lemma asserts that the base change map of equation labelled equation-base-change-map induces an isomorphism L(g')^*a(K) -> a'(Lg^*K) in three cases: for all K in D_QCoh(O_Y) when f is flat of finite presentation, for all such K when f is perfect and Y is Noetherian, and for K in D_QCoh^+(O_Y) when g has finite Tor dimension and Y is Noetherian (statement lines 1635-1657). Writing Y = Spec(A) and Y' = Spec(A'), the proof picks a perfect generator M of D_QCoh(O_X) by Derived Categories of Schemes, Theorem labelled perfect-theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh, notes that L(g')^*M is a generator, and reduces to the isomorphism of the global Hom complexes of equation labelled equation-iso, which suffices because the cone of L(g')^*a(K) -> a'(Lg^*K) then vanishes (proof lines 1659-1683). It then computes both sides: the left side becomes RHom_Y(Rf_*M, K) otimes^L_A A' using Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-affine-morphism-and-hom-out-of-perfect and Lemma labelled lemma-iso-global-hom, while the right side becomes RHom_{Y'}(Lg^*Rf_*M, Lg^*K) after the base change isomorphism of Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-compare-base-change (proof lines 1685-1707). The comparison map beta is identified with More on Algebra, Equation labelled more-algebra-equation-base-change-RHom, and is an isomorphism in the three cases by listing respectively Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general with More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-base-change-RHom part (1), More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-perfect-proper-perfect-direct-image with part (1) again, and Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemmas labelled perfect-lemma-direct-image-coherent and perfect-lemma-identify-pseudo-coherent-noetherian with part (4) (proof lines 1709-1731). The last part of the proof checks that the two identifications really are induced by equation labelled equation-iso, by writing the large commutative diagram with the alpha maps, the beta map and the maps mu, mu' built from the invertible transformation g'_* o a' -> a o g_* of Lemma labelled lemma-flat-precompose-pus, and reducing to the commutativity of a triangle between RHom_A(E, K), RHom_{A'}(E otimes^L A', K otimes^L A') and RHom_A(E, K otimes^L A'), which holds by the construction of beta in More on Algebra, Section labelled more-algebra-section-base-change-RHom (proof lines 1733-1823). Tracking which of the four comparison maps is the one induced by the base change map, through the generator argument and the two diagram chases, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The upper shriek functors of composable morphisms compose
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-shriek, for composable morphisms f : X -> Y and g : Y -> Z of FTS_S, the lemma asserts a canonical isomorphism (g o f)^! -> f^! o g^! (statement lines 4160-4165). The construction chooses a compactification i : Y -> Ybar of Y over Z and then X -> Xbar of X over Ybar, using More on Flatness, Theorem labelled flat-theorem-nagata and Lemma labelled flat-lemma-compactifyable twice; with a-bar and b-bar the right adjoints of Lemma labelled lemma-twisted-inverse-image for Xbar -> Ybar and Ybar -> Z, the composite a-bar o b-bar is the right adjoint for Xbar -> Z, so g^! = i^* o b-bar and (g o f)^! = (X -> Xbar)^* o a-bar o b-bar (proof lines 4167-4184). Letting U be the inverse image of Y in Xbar and a-bar' the right adjoint for U -> Y, one has f^! = j^* o a-bar', and the base change map gamma : (j')^* o a-bar -> a-bar' o i^* from equation labelled equation-sheafy defines the required arrow, which is an isomorphism on D_QCoh^+ by Lemma labelled lemma-proper-noetherian (proof lines 4186-4200). The rest of the proof shows independence of the choices: given two diagrams, More on Flatness, Lemma labelled flat-lemma-compactifications-cofiltered provides a compactification of Y dominating both, and More on Flatness, Lemma labelled flat-lemma-right-multiplicative-system with Categories, Lemmas labelled categories-lemma-morphisms-right-localization and categories-lemma-equality-morphisms-right-localization provides a compactification of X dominating both compatibly, reducing the comparison to one commutative diagram of compactifications (proof lines 4202-4266). The final step isolates the five base change maps gamma_A to gamma_E attached to the five cartesian squares, writes the required commutativity as gamma_B o gamma_E = (gamma_A o gamma_D) o gamma_C, uses Lemmas labelled lemma-compose-base-change-maps and lemma-compose-base-change-maps-horizontal to rewrite gamma_E = gamma_A o gamma_F and to move gamma_A past gamma_B, and observes that both sides are the base change map for the single square U_1 -> Xbar_1 -> Ybar_2, noting the last equality uses that the squares A and B meet in one point as in Remark labelled remark-going-around (proof lines 4268-4367). Managing the two compactification choices and the algebra of five base change maps is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Completion of a topological module with an I-adic open submodule
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a topological ring, a topological module over it, and a finitely generated ideal, the lemma asserts that if the module has an open submodule whose topology is I-adic then the completion has an open submodule whose topology is I-adic and the quotients of the completion by the powers of I agree with those of the module (statement lines 1024-1030). The proof chooses such an open submodule and notes that the powers of the ideal times it form a fundamental system of open submodules, so the completion of the module contains the completion of that submodule as an open submodule whose topology is I-adic by the corresponding algebra statement (proof lines 1032-1039). The claim is H2: the first half is a short transfer, and the second half requires a choice of generators and an application of the exactness criterion for completions, which is where finite generation is used.

items.title: Surjectivity of an etale morphism of McQuillan affine formal algebraic spaces and faithful flatness of the ring map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of the structure lemma for etale morphisms over a McQuillan space, the lemma asserts the equivalence of the surjectivity of the morphism, faithful flatness of the corresponding map of algebras, and faithful flatness of that map after passing to the quotient by any, or by some, weak ideal of definition (statement lines 4491-4502). The proof first shows that the last three formulations agree: a weak ideal of definition consists of topologically nilpotent elements, so it lies in the Jacobson radical, and for a flat map faithful flatness may be tested after quotienting by an ideal contained in the radical (proof lines 4504-4511). It then relates the first formulation to the third: surjectivity of the morphism implies that each of the morphisms between the spectra of the quotients, which is the base change of the morphism along a quotient of the target, is surjective, which is faithful flatness of the corresponding ring map (proof lines 4511-4516). Conversely, assuming the quotient maps are faithfully flat, a morphism from a quasi-compact scheme into the target factors through a quotient, and the base change of the morphism along that quotient is surjective, whence the morphism itself is surjective (proof lines 4516-4524). The claim is H2: the equivalence among the ring-theoretic formulations is a short transfer, and the geometric equivalence uses the factorisation of test morphisms through a quotient together with the stability of surjectivity under base change.

items.title: The colimit of Hom out of a Deligne system computes Hom on the open
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an open immersion j : U -> X of Noetherian schemes, a Deligne system (K_n) with value K in D^b_Coh(O_U) of the constant system (K_n|_U), and an object L of D^b_Coh(O_X), the lemma asserts that colim Hom_X(K_n, L) = Hom_U(K, L|_U) (statement lines 7919-7927). The proof is a sequence of reductions. First, for a distinguished triangle L -> M -> N -> L[1] one gets a map of long exact sequences because the colimits are exact by Derived Categories, Lemma labelled derived-lemma-representable-homological and Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-directed-colimit-exact, so the statement for two of the three objects implies it for the third by the 5-lemma, and using the truncation triangles of Derived Categories, Remark labelled derived-remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle one reduces to L with a single nonzero cohomology sheaf (proof lines 7929-7946). Next, choosing a bounded complex F^bullet of coherent modules and an ideal I cutting out X minus U with K_n represented by I^n F^bullet, the termwise split short exact sequences coming from stupid truncations give compatible systems of triangles, reducing to the case where F^bullet has one nonzero term (proof lines 7948-7962). The lemma is thus reduced to the isomorphism colim Ext^i_X(I^n F, G) -> Ext^i_U(F|_U, G|_U) for coherent F and G and all i >= 0, where the case i = 0 is Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma labelled coherent-lemma-homs-over-open (proof lines 7964-7972). For injectivity, an element whose restriction to U vanishes is represented in the abelian category of coherent modules via Derived Categories of Schemes, Proposition labelled perfect-proposition-DCoh, giving a surjection F'' -> F killing it; the kernel F' then yields a commutative diagram of colimits whose rows are exact, Artin-Rees makes the inverse systems (I^n F') and (I^n F'' cap F') pro-isomorphic by Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma labelled coherent-lemma-Artin-Rees, and induction on i plus the exactness of the rows forces the class to die (proof lines 7974-8026). For surjectivity, an element over U is killed by a surjection from a coherent O_U-module, which is extended to X by Properties, Lemma labelled properties-lemma-extend-finite-presentation; the same kernel and Artin-Rees argument, together with the fact that F/I^m Im(phi) is supported on X minus U and Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma labelled coherent-lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf, produces an element over X mapping to the given class (proof lines 8028-8086). Running the two reductions by triangles and truncations, and then the two Artin-Rees diagram arguments, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: The comparison map from the pulled back object tensored with the shriek of the structure sheaf to the shriek is well defined and associative
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-shriek, for a morphism f : X -> Y of FTS_S the lemma produces canonical maps mu_{f,K} : Lf^*K otimes^L f^!O_Y -> f^!K, functorial in K in D^+_QCoh(O_Y), and for a second morphism g : Y -> Z asserts the commutativity of the displayed hexagon relating mu_f, f^!mu_g and mu_{g o f} (statement lines 4426-4454). The proper case is disposed of by equation labelled equation-compare-with-pullback and, when g is proper as well, by Lemma labelled lemma-transitivity-compare-with-pullback, which proves the commutativity in greater generality (proof lines 4456-4461). The map is then defined by choosing a compactification j : X -> Xbar of X over Y and restricting the comparison map L fbar^*K otimes^L a-bar(O_Y) -> a-bar(K) of equation labelled equation-compare-with-pullback to X, which is legitimate because f^! = j^* o a-bar (proof lines 4463-4474). Independence of the compactification is proved by the same strategy as Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-well-defined: for g : Xbar_1 -> Xbar_2 with g^{-1}(j_2(X)) = j_1(X), the two maps fit into a commutative diagram by Lemma labelled lemma-transitivity-compare-with-pullback, and the maps sigma and tau restrict to isomorphisms over X by Lemma labelled lemma-compare-on-open; pulling back along j_1 and using the map gamma of equation labelled equation-sheafy together with Lemma labelled lemma-restriction-compare-with-pullback shows that both restrictions are the identity on j_2^*(...) and j_2^*a-bar_2(O_Y), which yields the commutative diagram asserting that the two constructions of mu_{f,K} agree under the identification alpha_g of the proof of Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-well-defined, after which the same categorical arguments show well definedness (proof lines 4476-4540; the author marks the last categorical step 'small detail omitted' and points at the lemma to mirror). The commutativity of the hexagon then follows from the construction of the isomorphism (g o f)^! -> f^! o g^! given in the first part of the proof of Lemma labelled lemma-upper-shriek-composition and from Lemma labelled lemma-transitivity-compare-with-pullback applied to Xbar -> Ybar -> Z (proof lines 4542-4557). Comparing the two compactification constructions through the gamma identifications, exactly as in the well definedness lemma for f^!, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of the preceding lemma on quotients of restricted power series algebras, the lemma adds that when the source ring is admissible -- for instance adic -- the four equivalent conditions there are also equivalent to a fifth one, in which finiteness of type of the induced map of quotients is required for a single ideal of definition rather than for all of them or for a cofinal system (statement lines 6660-6669). The proof shows that the fifth condition implies the first: for an arbitrary weak ideal of definition one has to show that the corresponding map of quotients is of finite type, and since the statement for the intersection of that ideal with the chosen one implies the statement for the ideal, one may assume the arbitrary ideal is contained in the chosen one (proof lines 6671-6679). The claim is H2: the reduction to a comparable ideal, the construction of the commutative diagram with exact rows, and the application of the nilpotent case of the finite type criterion are each displayed.

The easy direction reads discreteness off an etale cover; the converse is the substantive one: from a non-locally-quasi-finite U -> V one extracts a specialization u ~> u' lying over the same point v, compares the transcendence degrees d = trdeg_{kappa(v)} kappa(u) and d' = trdeg_{kappa(v)} kappa(u'), uses the scheme case of the dimension formula for specialisations to get d > d', and then shows that assuming u and u' have the same image in |X_v| produces a point r of R_v = U_v x_{X_v} U_v whose residue field is a finite separable extension of both kappa(u) and kappa(u'), forcing d = d'. That contradiction is the heart of the card and cannot be replaced by a formal argument.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: quasi-compactness together with the existence part of the valuative criterion forces a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over a scheme S to be universally closed (source lines 8797-8807). After reducing to Y affine and to the closedness of |X| -> |Y|, the proof replaces an arbitrary closed T contained in |X| by the preimage of a closed subscheme Z of an affine etale cover U, reduces closedness to stability under specialization, and then runs the valuative argument: a specialization y' ~> y with y' in f(T) gives a point x' represented by Spec(K) -> X and a diagram with Spec(O_{Y,y}), a valuation ring A contained in K dominating the image of O_{Y,y} (possible because y' differs from y), and the assumed criterion produces K'/K and A' dominating A with Spec(A') -> X; the closed point of Spec(A') then maps to a point x of T specializing to x' with f(x) = y. Both the reduction to the affine case and the specialization argument are essential.

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for an algebraic space X over S and a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-algebras A, there is a quasi-coherent subsheaf A' whose value on every affine object U of X_etale is the integral closure of O_X(U) in A(U) (source lines 9934-9943). items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with its two assertions: a quasi-separated universally closed morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion, and for f quasi-compact and quasi-separated universal closedness is equivalent to that criterion (source lines 8861-8872). items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: If f : X -> S is formally etale, then the restriction f|_U : U -> V to open subschemes with f(U) contained in V is formally etale. The retained proof runs the definition: for a solid diagram with a first-order thickening i : T -> T', formal ramifiedness (uniqueness part of formal etaleness) yields a unique S-morphism a' : T' -> X extending a, and since the underlying spaces of T and T' agree, a' factors through U, giving the unique dotted arrow into U. Retained author proof at lines 1580-1592.

items.title: Triviality of an invertible sheaf on a family product from triviality along the factors and the special fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: In the relative-Picard setup (proper, flat, finitely presented morphisms f : X -> S and g : Y -> S with sections sigma, tau), an invertible sheaf L on X x_S Y whose pullbacks along 1 x tau and sigma x 1 and whose restriction to the fibre over s are trivial becomes trivial over the whole product after shrinking S around s. The retained proof is a written two-input argument: the Kunneth lemma for the fibre product makes H^1(X_s x Y_s, O) -> H^1(X_s, O) (+) H^1(Y_s, O) injective, which is precisely the hypothesis needed to apply the multi-Picard lemma (lemma-H1-O-multiple-picard-flat-proper) to the two morphisms 1 x tau and sigma x 1, and the conclusion follows. Retained author proof at lines 9634-9650.

items.title: A cocone of schemes is a colimit if it is fpqc locally a colimit on overlaps
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a diagram of schemes over S with cocone W, if some fpqc covering {W_a -> W} trivializes the colimit property both for each W_a and for each overlap W_a x_W W_b (as colimits of the base-changed diagram), then W itself is the colimit of the diagram in the category of schemes. The retained proof writes out the decisive reduction: a morphism W -> T out of the cocone is the same thing as a collection of morphisms W_a -> T agreeing on the overlaps W_a x_W W_b, which is exactly the fpqc universal effective epimorphism property of the covering (Descent), so the compatible families indexed by the diagram glue uniquely through W. Retained author proof at lines 4199-4204.

items.title: Through every point of the image of a flat finitely presented map there is a locally quasi-finite flat chart
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Given a flat, locally finitely presented morphism f : X -> S and a point s in the image, the lemma produces a commutative triangle with g : S' -> S flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite, with s in the image of g and a map S' -> X over S, i.e. an fppf chart of s that is moreover locally quasi-finite and lands inside X. The retained proof is written out in three moves: the fibre X_s is nonempty, the open-ness-of-CM-locus lemma for flat finite presentation supplies a closed point x of X_s where f is Cohen-Macaulay, and the CM slice lemma then yields Z -> S etale-in-the-slice sense through x; setting S' = Z concludes. items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For morphisms of germs of algebraic spaces (X, x) -> (S, s), the property that the local ring O_{X_s, x} of the fibre is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay is etale local on the source-and-target in the pointed sense of the Descent chapter. The retained proof is written out: in a source-and-target etale diagram, the induced morphism of fibres U'_{v'} -> U_v is etale and maps u' to u (Descent lemma on etale maps of fibres), hence the strict henselizations of O_{U'_{v'}, u'} and O_{U_v, u} agree, and the more-algebra lemma that the henselization of a local ring is Cohen-Macaulay exactly when the ring is (Noetherian likewise) transfers the property. Retained author proof at lines 6205-6215.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, being a closed immersion is equivalent to each of: universally closed + unramified + monomorphism; universally closed + unramified + universally injective; universally closed + locally of finite type + monomorphism; universally closed + universally injective + locally of finite type + formally unramified. The retained proof is written out in two moves: the equivalence of the last four conditions follows from the chapter's lemma that universal injectivity equals monomorphism-ness for unramified maps, and then both directions reduce to representability of f (from the closed-immersion side and from the universally-closed-plus-unramified side), after which the schemes case cited from Etale Morphisms finishes. items.title: The relative dualizing complex of a proper flat finite presentation morphism is relatively perfect, has no positive cohomology after pushforward, and is self dual
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated Y and a proper flat finite presentation f : X -> Y with relative dualizing complex omega, the lemma asserts three properties: omega is Y-perfect, Rf_*omega has no cohomology in positive degrees, and O_X -> RSheafHom(omega, omega) is an isomorphism (statement lines 3027-3043). Because the formation of omega commutes with base change by Remark labelled remark-relative-dualizing-complex, the proof may assume Y affine (proof lines 3045-3049). For (1) it computes, for a perfect E, that Rf_*(E otimes^L omega) equals (Rf_*E^vee)^vee by three steps, using Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex, Lemma labelled lemma-iso-on-RSheafHom with Remark labelled remark-iso-on-RSheafHom and Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general, and the definition of the dual, concluding Y-perfectness by More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-characterize-relatively-perfect (proof lines 3051-3070). For (2) it rewrites Hom_Y(M, Rf_*omega) as Hom_Y(M otimes^L Rf_*O_X, O_Y) using adjunction, the construction of a, and Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-cohomology-base-change; since Rf_*O_X is perfect of tor amplitude in [0, N] by Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general and Y is affine, it is represented by a complex of finite projective modules in degrees [0, N] by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-perfect, so taking M = O_Y[-i] with i > 0 gives zero and hence the vanishing (proof lines 3072-3092). For (3) the proof writes a seven term chain of equalities for Hom_X(E, RSheafHom(omega, omega)) ending at Hom_X(E, O_X), using Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-internal-hom, the construction of omega, dualisation for perfect complexes by Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex, the identity from the first paragraph, double duality, and Leray (proof lines 3094-3122). To conclude, the proof notes that RSheafHom(omega, omega) lies in D_QCoh by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, takes E = O_X to get the map alpha corresponding to the identity, and uses that the cone of alpha has vanishing Hom from every perfect object together with the generation statement of Derived Categories of Schemes, Theorem labelled perfect-theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh to conclude that alpha is an isomorphism via the Yoneda lemma (proof lines 3124-3156). Computing the pushforward in terms of the dual of Rf_*E, and converting a functorial family of isomorphisms into an isomorphism by generation, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a finite type flat morphism with geometrically integral fibres is universally pure (statement lines 5123-5128, tag 05MC-adjacent). The proof takes a specialization in the base and a point of the source over its endpoint, uses integrality of the fibres to identify that point as the generic point of its fibre, and lifts the specialization along the flat morphism to end at the generic point of the special fibre, so that no impurity arises; since the hypotheses are preserved by base change, universal purity follows. The lifting step is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Injectivity of a map of finite type modules over a local base, tested on the associated points of the fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: stacks-project:flat.tex:local-snapshot-20261011
items.source_version: Stacks Project local source snapshot captured 2026-10-11; upstream commit not recorded
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that over a local base, for a flat finite type module pure along the special fibre, injectivity of a map of quasi-coherent modules is equivalent to injectivity of its stalk map at the associated points of the special fibre (statement lines 5546-5560, tag 05MC-adjacent). The proof replaces injectivity by the vanishing of the weakly associated points of the kernel, uses that those sit inside the relative associated points of the flat module, and that purity makes each relative associated point a specialization of a fibre point where injectivity is known. The reduction through weakly associated points is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma on the small pushforward i_{small,*} along a closed immersion i : Z -> X of algebraic spaces over S: on sheaves of sets it is fully faithful with essential image the sheaves restricting to the point sheaf off Z, on abelian sheaves it is fully faithful with essential image the sheaves supported on |Z|, and in both cases i_{small}^{-1} is a left inverse (source lines 2551-2578). items.title: Nine equivalent formulations of local finite typeness for morphisms of algebraic spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma collecting nine equivalent conditions for a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S to be locally of finite type (source lines 4614-4653): the intrinsic condition, the pointwise condition, base change to arbitrary and to affine schemes, existence of an etale cover of the base or of the source, the conditions on commutative diagrams of schemes over X and Y, and a Zariski local condition on Y. The proof is a two-step reduction: conditions (2), (3), (4), (5), (6), (7) and (9) are each shown to imply the diagram condition (8) by building a suitable cover and invoking permanence under composition, conditions (1), (7) and (8) are equivalent by definition, and (1) is then shown to imply all the remaining ones by base change stability and by taking U = X.

items.title: A flat quasi-compact surjective morphism of algebraic spaces is universally submersive
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a flat, quasi-compact and surjective morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, a subset T of |Y| is open (resp. closed) if and only if its preimage in |X| is, i.e. f is universally submersive (source lines 6122-6130). The proof builds a square of presentations: an affine etale cover V = coprod V_i -> Y, then for each i an affine etale cover U_i -> V_i x_Y X, so that U -> V is the disjoint union of the surjective flat quasi-compact morphisms U_i -> V_i of affine schemes. The topology on |Y| is by definition the quotient topology of |V|, and the criterion for f reduces to the scheme case for U -> V, which is the fpqc quotient topology lemma.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: a monomorphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S which is locally of finite type is separated and locally quasi-finite (source lines 5577-5583). Separatedness is formal from monomorphismhood; local quasi-finiteness is proved after a base change to an affine Y, where one chooses an affine etale U -> X, observes that U -> Y is of finite type and that the monomorphism hypothesis gives U x_X U = U x_Y U, so that the projections U x_Y U -> U are etale; the fibre of U -> Y over y is then a finite discrete set because it embeds into the fibre of the etale morphism U x_Y U -> U, and the criterion for quasi-finiteness in terms of fibres applies.

items.title: Pushforward of the structure sheaf along a universally closed morphism is integral over the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a quasi-compact, quasi-separated and universally closed morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, the sheaf f_*O_X is integral over O_Y, so that the normalization of Y in X is the factorization through the relative spectrum of f_*O_X (source lines 10144-10156). The proof is a genuine argument: after reducing to Y = Spec(R) it takes a section h, views it as a morphism to the affine line A^1_Y, forms the scheme theoretic image Z of h, shows h is quasi-compact, hence X -> Z has dense image and — because universal closedness is preserved by the factorization — is closed, so h(X) = Z set theoretically; a properness lemma then makes Z -> Y universally closed, and Z is affine over Y, hence integral, so the ideal of Z in R[T] contains a monic polynomial P with P(h) = 0.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a rational map phi from a reduced algebraic space X to a separated algebraic space Y over S, there is a unique morphism f : U -> Y on the domain of definition U representing phi (source lines 9811-9818). The proof compares two representatives (V, g) and (V', g'), which agree on a dense open W contained in V intersect V'; the equalizer E of the two restrictions is a closed subspace because it is the base change of the diagonal of Y, and since W is contained in E while W is dense, |E| equals |V intersect V'|; reducedness then upgrades this to E = V intersect V' scheme theoretically, so the representatives glue along the fppf surjection from the disjoint union of the V to U.

items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite type, the lemma asserts that the source is Noetherian if and only if the target is (statement lines 4654-4659). The proof first observes that a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space is adic*, so that by the corresponding statement for the adic* property one may assume both spaces are adic* (proof lines 4661-4665). It then invokes the criterion for Noetherianness of such a space, writes the target as a countable colimit as in the corresponding presentation lemma, base changes the morphism to each stage -- which is an affine scheme because the morphism is representable and affine -- and notes that the stages present the source as a colimit and that each induced morphism of stages is faithfully flat and of finite type (proof lines 4667-4677). The conclusion follows from the two algebra statements giving that Noetherianness ascends and descends along such a ring map (proof lines 4677-4679). The claim is H2: the argument reduces one type to another, then applies a criterion to convert the geometric statement into a statement about the stages, where the two directions are the two cited algebra statements.

items.title: A representable locally quasi-finite map from an affine formal algebraic space is representable by schemes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a map of presheaves on the fppf site whose source is an affine formal algebraic space and which is representable by algebraic spaces and locally quasi-finite is representable by schemes (statement lines 2380-2385). The proof tests against a morphism from a scheme: it has to show that the fibre product is a scheme, and it does so on quasi-compact open subspaces. Writing the source as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, the restriction of the projection to such a quasi-compact open subspace factors through one of the stages, and the resulting morphism into a product of that stage with the test scheme is a monomorphism, hence separated, and locally quasi-finite because the given map is; the criterion for a locally quasi-finite separated algebraic space over a scheme then makes each quasi-compact open subspace a scheme, and a criterion for being a scheme in terms of quasi-compact open subspaces finishes the argument (proof lines 2387-2409). The claim is H2: the reduction to quasi-compact open subspaces, the factorisation through a stage, and the two criteria applied at the end are all displayed, and the local quasi-finiteness hypothesis enters exactly once, in the middle step.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that projectivity, being a direct summand of a free module, and the vanishing of Ext one against every module are equivalent (statement lines 19011-19020). The proof does not quote the standard characterisations: it splits a surjection from a free module by the lifting property, uses that splitting to kill Ext one by a direct summand argument, and conversely exhibits the splitting of a presentation from the vanishing of Ext one (proof lines 19022-19060). Reading the vanishing of Ext one as the splitting of a presentation is the step that closes the cycle. H2.

items.title: Nilpotence of an element in a residue fibre is detected by the characteristic polynomial
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map whose target is finite free of rank n as a module, an element acts nilpotently on the fibre at a prime exactly when that prime contains the first n coefficients of the characteristic polynomial (statement lines 5771-5783). The proof does not use determinants of the action on generators: it compares the fibre characteristic polynomial with the reduction of the given one, applies Cayley-Hamilton on both sides, and reads the condition off the coefficients (proof lines 5785-5812). Reducing modulo the prime so that the two polynomials agree is the step that carries the argument. H2.

items.title: A halting configuration of a Turing machine entails the halting sentence
items.author: The Open Logic Project contributors

items.source_version: Open Logic Project git 1e960beff9ed (2026-08-14); unit content/turing-machines/undecidability; corpus local snapshot 20261013
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lem:halt-config-implies-halt at source lines 1648-1651: if the machine M run on input w is in a halting configuration after n steps, then the sentence C(M,w,n) describing that configuration entails the sentence E(M,w) which expresses that M has halted. The proof at source lines 1653-1673 has to pass between three different levels of description: the machine-level fact that a halting configuration exists, the first-order sentence C(M,w,n) which encodes a whole tape configuration by its clauses, and the existential disjunction E(M,w) over the pairs (q,sigma) for which delta(q,sigma) is undefined. The work is to pick the state q, the square m and the symbol sigma realised at time n, read off the two clauses Q_q(m,n) and S_sigma(m,n) inside C(M,w,n), and then show that these two clauses are one of the disjuncts of E(M,w) precisely because delta(q,sigma) is undefined. Nothing in the statement spells out that C(M,w,n) contains those two clauses or that the disjunction in E(M,w) is taken over exactly the undefined-transition pairs, so the reader has to supply that bookkeeping. No result outside the retained text is used.

items.title: The base change maps of two stacked cartesian squares compose to the base change map of the outer rectangle
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a commutative diagram of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes whose two squares are cartesian, with f and l as well as g and m Tor independent, the lemma asserts that the base change maps of equation labelled equation-base-change-map for the two squares compose to the base change map of the outer rectangle (statement lines 1237-1253). The proof first notes that g o f and m are then Tor independent, so the statement makes sense, marking that step 'details omitted', and sets a, b, c for the right adjoints of pushforward along f, g and g o f with primed versions for the base changes (proof lines 1255-1266). It writes the arrows gamma_{top}, gamma_{bot} and gamma_{rect} for the two squares and the rectangle as compositions using the canonical maps 1 -> l_* l^* and k^* k_* -> 1 together with the inverses of the base change isomorphisms xi_{top}, xi_{bot}, xi_{rect}, and notes that (g o f)_* = g_* o f_* gives c = a o b and c' = a' o b' (proof lines 1268-1296). The claim is then that gamma_{rect} equals gamma_{bot} o gamma_{top}, which is proved by contemplating a large diagram whose right hand side is the composition and whose left hand side is gamma_{rect}; the quadrilaterals commute by Categories, Lemma labelled categories-lemma-properties-2-cat-cats or the discussion before Categories, Definition labelled categories-definition-horizontal-composition, so it suffices to prove a reduced diagram commutes after inverting xi_{top}, xi_{bot} and xi_{rect} (proof lines 1298-1330). That reduced statement is obtained from a triangle commuting by the same categories lemma, together with two auxiliary quadrilaterals that commute by the cited references and the fact that the composition l_* -> l_* l^* l_* -> l_* is the identity, reducing everything to the identity k o a' o b' -> a o l_* o b -> a o b o m_* being xi_{rect}, which is the statement dual to Cohomology, Remark labelled cohomology-remark-compose-base-change (proof lines 1332-1372). Organising the diagram chase so that only the dual of the known composition of ordinary base change maps remains is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter divisors.tex (Divisors)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that on a regular scheme of dimension at most two, a coherent module is reflexive if and only if it is finite locally free (statement lines 2336-2345). The counted proof is a short case analysis by the dimension of the local ring at a point: a field in dimension zero, a discrete valuation ring in dimension one where reflexivity gives torsion freeness and torsion free finite modules are free, and a regular local ring of dimension two where reflexivity gives depth at least two and a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module over a regular local ring is free (proof lines 2347-2367). It is H2: the reduction and all three cases are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard facts about local rings of small dimension.

items.title: Equivalence of three local forms of local equidimensionality for the relative dimension function
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section preparing the key lemma
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence of three formulations of local equidimensionality for the relative dimension function, and shows that normal or Cohen-Macaulay schemes satisfy them (statement lines 8276-8297, tag 02RE-adjacent). The converse direction requires the observation that the set of points with a fixed value is open, and the two sufficient conditions come from the decomposition of a normal scheme into integral pieces and from the comparison of the relative dimension function with the dimension function given by local ring dimensions whose difference is locally constant. The openness argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with four assertions for a locally finite type morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces and its base change f' by g : Y' -> Y: the quasi-finite loci W and W' are open, W' is the preimage of W, and locally quasi-finite (resp. quasi-finite) morphisms are stable under base change (source lines 5323-5339).
