items.title: Quasi-compactness of a representable morphism of algebraic spaces tested after base change from quasi-compact spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a representable morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, quasi-compactness in the representable sense is equivalent to quasi-compactness of Z x_Y X for every quasi-compact algebraic space Z over Y (source lines 1212-1223). The first direction chooses a quasi-compact scheme U with a surjective etale U -> Z, observes that U x_Y X is a quasi-compact scheme by the representable sense of quasi-compactness, and concludes that Z x_Y X is quasi-compact because it receives a surjective etale morphism from U x_Y X. The second direction checks the definition of quasi-compactness of p : Z x_Y X -> Z on affine opens U of a scheme Z, where the preimage is U x_Y X and is quasi-compact by hypothesis.

items.title: The scheme theoretic image of a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with four assertions for the scheme theoretic image Z of a quasi-compact morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces: the kernel ideal I of O_Y -> f_*O_X is quasi-coherent, Z is the closed subspace it defines, the formation of Z commutes with etale base change, and |f|(|X|) is dense in |Z| (source lines 3249-3265). Part (4) then follows from the ideal being the unit ideal away from the closure of the image.

items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism f : X -> Y and an invertible sheaf L whose restriction to the fibre over y is ample, the lemma finds an open neighbourhood V of y such that L restricted to f^{-1}(V) is ample relative to V. The retained proof: reduce to Y affine; present X -> Y as the limit of a directed system of proper morphisms X_i -> Y_i with Y_i of finite type over Z and affine transition maps (Limits, lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian); descend L to a compatible system of line bundles L_i (Limits, lemma-descend-invertible-modules); use the colimit of residue fields to find a stage where the fibre bundle is ample (Limits, lemma-limit-ample); apply the finite-type case (Cohomology of Schemes, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood) to get V_i; pull back V_i along Y -> Y_i, closing with base change of ample bundles, affineness of X -> Y x_{Y_i} X_i, and ampleness under affine pullback (Morphisms, lemmas ample-base-change and pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample). The statement carries a reference environment citing EGA IV Corollary 9.6.4. Retained author proof at lines 14165-14194.

items.title: Blowing up a finite type ideal near a curve point where the restriction is ample
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings

items.title: Ind-quasi-affine morphisms compose
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states the class of ind-quasi-affine morphisms of schemes is stable under composition. The retained proof is written from the chapter's alternative-definition dictionary (collected this wave as L16109): given f : X -> Y and g : Y -> Z ind-quasi-affine, take a qcqs open V in Z and a quasi-compact open U of the total inverse image; the image f(U) is quasi-compact inside g^{-1}(V) so it sits in a quasi-compact open W (a union of finitely many affines); W -> V is quasi-affine by the dictionary, making W quasi-separated; applying the dictionary again to U inside the inverse image over W gives U -> W quasi-affine; the composition of quasi-affine morphisms (Morphisms, lemma composition-quasi-affine) yields U -> V quasi-affine; the dictionary's criterion closes the proof. Retained author proof at lines 19589-19603.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The property for a morphism of being ind-quasi-affine satisfies fpqc descent on the base. The retained proof is complete: base-change stability (lemma-base-change-ind-quasi-affine) gives one direction; for the descent direction one works Zariski locally on an affine base via the alternative characterization (lemma-ind-quasi-affine-alternative-definition), refines the fpqc covering to a single affine faithfully flat map g : Y' -> Y, and checks for every quasi-compact open U of X that U -> Y is quasi-affine exactly when U x_Y Y' -> Y' is, by the Descent chapter theorem that quasi-affineness is a descending fpqc property (Descent, lemma-descending-property-quasi-affine); quasi-compactness of base changes of quasi-compact opens is noted. Retained author proof at lines 19659-19678.

items.title: Avramov-type regularity: a perfect map into a target over a local complete intersection base forces both maps to be complete intersections
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Given a commutative diagram of schemes over a locally Noetherian base S, with Y -> S locally of finite type, f : X -> Y perfect, and X -> S a local complete intersection morphism, the lemma concludes X -> Y is a local complete intersection morphism and Y -> S is Koszul at every image point of X. The retained proof works entirely in the Noetherian world where regular and Koszul-regular sequences agree; after affine localization it chooses nested closed immersions into affine spaces over S, reads off the kernels J of O_{A^{n+m}_S, x} -> O_{X,x} and I of O_{A^n_S, f(x)} -> O_{Y,f(x)}, notes J is generated by a regular sequence (X -> S is lci) and O_{X,x} has finite tor dimension over O_{Y,f(x)} (f perfect), and applies the divided powers algebra lemma that a perfect map whose ambient ideal is generated by a regular sequence forces both I and J/I to be generated by regular sequences (Divided Power Algebra, lemma-perfect-map-ci). Retained author proof at lines 18376-18418.

items.title: Locally of finite type morphisms are etale-locally finite over smooth maps with geometrically integral fibres
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The local-local structure theorem: for f : X -> S locally of finite type and x over s with n equal to the local fibre dimension dim_x(X_s), there is a diagram with an elementary etale neighbourhood g : (X', x') -> (X, x), a second elementary etale neighbourhood e : (S', s') -> (S, s), a smooth map h : Y' -> S' of relative dimension n with geometrically integral fibres, and a finite map pi : X' -> Y' sending x' to y' with pi^{-1}(y') = {x'} and kappa(y') purely transcendental over kappa(s'); for finite presentation f the map pi can be taken of finite presentation. The retained proof reduces to S affine, applies the chapter's local structure lemma to obtain a smooth Y -> S with purely transcendental residue extension at y, uses etale-locality on X, builds an elementary etale neighbourhood whose pullback open Y' has geometrically irreducible fibres identifying the fibre with a prescribed affine space piece, selects the canonical points (x', s') and (y, s') above the originals, and verifies the outer rectangle satisfies all six listed properties; the author marks some minor details omitted inside this fully written construction. Retained author proof at lines 13462-13520.

items.title: Normalized base change of a flat finite type scheme over a Nagata Dedekind ring becomes smooth over the generic points of all fibres after a finite extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Let A be a Nagata Dedekind ring with fraction field K and X flat of finite type over A with B the integral closure of A in the function field algebra; the theorem produces a finite extension L/K such that the normalized base change Y -> Spec(B) is smooth at all generic points of all fibres. The retained proof is a long structured argument: it repeatedly uses that the smooth locus of a flat finitely presented map commutes with base change; it first picks L/K making (X_L)_red geometrically reduced (Varieties, finite-extension-geometrically-reduced), propagates geometric reducedness to Y_L through birationality and generic-point lemmas, obtains a dense smooth open of Y_L -> Spec(L), and reduces to the case where the smooth locus in the generic fibre is dense; the closing paragraph treats a closed point with maximal ideal m of B: a point y outside the good locus maps to one of the finitely many bad points x_i, O_{Y,y} is a local ring of the integral closure of the corresponding A_i in R(X) tensor L, the chosen extension L/K is a solution for A_i -> O_i so B_m -> O_{Y,y} is formally smooth in the adic topology (extension-of-DVRs criterion), whence the fibre local ring is a field with separable residue extension and the fibre is smooth at y. Retained author proof at lines 19291-19355.

primary.label: theorem-normalized-base-change-with-reduced-fibre

proof_spans.label: complete author proof of theorem-normalized-base-change-with-reduced-fibre

items.title: A geometrically irreducible open of a normal fibre thickens to geometrically integral fibres after an elementary etale base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For h : Y -> S of finite presentation and normal, and T an open subscheme of the fibre Y_s geometrically irreducible over kappa(s), the lemma finds an affine elementary etale neighbourhood (S', s') -> (S, s) and a quasi-compact open V of Y_{S'} whose fibres are all geometrically integral and with V_{s'} = T x_s s'. The retained proof is written: apply the chapter's fibre-geometrically-connected-reduced lemma to obtain the neighbourhood and V with geometrically connected fibres and the prescribed special fibre; all fibres of V -> S' are geometrically normal because normality of the map is stable under base change and open restriction (chapter lemma normal); geometrically normal plus Noetherian implies geometrically reduced, so irreducibility is the only remaining check; for t in S', the geometric fibre V_t x kappa(t)-bar is Noetherian, connected by the construction of S', and a connected Noetherian normal scheme is irreducible (Properties, lemma normal-Noetherian), which finishes. Retained author proof at lines 13345-13362.

items.title: Universally parametrizing the open-and-closed subschemes of a quasi-finite map that are finite over the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-finite finitely presented morphism X -> Y of affine schemes, the lemma constructs a finite presentation morphism Y_univ -> Y and an open U_univ of Y_univ x_Y X which is finite over Y_univ, universally representing the functor that assigns to Y' -> Y the open subschemes U' of Y' x_Y X finite over Y': every such U' is the inverse image of U_univ for a unique-on-pixels Y' -> Y_univ. The retained proof is written: quasi-finite = relative dimension 0 (cited Morphisms lemma), Noetherian approximation reduces to X, Y Noetherian (chapter lemma Noetherian-approximation-dimension-d with d = 0); a quasi-finite scheme over Y embeds as an open of a Y-finite scheme X' (Algebra, lemma quasi-finite-open-integral-closure); an open of Y' x_Y X inside the finite Y'-scheme Y' x_Y X' is automatically also closed, so it corresponds to an idempotent of the base-changed algebra Gamma(Y',O) tensor Gamma(X',O); the finite case (chapter lemma open-and-closed-in-finite, previously collected) produces the universal pair (Y'_univ, e'_univ); the locus where U'_univ escapes Y'_univ x_Y X has closed image T, and removing T gives Y_univ with the required property. Retained author proof at lines 22847-22888.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a commutative diagram X -> Y -> S of schemes with Y -> S smooth and X -> S perfect, the lemma concludes f : X -> Y is perfect. The retained proof is written as the standard graph-factorization: f factors as X -> X x_S Y -> Y where the first map is the graph i = (1, f) and the second the projection; the projection is perfect because it is the base change of the perfect map X -> S along the flat (smooth) map Y -> S (chapter lemma flat-base-change-perfect plus Morphisms, lemma smooth-flat); the graph i is a section of the smooth projection X x_S Y -> X (base-change of Y -> S, Morphisms, lemma base-change-smooth), hence a regular immersion (Divisors, lemma section-smooth-regular-immersion), hence perfect (chapter lemma regular-immersion-perfect, queued next); composition of perfect morphisms (chapter lemma composition-perfect) closes. Retained author proof at lines 17846-17866.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For S with an ample invertible sheaf and f : X -> S, the lemma lists eight equivalent conditions: projective, H-projective, quasi-projective plus proper, H-quasi-projective plus proper, proper with X carrying an ample line bundle, proper with an f-ample line bundle, proper with an f-very ample line bundle, and presentation as relative Proj of a quasi-coherent graded O_S-algebra generated in degree one by a finite type module. The retained proof is fully written: it first notes all conditions imply properness so the argument lives in the proper world, chains the Morphisms-chapter equivalences (projective-is-quasi-projective-proper, H-projective, projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), notes (1) implies (7) immediately from the definitions and (3)-(6) equivalence from the definition of quasi-projective, imports the just-collected quasi-projective five-way equivalence (lemma-quasi-projective, card L16072) to fuse (3), (5), (7), and constructs (8) from (2) by writing P^n_S as relative Proj of a polynomial algebra (Constructions, lemma-projective-space-bundle), realizing X as relative Proj of a graded quotient algebra via Divisors, lemma-closed-subscheme-proj, and checking the generation hypotheses; the converse is Divisors, lemma-relative-proj-projective. Retained author proof at lines 14047-14100.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a local map of local rings A -> B, essentially of finite type with A Noetherian and the residue field extension finite, any open V of Spec B containing a prime not lying over the closed point of A contains a prime q, not meeting the closed point of A, such that A -> B/q is a localization of a quasi-finite ring map. The retained proof is written: B is Noetherian; the punctured spectrum of B is Jacobson (Properties, lemma-complement-closed-point-Jacobson) so a closed point q can be chosen inside the nonempty open cut out from V by removing primes over m_A; the two-point spectrum of B/q plus the isolated-point criterion (Algebra, lemma-isolated-point-fibre) show finite type A-algebra C presenting B/q is quasi-finite at the corresponding prime, and Zariski's open locus for quasi-finiteness (Algebra, lemma-quasi-finite-open) finishes after a principal localization. Retained author proof at lines 14969-14991.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> S locally of finite type, an fppf covering {S_i -> S} with base changes f_i and projections g_i, and E in D_QCoh(O_X), the lemma asserts E is m-pseudo-coherent relative to S if and only if each Lg_i^* E is m-pseudo-coherent relative to S_i. The retained proof is written as a two-line formal combination of the chapter's two preceding lemmas: the fppf descent lemma (relative-pseudo-coherent-descends-fppf, which says relative m-pseudo-coherence over S descends/ascends along the fppf cover) and the post-composition lemma (relative-pseudo-coherent-post-compose, comparing relative pseudo-coherence over S and over S_i for the projections). Every named input is a chapter reference, and the author spells out both directions. Retained author proof at lines 20710-20721.

items.title: Any S-morphism between schemes weakly etale over S is itself weakly etale
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme S and morphism f : X -> Y over S with X and Y both weakly etale over S, the lemma concludes f is weakly etale. The retained proof is written: writing f as X -> X x_S Y -> Y, the second map is flat as a base change of the flat map X -> S; the first map is the base change of the flat diagonal Y -> Y x_S Y along X x_S Y -> Y x_S Y, hence flat; so f is flat. For the diagonal of f, the map X x_Y X -> X x_S X is an immersion, and the chapter's key lemma (lemma-key, flatness reflected from a closed subscheme along an immersion onto the diagonal) turns flatness of X over X x_S X into flatness of X over X x_Y X. Both halves of the definition of weakly etale then hold. Retained author proof at lines 19170-19182.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the scheme-theoretic generalization (the author flags it as such, subsumption of the field-theoretic fact that a separable purely inseparable extension is trivial) stating that a morphism which is both weakly etale and a universal homeomorphism is an isomorphism. The retained proof is written: the diagonal of a universal homeomorphism is a surjective closed immersion (cited Morphisms lemmas homeomorphism-affine and universally-injective), a closed immersion that is also flat is an isomorphism (cited Morphisms lemma characterize-flat-closed-immersions), so the diagonal is an isomorphism, i.e. f is a monomorphism (Schemes, lemma monomorphism); f is quasi-compact as a universal homeomorphism, and a flat surjective quasi-compact monomorphism is an isomorphism by the cited Descent lemma. Every step names its input. Retained author proof at lines 19195-19208.

items.title: Every qcqs algebraic space admits a finite filtration by closed subspaces whose strata become resolution spaces after admissible blowing ups
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space X over a scheme S there is an integer t and closed subspaces X = Z_0 containing Z_1 containing ... containing Z_t empty, each of finite presentation over X, with Z_0 -> X a thickening, such that each stratum Z_i minus Z_{i-1} admits an admissible blowing up Z'_i -> Z_i whose source has the resolution property. The retained proof first uses absolute Noetherian approximation (viewing X over Spec(Z), Limits of Spaces proposition-approximate) to descend to a space X_0 of finite presentation over the integers, noting the stratification and blowing-up centres pull back and that the resolution property goes up along affine morphisms (Derived Categories of Spaces, lemma-resolution-property-goes-up-affine; strict transforms of affine morphisms are affine, details omitted there), then argues by induction on the dimension of |X|: the chapter's lemma-blow-up-resolution-property gives a dense open U and a U-admissible blowup gaining the resolution property, and the induction hypothesis on the reduced closed complement finishes the filtration; the reduction from the non-reduced Z_0 to the reduced case is handled explicitly. Retained author proof at lines 13894-13933.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S and a point y of |Y|, the lemma identifies two numbers: the minimal d such that f has relative dimension <= d at every point over y (with d = -infinity off the image), and the dimension of the fibre X_k for any field-valued point in the class y. The retained proof is a fully written chart descent: choose an affine etale V -> Y with v over y, extract from the surjective etale map V x_Y Spec(k) -> Spec(k) a finite separable extension k'/k and the cartesian diagram of spectra (cited Properties of Spaces lemma points-cartesian and Morphisms lemma etale-over-field), replace X -> Y by the V-base change and X_k by X_{k'} justifying invariance of both numbers through the two cited dimension lemmas (dimension-decent-invariant-under-etale, dimension-fibre-after-base-change), reduce to k = kappa(y), then take a surjective etale affine scheme U -> X and conclude dim(X_k) = dim(U_k) = max dim_u(U_k) equals the relative-dimension bound by definition. Retained author proof at lines 7137-7180.

items.difficulty_reason: The flattening theorem for algebraic spaces: with B qcqs over a scheme S, X quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation over B, F a finite type quasi-coherent module on X whose restriction to the quasi-compact open U is of finite presentation and flat over U, there exists a U-admissible blowup B' -> B such that the strict transform F' is of finite presentation and flat over B'. The retained proof runs: etale-locally on X (strict transforms commute with etale localization, Divisors on Spaces) reduce to representable X -> B; etale-locally on B choose an affine W -> B, apply the schemes flattening theorem (More on Flatness, theorem-flatten-module) to get a finite type ideal on W whose blowup makes the strict transform flat and finitely presented; push the ideal down to B (lemma-push-ideal), form the corresponding blowup B' -> W' and control the double strict transform through the blowup-of-two-ideals and composition lemmas (Divisors on Spaces, blowing-up-two-ideals, strict-transform-composition-blowups, strict-transform-flat), concluding flatness and finite presentation of F' after descent along the etale cover. Retained author proof at lines 8796-8846.

items.difficulty_reason: For a representable proper map f : X -> Y of Noetherian algebraic spaces, quasi-coherent ideals J on Y and K controlling the open locus where f is an isomorphism, an inverse system (G_n) in Coh(Y, J), a coherent F on X and an isomorphism beta from the completed pullback of (G_n) to the I-adic completion of F in Coh(X, I), the lemma produces a map alpha : (G_n) -> (f_*F)^ in Coh(Y, J) whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of K. items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own theorem at source lines 1170-1173: the set of infinite binary sequences is not enumerable. The proof at source lines 1175-1222 is Cantor's diagonal argument carried out in full, and it is not a one-step application of a previously stated theorem in the unit. It has to set up the double indexing of an arbitrary enumeration as an infinite array of digits, define the diagonal string by flipping the diagonal entries, and then show by a genuine case analysis that the resulting string agrees with no row of the array: for a fixed row n the two strings differ at coordinate n, and the definition of d(n) makes that difference explicit in each of the two cases. The proof also has to be careful about the direction of the enumeration hypothesis, since it argues against an enumeration of a subset of the binary sequences rather than of the whole set. No result outside the retained text is used.

The proof at source lines 695-703 does not follow from the definition of a cardinal by a single unfolding. It first has to be seen that the union of X is an ordinal, which is left to the reader as an easy check because unions of ordinals are ordinals, and the real content is the second half: given an ordinal alpha in the union of X, one must find a cardinal b in X with alpha in b, use that b is a cardinal to conclude alpha is strictly smaller than b as a cardinal, then use b subseteq union X to obtain that b is at most union X, and chain the two strict/smaller comparisons to conclude alpha is not equinumerous with union X. The proof uses three distinct closure facts (union of ordinals, subset of a union, transitivity of the cardinal comparison) and the generalisation step at the end is what converts the pointwise statement into the cardinality assertion. items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own corollary cor:undecidable-sat at source lines 1537-1539: it is undecidable whether an arbitrary sentence of first-order logic is satisfiable. The proof at source lines 1541-1556 is a reduction that has to be assembled step by step. It assumes a Turing machine S deciding satisfiability and then describes a machine that would decide validity: copy the input sentence, write a negation symbol in front of it, run S on the negated sentence, and translate the answer back, using that a sentence is valid exactly when its negation is unsatisfiable. The description is given at the level of tape operations (moving the sentence one square, returning to square 1, writing the negation, inspecting square 1 for a stroke, erasing or writing one), so the reader has to accept that these are computable operations and that the resulting machine halts on every input. The contradiction is then with the already established unsolvability of the decision problem for validity. Nothing in the statement names the reduction or the two closure facts it uses. No result outside the retained text is used.

items.title: There is a universal Turing machine
items.author: The Open Logic Project contributors
items.work: Open Logic Project — Turing Machines: Undecidability
items.source_version: Open Logic Project git 1e960beff9ed (2026-08-14); unit content/turing-machines/undecidability; corpus local snapshot 20261013
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own theorem thm:universal-tm at source lines 1434-1443: there is a Turing machine U which on input (e,n) halts exactly when the machine with index e halts on n, and reproduces its output. The proof at source lines 1445-1512 is an outline construction rather than a machine written step by step, and that is how the author presents it (the source explicitly says that producing U is basically impossible and that the outline plus the Church-Turing thesis is what is offered). Its content is a simulation architecture: decode the index e to the right of the input into a list of unary blocks describing the instructions of M_e, write the start state and the number 1 next to that description, copy the input with each stroke replaced by a block of three strokes so that the simulated tape uses a three-symbol alphabet, and then repeat a cycle of steps that reads the simulated tape, finds the matching instruction, rewrites the simulated symbol, updates the recorded state, and moves the recorded head position. Each of those stages is a genuinely different block of machinery, and the last one has to handle the case in which the simulated machine halts, by converting the simulated tape back into a block of strokes. Because the argument is an outline completed by the Church-Turing thesis rather than an explicit machine, it is marked for human spot-check. No result outside the retained text is used beyond the thesis the author invokes.

items.title: Pullback of a principal divisor along an etale morphism is the sum over the irreducible components of the pushforwards of the restricted divisors
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-chow.tex (Chow Groups of Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-chow.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the pullback formula for principal divisors along an etale morphism at source lines 1679-1690, label lemma-etale-pullback-principal-divisor, whose proof occupies source lines 1692-1803. The proof has two independent halves: a cycle-theoretic reduction that the two sides have the same dimension and that equality can be checked coefficient by coefficient at generic points, using the scheme theoretic image and the commutativity of henselization with the morphism, and a local computation of the coefficient as a difference of lengths over the total rings of fractions of henselized reduced local Noetherian rings, which are not assumed to be domains. The local half then needs the flat unramified ring map to equate lengths over base and total space, an additivity statement for lengths over the quotients by the nonmaximal primes, and the observation that the index set splits as the disjoint union over the components. The counted statement records neither the coefficient comparison nor the length identity.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the compatibility of proper pushforward with rational equivalence at source lines 2175-2181, label lemma-proper-pushforward-rational-equivalence, whose proof occupies source lines 2183-2269. The proof reduces a locally finite sum of divisors on integral subspaces to a single summand and then splits into three cases according to the dimension of the image. The dimension-preserving case is disposed of by an alteration lemma, but the case where the image has dimension exactly k requires real work: the pushforward is first seen to be an integer multiple of the image class, then the image is shrunk to a scheme, the generic point is pulled back to a one-dimensional proper cover, that cover is proved to be a scheme through the codimension one criterion for the schematic locus and a limit argument, and only then does the scheme case give vanishing. The counted statement records none of the case distinction.

items.title: A finite free extension in which a monic polynomial acquires a root
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma adjoins a root of a monic polynomial by a finite free ring extension, and the proof is a 7-line construction that writes the extension down explicitly. It forms the quotient of a polynomial ring by the polynomial itself, so that the class of the variable is a root, observes that the quotient is finite free over the base because the polynomial is monic, and then quotes the statement that a monic polynomial over a ring is divisible by the linear factor corresponding to any of its roots to obtain the announced factorisation. items.title: For a perfect morphism the shriek of the structure sheaf is bounded coherent, of finite tor dimension, self dual, preserves bounded coherent objects and makes the comparison map an isomorphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-shriek, for a perfect morphism f : X -> Y of FTS_S the lemma asserts five things: f^!O_Y lies in D^b_Coh(O_X), has finite tor dimension over f^{-1}O_Y, makes O_X -> RSheafHom(f^!O_Y, f^!O_Y) an isomorphism, and that f^! maps D^b_Coh(O_Y) into D^b_Coh(O_X) and turns the comparison map mu_{f,K} of Lemma labelled lemma-map-pullback-to-shriek-well-defined into an isomorphism for all K in D_QCoh^+(O_Y) (statement lines 4797-4818). The proof notes that a flat finite presentation morphism is perfect of More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-flat-finite-presentation-perfect, then disposes of (a), (b) and (c) by reducing to affine X and Y, where Remark labelled remark-local-calculation-shriek translates them into assertions (1)(a), (1)(b) and (1)(c) of Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic, matched through Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemmas labelled perfect-lemma-tor-dimension-rel-affine, perfect-lemma-pseudo-coherent, perfect-lemma-identify-pseudo-coherent-noetherian and perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom (proof lines 4820-4834). For (d) and (e) the proof first collects six preliminary remarks: that f^! sends D^+_Coh into D^+_Coh by Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-coherent; the open immersion case where f^! = f^* by Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-open-immersion; the perfect proper case settled by Lemma labelled lemma-compare-with-pullback-flat-proper-noetherian; locality in X for both (d) and (e); closure of (e) under composition using the diagram of Lemma labelled lemma-map-pullback-to-shriek-well-defined; and the deduction of (d) from (e) for a composite (proof lines 4836-4872). These reduce the problem to affine X, where an immersion X -> A^n_Y is factored as a perfect closed immersion followed by an open immersion into A^n_Y -> Y using Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-quasi-affine-finite-type-over-S and More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-perfect-permanence, so it suffices to treat a perfect closed immersion and the projection A^n_Y -> Y (proof lines 4874-4880). For a perfect closed immersion one has f^!K = RSheafHom(O_X, K) by Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-closed-immersion and f_*f^!K = RSheafHom_{O_Y}(f_*O_X, K) with f_*O_X perfect, which gives boundedness above and hence (d), with one step marked 'Some details omitted' (proof lines 4882-4896); for the projection, (d) follows by repeated application of Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-affine-line, and (e) holds because it holds for the flat proper P^n_Y -> Y and A^n_Y is open in P^n_Y (proof lines 4898-4902). Reducing the general case to a factorization into a perfect closed immersion and a projection, and collecting the six closure remarks, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: For a Koszul regular ideal the Ext algebra of the quotient is the exterior algebra on its first Ext sheaf
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a ringed space Y with a sheaf of ideals I, quotient O_X = O_Y/I, the lemma asserts that if I is Koszul regular in the sense of Divisors, Definition labelled divisors-definition-regular-ideal-sheaf, then composition on RSheafHom_{O_Y}(O_X, O_X) induces isomorphisms wedge^i(SheafExt^1(O_X, O_X)) -> SheafExt^i(O_X, O_X) for all i (statement lines 3660-3674). The proof first recalls that composition is the map of Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-internal-hom-composition, which induces multiplication maps SheafExt^a otimes SheafExt^b -> SheafExt^{a+b} to be compared with More on Algebra, Equation labelled more-algebra-equation-simple-tor-product, so the assertion is that the multiplication map from the i-fold tensor power of SheafExt^1 factors through the wedge product and then is an isomorphism (proof lines 3676-3696). Working locally, one takes global sections f_1, ..., f_r generating I and forming a Koszul regular sequence, forms the strictly commutative differential graded algebra A = O_Y<xi_1, ..., xi_r> which is a divided power polynomial algebra on generators in degree -1 with d xi_i = f_i, and notes that the canonical map A^bullet -> O_X is a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 3698-3712). Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect then gives quasi-isomorphisms RSheafHom(O_X, O_X) -> SheafHom^bullet(A^bullet, A^bullet) -> SheafHom^bullet(A^bullet, O_X) whose differentials vanish, so SheafExt^i is SheafHom_{O_Y}(A^{-i}, O_X) (proof lines 3714-3726). For each j the derivation delta_j of degree 1 with delta_j(xi_i) = the Kronecker delta satisfies delta_j o d = -d o delta_j, hence defines a section of the corresponding Ext sheaf; the proof states that a computation shows delta_1, ..., delta_r map to a basis of SheafHom(A^{-1}, O_X) over O_X, and since delta_j o delta_j = 0 and delta_j o delta_{j'} = -delta_{j'} o delta_j the map factors through the exterior power, while the elements delta_{j_1} o ... o delta_{j_i} for increasing indices are checked to map to a basis of SheafHom(A^{-i}, O_X) over O_X, which gives the isomorphism (proof lines 3728-3758). Recognising the Ext algebra of a Koszul regular quotient as the derived Hom of the Koszul dga and reading the exterior algebra structure off the derivations is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Completely decomposed morphisms and coverings are stable under base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states both that the base change of a completely decomposed morphism of schemes is completely decomposed and that a completely decomposed family {X_i -> Y} remains so after any base change Y' -> Y. The retained proof is written: fix a point y' of Y' over y and a point x of X over y with kappa(x) = kappa(y); the fibre-product point dictionary (Schemes, lemma points-fibre-product) supplies a unique point x' of X' = X x_Y Y' over (y', x) with residue field kappa(x') = kappa(y'), obtained by the tensor product of fields computation kappa(x) tensor_{kappa(y)} kappa(y') = kappa(y') tensor kappa(y') whose unique prime is the diagonal; the stated uniqueness is exactly what turns the completely-decomposed condition at y into the one at y', and the family version is the identical argument applied to each member (the author's we omit the details covers only this mechanical reindexing). Retained author proof at lines 23175-23184.

items.title: Weakly etale morphisms are stable under base change, via flatness of the base-changed diagonal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a cartesian square with X' = Y' x_Y X, the lemma proves (1) flatness of the diagonal X' -> X' x_{Y'} X' follows from flatness of X -> X x_Y X, and (2) base changes of weakly etale morphisms are weakly etale. The retained proof is written: the diagonal of X' over Y' is the base change of the diagonal of X over Y along the map Y' x_Y Y' -> Y x_Y Y' restricted to the fibre square (the author's one-line identification X' x_{Y'} X' = Y' x_{(Y x_Y Y)} (X x_Y X)), and flatness is preserved under base change (cited Morphisms lemma base-change-flat); part (2) adds the unramified half — also base-change stable — and reads off the definition. Retained author proof at lines 19012-19018.

items.title: The two geometric fibre-count functions of a locally quasi-finite map agree and are bounded on quasi-compact sources
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a locally quasi-finite morphism f : X -> Y the lemma states (1) the number-of-geometrically-irreducible-components function n_{X/Y} of the two preceding chapter lemmas agrees with the number-of-geometrically-connected-components function (both denoted n_{X/Y}), and (2) if X is quasi-compact then n_{X/Y} attains a finite maximum. The retained proof is written: on geometric fibres of a locally quasi-finite map the fibres are discrete topological spaces (Morphisms, lemma locally-quasi-finite-fibres), where irreducible components and connected components coincide pointwise, giving the agreement; boundedness comes from the chapter's universally-bounded dictionary (Morphisms, lemmas characterize-universally-bounded and locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded): a quasi-compact source forces uniformly bounded geometric fibres, i.e. a finite maximum of the count function. Retained author proof at lines 21971-21978.

items.title: Every fppf covering is refined by a two-stage Zariski-then-finite-locally-free tower
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For an fppf covering {S_i -> S}, the lemma builds a Zariski open covering S = union U_j, surjective finite locally free W_j -> U_j, Zariski open coverings W_j = union W_{j,k}, and surjective finite locally free T_{j,k} -> W_{j,k} such that {T_{j,k} -> S} refines {S_i -> S} — the purely Zariski-local-on-the-base domination (in contrast to the etale-local L16107 and the qcqs-global finite L16118, both collected). The retained proof is written: start from the etale-local covering {V_a -> S'_a -> S} of chapter lemma dominate-fppf-etale-locally (card L16107); then the standard approximation remark (remark-topologies: a finite locally free surjection can be built Zariski-locally on the base dominating a given etale covering) supplies W_{j,k} mapping into individual S'_a; base change T_{j,k} = W_{j,k} x_{S'_a} V_a is finite locally free over W_{j,k} and lands inside S_i by construction — the author's everything is clear unpacks to this single fibre-product identity.

items.title: For perfect maps between locally Noetherian schemes, being lci is the tor-amplitude [-1,0] condition on the cotangent complex
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a perfect morphism f : X -> Y of locally Noetherian schemes the lemma gives the three-way equivalence: f is a local complete intersection morphism; NL_{X/Y} has tor-amplitude in [-1, 0]; NL_{X/Y} is perfect with tor-amplitude in [-1, 0]. The retained proof is written as the affines-to-schemes translation protocol: the chapter's lci-affine dictionary (lemma affine-lci) identifies lci-ness with the finite tor dimension condition on the naive cotangent complex of a polynomial presentation; the identification NL_{X/Y} with that naive complex on affines (chapter lemma NL-affine); the Derived Categories of Schemes comparison trio (affine-compare-bounded, tor-dimension-affine, perfect-affine) turns the module-theoretic amplitude statements into the scheme-global ones; and the resulting ring-level theorem is Divided Power Algebra, lemma perfect-NL-lci (a perfect map is lci iff its naive cotangent complex has tor-amplitude in [-1,0]). Every input is a named bridge. Retained author proof at lines 18488-18498.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section Thickenings

items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X, if the canonical morphism X -> Spec Gamma(X, O_X) (whose existence is Schemes, lemma morphism-into-affine) admits a retraction, then X is affine. The retained proof is written: denote f : X -> S and s : S -> X with s f = id_X; composing f s f = f, the two endomorphisms f s and id_S of the affine scheme S induce the same map on global sections (since f is an isomorphism on global sections by construction of S), and the fully faithfulness of Gamma on affines (the contravariant equivalence between affine schemes and rings, invoked through the uniqueness clause of the same Schemes lemma) forces f s = id_S; hence f is an isomorphism and X is affine. Retained author proof at lines 23554-23563.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a commutative square of sites with cocontinuous functors satisfying a compatibility condition on the auxiliary categories, the two composites of the pushforward with the pullback of the associated morphisms of topoi agree, and likewise for the composites involving the lower adjoints (statement lines 6865-6889). The proof is a complete computation: both composites are computed as limits over the auxiliary categories, using the identifications of the pullbacks and pushforwards with the functors on presheaves (proof lines 6892-6910); and the hypothesis on the functor between the auxiliary categories together with the general statement about limits differing by an initial object identifies the two limits, giving the first equality, while the second follows by uniqueness of adjoints (proof lines 6911-6914). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two limits. The claim is H2: a computation with each input named.

items.title: The completed tensor product of weakly pre-adic rings is weakly adic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For continuous homomorphisms of linearly topologized rings, the lemma asserts that the completed tensor product of two weakly pre-adic rings is weakly adic (statement lines 1755-1760). The proof uses the characterisation of weak adicness and the earlier analysis of the completed tensor product: that analysis gives admissibility of the completed tensor product, and its proof shows that the closure of the sum of the ideals generated by ideals of definition of the two rings is an ideal of definition (proof lines 1762-1770). It therefore remains to see that the closures of the powers of that ideal are open, which follows because the nth power contains the sum of the ideals generated by the nth powers of the two given ideals, and those closures are open by the hypothesis that the two rings are weakly pre-adic (proof lines 1770-1777). The claim is H2: the argument reuses the proof of the preceding lemma for the ideal of definition and then verifies the second half of the characterisation by a containment of powers, so it is short but complete and not a restatement.

items.title: Morphisms between formal spectra come from continuous ring maps
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For weakly admissible topological rings A and B over a scheme, the lemma asserts that every morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces from the formal spectrum of B to that of A is the formal spectrum of a unique continuous algebra map from A to B (statement lines 2354-2360). The proof constructs the ring map from the morphism: for each weak ideal of definition of B, the factorisation statement for morphisms from a quasi-compact object into a filtered colimit gives a weak ideal of definition of A such that the corresponding morphism of affine schemes factors through the spectrum of the quotient of A, and the universal property of the spectrum of an affine scheme turns this into an algebra map between the quotients (proof lines 2362-2369). These maps are compatible as the ideal varies, so they assemble into a map of rings, which is continuous because the preimage of each weak ideal of definition of B contains one of A, and the identity with the formal spectrum of that map holds by construction (proof lines 2369-2378). The claim is H2: the argument produces the ring map from compatible quotient maps and verifies both continuity and the identification with the given morphism, each with its own reason.

items.title: A k-algebra with exactly two k-subalgebras is k x k or k[epsilon]
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter curves.tex (Algebraic Curves)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file curves.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-no-in-between-over-k at source lines 3182-3187: if k is algebraically closed and k is contained in an algebra A which has exactly two k-subalgebras, then A is either k x k or the dual numbers k[epsilon]. The proof at source lines 3189-3199 is short but does real work: it translates the two-subalgebra hypothesis into the statement that any intermediate subring is k or A, picks an element t outside k, uses that to write A as a quotient k[x]/I, and then splits on the ideal I. The case I = 0 is excluded by exhibiting the intermediate subalgebra k[x^2]. In the remaining case the argument needs the algebraic closedness of k to factor the monic generator into linear factors, excludes degree greater than two by exhibiting the intermediate subalgebra generated by a product of two of those factors, and finally separates the two degree-two possibilities (distinct roots giving k x k, a repeated root giving k[epsilon]). Several of those steps are choices of a specific intermediate subalgebra, and the statement does not indicate them. No result outside the retained span is invoked.

primary.label: lemma-no-in-between-over-k (statement, Glueing and squishing)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following it (source lines 3189-3199)

items.title: Projective space bundle formula: the Chow groups of a projective bundle are free over the Chow groups of the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-chow.tex (Chow Groups of Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-chow.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the projective space bundle formula at source lines 4380-4403, label lemma-chow-ring-projective-bundle, whose proof occupies source lines 4405-4512. The two halves are different in kind. Injectivity is a short computation that must be iterated: the pushforward of the universal combination returns the top component, and multiplying by the Chern class before pushing forward strips one component at a time. Surjectivity is a reduction and induction: the class is decomposed into classes of integral closed subspaces, the statement is proved on the fibre products over their images and reassembled through locally finite sums, which reduces to an integral base and a single dominating subspace, and the induction on the dimension of the base shrinks to an open subspace, lifts cycles from the open and disposes of the difference through the exact sequence of the complement before quoting the scheme case. The counted statement records neither the induction nor the decomposition.

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement characterises representable morphisms of algebraic stacks which are universally injective as those whose every base change induces an injective map on topological spaces (author lemma at source lines 2833-2845, label lemma-characterize-representable-universally-injective). The proof (source lines 2847-2870) proves the non-trivial direction by choosing a smooth scheme cover of the test stack, where the base change is injective by hypothesis, and descending injectivity along the comparison square whose horizontal arrows are open and surjective and whose induced map to the fibre product of spaces is surjective (proof lines 2848-2868); the converse is recorded as following from the definitions. The descent along the comparison square is the content. H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects three facts about modules over a Dedekind domain: flatness is equivalent to torsion freeness, finite torsion free modules are finite locally free, and over a principal ideal domain finite torsion free modules are free. The first part reduces to the local rings of the domain, which are discrete valuation rings, where the equivalence is known, and the reduction is justified by the local nature of flatness and of torsion. items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the fibre product of two surjections of complete Noetherian local rings over a common quotient is again a complete Noetherian local ring. The proof builds an explicit presentation: it chooses a Cohen ring or the residue field itself according to the characteristic, uses the Cohen structure theorem to write the quotient as a quotient of a power series ring, lifts the two surjections to that power series ring using formal smoothness of power series rings over a Cohen ring and the lifting of continuous maps, and then presents the fibre product as a quotient of a power series ring in the variables of the base together with generators of the two kernels. Being a quotient of a complete local ring makes the fibre product complete.

items.title: Factoring a map of complexes through a K-flat complex up to homotopy
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma factors a map from a K-flat complex into an arbitrary complex through a K-flat complex, up to homotopy, with the factor map a quasi-isomorphism, and shows that flatness of the terms can be preserved. The proof is a pure exercise in the triangulated structure of the homotopy category: it completes the map to a distinguished triangle, replaces the cone by a K-flat complex with flat terms, uses the triangle axioms to build a new triangle whose third term is K-flat by the two-out-of-three property, maps it to the original triangle, and concludes that the new arrow is a quasi-isomorphism by two out of three. The improvement of the constructed complex to one with flat terms in each degree is obtained from the refinement lemma on distinguished triangles.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the category of finite projective modules over the fibre product of two rings with the category of triples of a finite projective module over one factor, a finite projective module over the other, and an isomorphism after base change. The proof reduces finite projectivity to finite presentation plus flatness, uses the earlier flatness and finiteness results to reduce to showing that the fibre product module is finitely presented, then chooses a surjection from a finite free module, compares the kernel with the fibre product of the kernels obtained after base change, verifies that the comparison map is an isomorphism, and concludes finite generation of the kernel from the exactness of the two sequences after tensoring, which is exactly where flatness of the two given modules is used.

items.title: Flatness and formal smoothness of a local map versus regularity of its special fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition proves the equivalence of three conditions on a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings: flatness together with geometric regularity of the special fibre, flatness together with formal smoothness of the fibre in the maximal-adic topology, and formal smoothness of the local map itself. One equivalence is quoted from the regular-fibre theorem and one implication follows from flatness of formally smooth maps plus base change, so the substance is the remaining implication: the author first replaces the rings by their completions, then chooses the standard diagram of a power series ring over a Cohen ring mapping to the target, cuts the target down by a regular sequence so that the special fibres become equal, and finishes with the lifting argument of the regular-fibre theorem in which a derivation into a square-zero ideal is adjusted by a map on differentials. The proof is a long, self-contained chain of reductions and is fully displayed.

items.title: Pseudo-coherence is local for a finite cover by principal open sets
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that pseudo-coherence of a complex can be checked after localising at finitely many elements generating the unit ideal. The proof is an induction on the difference between the highest degree in which cohomology can be nonzero and the bounding degree m: the exactness of localisation identifies the localised cohomology with the cohomology of the localised complex, finiteness of the localised cohomology in the top degree plus the cover lemma gives finiteness of that cohomology module over the ring, and a surjection from a finite free module together with projectivity produces a map to the complex whose cone vanishes in high degrees and whose localisations remain m-pseudo-coherent by the cone lemma, so the induction applies and the cone lemma finishes the argument.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the completed localisation of a mixed power series and polynomial algebra over a field of positive characteristic becomes geometrically regular after extending scalars from the fraction field. The proof is an induction on the degree of a finite purely inseparable field extension: the base case is regularity of the completion of a regular local ring, and the induction step adjoins a p-th root, replaces the field by a finite algebra over the base, computes the base change as a quotient of a polynomial ring over a field, and uses a derivation that does not vanish on the element whose p-th root is adjoined. The derivation is extended through localisation and completion, which makes the quotient regular by the degree-p criterion.

items.title: A product of pairs is henselian exactly when each factor is
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises henselian pairs among arbitrary products: the product pair is henselian if and only if every factor is. One direction is immediate from the fact that each projection is an integral ring map and the permanence of the henselian property under integral maps. For the other, the author works componentwise: elements of one plus the product ideal are units because they are componentwise, which puts the product ideal inside the Jacobson radical, and then a monic polynomial over the product with a factorisation of its reduction generating the unit ideal admits a lift of the factorisation because it does in every factor, which is exactly the defining property of a henselian pair.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the henselization and the strict henselization of a Noetherian local P-ring remain P-rings. The henselization case is quoted from the companion result for the henselian pair, and the strict henselization case is reduced to the condition on formal fibres. items.title: Lifting a formally smooth complete local algebra along a residue field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma lifts a formally smooth Noetherian complete local algebra over a residue field to a formally smooth local algebra over a Noetherian complete local ring, with prescribed special fibre. The proof reuses the standard diagram of a power series ring over a Cohen ring mapping to the target: because both the target and the special fibre of the power series ring are regular, the kernel of the surjection onto the target is generated by elements that extend to a regular system of parameters, and cutting the power series ring down by lifts of those elements leaves a power series ring whose special fibre is the target itself. The map from the Cohen ring is then formally smooth by the flat-fibre criterion, and base change along the given ring map produces the required lift.

items.title: Lifting an idempotent modulo an ideal after an etale base change that is an isomorphism on the quotient
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma lifts an idempotent of an integral algebra modulo an ideal after an etale base change which induces an isomorphism modulo that ideal. The proof picks a lift of the idempotent, applies the integrality helper to obtain a monic polynomial vanishing at that lift modulo the ideal, and then uses the factorisation lemma to split that polynomial, after an etale base change of the required kind, into factors congruent to a power of the variable and to a power of the variable minus one. The two evaluations of the factors at the lifted element multiply to zero, so their common vanishing locus avoids the closed set cut out by the ideal; closedness of the integral map on spectra produces a single element whose localisation separates the two loci, after which the two loci are disjoint and cover the spectrum, so that the corresponding idempotent lifts the given one by uniqueness of the splitting.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the inverse limit of a surjective system of modules flat over the successive quotients by powers of an ideal is flat over the ring, and that tensoring with any finite module commutes with the limit. items.title: The property of being a henselian pair is preserved by limits
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an inverse limit of henselian pairs, with the limit ideal, is again a henselian pair. The proof reduces to products and equalizers since limits in the relevant category are built from those, quotes the product case, and then treats an equalizer diagram of henselian pairs. The verification uses Gabber's criterion: elements of one plus the limit ideal are units because inverses are unique and the statement holds in the first pair, which puts the limit ideal inside the Jacobson radical, and then a polynomial of the shape used in the criterion, whose coefficients apart from the leading ones lie in the limit ideal, has a unique root near one in the first ring, whose images under the two parallel maps agree by uniqueness, so that root descends to the equalizer.

items.title: Ext out of an m-pseudo-coherent complex commutes with filtered colimits below degree minus m
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes Ext groups out of an m-pseudo-coherent complex against a filtered colimit of modules: in degrees below minus m the colimit of the Ext groups is the Ext group of the colimit, and in degree minus m the comparison map is injective. The proof uses the defining triangle that exhibits the complex as an extension of a bounded complex of finite free modules by a complex with vanishing cohomology above m, observes that Ext out of the second term vanishes in the relevant degrees, and deduces through the long exact sequence that Ext out of the given complex is isomorphic, respectively injective, into Ext out of the finite free complex. The remaining claim is that Ext out of a finite free complex commutes with filtered colimits, which follows by computing it with the Hom complex and using finiteness of the terms plus exactness of filtered colimits.

items.title: Reflexivity of the kernel of a surjection with reflexive middle term and torsion-free quotient
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that in an exact sequence of finite modules over a Noetherian domain, reflexivity of the middle term together with torsion freeness of the quotient forces reflexivity of the kernel. The proof dualises the sequence twice to obtain a commutative diagram in which the middle vertical arrow is an isomorphism and the right one is injective, reduces to the claim that the map induced on the double duals of the kernel is injective, and then proves that claim: the cokernel Q of the dualised sequence becomes zero after tensoring with the fraction field, because the map on the fraction fields is a split injection of vector spaces, so Q is torsion and has no maps into the ring. A diagram chase then identifies the left vertical arrow as an isomorphism.

items.title: Fields, complete local rings, the integers, one-dimensional local and Nagata rings, and Dedekind domains of characteristic zero are J-2
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition collects seven classes of rings that are J-2. The proof checks the relevant criterion for each class: for fields, the integers, one-dimensional Nagata rings and Dedekind domains with fraction field of characteristic zero it verifies the condition on finite purely inseparable extensions of residue fields, carrying out the one-dimensional Nagata case in detail, where either the prime is maximal, so the extension is finite over a regular ring, or it is minimal, where the Nagata condition makes the integral closure in the extension finite and hence a one-dimensional normal, therefore regular, domain. For complete local rings and for one-dimensional local rings it uses the criterion on finite extensions instead, reducing the first to the statement that a complete local domain is J-0 and observing in the second case that the regular locus is stable under generalisation on a finite spectrum.

items.title: Flat essentially finite type algebras and modules over a valuation ring are essentially of finite presentation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that over a valuation ring, a flat local homomorphism which is essentially of finite type is essentially of finite presentation, and that a finite module which is flat over the valuation ring is finitely presented over its algebra. The proof writes the algebra as a quotient of a localised polynomial algebra, chooses a presentation of the module over that localisation, and takes the intersection of the kernel with the polynomial algebra. That intersection localises back to the kernel, and the quotient it defines is a submodule of the module, hence flat over the valuation ring by torsion freeness, which combined with finiteness gives finite presentation over the polynomial algebra; exactness of localisation then identifies the localised submodule with the module.

Assuming (K_n|V) and (K_n|W) are pro-isomorphic to Deligne systems, the proof notes that the same holds on V cap W because restrictions to opens preserve Deligne systems, so the pro-systems on U cap V, U cap W and U cap V cap W are essentially constant, and the distinguished triangles of Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-exact-sequence-j-star together with Derived Categories, Lemma labelled derived-lemma-essentially-constant-2-out-of-3 show that (K_n|_U) is essentially constant with value K (proof lines 8382-8394). For an arbitrary L in D^b_Coh(O_X) the proof then writes a five row diagram of colimits of Ext^{-1} and Hom over V, W, V cap W and their intersections with U, whose vertical sequences are exact by Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-mayer-vietoris-hom and exactness of filtered colimits, and whose horizontal arrows are isomorphisms except the middle one by Lemma labelled lemma-lift-map and the invariance of colimits under pro-isomorphism, so the 5-lemma makes the middle arrow an isomorphism as well (proof lines 8396-8420). This shows that (K_n) is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system for K: taking a Deligne system (K'_n) with constant value K on U, which exists by Lemma labelled lemma-extension-by-zero, one has the same colimit of Hom_X(K'_n, L), so the two pro-systems are pro-isomorphic by Categories, Remark labelled categories-remark-pro-category-copresheaves (proof lines 8422-8425). Setting up the Mayer-Vietoris diagram so that the 5-lemma identifies the middle arrow, and then concluding pro-isomorphism from equality of colimits of Hom, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Gorensteinness of a flat finite presentation morphism is characterised by the existence of a Gorenstein quasi-finite morphism to affine space
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a flat locally finite presentation f : X -> S, a point x with image s and d = dim_x(X_s), the lemma shows the equivalence of four conditions: f is Gorenstein at x; there is an open U containing x with a locally quasi-finite morphism U -> A^d_S over S that is Gorenstein at x; the same with U -> A^d_S globally Gorenstein; and for every S-morphism g : U -> A^d_S from an open neighbourhood of x, quasi-finiteness of g at x implies that g is Gorenstein at x; in particular the Gorenstein locus is open (statement lines 6767-6784). The proof reduces to algebra: it chooses affine U = Spec(A) and V = Spec(R) with R -> A flat of finite presentation, replaces A by a principal localization so that a quasi-finite map R[x_1, ..., x_d] -> A exists by Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra, thus producing at least one pair (U, g) (proof lines 6786-6798). The statement is then translated, with the translation marked 'omitted', into the equivalence of (a) Spec(phi) Gorenstein at p, (b) Spec(A) -> Spec(R) Gorenstein at p and (c) the same in an open neighbourhood of p (proof lines 6800-6814). Since flatness is open by Algebra, Theorem labelled algebra-theorem-openness-flatness, one may assume R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A flat, and Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat produces R_0 of finite type over Z and R_0[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A_0 of finite type and flat spreading out the data; because the Gorenstein locus of a flat finite type morphism commutes with base change by Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-gorenstein, this reduces to Noetherian R (proof lines 6816-6828). Finally, with X and S affine and a factorization X -> A^n_S -> S with g flat quasi-finite and S Noetherian, the proof writes f^!O_S = g^!p^!O_S = g^!O_{A^n_S}[n] using Lemmas labelled lemma-upper-shriek-composition and lemma-shriek-affine-line, and concludes the equivalence of (a), (b) and (c) from Lemma labelled lemma-affine-flat-Noetherian-gorenstein (proof lines 6830-6841). Translating the geometric conditions into the algebra problem and then spreading out to the Noetherian case, with the shriek computation providing the link, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

Since beta and beta^vee are isomorphisms and the outside of the diagram is beta o alpha o eta_f by definition, the lemma follows (proof lines 2032-2034). items.title: Extension by zero commutes with a proper morphism over an open subscheme
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism f : X -> Y of Noetherian schemes, an open V of Y with U = f^{-1}(V) and the cartesian square relating them, the lemma asserts a canonical isomorphism Rj'_! o Rg_* -> Rf_* o Rj_! of functors D^b_Coh(O_U) -> Pro-D^b_Coh(O_Y), where the extension functors are those of Remark labelled remark-extension-by-zero (statement lines 8471-8486). For K in D^b_Coh(O_U) the proof takes a Deligne system (K_n) for U -> X whose restriction is constant with value K, representing Rj_!K in the pro category, observes that both Rj'_!Rg_*K and Rf_*Rj_!K restrict to the constant pro-object with value Rg_*K on V, the second because (Rf_*K_n)|_V = Rg_*(K_n|_U) = Rg_*K, and concludes by the uniqueness of Deligne systems in Lemma labelled lemma-extension-by-zero that it suffices to show that (Rf_*K_n) is pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system, which also gives functoriality (proof lines 8488-8502). The second paragraph shows this: the question is independent of the choice of (K_n) by the same uniqueness, and Lemmas labelled lemma-extension-by-zero-triangle and lemma-deligne-system-2-out-of-3 make the property a 2-out-of-3 property along distinguished triangles, so the truncation triangles of Derived Categories, Remark labelled derived-remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle reduce to a single coherent O_X-module F (proof lines 8504-8516). Writing J for an ideal cutting out Y minus V and J^n F for the image of f^*J^n otimes F -> F, the proof must show that (Rf_*(J^n F)) is a Deligne system; by Lemma labelled lemma-characterize-extension-by-zero the question is local on Y, so one takes Y = Spec(A) affine with J corresponding to an ideal I, and by Lemma labelled lemma-characterize-extension-by-zero-algebra it suffices to show that the inverse system (H^p(X, I^n F)) is pro-isomorphic to (I^n M) for some finite A-module M, which is Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma labelled coherent-lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-application (proof lines 8518-8533). Reducing the statement to a local algebra question about powers of an ideal in cohomology, via the uniqueness of Deligne systems and the 2-out-of-3 property, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for an adically complete module the associated primes of a tensor product with an arbitrary module never generate the unit ideal together with the extended ideal (statement lines 4348-4355, tag 05JC-adjacent). The proof views everything over the completion, picks an element whose annihilator is the given associated prime, uses that the element is nonzero to find a maximal ideal of the completion containing the extended prime, and concludes because the extended ideal lies in every such maximal ideal. The reduction to the completion is the substance, so the claim is H2.

items.title: Universal closedness of a representable morphism of algebraic spaces tested by base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a representable morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, universal closedness in the representable sense is equivalent to |Z x_Y X| -> |Z| being closed for every morphism Z -> Y (source lines 1516-1526). The proof is the same topological square argument as for submersiveness: choose a surjective etale V -> Y, use that V x_Y X -> V is universally closed as a morphism of schemes, and observe that in the square comparing |V x_Y X| -> |V| with |Z x_Y X| -> |Z| the horizontal arrows are open and surjective and the comparison map |V x_Y X| -> |V| x_{|Z|} |Z x_Y X| is surjective, so closedness of the left vertical arrow forces closedness of the right one; the converse is immediate.

items.title: A morphism of algebraic spaces is flat if and only if it is flat at every point

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S is flat if and only if it is flat at all points of |X| (source lines 6005-6009).
