items.difficulty_reason: The lemma (with the chapter's slogan 'Affineness is insensitive to thickenings') states that any thickening of an affine scheme is affine, citing EGA1 Proposition 5.1.9 for the finite-order case. Two retained proofs are collected: the short pointer proof (special case of Limits, proposition affine, quoted by name) and the substantive proof for a finite order thickening — the latter is written out in the retained span: given X ⊂ X' finite order with X affine, Serre's criterion (Cohomology of Schemes, lemma quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering) reduces affineness of X' to vanishing H^1 for quasi-coherent F; the nilpotent ideal I = Ker(O_{X'} -> i_*O_X) gives the filtration F_a = I^a F whose successive quotients are i_*G_a pushforwards from X (Morphisms, lemma i-star-equivalence), whose H^1 on X' equals H^1 on X (Cohomology of Schemes, lemma relative-affine-cohomology) and vanishes by affineness of X (Cohomology of Schemes, lemma quasi-coherent-affine-cohomology-zero); a finite induction concludes. The general case then rests on the collected pointer to the Limits proposition. Retained author spans: statement 156-165, proofs 167-170 and 172-206.

items.title: Four equivalent guises of finiteness for morphisms of algebraic spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y a morphism of algebraic spaces over S the lemma proves the equivalence of: (1) f finite; (2) f proper and locally quasi-finite; (3) f proper with |X_k| discrete for every field-valued point of Y; (4) f universally closed, separated, locally of finite type, with the same discreteness. The retained proof is complete: (1)=>(2)=>(3)=>(4) chain through the chapter's standard permanence lemmas; the heart is (4)=>(1), written out: universal closedness gives quasi-compactness, discreteness plus qc makes each field fibre finite, the elementary etale neighbourhood splitting lemma (chapter lemma etale-splits-off-quasi-finite-part) carves the fibre into a finite piece V and a remainder W whose image misses the centre, universal closedness closes the W-image so shrinking kills W entirely, etale-locally on Y the base change is finite, and integrality-is-etale-local finishes. Retained author proof at lines 7862-7900.

items.title: A geometric fibre of a map of spaces is connected exactly when every etale neighbourhood sees a connected ordinary fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S and a geometric point ybar of Y, the geometric fibre X_{ybar} is connected if and only if for every etale neighbourhood (V, vbar) -> (Y, ybar) with V a scheme the base change X_V -> V has connected fibre X_v. The retained proof: the category of etale neighbourhoods of ybar is cofiltered with a cofinal system of schemes (Properties of Spaces, cofinal-etale), so reduce to Y a scheme with closed-under-reference point y; then X_y geometrically connected over kappa(y) iff X_{ybar} connected iff (X_y)_{k'} connected for every finite separable k'/kappa(y) (Spaces over Fields, geometrically-connected section and characterize-geometrically-disconnected); finally every finite separable extension is realized on residue fields by an affine etale neighbourhood (More on Morphisms, realize-prescribed-residue-field-extension-etale), which turns the finite-separable test into the quantifier over etale neighbourhoods. Retained author proof at lines 8107-8124.

items.title: Relative perfection over a ring tested against all perfect pairings, via fibre boundedness and a generator
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For A a ring, X flat separated of finite presentation over A and K in D_QCoh(O_X): if RGamma(X, E (x) K) is perfect in D(A) for every perfect E, then K is Spec(A)-perfect. The retained proof is complete: first upgrade K to absolute pseudo-coherence — the improved variant of the pairing lemma (chapter lemma characterize-pcoherent-improved, in the revived queue) gives relative pseudo-coherence and the moot lemma (card L16171) converts it to absolute; the bounded-below detection proposition puts K in D^-(O_X). Fibrewise: for every prime p of A, the bounded-on-fibres criterion (card L16169) reduces perfection to Li^*K bounded below on the fibre Y over p; a Bondal-van den Bergh generator G of D_QCoh(O_X) (theorem bondal-van-den-Bergh) has its restriction Li^*G generating D_QCoh(O_Y) (remark pullback-generator), and the displayed duality computation — RHom_Y(Li^*G, Li^*K) = RGamma(X, G^vee (x) K) (x)_A k(p), justified by the dual-perfect-complex lemma and the compare-base-change lemma using flatness — is perfect over k(p) by hypothesis; the bounded-below detection proposition applied on the fibre concludes. Retained author proof at lines 12789-12829.

items.title: Smoothness and etaleness near a Noetherian closed subspace are detected on its infinitesimal neighbourhoods
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y locally of finite type with Y locally Noetherian and Z ⊂ Y closed with nth infinitesimal neighbourhoods Z_n, X_n = Z_n x_Y X: if every X_n -> Z_n is smooth then f is smooth along f^{-1}(Z); if every X_n -> Z_n is etale then f is etale along f^{-1}(Z). The retained proof is complete via the Artinian lifting criterion: at x over Z, a small extension B' -> B with the test diagram of the chapter's lifting-along-artinian-at-point lemma has nilpotent maximal ideal (B' Artinian), so the structure map beta factors through some Z_n and alpha through the corresponding X_n; the hypothesized lifting property of X_n -> Z_n supplies the dotted arrow, proving smoothness at x. Part (2) is (1) plus the etale = smooth of relative dimension zero characterization. Retained author proof at lines 5245-5256.

items.difficulty_reason: In the derived-Chow setup of the chapter (X/A as in lemma derived-chow with data n, Z, z, V, E and the diagram W -> Z -> X, W -> V -> P^n_A), for any K in D_QCoh(O_X) the identity Rq_*(Lp^*K (x) E)|_V = R(W -> V)_* K|_W holds on V, with p, q the projections of X x_A P^n_A. The retained proof is complete: c|_W : W -> V is a closed immersion of finite presentation (permanence lemma); the total direct image commutes with localization to V; property (5) of the Chow setup replaces E| by i_*O_W for the closed immersion i = (b, c)|_W; i is a closed immersion so i_*O_W = Ri_*O_W; the cohomology-base-change chain Rq'_* Ri_* Li^* Lp^*K = R(q' o i)_* Lb^*K collapses via q' o i = (W -> V) and Lb^* = restriction to W (etale note: W -> X etale, derived pullback equals restriction), which is the claim. Retained author proof at lines 12128-12162.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y flat and of finite presentation between spaces over S, the function n_{X/Y} on Y recording fibre dimensions (constructed in the base-change-dimension-fibres lemma) is lower semi-continuous. The retained proof: test after a surjective etale map g : V -> Y with V a scheme — since |g| is open, lower semi-continuity of the pullback function implies that of n_{X/Y}; shrink V affine, take a surjective etale U -> X with U an affine scheme; the equality n_{X/Y} = n_{U/Y} (dimensions are etale-invariant along the cover) reduces to the schemes statement (More on Morphisms, dimension-fibres-flat). Retained author proof at lines 7213-7224.

items.title: The fibre-dimension function of a proper map of spaces is upper semi-continuous
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y a proper morphism of algebraic spaces over S, the fibre-dimension function n_{X/Y} (from the base-change-dimension-fibres lemma) is upper semi-continuous. The retained proof is written out in full: for each d set Z_d = {x in |X| : the fibre of f at x has dimension > d}; the bounded-dimension-fibres lemma (Morphisms of Spaces, openness-bounded-dimension-fibres) makes Z_d closed in |X|; properness makes f(Z_d) closed in |Y|; and y lies in f(Z_d) exactly when n_{X/Y}(y) > d, which is the upper semi-continuity criterion. Retained author proof at lines 7235-7244.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces

items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y flat and locally of finite presentation between spaces over S, the set W of points where f is Cohen-Macaulay is open in |X| and for any base change g : Y' -> Y the corresponding set W' for f' equals (g')^{-1}(W). items.title: Collapsing a fibre of a proper family onto a separated finite-type target forces the whole family near the base point to factor through a finite subspace
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a commutative triangle X -> Y -> B of spaces over S with X -> B proper, Y -> B separated locally of finite type, and either (3a) the image of |X_k| -> |Y_k| finite or (3b) the image of the fibre over b in |Y| finite with B decent, there is an open B' through b through which X_{B'} -> Y_{B'} factors via a closed Z finite over B'. The retained proof: take Z the scheme-theoretic image of h; proper-pushforward lemmas make X -> Z surjective and Z -> B proper; the two fibre finiteness hypotheses make Z -> B quasi-finite at every point over b (Decent Spaces, conditions-on-fibre-and-qf); the in-source proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood lemma (this wave's L16242) turns that into finiteness over an open neighbourhood. The author's slogan: collapsing a fibre of a proper family forces nearby ones to collapse too. Retained author proof at lines 7960-7978.

items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y formally unramified between spaces over S, any solid diagram against a first order thickening T ⊂ T' of spaces over S admits at most one dotted arrow — the affineness hypothesis in the definition of formally unramified may be dropped. items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y an lci morphism of spaces over S, P smooth over Y, U -> X etale and i : U -> P a Y-immersion (the standard factorization picture), i is a Koszul-regular immersion of spaces. items.title: The number of geometric connected components of fibres of a proper flat finitely presented map is lower semi-continuous
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y proper, flat, of finite presentation between spaces over S, the function n_{X/Y} on |Y| counting geometric connected components of the fibres is lower semi-continuous. The retained proof is complete: etale-localize Y to an affine scheme; for y with n = n_{X/Y}(y) finite (Noetherian fibre), take the general Stein factorization X -> Y' -> Y (same wave, L16200); the Stein-fibre lemma (chapter lemma stein-universally-closed-residue-fields, in the revived queue) gives exactly finitely many points y'_1..y'_m of Y' over y with finite residue extensions; an etale neighbourhood splits Y' into disjoint scheme pieces V_i through the schemes-side etale-splits-integral lemma (More on Morphisms, lemma etale-makes-integral-split) with purely inseparable residue extensions, so the fibres X_{y'_i} are geometrically connected over k(y) and m = n; the pieces X_i = (f')^{-1}(V_i) are flat finitely presented over Y hence have OPEN images (Morphisms of Spaces, lemma fppf-open); on the common neighbourhood of the y-images, n_{X/Y} >= n. Retained author proof at lines 8360-8384.

items.title: Three equivalent chart tests for relative pseudo-coherence of complexes on algebraic spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y locally of finite type between spaces over S, m in Z, E in D_QCoh(O_X), the lemma proves the equivalence of: (1) E|_U is m-pseudo-coherent relative to V for every etale chart square from schemes U, V; (2) the same for one surjective chart; (3) for every affine chart square, RGamma(U, E) is m-pseudo-coherent relative to O_X(U) over O_Y(V). The retained proof is complete: (1)=>(3) imports the schemes dictionary More on Morphisms, lemma qcoh-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize; (3)=>(2) covers the chart by affines and reapplies the same dictionary; (2)=>(1) is the written comparison — for any second chart, pass to the fibre product U'' over V'' factoring through V' x_Y V, descend along the fppf-stability lemma (card L16106) and the post-composition invariance (card L16115), then pull back along the etale map whose pseudo-coherence input is finite-presentation (cards L16168/L16151-era dictionary; the cited lemmas relative-pseudo-coherent-descends-fppf, relative-pseudo-coherent-post-compose, pull-relative-pseudo-coherent, flat-finite-presentation-pseudo-coherent are all on record). The equivalence licenses the D_QCoh-only definition used by the two neighbouring characterization cards. Retained author proof at lines 10786-10831.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For first order thickenings X ⊂ X', Y ⊂ Y' over B, a map a : X -> Y and a module map A : a^*C_{Y/Y'} -> C_{X/X'}, the rule assigning to each etale U' over X' the set of B-morphisms a' : U' -> Y' restricting to a on U = X x_{X'} U' and inducing the given conormal map A|_U is a sheaf of sets on (X')_{spaces,etale}. items.title: Open-and-closed proper pieces of the special fibre of a henselian pair split off globally on spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces), section on thickenings of algebraic spaces
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For (A, I) a henselian pair, X separated of finite type over A with special fibre X_0, and Y ⊂ X_0 open and closed proper over A/I, there exists W ⊂ X open and closed, proper over A, with W_0 = Y. The retained proof is complete: take a surjective proper modification phi : X' -> X with X' admitting an immersion into P^n_A via the weak Chow lemma (Cohomology of Spaces, lemma weak-chow); the schemes-side twin (More on Morphisms, lemma split-off-proper-part-henselian) supplies W' ⊂ X' with W'_0 = Y' = phi^{-1}(Y); the images Q_1 = phi(|W'|) and Q_2 = phi(|X' \ W'|) are closed by universally-closed permanence, Q_1 carries only proper closed-subspace structures (image-proper-is-proper); the intersection Q_1 x Q_2 maps closed into Spec A and henselianity forces any of its points to lie over V(I), contradicting W'_0 = Y' — so Q_1 is open and closed, and W = the corresponding subspace of X satisfies W proper with W_0 = Y by descent along the surjection. Retained author proof at lines 8493-8520.

primary.label: lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian

items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y proper of algebraic spaces over S with Y locally Noetherian, the factorization X -> Y' -> Y has f' proper with geometrically connected fibres, pi FINITE (sharper than the general theorem's integral), f'_*O_X = O_{Y'}, Y' = Spec_Y(f_*O_X) the normalization. Retained author proof at lines 8148-8194.

items.difficulty_reason: For Z -> X formally unramified between spaces over S, the universal first order thickening Z' -> X is formally unramified. items.difficulty_reason: For a formal algebraic space X and a closed subset T of its reduction, the lemma asserts that the completion of X along T is locally countably indexed, locally adic* and locally Noetherian under the corresponding hypotheses on X, with the additional assumption that the complement of T maps quasi-compactly to the reduction in the first two cases (statement lines 8151-8164). The proof reduces all three statements to the affine case by choosing a presentation of X: the inverse image of T in each member is a closed subset, the base change of the completion along the member is the completion of the member along that subset, and these base changes form a presentation of the completion (proof lines 8166-8172). It then checks that the hypotheses transfer to the members: quasi-compactness of the complement passes to the complement of the inverse image, and the three properties of X pass to the members (proof lines 8172-8179). The conclusion is the affine statement proved earlier (proof lines 8177-8179). The claim is H2: the reduction is carried out by a presentation and a base change identity, the transfer of each hypothesis is stated, and the three cases are then settled by one named affine result.

items.title: The separation axioms for a morphism of formal algebraic spaces can be checked on affine base changes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of formal algebraic spaces and any of the separation axioms, the lemma states the equivalence of five formulations: the axiom itself; the axiom after base change to every scheme; after base change to every affine scheme; the statement that the affine base changes are of the corresponding type as formal algebraic spaces; and the axiom for the members of one presentation (statement lines 6884-6911). The first two implications are immediate once the stability of the axiom under base change is granted. The proof then supplies three genuinely different arguments. It passes from the third to the fourth by computing the relevant fibre product as a base change of the product of two affine schemes along the diagonal, and reading off that the result is quasi-compact, respectively an affine scheme with a closed immersion into that product (proof lines 6915-6926). It passes back from the fourth to the third by reading that computation backwards, using that the fibre products of an etale covering by affines form an etale covering of the square, to conclude the corresponding property for the diagonal (proof lines 6928-6950). The passage from the third to the fifth uses the presentation of the target, writes each member as a filtered colimit of affine formal subschemes, notes that the diagonal for the member is the colimit of the diagonals for the pieces, and concludes by testing after base change along affine schemes into the square, which is exactly what the factorisation statement for such colimits allows (proof lines 6952-6972). The final implication produces a fibre product square for the coproduct of the members of the presentation and uses the descent statement for representable transformations to transfer the property from the left vertical arrow to the right one (proof lines 6974-6981). The claim is H3: four implications are proved by four independent mechanisms -- a fibre product computation with the diagonal, its converse through an etale cover of the square, a colimit argument over a presentation, and a descent along a covering -- and each is displayed.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-chow.tex (Chow Groups of Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file spaces-chow.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the characterisation of the points of finite nonzero length as the generic points of the support of a coherent module at source lines 558-579, label lemma-length-finite, whose proof occupies source lines 581-623. The first half is a translation: coherence, support and length are compatible with an etale chart, and the condition that the point be a generic point of a component of the support becomes the condition that the support of the stalk be the maximal ideal, at which point an algebra criterion for finite modules over a Noetherian local ring settles the equivalence of the three conditions and shows the choice of chart is immaterial. The second half is genuinely topological: for a decent space one must compare, along the chart, which specialisations lift and which descend, and then invoke soberness of both underlying spaces to identify the generic points of the support with those of the pulled back support. The counted statement records neither the chart translation nor the specialisation argument.

The proof does not repeat the geometric work of the rational function case; instead it manufactures a situation in which the invertible sheaf becomes trivial, by taking a torsor over the base and pulling everything back along the flat projection from the fibre product. items.difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the surjectivity of pullback for affine bundles at source lines 3947-3955, label lemma-pullback-affine-fibres-surjective, whose proof occupies source lines 3957-4014. The proof is a reduction-plus-induction argument rather than a computation: the class is decomposed into classes of integral closed subspaces whose images in the base are again locally finite, which allows the statement to be checked on the fibre products over those images and then reassembled; this reduces to an integral base carrying the class of a single dominating subspace and makes induction on the dimension of the base available. The induction step shrinks to an open subspace, lifts the resulting class to the whole base, and disposes of the difference through the exact sequence of the complement. Only at the end does the fibrewise hypothesis enter, through the descent of the generic fibre isomorphism to an open subspace. The counted statement records none of these steps.

items.title: Finite projective modules over a henselian pair are the same as over its quotient
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that reduction modulo the ideal of a henselian pair induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of finite projective modules over the ring and over its quotient. Surjectivity is the substance: the given finite projective module over the quotient is first lifted to a finite projective module over an etale extension which induces an isomorphism on the quotient, and since the pair is henselian that etale map has a section, along which the lifted module is base changed to produce the required module over the ring. Injectivity reduces to Nakayama and a standard cancellation: an isomorphism modulo the ideal lifts to a surjection by projectivity, a reverse surjection is constructed the same way, and the composition of the two is an isomorphism because it reduces to one, hence both maps are isomorphisms.

items.title: Inverse limits of rings along surjections with locally nilpotent kernels are henselian pairs
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the inverse limit of a system of rings whose transition maps are surjective with locally nilpotent kernels, together with the kernel of the projection to any stage, is a henselian pair. The proof first checks that an element which is a unit modulo some stage is a unit in the limit, using the local nilpotence of the kernels, so that the ideal of the pair lies in the Jacobson radical. Then a monic polynomial with a factorisation of its reduction which generates the unit ideal is lifted factor by factor through the system, and at each stage the lifted factors are checked to generate the unit ideal by comparing the spectra of the polynomial rings over two stages, which are homeomorphic because the kernel is locally nilpotent.

items.title: Compact support duality is compatible with restricting to an open subscheme
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file duality.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: With the notation of Lemma labelled lemma-duality-compact-support, for an open subscheme U' of U the lemma asserts that the square relating the two duality isomorphisms Hom_k(H^i(U, K), k) = H^{-i}_c(U, RSheafHom(K, omega)) and its primed version commutes, where the left vertical arrow is the contragredient of the restriction map and the right one is the covariance map of Remark labelled remark-covariance-open-lower-shriek (statement lines 9189-9207). The author opens the proof with 'We strongly urge the reader to skip this proof' but the argument is written out in full: choose X and M as in the proof of Lemma labelled lemma-duality-compact-support, drop the subscripts from RSheafHom and the derived tensor product, and write both H^i(U, K) and H^i(U', K|_{U'}) as colimits over the powers of ideals I and I' with I' contained in I chosen as in Remark labelled remark-covariance-open-j-lower-shriek, so that the restriction map is induced by the maps (I')^n -> I^n (proof lines 9209-9240). Similarly both compact support groups are written as limits of H^i(X, RSheafHom(M, omega) otimes^L I^n) and its primed version, so that the right vertical arrow is deduced from the same maps (proof lines 9242-9254). The first intermediate square commutes because the horizontal arrows of Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-internal-hom-evaluate are functorial in all three entries, and the remaining square commutes because the duality isomorphism Hom_k(H^i(X, L), k) = Ext^{-i}_X(L, omega) = H^{-i}(X, RSheafHom(L, omega)) is functorial in L in D_QCoh(O_X) (proof lines 9256-9273). Tracking the two functorialities, one in the powers of the ideals and one in the duality isomorphism, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

After the usual abbreviation conventions the proof recalls that beta is an isomorphism and that alpha comes from the adjoint isomorphism beta^vee : g'_* o a' -> a o g_* of Lemma labelled lemma-flat-precompose-pus, and rewrites the top horizontal arrow as a three step composition through the unit and counit of the adjunction (g^*, g_*) using that their composite is the identity (proof lines 1890-1906). It then exhibits the large diagram whose two squares commute by Categories, Lemma labelled categories-lemma-properties-2-cat-cats, whose triangle commutes by the observation above, and whose pentagon commutes by Categories, Lemma labelled categories-lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints (proof lines 1908-1935). Since beta and beta^vee are isomorphisms and the outside of the diagram equals Tr_f o alpha o beta, the lemma follows (proof lines 1937-1941). Identifying the top arrow with the unit-counit composition and locating the category-theoretic identity that makes the pentagon commute is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma expresses a sheaf on the colimit site as the filtered colimit of the pullbacks of its pushforwards along the transition morphisms, with transition maps satisfying a cocycle condition (statement lines 4214-4226). The proof is a complete argument: the canonical maps are defined as counits of the adjunctions (proof lines 4229-4237); the cocycle condition follows from the general composition rule for counits (proof lines 4238-4242); and the identification of the colimit with the sheaf is obtained by evaluating at an object and comparing with the description of the values supplied by the companion result (proof lines 4243-4263). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two colimit descriptions. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.

items.title: The formal completion of an affine scheme along a closed subset, and its types
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme X with a closed subset T, the lemma asserts three things about the formal completion of X along T: that it is adic* when the complement of T is quasi-compact, that it is the formal spectrum of the adic completion with respect to a finitely generated ideal cutting out T, and that it is Noetherian when X is (statement lines 3275-3287). The proof reduces the first two assertions to the second: if either the complement is quasi-compact or the scheme is Noetherian, then T is cut out by a finitely generated ideal, and in the Noetherian case the adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, so it suffices to identify the completion in the case of an ideal cut out by finitely many elements (proof lines 3289-3296). That identification is a direct computation: a morphism from an affine scheme into X whose image lies in T has each of the chosen generators nilpotent after pullback, so some power of the ideal maps to zero, which says exactly that the functor is the filtered colimit of the spectra of the quotients by the powers of the ideal, that is the formal spectrum of the adic completion (proof lines 3298-3306). The claim is H2: the reduction of the two other assertions to the second uses the finite generation criterion in one case and permanence of Noetherianness under completion in the other, and the explicit identification of the functor is carried out.

items.title: A taut map from a pre-adic ring with finitely generated ideal of definition to a complete ring is adic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a taut continuous map from a pre-adic ring with a finitely generated ideal of definition to a complete ring makes the target adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition, and the map itself adic (statement lines 1556-1563). The proof fixes a finitely generated ideal of definition of the source, forms the closures of the images of its powers in the target, and uses completeness to write the target as the limit of the quotients by those closures (proof lines 1565-1568). It then compares this with the adic completion of the target with respect to that ideal: the algebra statement for completions with respect to a finitely generated ideal identifies the quotients of the completion with those of the target, so the canonical map from the completion is continuous with dense image, and it is taut because the tautness of the original map identifies the image ideals (proof lines 1568-1575). Since a continuous taut map with dense image is open and surjective, the topology on the target is the adic one, which gives the conclusion (proof lines 1575-1578). The claim is H2: the construction of the two completions, the comparison of their quotients, and the final openness argument are each displayed, and the hypotheses enter at specified points.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in characteristic zero smoothness at a prime, freeness of the module of differentials at that prime, and regularity of the local ring are equivalent for a finite type algebra over a field (statement lines 39037-39049). Choosing the nonzerodivisor so that the induction descends is the step that carries the last implication. H2.

items.work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), section on smooth ring maps
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four facts about completion: surjectivity lifts from the reduction modulo the ideal, surjectivity of the map lifts, a short exact sequence with flat quotient stays exact after completion, and the natural map from the completed base tensor a finite module to its completion is surjective (statement lines 22787-22801). The proof does not treat the four separately: it uses Nakayama over the nilpotent truncations to propagate surjectivity, obtains exactness from left exactness of limits plus flatness, and reduces the finiteness statement to a free presentation (proof lines 22803-22840). Reusing the first assertion for the last is the step that keeps the proof short. H2.

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that over a separably closed field the tensor product of two algebras each having a unique minimal prime again has a unique minimal prime (statement lines 11322-11327). The proof does not argue with minimal primes directly: it passes to the perfect closure, which is algebraically closed under the hypothesis, proves irreducibility of the fibres in that case, and applies the criterion for flat ring maps with irreducible fibres to the tensor product (proof lines 11329-11360). Passing to the perfect closure so that the field becomes algebraically closed is the step that simplifies the geometry. H2.

items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-tensor-with-complex-homotopy at source lines 6155-6160: the functor of the preceding lemma, tensoring a dg E-module with the complex K, defines an exact functor of triangulated categories from the homotopy category of dg E-modules to the homotopy category of complexes of O-modules. The proof at source lines 6162-6181 is a short but genuine exactness check. It first passes to the homotopy categories using the author's functoriality lemma, and then has to show that distinguished triangles go to distinguished triangles. Concretely, starting from an admissible short exact sequence of dg E-modules, it uses a graded splitting of the sequence to build a map between the tensored terms, checks that the resulting sequence of complexes is termwise split exact, and concludes that it is a distinguished triangle in the homotopy category of complexes of O-modules. items.work: Stacks Project — Morphisms of Algebraic Stacks
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file stacks-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement gives four equivalent conditions for a morphism of algebraic stacks to be locally quasi-finite: local quasi-finiteness itself, quasi-DM-ness together with a test over algebraic spaces, the existence of locally quasi-finite flat finitely presented covers over every test object, and one such cover over a single flat finitely presented cover of the target (author lemma at source lines 5134-5154, label lemma-characterize-locally-quasi-finite). The proof (source lines 5156-5215) runs the four implications, using the quasi-DM characterization in the first, the covering criterion in the second and fourth, and composition permanence at the end (proof lines 5156-5214). The construction of the covers and the closing permanence step are the substance. H3.

items.title: For a representable morphism, quasi-compactness is tested after arbitrary base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file stacks-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a morphism of algebraic stacks representable by algebraic spaces is quasi-compact if and only if every base change of it along a morphism from a quasi-compact algebraic stack is quasi-compact (author lemma at source lines 1918-1929, label lemma-characterize-representable-quasi-compact). The proof (source lines 1931-1961) proves the forward direction by presenting a quasi-compact test object and descending quasi-compactness along a smooth surjection, and the reverse direction by testing affine opens and applying the local criterion for quasi-compactness of a morphism of algebraic spaces (proof lines 1932-1960). The reduction to presentations and the local test on affine opens are the content. H3.

items.title: Local quasi-finiteness of a representable morphism is equivalent to discreteness of all field fibres
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project — Morphisms of Algebraic Stacks
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file stacks-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a morphism of algebraic stacks representable by algebraic spaces is locally quasi-finite if and only if it is locally of finite type and the space of every field-valued fibre is discrete (author lemma at source lines 4913-4925, label lemma-representable-by-spaces-quasi-finite). The proof (source lines 4927-4948) treats the forward direction by base change to a field, and the reverse direction by presenting the target, checking the property along the cover and applying the characterization for algebraic spaces (proof lines 4928-4946). The reduction through a smooth cover and the application of the scheme-free characterization are the content. H3.

The reduction through the presentation is the substance. H3.

items.title: For a representable morphism, separatedness is equivalent to the diagonal being a closed immersion, universally closed or proper
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project — Morphisms of Algebraic Stacks
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file stacks-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that for a morphism of algebraic stacks representable by algebraic spaces, separatedness and the three diagonal conditions (closed immersion, universally closed, proper) are equivalent (author lemma at source lines 451-461, label lemma-representable-separated-diagonal-closed). The proof (source lines 463-496) presents the morphism by algebraic spaces, uses the base change formula for the diagonal and the covering criterion to move every condition to the presentation, applies the corresponding equivalence for algebraic spaces, and closes the circle by identifying the diagonal of an arbitrary base change with a base change of the diagonal (proof lines 463-495). The reduction through the presentation and the two implications are the content. H3.

The identification of the two diagonals is the substance. H3.

items.title: A quotient of a smooth space by a flat finitely presented group is smooth over the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project — Morphisms of Algebraic Stacks
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file stacks-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that if a smooth algebraic space carries an action of a group algebraic space flat and locally of finite presentation over the base, then the quotient stack is smooth over the base (author lemma at source lines 7697-7703, label lemma-smooth-quotient-stack). The proof (source lines 7708-7725) applies the flat groupoid theorem, checks smoothness of the structure morphism after the flat finitely presented covering by the source of the action and descends (proof lines 7708-7724). The base change computation and the descent step are the substance. H3.

items.title: An integral stack has a sober irreducible space with a unique generic point and a dense open gerbe over an integral scheme
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project — Morphisms of Algebraic Stacks
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file stacks-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that an integral algebraic stack has a sober irreducible space with a unique generic point, and contains a dense open substack which is a gerbe over an integral scheme (author lemma at source lines 10650-10658, label lemma-structure-integral-stack). The proof (source lines 10660-10684) applies the sobriety proposition, takes the dense open gerbe supplied by the open stratum result, argues that its base is decent with irreducible space, that reducedness of the gerbe forces the base to be reduced and hence integral, and finally shrinks the base to an integral scheme (proof lines 10660-10683). The reducedness argument on the base is the substance. H3.

items.title: In a 2-commutative triangle with a surjective arrow, quasi-compactness of one leg implies quasi-compactness of the other
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project — Morphisms of Algebraic Stacks
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file stacks-morphisms.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that in a 2-commutative triangle of morphisms of algebraic stacks, quasi-compactness of one leg together with surjectivity of the opposite arrow forces quasi-compactness of the remaining leg (author lemma at source lines 2013-2025, label lemma-surjection-from-quasi-compact). The proof (source lines 2027-2041) tests the definition of quasi-compactness against an arbitrary quasi-compact stack mapping to the apex, uses that surjectivity survives base change, and concludes with the criterion that quasi-compactness descends along a surjective morphism (proof lines 2028-2039). The verification of the defining property at an arbitrary test object is the content. H2.
